apps.name: AdonisJS Auth
apps.line: Authentication guards and sessions for AdonisJS apps.

free.text: Free MIT package; you run it

cells.freeUsers: No licence user cap; you host
cells.sso: No hosted SSO fee; custom integration

facts.label: Hosted billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: core has no MAU, stored-user, login or dashboard-seat meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: Core MIT licence has no monthly-user production cap or mandatory subscription.

facts.label: Core paid minimum
facts.value: Not applicable: no paid-core production plan or minimum usage commitment.

facts.label: Plus subscription
facts.value: Advertised early-adopter personal access $149/year; regular price $249/year; annual only.

facts.label: Core overage pricing
facts.value: Not applicable: no licence tier ladder, usage rounding or excess-user fee.

facts.label: Plus project allowance
facts.value: One personal subscription covers unlimited projects; no published per-app-user add-on tariff.

facts.label: Business baseline completeness
facts.value: Core Auth alone does not supply the required customer organizations/invitations plus 1 or 10 SAML connections; complete A/B baseline unsupported by core alone.

facts.label: Hosted organization quota/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-hosted Auth organizations or member-count plan allowance.

facts.label: Connection/directory fees
facts.value: Not applicable to core: no hosted SAML/OIDC/SCIM connection sale or per-directory billing.

facts.label: Core seats/projects/environments
facts.value: Not applicable: code library has no developer dashboard-seat/project/domain quota.

facts.label: Plus personal access
facts.value: Published personal licence: one developer; unlimited projects, no sharing of subscriber access.

facts.label: Plus team availability discrepancy
facts.value: Terms describe a licence for up to 10 people; current sales FAQ says no team licence yet.

facts.label: Email delivery dependency
facts.value: external_service/operator SMTP or API transport via optional @adonisjs/mail; SMTP, SES, Mailgun, SparkPost, Resend, Brevo and Postmark documented.

facts.label: Included sends and channel rates
facts.value: Not applicable: Auth is not a hosted email/SMS/WhatsApp sender and grants no destination-based delivery allowance.

facts.label: Vendor usage cap behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no core hosted quota pause, auto-upgrade, recharge or vendor billing alert.

facts.label: Other core billable meters
facts.value: Not applicable: no core request/token/security-add-on/transaction billing unit.

facts.label: Core account/country eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to MIT code use: no hosted production account or seller-country approval required by Auth.

facts.label: Optional Plus eligibility
facts.value: Personal licence accepts an individual; terms use Indian governing law.

facts.label: Core signup/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable: install public code; no hosted Auth trial, card, company domain or sales approval.

facts.label: Plus access and refund
facts.value: Plus is purchased access; private npm registry requires dashboard-issued token. Published refund window: 30 days.

facts.label: Core scope
facts.value: Embedded TypeScript/Node.js HTTP authentication library: session, opaque access-token and HTTP Basic guards plus user-provider interfaces.

facts.label: Account flows versus authentication
facts.value: Core excludes registration, verification, account activation, password recovery, email updates and authorization.

facts.label: Optional commercial layer
facts.value: AdonisJS Plus supplies Persona account-operation mixins, Permissions and copyable full-stack Feature Packs.

facts.label: Runtime and data operator
facts.value: Developer runs application, user database, token/session storage, secrets, deployment, patching and backups.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in AuthFinder verifies UID/password; configurable identifier fields default to email; username/phone identifiers possible.

facts.label: HTTP Basic
facts.value: built_in Basic guard authenticates credentials on each request; documentation discourages production use.

facts.label: Email-link/code, phone OTP, wallet
facts.value: Native core login methods for these flows not published in current guard/export documentation.

facts.label: Anonymous/guest identities
facts.value: No documented persisted anonymous-auth identity and data-preserving upgrade API established.

facts.label: Social provider plugin
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/ally: Google, GitHub, Discord, Facebook, Spotify, LinkedIn OAuth/OIDC, Twitter OAuth1 and X OAuth2 drivers.

facts.label: Provider setup/extension
facts.value: Register client ID/secret and exact callback URL at provider; missing providers can use a custom Ally driver.

facts.label: Passkey extension
facts.value: plugin Persona passkeys: registration for signed-in users, discoverable passwordless login, required device user verification; not a core guard feature.

facts.label: Passkey domain and session completion
facts.value: RP name, RP ID and allowed origins configured; changing RP ID makes existing credentials unusable; app creates its auth session after verification.

facts.label: Core second factors
facts.value: Core has no documented built-in MFA enrollment/enforcement/recovery-code system.

facts.label: TOTP extension
facts.value: plugin Persona TOTP: encrypted pending/active secrets, QR enrollment, replay protection and app-controlled login challenge.

facts.label: TOTP recovery and disabling
facts.value: Default 10 hashed single-use recovery codes; regenerating replaces old codes; disabling clears TOTP and codes.

facts.label: Core account operations
facts.value: Registration, activation, email verification/recovery/email changes are explicitly outside core Auth.

facts.label: Email extension
facts.value: plugin Persona managed email keeps verified and pending addresses separately, verifies tokens and switches email atomically.

facts.label: Password reset extension
facts.value: plugin Persona issues hashed reset tokens and atomically verifies/updates password; caller clears reset tokens after success.

facts.label: Sensitive changes and deletion
facts.value: Core user.validatePassword checks current password; self-delete route and related-data cleanup are app code.

facts.label: Session representation
facts.value: Session guard stores user ID in the session; reads user from provider on authenticated requests; uses @adonisjs/session.

facts.label: Session lifespan and cookie settings
facts.value: Documented config uses age 2h, HttpOnly true, Secure in production and SameSite lax; all are app-configurable.

facts.label: Login/logout scope
facts.value: Login regenerates session ID; logout removes guard's auth key, clears remember cookie and deletes current remember token when present.

facts.label: Remember me
facts.value: Optional DB-backed hashed remember token, default age 2 years; exchanged/recycled to restore an expired session; encrypted HttpOnly cookie.

facts.label: Token representation and expiry
facts.value: Opaque bearer tokens, SHA-256 hashes in operator DB; default no expiration; configurable per provider/token.

facts.label: Token revocation and abilities
facts.value: Provider can list/delete individual/all user tokens; tokens have names, abilities, expiry and last-used metadata.

facts.label: Other-device session management
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/session >=8 supports explicit tagging and SessionCollection listing/destruction on memory/Redis/database stores.

facts.label: Native business federation
facts.value: No current packaged SAML SP/IdP, generic customer OIDC connection manager or OAuth authorization-server role established for Auth.

facts.label: Extension boundary
facts.value: custom_code custom guards/user providers can connect external identity systems; official example implements a JWT guard.

facts.label: Authorization plugin
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/bouncer supplies code-defined abilities/policies; core Auth only establishes authenticated user.

facts.label: Premium RBAC and tenant pattern
facts.value: plugin @adonisplus/permissions plus custom TeamMember model/pivots supports team-scoped roles and permissions.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: No official built-in/core or Plus SCIM user/group provisioning endpoint, deactivation contract or connector established.

facts.label: Core UI
facts.value: Core Auth is backend/headless; it does not host a universal login page or subscriber dashboard for app users.

facts.label: Starter screens
facts.value: Official hypermedia/React/Vue kits provide working login/signup/logout and an authenticated dashboard; API kits provide signup/login endpoints.

facts.label: Premium ready flows
facts.value: Plus Feature Packs supply editable account/security flows for React, Vue, Edge and API applications; full instructions require subscription.

facts.label: Brand/domain model
facts.value: App owns frontend templates, route URLs, domains and deployment; no vendor auth-domain/branding plan charge.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/i18n loads app-owned JSON/YAML translations and resolves locale/fallbacks; supported UI languages depend on app files.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Starter redesign documents autocomplete, aria-invalid and pending-submit states; no formal auth-screen WCAG/VPAT assessment found.

facts.label: Server runtime
facts.value: Auth 10.1.0 requires Node >=24.0.0; peer framework ^7.0.0 (also named next range); ESM package.

facts.label: Official web integrations
facts.value: Hypermedia Edge/Alpine, Inertia React/Vue, API and API-monorepo starters documented.

facts.label: Mobile/desktop API consumers
facts.value: Opaque bearer-token guard is documented for native mobile, desktop and third-party API clients.

facts.label: Social stateless mode
facts.value: Ally supports stateless flows for API/mobile integrations, with browser-state checks disabled in that mode.

facts.label: Default user data store
facts.value: Built-in user providers use Lucid models; starter kits default to SQLite. Custom providers can use other data sources.

facts.label: Guard-specific prerequisites
facts.value: Session guard needs @adonisjs/session; remember-me/access tokens need their database tables/providers; Basic guard checks user credentials.

facts.label: Persona peers
facts.value: Persona targets core ^7, Lucid ^22; optional module peers include Ally ^6, Session ^8, I18n ^3, Vine ^4 and SimpleWebAuthn server ^14.0.2.

facts.label: Deployment and upgrades
facts.value: Deploy standalone compiled Node app; guide covers production config, migrations, Docker and process operation.

facts.label: Storage/recovery responsibility
facts.value: Back up chosen user DB, relevant token/session data and encryption secrets using operator/provider procedures; no Auth-specific backup/restore appliance or sizing table established.

facts.label: Custom authentication logic
facts.value: Implement GuardContract and user-provider contracts; configure multiple guards; customize lookup/hash column and route middleware.

facts.label: Events and hooks
facts.value: Session guard emits login/authentication attempts, success/failure and logout events; access-token guard emits authentication attempt/success/failure.

facts.label: Additional fields
facts.value: App-defined Lucid model columns/relationships carry profile and business data; Persona social records preserve provider snapshots separately.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: custom_code Lucid create/find/update/delete plus app routes/policies; no core vendor management console.

facts.label: Ban/impersonation
facts.value: No current native suspension flag/workflow or audited support-impersonation facility established in core/Plus docs.

facts.label: Ally/core account matching
facts.value: Ally fetches provider identity; app decides how to find/create local user and log in.

facts.label: Persona identity linking
facts.value: plugin Persona keys by provider + provider_user_id, supports authenticated link/unlink/re-sync, and reports email collision without silent auto-link.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: No native persisted-guest upgrade/data-transfer implementation established; app-owned anonymous data would need explicit custom merging.

facts.label: Password timing and fixation protections
facts.value: AuthFinder performs hashing even for unknown UID and uses common invalid-credentials errors; session login regenerates ID.

facts.label: Password hashing
facts.value: Core hash service offers default Scrypt and optional Argon2/Bcrypt drivers; AuthFinder hashes dirty password values.

facts.label: Optional password/email checks
facts.value: plugin Persona/Vine rules enforce configured password policy, HIBP compromised-password check and bundled disposable-domain rejection.

facts.label: CSRF/security middleware
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/shield, preconfigured in web starter, supplies CSRF token/header and security-header protections.

facts.label: OAuth security maintenance
facts.value: Ally 6.3.1, September 27, 2026 fixes missing-state-cookie callback bypass; current latest release retrieved is 6.3.2.

facts.label: Native CAPTCHA/phone-abuse control
facts.value: No built-in Auth/Persona CAPTCHA integration or managed phone-fraud spending control established.

facts.label: Hosted request quotas
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-operated login/API endpoint or per-plan burst quota.

facts.label: Configurable rate limits
facts.value: plugin @adonisjs/limiter defines app limits using Redis/database/memory stores; login-key/failure penalty patterns documented.

facts.label: Persona token throttling
facts.value: Email-verification/reset token creation supports opt-in throttle; default throttle window 60 seconds; repeated request returns null.

facts.label: Audit integration
facts.value: Auth guard events and app logs can feed custom audit persistence; no core hosted security-event dashboard.

facts.label: Managed audit retention/fee
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor audit-storage allowance, retention days or log-streaming tariff for core.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and hashes
facts.value: custom_code/operator DB export can include user IDs, profile columns and stored password hashes; app owns these rows.

facts.label: Linked factors and portability
facts.value: Persona data includes social identity rows, TOTP/recovery columns and passkey/public-key tables; migrate their schemas and encryption key requirements explicitly.

facts.label: Hash migration building blocks
facts.value: custom_code choose configured Scrypt/Bcrypt/Argon2 or custom hash driver; docs cover selecting legacy driver then rehashing on successful login.

facts.label: Import without double hashing
facts.value: custom_code raw/quiet Lucid inserts can preserve supplied hashes; ordinary User save/create runs AuthFinder hashing hook.

facts.label: User deletion
facts.value: custom_code delete user/model plus application-selected related records; sessions, tokens, factors and app-owned data require explicit cleanup/schema rules.

facts.label: Vendor closure/retention
facts.value: Not applicable to core library: there is no hosted Auth customer account/database to close or vendor backup deletion clock.

facts.label: Runtime data location
facts.value: Chosen by app operator and hosting/database/session/mail/identity providers; code has no fixed vendor account-data region.

facts.label: Hosted processing/assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to core code: no vendor-run app-user processor/DPA/subprocessor list or hosted-auth SOC/SLA scope.

facts.label: Name and project
facts.value: AdonisJS Auth; npm @adonisjs/auth; official repository adonisjs/auth.

facts.label: Maintainer and governance
facts.value: AdonisJS project, led by an individual maintainer with a core team; official packages are under @adonisjs and the AdonisJS GitHub organization.

facts.label: Core availability
facts.value: Active public repository, not archived/disabled; pushed_at 2026-10-16T07:28:06Z.

facts.label: Released framework and package
facts.value: AdonisJS v7 released February 25, 2026; Auth 10.1.0 released April 9, 2026.

facts.label: Core commercial rights
facts.value: MIT: use, modify, distribute, sublicense and sell subject to copyright/permission notice; no production royalty.

facts.label: Social adapter licence
facts.value: @adonisjs/ally is separately MIT-licensed.

facts.label: Plus licence
facts.value: Commercial personal licence for one developer; product/client use permitted; sharing access and redistributing packs as starter kits/templates prohibited.

facts.label: Plus cancellation rights
facts.value: Terms grant perpetual use of included materials; sales FAQ says used components remain, while updates/docs/private Discord end after paid access.

facts.label: Starter-template licensing scope
facts.value: Separate reusable-template licence grant not located; inertia-react manifest is private:true and license:UNLICENSED.

facts.label: Hosted status/SLA
facts.value: Not applicable: library publishes no vendor-operated authentication endpoint uptime or customer SLA.

facts.label: Core release evidence
facts.value: Latest returned stable release Auth v10.1.0, April 9, 2026 at 12:59:26Z; intended-URL storage on unauthorized redirects.

facts.label: Security reporting
facts.value: Project security policy directs private email reports and promises prompt handling of vulnerabilities.

facts.label: Version support horizon
facts.value: No fixed per-Auth-major EOL calendar or long-term-support/security-fix deadline established.

facts.label: Community help
facts.value: Official docs/community routes include Discord and GitHub forum/issues; package bug route points to adonisjs/auth/issues.

facts.label: Paid help commitment
facts.value: Optional $500/month professional support advertises private Slack, priority email and response within 24 hours; custom faster terms discussed separately.

apps.name: Amazon Cognito
apps.line: Hosted user accounts and login for AWS apps.

free.text: 10,000 monthly active users on Lite or Essentials

cells.freeUsers: 10,000 direct or social MAU/month
cells.sso: $0.015 per enterprise MAU after 50 free

mau.math: The first 10,000 users are free, so 1,000 users cost $0 for auth. Each user after that costs $0.0055. AWS infrastructure and other services cost extra.
The first 10,000 users are free, so 10,000 users cost $0 for auth. Each user after that costs $0.0055. AWS infrastructure and other services cost extra.
The first 10,000 users are free. Each user after that costs $0.0055, so 50,000 users come to $220 for auth. AWS infrastructure and other services cost extra.
The first 10,000 users are free. Each user after that costs $0.0055, so 100,000 users come to $495 for auth. AWS infrastructure and other services cost extra.

facts.label: Counted user and window
facts.value: MAU = user with an identity operation in a calendar month, including sign-in, refresh, password/attribute changes or AdminGetUser; repeats do not add users.

facts.label: Pool and edition aggregation
facts.value: Feature plan applies to the whole user pool. A user active under multiple plans in one month is assigned the highest priced active plan.

facts.label: Linked enterprise identity billing
facts.value: Official cost-management and quota pages disagree about a linked SAML/OIDC user's direct-only activity.

facts.label: Standard production allowance
facts.value: Lite/Essentials: 10,000 direct/social MAU/month; Plus: none. Allowance is shared per account or AWS organization.

facts.label: Enterprise federation allowance
facts.value: 50 SAML/OIDC MAU/month/account or organization, including Plus.

facts.label: Legacy allowance cutoff
facts.value: Pricing: qualifying Lite pools before November 22, 2024, 10am Pacific, plus certain existing accounts, retain 50,000 MAU. FAQ instead says before November 21.

facts.label: Minimum commitment
facts.value: No Cognito minimum fee or upfront commitment; taxes separate.

facts.label: Direct/social rate inputs
facts.value: USD/MAU: Lite $0.0055 after free allowance through 100,000 total; next 900,000 $0.0046. Essentials $0.015; Plus $0.020.

facts.label: Regional and higher-volume rate card
facts.value: Complete interactive regional/higher-volume tables could not be extracted.

facts.label: Business scenarios
facts.value: Full business A/B total unknown: app-owned tenancy, membership roles and invitation acceptance still need implementation; SAML-active user count also needs an assumption.

facts.label: Customer organizations and fees
facts.value: Multi-tenancy can be built with pools or app clients; no packaged organization/member/invitation tariff established.

facts.label: SAML/OIDC fees
facts.value: All plans: $0.015 per enterprise MAU above F09 allowance; not per connection.

facts.label: Apps, pools and identity providers
facts.value: Default per pool: 1,000 app clients and 300 IdPs. Per account/Region: 1,000 user pools; quota increases can be requested.

facts.label: Domains and builder access
facts.value: One custom plus one prefix domain per pool; four custom domains per account/Region. Builder administration uses AWS IAM.

facts.label: Default and own email
facts.value: AWS default email delivery is limited to 50 emails/day/account; own SES configuration supports higher sending needs. Email OTP/MFA requires own SES.

facts.label: SES delivery rate
facts.value: SES à la carte outbound email: USD $0.10/1,000 emails, plus $0.12/GB attachment data; other SES plans/features have their own rates.

facts.label: SMS delivery and setup
facts.value: Cognito can use AWS End User Messaging SMS directly, or SNS as an intermediary. First use starts in a sandbox; delivery/origination charges depend on destination and configuration.

facts.label: Alternative message providers
facts.value: Custom email/SMS sender Lambda triggers can call another provider; encrypted codes use KMS and the AWS Encryption SDK.

facts.label: Usage, request and delivery limits
facts.value: MAU overage is metered; request quotas can throttle; message quotas/sandbox rules can stop delivery independently of user allowance.

facts.label: Hard budget stop
facts.value: No Cognito-specific automatic monetary spending cap or billing grace period located.

facts.label: M2M authorization
facts.value: Successful token responses are billed; no app-client fee. Published us-east-1 example: USD $0.00225/response.

facts.label: Other billable resources
facts.value: Purchased API capacity, replication (Essentials/Plus) and dependent Lambda, KMS, WAF, delivery and logs can add charges.

facts.label: Individual account eligibility
facts.value: Self-service AWS account setup is documented for individuals as well as organizations, subject to legal capacity and payment verification.

facts.label: Country eligibility
facts.value: Complete Cognito-specific list of permitted/restricted builder countries not established.

facts.label: Self-service, payment and trial
facts.value: AWS account/IAM setup is the public entry path; valid payment method required. Cognito allowances are distinct from temporary AWS promotional credits.

facts.label: User-pool scope
facts.value: Hosted account directory, registration, login, verification, JWT sessions and federation; editions Lite, Essentials and Plus.

facts.label: Identity-pool scope
facts.value: Federates authenticated or guest identities into temporary AWS credentials; can be used with or without a user pool.

facts.label: Operating responsibilities
facts.value: AWS operates the directory; builder operates application code, IAM permissions, integrations, message configuration and any Lambda extensions.

facts.label: Password and code methods
facts.value: Password/SRP and custom challenge flows: Lite+. First-factor email/SMS OTP: Essentials/Plus.

facts.label: Anonymous use
facts.value: Identity pools can issue temporary guest AWS credentials without an external login.

facts.label: Email login links and wallets
facts.value: Native email magic-link login and native wallet login were not established.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: User-pool integrations: Google, Sign in with Apple, Facebook and Login with Amazon; provider registration/configuration required.

facts.label: Other providers
facts.value: Generic OIDC and SAML integration can broker compatible providers; no named built-in GitHub user-pool integration established.

facts.label: Passkeys: gate and role
facts.value: Opt-in WebAuthn first factor in Essentials/Plus; managed login or custom SDK/API integration. Verified passkeys can meet MFA with MULTI_FACTOR_WITH_USER_VERIFICATION.

facts.label: Passkeys: domain and client limits
facts.value: RP ID must match the web domain; mobile apps need the RP domain's .well-known association. Domain changes can require credential re-enrollment.

facts.label: MFA factors by edition
facts.value: SMS and authenticator-app TOTP: Lite+. Email MFA: Essentials/Plus with SES. Local-user MFA is distinct from an upstream IdP's MFA.

facts.label: Account recovery restrictions
facts.value: Password recovery must use a channel different from the user's preferred email/SMS MFA; administrator reset is a documented fallback.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: Native printable backup/recovery-code flow not located.

facts.label: Verification, reset and address changes
facts.value: Signup confirmation, attribute verification and password recovery use message/API flows; users need a verified recovery destination or administrative help.

facts.label: User deletion and invitations
facts.value: DeleteUser/AdminDeleteUser support removal; AdminCreateUser can send a welcome message and temporary password for first login.

facts.label: Token and browser lifetimes
facts.value: ID/access tokens: configurable 5 minutes–1 day. Refresh token: default 30 days, configurable 1 hour–10 years. Managed-login cookie lasts 1 hour.

facts.label: Rotation and revocation
facts.value: Refresh rotation supports up to 60 seconds grace; RevokeToken ends a refresh-token family, while GlobalSignOut/AdminUserGlobalSignOut end the user's Cognito sessions.

facts.label: SAML/OIDC roles
facts.value: User pools accept upstream SAML 2.0 or OIDC identities, then issue OIDC/JWT tokens to applications.

facts.label: Groups and app roles
facts.value: Users can belong to multiple groups; group claims and IAM role precedence can support application authorization. Groups are not nested.

facts.label: Tenant isolation
facts.value: App-client-per-tenant design shares one directory; all pool users can potentially sign in through any client unless the app enforces restrictions.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: Native Cognito SCIM server, supported SCIM version, group sync and deactivation contract not located.

facts.label: Hosted screens by edition
facts.value: Classic hosted UI: Lite+. Managed login: Essentials/Plus; provides signup, sign-in, password reset and configured MFA/passkey flows.

facts.label: Embedded and profile UI
facts.value: AWS points to Amplify Authenticator components, official client libraries and direct API integration; app-owned account/profile screens remain integration work.

facts.label: Branding by edition
facts.value: Classic UI supports logo/CSS changes; Essentials/Plus managed login adds a visual branding editor.

facts.label: Custom domains
facts.value: Custom login domain requires DNS ownership and an ACM certificate in us-east-1, plus the Cognito/CloudFront configuration.

facts.label: Managed-login translations
facts.value: German, English, Spanish, French, Bahasa Indonesia, Dutch, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Public Cognito managed-login conformance report or explicit WCAG version/level not located.

facts.label: Web and server integration
facts.value: Official Amplify JavaScript/React integration; direct AWS SDK APIs and compatible OIDC libraries are alternative integration paths.

facts.label: Runtime compatibility precision
facts.value: A single current minimum Node/browser/edge version matrix covering all Cognito integration paths was not established.

facts.label: Official mobile clients
facts.value: AWS links Amplify Swift (iOS), Android, React Native and Flutter authentication guides.

facts.label: Required and optional services
facts.value: AWS account, permissions, pool and app client are core prerequisites; no customer database is required merely to store Cognito user-pool identities.

facts.label: Self-hosted operations
facts.value: Not applicable to the Cognito service: no customer-run production Cognito server edition is established.

facts.label: Hooks and custom attributes
facts.value: Lambda triggers cover signup, authentication, migration, messages and token customization; custom attributes can store application-specific profile fields.

facts.label: Execution limits and delivery
facts.value: Most triggers are synchronous with a fixed 5-second response deadline; retryable timeouts can be retried, without a fixed retry count promised.

facts.label: User management
facts.value: Console/admin API support listing, creating, enabling/disabling, deleting, updating attributes, password reset and group management.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Packaged support-agent impersonation/audited act-as-user feature not located.

facts.label: Link and unlink identities
facts.value: AdminLinkProviderForUser links a trusted federated identity to a profile; AdminDisableProviderForUser unlinks it. Up to five federated identities per profile.

facts.label: Guest upgrade scope
facts.value: Identity pools support authenticated and guest identities; app-data merging and conversion into a user-pool account are not established as one automatic workflow.

facts.label: Threat protection by edition
facts.value: Plus offers configurable adaptive risk responses and compromised-credential checks; compromised-password detection does not inspect SRP/custom-auth passwords.

facts.label: WAF and messaging abuse
facts.value: Optional AWS WAF rules can count/block/challenge traffic; CAPTCHA is presented in hosted pages. SMS has sandbox, sender and optional Protect controls.

facts.label: Login and M2M throughput
facts.value: Default UserAuthentication category: 120 requests/second/account/Region; ClientAuthentication M2M: 150/second. Categories pool relevant operations.

facts.label: Administrative and resource quotas
facts.value: Defaults include 30 list requests/second and 15 user-pool read/update requests/second; per-user read/write operations have a separate 10/second limit.

facts.label: CloudTrail audit history
facts.value: Cognito integrates with CloudTrail for documented API/hosted-login events. CloudTrail Event history retains 90 days of regional management events, with no viewing charge.

facts.label: Threat events and exports
facts.value: Plus threat-protection history: two years. User-activity exports go to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose; delivery errors can use CloudWatch without Plus.

facts.label: Profile and group export
facts.value: ListUsers returns paginated user details/attributes; AWS's export guidance copies profiles, groups and memberships into DynamoDB via Step Functions.

facts.label: Credential export
facts.value: The export guidance excludes passwords. Public password-hash, TOTP-secret and passkey-credential export procedures were not located.

facts.label: CSV import and supported hashes
facts.value: Current CSV import supports BCRYPT, SCRYPT, ARGON2ID and PBKDF2_SHA256 password hashes, subject to documented encoding/algorithm restrictions.

facts.label: Lazy migration and reset path
facts.value: Migration Lambda can verify a legacy password during password sign-in or handle forgot-password migration; CSV imports without a usable hash require reset.

facts.label: Delete user/pool and restoration window
facts.value: User removal has API/console paths. Deleted user pools are inactive for 14 days, then AWS begins cleanup; contact Support within that window for accidental-deletion recovery.

facts.label: Close account and contract return
facts.value: AWS account closure has a 90-day reopening period. Agreement provides a general 30-day retrieval period; incorporated DPA provides up to 90 days for scoped Customer Data.

facts.label: Individual deletion and backup purge time
facts.value: Exact final retention/purge timer for a deleted individual user across AWS internal backups, and external-service copies, not established.

facts.label: Selectable user-pool Regions
facts.value: Regional endpoints include us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1 and ap-northeast-1, among others.

facts.label: Replication and transfers

facts.label: Privacy documents
facts.value: Public AWS DPA and subprocessors list; selected Regions/services determine relevant subprocessors. AWS Privacy Notice concerns separate covered data.

facts.label: Assurance scope
facts.value: AWS's Cognito compliance page names SOC, PCI, FedRAMP and HIPAA assessment programs; detailed audit reports are accessed through AWS Artifact.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Amazon Cognito, an Amazon Web Services (AWS) product; user pools and identity pools have distinct roles.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: User pools and identity pools are publicly offered; Cognito Sync stopped accepting new customers starting July 30, 2026; existing Sync customers may continue.

facts.label: Hosted-service use rights
facts.value: Proprietary hosted service governed by the AWS Customer Agreement and Service Terms; usage fees apply.

facts.label: Client-library license

facts.label: Contractual service availability
facts.value: Cognito user-pool SLA: at least 99.9% monthly uptime per AWS Region; eligible credits 10%, 25% or 100% according to the published shortfall bands.

facts.label: Public live status extraction

facts.label: Maintenance evidence
facts.value: Cognito document history records October 1, 2026 WAF response changes and July 13, 2026 password-hash import; Amplify releases list aws-amplify 6.22.2 and auth 6.21.2.

facts.label: Basic support and paid plan
facts.value: Basic Support is included; public documentation/community routes exist. Business Support+ costs the greater of USD $29/month/account or the published tiered percentage of AWS charges.

facts.label: Paid response and plan lifecycle

facts.label: Billing unit and window
facts.value: Auth rate card uses monthly active users (MAU). Billing docs define 30-day periods starting on plan change, with resource counters resetting at the next period.

facts.label: Precise active-user counting rule
facts.value: Exact qualifying activities, anonymous-user exclusions, cross-project deduplication and treatment of token-only/API-only activity were not established.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: $0; 75,000 MAU, 5 GB API bandwidth, 2 GB storage; one Free billing organization and two projects with shared resources. Cannot buy overages.

facts.label: Regional Start minimum
facts.value: From $10/month for eligible organizations; 100,000 MAU, 80 GB bandwidth, 40 GB storage and seven-day daily backups.

facts.label: Pro minimum
facts.value: From $25/month, including one project and 200,000 MAU per project. Additional projects $15 each.

facts.label: Enterprise commitment
facts.value: Custom quote. Universal minimum price, annual commitment and negotiated allowance not published.

facts.label: Paid usage price
facts.value: Pro includes 200,000 MAU/project, then $3 per 1,000 additional users. Free has no purchased overage. Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Start usage and project rules
facts.value: Pricing asset gives Start 100,000 MAU and additional projects $5; rows without a Start override inherit Pro values, including the displayed additional-user rate.

facts.label: Business scenario feasibility
facts.value: Required native SAML connection counts cannot be met by the verified current native offer. Teams/roles/invitations exist, but app-user SAML is still coming soon.

facts.label: Customer team limits
facts.value: Free: 100 teams/project. Start: 1,000 teams/project in current pricing asset. Pro/Enterprise: unlimited teams in comparison.

facts.label: Member and invitation caps
facts.value: No complete plan-specific numerical per-team member or pending-invitation cap found in the team guides/pricing. Team-create reference allows at most 100 role strings, each 81 characters.

facts.label: Business SSO and sync fees
facts.value: Auth SSO row: Free/Pro unavailable; Enterprise coming soon. Native app-user SAML connection or SCIM sync rate card not published.

facts.label: Cloud builder/project limits
facts.value: Free: one builder, two projects and three connected websites/apps per project. Start: three builders and ten websites/apps per project. Pro/Enterprise: unlimited builders/platforms; Pro includes one project plus $15/additional project.

facts.label: Self-hosted builder organizations
facts.value: Current installation guide permits one new builder organization per instance; existing organizations from upgrades are preserved. This restriction does not apply to application teams.

facts.label: Cloud email delivery
facts.value: Built-in SMTP sends generic Auth emails. Custom SMTP/templates documented on Pro and higher; current Start comparison inherits enabled custom SMTP from Pro.

facts.label: Phone delivery
facts.value: Cloud bills per SMS sent by destination; Free phone OTP unavailable in comparison. Examples in current USD rate table: India $0.003, North America (+1) $0.02, UK $0.08 per SMS.

facts.label: Self-hosted delivery
facts.value: Operator configures SMTP and an SMS provider. Documented SMS choices: Twilio, Textmagic, Telesign, MSG91 and Vonage.

facts.label: Limit behavior
facts.value: Free cannot buy excess resources: new user creation/team invites, uploads, functions or Realtime can be disabled according to the exceeded resource; bandwidth exhaustion can deny API access. Pricing FAQ broadly calls this a freeze/read-only Console.

facts.label: Budget controls
facts.value: Pro budget cap covers add-ons, excluding recurring plan cost. Default budget email checkpoint 75%; up to three checkpoints configurable.

facts.label: Other relevant resource prices
facts.value: Pro: extra bandwidth $15/100 GB, storage $2.8/100 GB, executions $2/million, GB-hours $0.06, database reads $0.060/100k and writes $0.10/100k.

facts.label: Compliance/log add-ons
facts.value: Pro BAA is paid and prorated; Enterprise signed BAA is available. API usage logs are off by default; continuous transmission/storage is a separate add-on.

facts.label: Solo-builder and regional eligibility
facts.value: Free is available to individual developers; Start targets indie developers/freelancers and requires a payment card issued in an eligible country. Full Cloud seller-country eligibility list not found.

facts.label: Start country evidence
facts.value: Current pricing asset fallback list: IN, NP, NG, PK, BD, PH, EG, KE, VN, DZ, MA, LK, TN, UZ, UG, GH, KH, ET, TZ. Server-provided eligibleCountries may override it.

facts.label: Self-service and free entry
facts.value: Free, eligible Start and Pro have self-service project/upgrade paths; Enterprise uses a sales path. Free is ongoing rather than a fixed-day trial.

facts.label: Payment and card conditions
facts.value: Paid subscriptions require a valid payment method. Billing docs list credit/debit cards; Indian cards may require authorization up to $150, which is not an immediate charge.

facts.label: Universal card-free signup guarantee
facts.value: No universal no-card or payment-verification exemption for every new Free account found.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Managed backend with Auth on Appwrite Cloud, or self-hosted backend server. Supplies accounts, login, sessions, verification, MFA, teams and user administration.

facts.label: Who operates Cloud
facts.value: Vendor manages Cloud infrastructure; builder manages app UI, access permissions, provider setup, account recovery flows and suitable resource/budget choices.

facts.label: Who operates self-hosting
facts.value: Builder operates Docker/Kubernetes infrastructure, databases, queue/cache, storage, mail/SMS configuration, TLS, patching, backups and restores.

facts.label: Passwords and email passwordless
facts.value: Built-in email/password with Argon2 hashing, magic URL and six-digit email OTP. Email verification is optional for login; permissions can require verified status.

facts.label: Phone and anonymous
facts.value: Native SMS OTP and anonymous guest sessions. Anonymous users lose access if the session expires or browser data is cleared unless upgraded to a permanent account.

facts.label: Custom and wallet methods
facts.value: Custom-token login permits your trusted backend to exchange externally verified identity for an Appwrite session. Native wallet-signature login was not established.

facts.label: Named OAuth providers
facts.value: Released provider configuration includes Amazon, Apple, Appwrite, Auth0, Authentik, Autodesk, Bitbucket, Bitly, Box, Cloudflare, Dailymotion, Discord, Disqus, Dropbox, Etsy, Facebook, Figma, FusionAuth, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Hugging Face, Kakao, Keycloak, Kick, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Notion, OIDC, Okta, PayPal, Podio, Resend, Salesforce, Slack, Spotify, Stripe, TikTok, Tradeshift, Twitch, Webflow, WordPress, X, Yahoo, Yammer, Yandex, Zoho and Zoom.

facts.label: Generic OIDC and mobile flows
facts.value: Native generic OIDC adapter supports discovery/manual endpoints. OAuth guide documents web, Apple, Android, Flutter and React Native redirect handling; provider access/refresh tokens can be managed through sessions.

facts.label: Native passkeys
facts.value: Cloud and self-hosted 2.5+: native WebAuthn primary sign-in with user verification; passkey session satisfies MFA. Registration requires an already signed-in account; username-free sign-in follows.

facts.label: Passkey limits and domains
facts.value: Up to 10 keys/user including pending registrations; registration challenge 5 minutes; recent login/MFA within 10 minutes for adding/deleting; sign-in exchange token 1 minute. RP ID cannot change while any keys exist.

facts.label: Passkey clients
facts.value: Web, Android Credential Manager and Apple associated-domain setup documented. Flutter uses external passkeys package; React Native uses react-native-passkey. Native clients still need a domain serving association files.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: TOTP authenticator, verified email, SMS and single-use recovery codes. An email-OTP first factor cannot reuse email as its second factor; same rule for phone OTP/SMS.

facts.label: Recovery-code wording conflict
facts.value: MFA guide says codes can only be generated once, but released 2.7.1 includes authenticated recovery-code Get and Update/regenerate operations.

facts.label: Verification and reset
facts.value: Email/phone verification, password recovery, email/password/phone updates native. Email recovery link valid 1 hour; newer recovery and email-verification OTPs are six digits, valid 15 minutes.

facts.label: User-facing deletion
facts.value: Users API deletes accounts from trusted backend; Account update-status blocks rather than erases. An app's delete-account screen needs an authorized server flow.

facts.label: Sessions and storage
facts.value: Native persistent server sessions; default limit 10/user, configurable maximum 100, with oldest session removed when exceeded. Web uses secure cookie with localStorage fallback.

facts.label: Duration and JWTs
facts.value: Released 2.7.1 email-session code uses project maximum or one-year constant fallback; optional session duration minimum 60 seconds. User JWT default 900 seconds, maximum 3600 in released code.

facts.label: Revocation and lost devices
facts.value: Account/Users APIs list and delete one/all sessions. Current security guide documents project-wide force sign-out, including JWT-backed requests and open Realtime connections.

facts.label: Business protocols and direction
facts.value: Generic OIDC/OAuth upstream login supported; project OAuth2 server issues downstream OAuth 2.1/OIDC tokens with PKCE, rotating refresh tokens and discovery. Native app-user SAML remains coming soon.

facts.label: Customer teams and roles
facts.value: Native team per tenant, memberships, owner-managed invites/removal and arbitrary role strings; resource permissions can reference team/role membership.

facts.label: Invitation acceptance and privacy
facts.value: Client invite creates pending membership, sends email and activates on acceptance. Server membership creation bypasses acceptance and immediately grants access. Membership name/email/MFA visibility can be restricted.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: No current native app-user SCIM Users/Groups provisioning/deactivation offer, version matrix or fee found.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: API-first: implement login, signup, verification, reset, MFA and account management in your app using SDKs/quick starts. React library is beta; templates do not establish a complete hosted universal login/profile/org portal.

facts.label: Branding
facts.value: App owns login UI. Free built-in emails keep vendor branding and generic templates; Pro comparison removes email branding and allows custom SMTP/templates.

facts.label: Custom API domain
facts.value: Custom API endpoint can use your domain via CNAME, verification and TLS; recommended to keep cookies same-site. Domain-registration/DNS quotas: Free 1, Start 3, Pro 50 per organization.

facts.label: Template languages
facts.value: Native localized email templates selected by client.setLocale or X-Appwrite-Locale. Released locale-code reference includes English, French, German, Spanish, Arabic variants, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Chinese variants and many others.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No customer-Auth WCAG conformance report or VPAT found in current product, SDK and template docs.

facts.label: Web/server SDKs
facts.value: Official Web SDK and beta React library; SSR docs cover Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Gatsby and Remix. Server SDKs include Node.js, Python, PHP, Dart, Ruby, .NET, Go, Swift, Kotlin and Rust.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official Flutter, React Native, Apple and Android clients; Unity SDK beta. OAuth callbacks need platform-specific URL schemes; email links may need deep links.

facts.label: Database and service prerequisites
facts.value: Self-hosted setup supports PostgreSQL (default), MariaDB or MongoDB, plus backend stack services. Cloud runs these dependencies; builder configures external auth/delivery providers as needed.

facts.label: Self-host installation and sizing
facts.value: Docker Compose v2 or Kubernetes/official Helm path. Published minimum: two CPU cores, 4 GB RAM, 2 GB swap, Docker-capable OS.

facts.label: Self-host updates and backups
facts.value: Follow versioned update/migration guide; 2.7.0 to 2.7.1 has no schema changes. Back up databases, file/function/site volumes, configuration and encryption keys; restore to fresh installation.

facts.label: Managed backups
facts.value: Start announcement: daily backups retained seven days. Pro table: daily/seven days. Cloud also keeps internal disaster recovery backups, some PITR seven days or backups every four hours/seven-day retention.

facts.label: Custom fields and logic
facts.value: User/team JSON preferences, maximum 64 kB; labels and role-based permissions. Custom token flow can integrate externally verified identity. Events can invoke Functions, Realtime or webhooks.

facts.label: Webhooks and delivery
facts.value: Free two webhooks/project, Start 50, Pro unlimited. POST notifications have HMAC-SHA1 verification over webhook URL plus raw body; key rotation supported.

facts.label: User management
facts.value: Console and privileged Users API create/list/search/update/block/delete users, manage sessions, identities, factors and passkeys. API-key scopes control server administration.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Trusted operator can impersonate a user by ID/email/phone after operator login and enabling impersonator capability; grants users.read. Target permissions apply and operator identity appears as impersonatorUserId.

facts.label: Linking identities and guest upgrade
facts.value: Signed-in user can run OAuth flow to link identities; emails are unique across users and identities. Guest can attach permanent email/password, phone, magic URL or OAuth identity.

facts.label: Abuse and password protection
facts.value: Native endpoint throttles, CORS, Cloud DDoS protection, password length/character rules, dictionary, personal-data checks, history up to 20 and email-provider policies. Cloud breached-password detection on by default, optional reject/block enforcement.

facts.label: Published rate limits
facts.value: Account creation: 10/hour/IP in current reference. Passkey registration: 10/hour/user and passkey sign-in 10/hour/IP. Email-verification OTP send/confirm share 10/hour/user guide limit.

facts.label: Server and SSR rate behavior
facts.value: SSR unauthenticated requests can share one server IP limit; sessions.write API key can bypass applicable client rate limits. Released email-session code labels 10 attempts using project/URL/email abuse key.

facts.label: Audit and retention
facts.value: Auth user Activity logs include actor, event, location, IP, date and optional reason. Free retention one hour; Pro seven days. Current Start comparison inherits Pro seven days; Enterprise card advertises 90 days while table says custom.

facts.label: Exit and export
facts.value: Cloud-to-self-host migration can select accounts, databases/rows, files, functions and sites; source remains intact. Server user model documents IDs, password hash, algorithm/options; identity APIs expose provider links.

facts.label: Credential portability limits
facts.value: No universal no-reset foreign migration, complete credential-export format, self-service export fee schedule or cross-RP passkey transfer guarantee found.

facts.label: Import hashes and IDs
facts.value: Users API lists Argon2, bcrypt, MD5, PHPass, scrypt, modified scrypt and SHA import methods. Custom IDs up to 36 characters: letters, digits, period, hyphen, underscore; cannot start with special character.

facts.label: Migration sources and exclusions
facts.value: Official Firebase, Supabase and self-hosted import guides; migration usage into Cloud is not charged by Appwrite in Firebase/Supabase guides. Those guides exclude OAuth-user migration and require fresh provider authentication.

facts.label: User deletion
facts.value: Trusted Users API deletes the user and invokes identity/target cleanup. Identity guide warns associated identities and targets can be removed asynchronously by background work.

facts.label: Cloud account retention
facts.value: Privacy policy gives Console account deletion and privacy-request contact, with legal/tax/litigation retention exceptions; public activity may remain accessible after account closure.

facts.label: Cloud regions
facts.value: Available: Frankfurt (FRA), New York (NYC), Sydney (SYD), San Francisco (SFO), Singapore (SGP), Toronto (TOR). Bangalore, Amsterdam and London are coming soon/TBD.

facts.label: Residency boundaries
facts.value: Core-region isolation is documented; privacy policy allows international transfers to service providers and safeguards including adequacy decisions/SCCs. Self-host operator chooses locations.

facts.label: DPA and processing evidence
facts.value: Public privacy and GDPR pages; DPA downloadable/signable inside organization Settings. Complete current contractual DPA/subprocessor attachment not inspected without login.

facts.label: Assurance and BAA
facts.value: Vendor states SOC 2 compliance and shows Type II badge. Pro has compliance add-ons; HIPAA guide documents paid click-through BAA for Pro and signed Enterprise BAA.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Appwrite Auth, the authentication service within Appwrite. Privacy policy identifies Appwrite Code Ltd.; source is appwrite/appwrite.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active Cloud offer and self-hosted release 2.7.1, published 2026-11-04T16:23:46Z. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found.

facts.label: Retirement and cleanup notices
facts.value: Appwrite Assistant retired in self-hosted 2.4 (2026-10-08). Since 2026-06-29, Free projects paused for 90 days are deleted, including resources, after warning emails.

facts.label: Current security incident
facts.value: Appwrite’s November 4 report confirms that an attacker read one customer’s Function code/logs and changed its code for 31 seconds. A separate Frankfurt credential could have read secret environment variables in 1,022 notified Sites/Functions projects; no such reads were evidenced, but incomplete provider audit logs prevent ruling them out. This does not establish exposure of Auth user-password records. Appwrite says the flaw was fixed and internal credentials rotated; self-hosted fix: 2.7.1.

facts.label: Company direction
facts.value: On November 14, 2025, Appwrite said it was moving beyond a backend platform toward a broader cloud development platform.

facts.label: External certificate compromise response
facts.value: Appwrite reported the October 2026 eMudhra intermediate-certificate compromise and said Appwrite Cloud was patched; self-hosted operators need a patched release to reject the compromised chains.

facts.label: Self-hosted license
facts.value: Server 2.7.1 uses BSD-3-Clause terms: commercial redistribution and modification allowed with copyright/conditions/disclaimer retained; no unauthorized endorsement using Appwrite/contributor names.

facts.label: Hosted commercial terms
facts.value: Cloud use is governed by Terms and Conditions; subscriptions renew monthly, with cancellation available via account management/support. Education plan commercial misuse is expressly prohibited.

facts.label: Status and uptime
facts.value: Public status site covers Auth by region. Uptime policy: Free N/A; Pro 99.5% monthly, Scale 99.9%, Enterprise 99.95%. Scale not a current public pricing card; Start SLA not specified.

facts.label: Availability wording conflict
facts.value: SOC page says minimum 99.99%, while explicit plan SLA gives lower percentages and pricing emphasizes Enterprise SLA.

facts.label: Release/security policy
facts.value: 2.7.1 security patch published November 4, 2026; security policy supports latest stable/current minor patch and directs users to release policy. Reports via private advisory/email.

facts.label: Support-policy drift
facts.value: Release-policy table still names self-hosted 1.5.x and ten-year extended security support, while pinned SECURITY.md emphasizes latest stable/current minor.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Free community; Start/Pro email; Enterprise custom support, including Slack advertised. Public support SLA defines Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers but mapping/prices are not established for all current plans.

facts.label: Response targets
facts.value: Gold Critical 1h/High 4h, Platinum Critical 15m/High 1h, 24/7. Silver Medium 2/Low 3/Question 4 business days; critical/high unsupported. Standard hours 9am to 5pm Pacific, weekdays excluding holidays.

free.text: Free MIT library; you host it

cells.freeUsers: No licence user cap; you host
cells.sso: Free MIT OIDC strategy; SAML not included

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: no core MAU, stored-user, login, token or dashboard-seat billing meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: No MIT core licence fee or licence-imposed monthly-user production allowance.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable to the open-source core and Phoenix libraries.

facts.label: Usage price formula
facts.value: Not applicable: no core hosted plan tiers or overage tariff.

facts.label: Customer organizations and invitations
facts.value: No complete built-in customer-organization, member-invitation or per-organization billing package established.

facts.label: Business OIDC software fees
facts.value: OIDC strategy uses the MIT core licence; no per-connection royalty imposed by that licence.

facts.label: Directory-sync software fees
facts.value: Optional ash_scim 0.1.0 uses MIT, with no directory-count tariff in the licence.

facts.label: Builder seats/projects
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted developer dashboard/project/environment/domain plan caps.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: Magic-link, confirmation and reset flows use application-supplied Sender callbacks and delivery/templates.

facts.label: SMS/OTP delivery
facts.value: Preview 5.0.0-rc.16 OTP strategy supplies request/sign-in mechanics but requires a sender.

facts.label: Hosted usage-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no core monthly allowance that automatically bills, upgrades or stops requests.

facts.label: Other core billable limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no core request/token/audit-retention/transaction fee rate card.

facts.label: Hosted-account eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to embedded MIT-licensed software use.

facts.label: Self-service and trial
facts.value: Not applicable: public Mix dependencies and installer instructions, with no hosted core trial/card gate.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Elixir authentication extension for Ash resources: local accounts, login strategies, token handling and configurable account flows.

facts.label: Core versus UI
facts.value: Ash Authentication provides strategies/Plug routing; Ash Authentication Phoenix adds route helpers, controller integration and LiveView components.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer runs the application, user/token/identity resources, migrations, secrets and background cleanup supervision.

facts.label: Local passwords
facts.value: built_in stable Password strategy registers/signs in users using a unique email/username and stored hash.

facts.label: Magic-link login
facts.value: built_in stable MagicLink strategy; 10-minute token default; single_use_token? true.

facts.label: Magic-link interaction default conflict
facts.value: Stable tutorial says interaction is now required by default; 4.15.1 DSL and tagged code default require_interaction? to false.

facts.label: Delivered OTP codes
facts.value: preview: 5.0.0-rc.16 has an OTP strategy with request/sign-in actions, sender, token resource and brute-force strategy.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet flows
facts.value: No first-party durable guest-account/upgrade or cryptocurrency wallet-signature strategy established.

facts.label: Stable social presets
facts.value: Stable API includes first-party Apple, GitHub, Google and Slack strategies, plus Auth0 and generic OAuth2/OIDC.

facts.label: Preview provider presets
facts.value: Preview 5.0.0-rc.16 API adds named Microsoft and Okta strategies.

facts.label: Stable passkeys
facts.value: No first-party WebAuthn/passkey strategy established in the stable 4.15.1 API/source.

facts.label: Preview passkeys and security keys
facts.value: preview WebAuthn strategy supports FIDO2 security keys, platform authenticators and discoverable passkeys; requires optional Wax and a credential resource.

facts.label: Preview domains and existing-user enrollment
facts.value: Configure rp_id and full origin; dynamic tenant values supported. Adding a key to an existing authenticated user requires custom controller/Wax registration code.

facts.label: Stable MFA/recovery scope
facts.value: No stable 4.15.1 local TOTP, recovery-code or first-party passkey-factor implementation established.

facts.label: Preview authenticator-app codes
facts.value: preview TOTP strategy uses nimble_totp and supports setup, confirm_setup, sign-in and verify actions.

facts.label: Preview recovery codes
facts.value: preview RecoveryCode strategy generates hashed, single-use backup codes; regenerating deletes old codes; brute-force protection required.

facts.label: Preview passkeys as second factor
facts.value: Verify-only WebAuthn mode adds webauthn_verified_at to the authentication token on success.

facts.label: Email/change confirmation
facts.value: Stable Confirmation add-on can require confirmation at signup and before changes such as email address take effect.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Stable password strategy can enable resettable; generated request/reset actions use a sender and a reset token, default {3, :days}.

facts.label: Password change versus account UI
facts.value: Phoenix guide explicitly says no prebuilt password-change component; provides a recipe for the generated change_password action and custom UI.

facts.label: JWT lifetime and defaults
facts.value: Stable tokens.enabled? false by default; when enabled, token_lifetime {14, :days}, signing_algorithm HS256.

facts.label: Token storage and revocation model
facts.value: store_all_tokens? and require_token_presence_for_authentication? default false; presence mode requires storage enabled.

facts.label: Browser/bearer session helpers
facts.value: Plug helpers load from session or bearer header, store a user while renewing the session, and revoke current session/header tokens.

facts.label: Global logout
facts.value: Stable LogOutEverywhere add-on invalidates a user's tokens; requires tokens enabled, store_all_tokens? and require_token_presence_for_authentication?.

facts.label: Remember-me tokens
facts.value: Stable RememberMe strategy has a configurable default {30, :days}; requires a compatible primary strategy and explicit cookie/controller handling.

facts.label: Refresh tokens: local versus provider
facts.value: Stable tokens guide says local authentication refresh tokens are not yet included; custom implementation is possible.

facts.label: Business OIDC role
facts.value: Stable Oidc strategy is a client/relying party for an external OIDC server and builds on OAuth2/Assent.

facts.label: SAML and issuer roles
facts.value: No first-party SAML SP/IdP or OAuth/OIDC authorization-server implementation established in the reviewed authentication package.

facts.label: Preview dynamic business connections
facts.value: preview DynamicOidc reads customer IdP configuration from an OidcConnection resource, optionally scoped to the current Ash tenant.

facts.label: Roles and permissions
facts.value: Use underlying Ash policies and application-defined attributes/relationships; Phoenix guide illustrates role-based mount checks.

facts.label: Tenant isolation
facts.value: Underlying Ash supports attribute/context multitenancy; set tenant before auth plugs for multitenant users/tokens.

facts.label: SCIM integration
facts.value: plugin: ash_scim 0.1.0 exposes SCIM 2.0 Users and optional Groups/memberships over app-defined Ash resources.

facts.label: Branding/UI

facts.label: Own domains

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Phoenix UI accepts Gettext-compatible translation functions/backends and ships templates/translations.

facts.value: Phoenix integration 2.17.4 source contains de and sv auth.po catalogs (German and Swedish).

facts.label: Data layer and cleanup prerequisites
facts.value: Define app user and token resources with a persistent Ash data layer; tutorial uses AshPostgres and an auth supervisor.

facts.label: Provider identities and token storage
facts.value: UserIdentity resource stores mappings plus provider access/refresh token attributes and configurable read/upsert/destroy actions.

facts.label: Hash/provider dependencies

facts.label: Notifications and custom fields

facts.label: Account administration
facts.value: Registration/sign-in actions are generated for configured strategies; app can define additional Ash create/read/update/destroy actions.

facts.label: Dashboard, ban and impersonation

facts.label: Multiple provider identities

facts.label: Link/unlink safety and guests

facts.label: Session renewal

facts.label: Phoenix browser protections
facts.value: Phoenix integration setup includes protect_from_forgery and put_secure_browser_headers; sign-out confirmation completes with a CSRF-protected DELETE.

facts.label: Enumeration and abuse controls
facts.value: Stable password/magic-link request docs identify timing leaks with synchronous delivery and recommend asynchronous sender work.

facts.label: Core numeric quotas
facts.value: No universal stable requests-per-window, burst limit or failed-login lockout threshold established.

facts.label: Authentication audit

facts.label: Audit retention/privacy

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and local hashes on exit

facts.label: Provider identity migration
facts.value: UserIdentity has app-owned provider uid/strategy/user_id mappings and access/refresh-token storage.

facts.label: Import existing users
facts.value: Underlying Ash create/bulk-create/upsert actions can implement an app-controlled migration into chosen resources.

facts.label: Hash compatibility/lazy migration
facts.value: HashProvider defines hash, valid? and timing-simulation callbacks; custom providers can validate app-selected stored formats.

facts.label: User deletion
facts.value: Use an application-declared Ash destroy action and its policies/data-layer behavior for durable account deletion.

facts.label: Token cleanup/retention
facts.value: Auth supervisor's TokenResource.Expunger periodically removes expired token/revocation records.

facts.label: Data location
facts.value: Operator selects application/data-layer locations; external email/OAuth/OIDC providers have their own processing locations.
