facts.label: Vendor billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: no MAU, returning-user, stored-user, login or token billing unit for this embedded library.

facts.label: Free production use
facts.value: Core software has no licensing cost, including commercial production use; no numerical-user free-tier reset or production sandbox limit is imposed by MIT.

facts.label: Minimum paid auth commitment
facts.value: Not applicable: no required paid production subscription or annual core-Identity licence commitment.

facts.label: Usage tiers and overage formula
facts.value: Not applicable: no core per-user brackets, invoice rounding, prepaid credits or token/connection overage tariff.

facts.label: Organization fees and limits
facts.value: Core Identity has user/role/claim/login entities, not a customer-workspace membership/invitation product. Tenant tables, scoped roles and invitations require application code or a separate framework.

facts.label: SSO/SCIM connection fees
facts.value: Not applicable as a core vendor tariff: no paid SAML/OIDC/SCIM connection allowance in the MIT account library.

facts.label: Builder seats, apps and domains
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted Identity dashboard seat, project/environment or custom-domain quota.

facts.label: Email delivery prerequisites and cost
facts.value: Application implements/configures IEmailSender for confirmation, changed-address confirmation and password reset. Sender choice and actual volume determine external delivery charges.

facts.label: SMS and other factor delivery
facts.value: Email/phone token-provider code exists; delivery and any SMS UI/integration are developer/external-service work. TOTP uses an authenticator app and requires no SMS send.

facts.label: Hosted over-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no MAU quota that auto-bills, suspends an Identity tenant or forces a paid plan upgrade.

facts.label: Other billable package limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no core API/token/MFA/audit-event/transaction-fee tariff.

facts.label: Hosted account and country eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-operated Identity production tenant, seller account or country-specific auth signup requirement for the embedded MIT libraries.

facts.label: Trial, card and self-service start
facts.value: Not applicable: project templates/NuGet configuration replace a hosted-auth trial, credit-card check or sales step.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: embedded .NET framework libraries: users, passwords, profile data, roles, claims, tokens, account confirmation, sign-in and management UI/API building blocks.

facts.label: UI, API and protocol boundaries
facts.value: Default Identity UI/Razor class library and Blazor Individual Accounts components supply account screens; MapIdentityApi supplies a limited JSON account API with cookies or proprietary bearer tokens.

facts.label: Who runs accounts
facts.value: Developer runs the .NET app, persistent user store, Data Protection keys, email/SMS integration, logs, deployment, patches and backup/restore arrangements, directly or through chosen providers.

facts.label: Password login and registration
facts.value: built_in UserManager/SignInManager with default Razor/Blazor account UI; JSON /register and /login endpoints are available through MapIdentityApi.

facts.label: Passwordless passkey login
facts.value: built_in in .NET 10 Identity: add passkeys to existing users, support app-implemented passwordless creation and passkey sign-in. Blazor template supplies ready-made integration.

facts.label: Magic link, first-factor email/phone code and wallet
facts.value: No corresponding complete first-factor sign-in flow in the reviewed default UI and MapIdentityApi routes; custom_code or separate integration is needed.

facts.label: Anonymous accounts
facts.value: No built-in stored anonymous-user creation and guest-upgrade lifecycle in the reviewed Identity entities/routes; implement an application guest identity and later merge as needed.

facts.label: Microsoft-maintained social integrations
facts.value: Framework authentication integrations support Facebook, Google, Microsoft Account and X/Twitter, configured with provider application credentials and callbacks.

facts.label: Apple, GitHub and other providers
facts.value: Not part of the four named first-party provider integrations documented here. Additional providers require an OIDC/OAuth configuration or community adapter, depending on the provider.

facts.label: Built-in passkey availability
facts.value: ASP.NET Core Identity .NET 10 supports WebAuthn/FIDO2 primary authentication. Only the Blazor Web App template includes ready-made passkey registration, sign-in and management UI.

facts.label: Browser UX, autofill and management
facts.value: Blazor guide documents adding, renaming and deleting passkeys, explicit passkey login, and conditional autofill when supported by the browser/authenticator.

facts.label: Passkey defaults and attestation
facts.value: Released defaults: user verification required, resident key preferred, authenticator timeout 5 minutes, challenge 32 bytes. Attestation statement verification is not performed by default.

facts.label: Passkey domains and HTTPS
facts.value: ServerDomain configures relying-party scope; when absent the host is used. Production passkey operations require HTTPS; host/forwarded-host validation and deliberate subdomain scope are required.

facts.label: Recovery and enrollment limits
facts.value: Default Blazor template requires a backup password or external provider. Passkey-only custom flows need their own recovery policy, such as additional passkeys or appropriate recovery mechanisms.

facts.label: Blazor passkey management limit
facts.value: Released .NET 10.0.14 Blazor Manage/Passkeys template sets MaxPasskeyCount=100 per user and refuses an additional passkey at that count.

facts.label: Authenticator second factor
facts.value: built_in TOTP through default token providers and UserManager/SignInManager; compatible with Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator and other compliant apps. User enrollment enables TwoFactorEnabled.

facts.label: Email/SMS second-factor building blocks
facts.value: built_in EmailTokenProvider and PhoneNumberTokenProvider can validate codes for a confirmed corresponding address/number; application supplies sending and the challenge UI/workflow.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: Default UI generates 10 recovery codes; UserManager replaces the prior set and redeems a code through the configured recovery-code store.

facts.label: Enforcement and passkey distinction
facts.value: App can enforce stronger access with policies/claims and require enrollment. PasskeySignInAsync validates the credential and signs in with bypassTwoFactor:true; passkeys are not a built-in second-factor challenge.

facts.label: Account confirmation
facts.value: built_in email confirmation tokens, resend and confirmation UI/JSON routes. RequireConfirmedEmail/PhoneNumber/Account are configurable; base SignInOptions defaults are false.

facts.label: Confirmation and reset expiry
facts.value: Default DataProtectorTokenProvider lifetime is 1 day, configurable; email-confirmation and password-reset flows use configured token providers.

facts.label: Password reset and password change
facts.value: Default UI and JSON API provide forgotten-password/reset flows; API /manage/info can change password with the old password. UserManager validates reset tokens and the new password.

facts.label: Email changes and phone confirmation
facts.value: Default UI stages a changed email through a confirmation link; UserManager also exposes phone-number token generation/verification/change operations.

facts.label: Self-service deletion
facts.value: Default UI Personal data page can delete the user through UserManager and sign out. It checks the current password when the user has one.

facts.label: Cookie session lifetime
facts.value: CookieAuthenticationOptions default ticket expiry is 14 days, with sliding expiration enabled; a persistent versus browser-session cookie is selected at sign-in.

facts.label: Cookie protection and key prerequisites
facts.value: Cookies use Data Protection; default cookie flags are HttpOnly=true, SameSite=Lax, SecurePolicy=SameAsRequest. App must configure HTTPS/key persistence for its deployment.

facts.label: Logout and sign out everywhere
facts.value: SignInManager.SignOutAsync clears relevant sign-in cookies. Updating a user's security stamp invalidates old cookies when validated; default validation interval is 30 minutes.

facts.label: JSON bearer and refresh tokens
facts.value: Default bearer-token lifetime is 1 hour; refresh-token lifetime is 14 days, configurable. Tokens are proprietary Data Protection tickets rather than JWTs.

facts.label: Bearer revocation limits
facts.value: Refresh endpoint validates refresh expiry and the user's security stamp. The bearer handler accepts valid unexpired protected access tickets without a per-request user-stamp database check; bearer sign-out itself is a no-op.

facts.label: OIDC client versus identity server
facts.value: Adjacent Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect middleware can make the app a confidential interactive OIDC client. Core Identity is local account management, not an OIDC issuer/OAuth authorization server.

facts.label: SAML role
facts.value: No built-in SAML service-provider/identity-provider or broker implementation in the reviewed Identity core/API surface; a separate integration or provider is required.

facts.label: Roles, claims and organizations
facts.value: built_in UserManager/RoleManager role membership and claims plus ASP.NET Core role/policy authorization. Customer workspaces, invitations and tenant-scoped membership/isolation require app models/logic.

facts.label: SCIM account provisioning
facts.value: No SCIM Users/Groups provisioning API or automatic directory deprovisioning in the reviewed Identity source/API route inventory.

facts.label: Ready-made account UI
facts.value: Default Razor Pages Identity UI includes registration/login/logout, password/email management, external logins, TOTP/recovery, and personal-data download/delete. Blazor Individual Accounts supplies generated account components.

facts.label: Headless API scope
facts.value: MapIdentityApi maps registration/login/refresh, email confirmation/resend, password recovery, 2FA management and profile/password info; clients supply UI.

facts.label: Branding and domain control
facts.value: Developer controls app layouts, scaffolded/generated screens, routes, host and domain. No Identity branding-removal tier or hosted custom-domain fee.

facts.label: Localization support
facts.value: ASP.NET Core localization services and custom/scaffolded UI can translate account flows; IdentityErrorDescriber has overridable error methods for application localization.

facts.label: Complete UI language coverage
facts.value: No complete, version-specific list of fully translated Identity default UI languages found in reviewed localization, scaffolding, core and released UI material.

facts.label: Accessibility assessment
facts.value: No module-specific WCAG conformance report/VPAT for the .NET 10 Identity account UI found in reviewed UI/passkey guides and official-site searches.

facts.label: Framework and server runtime
facts.value: ASP.NET Core .NET 10 server libraries for Razor Pages, MVC, Blazor Web Apps and web APIs; .NET runs cross-platform on supported Windows, Linux and macOS systems.

facts.label: Package compatibility and version choice
facts.value: Published Identity EF Core 10.0.14 targets net10.0 with matching Identity Stores and EF Core Relational dependencies. Current maintained runtime lines include 10, 9 and 8 on the checked date.

facts.label: SPA and nonbrowser clients
facts.value: Official Identity API guide covers Angular, React, Vue and Blazor WebAssembly backends. Cookie mode is recommended for browsers; proprietary bearer mode supports clients that cannot use cookies.

facts.label: Native/mobile compatibility evidence
facts.value: No Identity-specific official iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter SDK or native passkey compatibility matrix found in reviewed account/API/passkey docs and released Identity inventory.

facts.label: Database and storage
facts.value: Default examples use EF Core with SQL Server or SQLite; custom IUserStore and related capability interfaces can support other databases/access approaches.

facts.label: Account schema and passkeys
facts.value: Standard Identity model stores users, roles, user-role joins, claims, external logins and user tokens. .NET 10 passkey integration adds passkey storage and requires appropriate schema/version migration.

facts.label: Data Protection and multi-instance operation
facts.value: Persist and protect the app's Data Protection key ring; configure shared keys/application isolation as appropriate across instances and deployments.

facts.label: Messaging and provider credentials
facts.value: Application supplies mail delivery, optional SMS delivery and provider app secrets/callbacks. QR generation is an optional UI addition; TOTP verification is server-side.

facts.label: Hosting and deployment
facts.value: Deploy as an ASP.NET Core app using the supported host/runtime setup; official guide covers publishing, framework-dependent/self-contained deployment and hosting choices.

facts.label: Key lifecycle and updates
facts.value: Data Protection has documented key creation/activation/expiration/revocation behavior; .NET servicing policy requires current patches within the supported release line.

facts.label: Complete backup/restore and sizing
facts.value: No combined Identity-specific tested backup/restore runbook, RPO/RTO, hardware minimum or monthly-user/RPS capacity guarantee found in reviewed hosting, storage, key-management and source material.

facts.label: Custom users and validation logic
facts.value: Application extends user models, custom stores, UserManager/SignInManager, validators, password hashers, claims factories and confirmation/token-provider services through dependency injection.

facts.label: Authentication callbacks and metrics
facts.value: Cookie/provider events, sign-in services and Identity logging/metrics can feed custom logic. .NET 10 Identity emits a Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity meter with sign-in-related instruments.

facts.label: User and role administration
facts.value: UserManager/RoleManager and capable stores support create/find/update/delete users, password/factor/login management and role/claim operations in application code.

facts.label: Blocking users and offboarding
facts.value: Application can use lockout state/SetLockoutEndDateAsync and custom sign-in rules, update security stamps, remove credentials or delete users.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: No dedicated audited admin impersonation workflow in the reviewed Identity UI/API/source inventory. A support impersonation feature requires app code and its own permissions/audit controls.

facts.label: Linking external accounts
facts.value: Default Manage/ExternalLogins can challenge a provider for the signed-in user, validate callback state/user identity and call AddLoginAsync. A provider login can be associated with only one local account.

facts.label: Unlinking safeguards
facts.value: Default UI supports removing an external login and refreshing the current sign-in. It shows its remove button when the user has a password or more than one external login.

facts.label: Guest upgrades
facts.value: No built-in stored anonymous-account upgrade/merge flow. Application code must preserve/reassign guest data when a durable Identity account is created or linked.

facts.label: Password and account-lockout policy
facts.value: Identity defaults: minimum 6 characters, at least one unique character, upper/lower/digit/nonalphanumeric required; lockout defaults 5 failures and 5 minutes, allowed for new users.

facts.label: TOTP and other attack controls
facts.value: TOTP verification and account-lockout integration protect enabled challenge flows. CAPTCHA, breached-password checks and SMS spend/fraud protection are custom/external additions in the reviewed core.

facts.label: CSRF and rate-limiter setup
facts.value: ASP.NET Core has antiforgery support for cookie-backed web forms and opt-in endpoint/global rate-limiting middleware with configurable algorithms/partitioning.

facts.label: Per-account lockout versus request rate
facts.value: Configured account lockout is a failed-credential counter, not a requests-per-minute quota. Default JSON login counts failures; default released Razor/Blazor login does not.

facts.label: App-defined API throttles
facts.value: Framework middleware supports fixed/sliding-window, token-bucket and concurrency policies, global or endpoint configuration, queuing and custom rejection handling.

facts.label: Universal throughput promise
facts.value: No Identity-wide login/admin RPS, concurrency allowance or common endpoint burst ceiling published in reviewed source, API, rate-limit and hosting material.

facts.label: Events, logs and metrics
facts.value: Identity logs sign-in/account/security operations with ILogger event IDs; .NET 10 includes Identity meters for sign-in and user-management observability. App configures collection/destinations.

facts.label: Audit retention and export guarantee
facts.value: No managed Identity audit-retention days, immutable event store, guaranteed export window or webhook retry contract found in reviewed logging/source/API material.

facts.label: Built-in personal-data download
facts.value: Default UI returns PersonalData.json containing properties marked PersonalData (including derived protected personal fields), external login provider keys and the user's authenticator key.

facts.label: Password-hash export
facts.value: Default personal-data download does not include PasswordHash; app owner can export that field from the app-controlled store/database with its actual hash format/parameters.

facts.label: Roles, factors, tokens and passkeys on exit
facts.value: Full migration needs the relevant role/claim/link/token/passkey records and application schema mappings; default personal-data JSON does not export the whole relational account model.

facts.label: Identity-format password migration
facts.value: Built-in PasswordHasher recognizes Identity V2/V3 format markers and can return SuccessRehashNeeded; current V3 uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 128-bit salt, 256-bit subkey and default 100000 iterations.

facts.label: Bulk/lazy import path
facts.value: Application migrates records/IDs/schema and provider links into its store; custom stores/hashers support tailored migrations. No hosted import-row quota or universal import wizard.

facts.label: Deletion behavior
facts.value: Default self-service deletion calls UserManager.DeleteAsync, signs out and logs deletion. Default EF relationships cover linked Identity records; application-owned extra data needs deliberate deletion handling.

facts.label: Data retention and project closure
facts.value: No library-wide deleted-user backup retention, log retention period or deletion-completion SLA found in reviewed GDPR, store, hosting, logging and Microsoft privacy sources.

facts.label: Data location
facts.value: Developer chooses app, account database, key storage, logs and backup locations. No fixed Microsoft Identity hosting region or region-selection tier applies.

facts.label: Privacy and legal scope
facts.value: Microsoft's public privacy statement and Learn website terms cover their stated products/services/website interactions; embedded ASP.NET Core code is separately MIT-licensed.

facts.label: Independent assurance for this module
facts.value: No Identity-module-specific public SOC 2/ISO report or processing/subprocessor contract applicable to a developer-operated Identity deployment established in reviewed sources.

facts.label: Name, project and company
facts.value: ASP.NET Core Identity, maintained in Microsoft's dotnet/aspnetcore project; Microsoft Corporation is the publisher of the current EF Core Identity package.

facts.label: Current lifecycle
facts.value: Maintained, public source and templates; .NET 10 LTS current checked patch 10.0.14. Main repository is not archived or disabled.

facts.label: Version sunsets and old package names
facts.value: Official policy ends .NET 8 and .NET 9 support on November 10, 2026. .NET 10 support ends November 14, 2028. Some old Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity NuGet versions are marked deprecated.

facts.label: Related ASP.NET Core security advisory
facts.value: Microsoft disclosed critical CVE-2026-88092 in Kestrel, an HTTP request-smuggling vulnerability affecting ASP.NET Core runtime packages through .NET 10.0.12; the patched .NET 10 release is 10.0.13.

facts.label: Core licence and commercial use
facts.value: ASP.NET Core v10.0.14 source uses MIT: free commercial use, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale with copyright/permission notice retention; no warranty.

facts.label: Current persistence package licence
facts.value: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore 10.0.14 metadata declares MIT and targets net10.0, with Microsoft.Extensions.Identity.Stores and EF Core Relational 10.0.14 dependencies.

facts.label: Website terms versus software licence
facts.value: Microsoft Learn's Terms of Use cover its website/profile/services; the separately supplied ASP.NET Core source has its own MIT software licence.

facts.label: Service status and uptime promise
facts.value: Not applicable: no Microsoft-operated Identity auth endpoint or tenant SLA for this embedded software.

facts.label: Current release and patch evidence
facts.value: Microsoft support policy and .NET release notes list .NET 10.0.14, October 25, 2026; Identity EF Core 10.0.14 is published, and matching released source was read.

facts.label: Support windows
facts.value: Official policy: .NET 10 LTS active through November 14, 2028; .NET 9 STS and .NET 8 LTS in maintenance through November 10, 2026. Remain current on released patches.

facts.label: Security report and repository policy
facts.value: Main ASP.NET Core repository is active/nonarchived. Security policy directs private reports to MSRC and links the .NET support policy and possible bounty programme.

facts.label: Support channels and paid help
facts.value: Official support page links community questions, GitHub bugs/features and Microsoft professional support/Unified options; personal support may incur a fee.

facts.label: Optional Unified Enterprise pricing
facts.value: Microsoft's US plan page states USD $50,000 minimum contract price, with graduated rates based on historical annual Microsoft product spend.

facts.label: Optional Unified response targets
facts.value: Plan page: critical Sev 1 1 hour for non-Azure products, Sev A 1 hour (24x7), Sev B 2 hours (24x7 on request), Sev C 4 business hours.

facts.label: Private security-report acknowledgement
facts.value: Repository security policy says a vulnerability-report response should arrive within 24 hours, through MSRC private reporting.

facts.label: Community response and Identity-only fee
facts.value: No guaranteed community response target or fixed Identity-only support/incident tariff found in the checked .NET support and Unified plan pages.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: B2C Essentials: $35/month, 500 MAU.

facts.label: Billing commitments and taxes
facts.value: Self-service offers monthly or annual billing; can upgrade or downgrade at any time. Enterprise depends on agreement.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Paid MAU bands; Enterprise quote. Complete dynamic price ladder unknown.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: A/B: unknown; dynamic B2B prices not retrieved.

facts.label: Organization plan allowances
facts.value: Organizations: Free 5; B2C Essentials/Professional 10.

facts.label: Organization system limits
facts.value: Per tenant: 100,000 organizations; per organization: 100,000 members, 10 connections; role assignments per organization member: 50.

facts.label: SSO and account-sync fees
facts.value: Free adds one enterprise connection, SCIM and self-service SSO; B2B Essentials offers enterprise-connection add-ons. Exact add-on fees, setup fee and paid connection allowances unknown.

facts.label: Developer team and project caps
facts.value: Free: 1 tenant/3 contributors; B2C Essentials: 3/unlimited; B2C Professional: 12/unlimited.

facts.label: Environments
facts.value: Non-Enterprise subscriptions can tag only one tenant as Production.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: External SMTP/email provider required for production emails. Built-in sender is testing-only, 10 emails/minute, no custom templates/from address.

facts.label: SMS delivery and costs
facts.value: SMS/voice MFA and SMS passwordless documented; destination rates and bundled paid sends not established.

facts.label: What happens at usage limits
facts.value: Official billing article says automatic next-tier upgrade after three consecutive months above plan limits. Spending cap and exact Free transition behavior unknown.

facts.label: Request-limit enforcement
facts.value: API request limits are separately enforced; cannot rely on billing grace to prevent request throttling.

facts.label: Other billable limits
facts.value: M2M token and security add-ons exist; full rate card unknown.

facts.label: M2M definition
facts.value: Count of Client Credentials access tokens issued per calendar month, excluding tokens for Auth0 Management API.

facts.label: Market and account eligibility
facts.value: unknown: complete restricted-country list and explicit individual production-account eligibility.

facts.label: Self-service and trial rules
facts.value: Self-service signup; no signup card.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: 22 days; automatically moves to Free after trial. Paid trial features have exceptions.

facts.label: Contract country restrictions
facts.value: The linked MSA names Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk regions of Ukraine as restricted locations; also restricted persons/end uses.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Hosted customer identity service: accounts, login, verification, authorization, and business login federation.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Auth0 operates Public Cloud and dedicated managed Private Cloud. Private Cloud options include AWS and Azure.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: yes; built_in database login with identifier and password.

facts.label: Email and phone codes
facts.value: Email one-time code: yes. SMS one-time code: yes. Built-in authentication; external delivery dependency.

facts.label: Email link
facts.value: yes for Classic Login; unavailable in Universal Login. Request and link response must use the same browser.

facts.label: Anonymous sessions
facts.value: yes; Identity Conversion Suite offers anonymous sessions and API access tokens. Minimum plan and fee unknown.

facts.label: Social: Google
facts.value: yes; built_in connection; configure provider credentials.

facts.label: Social: GitHub
facts.value: yes; built_in OAuth connection; register GitHub OAuth application and configure its credentials.

facts.label: Social: Apple
facts.value: yes; native iOS Sign in with Apple; requires paid Apple Developer account.

facts.label: Social: other providers
facts.value: Marketplace catalogue and generic custom social connections documented. Complete provider list and personal Microsoft app-user setup not verified.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: yes; database connections; web Universal Login, embedded native and Android/iOS APIs. Limit: 20 passkeys/user. Conditional autofill or button; passwords can remain usable.

facts.label: Passkey plan
facts.value: Included on Free.

facts.label: MFA factors and recovery
facts.value: Authenticator OTP, SMS, voice, email, Guardian push, WebAuthn/security keys and recovery codes documented. Availability depends on plan.

facts.label: MFA plan gates
facts.value: Pro MFA = OTP apps/Cisco Duo; Enterprise MFA = push, WebAuthn and phone/email codes.

facts.label: MFA source disagreement
facts.value: Billing article classifies SMS/voice as Pro MFA; quota docs classify SMS/phone as Enterprise MFA.

facts.label: Email verification
facts.value: yes; links, OTP and Management API methods. Default signup verification email; OTP requires Universal Login, Flexible Identifiers and Identifier-First login. OTP lifetime 900 seconds.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: yes; support documents one-use Management API password-change tickets.

facts.label: Profile changes and self-deletion
facts.value: Profile root attributes can be updated; method depends on connection/upstream provider. Complete user-facing change-email, phone verification and self-delete flows not established.

facts.label: Sessions and revocation
facts.value: Cookie sessions; application/Auth0/upstream IdP layers. Management API lists active user sessions and revokes one or all.

facts.label: Session expiry and refresh
facts.value: Idle and maximum lifetime configurable for persistent/non-persistent sessions. Exact plan-specific maximums and refresh expiry unknown.

facts.label: Business login standards
facts.value: SAML identity-provider and service-provider configurations; OAuth 2.0/OIDC login flows; Auth0 can broker upstream connections.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: Customer organizations can have their own login connections/branding; a user may belong to multiple organizations. Roles can control access; custom customer-admin dashboard can use these roles.

facts.label: Organization invitations
facts.value: yes; email invitation lets an existing or new user log in/sign up and join, optionally with predefined roles.

facts.label: SCIM sync
facts.value: Inbound SCIM 2.0: users and groups create/read/update/delete/search. Deactivation blocks user, ends Auth0 sessions and revokes refresh tokens; configured backchannel logout can notify apps.

facts.label: Login screens
facts.value: Auth0-hosted Universal Login; Classic Login also hosted. Embedded login alternative documented. Universal Login is actively developed; Classic no longer receives updates.

facts.label: Account screens
facts.value: unknown: complete ready-made account settings/profile/deletion screens and their plan gates.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Custom domain supported, including free verified card; card not charged. Theme/templates/text customizable. Domain change invalidates existing sessions; passkeys tied to rpId domain.

facts.label: Custom-domain documentation conflict
facts.value: Tenant Settings recommends custom domains only on paid plans; current Custom Domains guide permits free domain with card verification.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: Localized Universal Login; documented examples: English, Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, Dutch and Danish. Locale codes and custom translations documented.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Vendor says Universal Login uses WCAG 2.2 AA and EN 301 549; screen-reader labels/errors and default color contrast described.

facts.label: Web frameworks and runtimes
facts.value: Official React browser SDK quickstart; React 18.x+, setup Node.js 20 LTS+, npm 10+/yarn 1.22+/pnpm 8+. Navigation also names Angular, JavaScript, Vue, Flutter Web and Svelte.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official iOS/macOS Auth0.swift quickstart; index also names Android, React Native, Expo, Flutter, Flutter Windows, Kotlin Multiplatform, .NET mobile, MAUI, Ionic/Capacitor, UWP and WPF/WinForms.

facts.label: Database and service prerequisites
facts.value: Auth0 tenant stores application/connection/user assets. Can use Auth0-managed user store or an upstream identity provider.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: not_applicable: researched managed auth service; Private Cloud is also managed.

facts.label: Custom logic and events
facts.value: Actions: custom JavaScript on Node.js with login/registration/password triggers. Action size <=100 kB excluding imported npm modules; trigger execution <=20 seconds; execution logs 10 days.

facts.label: Webhooks and event streams
facts.value: User/group changes can stream to custom webhook, AWS EventBridge or custom Action.

facts.label: User administration and API
facts.value: Dashboard and Management API create, retrieve, modify and delete users.

facts.label: Block, search and impersonation detail
facts.value: SCIM deactivation blocks users; user endpoints searchable. General dashboard ban workflow, impersonation controls and their plan gate unknown.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking
facts.value: yes; explicit linking merges identities under primary user_id; authenticate both accounts first. Secondary metadata discarded unless developer merges it; unlink endpoint documented.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: Anonymous activity can transfer to authenticated user via same-domain cookie or IP-bound transfer ticket; custom app flow required.

facts.label: Abuse protection
facts.value: Configurable bot detection/CAPTCHA, suspicious-IP throttling, brute-force protection and breached-password detection.

facts.label: SMS abuse control
facts.value: SMS Fraud Protection uses increasing wait times between code requests.

facts.label: API and login rate limits
facts.value: Free: Authentication API burst 300, sustained 300/minute; Management API burst 2, sustained 2/second. Passwordless start: 50/hour/IP; token endpoint: 30/second, subject to API-wide cap.

facts.label: Audit retention
facts.value: B2C/B2B Essentials 5 days; B2C/B2B Professional 10 days; Enterprise 30 days. External log streaming available; indexing can be delayed.

facts.label: Free audit retention
facts.value: Free: 1 day.

facts.label: Password-reset scope
facts.value: Database users: hosted reset email link or Dashboard/Management API password change. Social/enterprise users reset at upstream provider. Reset expires the user session.

facts.label: Session administration plan and caveats
facts.value: Session listing and individual/all-session deletion API endpoints require Enterprise. Deletion asynchronous/eventually consistent. Refresh tokens can survive logout/session deletion and need separate handling.

facts.label: Organization-specific roles
facts.value: 350 roles per organization. Tenant admins create/edit/delete roles; organization editors assign/remove roles for members. Tenant roles and organization roles can both contribute token permissions.

facts.label: Localized UI codes and limits
facts.value: sq, am, ar, ar-EG, ar-SA, hy, az, eu-ES, bn, bs, bg, ca-ES, zh-HK, zh-CN, zh-TW, hr, cs, da, nl, en, en-CA, et, fa, fi, fr-FR, fr-CA, gl-ES, ka, de, el, gu, he, hi, hu, is, id, it, ja, kn, ko, lv, lt, mk, ms, ml, mr, mn, cnr, my, no, nb, nn, pl, pt-BR, pt-PT, pa, ro, ru, sr, sk, sl, so, es, es-AR, es-419, es-MX, sw, sv, tl, zgh, ta, te, th, tr, uk, ur, vi, cy.

facts.label: Profile export
facts.value: NDJSON or CSV bulk user export via Dashboard/Management API; not available on Free. Select fields; connection_id optional for all connections.

facts.label: Password hashes and MFA export
facts.value: Support request; PGP encryption and eligibility review. Not every request qualifies; no ETA. Requires written approvals and signed executive acknowledgment. Fee and plan eligibility unknown.

facts.label: Import and migration in
facts.value: Bulk JSON import via Dashboard/API into Auth0 database, or import-mode custom database. File limit 500KB; remove auth0 prefix from exported IDs to preserve IDs when reimporting.

facts.label: Deletion and retention
facts.value: User deletion via API/Dashboard; active customer data retained. Free customers with all tenants inactive for 150 days scheduled for tenant/data deletion.

facts.label: Account closure
facts.value: Downgrade to Free before Dashboard tenant deletion; remove custom domains first. Account/billing-data removal requires assistance. Backup purge schedule and legal retention exceptions unknown.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Public Cloud selectable region: Australia, Canada, Europe, Japan, United Kingdom, USA. Specific sub-locality assigned automatically.

facts.label: Residency scope
facts.value: unknown: backup/log/support-data locations and full regional price/plan restrictions.

facts.label: Privacy evidence
facts.value: Public legal hub links Data Processing Addendum, SCCs and Sub-processor Information.

facts.label: Assurance evidence
facts.value: Vendor claims annual SOC 2 Type 2 covering all five Trust Services Criteria and ISO 27001/27017/27018 audits. Reports/certificates requested through Support; not independently reviewed.

facts.label: Name, aliases, owner, URLs
facts.value: Auth0; owner: Okta. Site https://auth0.com/; docs https://auth0.com/docs/.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Available; self-service entry advertised. Signup not tested.

facts.label: Mobile Driver’s License feature retirement
facts.value: Auth0 ended the free trial for the Mobile Driver’s License Verification Service Early Access after May 11, 2026 and removed access for enrolled tenants; the changelog says these capabilities are not planned as part of Auth0.

facts.label: Recent service incidents
facts.value: Auth0 status history reports a resolved third-party full disruption in US-1 on October 23, 2026 (17:39–17:45 UTC) and partial elevated errors in multiple cloud environments on October 14 (05:01–05:32 UTC).

facts.label: License and commercial-use rules
facts.value: Hosted service governed by Okta subscription terms and the Auth0 self-service product schedule; not a self-host server license.

facts.label: License: sample SDK
facts.value: Auth0 React SDK: MIT; use, change, distribute and sell permitted subject to the notice condition.

facts.label: Service status and availability promise
facts.value: Status: https://status.auth0.com/. Enterprise Public/Private Cloud core-service monthly availability promise: >=99.99%; credits requested within 5 business days.

facts.label: Release and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Sample React SDK release page marks v2.30.0 latest; displayed release time: 30 Oct 11:45.

facts.label: Support route
facts.value: Support portal; Standard targets: urgent 1 business hour, high 4 business hours, normal 1 business day, low 2 business days. Standard hours 06:00 to 18:00 customer local time, Monday to Friday.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: no Authboss MAU, returning-user, stored-user, login-request or message billing meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: No core MIT licence charge or licence-imposed monthly application-user cap.

facts.label: Paid production commitment
facts.value: Not applicable: no required paid Authboss plan, minimum subscription or annual service contract for this library edition.

facts.label: Software usage formula
facts.value: Core software licence subtotal = 0 at every researched user count; bundled module activation has no per-module licence meter.

facts.label: Business cost basis
facts.value: Complete fixed organization/invitation/role plus SAML baselines are unsupported as packaged Authboss capabilities.

facts.label: Organization plan allowances/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: library offers no vendor customer-organization subscription plan or paid team/member allowance.

facts.label: Managed SSO/SCIM connection prices
facts.value: Not applicable: no managed business-connection product or SAML/SCIM tariff in this embedded account toolkit.

facts.label: Builder seats/projects/environments
facts.value: Not applicable: no Authboss-hosted dashboard, developer-seat quota or project/environment allowance.

facts.label: Email sender dependency
facts.value: external_service/custom_code: app provides Mailer; bundled SMTPMailer accepts an SMTP server/authentication configuration.

facts.label: Default mailer behavior
facts.value: defaults.SetCore installs a LogMailer writing to the supplied output, not a production email-delivery subscription.

facts.label: SMS sender dependency
facts.value: sms2fa requires an SMSSender implementation; Setup returns an error if SMS.Sender is not set.

facts.label: Hosted over-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor quota-triggered upgrade, spending cap or billing grace period.

facts.label: Other vendor charges
facts.value: Not applicable to core software billing: no Authboss token/request/security-addon or payment-transaction tariff.

facts.label: Hosted account eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable: using the MIT library does not require a vendor production account, seller-country approval or company-domain signup.

facts.label: Hosted trial/self-service
facts.value: Not applicable: public Go module/configuration rather than hosted trial days, sales approval or card gate.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Go account/authentication toolkit with selectable modules for password auth, registration, confirmation, recovery, expiry, lockout, remember-me, OAuth2 and OTP/2FA.

facts.label: Integration boundary
facts.value: App supplies user/server storage, client session/cookie state and HTTP/rendering pieces; default implementations exist for several HTTP components.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer runs the Go app and storage/session implementations and supplies renderers and external delivery services.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in module auth validates submitted PID/password against the stored hash with Config.Core.Hasher and sets the login session on success.

facts.label: One-time password login
facts.value: built_in otp module creates/clears saved one-time passwords and consumes them when used instead of the regular password.

facts.label: Email magic-link/code login
facts.value: No dedicated email magic-link or email-code sign-in module is bundled in v3.5.3; confirmation/recovery links and setup-email authorization have different purposes.

facts.label: Phone-first, anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No bundled phone-first sign-in, anonymous-account lifecycle or wallet-signature module in the v3.5.3 module inventory.

facts.label: Google social login
facts.value: built_in OAuth2 module includes GoogleUserDetails resolver, returning uid/email from Google's user-info endpoint.

facts.label: Facebook social login
facts.value: built_in OAuth2 module includes FacebookUserDetails resolver returning uid/email/name.

facts.label: GitHub and Microsoft integration route
facts.value: custom_code: generic OAuth2Provider accepts app configuration and FindUserDetails; no named GitHub/Microsoft resolver is bundled alongside Google/Facebook.

facts.label: Apple-specific integration
facts.value: A complete Apple-specific Authboss integration/configuration was not established in checked official docs and resolver code.

facts.label: External OAuth1 plugin
facts.value: plugin: authboss-oauth1 provides separate OAuth1 routes/provider configuration and user-store interfaces.

facts.label: Passkey support
facts.value: No built-in WebAuthn registration/assertion, passkey autofill or passkey-recovery module in the v3.5.3 released inventory.

facts.label: TOTP second factor
facts.value: built_in totp2fa supports setup/QR/confirmation, login validation and factor removal; explicitly construct TOTP and call Setup.

facts.label: SMS second factor
facts.value: built_in sms2fa supports phone enrollment/confirmation, login validation and removal using app-supplied SMSSender.

facts.label: Factor recovery codes
facts.value: built_in twofactor supplies regeneration and single-use recovery codes; stored codes are bcrypt-hashed.

facts.label: Setup email authorization
facts.value: Config.Modules.TwoFactorEmailAuthRequired optionally requires email authorization on the current device before enrolling a factor.

facts.label: User registration
facts.value: built_in register creates an account using CreatingServerStorer; optional arbitrary fields are allowed through explicit interfaces/preservation whitelist.

facts.label: Email confirmation
facts.value: built_in confirm stores selector/verifier, emails a token, marks confirmed on valid redemption and can prevent unconfirmed login/resources.

facts.label: Password recovery
facts.value: built_in recover emails a reset link, verifies stored token credentials/expiry, changes hash and clears reset credentials.

facts.label: Change address and self-delete flows
facts.value: No dedicated change-email/phone account-profile or user-deletion module in the released module set; application code must own those account operations.

facts.label: Session backend and cookie security
facts.value: custom_code/external_library: SessionState and CookieState are app-supplied ClientStateReadWriter implementations.

facts.label: Idle expiration
facts.value: built_in expire middleware tracks last activity and clears the current session after Config.Modules.ExpireAfter; default is 1 hour.

facts.label: Remember-me persistence
facts.value: built_in remember stores hashed remember tokens, rotates them on use and restores a half-authenticated session.

facts.label: Logout
facts.value: built_in logout clears all current session state except configured whitelist keys and removes known Authboss cookies; default route method DELETE.

facts.label: Password changes and all-device logout
facts.value: UpdatePassword hashes/saves the password and invalidates remember tokens when supported; core explicitly says deleting every logged-in session needs mechanisms it does not provide.

facts.label: OAuth2 role versus business SSO
facts.value: Bundled oauth2 is a client login flow with app-configured providers/resolvers; no SAML or OIDC identity-provider/server module is in the released inventory.

facts.label: Organizations/invitations/customer roles
facts.value: Not applicable to offered product modules: no customer-organization workspace/invitation/role product is supplied.

facts.label: SCIM account synchronization
facts.value: Not applicable to this offering: no business directory/provisioning connector module or hosted SCIM service.

facts.label: Core UI rendering
facts.value: Core exposes Renderer for app HTML templates; bundled defaults.JSONRenderer supports JSON/API responses.

facts.label: Optional ready-made views
facts.value: plugin: authboss-renderer includes login, registration, recover, TOTP/SMS setup/validation and 2FA recovery templates, plus email templates.

facts.label: Template branding/customization
facts.value: Optional renderer can override layout/page templates by supplying an override directory; developer may instead implement its own Renderer.

facts.label: Domains and generated links
facts.value: Config.Paths.RootURL/Mount and optional Mail.RootURL control application routes and email link roots.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Core.Localizer interface translates keys using context; default English text is used when no localizer/translation is provided.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public accessibility conformance report or tested language/accessibility matrix established for the optional default views.

facts.label: Runtime and dependencies
facts.value: v3.5.3 declares Go 1.24.0 and toolchain go1.24.5; imports module github.com/aarondl/authboss/v3.

facts.label: Framework integration
facts.value: Go net/http integration with replaceable Router, ErrorHandler, Responder, Redirector, BodyReader and renderers; quick-start shows chi mounting.

facts.label: Mobile/frontend API route
facts.value: API clients can use the JSON renderer/body reader; MailRouteMethod can use POST so a frontend passes an email token to the API.

facts.label: Native client SDK support
facts.value: No native iOS, Android, React Native or Flutter SDK package is shipped in the v3.5.3 server-side Go module inventory.

facts.label: User/database implementation
facts.value: ServerStorer Load/Save and module-specific extensions plus matching User interfaces are app implemented; core does not select a database engine/schema.

facts.label: Password hasher
facts.value: Hasher interface has GenerateHash and CompareHashAndPassword; bundled bcrypt implementation is used by default when no custom hasher is supplied.

facts.label: Mail/UI/session prerequisites
facts.value: Email modules need Mailer and email rendering; all login flows need configured state/body/router support; TOTP/SMS require secure sessions.

facts.label: Operating responsibilities
facts.value: Embed Authboss into the developer's Go server; database/session services, backup/restore and app recovery follow the developer's implementations.

facts.label: Capacity guidance
facts.value: No published Authboss-specific production user capacity, hardware sizing or verified throughput limit established.

facts.label: Sample deployment scope
facts.value: Official authboss-sample explicitly says it is an API demonstration, not a seed project for production copying.

facts.label: Events/hooks
facts.value: Events.Before/After register synchronous handlers for auth, OAuth2, registration, recovery, logout and factor changes; handlers can intercept the request.

facts.label: Custom fields and authorization
facts.value: ArbitraryUser/ArbitraryValuer support app-selected registration fields; middleware can require full authentication and/or 2FA.

facts.label: Account creation and lock administration
facts.value: CreatingServerStorer supports New/Create; lock module exposes Lock(ctx,key) and Unlock(ctx,key).

facts.label: Search/delete/impersonation dashboard
facts.value: Core supplies storage contracts rather than a hosted user-management dashboard; search, delete and impersonation are not methods of the core ServerStorer contract.

facts.label: OAuth identity mapping
facts.value: OAuth2ServerStorer.NewFromOAuth2 receives provider/details and is responsible for finding/updating an existing user; SaveOAuth2 persists insert/update.

facts.label: Unlink/guest upgrade flows
facts.value: No dedicated provider-unlink or anonymous-to-registered merge module in v3.5.3; these app account transitions require custom code.

facts.label: CSRF and general request throttling
facts.value: custom_code/external_library: project explicitly requires the app to add CSRF middleware and general endpoint request throttling.

facts.label: Account lockout
facts.value: built_in lock uses LockableUser state; defaults LockAfter=3, LockWindow=5 minutes, LockDuration=12 hours; configure middleware on protected routes.

facts.label: Breached passwords and bot checks
facts.value: No built-in breached-password service or CAPTCHA/bot-check integration in the released modules; app validation/middleware must supply such controls.

facts.label: SMS resend cooldown
facts.value: sms2fa code limits sends with a timestamp in the current session and a 10-second cooldown.

facts.label: Hosted API request allowance
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor endpoint quota, shared MAU burst allowance or paid throughput tier.

facts.label: Events and logging integration
facts.value: Core provides auth/account event hooks and Logger/ContextLogger/RequestLogger interfaces for application logging.

facts.label: Managed audit retention/export plan
facts.value: Not applicable: no Authboss-operated audit storage, retention subscription or managed log-export service.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and hashes on exit
facts.value: Application owns persisted User data through its storage implementation, including PID and password string when AuthableUser is used.

facts.label: OAuth identity/token data
facts.value: OAuth2User exposes provider, uid, access/refresh token and expiry through the developer's user implementation.

facts.label: Vendor export service/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-owned user store, paid export route or support-mediated account dump in the library deployment.

facts.label: Custom hash/import integration
facts.value: Existing users can be exposed through the app's ServerStorer/User implementations; custom Hasher can supply hash verification/generation.

facts.label: Bulk/lazy migration guide
facts.value: No published complete hash-import matrix, bulk migration procedure or lazy-rehash workflow established in the checked project docs/code.

facts.label: Delete account records
facts.value: User/account deletion is app storage/admin code; base ServerStorer exposes Load/Save and no universal Delete method.

facts.label: Vendor retention/closure
facts.value: Not applicable: no Authboss-hosted tenant/account, storage backups or vendor-defined app-user retention schedule.

facts.label: Hosting regions/residency plan
facts.value: Not applicable: developer chooses the Go app/database/session deployment; Authboss does not offer vendor-hosted regions.

facts.label: Hosted processing/privacy contracts
facts.value: Not applicable: MIT code licence, not a vendor-hosted user-processing service, DPA or subprocessor plan.

facts.label: Independent security assurance
facts.value: No publicly linked Authboss-specific independent code-audit or assurance report established.

facts.value: Authboss; Go module github.com/aarondl/authboss/v3; public project maintained by an individual maintainer and contributors.

facts.label: Core billing unit
facts.value: No upstream usage invoice for MIT core: no mandatory MAU, returning-user, stored-user, login, token or SAML-connection software meter.

facts.label: Enterprise count definition
facts.value: Licensed capacity counts active internal and external accounts separately, not monthly login activity. Disabled accounts, the anonymous user and service accounts including agent accounts are excluded; validation/counting is local.

facts.label: Internal versus external user
facts.value: Internal users can use Authentik’s application dashboard/user settings. External users cannot use those screens; they access an application and may use direct account-management flows.

facts.label: Ongoing free production use
facts.value: Open Source is free for self-hosted production under MIT; core SSO, MFA, local users/groups/roles, invitations and configuration/policy features have no paid-production time limit.

facts.label: Enterprise rates and annual commitment
facts.value: Enterprise: $5 per workforce/internal user per month and $0.02 per customer/external user per month, billed annually; agent/service accounts included. Current page shows '$' without a visible ISO currency code.

facts.label: Minimum and trial entry
facts.value: February 4, 2025 announcement removed minimum user counts for paid plans; current pricing publishes the same per-user entry model without a separate base fee. Enterprise Plus starts at $20,000 annually.

facts.label: Enterprise software arithmetic and volume pricing
facts.value: Published unit-rate component = internal capacity × $5/month + external capacity × $0.02/month, billed for a year. Enterprise Plus offers volume discounts/custom agreements; numeric discount brackets are not published.

facts.label: Business scenario fit boundary
facts.value: Core provides groups, role/object permissions, SAML sources/providers and configurable enrollment invitations. These can be configured into an application-owned customer model; a turnkey B2B organization/membership-invitation service is not established.

facts.label: Customer grouping and fees
facts.value: Free core supports users in groups, group hierarchy, custom attributes and role inheritance, with no published per-group/member/invitation software fee. Universal technical group/member/invitation maximums were not found in the checked guides.

facts.label: Schema-isolated tenancy edition
facts.value: Enterprise multi-tenancy, available since 2024.2, is alpha; one PostgreSQL schema and Install ID per tenant. Each additional tenant needs its own license(s); default tenant must have a valid license to create others.

facts.label: Invitation behavior
facts.value: Core enrollment invitations support preset attributes, flow restriction, expiry and single-use deletion; New Invitation form defaults to 48 hours. Link can be copied or sent by configured SMTP/background worker.

facts.label: SSO and basic SCIM fees
facts.value: Core SAML/OIDC sources and providers plus native inbound SCIM and static-token outbound SCIM are included without a separate per-connection license fee.

facts.label: Paid provisioning variant
facts.value: Outbound SCIM using OAuth-acquired short-lived tokens requires Enterprise. Static-token mode remains the documented default; OAuth source embedding inside another flow also requires Enterprise Source stage.

facts.label: Builder seats, apps, domains and environments
facts.value: No hosted dashboard-seat/project allowance applies to core. Server users, application/provider objects, brands/domains and deployment environments are operated by you.

facts.label: Email sender and costs
facts.value: Your SMTP service sends verification/recovery/magic-link/invitation/MFA emails. Global and per-stage SMTP settings, TLS and custom templates are supported; no included send quota or Authentik message tariff is published.

facts.label: SMS, Duo and CAPTCHA extras
facts.value: SMS MFA uses your Twilio account or generic HTTP provider. Duo and CAPTCHA use their respective external services; SMTP/SMS/provider prices are outside the software subscription.

facts.label: Enterprise expiry and capacity enforcement
facts.value: Current licensing guide warns admins near expiry; capacity warnings occur after two weeks since last valid usage, all-interface warnings after four weeks, and read-only mode after six weeks. Expiry over six weeks also triggers read-only.

facts.label: Free core resource limits
facts.value: No free-to-paid user overage, automatic upgrade or vendor spend cap applies to MIT core.

facts.label: Other billable features and commitments
facts.value: Enterprise gates enhanced before/after audit detail, CSV exports, Source stage, some provisioning/device/security features; Plus adds custom support/FIPS arrangements. No separate upstream per-request/token/payment-transaction fee is published.

facts.label: Solo-builder entry and market restrictions
facts.value: MIT core can be used commercially without buying an Enterprise subscription or company account. Commercial terms contain export-control/embargo restrictions; no exhaustive current seller-country list or universal individual-buyer eligibility rule was published in the checked pages.

facts.label: Self-service installation and paid purchase
facts.value: Core install is self-service. Enterprise license keys can be purchased through Customer Portal using the deployment Install ID and desired internal/external capacity, then installed locally.

facts.label: Enterprise trial terms
facts.value: Trial is requested through the sales/contact route; a fixed duration, automatic production entitlement, card requirement and trial-to-paid conversion schedule were not published on the checked public pricing/start/licensing pages.

facts.label: Product and deployment scope
facts.value: Self-hosted identity provider/SSO server with local accounts, enrollment, authentication flows, sessions, recovery, federation, user administration and protocol providers.

facts.label: Edition boundary
facts.value: Open Source is free core. Enterprise and Enterprise Plus add the same commercial product features; Plus adds custom contracting/support, multi-instance support and FIPS-oriented arrangements.

facts.label: Who operates accounts and infrastructure
facts.value: Developer/operator runs server and worker containers, PostgreSQL, any outposts, file storage, mail integration, backups, monitoring and upgrades for both free and paid editions.

facts.label: Password and email identifiers
facts.value: built_in Password stage validates local passwords, app passwords, LDAP or Kerberos backends; Identification accepts username, email or UPN.

facts.label: Email magic-link login
facts.value: built_in configured flow: official example/flows-login-email-magic-link.yaml signs an identified user in after following an emailed confirmation link.

facts.label: Email codes and phone codes
facts.value: Native Email and SMS authenticators send one-time codes for enrolled users during Authenticator Validation; SMS can also verify a phone during enrollment.

facts.label: Anonymous, phone-first and wallet login gaps
facts.value: Native anonymous guest creation/upgrade, a standalone phone-first sign-in flow and crypto-wallet login were not established from the checked core stages, source and client documentation.

facts.label: Named social and federated logins
facts.value: Documented sources include Google OAuth/Workspace SAML, GitHub OAuth, Microsoft Entra ID OAuth and Apple ID. General source guidance also names Facebook, X/Twitter, Discord and Twitch.

facts.label: Apple and generic source conditions
facts.value: Apple setup requires a registered public top-level domain, Apple identifiers/key/team configuration; .local and non-public domains do not work. Generic OAuth/OIDC/SAML sources support other compatible providers.

facts.label: Passkeys and passwordless mode
facts.value: built_in WebAuthn/FIDO2 enrollment supports roaming security keys, Windows Hello/Touch ID/Face ID and passkeys. Authenticator Validation can implement passwordless login; discoverable credentials enable username-less selection.

facts.label: Conditional autofill and domain
facts.value: Identification stage supports passkey conditional UI since 2025.12, with fallback to normal identification. Requires HTTPS except localhost, compatible browser/discoverable credential and the same hostname as enrollment.

facts.label: MFA factor set and price
facts.value: Core setup/validation supports TOTP, WebAuthn/security keys/passkeys, static recovery codes, email OTP, SMS and Duo.

facts.label: MFA enforcement and recovery codes
facts.value: Validation can Skip, Deny or Configure when no matching factor exists; the shipped flow permits password-only users without a factor. Multiple validation stages can require different methods. Static backup codes are single-use; released setup defaults are six codes, length 12.

facts.label: Lost-authenticator recovery
facts.value: Users with access can manage enrolled devices; administrators can remove a lost MFA authenticator and issue a configured recovery link/email. An official email-plus-MFA recovery example is provided.

facts.label: Verification and password reset
facts.value: Native Email stage supports verification/recovery links; configured brand recovery flow enables self-reset/admin recovery links. SMS setup has a verify-only phone-ownership mode.

facts.label: Email address change and verified claims
facts.value: User email changes are controlled globally/per-user or through custom flows. Since 2025.10, default OIDC email_verified is false; official guide configures verification flow, stored verified-address attribute and matching claim mapping.

facts.label: Self-delete and inactive recovery behavior
facts.value: User Delete stage enables a configured unenrollment flow but performs deletion without its own confirmation prompt. Email-stage Activate user on success can reactivate an inactive user when explicitly enabled.

facts.label: Browser sessions and device controls
facts.value: User Login creates a server-side session; default duration seconds=0 means browser-session lifetime, subject to browser restore behavior. Explicit duration makes it persistent; remember-device defaults 30 days, remember-me offset zero/hidden.

facts.label: OIDC token durations and refresh
facts.value: Released OAuth provider defaults: authorization code one minute, access token one hour, refresh token 30 days. Provider configuration controls these lifetimes and rotation behavior.

facts.label: Revocation and single logout
facts.value: Users/admins can delete sessions and refresh tokens; deactivation revokes active sessions. SLO supports configured OIDC front/back-channel and SAML-connected applications.

facts.label: Downstream business SSO
facts.value: Core acts as OIDC/OAuth authorization server/OpenID Provider and SAML 2.0 IdP for application providers; SAML supports metadata exchange and HTTP Redirect/POST.

facts.label: Upstream enterprise identity federation
facts.value: Core OAuth/OIDC and SAML sources make Authentik the relying party/SAML SP against an external identity provider. A deployment can issue and broker login at the same time.

facts.label: Customer workspace and membership model
facts.value: Core groups, many-to-many user membership, attributes, app bindings and role/object permissions can represent customer access. No distinct first-class customer-organization membership/role/invite API was established.

facts.label: Invitations and delegated administration
facts.value: Core invitation enrollment can pre-fill attributes and assign groups; roles provide global/object permissions and can be inherited through groups.

facts.label: Brand, tenant and billing organization distinctions
facts.value: Brands choose domain-specific appearance/default flows. Enterprise alpha tenants separate database schemas/Install IDs. Customer Portal organizations hold license/billing members and keys.

facts.label: Inbound SCIM provision/deprovision
facts.value: Native SCIM source provides v2 Users/Groups list/create/update/delete plus discovery resources, using a generated service-account Bearer token. Released model maps SCIM active to local is_active.

facts.label: SCIM tenant-wide trust boundary
facts.value: Inbound source correlates users by userName and groups by displayName across the tenant; group membership can refer to any user UUID in the tenant. Source tokens are high-trust provisioning credentials.

facts.label: Outbound SCIM variants
facts.value: SCIM 2.0 provider provisions/synchronizes Authentik users/groups to another application as a backchannel provider. Static-token mode is core; OAuth-token mode requires Enterprise.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Self-hosted browser flow UI for authentication/enrollment/recovery, user application dashboard/settings, and Admin interface. Flows/stages/policies customize the process.

facts.label: Custom or headless UI
facts.value: Flow Executor API can drive a custom login interface with challenge/response components and persistent cookies. Separate headless executor currently supports Identification, Password and Authenticator Validation for LDAP/RADIUS outposts.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Core brands support exact/wildcard/default domains, title, logo, favicon, flow background, custom CSS and default flows; operator supplies domain/TLS/proxy.

facts.label: Domain migration caveat
facts.value: Passkey conditional UI requires the same hostname used for enrollment; Apple sign-in requires a public registered domain and matching callback setup.

facts.label: Language evidence
facts.value: Released frontend declares 20 locale codes: ar, bg-BG, cs-CZ, de-DE, en, en-XA, es-ES, fi-FI, fr-FR, it-IT, ja-JP, ko-KR, nb-NO, nl-NL, pl-PL, pt-BR, ru-RU, tr-TR, zh-Hans, zh-Hant.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No current public scoped WCAG conformance statement, VPAT/ACR or independent accessibility report was established from the checked UI, developer, security/audit and official search evidence.

facts.label: Application integration and official API clients
facts.value: SSO integrates through OIDC/SAML or proxy/outpost protocols. Official maintained management API clients are Go, Python, Rust and Node/TypeScript, generated from OpenAPI v3.

facts.label: Runtime/framework boundary
facts.value: Authentik server/worker run as self-hosted container services with PostgreSQL. Application code can be elsewhere when it implements the supported redirect/token or proxy integration.

facts.label: Mobile/device client options
facts.value: OIDC public clients can use authorization code with PKCE; device-code flow is supported for limited-input devices. WebAuthn supports platform/hybrid authenticators through compatible browser/device capabilities.

facts.label: Native SDK and compatibility matrix gap
facts.value: Dedicated first-party iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter auth SDKs and a complete native passkey/session version matrix were not established in the checked official API-client, protocol, flow and authenticator material.

facts.label: Database, worker and file prerequisites
facts.value: Server and worker containers plus PostgreSQL; current configuration supports PostgreSQL 14 to 18 for application data, sessions and background-task coordination. Uploaded files/CSV reports use mounted storage or external S3.

facts.label: Redis and optional outposts
facts.value: Current architecture uses PostgreSQL for the former Redis roles; official November 13, 2025 article documents Redis removal. Outposts add protocol-specific proxy/LDAP/RADIUS/RAC services where used.

facts.label: Install and published sizing
facts.value: Docker/Podman Compose guide covers tests and small production, requiring at least two CPU cores and 2 GB RAM. Kubernetes uses Helm; AWS installation is also linked from official installation/pricing guidance.

facts.label: Backups, HA and upgrades
facts.value: Back up PostgreSQL plus relevant /data or S3, /certs, custom templates and blueprints. Upgrade sequentially through releases using latest patches; downgrade is unsupported and outposts must match server version.

facts.label: Custom logic and user fields
facts.value: Core flows/stages, custom user/group attributes, property mappings and Expression policies support server-side Python logic for branching, routing, prompt validation and access decisions.

facts.label: Native webhooks and event routing
facts.value: Notification rules can select events and deliver through local UI, email, generic HTTP POST JSON or Slack/Discord webhooks. Webhook body/header mappings customize payloads and headers.

facts.label: Paid extension boundaries
facts.value: Enterprise Source stage embeds an OAuth/SAML round-trip in a flow; scheduled offboarding, PAM and object lifecycle reviews have explicit preview status. Core generic expressions/flows remain separate.

facts.label: Administration, search and blocking
facts.value: Core Admin interface and REST API manage users, attributes, groups/roles, credentials, recovery, sessions and tokens; search/AKQL filters and bulk deletion are documented. Deactivation blocks authentication and revokes active sessions.

facts.label: Impersonation controls
facts.value: Native user impersonation is governed by permissions and a global setting; system default enables impersonation and requires a reason. Admin UI supports starting and ending the impersonated session.

facts.label: Identity linking and unlinking
facts.value: User settings exposes Connected services for configured sources; OAuth source policies control linking. Source matching defaults to source-specific identifier and offers email/username link-or-deny modes.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and temporary users
facts.value: A general anonymous guest-to-registered upgrade or merge of arbitrary existing user IDs was not established. SAML transient NameID accounts are a distinct documented temporary-user mechanism.

facts.label: Password/bot/reputation protection
facts.value: Core Password policy supports length/character rules, zxcvbn and optional HIBP prefix-query exposure checks. Reputation tracks username/IP failures/successes; CAPTCHA stage supports reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Turnstile and self-hostable Cap.

facts.label: MFA and email abuse defaults
facts.value: Code validation has configurable exponential backoff, factor 1 by default (one, two, four seconds after consecutive failures); zero disables it. Email recovery defaults to five attempts in a five-minute window.

facts.label: Password-attempt scope
facts.value: Released Password stage default allows five failed submissions before canceling that flow; durable account lockout requires additional reputation/User Write configuration.

facts.label: Endpoint throughput/rate quotas
facts.value: No universal requests-per-minute login/Admin API entitlement or per-MAU burst allowance was published in the checked installation, configuration, API, hardening and monitoring pages.

facts.label: Core events and retention
facts.value: Core events record login/authentication, account/configuration changes and other system/admin actions. Default internal event retention is 365 days, configurable; changing retention affects new events.

facts.label: Enterprise audit detail and export
facts.value: Enterprise adds before/after object-change detail, event maps/charts and CSV reports/exports. Core event details show that a change occurred and its model/application without the paid diff presentation.

facts.label: Profile/identifier export paths
facts.value: Core user API returns profiles, numeric pk, uuid/uid, attributes, groups and roles. Enterprise user/event CSV exports contain the same data as their corresponding APIs.

facts.label: Database credential portability
facts.value: Self-operated PostgreSQL backup preserves persistent user data; released user model stores password verifiers, TOTP model stores its secret key, static model stores recovery tokens, WebAuthn model stores credential/public-key metadata, and source connection models store links.

facts.label: Blueprint export is not full credential backup
facts.value: Core ak export_blueprint exports eligible configuration/user objects through their ordinary serializers; flow export covers attached flow objects. Write-only/read-only exclusions and omitted models mean this is not a full database backup.

facts.label: Pre-hashed password import
facts.value: Native set_password_hash Admin API action accepts a validated Django-encoded password in the password request field; blueprint imports support password_hash. Released validator identifies the configured hasher and decodes format before storage.

facts.label: Bulk configuration, source migration and IDs
facts.value: Blueprints import native model data; LDAP/OAuth/SAML/SCIM sources can bridge existing directories/IdPs. Enterprise Source stage supports a legacy-provider step inside a migration flow.

facts.label: Deletion and audit retention
facts.value: Admins can deactivate/delete users; configured User Delete stage supports self-unenrollment. System GDPR-compliance setting defaults true and deletes events caused by the deleted user; event retention defaults 365 days and is configurable.

facts.label: Commercial cancellation and account closure
facts.value: Portal billing lets owners cancel renewal; the key remains valid through the paid period and stays installed until removed/expired. Portal organization deletion requires contacting the company.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Self-chosen for server, PostgreSQL, files, backups and logs in both editions. No managed Authentik production region selector is offered.

facts.label: Public privacy/legal evidence
facts.value: Privacy policy effective/updated January 7, 2024 covers company services and explicitly excludes processing on business customers’ behalf under separate agreements. Subscription Terms section 12 addresses customer privacy duties and possible transfer clauses.

facts.label: Independent assessment evidence
facts.value: Official audit index links Cure53 May/June 2023 code audit, Cobalt November 2024 pentest and Include Security September 2025 assessment, with public report/retest links and company responses.

facts.label: Protocol/FIPS assurance boundaries
facts.value: Company claims OpenID certification. Enterprise Plus advertises FIPS-compliant/FedRAMP-oriented deployment arrangements; product-feature docs distinguish these custom arrangements from ordinary Enterprise features.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: authentik (row spelling: Authentik); Authentik Security Inc., a Delaware corporation with principal offices in Pennsylvania. Site https://goauthentik.io/; docs https://docs.goauthentik.io/; source https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik.

facts.label: Shutdown, sunset and acquisition search
facts.value: No official product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the checked homepage, blog index, current pricing, release and repository evidence.

facts.label: Stable release and feature maturity
facts.value: Latest stable release version/2026.8.5 published 2026-10-21T12:57:59Z; prerelease=false. Current docs select 2026.8. Enterprise multi-tenancy is alpha; scheduled offboarding/PAM and several device/lifecycle features are preview.

facts.label: Core and component licenses
facts.value: MIT for core outside stated exceptions; client-side JavaScript is MIT Expat. website/ content is CC BY-SA 4.0; enterprise/ has a separate proprietary/source-available license; third-party components retain their own licenses.

facts.label: Enterprise code production rights
facts.value: Enterprise server code requires compliance with Subscription Terms or another agreed contract and a valid subscription for the correct user seats. Development/testing copying and modification are allowed without subscription under the stated EE license.

facts.label: Commercial license wording conflict
facts.value: Current pricing and license management use internal/external user capacity, while Subscription Terms sections 1/5 describe paid Hosts, internal use and host true-ups; the EE license itself refers to user seats.

facts.label: Hosted status and uptime SLA
facts.value: No vendor-hosted production authentication service is offered, so an upstream service-status uptime percentage is not applicable to this self-hosted scope.

facts.label: Current maintenance and supported branches
facts.value: Latest stable version/2026.8.5 released October 21, 2026; repository active/not archived. Current security policy lists latest patches of 2026.5.x and 2026.8.x as supported.

facts.label: Community versus ticket/Plus support
facts.value: Core community help is Discord/GitHub without paid support. Enterprise ticket support requires annual subscription over US$1,000; Enterprise Plus starts at $20,000/year and includes contract-specific channels/response commitments.

facts.label: Response terms and vulnerability route
facts.value: Subscription Terms promise reasonable commercial effort to respond next business day for the selected support plan. Current support docs defer Plus response times to agreement. Vulnerabilities go through the private GitHub advisory portal, with acknowledgment as quickly as possible.

facts.label: Free/Developers MAU rate

facts.label: Business MAU rate

facts.label: Enterprise MAU rate

facts.label: Plan changes

facts.label: Business scenarios
facts.value: Our calculation: A and B totals cannot be established from the public evidence. Required customer organizations/invitations and incoming SAML connections are not sufficiently specified.

facts.label: Organization allowances and fees
facts.value: No public allowance or rate found for customer organizations, members/organization or customer membership invitations.

facts.label: SSO feature pricing
facts.value: Pricing includes enterprise login and SAML SSO across Free, Developers, Business and Enterprise; no separate public connection rate is shown.

facts.label: SCIM fees

facts.label: Free/Developers applications and seats

facts.label: Business applications and seats

facts.label: Enterprise applications and seats

facts.label: Extra builder capacity
