facts.label: Projects, environments and domains
facts.value: Complete included project/environment counts, multiple custom-domain limits and cross-project sharing rules are not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Free message allowance
facts.value: 100 SMS plus WhatsApp OTP messages/month, shared across the two channels on Free.

facts.label: SMS: US and Canada
facts.value: Cloud Developers/Business/Enterprise: US/Canada $0.02 per SMS message.

facts.label: SMS: other destinations

facts.label: WhatsApp: Developers

facts.label: WhatsApp: Business/Enterprise
facts.value: Cloud Business/Enterprise: linked country rate card or customer-supplied gateway.

facts.label: Email delivery and custom sender
facts.value: Custom sender email uses external SMTP; SendGrid and generic SMTP setup are documented. BYO email gateway is Business/Enterprise in pricing.

facts.label: Default email allowance and price
facts.value: A numeric included monthly email allowance, provider delivery rate and automatic overage rule were not found.

facts.label: Usage enforcement
facts.value: Hard limits cannot be exceeded; vendor may enforce soft limits with quota-exceeded or temporarily-unavailable responses. Repeated excess may lead to termination.

facts.label: Free cap and spending controls
facts.value: No exact Free 100-message exhaustion behavior, automatic paid upgrade, grace period, configurable spending cap or charge-alert threshold was found.

facts.label: Machine tokens and advanced security charges
facts.value: Machine-to-machine client credentials are documented; a separate token allowance/rate and a complete advanced-security add-on price list were not found.

facts.label: Individual account eligibility
facts.value: An individual aged 18 or over with legal capacity can accept hosted terms; an entity representative must have authority.

facts.label: Market and restricted uses
facts.value: Hosted use is subject to UK, EU and US sanctions/export controls; restricted persons and comprehensively sanctioned territories are excluded. AUP prohibits categories including gambling, phishing and malicious content.

facts.label: Self-service and card
facts.value: Cloud Free has a public self-service start, no credit card required; no expiry is stated for the ongoing Free plan. Paid self-service checkout is documented.

facts.label: Money-back terms
facts.value: Pricing advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee for any SaaS plan; hosted terms §9.2 say cancellation gets no refund and §4 describes discretionary credits.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Hosted identity service and self-hosted identity server: accounts, login, verification, sessions, user management, OIDC and SAML single sign-on.

facts.label: Cloud and private-cloud operator
facts.value: Vendor operates Cloud and managed private cloud; hosted infrastructure operation and upgrades are included. Customer operates its application and integration.

facts.label: Self-host operator
facts.value: Customer runs servers, PostgreSQL, Redis, networking, TLS, upgrades, monitoring and backups; maintenance services can be contracted.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built in: username/email/phone login identifiers with password where that login method is enabled; available in the Free authentication feature set.

facts.label: Email link and code
facts.value: Built in: email magic-link and email OTP login. Email link is selected in email/mobile login verification settings.

facts.label: Phone code login
facts.value: Built in: SMS and WhatsApp OTP login, with delivery quotas/rates and optional paid-plan custom provider.

facts.label: Anonymous accounts
facts.value: Built in for Native App, SPA and Traditional Web App client types; anonymous users can later become registered users.

facts.label: Wallet login
facts.value: SIWE appears in the request-limit table, but a supported wallet-login setup, client/platform scope and plan entitlement were not established.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Built-in provider catalog: Apple, Google, Facebook, GitHub, LinkedIn, WeChat Mobile and WeChat Web.

facts.label: Microsoft login scope
facts.value: Built-in Microsoft Entra ID OAuth/OIDC connection supports an organizational tenant, multiple organizations, and organizational plus personal accounts; personal-only account mode is not yet supported.

facts.label: Passkeys: first factor and fallback
facts.value: Built-in passkey login on all Cloud plans. Can run with password/passwordless fallback, or as passkey-only through custom login method settings.

facts.label: Passkeys: platform and association
facts.value: Documented platforms include iOS 16/macOS 13 or later and Android 9/API 28 or later. Embedded WebView use requires iOS/Android application associations.

facts.label: Passkeys: portability detail
facts.value: Conditional autofill guarantees, moving relying-party domains without re-enrollment, and exporting usable passkey credential records were not established.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Built-in TOTP authenticator codes, email OTP/link, phone OTP and additional password; disabled, optional or mandatory enrollment modes, plus remembered devices.

facts.label: MFA enrollment grace and recovery
facts.value: Mandatory MFA can allow enrollment on next login. Per-user enrollment grace is 10 days and can be extended/cancelled; recovery-code configuration defaults to 16 codes.

facts.label: Adaptive MFA maturity
facts.value: Pricing and current MFA feature page advertise adaptive challenges based on risk; repository README still labels Adaptive MFA 'coming soon'.

facts.label: Verification and contact changes
facts.value: Email/phone verification can be enabled and required; account-verified criteria can require any or all configured claims. User Settings lets people manage email, phone, username and password.

facts.label: Forgot/reset password
facts.value: User recovery via email link/OTP, phone OTP, or both; phone channel can be WhatsApp or SMS. Validity duration is configurable.

facts.label: User-initiated deletion
facts.value: Optional Delete Account screen/button in User Settings; SDKs can open it directly. Initiation deactivates the user and immediately invalidates their sessions.

facts.label: SSO and refresh sessions
facts.value: Authgear-domain cookies share SSO across a project's apps; SDK token/refresh sessions are separate for each application. Persistent sessions are default.

facts.label: Session lifetimes
facts.value: Documented SSO default maximum 31,449,600 seconds (52 weeks) and idle timeout 2,592,000 seconds (30 days). Per-client refresh lifetime and idle settings are configurable.

facts.label: Session revocation
facts.value: User Settings can manage sessions; Admin API supports revokeSession and revokeAllSessions for a chosen user.

facts.label: Sender-bound refresh tokens
facts.value: DPoP validation is available for Native App clients using newer mobile SDKs; Web SDK does not support it.

facts.label: SAML role
facts.value: SAML 2.0 identity provider: Authgear issues assertions to downstream service-provider apps, with Salesforce/Dropbox examples and SAML single logout.

facts.label: OIDC and enterprise-provider role
facts.value: Authgear supplies OIDC login to applications; named upstream providers include Microsoft Entra ID, ADFS and Azure AD B2C.

facts.label: Incoming SAML customer connections
facts.value: Public implementation details for using Authgear as a SAML service provider/broker to a customer's own SAML identity provider remain unclear.

facts.label: Roles and groups
facts.value: Built-in project-level roles and groups. Assign roles directly to users or through groups; roles appear in UserInfo and JWT claims; Portal and Admin API support management.

facts.label: Customer workspaces and invitations
facts.value: B2B page advertises multi-tenancy, but an isolated customer-organization object, invitation lifecycle, per-organization roles and delegated customer-admin controls were not documented in the checked API material.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: Native SCIM: unavailable according to Authgear's own current product-comparison table, which explicitly says 'no SCIM' for Authgear.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Hosted AuthUI includes signup/login and prebuilt User Settings: profile, login IDs, password, social connections, MFA and sessions.

facts.label: Custom UI
facts.value: A headless Authentication Flow API path is documented; custom signup/login UI requires another server and customer implementation.

facts.label: Branding: Free/Developers
facts.value: Cloud Free/Developers: logo/theme/CSS customization; removal of Authgear branding is not included.

facts.label: Branding: Business/Enterprise
facts.value: Cloud Business/Enterprise: logo/theme/CSS customization and removal of Authgear branding included.

facts.label: Cloud custom-domain gate
facts.value: Pricing marks Custom Domain included on all four plans; domain documentation says a paid subscription is required.

facts.label: Domain activation and migration
facts.value: Customer verifies DNS ownership and activates the custom domain; documentation says the default authgear.cloud endpoint becomes unusable and SDK endpoints must be updated.

facts.label: Built-in translations
facts.value: Chinese (Hong Kong, Simplified, Traditional), Dutch, English, Filipino, French, German, Greek, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Polish, Portuguese (general/Brazil/Portugal), Spanish (general/Latin America/Spain), Thai and Vietnamese.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A public accessibility statement, WCAG conformance report or VPAT for AuthUI was not found in this bounded check.

facts.label: Web frameworks and server integrations
facts.value: Official client guides: React, Vue, Angular and vanilla JavaScript. Server-web guides: Next.js, Express, Laravel/PHP, Flask/Python, ASP.NET Core MVC and Spring Boot/Java.

facts.label: Backend validation and runtime limits
facts.value: Application backend validates JWT signature, issuer, audience and relevant claims against JWKS; a full edge-runtime support/version matrix was not found.

facts.label: iOS SDK
facts.value: Official iOS SDK supports iOS 11.0+. Current tutorial uses iOS 17+, Xcode 16+ and Swift 6; earlier deployments can use completion handlers.

facts.label: Android SDK
facts.value: Official SDK supports Android 5.0/API 21+; both Jetpack Compose and classic Views are documented.

facts.label: Cross-platform and other clients
facts.value: Official guide index includes React Native, Flutter, Capacitor/Ionic and Xamarin; manual OIDC integration is also documented for clients without an SDK.

facts.label: Native biometric login
facts.value: Built-in device-key biometric login: iOS 11.3+ and Android 6/API 23+. SDK registers a public key; private key stays in device Keychain/Keystore.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Cloud owns identity infrastructure; your app needs registered client/redirect settings and backend token validation. Custom UI, BYO messaging and third-party login providers have their own dependencies.

facts.label: Self-host storage and services
facts.value: PostgreSQL is the only supported database; Helm recommends PostgreSQL 16+ with pg_partman, at least 5GB storage, and Redis 6.2+. Optional avatar storage uses S3, GCS or Azure Blob.

facts.label: Production deployment
facts.value: Official Helm chart is recommended for Kubernetes production; guide minimum Kubernetes 1.23, basic recommended 2 CPUs and 4GB RAM, external production-ready PostgreSQL/Redis, DNS and TLS.

facts.label: Docker and backup responsibilities
facts.value: Docker Compose example is for local use with development defaults. A separate VM/Compose reference architecture covers production availability, ingress, monitoring and backing up PostgreSQL audit data.

facts.label: Blocking and asynchronous events
facts.value: Built-in events/hooks before or after auth operations; blocking hooks can allow/deny or alter an operation. Non-blocking delivery order is unspecified.

facts.label: TypeScript hooks and webhooks
facts.value: JavaScript/TypeScript modules run in Deno with external-network access, but no file/environment access. Webhooks POST over HTTPS and support HMAC-SHA256 body signatures.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Portal plus JWT-authenticated GraphQL Admin API: create/read/search/update users, disable/re-enable, verify claims, reset passwords, delete/anonymize accounts and manage roles/groups.

facts.label: Session creation and impersonation boundary
facts.value: A createSession mutation is documented for zero-downtime migration, but is disabled by default and requires contacting Authgear to enable it.

facts.label: Linking at signup
facts.value: Account linking can match provider email/phone/username to an existing account; login_and_link requires authenticating the existing account before attaching the new identity.

facts.label: Link/unlink after sign-in
facts.value: Signed-in users can link/unlink OAuth providers in User Settings. Dedicated start/finish link/unlink methods are currently Web SDK only.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: promoteAnonymousUser upgrades a guest while preserving its sub/user ID.

facts.label: Account lockout and password policy
facts.value: Configurable failed-attempt lockout by user or user+IP, selected authenticators, reset period and increasing lock duration. Password policy supports length, character rules, zxcvbn strength, excluded keywords and reuse prevention.

facts.label: Bot challenges
facts.value: Customer-configured Google reCAPTCHA Challenge v2 or Cloudflare Turnstile Managed widget; can require CAPTCHA for signup/login, password or passwordless flows, and reset.

facts.label: SMS pumping protection
facts.value: Fraud Protection examines unverified OTP ratios by IP/country and countries targeted by one IP. Observe mode flags; Protect mode blocks; allowlists and event logs are documented.

facts.label: Authentication request limits
facts.value: Defaults when no override is specified: 60 requests/IP/minute and 10 requests/user/IP/minute. Signup: 7/IP/168 hours; password/TOTP/passkey/biometric: 60/IP/minute and 10/user/IP/minute.

facts.label: Messaging limits and OTP settings
facts.value: Email: 200/IP/minute, 50/target/24 hours. SMS: 60/IP/minute, 10/target/hour. Passwordless email/SMS trigger and validate limits: 60/IP/minute; default resend cooldown 60 seconds.

facts.label: Admin API burst capacity
facts.value: A separate endpoint-specific Admin GraphQL sustained/burst allowance and guaranteed reset/retry headers were not found.

facts.label: Audit events and access
facts.value: Portal and Admin API expose login success/failure, identity changes, user/session actions, messaging and administrative/configuration/collaborator actions.

facts.label: Audit retention: Free/Developers
facts.value: Cloud Free/Developers: 1 day.

facts.label: Audit retention: Business
facts.value: Cloud Business: 60 days.

facts.label: Audit retention: Enterprise
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise: 180 days.

facts.label: Log streaming and self-host logs
facts.value: Datadog streaming sends all project audit entries in batches about once a minute. Self-host background worker must run; customer owns database and downstream retention.

facts.label: Profile and identity export
facts.value: Self-service asynchronous Admin-authenticated export to CSV or newline-delimited JSON; supports user IDs, contact/profile fields, custom attributes, roles, groups, disabled status and linked identities.

facts.label: MFA and passkey export contents
facts.value: Export schema includes MFA email addresses, phone numbers and TOTP secret/URI records. It exposes passkey_count and biometric_count.

facts.label: Password-hash export promise and procedure
facts.value: Homepage explicitly promises export including password hashes. The linked User Export API guide/schema lists no password-hash pointer or documented hash-export procedure.

facts.label: Bulk import and supported hashes
facts.value: Asynchronous JSON User Import API, Admin JWT authentication, request body up to 500KB; bcrypt password format explicitly supported.

facts.label: Import constraints and IDs
facts.value: On upsert, existing password is ignored; an initial import without a password cannot later add it through another import. Custom attributes can hold external IDs; caller-selected sub was not established.

facts.label: Rolling and session-preserving migration
facts.value: Rolling migration needs application code that accepts old and Authgear sessions. Zero-downtime path imports accounts and exchanges a verified old session through gated createSession.

facts.label: End-user retention and deletion
facts.value: User deletion can be immediate or scheduled through Portal/Admin API; self-service defaults to 30 days deactivation, configurable 1–180 days. Deactivated users cannot sign in.

facts.label: Vendor-account closure and export
facts.value: Hosted terms allow cancellation at any time and require customer export before termination, with a reasonable opportunity to retrieve content.

facts.label: Contractual processor deletion and backups
facts.value: DPA §12 provides return/deletion on request or termination and written confirmation within 60 days. Encrypted backups age out on standard rotation, no longer than 90 days.

facts.label: Privacy-policy retention limits
facts.value: Policy gives purpose-based retention rather than one universal day count. A 30-day deletion statement appears in the Google Portal-data section; collaborator-shared data may persist for remaining users.

facts.label: Shared Cloud regions
facts.value: Data-sovereignty page says choose United States or Hong Kong when creating a Cloud project. Pricing FAQ and privacy policy still describe primary hosting in the USA.

facts.label: EU and self-selected residency
facts.value: EU shared-Cloud region is coming soon/waitlist. Self-host anywhere you operate; managed private cloud can use an agreed country including UK/EU.

facts.label: Provider and transfer scope
facts.value: Subprocessor list identifies GCP for infrastructure across global GCP regions and separately names US/Ireland support, billing and Portal providers.

facts.label: Processing and transfers
facts.value: Public DPA and subprocessor schedule; customer is controller and vendor processor for covered end-user data, with SCC/UK transfer mechanisms and breach notification within 72 hours of awareness.

facts.label: Assurance claims and reports
facts.value: Authgear claims ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II. Security page directs readers to contact the vendor; public full audit reports, exact assessment scope and current expiry were not obtained.

facts.label: Security controls and training use
facts.value: DPA technical annex describes encrypted transport, AES-256 data-at-rest protection/KMS and controlled personnel access; it disallows training vendor ML models on end-user personal data.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Authgear; built by Skymakers. Official site https://www.authgear.com/; documentation https://docs.authgear.com/.

facts.label: Contracting entities
facts.value: Hosted SaaS: Skymakers Digital Limited, England and Wales. Enterprise software license: Oursky Limited, Hong Kong.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Available: public Free/paid Cloud entry and self-host deployment guides; stable release 2026-10-22.0 published 2026-10-22.

facts.label: Legacy Auth UI retirement
facts.value: Release 2026-03-17.0 fully retired the legacy v1 Auth UI; all flows use the v2 UI.

facts.label: Open-source core license
facts.value: authgear-server main: Apache-2.0; permits commercial use, modification and distribution, subject to license and notice conditions.

facts.label: Enterprise software license
facts.value: Proprietary Enterprise license: subscription and quote govern use; own applications/internal business use, with restrictions on redistribution and service-bureau use.

facts.label: Hosted availability commitment
facts.value: Published standard SLA: paid plans 99.95% uptime per calendar month, excluding Free, beta/preview and listed external/customer-caused downtime.

facts.label: SLA remedy
facts.value: On a confirmed missed monthly commitment, customer must request a future-service credit of 10% of that month's paid fees; no cash refund.

facts.label: Public status page
facts.value: A public official incident/status dashboard URL was not found in the pages checked.

facts.label: Server release evidence
facts.value: Latest returned public stable release: 2026-10-22.0, published 2026-10-22 16:07:15 UTC; notes include WebView passkeys, Datadog streaming and security fixes.

facts.label: Security and SDK support policy
facts.value: Security policy supports the latest stable release; report through GitHub advisories or security@authgear.com, follow up after 48 hours without reply. Commercial SDK support covers latest major versions.

facts.label: Plan support entitlement conflict
facts.value: Pricing: Free community, Developers priority email, Business dedicated Slack, Enterprise 24/7/account manager. Statement of Support instead places Developer/Business in Community and names Standard/Premium options including a 'Plus' plan.

facts.label: Response tiers and paid assistance
facts.value: Statement of Support S1 first reply: Standard 1 business day; Premium 4 business hours; Premium 24x7 4 hours; Mission Critical 1 hour. Tier prices are not public.

apps.name: Authing
apps.line: Hosted login and user management with developer APIs.

free.text: Free up to 8,000 MAU; one app

cells.freeUsers: 8,000 MAU; one app and one social connection
cells.sso: Basic lists 1 connection; Advanced lists 3

mau.math: 1,000 users is within the 8,000 free limit. The free plan and the required add-ons for users, organizations and SSO total ¥0 a month.
The B2C Basic plan for 10,000 users: ¥1,190 base plus ¥0 for required add-ons, so ¥1,190 a month.
50,000 users is above the 10,000-user limit of the public B2C plans. The plan for this many monthly users and its required charges still need a quote.
100,000 users is above the 10,000-user limit of the public B2C plans. The plan for this many monthly users and its required charges still need a quote.

facts.label: Monthly active user definition
facts.value: MAU: any user who authenticates within one user pool during a month.

facts.label: Counting details and purchased capacity
facts.value: Public calculator selects monthly capacity bands. Exact month timezone, failed-login/refresh counting and identity deduplication across user pools were not established.

facts.label: Ongoing free allowance
facts.value: 免费版: ¥0; up to 8,000 MAU, one self-built application and one social account connection.

facts.label: Minimum public monthly price
facts.value: B2C 基础版 (Basic): ¥139/month at the 1,000-MAU calculator setting. B2B Basic: ¥3,699/month at the 500-MAU setting.

facts.label: Payment, tax and contract differences
facts.value: Chinese terms require prepayment and renewal payment at least seven days before expiry. English terms default to invoices due in 30 days, non-refundable fees and tax exclusions.

facts.label: B2B monthly bands and annual selector
facts.value: Basic: 500 MAU ¥3,699/month; 1,000 ¥5,799/month. Advanced: 500 ¥6,299/month; 1,000 ¥10,999/month. Above 1,000: contact sales.

facts.label: Business scenario coverage
facts.value: Both required business totals remain unresolved. Baseline A has a public candidate price, but conflicting rights; baseline B exceeds public B2B user and SSO bands.

facts.label: Advertised B2B tenant caps
facts.value: B2B Basic card: 50 tenants. B2B Advanced card: 100 tenants. Tooltip says tenant count depends on version and MAU must be subscribed separately.

facts.label: Multi-tenant entitlement disagreement
facts.value: The global comparison shows multi-tenant Beta unavailable in Free/Basic/Advanced and as-needed in Enterprise; B2B cards explicitly offer 50/100 tenants.

facts.label: Advertised SSO connections and fees
facts.value: B2B Basic card: one enterprise connection; Advanced: three. No extra-connection or per-SAML/setup rate found. Global comparison puts enterprise connections only in Enterprise.

facts.label: Provisioning price gate
facts.value: Global comparison places identity provisioning and Sync Center in Enterprise; B2B Advanced card advertises synchronization/provisioning. No standalone SCIM tariff established.

facts.label: Apps and developer collaborators
facts.value: Free: one self-built app, no collaborator allocation shown. Basic: 10 apps and five collaborating administrators. Advanced: 20 apps and ten collaborators. Enterprise: as needed.

facts.label: Project/environment/domain ceilings
facts.value: Separate project or environment allowances, staging isolation rules, extra collaborator prices and custom-domain counts were not found.

facts.label: Included SMS
facts.value: Free: ten sends total; Basic: 300 sends/month; Advanced: 1,500/month; Enterprise: 12,000/month.

facts.label: SMS providers and geography
facts.value: Built-in SMS delivery; custom configuration documents Chuanglan 253, Aliyun and Tencent. International SMS requires configured Aliyun/international service; custom gateway is Advanced/Enterprise in the matrix.

facts.label: Email delivery and allowance
facts.value: From 2025-02-26, public-cloud free user pools receive 50 email sends/day; paid pools and pools using a custom provider are unaffected by that notice. Default email service uses Aliyun Enterprise Mail.

facts.label: At quota or nonpayment
facts.value: Precise MAU/SMS/email exhaustion behavior, automatic upgrade, grace period and spend caps were not published in the pricing, trial or general contract pages read.

facts.label: Security, automation and resource quotas
facts.value: Basic: five Pipeline workflows and five webhooks; Advanced: ten of each. Advanced data resources/nodes: 1/100; Enterprise: 10/1,000 with add-ons advertised.

facts.label: Custom database and other add-ons
facts.value: Custom database, cross-app SSO, own SMS gateway and password-policy features appear in Advanced/Enterprise. Private deployment is a paid Enterprise add-on; Enterprise quantities are negotiated.

facts.label: Home market and entry path
facts.value: China-facing offer with Chinese documentation, WeChat integrations and phone-number or third-party account registration described in the privacy policy.

facts.label: Individual and foreign-country eligibility
facts.value: A complete seller-country list, overseas individual purchasing rules, and accepted foreign phone/payment requirements were not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Self-service free use and feature trial
facts.value: Free developer plan is presented separately from a 30-day feature trial. Each ToB, ToC and ToE scene can be tried once; trial usage remains limited.

facts.label: Card/company-domain requirements
facts.value: No explicit card-free or company-domain-free production signup promise found.

facts.label: Type and coverage
facts.value: Vendor-hosted identity service; licensed private deployment also offered. Accounts, login, sessions, profile management, permissions and SSO.

facts.label: Hosted operations
facts.value: Authing operates and maintains its own software. The customer operates its app and external identity/data sources and is responsible for its data backups.

facts.label: Private deployment responsibilities
facts.value: Authing offers planning, installation into the customer's private cloud, delivery and continuing support; detailed patch/restore ownership is contract-specific.

facts.label: Password and email/phone codes
facts.value: Built-in username/password, email/password and phone/password; email OTP and SMS OTP login/registration are documented.

facts.label: Other basic methods
facts.value: No confirmed native anonymous-login, guest-upgrade, wallet-login or email magic-link flow established in the login guide and public authentication schema.

facts.label: Headless login restriction
facts.value: API V3 /api/v3/signin and /frontend-signin explicitly do not implement MFA, information completion or first-login password reset; use the OIDC authentication flow when these are needed.

facts.label: Documented social providers
facts.value: WeChat, QQ, Weibo, GitHub, Facebook, Twitter, Google, Apple, Alipay, Slack, Gitee, GitLab, Baidu, LinkedIn, NetEase Yidun, QingCloud, Instagram, Douyin, Kuaishou, Xiaomi and Line.

facts.label: Social plan cap and setup
facts.value: Free includes one connection; paid Basic/Advanced cards advertise unlimited social connections. Providers require their own identity-source setup and supported platform mode.

facts.label: Passkey sign-in and enrollment behavior
facts.value: Native FIDO2/WebAuthn first-factor passkeys and a second-factor passkey option are documented, using biometrics, device PIN or security keys.

facts.label: Passkey gates and platform detail
facts.value: The passkey guide does not settle a first-factor minimum paid plan, conditional autofill, full browser/mobile compatibility, or a passkey-specific recovery procedure.

facts.label: MFA factors, enforcement and recovery
facts.value: SMS, email OTP, authenticator TOTP and facial MFA are documented; passkey/security key second-factor setup has its own guide. TOTP enrollment shows a recovery code/key and supports unbinding in Personal Center.

facts.label: MFA plan quantity
facts.value: Matrix: Free and Basic show no MFA; Advanced shows 1; Enterprise as needed. The meaning of the Advanced quantity 1 and individual factor entitlements are unresolved.

facts.label: Verification, reset and profile changes
facts.value: Built-in email verification, phone/email binding and unbinding, password change and password reset using email or SMS code; hosted Personal Center supplies profile/account controls.

facts.label: End-user account deletion
facts.value: V3 offers a verified self-deletion request using email code, phone code or password, then /api/v3/delete-account using the returned temporary deleteAccountToken.

facts.label: Tokens and refresh
facts.value: OIDC authorization-code SDK flow returns access/ID tokens, expiry metadata and, with offline_access, a refresh token; logout URL flow is documented.

facts.label: Session/device revocation
facts.value: Console can force a user out of every app in the user pool. Public V3 schemas also expose session listing/batch or all-session deactivation and a user's device-session revoke operation.

facts.label: Expiry limits and rotation policy
facts.value: A complete current plan-specific idle/max-session, access-token and refresh-token lifetime/rotation table was not found.

facts.label: Upstream business SSO
facts.value: SAML 2.0, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, CAS, LDAP, Windows AD and Azure AD connections are documented. Authing can consume an external SAML IdP's assertions.

facts.label: Identity-provider role
facts.value: Authing can issue SAML 2.0 assertions to service providers and act as an OIDC/OAuth identity provider for applications.

facts.label: Customer workspace model
facts.value: A user pool can contain customer tenants with tenant-specific membership, applications, identity sources, branding and delegated tenant administration.

facts.label: Invitations and roles/permissions
facts.value: Tenant console documents email/shareable-link invitations with app and validity selection. Tenant access control supplies delegated administrators and resource permissions scoped to the tenant.

facts.label: SCIM and synchronization evidence
facts.value: Authing documents upstream/downstream identity synchronization; an official 2021 customer case explicitly identifies SCIM/LDAP communication for user/organization provisioning.

facts.label: Customer-facing SCIM scope
facts.value: Current public SCIM version, tenant-specific server configuration, Users/Groups coverage, deactivation/session consequences and price could not be settled.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Hosted login/register/reset pages, embedded Guard normal/modal forms and hosted Personal Center; custom UI can use SDK/API.

facts.label: Branding controls
facts.value: Basic adds custom login, message templates and user agreements. Advanced/Enterprise add brand-identity and custom-domain cells in the global comparison.

facts.label: Custom-domain edition and setup
facts.value: Dedicated guide limits the hosted feature to B2B/B2E Advanced or higher, whereas the general matrix shows Advanced without that scene restriction.

facts.label: UI languages
facts.value: Guard 5 web reference lists zh-CN, zh-TW, en-US and ja-JP. An older React component guide lists Chinese/English only.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public WCAG conformance statement, VPAT or accessibility audit report found in the UI and policy pages checked.

facts.label: Web/backend integrations
facts.value: Official SDK index includes Java, JavaScript/Node.js, Python, PHP, C#, Go and Ruby; quickstarts include React, Vue, Angular, Express and Spring Boot.

facts.label: Runtime/version limits
facts.value: Published React integration distinguishes React 16/17 and React 18 packages. authing-js-sdk 4.23.55 declares Node >=8.9; no verified current edge-runtime compatibility matrix found.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official references cover Android, iOS/Swift, React Native, Flutter and WeChat mini-program clients; social inventory distinguishes mobile and web provider modes.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Native hosted user store does not require a builder-operated database/cache. The builder still supplies its app and upstream provider credentials; email/SMS can use vendor or configured external delivery.

facts.label: Private service dependencies
facts.value: Published deployment examples include PostgreSQL 12.5, Redis 4.0, Elasticsearch/Logstash 7.7, object storage and Authing Server 1.2.0.

facts.label: Deployment paths and sizing
facts.value: Bare metal and single-host Docker Compose guides publish minimum 8 x86 cores, 32 GB RAM, 500 GB disk and 100 Mbps; recommended 16 cores, 64 GB, 2 TB and 1 Gbps.

facts.label: HA deployment example
facts.value: Kubernetes guide describes a multi-zone/load-balanced private architecture; client >=1.19.4, server >=1.18.3. Master minimum 2 cores/8 GB/500 GB; worker 4 cores/16 GB/1 TB; 1 Gbps networking.

facts.label: Current upgrade/restore playbook
facts.value: No complete current private-edition upgrade, supported-component lifecycle, backup schedule and tested restore/runbook found in the three deployment guides and general terms.

facts.label: Custom logic and fields
facts.value: Pipeline runs tenant-isolated JavaScript hooks in the vendor's serverless environment, for signup/login/custom authentication logic. User schema supports custom fields.

facts.label: Webhook events and delivery contract
facts.value: Webhooks POST login, registration, profile/password, MFA, deletion, permission and other events. JSON and form payloads are supported; secret-header documentation disagrees.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Console and Management SDK/API support creating, searching, editing and disabling accounts; V3 documents bulk deletion, external identities, roles/groups/departments and login history.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: No documented production-safe user impersonation control, consent/audit policy or minimum plan established.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking identities
facts.value: Provider connections support configurable field matching or explicit binding. V3 has external-identity link/unlink flows; the older two-account merge requires both account tokens.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: No native anonymous-account-to-registered-account upgrade flow established.

facts.label: Abuse and password controls
facts.value: Matrix includes brute-force protection from Basic, stronger password rules/rotation and registration allowlists from Advanced. Public authentication schema includes a human-verification-aware frontend sign-in endpoint.

facts.label: Web-origin restriction
facts.value: Web safe-domain/CORS configuration is documented; the guide explicitly says Free does not support it. Protocol, domain and port must match exactly; no subdomains/wildcards.

facts.label: API burst rate
facts.value: Current public-cloud V3 documentation: all editions share a limit of 150 requests/second per user pool; excess requests receive HTTP 429 and the restriction is lifted after three seconds.

facts.label: Messaging request limits
facts.value: SMS configuration guide states SMS interface QPS 100; authentication API allows one email per address per channel per minute.

facts.label: Audit event coverage
facts.value: Console audit logs distinguish administrator operations and end-user behavior such as sign-in/sign-out. Management API exposes user login history; webhooks cover authentication/account changes.

facts.label: Audit retention by plan
facts.value: Free: up to one day; Basic: three days; Advanced: ten days; Enterprise: 30 days.

facts.label: Profile and identity export
facts.value: Tenant console supports exporting its user list with export history/download; management list-users supports paginated profiles, optional custom data and identities.

facts.label: Passwords and passkey portability
facts.value: Full default-password-hash/salt export and passkey-credential export were not established. V3 offers ciphertext retrieval only for configured custom encryption such as RSA/SM2.

facts.label: Bulk and lazy migration in
facts.value: API/script bulk migration and first-login lazy migration through a custom database are documented; fully external database mode is also described.

facts.label: Legacy hash compatibility and IDs
facts.value: Custom password encryption/verification uses uploaded Node.js .js/.zip code, optionally including node_modules. The guide warns changes take effect immediately and affect existing users.

facts.label: Delete app users

facts.label: Type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Python protocol toolkit: OAuth 1.0/2.0 clients, authorization servers, resource-server validation and OpenID Connect client/provider building blocks.

facts.label: Project/component boundary
facts.value: Authlib covers protocol integrations; joserfc is the JOSE/JWT successor dependency; OTP Auth is a separate HOTP/TOTP project.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer/chosen host operates app and any authorization/resource server, user/token/client stores, signing keys, sessions, updates, backup and recovery.

facts.label: Password/email-password login
facts.value: custom_code: resource-owner password grant delegates authenticate_user(username,password) to app code; server example assumes an existing user login/account system.

facts.label: Magic link/email/phone/wallet/guest
facts.value: Custom account/identity integration required; no bundled email magic-link/OTP, phone-code/wallet verifier or saved guest-account creation/upgrade flow.

facts.label: Provider integration model
facts.value: Generic OAuth/OIDC registry and configurable endpoints/discovery; app implements callback, identity mapping, local account/session and provider credentials.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: Official client recipes use Google OIDC discovery, openid/profile/email scopes and validated token userinfo.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: Official generic/web client recipes configure GitHub OAuth endpoints and user:email scope, then fetch profile/API data.

facts.label: Apple, Microsoft and others
facts.value: Generic/custom OAuth/OIDC configuration can be registered; no universal bundled Apple/Microsoft adapter or wrapper-specific native platform support matrix is claimed.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: custom_code/other package or external IdP required; Authlib has no bundled WebAuthn registration/assertion verifier, key inventory or conditional-autofill UI.

facts.label: MFA/OTP scope
facts.value: No bundled MFA enrollment/enforcement/recovery-code account flow. HOTP/TOTP are supplied by the separate OTP Auth project, not Authlib's package.

facts.label: OIDC authentication context
facts.value: Protocol claims/hooks can carry auth_time, acr and amr; the authorization app supplies how authentication/freshness requirements are satisfied.

facts.label: Verification/reset/account changes
facts.value: Application or external IdP owns signup, email/phone confirmation, password reset/change and account deletion; core is protocol tooling.

facts.label: Local login sessions
facts.value: Application/framework owns end-user session creation, lifetime, cookies and device logout; OAuth callbacks return tokens/profile for the app to handle.

facts.label: Client state and token persistence
facts.value: Framework integration stores transaction state/nonce/PKCE data in framework session or configured cache; token persistence/update callbacks belong to the app.

facts.label: Default OAuth server access-token expiry
facts.value: Bearer generator defaults: authorization_code/password/client_credentials 864,000 seconds; implicit 3,600 seconds; other grants default 3,600. Overridable by server configuration/generator.

facts.label: Authorization code expiry
facts.value: SQLAlchemy authorization-code mixin is_expired uses 300 seconds; integration example explicitly checks it in query_authorization_code.

facts.label: Refresh tokens
facts.value: Flask server refresh-token generation defaults off; custom RefreshTokenGrant supplies lookup/user/expiry/revocation. INCLUDE_NEW_REFRESH_TOKEN defaults False.

facts.label: Revocation/introspection
facts.value: Built-in RFC7009/RFC7662 endpoint/validator primitives; app implements storage queries, permission checks, revocation and routes.

facts.label: OIDC logout
facts.value: RP-Initiated Logout client helpers and server EndSessionEndpoint are supported; app supplies local session termination, keys/registration and confirmation UI.

facts.label: OIDC roles
facts.value: Built-in generic OIDC relying-party clients plus provider primitives for Flask/Django: authorization code/implicit/hybrid, UserInfo, discovery/registration and RP logout components.

facts.label: Enterprise assertion bridge
facts.value: Optional draft ID-JAG grant can accept assertions from trusted external IdPs for cross-application access; requires issuer/subject/tenant-aware user mapping and permission/replay hooks.

facts.label: SAML
facts.value: Not shipped in current Authlib; funding guide lists SAML 2.0/RFC7522 as future v3 work.

facts.label: Customer organizations/roles
facts.value: custom_code required for workspaces, memberships, invitations, tenant isolation and customer-admin roles. OAuth clients/scopes are not that model.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: No published SCIM Users/Groups/provisioning implementation or deactivation contract found.

facts.label: Ready account/consent screens
facts.value: No production login/signup/profile/MFA or hosted account UI; server examples require app-owned render_template/current_user and routes.

facts.label: Branding/domains
facts.value: App controls frontend/authorization-server branding, domains and issuer URLs; no vendor branding-removal/domain subscription tier.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: App supplies localized login/consent/profile UI. OAuth server docs describe error-description i18n support as incomplete work.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Authlib-specific published WCAG/VPAT or independently assessed account UI report found.

facts.label: Runtime and core dependencies
facts.value: Authlib 1.9.4 requires Python>=3.10, cryptography>=45.0.1 and joserfc>=1.6.8.

facts.label: Web client/server integrations
facts.value: Official web clients: Flask, Django, Starlette and FastAPI via Starlette. Official provider integrations: Flask/Django; async Starlette/FastAPI provider work remains a funding goal.

facts.label: HTTP clients and changed transport
facts.value: Requests OAuth sessions and sync/async HTTPX2 clients are available. Since 1.8, authlib.integrations.httpx_client uses httpx2, with deprecated httpx fallback.

facts.label: Mobile/desktop clients
facts.value: No Authlib native iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop SDK or supported-OS matrix found; Python protocols can support apps built separately.

facts.label: Client prerequisites
facts.value: Selected framework/HTTP library, provider registration/credentials, public callbacks and session/cache for transaction state; app decides local user/session/token persistence.

facts.label: Server prerequisites
facts.value: App implements user/client/code/token models or equivalent storage, query/save/revoke hooks, routes and signing-key/issuer configuration. SQLAlchemy helpers/mixins are optional building blocks.

facts.label: Keys/storage protection
facts.value: Operator supplies TLS, client secrets, OIDC/JOSE keys and secure token storage; optional framework and cryptographic backend versions must be selected.

facts.label: Operations/backups/upgrades
facts.value: Runs inside the selected Python application. Operator deploys, patches and backs up its user/client/code/token data, session state, issuer configuration and keys.

facts.label: Published capacity/sizing
facts.value: No universal Authlib hardware-sizing, concurrency or guaranteed requests-per-second capacity found.

facts.label: Custom protocol/account logic
facts.value: Subclass grants/endpoints/validators; implement storage, user mapping, scope/permission, issuer/key and token generators; client compliance hooks customize provider exchange.

facts.label: Events/webhooks
facts.value: Flask/Django server signals include client_authenticated/token_revoked; client token-update signals/callbacks let the app persist provider refresh results.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: App/IdP supplies user create/search/ban/delete/profile support and admin screens; Authlib does not provide a global user-management API or impersonation console.

facts.label: OAuth client registration/management
facts.value: RFC7591/7592 endpoint primitives create/read/update/delete OAuth client registrations with app-supplied authentication, storage and permission methods.

facts.label: Account linking/guest upgrade
facts.value: custom_code required for mapping provider identities, safe linking/unlinking/merging and saved-guest conversion.

facts.label: Protocol state, nonce and PKCE
facts.value: Client framework helpers bind state to session; OIDC validates configured expected nonce. PKCE client config uses S256; server CodeChallenge extension must be registered/configured.

facts.label: TLS/redirect/scope checks
facts.value: Secure-transport helper and protocol/client metadata/scope validation are included; app must configure trustworthy issuers/redirects, registration permissions and endpoint policies.

facts.label: Credential/bot protections
facts.value: No bundled password validation/breach feed, CAPTCHA, MFA lockout, SMS budget or saved attempt-counter policy; app/IdP/proxy supplies them.

facts.label: Numeric rate/burst limits
facts.value: No Authlib-operated MAU/request quota or built-in universal login/management requests-per-window contract.

facts.label: Logging and audit events
facts.value: Python logging uses authlib loggers; client token-update and server authentication/revocation signals/callbacks can feed app audit records.

facts.label: Export user profiles/passwords
facts.value: App/IdP owns user profile and credential data; Authlib has no canonical user/password table or bulk user export format/service.

facts.label: Export protocol records
facts.value: App-controlled client/code/token models and optional SQLAlchemy helpers expose identifiers, metadata, scopes, expiry/revocation timestamps and token values for operator tooling.

facts.label: Import/migration into app
facts.value: custom_code/framework tooling imports into the app's own user/client/token stores and integrates the required methods. No Authlib account/hash import wizard.

facts.label: Protocol/library migration guidance
facts.value: Docs cover Flask-OAuthlib-style client transition, httpx2 transport changes and authlib.jose to joserfc migration, including changed exception/key/config APIs.

facts.label: Account deletion/retention
facts.value: Application/IdP must delete users and associated data, invalidate sessions/tokens and apply its own backup/log retention. No built-in self-delete account endpoint.

facts.value: Polar subscription cancellation takes effect next billing cycle; billing-data retention follows Polar privacy/legal obligations rather than app-user retention.

facts.value: Self-chosen application/user/token/session infrastructure and configured external providers; no Authlib-operated identity region selector.

facts.value: Not applicable to Authlib as hosted identity processor; code runs in the user's app.

facts.label: Independent assurance
facts.value: No Authlib-specific public SOC 2/ISO certificate or independent completed security-audit report found in the checked project sources.

facts.value: Authlib; Python import/package authlib/Authlib; project repository authlib/authlib. Maintained by an individual maintainer.

facts.value: Paid checkout displays Hsiaoming Ltd; Polar Software, Inc. is the checkout merchant of record/reseller. Repository commercial license identifies an individual licensor.

facts.label: Free production software

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment

facts.label: Usage-price formula
facts.value: No paid usage tier or rounding formula applies to the Apache server; per-user/org/SSO monetary software license component is zero.

facts.label: Business baseline fit
facts.value: Native customer organizations, multi-org memberships, org-specific roles and SAML exist. Built-in invitation operation is platform enrollment, not an org-scoped existing-user join invitation.

facts.label: Organization/member limits and charges
facts.value: No per-org/member/role software license charge. A universal maximum org count or members per org was not published in the checked current guide/schema/configuration.

facts.label: Invitation scope, batch and lifetime
facts.value: Super-admin _invite_members accepts at most 100 emails per request, creates new platform users with default global roles and sends magic-link or setup-password mail. Existing addresses are skipped; all-existing input returns AlreadyExists. Invite verification record lifetime is 30 minutes.

facts.label: SSO and SCIM software fees
facts.value: Native incoming org SAML/OIDC, downstream SAML IdP/OIDC provider and per-org SCIM endpoint carry no separate upstream connection/directory software license fee.

facts.label: Builder seats, apps and environments
facts.value: No managed dashboard-seat/project/environment allowance applies to this self-hosted scope. Operator creates instances/client registrations/domains and supplies the admin secret.

facts.label: Email delivery and unavoidable configuration
facts.value: Your SMTP service sends verification, reset, magic-link, invitation and email-OTP messages. Enabling email verification requires configured SMTP host, positive port and sender address at startup.

facts.label: SMS and other providers
facts.value: SMS OTP uses your Twilio credentials/sender; social/enterprise login uses independently configured identity providers. No included SMS quota or destination rate is published by Authorizer.

facts.label: Over-limit billing versus access
facts.value: No free-to-paid transition, monetary user overage, automatic upgrade or upstream spending cap applies.

facts.label: Other billable limits
facts.value: No upstream per-request/token/audit/security-feature or transaction tariff is published for this open-source server.

facts.label: Solo and market eligibility
facts.value: Apache license grants rights to individuals/legal entities worldwide; self-hosting does not require opening a paid Authorizer production account.

facts.label: Self-service entry and trial scope
facts.value: Self-service source/binary/Docker/Kubernetes/Helm installation. No Authorizer-managed production trial, card requirement or company-domain purchase rule applies to the documented free server entry.

facts.label: Product type and account scope
facts.value: Self-hosted authentication/authorization server with local accounts, verification/recovery, sessions, social login, passkeys/MFA, organization SSO/SCIM and optional embedded OpenFGA authorization.

facts.label: Enterprise features versus paid editions
facts.value: Enterprise documentation covers organizations, SAML/OIDC and SCIM in the same Apache-2.0 server; no separate paid Enterprise plan or mandatory commercial feature license was published.

facts.label: Operator responsibilities
facts.value: Developer/operator deploys the binary/container, database, session store, DNS/TLS/proxy, SMTP/SMS integration, monitoring, backups and upgrades.

facts.label: Password login and phone identities
facts.value: built_in email/password and phone-number/password login; signup requires a password and at least email or phone. Current schema supports phone-only accounts.

facts.label: Magic link, email/SMS codes
facts.value: Native magic_link_login sends an email link valid 30 minutes. Email/SMS OTP are native MFA methods when SMTP/Twilio is configured.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet methods
facts.value: Native application guest-account creation/upgrade and crypto-wallet sign-in were not established from current docs, schema and released signup/login surfaces.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Native configured providers: Google, GitHub, Facebook, LinkedIn, Apple, Discord, Twitter, Twitch, Roblox and Microsoft.

facts.label: Email attestation and Microsoft conditions
facts.value: Provider-owned email signals are checked. Microsoft requires an explicit trusted tenant/allowed-tenant choice or xms_edov attestation where applicable; generic enterprise identities are not safely identified by email alone.

facts.label: Passkey login and MFA scope
facts.value: Native WebAuthn registration, discoverable username-less login, self-list/delete and passkey-as-MFA. Primary passwordless passkeys remain available even when MFA is disabled; admin-secret dashboard login has no passkey route.

facts.label: Passkey domain, client UX and compatibility
facts.value: Released relying-party code requires a resident credential and user verification, binds RP ID to hostname and allowed origin to scheme/host, and enforces a 60-second ceremony timeout.

facts.label: Factors, defaults and enforcement
facts.value: TOTP, email OTP, SMS OTP and passkey MFA are enabled by default, subject to provider configuration; --enforce-mfa defaults false. Users may skip the first offer; enrolled factors are subsequently required.

facts.label: Recovery codes and lockout
facts.value: TOTP enrollment issues 10 single-use recovery codes once; stored codes are SHA-256 hashes. OTP/TOTP/recovery verification shares five failed attempts per user in a 15-minute sliding window; the sixth failing attempt is blocked.

facts.label: Lost-factor administration
facts.value: lock_mfa lets a user without usable fallback lock their account; all login methods then refuse it. Admin _update_user reset_mfa clears the lock/overrides and deletes all enrolled authenticators and WebAuthn credentials.

facts.label: Email/phone verification and reset
facts.value: Native verification/resend, forgot/reset-password and phone/SMS OTP paths; email verification requires configured mail settings. Reset-password success synchronously revokes existing sessions/refresh tokens.

facts.label: Profile/email/password changes
facts.value: Authenticated update_profile changes profile/email/phone; password changes require the documented old/new confirmation flow. Current implementation clears email verification on changed address when verification is enabled and revokes sessions on email/password changes.

facts.label: End-user deletion boundary
facts.value: Documented self-service deactivate_account marks the account revoked; a native hard-delete-self flow was not established. Hard delete is a super-admin _delete_user operation.

facts.label: Session/token model and lifetimes
facts.value: HTTP-only browser session cookies plus signed JWT access/ID tokens. Released native password flow falls back to 30-minute access/ID expiry; session token lasts 24 hours; refresh defaults 2,592,000 seconds (30 days), configurable.

facts.label: Revocation and logout
facts.value: logout, refresh-token revoke, admin revoke-access and password-reset/session validation paths are available. Current introspection/session checks consult revocation state; optional OIDC back-channel logout is documented.

facts.label: Multi-device management gap
facts.value: A general end-user device/session inventory with per-device revocation UI and a universal simultaneous-session cap was not published in the checked account, token and SDK documentation.

facts.label: OIDC and downstream SAML roles
facts.value: Native OAuth2/OIDC issuer for apps and per-organization SAML 2.0 IdP for downstream SPs. SAML supports signed assertions, metadata and documented SP-/IdP-initiated modes.

facts.label: Corporate identity broker roles
facts.value: Per-org OIDC relying-party broker and SAML SP accept upstream corporate identity, JIT-provision users and add org membership. One OIDC and one SAML upstream connection per org.

facts.label: Native customer organizations and roles
facts.value: First-class organizations, many-to-many memberships and independent per-org app roles; reserved authorizer:org_admin delegates that organization’s members/SSO/SCIM/domain settings.

facts.label: Invitations and routing limits
facts.value: Native platform invitations do not take org_id or attach membership; a new user can later be added with _add_org_member, or membership arrives through SSO JIT/SCIM. Verified domains are routing hints only.

facts.label: SCIM scope and offboarding
facts.value: Native per-org SCIM v2 Users/Groups provision/update APIs, discovery and token rotation. Org derives from hashed bearer credential; user active=false and DELETE deactivate/revoke rather than hard-delete.

facts.label: SCIM group and attribute behavior
facts.value: Groups are org-scoped and memberships are FGA tuples, projected into org roles/SAML groups. Nonmember user additions are skipped; unsupported user PATCH paths/remove operations are skipped, while unsupported group paths return 400.

facts.label: Ready-made and custom screens
facts.value: Built-in /app login and /dashboard administration; React components for signup/password/social/magic link/reset/OTP/TOTP/MFA setup/passkey login/register. Headless GraphQL/REST/gRPC support custom UI.

facts.label: Branding and custom domain
facts.value: Self-host on your own domain using canonical --url plus TLS/proxy; build a custom frontend with SDKs/APIs or modify licensed UI source. No upstream per-domain/branding-unlock software fee is published.

facts.label: Passkey/domain migration
facts.value: Released WebAuthn RP ID/origin derives from the host supplied to the relying-party implementation; registered public-key credentials are origin/RP-bound.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: No official current supported-language list, translation-completeness matrix or documented localization configuration was established from current UI/SDK/configuration documentation and released file-tree searches.

facts.label: Accessibility assurance
facts.value: No scoped current WCAG conformance report, VPAT/ACR or independent accessibility assessment was found in the checked official UI, project/security and documentation evidence.

facts.label: Official web/backend integrations
facts.value: Official JS/TypeScript, React, Go, Python, Vue and Svelte integrations. JS supports browser UMD, CommonJS/ESM and Node; React supports GraphQL/REST, while Go supports native gRPC/REST/GraphQL.

facts.label: Published package versions versus stale docs
facts.value: Publisher registry: JS latest 4.0.0 (Node >=16), React latest 2.2.0 (Node >=18), Python stable 0.3.0 (Python >=3.9). Vue latest points to 1.0.0-beta.0, beta to 1.0.0-beta.2; Svelte latest 0.1.8.

facts.label: Mobile and native clients
facts.value: Official React Native Expo integration uses JS SDK plus AuthSession/WebBrowser/SecureStore and authorization code/PKCE. OIDC guide also shows generic mobile/Flutter protocol integration.

facts.label: Flutter and planned native SDKs
facts.value: Official Flutter SDK guide explicitly says the repository is a placeholder with no source/package on pub.dev; dedicated React Native, Android and iOS SDKs remain listed as planned.

facts.label: Database and service dependencies
facts.value: Documented adapters include PostgreSQL, Yugabyte/CockroachDB, MySQL/PlanetScale/MariaDB, SQLite, libSQL/Turso, SQL Server, MongoDB, ArangoDB, Cassandra/ScyllaDB, DynamoDB and Couchbase. Redis shares sessions/rate state; absent Redis uses local memory.

facts.label: SQL backend caveats
facts.value: 2.4.4 release recommends upgrades for all SQL deployments, reports 12-backend test target and says SQL Server still has two failing upsert tests outside test-all-db; PlanetScale/Yugabyte were not executed for that release.

facts.label: Build toolchain mismatch
facts.value: Getting-started/README say Go >=1.24; released 2.4.4 go.mod declares Go 1.26.6 and Docker build uses golang:1.27. Docs say Node >=18 when building web UIs.

facts.label: Deployment and persistence
facts.value: Official binary, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and platform deployment guides; persistent SQLite volume or external database, stable cryptographic keys, production TLS/proxy and shared Redis for replicated session state.

facts.label: Backups, upgrades and sizing gaps
facts.value: v1-to-v2 migration documents capturing old config, supplying flags and testing retained user data. No complete public database/files/keys recovery runbook, universal CPU/RAM minimum or MAU capacity guarantee was established.

facts.label: Custom data and token logic
facts.value: Native app_data map on user signup/profile/admin update; custom access-token script flag runs JavaScript in embedded Otto with a five-second timeout and blocks overwriting reserved security claims.

facts.label: Webhooks, signing and delivery
facts.value: Native event webhooks with custom headers, HTTP POST JSON, HMAC-SHA256 X-Authorizer-Signature keyed on client secret, and request/response/status logs. Dispatcher has a 30-second HTTP timeout and SSRF destination checks.

facts.label: User administration and API
facts.value: Built-in admin dashboard and super-admin API list/search/fetch/update/delete users, revoke/enable access, invite users, reset MFA and view audit/webhook data. Native org-admin operations are separately scoped.

facts.label: Impersonation gap
facts.value: A conventional super-admin human-user impersonation UI/API was not established in the checked schema, admin guide and released user service.

facts.label: Linking identity methods
facts.value: Social account selection/linking has a documented email-attestation/ownership contract. Enterprise OIDC identity is keyed by org/issuer/subject and rejects an existing-email collision; profile updates can add a local password to an account lacking one.

facts.label: Unlinking, merge and guest upgrade gaps
facts.value: General social-provider unlink, merging two independent existing user IDs and a data-preserving anonymous guest upgrade were not established.

facts.label: Brute-force, request and transport defenses
facts.value: Native per-IP request limits, per-user password/OTP failure counters, CSRF/origin checks, secure-cookie settings, trusted-proxy configuration, security headers and webhook SSRF protection.

facts.label: Password policy
facts.value: Released validator checks Go string byte length 6 to 36; when strong-password checking is on, also requires uppercase, lowercase, digit and a special character. Disabling strong checks retains length bounds.

facts.label: Default request quotas and responses
facts.value: Built-in per-IP default sustained 30 requests/second, burst 20. Exceeding limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 1; rate-limit-rps=0 disables it.

facts.label: Replication, outage and per-user limits
facts.value: Redis shares an atomic sliding-window rate counter across replicas; local single-node mode uses a token bucket. Redis rate-backend errors fail open by default, or return 503 when fail-closed is selected. Password and OTP counters separately limit failures per user.

facts.label: Audit and webhook history
facts.value: Native audit log has actor/action/resource/IP/user-agent/timestamps; admin paginated query filters actor/action/resource/time. Webhook logs expose delivery status/request/response and are separately queryable.

facts.label: Retention and export limits
facts.value: A universal audit/webhook retained-days default, automatic purge schedule, durable event replay/streaming guarantee and complete packaged audit export were not published in the checked API/config/security/metrics sources.

facts.label: Profile/identifier exit
facts.value: Admin _users/_user and API/SDK surfaces return profile/ID/roles/app_data. Operator controls native database records; no separate upstream export fee is imposed.

facts.label: Stored credentials and related data
facts.value: Released database schemas retain native password verifier, org memberships/federated data, encrypted TOTP secrets, hashed recovery codes and WebAuthn credential/public-key/counter data.

facts.label: Packaged export and full recovery tooling
facts.value: No documented current credential-preserving bulk export endpoint/CLI or complete native restore package was found in current APIs, released tree/schema and v1-to-v2 guidance.

facts.label: Current migration paths and hash support
facts.value: Official migration guide covers Authorizer v1 to v2 configuration/data transition. Native password signup/change/validation uses bcrypt; released user/admin API has no documented general password-hash import field.

facts.label: Proposed cross-provider tool is not shipped proof
facts.value: Official-org June 8, 2026 migration-tool document is explicitly Draft for review. It proposes authorizer-migrate, AMF, _import_users, multiple hash algorithms and lazy verification; those operations were not found in released 2.4.4 schema/tree.

facts.label: Deactivation versus deletion
facts.value: User self-deactivation writes a revoked timestamp and asynchronously cleans session state; token validation also checks deprovisioned users. Super-admin hard deletion uses user id and SQL backend transactionally removes listed user-owned rows.

facts.label: Retention and closure periods
facts.value: No universal public audit/webhook/database-backup retention or erasure deadline, or vendor subscription-closure procedure, was published for this self-hosted offer.

facts.label: Authentication data location
facts.value: Self-chosen: operator places supported database, Authorizer instances, Redis/session state, backups and logs on selected infrastructure.

facts.label: Public product privacy/processing policies
facts.value: A dedicated current Authorizer-hosted auth-data DPA/subprocessor list, product privacy policy and separate commercial subscription terms were not established through site/docs/blog/legal-path searches.

facts.label: Security/assurance scope
facts.value: Public security policy, advisories, release-test descriptions and license are available. No current independent SOC 2/ISO 27001/FIPS certificate, complete audit report or product DPA was established in checked official evidence.

facts.label: Name, stewardship and official URLs
facts.value: Authorizer; authorizerdev community project led by an individual maintainer. Official site https://www.authorizer.dev/; docs https://docs.authorizer.dev/; source https://github.com/authorizerdev/authorizer.

facts.label: Lifecycle and version sunset
facts.value: No product-wide shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the checked site, blog, repository/release and governance evidence. Security policy explicitly marks 1.x EOL; current supported major is 2.x.

facts.label: Current stable availability
facts.value: Server 2.4.4 published 2026-11-01T09:17:27Z, prerelease=false. Repository archived=false, disabled=false; last pushed November 1, 2026 at this check.

facts.label: Server license and commercial use
facts.value: Current server distribution is Apache-2.0 with no-charge commercial use, modification and redistribution subject to its license/NOTICE conditions.

facts.label: SDK component licenses
facts.value: Official JavaScript and React SDKs are MIT; Go SDK is Apache-2.0. Python SDK documentation/package metadata identify Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Status page and availability promise
facts.value: A managed production-auth uptime SLA/status page is not applicable to the documented self-hosted server.

facts.label: Release and maintenance policy
facts.value: Current stable server 2.4.4 released November 1, 2026. Security policy supports current major 2.x and previous major for six months after a new major; its table marks 1.x EOL.

facts.label: Support routes and staffing
facts.value: Community Discord/GitHub issues/discussions, maintainer/project contribution channels and private GitHub Security Advisories for vulnerabilities. Published maintainer list has one active project lead/core maintainer.

facts.label: Security response targets
facts.value: Security policy targets acknowledgment within 72 hours, triage within seven days, accepted critical/high fixes within 30 days of triage, and coordinated disclosure typically within 90 days or earlier after fix.
