facts.label: Published usage unit
facts.value: Billable API calls, billed monthly on the homepage; endpoint billing/caching rules distinguish billable and free operations.

facts.label: Additional contractual billing floor
facts.value: Terms charge the greater of API-call count or total access-record count and bill on the contracted billing cycle.

facts.label: Initial free production allowance
facts.value: First 1,000 billable calls per account are free; terms explicitly say the counter does not reset at month end.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment and payment
facts.value: Usage-based public offer; contract prices/cycle follow the Order, and default invoice payment is due within 30 days.

facts.label: Public rate versus contract fallback
facts.value: Homepage: 0.0012 USD per call, billed monthly. Public terms fallback: €0.0011 per billable call unless specified otherwise.

facts.label: Native password surcharge
facts.value: Billing docs add $0.011 for each password-based connection login request.

facts.label: Volume brackets and rounding
facts.value: No public volume-discount brackets, fractional invoice rounding method or universal negotiated rate schedule was located.

facts.label: Business comparison result
facts.value: Both fixed business scenarios can be assembled using tenants, SAML, roles/access records and invites. Exact bills depend on calls and outside delivery; conditional examples are 24 USD for A and 240 USD for B.

facts.label: Customer organization model and fees
facts.value: Application accounts are builder-owned resources; Authress tenants configure customer login/SSO and access records represent membership/roles. Homepage charges no additional configuration fee.

facts.label: Invitation behavior
facts.value: Native invite API creates a permission-grant invitation; schema expiry is seven days, and acceptance can log in the user and grant roles.

facts.label: Member and resource limits
facts.value: Public API group schema permits at most 100 users per group; a dated release increased default group/access-record quantity soft limits from 100,000 to two million.

facts.label: Organization-specific cap precision
facts.value: No separate published cap or per-active-organization/member fee for application accounts, nor a complete invitation-frequency quota, was found.

facts.label: Business SSO pricing
facts.value: Homepage advertises unlimited SSO connections and no enterprise feature tax; connection configuration has no extra published per-connection price.

facts.label: SCIM fee and scope precision
facts.value: A separate SCIM charge, connection minimum, connector edition or setup fee was not established.

facts.label: Applications, environments and domains
facts.value: Login box can serve multiple registered applications; docs recommend three separate Authress accounts for production, non-production and sandbox. Multiple simultaneous custom domains are supported.

facts.label: Builder seats and numeric project caps
facts.value: No explicit dashboard-seat, registered-application, account/environment or simultaneous-custom-domain maximum/overage schedule was located.

facts.label: Email delivery responsibility
facts.value: Custom magic-link/email-code flows use the builder's receiver/backend and chosen sender; invitation links are also delivered by the builder.

facts.label: SMS delivery and phone mapping
facts.value: Phone/SMS custom login requires the builder to map the number to an identity/email, generate/store a code mapping when needed and send the SMS through its service.

facts.label: Request limits and free-use exhaustion
facts.value: Rate-limited routes return HTTP 429; terms say exceeding an account tier can restrict requests and upgrading can remove that restriction.

facts.label: Spend visibility versus hard cap
facts.value: Homepage offers current/projected spend visibility; a customer-configurable hard dollar cap, alert threshold and exact automatic billing activation rule were not found.

facts.label: Other metered operations
facts.value: User-token mutations, user/resource permission queries and service-client public-key routes can be billable; unlisted routes are also billable under the docs.

facts.label: Stored grants and optional external charges
facts.value: Stored access-record floor and password-login premium can add costs; custom delivery and cloud audit consumers have their own service dependencies.

facts.label: Individual eligibility and countries
facts.value: A complete seller-country list and a consistent explicit sole-person production eligibility rule were not established.

facts.label: Self-service entry
facts.value: Homepage offers Try it out; documentation describes portal account/application/connection setup and SDK integration.

facts.label: Trial and signup gates
facts.value: Fixed trial days, mandatory credit card, compulsory company email and the exact payment activation gate were not found publicly.

facts.label: Hosted product scope
facts.value: Authentication, user identities, login, sessions, verification integrations, SSO federation and a separate authorization/access-record engine.

facts.label: Hosted operating responsibility
facts.value: Authress operates identity/permission infrastructure, replication, failover and service deployment; the builder operates application logic and integration.

facts.label: Local operating responsibility
facts.value: Builder runs the local container and configures local SDK endpoints; no Authress account is required for local development.

facts.label: Email/password
facts.value: PASSWORD is an explicit identity-connection type and password-based login requests have a documented premium.

facts.label: Email magic link
facts.value: Supported through custom_code plus external_service: generate a signed Authress login URL in a privileged backend and send it to the email address.

facts.label: Numeric email code and phone code
facts.value: Supported through custom_code plus external_service: builder generates a numeric code, stores its login-URL mapping and builds code entry; SMS adds phone-to-identity mapping.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No explicit native anonymous-account/guest token or crypto-wallet sign-in implementation was located.

facts.label: Named social provider integrations
facts.value: Official provider guide index lists Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft Entra/Azure AD, Salesforce, Zoho, Yahoo! and Facebook/Meta.

facts.label: Provider-specific setup and generic connections
facts.value: Google has its own client/callback setup; Apple requires Services ID/key configuration. Generic OAuth/OIDC and SAML connection setup is also documented.

facts.label: First-factor passkeys
facts.value: Built-in WebAuthn/passkey connection can be enabled in Identity Connections; first-factor passkeys were announced December 15, 2023.

facts.label: Passkey portability and recovery details
facts.value: Conditional autofill support, exact browser/native-mobile matrix, relying-party domain migration and credential export/recovery guarantees were not established.

facts.label: Authenticator and security-key factors
facts.value: Built-in TOTP and hardware/software WebAuthn keys; factors can be added to existing social/federated identities, with multiple additional keys.

facts.label: Recovery and additional MFA factors
facts.value: A complete recovery-code/lost-all-devices flow, numeric SMS/email as native second factors and exhaustive tenant MFA enforcement rules were not found.

facts.label: Email verification and identity changes
facts.value: Automatic linking requires trusted connections and verified matching email; provider email changes are refreshed on login. Link new identity then unlink old can handle identity changes.

facts.label: Password reset and native phone confirmation
facts.value: A complete native reset-password endpoint/delivery/expiry flow and native phone confirmation lifecycle were not established.

facts.label: User deletion UI versus API
facts.value: Public API provides asynchronous DELETE /v1/users/{userId}; a ready-made universal end-user delete-account screen was not located.

facts.label: JWT and session lifetimes
facts.value: Default access JWT expiry is 24 hours; default session expiry is 30 days. Tenant configuration can override expiry.

facts.label: Revocation and multiple devices
facts.value: SDK supports session listing/revocation; app configuration can disable multiple sessions. Logout deletes the session, but already issued identity JWTs are not automatically invalidated.

facts.label: Business protocol direction
facts.value: Authress accepts SAML2 and OIDC/OAuth identity connections and issues signed OpenID-compatible JWTs; API schema also supports application user delegation to third-party SAML/OpenID services.

facts.label: Customer account membership and roles
facts.value: Access records assign users/groups roles over account resources such as Accounts/{id}; one user can be authorized for multiple accounts.

facts.label: Customer admin and onboarding UI
facts.value: Invites and customer-managed SSO can be built using native APIs; builder supplies the forms, backend permission checks and business-account creation.

facts.label: SCIM completeness
facts.value: Overview advertises SCIM identity-provider synchronization; public SCIM version, user/group schema, connector setup and deactivation-to-session behavior were not established.

facts.label: Hosted login and user configuration
facts.value: Automatically configured hosted login box; LoginClient can open hosted user configuration/security-key screens. Custom login pages can call the SDK.

facts.label: Theme and custom login presentation
facts.value: Portal controls brand styles, support links and displayed identity connections; more complex onboarding can use a builder-hosted login page.

facts.label: Custom domains and migration
facts.value: Multiple simultaneous owned custom domains are supported for API access and generated-token issuers.

facts.label: Managed login locales
facts.value: Published list has 31 locale codes: af, bn, da, de, de-AT, de-DE, de-CH, en, en-AU, en-CA, en-GB, en-US, es, es-AR, es-CL, es-MX, es-ES, fr, fr-BE, fr-CA, fr-FR, fr-CH, it, it-IT, it-CH, ja-JP, pl-PL, pt, pt-BR, pt-PT, uk-UA.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No scoped WCAG conformance statement, VPAT or independently assessed accessibility report was located.

facts.label: Official API SDKs and infrastructure integrations
facts.value: SDK index lists C#/.NET, Go, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Terraform, OpenTofu, Amplify AppSync and Postman.

facts.label: Browser and framework integration
facts.value: Official @authress/login JavaScript/TypeScript browser client; official authentication docs link React and Vue starter kits.

facts.label: Current JavaScript runtime metadata
facts.value: @authress/login 2.6.480 declares Node >=20; @authress/sdk 3.2.289 declares Node >=22.

facts.label: Official React Native client
facts.value: Authress-owned login-react-native client documents iOS/Android browser/deep-link login, encrypted storage and device/identity helpers.

facts.label: Flutter and other native clients
facts.value: SDK community page identifies a FlyingDarts Flutter community integration. Separate first-party Swift/native-Android login SDK coverage was not established.

facts.label: App, credentials and data prerequisites
facts.value: Hosted integration needs an Authress account, registered application/connection, allowed redirects and client configuration; builder supplies its application/business database and backend where custom flows require it.

facts.label: Optional dependencies and cost ownership
facts.value: External identity-provider registration, email/SMS delivery and audit-stream destinations are builder-configured where used. Permission caching can reduce calls.

facts.label: Authress Local deployment
facts.value: Development container documented for Docker/Podman/Nomad, exposing local service on port 8888 and allowing test identity tokens.

facts.label: Production self-host operations
facts.value: Production-hardened self-host instructions, supported database versions, sizing, HA backup/restore and long-term upgrade policy were not established for Authress Local.

facts.label: Custom login and claims
facts.value: Custom service-client assertions/login flows and user token-configuration APIs are available; public schema gives token defaultClaims a 1,024-byte maximum.

facts.label: Events and step-up extension
facts.value: Auth/audit events can trigger external logic. Step-up authorization documentation is labelled Beta and requires support enablement.

facts.label: User query and management API
facts.value: Public API has paginated user listing, user lookup/deletion, linked identities, devices, tenants, groups, roles and access-record operations.

facts.label: Banning, impersonation and admin precision
facts.value: A universal ban/unban operation, support-user impersonation flow and its safeguards were not established.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking
facts.value: Explicit identity linking authenticates the additional provider and preserves the chosen Authress user ID; unlinking is supported and cannot remove the last identity.

facts.label: Automatic linking
facts.value: Matching email can automatically link only when both connections enable Automatic Linking and both supply email_verified:true.

facts.label: Anonymous-to-registered upgrade
facts.value: No documented anonymous-user upgrade/preserved-ID lifecycle was found.

facts.label: Session abuse protections
facts.value: Rotating session credentials, reuse/compromise detection and device-bound protection are described; MFA and endpoint throttling add controls.

facts.label: Bot, breached-password and SMS controls
facts.value: No complete native CAPTCHA/bot configuration, breached-password check, failed-attempt lockout schedule or built-in SMS spend/fraud controls was located.

facts.label: Rate-limit tiers
facts.value: Special: one call/hour per resource; Portal: one/minute; Tier 1: one/second; Tier 2: approximately 100/second; Tier 3 is labelled Unlimited but has an account-configured default 1,000 RPS ceiling.

facts.label: Endpoint routing and recovery
facts.value: Authentication/session routes and permission authorization checks use Tier 3; GET users uses Tier 1; individual user lookup uses Tier 2. Exceeded limits return 429.

facts.label: Audit event access and export
facts.value: Portal audit dashboard shows recent requests/results and aggregates; AWS EventBridge and GCP Pub/Sub integration exposes AccessChanged, AuthorizationRequest and UserLogin events.

facts.label: Event delivery and retention precision
facts.value: EventBridge can duplicate events, and consumers should deduplicate by eventId. Exact portal retention days, replay window, maximum retry age and audit destination costs were not established.

facts.label: Profile and authorization export primitives
facts.value: Paginated user/profile APIs and roles/groups/access-record APIs expose retrievable JSON data; hosted downtime guide mentions configuration export tools/support.

facts.label: Credential and full exit portability
facts.value: Password-hash and WebAuthn private/credential export, a complete stable account-link archive, guaranteed export fee and turnkey provider migration format were not established.

facts.label: Federation-first migration
facts.value: Connect existing IdP, optionally reuse its provider sub during migration, verify the new Authress-issued tokens, add direct providers and link user identities.

facts.label: Remaining user and password import precision
facts.value: Remaining unlinked-user migration is support-assisted; no supported hash algorithm list, public bulk-hash import, lazy password validation endpoint or guaranteed no-reset migration was located.

facts.label: User deletion and retained authorization data
facts.value: User DELETE is asynchronous. Privacy says login/identity data is deleted 30 days after the respective deletion API is called; authorization data/internal user IDs persist while the customer account exists.

facts.label: Vendor-account closure and retention
facts.value: Privacy directs account deactivation through support@authress.io; user data is deleted 30 days after confirmed deactivation and is not recoverable afterwards.

facts.label: Backup and log deletion precision
facts.value: Exact hosted backup purge times, legal-hold exceptions and audit event-by-event retention/deletion windows were not found.

facts.label: Residency controls and data split
facts.value: Per identity connection, profile data can be restricted/encrypted in a chosen region. Secure identity data including user/session IDs and audit data is globally replicated; users are otherwise replicated globally by default.

facts.label: Published residency country choices
facts.value: Public identity-connection schema lists ZAF, HKG, IND, JPN, KOR, SGP, AUS, IDN, CAN, DEU, CHE, SWE, ITA, IRL, GBR, FRA, ISR, BHR, ARE, BRA and USA.

facts.label: Policy location and transfer scope
facts.value: Privacy describes customer-selected storage/within-region replication, but also EU hosting, Swiss operations and authorized transfers to the US/other operating countries.

facts.label: Personal-data and ownership wording
facts.value: Homepage claims GDPR-compliant processing; terms restrict GDPR/regulated data yet separately protect expressly defined User Profile Data and describe it as Authress-owned. Privacy states customer ownership of user data.

facts.label: Public assurance documents and subprocessors
facts.value: No public DPA, complete named subprocessor roster, scoped SOC 2 report or ISO 27001 certificate was located. Privacy names hosting/storage/infrastructure and communication/support supplier categories.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Authress; public hosted identity and permission service. Terms identify Rhosys AG; homepage footer names Winterthur, Switzerland.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Public start/setup routes and current documentation are available. Login SDK 2.6.480 and API SDK 3.2.289 have 2026 publications.

facts.label: Hosted platform commercial rules
facts.value: Proprietary subscription/service agreement; customer may use the service under its Order and restrictions.

facts.label: JavaScript login SDK license
facts.value: Apache-2.0 for Authress/authress-login.js and @authress/login.

facts.label: Local development server license
facts.value: Authress Local source carries GNU AGPL v3.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Official status page covers authorization, login/authentication, management portal, knowledge base and starter/demo components.

facts.label: SLA figures and scope
facts.value: Homepage promises 99.995% for default regions; billing docs describe 99.999 for non-list Tier 2 & 5 and 99.99 for other/list operations.

facts.label: Current package publication evidence
facts.value: @authress/login 2.6.480 published 2026-09-03T12:23:18.904Z; @authress/sdk 3.2.289 published 2026-09-26T20:35:00.364Z.

facts.label: Support window and local version precision
facts.value: No universal SDK LTS/security-fix duration or production-supported Authress Local version policy was located.

facts.label: Support routes and advertised response
facts.value: Homepage offers email/Discord and developer-support response within 24h for all customer sizes; migration/local docs also direct users to support/community.

facts.label: Coverage and escalation precision
facts.value: Support timezone, staffed hours, calendar versus business-day interpretation, emergency escalation and dedicated architecture-support pricing were not established.

facts.value: Exact direct-plan minimum fee and currency code not published in the checked pricing/legal pages.

facts.label: Marketplace monthly edition
facts.value: Vendor-linked AWS Marketplace offer: one-month Enterprise license for 100,000 MAUs, $5,000.00/month, includes passkeys.

facts.label: Taxes and termination terms
facts.value: Direct terms exclude GST; general termination notice is at least 90 days, subject to any minimum initial term; prepaid fees are non-refundable on termination.

facts.label: Direct usage schedule
facts.value: Professional described for up to 20,000 MAUs, advertised from $0.05/MAU/month; Enterprise 20,000+ with custom volume prices and annual commitment.

facts.label: Core verification and add-on pricing
facts.value: Core platform says no per-verification charges; Enterprise-only specialized add-ons are separately available, without public rate cards.

facts.label: Business baseline applicability
facts.value: Public materials do not establish an Authsignal-only configuration supplying customer memberships/invitations/roles plus one or ten customer SAML connections.

facts.label: Customer organization limits and fees
facts.value: Included customer organizations, members per customer organization, invitation limits and organization-specific fees not published in the checked app-auth documentation.

facts.label: Business SSO and provisioning charges
facts.value: No public price or included connection count for app-customer SAML/SCIM directories found. Portal SAML is documented separately, without a standalone price in its guide.

facts.label: Developer team access
facts.value: Admin, Support analyst and Read only roles; organization role with per-tenant overrides or No access; email invitation and deactivate/reactivate supported.

facts.label: Developer seat, tenant and app caps
facts.value: Included builder-seat, tenant/app-client counts and related overage fees not published.

facts.label: Environment isolation
facts.value: Create distinct tenants for separate environments/brands; app clients have separate token durations and audience IDs; Terraform can promote configuration between tenants.

facts.label: Email delivery dependencies
facts.value: Email OTP/magic link providers: Bird, Mailjet, Mailgun, Mandrill, SendGrid, custom SMTP or delivery webhook; Authsignal’s own sender is offered for development.

facts.label: SMS delivery dependencies
facts.value: SMS provider setup supports Bird, Twilio, MessageMedia, TNZ, Modica Group and webhook delivery.

facts.label: WhatsApp, push and specialized channels
facts.value: WhatsApp requires a configured provider and is an Enterprise feature in pricing; push can use a webhook for the customer’s mobile-app notifications.

facts.label: MAU overflow and trial expiry
facts.value: Exact usage-overage behavior, spending cap, trial-expiry grace and auto-upgrade/suspension thresholds not published in checked pricing/legal/setup pages.

facts.label: Authentication throttling behavior
facts.value: Sending/country limits block requests with HTTP 429; code-submission limits return isVerified=false and MAX_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED.

facts.label: Compulsory and optional extra charges
facts.value: Enterprise add-on rates, message rates and core plan minimum are unpublished; direct annual commitment and external identity/app infrastructure must be included separately.

facts.label: Individual/commercial eligibility
facts.value: Terms recognize an individual or entity and acquisition for trade; privacy policy defines customer as company, organization or person.

facts.label: Builder-country restrictions
facts.value: Complete supported/restricted billing-country or builder-country list not found.

facts.label: Trial entry
facts.value: Self-service account signup advertised; 30 days, full platform access, no credit card; production-ready configuration and real-environment proof of concept allowed.

facts.label: Paid production route
facts.value: Professional/Enterprise direct offers require an annual commitment; pricing asks for requirements/MAU volume and states a minimum. Enterprise also purchasable via AWS Marketplace.

facts.label: Product scope
facts.value: Hosted authentication/orchestration layer for an existing app/identity stack: passkeys, passwordless methods, MFA, step-up, risk rules, user/authenticator records and optional access/refresh-token sessions.

facts.label: Account-system boundary
facts.value: Passwordless action guide first looks up the user in the app database or external IdP; Authsignal user records are automatically created when an action is tracked with that app’s userId.

facts.label: Operator responsibilities
facts.value: Authsignal operates the hosted API, UI, auth records, encryption and continuous backups on AWS; customer runs its app/backend and retains responsibility for uploaded-data backups.

facts.label: Email passwordless methods
facts.value: Email OTP and email magic links support primary passwordless authentication and verification; Professional core methods plus trial/Enterprise.

facts.label: Phone authentication
facts.value: SMS OTP supports primary sign-in or adaptive MFA; WhatsApp OTP is separately configured and listed as Enterprise in pricing.

facts.label: Passwords, anonymous users and wallets
facts.value: Native password validation/reset, managed anonymous accounts and wallet-login methods not established in the checked method/API catalogue.

facts.label: Social-provider support
facts.value: No native Google/Apple/GitHub/Microsoft social-connection catalogue found; Authsignal integrates alongside the existing identity provider.

facts.label: Passkey availability and first factor
facts.value: Professional includes FIDO2-certified passkey server; custom web/native SDKs and hosted UI support enrollment, primary sign-in and step-up.

facts.label: Web autofill and origins
facts.value: Web SDK supports passkey signIn with autofill=true; configured primary domain must match the app domain, with expected origins for subdomains.

facts.label: Mobile association requirements
facts.value: Native passkeys use the matching web relying-party domain; iOS webcredentials association and Android assetlinks.json plus app SHA-256 expected origin required.

facts.label: Passkey recovery and device limitations
facts.value: Guides recommend another enrolled method such as email/SMS and support multiple authenticators; app handles unavailable/cancelled passkey prompts.

facts.label: MFA and adaptive policy
facts.value: Professional includes passkeys, email/SMS OTP, TOTP, push and no-code risk rules; rules can require challenges for sensitive actions or new/risky devices.

facts.label: Recovery through support and alternate factors
facts.value: Admin/Support analyst can remove lost authenticators after independently verifying the user; hosted UI prevents removing the final remaining authenticator.

facts.label: Backup recovery codes
facts.value: Managed recovery-code generation, count, storage, regeneration and redemption procedure not found in the relevant public guides/API index.

facts.label: Email/phone verification
facts.value: OTP/magic-link enrollment verifies contact ownership; programmatic enrollment bypasses that check and requires the customer to have verified the contact already.

facts.label: Changing authentication methods
facts.value: Hosted settings let an already challenged user add/remove methods; enrollment tokens authorize additional authenticators only from a strongly authenticated context.

facts.label: Password reset and user-initiated deletion UI
facts.value: Native password-reset flow or a full ready-made end-user delete-account screen not published in the checked materials.

facts.label: Optional managed sessions
facts.value: Enable tenant JWKS, create app clients with separate access/refresh lifetimes; exchange a successful challenge client token for access and refresh tokens.

facts.label: Refresh and revocation
facts.value: Refresh tokens are single-use; refresh returns replacements and revokes previously issued tokens. Revoke one session or all user sessions; SDK validation checks revocation as well as signature.

facts.label: Challenge tokens versus app sessions
facts.value: FAQ gives a configurable ten-minute default for OTP/magic-link challenge tokens; app session token durations are configured separately per client.

facts.label: OIDC provider role
facts.value: Authsignal acts as an OIDC provider for passwordless/MFA challenges, including Azure AD B2C custom policies; init-auth first scopes the request to an already identified userId.

facts.label: SAML role and audience
facts.value: SAML 2.0 SP for Authsignal Admin Portal login to the developer’s existing IdP.

facts.label: App-customer SAML/OIDC broker role
facts.value: Native incoming customer SAML connection management or a full enterprise SSO broker catalogue for app users not found.

facts.label: Customer organization membership and authorization
facts.value: No native app-customer organization membership/invitation/role-permission model established.

facts.label: SCIM account synchronization
facts.value: Public SCIM version, user/group endpoints, directory configuration, deactivation semantics and price not found.

facts.label: Hosted and custom UI
facts.value: Hosted challenge/enrollment page via redirect or iframe modal; custom UI through Web/Mobile SDKs; React UI components available.

facts.label: Authenticator settings screens
facts.value: Hosted self-service settings after verification allow viewing, adding and removing enrolled methods; last remaining method cannot be removed.

facts.label: React component restriction
facts.value: Official React SDK currently supports re-authentication flows only.

facts.label: Branding and domains by plan
facts.value: Professional includes branded screens and custom domains; theme editor customizes colors, borders, alignment, text and hosted custom fonts.

facts.label: Multiple and API domains
facts.value: Multiple hosted-UI domains require Enterprise and support enablement; a branded Client API domain also requires support and DNS validation.

facts.label: Supported hosted UI locales
facts.value: English en; French fr; Canadian French fr-ca; German de; Spanish es; Italian it; Dutch nl; Polish pl; Brazilian Portuguese pt-br.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Pricing claims screen-reader and keyboard-accessible interfaces; public WCAG conformance level, VPAT or independent audit report not established.

facts.label: Server runtimes
facts.value: Official Server SDKs: Node.js, C#, Java, Ruby, Python, PHP and Go; regional REST API also available.

facts.label: Web frameworks and official packages
facts.value: Browser Web SDK plus React component SDK; official NextAuth.js/Next.js integration guide uses the app’s existing NextAuth account/session model.

facts.label: Runtime/version matrix
facts.value: Exact supported Node/server-runtime versions and an edge-runtime compatibility guarantee not published in checked SDK setup/package metadata.

facts.label: Native and cross-platform SDKs
facts.value: Official Swift/iOS, Kotlin/Android, React Native, Flutter and .NET MAUI SDKs.

facts.label: Documented mobile requirements
facts.value: iOS passkeys 15+, autofill 16+; Android 6/API 23+, Java 17; React Native 0.73+ recommended with Java 17/AGP 8+; MAUI .NET 10 with iOS 15+/Android API 23+.

facts.label: Required app/services
facts.value: Own application/backend and user lookup or IdP; Authsignal tenant credentials; email/SMS provider configuration for delivery; mobile app and optional notification infrastructure for push.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented hosted Authsignal service; SDKs/REST clients call vendor-operated regional APIs.

facts.label: Custom decisions and data
facts.value: No-code classic rules target risk signals, user/action custom attributes and business context; Enterprise adds the branching Flows builder and Terraform configuration management.

facts.label: Webhook events and signature checks
facts.value: Challenge-delivery, authenticator lifecycle, action.verify and action/challenge log events; SDK checks raw body and X-Signature-V2, with five-minute replay tolerance by default.

facts.label: Synchronous webhook failure behavior
facts.value: A non-2xx challenge-delivery response fails the challenge; action.verify non-2xx/timeout blocks transition to CHALLENGE_SUCCEEDED and is not automatically retried.

facts.label: Background event reliability
facts.value: Authenticator-event delivery: three total attempts, at least 30 seconds apart; log events batched up to 500 after challenge-token duration and failed batches periodically retried until success.

facts.label: Webhook retry-count discrepancy
facts.value: Event-type guide says authenticator events have up to three retries; delivery guide says three attempts in total.

facts.label: Arbitrary hosted code and execution quota
facts.value: No public arbitrary-code hook runtime, execution-time limit or complete rule/flow/webhook quota/pricing schedule found.

facts.label: User CRUD and search
facts.value: Track action with unique userId auto-creates auth record; get/update/delete through Server SDK/API; query filters include username, email, phoneNumber and token with lastEvaluatedUserId pagination.

facts.label: Support administration
facts.value: Portal searches by email/user ID and exposes methods and recent actions; Admin/Support analyst can reset authenticators and invalidate devices.

facts.label: Ban and impersonation APIs
facts.value: Dedicated full-account ban/impersonation mechanism and its audit/approval controls not established in checked user APIs and administration guides.

facts.label: Multiple factors on one identity
facts.value: Bind multiple authenticators to the same userId, requiring existing-factor verification or a strongly authenticated enrollment token.

facts.label: Cross-account linking and guest upgrade
facts.value: Cross-userId merge/unmerge, social-account linking and managed guest-to-registered upgrade procedure not found.

facts.label: Abuse and risk rules
facts.value: Configurable OTP sending/submission/country throttles; no-code rules use IP/device/user risk, new devices, known bots, anonymous IP and travel signals.

facts.label: SMS pumping protection
facts.value: Optional per-country or number-group SMS quotas; no default country limit. Verified-code sends are removed from the country count.

facts.label: CAPTCHA and breached-password checks
facts.value: Native CAPTCHA integration/defaults and leaked-password screening service not established in the checked auth-method, risk and pricing docs.

facts.label: Default send throttles
facts.value: Rolling windows: SMS/WhatsApp 6 sends per 10 minutes, five-second cooldown; Email OTP/magic links 12 per 10 minutes, ten-second cooldown; push 6 per 10 minutes without default cooldown.

facts.label: Default code-submission throttles
facts.value: SMS/WhatsApp/email OTP/TOTP: 10 submissions per five minutes; every submitted code counts, even correct ones; counts are per user/authenticator in a flow.

facts.label: Configurable throttle ranges
facts.value: Sending limits: 1 to 100 sends/window, up to six limits/authenticator; country limits: 1 to 1,000, up to five limits; submission: one limit, 1 to 100 attempts/window.

facts.label: Aggregate API request capacity
facts.value: Universal core API requests/second, concurrency allowance, plan-specific throughput and capacity-overage price not published.

facts.label: Audit and activity access
facts.value: Portal displays user/actions timeline and configuration/team audit activity; action.log_created and challenge.log_created deliver audit snapshots in background batches.

facts.label: Audit retention and export fees
facts.value: Exact per-plan activity/audit/webhook-history retention, export-volume allowance and log-shipping price not published.

facts.label: Profile extraction
facts.value: GET /users supports filtered/paginated JSON profile records; get-user/authenticator APIs expose contact, enrollment and credential metadata.

facts.label: Contractual exit copy
facts.value: Request a data copy any time before one month after termination; vendor provides common electronic format and can charge reasonable costs; no software compatibility warranty.

facts.label: Credential export and passkey portability
facts.value: Public get-authenticators schema exposes passkey credential ID/AAGUID/device metadata but does not include credentialPublicKey; complete public-key/TOTP-secret/relationship export process and fee not established.

facts.label: Keep current users and identifiers
facts.value: Use the existing app/IdP userId when tracking actions; no wholesale primary-user migration required for the add-on model.

facts.label: Verified contact and passkey import
facts.value: Programmatic enrollment supports verified email OTP, email magic link, SMS and PASSKEY; passkeys require credentialId plus credentialPublicKey.

facts.label: Bulk passkey migration
facts.value: Batch enrollment endpoint accepts at most 1,000 authenticator items per request; current schema verificationMethod is PASSKEY; requires userId, credentialId and base64url credentialPublicKey.

facts.label: Password hash and TOTP-secret migration
facts.value: Supported password-hash algorithm import or TOTP shared-secret import contract not published in checked programmatic guides/API catalogue.

facts.label: Delete auth user
facts.value: Server Delete User permanently removes user, authenticators, action history and associated session data; asynchronous and may take a few minutes.

facts.label: Published privacy retention
facts.value: Privacy policy says conversation/personal data may be kept up to six years unless account deleted, then not longer than 60 days; other clauses allow legal/regulatory retention and describe difficult-to-erase backups.

facts.label: Account closure and backup erasure detail
facts.value: Terms provide requested deletion with reasonable prompt efforts; fixed per-user backup expiry, exact operational-log retention and automatic vendor-account closure procedure not published.

facts.label: Documented API regions
facts.value: US Oregon; AU Sydney; EU Ireland; CA Montreal; UK London, with separate regional base URLs.

facts.label: Data and backup location scope
facts.value: Terms allow storage in US/EU/Australia and access from those plus New Zealand; security says AWS database backups replicate to a separate AWS region.

facts.label: Residency price and all-data guarantee
facts.value: Exact region-selection fees, backup-region pairs, log/support location matrix and all-plan country-specific residency guarantee not published.

facts.label: Assurance claims and dates
facts.value: Security policy updated 2026-08-31 claims SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 valid through 2029, and FIDO2 Server certification.

facts.label: Audit reports and security controls
facts.value: SOC 2 report available by contacting support; vendor describes TLS 1.2+, KMS-encrypted database, continuous point-in-time backups, review/testing and 24/7 engineering on-call.

facts.label: DPA and BAA evidence
facts.value: Privacy policy offers a DPA for EU/Swiss data processing by contacting vendor; pricing advertises negotiated Enterprise DPA/BAA and compliance due diligence.

facts.label: Subprocessor register
facts.value: Security names AWS hosting and Stripe payments, but a complete public dated subprocessor list, processing countries and change-notice contract not found.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Authsignal; Authsignal Ltd, New Zealand; official website authsignal.com and docs.authsignal.com.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Current 30-day trial and paid production offers; product and SDK changelogs contain October 2026 updates; no whole-service shutdown/sunset/acquisition notice found.

facts.label: Recent API service incident
facts.value: The status page reports that a portion of US-region API requests returned errors between 19:45 and 23:00 UTC on October 29, 2026; service was restored.

facts.label: Hosted platform rights
facts.value: Proprietary SaaS under public terms; vendor retains service/software intellectual property; customer retains its Data.

facts.label: Checked SDK license
facts.value: Official @authsignal/node SDK: MIT, allowing commercial use, modification and redistribution with the notice/disclaimer retained.

facts.label: Public status evidence
facts.value: Public status page lists regional APIs and portal; the Oct 29 incident report says some US API requests returned errors from 19:45 to 23:00 UTC, then service was restored.

facts.label: Uptime and support SLA
facts.value: Enterprise offers negotiated SLAs; public numeric uptime percentage, measurement period, credit schedule and claim procedure not found.

facts.label: Current maintenance evidence
facts.value: Official product and SDK/API changelogs contain October 2026 changes, including rate controls, last-passkey protection and SDK fixes.

facts.value: Main package @authsignal/node is 3.2.3; GitHub release v3.2.3 published 2026-09-30T02:48:11Z and marked prerelease; newest non-prerelease in fetched release list is v3.0.1 dated 2026-08-17T23:09:26Z.

facts.label: Supported-version/security lifecycle
facts.value: Complete supported-major matrix, SDK/private-server end-of-support dates and fixed vulnerability-patch deadlines not published in checked release/security/docs pages.
