facts.label: Billing unit and scope
facts.value: Per-app backend subscription plus monthly API requests, database storage, file storage and transfer. Auth logins count as requests; dashboard class loading/Admin App operations also consume requests.

facts.label: Monthly counting definition
facts.value: Help center describes the monthly sum of requests, with transactions, queries, Cloud Function calls, HTTP and push requests; its example describes a 30-day period.

facts.label: Free allowances
facts.value: Free: 25,000 requests/month, 250 MB database, 1 GB transfer, 1 GB files, one app per subscription and one Cloud Code job. Up to five Free projects per account.

facts.label: Free production scope
facts.value: No explicit production prohibition found in current service terms; Free pricing is described as prototyping/experimentation, not a contractual production SLA. Verification mail and security-setting gates still apply.

facts.label: Monthly base — MVP
facts.value: US$25 per app/month, monthly billing; includes 500,000 requests, 1 GB database, 250 GB transfer and 50 GB files.

facts.label: Monthly base — Pay As You Go
facts.value: US$100 per app/month, monthly billing; includes 5 million requests, 3 GB database, 1 TB transfer and 250 GB files.

facts.label: Monthly base — Dedicated and Enterprise
facts.value: Dedicated US$500 per app/month, monthly billing; Enterprise/custom infrastructure and SLAs are contact-sales.

facts.label: Annual billing — MVP
facts.value: US$15/app/month equivalent, billed annually. Fees exclude taxes unless stated otherwise.

facts.label: Annual billing — Pay As You Go
facts.value: US$80/app/month equivalent, billed annually. Fees exclude taxes unless stated otherwise.

facts.label: Annual billing — Dedicated
facts.value: US$400/app/month equivalent, billed annually. Fees exclude taxes unless stated otherwise.

facts.label: Request overages
facts.value: MVP: US$5 per extra 100,000 requests. Pay As You Go: US$2 per extra 100,000 requests.

facts.label: Storage and transfer overages
facts.value: Extra database: US$15/month per GB; extra files: US$1 per 10 GB; extra transfer: US$0.10 per GB.

facts.label: Business scenarios
facts.value: The fixed SAML business baselines have no verified ready-made Back4app Backend package. Customer organizations/invitations and SAML integration require app code and an external identity service.

facts.label: Customer organizations and member limits
facts.value: Customer workspaces, memberships and invitations are custom application data/workflows. No packaged org/member/invitation quota or per-org rate was found in the backend auth offer and pricing.

facts.label: SSO and SCIM fees
facts.value: Custom-adapter enterprise SSO is advertised, but no SAML/OIDC connection allowance, connection fee, SCIM tier or setup tariff is published on the checked pricing/auth/integration pages.

facts.label: Builder collaborators — Free
facts.value: No collaborators included.

facts.label: Builder collaborators — MVP
facts.value: Up to 3 collaborators; Owner and custom Collaborator roles.

facts.label: Builder collaborators — Pay As You Go
facts.value: Up to 7 collaborators; Owner and custom Collaborator roles.

facts.label: Builder collaborators — Dedicated
facts.value: Up to 20 collaborators; Owner and custom Collaborator roles.

facts.label: Apps and environments
facts.value: One app per backend subscription; Free account can have up to five projects. Core Settings can clone an app/database; version docs advise testing upgrades in a development app.

facts.label: Built-in email and sender gate
facts.value: Hosted verification/reset flows exist. Verification requires enabled settings and, per recent vendor testing, a validated account card; password-reset email was available without that gate.

facts.label: Own email provider
facts.value: SendGrid/Mailgun integration is documented. SendGrid route uses a separate email-adapter npm module and support-assisted provider/template configuration.

facts.label: Mail allowance and OTP costs
facts.value: No exact included hosted verification/reset send quota or overage tariff found in pricing/email docs. SMS/email OTP tutorial requires Twilio Verify; email OTP also uses SendGrid.

facts.label: Monthly-limit behavior
facts.value: Terms distinguish prepaid access stopping at its limits, postpaid usage charges and a general overage-invoicing clause; pricing advertises MVP/PAYG request overages.

facts.label: Rate-limit recovery and spend controls
facts.value: Help center says excess requests are dropped until the app's trailing one-minute request average falls below its limit. No current hard dollar cap or guaranteed overage-alert/grace-period rule found in pricing/terms.

facts.label: Other paid features
facts.value: Dedicated point-in-time restore add-on US$100/month; custom infrastructure, professional services and custom agreements are contact-sales. Request/storage/transfer costs also cover non-auth backend activity.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Service-account holder must be at least 18, legally capable of contracting and not barred by applicable law; acting for a company requires authority to bind it.

facts.label: Country eligibility
facts.value: No complete accepted/restricted-country signup or payment matrix found in current terms, privacy notice or backend pricing.

facts.label: Self-service and card gate
facts.value: Free backend app creation is self-service; pricing says no card required to start. Vendor's Sep 2026 auth guide says email verification requires a validated card, while password-reset email does not.

facts.label: Product type and auth scope
facts.value: Hosted backend-as-a-service with accounts, password/social login, anonymous users, sessions, verification/reset, roles and permissions; custom Cloud Code/adapters extend it.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Back4app provisions the backend/database/APIs and runs Cloud Code infrastructure. Builder configures access rules, frontend, integrations and app security; contract leaves backup/protection responsibilities with the customer too.

facts.label: Password and anonymous login
facts.value: Built-in username/email-password and anonymous guest accounts; registration/login use Parse.User and create a session.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: Custom-code pattern: requestMagicLink creates/stores/emails a short-expiry single-use token; redeemMagicLink verifies it and returns a session for SDK adoption.

facts.label: Email/phone code login
facts.value: Official tutorial implements SMS/email OTP login through custom Cloud Functions and Twilio Verify; email sending also needs SendGrid.

facts.label: Wallet login
facts.value: No documented hosted wallet-signature login flow, named wallet adapter or applicable plan found in auth, passwordless and current adapter material.

facts.label: Social providers documented for hosted apps
facts.value: Google, Apple, Facebook, Twitter/X and VK are listed in the vendor's Oct 2026 dashboard/implementation note. Google/Apple have platform-specific tutorials.

facts.label: GitHub and automatic linking claims
facts.value: Auth marketing lists GitHub and automatic linking of existing users; the newer vendor engineering article reports GitHub not configured on its hosted test app and requires explicit signed-in linking instead of email-based merging.

facts.label: Passkey implementation path
facts.value: Vendor describes plugging an external passkey provider into custom auth adapters/authData. This is an integration/custom-code path, not a verified packaged Back4app WebAuthn flow.

facts.label: Passkey compatibility and gates
facts.value: No hosted passkey browser/native matrix, autofill contract, relying-party-domain migration guide, recovery implementation or dedicated fee found in those sources.

facts.label: Administrator MFA
facts.value: Back4app account MFA is documented using Google Authenticator and a six-digit code during dashboard login.

facts.label: App-user MFA — upstream versus hosted
facts.value: Documented Parse 7.5.2 source includes a configurable mfa adapter with TOTP/SMS and recovery material. Managed-service enablement, minimum plan and a full customer-user enforcement/recovery workflow are not established by Back4app's MFA guide.

facts.label: App-user OTP and recovery boundary
facts.value: SMS/email OTP through Twilio Verify is a documented custom integration. No verified turnkey lost-all-factors flow or hosted recovery-code policy was found.

facts.label: Email verification and address changes
facts.value: Enabling verification adds emailVerified; setting/changing email resets it false and sends a confirmation link. Custom options expose verification-token duration.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Built-in email reset with a hosted choose-password form; React tutorial shows a custom request screen and template settings.

facts.label: Phone verification and account deletion
facts.value: Phone validation is through the Twilio Verify custom integration. User deletion is Parse DELETE /users/:objectId with authenticated permissions; app must supply the user-facing control.

facts.label: Session model and expiry
facts.value: Server-side _Session records; tokens are supplied on subsequent API calls. Back4app custom-options doc says sessionLength defaults to one year in seconds and expireInactiveSessions defaults true.

facts.label: Revocation and multiple devices
facts.value: Logout deletes the calling session. Other devices remain signed in; a custom signOutEverywhere function can remove the user's other _Session rows.

facts.label: Password changes and refresh boundary
facts.value: Vendor's hosted run reports setting/changing password through a session revoked prior sessions and returned a new token. Revocable expiry returns invalid-session error 209.

facts.label: Enterprise standards and protocol role
facts.value: Enterprise SSO is a custom-adapter/external-identity-service composition. No packaged native SAML SP, OIDC provider server or SCIM endpoint is established for the managed offer.

facts.label: Roles and authorization
facts.value: Built-in hierarchical roles, object ACLs, class-level permissions and protected fields; app code can implement org-level rules.

facts.label: Organizations and invitations
facts.value: Customer organizations, memberships, invitation expiry, org admins and account switching require custom app models/workflows or an external service.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: No managed SCIM version, user/group sync contract, deactivation behavior or priced SCIM add-on found in pricing, auth offer, SaaS integration requirements or adapter registry checked.

facts.label: End-user screens
facts.value: Builder-created login/signup/profile interfaces using SDKs; official React and Flutter examples provide source/templates. Hosted password-reset/email-action pages are available.

facts.label: Branding and template gates
facts.value: Editable email templates and custom Parse options: included from MVP; Free excluded in pricing. Custom action-page HTML and URLs can be configured.

facts.label: Custom domains and SSL plan gate
facts.value: Custom Domain and SSL Certificate feature rows are included on Pay As You Go and Dedicated; excluded on Free/MVP. Published custom-domain hosting uses CNAME to the app's b4a.app subdomain.

facts.label: Email localization
facts.value: Help article documents parse-server-email-adapter-multiple-languages, a localeIdentifier user field and custom locale JSON; default en_US, with pt_BR example.

facts.label: UI locales and accessibility
facts.value: No complete end-user UI language list or public accessibility conformance report found in auth, React/Flutter screen guides and localization material.

facts.label: Web frameworks and APIs
facts.value: Official guides cover JavaScript/Node, React/Angular, React Native, PHP, .NET and REST/GraphQL; API feature page also names Next.js, Vue and other JS frameworks.

facts.label: Published release runtime
facts.value: Back4app's release note describes Parse 7.5.2 with Node.js 18 and Parse JS SDK 4.

facts.label: Vendor-observed app runtime
facts.value: Back4app's Oct 23, 2026 linking test reports Parse 7.5.2, Cloud Code Node 19.9 and client SDK 8.6.2.

facts.label: Native Apple and Android
facts.value: Back4app documents Swift/ParseSwift and Android Java/Kotlin integration; Apple sign-in guide uses AuthenticationServices and requires a non-personal Apple developer team.

facts.label: React Native, Flutter and desktop
facts.value: React Native uses Parse plus AsyncStorage; Flutter guide targets Android/iOS and local session storage. API feature page lists Flutter Web/Windows/macOS/Linux and Apple macOS/watchOS.

facts.label: Managed dependencies
facts.value: Back4app provisions backend, database, APIs and storage; client supplies SDKs/app keys and app-specific Cloud Code. External senders/OTP/SSO services need their own configuration/accounts.

facts.label: Database versions and providers
facts.value: Version guide says selecting Parse 8.6.117 requires MongoDB 8.x or higher. Pricing lists AWS/DigitalOcean and, on higher plans, Mongo Atlas; backup policy also discusses PostgreSQL deployments.

facts.label: Self-hosting and custom deployment scope
facts.value: Standard offer is managed hosting. Enterprise/on-premises/build-on-your-cloud arrangements are contact-sales; independently running Parse after export is a separate deployment.

facts.label: Custom logic and fields
facts.value: Custom Parse objects/user fields and JavaScript Cloud Functions support validation, database events and external npm integrations; deployment uses cloud/main.js and a public folder.

facts.label: Jobs and webhooks
facts.value: Cloud Code jobs included: Free 1, MVP 3, Pay As You Go 7, Dedicated unlimited. API page advertises object/function webhooks, custom headers, payload transforms, retries and webhook logs.

facts.label: Webhook delivery detail
facts.value: No exact retry/backoff sequence, event-retention window, HMAC signature format or durable delivery guarantee found in API feature, Cloud Code and logs docs checked.

facts.label: Admin operations and access
facts.value: Dashboard Database Browser supports create/read/update/delete/filter/export; API/SDKs manage users, roles and sessions. Core Settings supports key editing, restart, clone, transfer and app deletion.

facts.label: Bans and impersonation
facts.value: App-side bans can be implemented in Cloud Code; vendor's auth guide notes paid password-policy/account-lockout settings and a Free-plan custom-validation alternative. Parse user API documents master-key /loginAs.

facts.label: Account linking and unlink safety
facts.value: Explicit authenticated PUT on the user's authData links/unlinks methods. Vendor's Oct 2026 test found removing the last login method could orphan an account unless its custom server hook blocks it.

facts.label: Guest-to-registered upgrade
facts.value: Password/provider credentials can be added to the same guest _User. Vendor notes setUsername()/linkWith() SDK helpers strip anonymous authData, while its plain set/save flow can preserve the guest ID.

facts.label: Password policy and access controls
facts.value: Vendor advertises bcrypt, length/complexity rules and failed-login lockouts. Recent auth guide says dashboard password policy/lockout controls are read-only on Free; custom beforeSave validation can enforce app rules.

facts.label: Bot, breached-password and delivery abuse
facts.value: No packaged CAPTCHA, breached-password database check or end-user SMS spending/fraud limit found in auth/custom-options/OTP/security materials.

facts.label: Rate window and recovery
facts.value: Help docs say requests/second is per app, calculated over 60 seconds; excess traffic is dropped until trailing one-minute average recovers.

facts.label: Observed rate-limit response
facts.value: Vendor's Oct 2026 Free-plan engineering run reports HTTP 400 with Parse code 155, and backs off on that body; it used 16 requests/second for its seed workload.

facts.label: Current per-plan burst quotas
facts.value: No complete current login/admin/Cloud Code request-rate table by Free/MVP/PAYG/Dedicated found in current pricing/API page and rate-limit help sources.

facts.label: Event and log access
facts.value: Dashboard exposes System, Info, Error and Access logs; request access details include who/how/status, and Cloud Code can log app-specific auth actions.

facts.label: Access log retention — Free
facts.value: 1 day.

facts.label: Access log retention — MVP
facts.value: 7 days.

facts.label: Access log retention — Pay As You Go
facts.value: 14 days; third-party real-time logging option.

facts.label: Access log retention — Dedicated
facts.value: 28 days; third-party real-time logging option.

facts.label: Profile and ID export
facts.value: Dashboard class export supports JSON/CSV. JSON download link is emailed as a zip; CSV downloads immediately; support can help if JSON export email does not arrive.

facts.label: Passwords, authData and full exit
facts.value: Vendor's Oct 2026 exit test says API user exports omit password hashes; keeping existing passwords needs database access/dump. Files must be downloaded/reuploaded and Cloud Code retained separately.

facts.label: Export entitlement and portability limits
facts.value: No complete plan-specific hash-export assistance fee, export completion SLA or provider/passkey credential portability contract found in pricing, export help and exit documentation.

facts.label: Migration into Back4app
facts.value: Documented Parse migration connects an existing database, uploads Cloud Code and moves files; CLI @back4app/m2b4a restores database dumps and uploads files.

facts.label: CSV/profile import and custom IDs
facts.value: Dashboard imports CSV with typed Date/GeoPoint/Pointer columns; custom options expose allowCustomObjectId. These are generic data tools.

facts.label: Foreign password migration
facts.value: No published foreign-hash algorithm matrix, lazy password migration recipe or seamless non-Parse credential-import guarantee found in migration/CSV/custom-options docs.

facts.label: App-user deletion
facts.value: Parse user API permits authenticated DELETE; builder must implement related-record/file cleanup and retention rules. Dashboard can delete rows/classes and Core Settings deletes the app.

facts.label: Backups — Free
facts.value: No included backups.

facts.label: Backups — MVP and Pay As You Go
facts.value: Automatic daily snapshots retained seven days; recovery assistance through support/live chat.

facts.label: Backups — Dedicated and PostgreSQL
facts.value: Dedicated purchased on/after June 25, 2025: hourly backups retained 3 days, daily 7 days, weekly 28 days; PITR optional. PostgreSQL: daily backups retained 30 days and PITR unavailable.

facts.label: Builder account closure and retained copies
facts.value: Help: delete all apps, then contact support with the account email. Terms allow account cancellation by email; DPA requires customer-data deletion at contract end with backup/archive and legal-retention exceptions.

facts.label: Final erasure deadline
facts.value: No numeric maximum after termination for all backup/archive deletion found in current DPA/terms/privacy and backup policy; DPA refers to Back4app's retention schedule.

facts.label: Regions — Free
facts.value: USA.

facts.label: Regions — MVP and Pay As You Go
facts.value: USA, Europe, Asia, Australia.

facts.label: Regions — Dedicated and custom Enterprise
facts.value: Dedicated: any AWS region. Enterprise multi-region/other-cloud arrangements are contact-sales.

facts.label: Regional API routing
facts.value: After region changes, parseapi.back4app.com still routes through US servers. Help center instructs using the app-specific *.b4a.io endpoint and updating clients.

facts.label: Data scope and cross-border terms
facts.value: Stored auth data includes user profiles, credential material and session records. DPA permits international transfers under applicable safeguards; privacy notice separately describes account/site data processing.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Public DPA updated June 16, 2025 is incorporated into service terms. Linked third-party list, effective Nov 22, 2024, names AWS, Cloudflare, MongoDB and DigitalOcean.

facts.label: Assurance claims and report scope
facts.value: Pricing marks ISO 27001/SOC 2 Type 2 for Pay As You Go/Dedicated and HIPAA only on Dedicated after a BAA. DPA describes an annual internal audit report available on written request under confidentiality.

facts.label: Public assurance detail
facts.value: Current certificate issuer/scope/expiry, SOC 2 observation period and an openly downloadable independent audit report were not established from pricing, GDPR page, DPA and subprocessor material.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Back4app; legal operator Back4app, Inc. This record covers Back4app Backend, the managed Parse backend with an auth subsystem.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active public backend offer, self-service app creation and current release/version docs. No current shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in those pages and the official shutdown-contingency FAQ.

facts.label: Parse Server authentication security update
facts.value: Back4app release notes say Parse Server 7.5.2 became the default stable version under “Oct 25” and includes a critical OAuth fix that isolates authentication credentials per app.

facts.label: Hosted-service terms
facts.value: Service use is governed by Terms of Service updated June 16, 2025; limited rights to use the service for developing/testing/running apps. Customer keeps its User Content ownership.

facts.label: Underlying Parse license
facts.value: The documented Parse Server 7.5.2 source is Apache-2.0; its license is distinct from Back4app's service contract.

facts.label: Hosted SLA
facts.value: Standard pricing excludes SLA for Free/MVP/PAYG; Dedicated SLA says Contact Us and Enterprise offers custom SLAs. No public percentage, credit formula or exclusions are specified there.

facts.label: Official public status page
facts.value: No current official incident-history/status URL verified from pricing, support, docs and targeted lifecycle/status searches. A guessed status.back4app.com endpoint was inaccessible.

facts.label: Version selection and release evidence
facts.value: Owner can change Parse Server version in settings. Version doc updated Oct 28, 2026 discusses 8.6.117; release page calls 7.5.2 the default stable release under its Oct 25 heading.

facts.label: Patch and support policy
facts.value: No fixed fleet-wide security patch deadline, complete current supported-version/EOL matrix or managed-runtime support-duration commitment found in release/version docs and terms.

facts.label: Support routes and plan gates
facts.value: Community plus email/ticket on all listed plans; Dedicated adds priority support/scheduled calls/training. Support page offers chat, tickets, Slack and Stack Overflow.

facts.label: Support response commitment
facts.value: No fixed response/resolution hours, staffed schedule or incident priority timing found in public pricing/support/terms.

apps.name: Backendless
apps.line: Backend platform with user accounts, login, and sessions.

free.text: Cloud Free includes 50 API requests/minute

cells.freeUsers: No MAU allowance; 15,000 objects per table
cells.sso: No published customer SSO connection price

mau.math: Each user makes 2 requests, so 1,000 users make 2,000. If that fits the Free plan, the cost is $0 per 30-day cycle. The full cost depends on real traffic and resources.
Each user makes 2 requests, so 10,000 users make 20,000. If that fits the Free plan, the cost is $0 per 30-day cycle. The full cost depends on real traffic and resources.
Each user makes 2 requests, so 50,000 users make 100,000. In this assumed case, the Scale Fixed base is $15, plus $0 for extra use over the limit.
Each user makes 2 requests, so 100,000 users make 200,000. In this assumed case, the Scale Fixed base is $15, plus $0 for extra use over the limit.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found.

facts.label: Billing scope and unit
facts.value: Cloud pricing per application; unlimited builder seats; no separate MAU/returning-user/stored-user rate card.

facts.label: Scale Variable definition
facts.value: Sum of daily rates over 30-day cycle; each day priced by the highest minute’s total API requests in that 24-hour period.

facts.label: Scale Fixed definition
facts.value: Selected monthly tier fee plus overage charges for the hours in which traffic exceeds that tier.

facts.label: Free Cloud capacity
facts.value: $0; 50 API requests/minute; 20 data tables; 15,000 objects per table; 1 GB files; 2 custom roles; unlimited builder seats.

facts.label: Free production and legacy limits
facts.value: 2023 official plan notice explicitly calls Free production-capable; up to 5 Free apps/account; it also states 1,000 requests/day and older table/realtime limits.

facts.label: Current Free daily cap
facts.value: Whether the old 1,000 requests/day limit remains enforced is not settled by the current pricing page, which does not repeat it.

facts.label: Cloud minimum paid commitment
facts.value: USD $15/month for Scale Fixed tier 1; Scale Variable tier 1 $0.50/day, or $15 over a 30-day cycle (our calculation).

facts.label: Self-hosted license and optional services
facts.value: Pro single-server Community Edition license $0; support $7,200/year; unlimited upgrades $7,200/year; support+upgrades bundle $10,000/year.

facts.label: Managed service minimum
facts.value: Managed Backendless subscription price and minimum term not publicly quoted on checked managed/pricing pages.

facts.label: Scale Fixed hourly overage calculator
facts.value: Public calculator initializes baseFee=0.15 and computes hourly overage as USD 0.15 × reached tier × (reached tier − selected tier), with currency display rounded to 2 decimals.

facts.label: Scale resource bundle
facts.value: 100 tables, 100,000 objects per table, 10 GB files, 3 custom roles, 10 email templates, 5 Cloud Code scripts and 5-second script execution.

facts.label: Business scenario availability
facts.value: No priced native customer SAML connection/organization-membership-and-invitation package found; business totals below cannot be established.

facts.label: Customer organization fees and limits
facts.value: No native customer-organization/member/invitation quota or per-organization rate card found.

facts.label: Enterprise connections and sync fees
facts.value: No published customer SAML/OIDC enterprise-connection or SCIM-directory per-connection, setup or minimum fee found.

facts.label: Builder seats and apps
facts.value: Unlimited developer seats on all Cloud plans at no extra seat charge; all pricing is per app; official Free notice permits 5 Free apps/account.

facts.label: Builder team permissions and keys
facts.value: Cloud comparison: Free 1 custom API key; Scale 10. Team Permissions included on Scale, absent on Free.

facts.label: App auth email
facts.value: Backendless has app email settings used for signup confirmation and password recovery; can configure custom SMTP sender/server using SSL/TLS.

facts.label: General Email API prerequisites
facts.value: Email API requires configured mail server; messages go through that server; without server info API errors.

facts.label: SMS and phone delivery
facts.value: Free Twilio integration plugin on a paid Backendless plan; own Twilio account/SID/token and Twilio-registered sender number required.

facts.label: Traffic caps and spend controls
facts.value: Scale Variable/Fixed let builder set maximum tier; requests beyond that threshold are rejected with an error.

facts.label: Free and paid limit behavior
facts.value: Free is hard-limited; Scale can incur higher tiers/overages unless capped. Switching to Free while over its limits blocks requests.

facts.label: Billing triggers, refunds and inactivity
facts.value: Scale cycle normally 30 days; exports/cloning/Free switch can trigger an interim bill. Payments non-refundable; inactive accounts/apps may be terminated after at least 2 months.

facts.label: Auth-related Function Packs
facts.value: 64 total custom roles $20/month or $200/year; Management/Admin API $20/month or $200/year; Enterprise Security $399/month or $4,000/year.

facts.label: Other relevant resource packs
facts.value: Extra 200,000 objects $10/month or $100/year; extra 50 tables $25/month or $250/year; extra 10 GB files $20/month or $200/year.

facts.label: Cloud Code expansion prices
facts.value: Unlimited scripts $60/month or $600/year; 20-second execution $30/month or $300/year; 1-second timers $50/month or $500/year.

facts.label: Conflicting cache pack price
facts.value: Same current pricing page lists Additional 100 objects in cache twice: $20/month/$200/year and $5/month/$50/year.

facts.label: Individual and country eligibility
facts.value: Cloud terms allow developers; under 13 prohibited; under 18 needs parent/guardian approval. Pro EULA accepts an individual or business entity.

facts.label: Supported customer countries
facts.value: Complete permitted/restricted customer-country list not published in checked terms, pricing and privacy pages.

facts.label: Self-service Cloud and trial
facts.value: Free Cloud signup, no credit card required; new apps start on Free rather than a fixed-length trial; Scale upgrade self-service.

facts.label: Pro entry conditions
facts.value: Free Community Edition license requested during installation; license key required for ongoing development and production; clustered and managed arrangements use sales.

facts.label: Auth product scope
facts.value: Backend platform with native users, registration/login/logout, password recovery, custom profiles, roles and sessions; other backend and UI tools included.

facts.label: Deployment editions
facts.value: Cloud is vendor hosted; Pro is self-hosted; Managed Backendless operates Pro in a chosen server environment.

facts.label: Cloud operator responsibilities
facts.value: Vendor hosts runtime/database; developer configures user schema, roles, permissions, session policy, frontend and integrations.

facts.label: Pro and Managed responsibilities
facts.value: Pro operator provides and manages infrastructure; Managed service includes monitoring, load balancing, backups, security audits, patching and upgrades.

facts.label: Email/username password
facts.value: Native registration and login; identity column defaults to email and can be changed to a unique nickname, phone number or other property.

facts.label: Anonymous/guest login
facts.value: Native Guest Login creates a Users record, objectId and user-token; GuestUser role; optional persistent client login.

facts.label: Phone code login
facts.value: plugin + external_service: Twilio plugin supports two-step phone-code login, phone+password+SMS login and registration phone confirmation.

facts.label: Passwordless server primitive
facts.value: Native passwordless login by objectId available only in trusted CloudCode with CloudCode API key.

facts.label: Email link/code and wallet login
facts.value: No native maintained email magic-link/OTP or wallet-signature sign-in contract found in checked User Service docs, Marketplace and core SDK methods.

facts.label: Configured social providers
facts.value: OAuth2 setup docs give Facebook, Google, GitHub and LinkedIn provider configuration; Twitter has OAuth1 access-token/secret login.

facts.label: Apple sign-in
facts.value: Free Login With Apple Marketplace plugin; paid Backendless app required; exchanges Apple proof for Backendless user/session.

facts.label: Microsoft and other providers
facts.value: Generic provider-code OAuth2 API exists; complete current provider catalogue and explicit Microsoft tenant/endpoint guarantees not established in public setup text.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: No native WebAuthn/passkey registration/assertion, autofill, client/domain compatibility or recovery contract found.

facts.label: Authenticator-app MFA
facts.value: Free 2FA Login plugin: password login returns transactionId for TOTP-enabled user; authWith2FA completes session using authenticator code.

facts.label: SMS second factor
facts.value: Twilio plugin can verify phone/password then send SMS code; session returned only after transaction/code confirmation.

facts.label: Recovery and other factors
facts.value: No public native backup/recovery codes, lost-authenticator process, email-MFA or passkey/security-key MFA policy found.

facts.label: Email confirmation
facts.value: Native optional confirmation, disabled by default; confirmation link changes pending status to enabled; login blocked until confirmed when required.

facts.label: Password reset and recovery
facts.value: Native recovery API supports generated temporary password or link to a form where user chooses new password; one email flow active at a time.

facts.label: Profile changes and account deletion
facts.value: Update User Object API changes profile/registration properties; Remove User deletes the Users record under configured security permissions.

facts.label: Phone verification
facts.value: Twilio plugin sends registration code and completes registration with phoneNumber, transactionId and transactionCode.

facts.label: Session model
facts.value: Server session identified by user-token header; new token generated on successful login; SDKs manage it; isValidLogin validates a saved token.

facts.label: Session lifetime
facts.value: Inactivity-based timeout, reset by each API call; official guide gives 3,600-second default and configurable maximum 2,592,000 seconds (30 days).

facts.label: Cookie authorization
facts.value: Optional user-auth-cookie; header takes priority; cookie duration matches session duration and applies to the domain used for login.

facts.label: Concurrent login policy
facts.value: Configurable maximum simultaneous sessions with the same credentials; API errors include 3002/3044 for concurrency limits.

facts.label: Logout and paid session manager
facts.value: Native logout terminates supplied token’s session; Enterprise Security Session Manager lists sessions, can log out all sessions for a user and copy session token.

facts.label: OAuth protocol role
facts.value: Backendless consumes external OAuth1/OAuth2 provider tokens and establishes its own user session; mapping of provider fields supported.

facts.label: Business SAML/OIDC standards
facts.value: No public native customer SAML SP/IdP configuration, generic OIDC discovery/JWKS/ID-token contract or organization-specific enterprise-connection guide found.

facts.label: Roles and resource permissions
facts.value: Built-in auth/social/client roles plus custom app-wide roles; global, table/container and record/file permissions; Owner Policy links records to ownerId.

facts.label: Customer organizations and invitations
facts.value: No ready-made customer organization lifecycle, membership/invitation expiry or customer-admin console contract found.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No native SCIM 2.0 users/groups provisioning, deactivation behavior or managed SCIM integration contract located.

facts.label: Ready-made auth screens
facts.value: Free Marketplace Login Screen and Password Recovery Screen templates; built-in confirmation/reset system pages; editable UI Builder frontend.

facts.label: Frontend scope
facts.value: UI Builder produces browser SPAs or mobile-packaged apps; can also use Backendless APIs from your own frontend.

facts.label: Theme and messaging branding
facts.value: UI Builder themes and CSS/LESS extensions; editable auth pages and email templates.

facts.label: Custom domains and TLS
facts.value: One or more custom app domains; multiple domains and generated custom-domain SSL certificates require Scale; custom domain supports API and file URLs.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: No complete shipped auth-UI language catalogue or public WCAG/VPAT conformance report found in checked UI/template/auth documentation.

facts.label: Web clients and runtimes
facts.value: Official JavaScript SDK for browser/Node.js, TypeScript definitions and REST; CloudCode supports Java, JavaScript and Codeless.

facts.label: Native and mobile clients
facts.value: Official Android/Java, iOS and Flutter login APIs document identity/password and persistent login support.

facts.label: Cloud prerequisites
facts.value: Backendless supplies its Users/data storage and auth backend; app ID/API key and configured app required; own frontend unless using UI Builder.

facts.label: Self-hosted dependencies
facts.value: Pro Community Edition: Kubernetes single node; MySQL 8+, Redis 6+, MongoDB 5+ and mounted host filesystem.

facts.label: Self-hosted sizing
facts.value: Pro Community guideline: at least 8 GB RAM and 20 GB free disk; at least 4 CPU cores recommended; 16 GB RAM recommended for larger workloads.

facts.label: Installation and upgrades
facts.value: Ubuntu Pro Manager installation sets up k3s, Node.js 14 and manager; manager can start/stop/restart/upgrade services and inspect logs.

facts.label: Backup and restore
facts.value: Cloud Scale includes scheduled daily backups with support-assisted restore; Free has no included daily backup. Pro export/import uses mysqldump/mysql; custom timer can create app export archives.

facts.label: Self-hosted commercial scope
facts.value: Single-server free Core license; clustered high-availability minimum 3 nodes quoted separately; FlowRunner, Visualizations and Dashboards excluded from free Core.

facts.label: Auth hooks and fields
facts.value: Custom Users properties, regex validators and dynamic schema; before/after API event handlers, including guest-login events; Java/JS/Codeless CloudCode.

facts.label: Execution limits and delivery semantics
facts.value: Cloud Code has plan execution/script limits; no universal auth-event webhook retry, signature or delivery guarantee found.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Console can create/edit/search/filter/delete user records and manage roles; native APIs include find-by-ID/identity, update and remove.

facts.label: Disable and re-enable access
facts.value: Console can disable user; CloudCode-only Disable User sets DISABLED; native enable/update-status methods present in official SDK.

facts.label: Impersonation boundary
facts.value: Enterprise Security Session Manager permits copying an existing user-token to impersonate an active user; trusted CloudCode passwordless API logs in by objectId.

facts.label: Guest account upgrade
facts.value: Native registration with the guest objectId converts it to a regular account; OAuth2 login also accepts guestUser from Guest Login.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking providers
facts.value: No explicit maintained arbitrary multi-provider link/unlink or collision/verified-email merge contract found.

facts.label: Brute-force lockout
facts.value: Configurable failed-login threshold and unlock wait time under Users > Login; unlimited unsuccessful logins is also configurable.

facts.label: Bot checks
facts.value: Free UI Builder ReCaptcha component uses reCAPTCHA v2; developer integrates it and follows its documentation.

facts.label: Leaked passwords and SMS fraud
facts.value: No native breached-password database check, phone fraud-scoring policy or per-app SMS spend ceiling documented in checked auth/plugin references.

facts.label: Cloud request thresholds
facts.value: Free 50 requests/minute; Scale prices peak requests/minute and allows maximum tier ceiling that rejects excess requests.

facts.label: Private-server rate scope
facts.value: Pro removes Cloud functional API count/per-second quotas; actual throughput bounded by provisioned system resources.

facts.label: Ordinary application logs
facts.value: Logging API writes developer-submitted messages to /logging files; date-based or maximum-size policy; level filtering, viewing/download/archive/delete.

facts.label: Paid audit log and sessions
facts.value: Enterprise Security audit log tracks Console changes to settings/security/users/data/messaging/Marketplace/CloudCode/UI; filters, search, download and deletion permissions.

facts.label: Audit retention and event completeness
facts.value: Fixed retention days, immutable external stream, full end-user authentication event list and automatic long-term archive policy not established.

facts.label: User data export
facts.value: Console CSV user export; Manage Export can include app settings, schema and data in an app ZIP; Cloud-to-Pro user/data/file migration supported.

facts.label: Identifiers and credentials portability
facts.value: Profile/objectId export documented; current supported password-hash export algorithm/format and provider-credential/passkey portability contract not located.

facts.label: Exit charges and rights
facts.value: No separate standard CSV-export fee listed; Scale export can trigger settlement of accrued usage; Pro server reuse/redistribution remains subject to proprietary EULA.

facts.label: Bulk data and identifier import
facts.value: Console imports app ZIP/settings JSON/table CSV; CSV can include unique objectId using STRING_ID for string or numeric IDs, or generate IDs automatically.

facts.label: Firebase password-hash import
facts.value: Dedicated Firebase Users import accepts Firebase CSV and Hash Config to process imported user password hashes.

facts.label: Other hash/provider migration
facts.value: General bcrypt/Argon2/PBKDF2 hash importer, lazy migration/rehash and complete external provider-link import contract not found.

facts.label: User deletion and guest cleanup
facts.value: Remove User deletes Users record; abandoned guest accounts are purged after their associated session expires.

facts.label: Contractual erasure timing
facts.value: DPA: customer deletion instruction complied with as soon as reasonably practicable, maximum 30 days unless EU/member-state law requires storage; agreement expiry also maximum 30 days with stated retrieval exception.

facts.label: Backup retention and actual account closure
facts.value: Exact backup expiry, restore retention, purge propagation and end-to-end developer-account closure steps not published in checked pricing/policies.

facts.label: Vendor personal-data policy
facts.value: Privacy notice retains personal data as necessary for service/legal/dispute purposes; access/correction/deletion requests through account settings or contact.

facts.label: Cloud hosting regions
facts.value: Choose North American/U.S. cluster or EU cluster at app creation; official article says app users, data and files remain in chosen zone.

facts.label: Region changes and private deployments
facts.value: US↔EU migration requires support and administrative fee; no public fee amount in checked article; Pro/Managed can use a chosen cloud/private location.

facts.label: Residency scope beyond app data
facts.value: No complete same-zone guarantee covering all logs/backups/support telemetry or a current named subprocessor-region inventory found.

facts.label: Public processing agreement
facts.value: Public DPA covers uploaded/displayed/backed-up User Personal Data; customer controller or processor and Backendless processor/subprocessor; updated 2018-08-21.

facts.label: Subprocessor and assurance reports
facts.value: No current named core subprocessor register or scoped SOC 2/ISO assessment report with examination dates found in checked security/legal/pricing pages.

facts.label: HIPAA and enterprise security claims
facts.value: Vendor markets HIPAA-related tools through Enterprise Security pack, $399/month or $4,000/year; private/Managed deployment has separate terms.

facts.label: Name, owner and official pages
facts.value: Backendless; Backendless Corp.; Cloud, Backendless Pro and Managed Backendless.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Public self-service Cloud offer remains available; official staff statement on 2025-07-07 says actively maintained and no shutdown plans.

facts.label: Plan sunsets
facts.value: Cloud 9 sunset 2023-08-01; Springboard ended 2024-01-01; Cloud 99 phase-out 2024-05-01 with automatic Scale Variable transition described for May 2.

facts.label: Hosted service rights
facts.value: Proprietary hosted service under Terms of Service; user retains ownership of its own content; no open-source server grant in Cloud terms.

facts.label: Pro production license
facts.value: Proprietary object-code license for internal/external business applications; OEM/resale/distribution requires separate rights; continuous development/production needs a license key.

facts.label: Client SDK license
facts.value: JavaScript SDK package declares ISC; public source is available in Backendless/JS-SDK.

facts.label: Cloud availability promise
facts.value: Standard Terms state no guaranteed service uptime/API response time; support has no guaranteed response without a contract.

facts.value: MIT allows commercial deployment without a per-user license charge; no hosted free-user allowance applies.

facts.label: Infrastructure Starter

facts.label: Starter security access

facts.label: Infrastructure Pro usage

facts.label: Business scenarios

facts.label: Core organization limits
facts.value: organization plugin: organizations per creator unlimited by default; members per organization 100; invitations per user 100; limits configurable; invitations expire after 48 hours by default.

facts.label: Core SSO and SCIM fees
facts.value: No license fee for the separately MIT-licensed packages identified in F04. Infrastructure charges are a separate offer.

facts.label: Managed connections
facts.value: Pro: SSO one included, then $50/month/connection; Directory Sync one included, then $50/month/connection.

facts.label: Self-service dashboard plan
facts.value: SSO introduction directs customers to enterprise sales for self-service setup; pricing explicitly lists it on Pro. Minimum plan wording conflicts.

facts.label: Core SSO registration limit
facts.value: providersLimit defaults to 10 providers per registering user; configurable number or function; 0 disables registration.

facts.label: Core builder seats/projects
facts.value: Vendor dashboard-seat and project caps do not apply to the embedded library.

facts.label: Infrastructure seats
facts.value: Starter one dashboard seat; Pro unlimited. Project/environment/domain caps not established.

facts.label: Core email sender
facts.value: Bring a transactional email provider and implement sending callbacks; Better Auth itself does not bundle core message delivery.

facts.label: Core phone sender
facts.value: phoneNumber plugin needs developer-provided sendOTP; phone login/verification requires delivery.

facts.label: Managed message prices
facts.value: Pro: $0.001/email; $0.09/SMS.

facts.label: Managed mail service
facts.value: Optional @better-auth/infra email service includes templates for verification, reset and invitations.

facts.label: Managed SMS scope
facts.value: Auth-flow SMS service supports E.164 numbers; docs say global delivery, without an exhaustive destination price/availability table here.

facts.label: Core quota behavior
facts.value: No vendor billing quota applies. Configured throttles and application/database capacity still constrain requests.

facts.label: Infrastructure over-limit safeguards
facts.value: Starter stopping/grace rules, spending caps, alerts, automatic upgrades and overage billing granularity not found.

facts.label: Infrastructure extras
facts.value: Pro dashboard custom domain $25/month; log drain $25/month. Enterprise prices custom.

facts.label: Core account eligibility
facts.value: Vendor production-account eligibility is not applicable to installing MIT code in one's own app.

facts.label: Infrastructure countries and individuals
facts.value: Exhaustive allowed/restricted builder countries and a specific individual-account eligibility rule not found.

facts.label: Core entry path
facts.value: Install package and configure application; sales, vendor signup and a vendor payment card are not installation steps.

facts.label: Infrastructure self-service and trial
facts.value: Getting-started documents dashboard signup and project/API-key creation. Card requirement, trial duration and Starter production permission remain unknown.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Embedded TypeScript library: accounts, login, sessions and verification; plugins add organizations, MFA and enterprise login.

facts.label: Optional managed service
facts.value: Infrastructure extends an existing instance with administration, security, messaging and enterprise services.

facts.label: Who operates core
facts.value: Developer deploys the handler in their application and supplies storage and configuration. Patching and recovery belong to that deployment's operator.

facts.label: Who operates add-on
facts.value: Infrastructure requires a working Better Auth installation plus a vendor account/API key and @better-auth/infra.

facts.label: Email/password
facts.value: Built in, opt-in emailAndPassword.enabled; default password length 8–128 characters.

facts.label: Email link
facts.value: magicLink plugin from better-auth/plugins; developer supplies sendMagicLink; can disable automatic signup.

facts.label: Email code
facts.value: emailOTP plugin: sign-in, email verification and password-reset codes; developer supplies sendVerificationOTP.

facts.label: Phone code
facts.value: phoneNumber plugin supports phone signup/sign-in and verification with custom SMS sending.

facts.label: Anonymous login
facts.value: anonymous plugin creates a guest user/session, with account-link callback when the guest registers.

facts.label: Wallet login
facts.value: SIWE plugin supports Sign In With Ethereum, ERC-4361; configure nonce and signature verification.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: Built-in Google OAuth provider; own client credentials and redirect configuration required.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: Built-in Apple provider; Apple developer credentials required, including a signed client secret that expires and must be renewed.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: Built-in GitHub provider; own OAuth credentials; email scope/permission configuration required.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: Built-in Microsoft/Entra provider; own credentials and tenant configuration. Version 1.7 uses oid for account identity and documents migration from 1.6 sub.

facts.label: Additional social providers
facts.value: Official provider navigation includes Discord, Facebook, GitLab, LinkedIn, Slack, Spotify, Twitch, X and others. Generic OAuth is a separate plugin.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: Separate @better-auth/passkey plugin using SimpleWebAuthn; first-factor sign-in and conditional autofill documented. Registration normally requires a session; passkey-first signup needs explicit configuration and server identity resolution.

facts.label: Passkey recovery and domains
facts.value: Autofill requires correct webauthn autocomplete and browser support. Fallback must use another configured method. Changing the RP ID/domain needs a migration plan; automatic credential portability not established.

facts.label: MFA methods and recovery
facts.value: twoFactor plugin: authenticator TOTP, email/phone OTP through a custom sender, backup recovery codes and trusted devices. Passwordless enrollment requires allowPasswordless: true.

facts.label: MFA enforcement
facts.value: Default challenges cover credential sign-in endpoints for email, username and phone. OAuth, passkey, email OTP, magic link and anonymous login need custom hooks to enforce a second factor.

facts.label: Email verification and reset
facts.value: Email confirmation and password-reset links use developer sending callbacks. Verification requirements are configurable.

facts.label: Address change and user deletion
facts.value: Email change and user deletion require opt-in. New-email verification is the default change behavior; deletion can require password, fresh session or emailed confirmation.

facts.label: Phone confirmation/change
facts.value: Phone plugin verifies codes and supports updating the current user's phone after verification.

facts.label: Session lifecycle
facts.value: Cookie session token with server storage; defaults: expiry 7 days, update age 1 day, freshness 1 day. Supports listing, revoking one, other or all sessions.

facts.label: Revocation caveats
facts.value: Cookie-cached sessions can persist elsewhere until cache expiry unless revalidated. Sensitive built-in operations check storage. Secondary-storage deletion failures can leave sessions valid until expiry.

facts.label: Business protocol role
facts.value: @better-auth/sso accepts upstream OIDC/OAuth2 and SAML 2.0 providers; app acts as relying party/service provider, with organization provisioning.

facts.label: Organizations, invitations and roles
facts.value: organization plugin provides workspaces, memberships, teams, invitations, owner/admin/member roles and custom access control. App must apply organization context to its own data access.

facts.label: SCIM protocol and dependencies
facts.value: Separate @better-auth/scim: inbound SCIM 2.0 Users/Groups, create/update/deactivate/delete; needs native interactive database transactions. Cloudflare D1 is unsupported for this plugin.

facts.label: SCIM offboarding
facts.value: Final active source deactivation/deletion removes sessions. Future sign-in must be blocked by application policy. Groups need role projection; provisioning does not create a login method.

facts.label: Login and account UI
facts.value: Core exposes client APIs/hooks for app-owned screens. Complete first-party ready-made sign-in, signup, profile and hosted login screen catalog not established.

facts.label: Admin dashboard UI
facts.value: Optional Infrastructure dashboard manages users, sessions, organizations, analytics and audit events.

facts.label: Own branding and auth domain
facts.value: Own application controls UI and auth baseURL; cookie/origin and passkey RP ID settings must match the deployment. No vendor-managed domain quota applies to core.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: Separate @better-auth/i18n plugin translates error messages; ships 22 locales and accepts custom translations/detection. It does not establish translated app screens.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Public accessibility conformance report for end-user screens not found in installation, basic usage, client or i18n docs.

facts.label: Web client frameworks
facts.value: Official clients: React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and vanilla JavaScript.

facts.label: Server/runtime integrations
facts.value: Standard Request/Response handler; installation lists Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, React Router, SolidStart, Hono, Cloudflare Workers, Express, Elysia, TanStack Start and Expo integrations.

facts.label: Mobile
facts.value: Official Expo integration supports React Native and web, with a Better Auth backend. Current guide targets Expo SDK 55, React Native 0.83 and React 19.2.

facts.label: Desktop
facts.value: Official @better-auth/electron integration uses system-browser login. Supports two major versions behind Electron's latest stable major.

facts.label: Other native clients
facts.value: Dedicated first-party Swift, Kotlin and Flutter SDK/version coverage not established from the installation, client and Expo guides.

facts.label: Database and optional cache
facts.value: Supported database/adapter paths include SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Prisma, Drizzle and MongoDB; optional secondary storage for sessions and other transient data.

facts.label: Stateless limits
facts.value: Database-free mode exists, but most plugins need a database. Configure secret, base URL and request handler; OAuth needs provider credentials.

facts.label: Schema and upgrades
facts.value: Generate/apply migrations when schemas/plugins change. Built-in Kysely can use CLI migrate; ORM users generate schema then use their migration tools.

facts.label: Operations and sizing gaps
facts.value: No fixed hardware sizing or end-to-end backup/restore runbook found in installation, database and performance guides.

facts.label: Custom logic and events
facts.value: Before/after request hooks, database hooks and custom logic execute in the application's runtime. Hook-driven outbound notifications are custom code, not a guaranteed vendor webhook delivery queue.

facts.label: Extra fields
facts.value: Core schemas support developer-defined fields and generated migrations.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: admin plugin APIs support create, list/search, role changes, bans, deletion and session management. Privileged routes require admin authorization.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: Admin impersonation sessions default to 1 hour; impersonating admins needs explicit permission. Legacy allowImpersonatingAdmins is deprecated.

facts.label: Link and unlink
facts.value: Verified matching-provider emails can link accounts automatically by default. Manual linking requires a signed-in user; unlinking the last method is blocked unless explicitly allowed.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: Anonymous plugin calls onLinkAccount; developer moves app data. Guest is normally deleted after upgrade. Pending MFA does not complete linking early.

facts.label: Core abuse controls
facts.value: Built-in configurable throttling; password hashing and origin/cookie protections documented.

facts.label: CAPTCHA
facts.value: Optional core captcha plugin supports Turnstile, reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, CaptchaFox and Vercel BotID. Defaults protect email signup/sign-in/reset only; other paths need configuration.

facts.label: Compromised passwords
facts.value: Optional haveIBeenPwned plugin uses the external HIBP API; rejects compromised signup/password changes; checks send a hash prefix.

facts.label: Managed security
facts.value: Optional Sentinel documents credential-stuffing, bot, suspicious-IP, impossible-travel and velocity controls, with configurable log/challenge/block behavior.

facts.label: Core login limits
facts.value: Production default 100 requests/10 seconds per connecting IP; email sign-in and two-factor paths 3/10 seconds. Development default off; auth.api server calls bypass it.

facts.label: Limit recovery and storage
facts.value: HTTP 429 and X-Retry-After; default in-memory counters; database/secondary/custom atomic storage options. Configure trusted proxies for reliable client IPs.

facts.label: Managed API limits
facts.value: Separate Infrastructure management-API request quotas and burst recovery rules not established.

facts.label: Own logging
facts.value: Hooks can write events to operator-owned storage; core does not establish a vendor-managed log retention promise.

facts.label: Managed audit events
facts.value: dash() captures signup/sign-in, profile, verification and other events; query/filter APIs with pagination, max 100/page.

facts.label: Managed retention
facts.value: Starter 1 day; Pro 7 days; Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Exit data
facts.value: Own database schema contains user IDs/profiles, account provider IDs and password hashes; direct database export is possible in principle. A turnkey cross-provider export format/fee is not established.

facts.label: Credential portability
facts.value: Passkey schema stores credential IDs/public keys and related metadata. Keeping exported rows does not establish usable credentials at another RP ID/domain.

facts.label: Migration in
facts.value: Official Auth0 guide uses a developer-run migration script for profiles/accounts and organization data; bcrypt verification needs a custom verifier. Other hash formats require changes.

facts.label: Migration limits
facts.value: Guide says existing sessions cannot carry over; invitations and connection configuration need separate handling. Role mapping is an example requiring customization.

facts.label: Core deletion
facts.value: Opt-in deleteUser hard-deletes user data from the database; callbacks allow application cleanup.

facts.label: Managed data deletion
facts.value: DPA says delete or return personal data after termination unless law requires retention. Exact backup purge and all-data deletion deadlines not stated.

facts.label: Retention and closure
facts.value: Privacy policy uses purpose-based retention without fixed general periods. Complete vendor account/project closure steps and backup exceptions not found.

facts.label: Core data location
facts.value: Operator chooses application/database hosting; no vendor core-region selector applies.

facts.label: Infrastructure residency
facts.value: Named selectable production, backup and log regions, region-change rules and residency fees not found. Privacy permits international transfers including the US.

facts.label: Public privacy agreement
facts.value: Public DPA covers service processing; subprocessors list available on request; audit documentation may be requested.

facts.label: Independent assurance scope
facts.value: Public named subprocessor list and completed independent audit report with period/scope not established.

facts.label: Core telemetry
facts.value: Optional anonymous telemetry is disabled by default. Vendor says it excludes personal data and secrets; code/config can enable it.

facts.label: Name, aliases, owner, URLs
facts.value: Better Auth; official TypeScript authentication project and docs. No previous product name established in this check.

facts.value: Vercel announced it is acquiring Better Auth on July 7, 2026; Better Auth says it is joining Vercel. Vercel states the library stays open source under MIT, keeps its name and continues development.

facts.value: MIT; commercial use, modification and distribution allowed with required copyright and license notice; no warranty.

facts.value: Terms put service levels in a separate SLA/order form; absent one, commercially reasonable efforts apply.

facts.value: General support response/resolution target and staffed hours not found.
