facts.label: Standard Cloud billing unit
facts.value: Flat dedicated-instance subscription, monthly or yearly; Basic/Premium/Enterprise have unlimited stored users/MAUs and no per-user or per-connection fee.

facts.label: PAYG and negotiated meter
facts.value: PAYG deducts prepaid balance by the minute at the tier’s hourly rate. Enterprise HA is an annual custom contract priced on users, SLA and support scope.

facts.label: Free hosted allowance
facts.value: No ongoing free Cloud plan is advertised: only US$4/30-day Basic PAYG credit.

facts.label: Self-host free-production software
facts.value: Apache core may be self-hosted without a per-user/per-application license bill. Software cost is $0; infrastructure, sender accounts and operations remain yours.

facts.label: Lowest paid entry and commitment
facts.value: Basic: US$9/month subscription, or US$0.018/hour PAYG billed by the minute. Standard monthly plans do not require an annual support contract.

facts.label: Renewal, cancellation and refunds
facts.value: Subscriptions auto-renew; cancellation stops future renewals and keeps access through the paid period. Subscriptions/top-ups generally non-refundable, with stated error/non-provisioning/vendor-termination exceptions.

facts.label: Cloud Basic prices
facts.value: US$9 monthly; US$80 annually (vendor displays $6.67/month equivalent); US$0.018/hour PAYG, charged by minute.

facts.label: Cloud Premium prices
facts.value: US$25 monthly; US$200 annually (vendor displays $16.67/month equivalent); US$0.05/hour PAYG, charged by minute.

facts.label: Cloud Enterprise prices
facts.value: US$59 monthly; US$450 annually ($37.50/month equivalent); US$0.12/hour PAYG, charged by minute.

facts.label: Enterprise HA and self-host support
facts.value: Enterprise HA custom annual quote; global annual self-host support price not published.

facts.label: China Commercial edition price
facts.value: 人民币 ¥5,899/year; annual private-deployment service, unlimited active users, applications and identity connections.

facts.label: China Enterprise edition price
facts.value: Enterprise 人民币 ¥12,599/year; annual private-deployment service, unlimited active users, applications and identity connections.

facts.label: China Xinchuang edition price
facts.value: Xinchuang adaptation edition: project quote, no public fixed numeric fee.

facts.label: Business scenario eligibility
facts.value: Native organizations, roles, invitation registration and shared-application support are documented. A 10-customer-org Premium fit depends on how its 10-org cap counts the mandatory built-in organization.

facts.label: Basic organization allowance
facts.value: Cloud Basic: 1 organization; no per-user or per-SSO-connection fee.

facts.label: Premium organization allowance
facts.value: Cloud Premium: 10 organizations.

facts.label: Enterprise organization allowance
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise and Enterprise HA: unlimited organizations; self-host core has no published organization-count software license limit.

facts.label: Members, invitation and role count caps
facts.value: Numeric per-organization member, role, group and invitation count/overage limits were not established. Invitation usage quotas are individually configurable.

facts.label: Business SSO and SCIM charges
facts.value: All standard Cloud tiers include OIDC, SAML enterprise connections and SCIM, with unlimited connections and no per-connection fee. Self-host core includes these capabilities.

facts.label: Applications and environments
facts.value: Basic 10 applications; Premium/Enterprise/HA unlimited applications. Enterprise/HA include one staging instance; no staging instance is included in Basic/Premium.

facts.label: Builder access and custom-domain caps
facts.value: All Cloud plans give full admin console access. Basic no custom domain; Premium 1; Enterprise/HA 5. Numeric builder-seat caps/seat fees were not found.

facts.label: Email dependency and charges
facts.value: Configure your own SMTP, SendGrid, Resend, Azure ACS or other supported email provider. Cloud all tiers permit own providers; no included authentication-send quota or per-email Cloud tariff was found.

facts.label: SMS dependency and routes
facts.value: external_service delivery through supported connectors such as Twilio SMS/Verify, Amazon SNS, Azure ACS, Alibaba/Tencent SMS or Custom HTTP SMS. Customer supplies credentials and pays provider fees.

facts.label: MAU limit and sizing behavior
facts.value: Standard plans advertise unlimited users/MAU; suggested user counts are guidance, never throttled. No automatic MAU overage charge is listed.

facts.label: Balance and subscription exhaustion
facts.value: PAYG instances stop when balance runs out; after 7 days without top-up the vendor may delete them and their Customer Data. Ended/failed subscriptions may be suspended and later deleted.

facts.label: Other priced resource gates
facts.value: Webhook caps Basic 3 / Premium 20 / Enterprise and HA unlimited. Built-in payments/subscriptions, ABAC/custom models and expiring permissions require Premium or higher in Cloud.

facts.label: Individual eligibility and countries
facts.value: Terms are between “you” and Casbin Inc., with a separate authority clause when acting for an organization. Service is subject to US export controls and comprehensively sanctioned-country/restricted-party exclusions.

facts.label: Home-market and regional offer
facts.value: Global Cloud is priced in USD; China Commercial/Enterprise are quoted in RMB annually and marketed for private deployment. Cloud privacy policy describes a business service not directed to children under 16.

facts.label: Self-service trial
facts.value: New accounts get US$4 credit valid for 30 days, for a Basic pay-as-you-go instance. Standard paid instances can be created through the public console path.

facts.label: Card and signup prerequisites
facts.value: Paid monthly/yearly instances and balance top-ups use Stripe; exact no-card trial eligibility and mandatory company-email/domain requirements were not established.

facts.label: Account-product scope
facts.value: Complete identity/access server: accounts, registration/login, verification/recovery, sessions, user administration, SSO federation and Casbin-based authorization.

facts.label: Deployment and edition scope
facts.value: Free Apache-2.0 self-host server; dedicated managed Cloud Basic/Premium/Enterprise/Enterprise HA; annual self-host support contracts. China site separately offers Commercial, Enterprise and Xinchuang private-deployment editions.

facts.label: Cloud operator responsibilities
facts.value: Vendor hosts a dedicated instance/database, applies automatic Casdoor upgrades, manages HTTPS certificates and provides plan support. Builder configures users, providers, permissions and its own product integration.

facts.label: Self-host operator responsibilities
facts.value: Builder runs the server, SQL database, TLS/reverse proxy, storage, optional Redis, external senders, patches, backups and recovery.

facts.label: Passwords and one-time codes
facts.value: built_in username/email password login and email/phone verification-code login. Cloud Basic includes these methods; email/SMS require configured senders.

facts.label: Magic-link login
facts.value: built_in email sign-in link, optionally sign-up; Cloud Basic includes magic links. Link is single-use, bound to the requesting browser, default validity 10 minutes.

facts.label: Anonymous / guest login
facts.value: built_in guest accounts through the token endpoint when Enable signup and Enable guest signin are on; unavailable in built-in organization.

facts.label: Wallet login freshness
facts.value: Current v4 wallet-login support is unclear. English MetaMask/Web3-Onboard docs return 404; released v4.25 tree contains Web3 UI files only under web-old.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Native connectors include Google, GitHub, Apple, Microsoft/Azure AD, Facebook, Discord, GitLab, LinkedIn, Slack, WeChat, DingTalk, Lark, QQ and others listed in the provider table.

facts.label: Generic federation
facts.value: OIDC provider type connects additional OIDC identity providers; custom OAuth provider integration is documented for non-listed services.

facts.label: WebAuthn first factor
facts.value: built_in passkey/security-key sign-in on Cloud Basic and self-host core. Users register/delete credentials in My Account, then can sign in using WebAuthn.

facts.label: Origins, fallback and MFA interaction
facts.value: Requires HTTPS except localhost and an origin matching the public Casdoor URL. Credential is scoped to the WebAuthn site/origin; configured password/code/social paths can remain alternatives.

facts.label: Conditional autofill and native passkey matrix
facts.value: A published conditional-autofill/discoverable-credential behavior matrix and minimum native client/browser versions were not established.

facts.label: MFA factors in Basic/core
facts.value: built_in TOTP authenticator codes, SMS and email second factors; Cloud Basic includes optional MFA.

facts.label: Required MFA and RADIUS plan gates
facts.value: Cloud Premium+ can require MFA for an organization; Cloud Enterprise+ supports MFA against your external RADIUS server. These controls are available in self-host core.

facts.label: Recovery codes and factor loss
facts.value: Every supported MFA method provides single-use recovery codes, saved during setup. Each used code becomes invalid.

facts.label: Verification and password reset
facts.value: built_in configurable email/phone verification at signup; forgot-password page sends a code or configured email reset link through an applicable provider.

facts.label: Profile edits and user deletion
facts.value: Account items control self/admin/immutable edits to email, phone, password and other profile fields. Native delete-user API supports deleting an account, subject to permissions and optional soft deletion.

facts.label: Session records versus storage
facts.value: SQL session records track user/application and multiple session IDs; session cookie backing store defaults to files in ./tmp, with optional Redis/Redis Cluster.

facts.label: Session and token lifetime settings
facts.value: Application Cookie expire default 720 hours; without Remember me session capped at 24 hours. Global sessionCookieLifeTime falls back to 2,592,000 seconds/30 days. Access/refresh token lifetimes are configurable per application.

facts.label: Revocation and device management
facts.value: Users/admins can inspect device/IP/last activity and end individual or all sessions. Ending a session expires its access/refresh tokens; password change, forbidding or deleting a user expires their tokens across applications.

facts.label: SSO logout behavior
facts.value: Native SSO logout, OIDC RP-initiated/back-channel logout and SAML Single Logout are documented. Exclusive sign-in can limit concurrent sessions per app or across the user’s organization.

facts.label: OIDC and SAML provider roles
facts.value: Casdoor is a downstream OAuth2/OIDC authorization server and SAML 2.0 identity provider, while also accepting upstream OIDC/OAuth and SAML IdPs as a service provider/broker.

facts.label: SAML flow direction and other protocols
facts.value: As IdP: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO and bidirectional SLO. As incoming SAML SP: response must match same-browser AuthnRequest/InResponseTo; unsolicited IdP responses are not accepted by that described flow.

facts.label: Organization membership and isolation
facts.value: Each account belongs to exactly one Casdoor organization. Separate organizations hold their own users/apps/branding; org admins manage their org and global built-in admins can manage all.

facts.label: Shared product app and roles
facts.value: A built-in-owned shared application can serve all organizations using -org-<name> client IDs. Roles support direct users, group-derived membership and role hierarchy; permissions use Casbin enforcement APIs.

facts.label: Invitations and customer administration
facts.value: Native invitation-based registration: random/regex code, quota, optional identity restriction/expiry, copyable signup link and optional signup-group assignment, including OAuth signup.

facts.label: SCIM resources and Cloud gate
facts.value: built_in SCIM 2.0 service-provider API for User and Group create/read/replace/patch/delete; included on all standard Cloud plans. Organization supplied through enterprise-user extension; scope is enforced.

facts.label: SCIM suspension caveat
facts.value: SCIM active=false offboarding is not established by the current docs/source. v4.25 returns active based on forbidden/deleted state, but inspected incoming mapping/PATCH switches do not map active into those flags.

facts.label: Hosted screens
facts.value: Native server-hosted login, signup, forgot-password, MFA setup and self-service account pages; all Cloud tiers include the hosted login/signup/account experience.

facts.label: UI integration and forms
facts.value: Frontend/backend SDKs construct sign-in URLs/callbacks; applications can configure signup/signin/account fields, provider buttons, themes and custom external Signin URL.

facts.label: Cloud branding and domains by plan
facts.value: Basic: logo/colors/background/themes and provider subdomain, no custom domain/brand removal/HTML-CSS. Premium: 1 custom domain plus those branding controls. Enterprise/HA: 5 domains.

facts.label: Self-host customization and domain migration
facts.value: Self-host can configure its own public origin, HTTPS and custom HTML/CSS/page fields; organization-admin content is sanitized/restricted compared with global-admin content.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: Cloud advertises 11 UI languages. Released locale files: German, English, Spanish, French, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese and Chinese.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A scoped WCAG conformance statement, VPAT/ACR or independent accessibility report was not found in the checked official UI/security pages.

facts.label: Official web and backend SDKs
facts.value: Official integration index lists JS, React, Vue, Angular, Next.js/Nuxt paths; Go, Java/Spring, Node.js, Python, PHP, .NET, Rust, C/C++, Dart and Ruby backend integrations.

facts.label: Runtime and server deployment boundary
facts.value: Server is Go/Beego with React frontend; prebuilt binaries for Windows/Linux/macOS, x86_64/arm64. Browser/edge clients can speak HTTP/OIDC; the database-backed Go server is not advertised as an edge-worker library.

facts.label: Native mobile and desktop SDKs
facts.value: Official index lists Android, iOS, React Native, Flutter, Unity/.NET and uni-app; desktop paths include Electron, WPF/WinForms/Avalonia and C++/Qt.

facts.label: Apple and Android concrete requirements
facts.value: Current iOS SDK uses authorization-code+PKCE with ASWebAuthenticationSession and no client secret. Android Kotlin/Java SDK requires minSdk 21+ and also uses PKCE without a bundled client secret.

facts.label: Database, cache and sender requirements
facts.value: Self-host SQL options include MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite 3 and TiDB. Redis is optional for one process and needed for shared multi-replica sessions.

facts.label: Source toolchain discrepancy
facts.value: Install guide says Go 1.21+; current README says Go 1.26+ and released v4.25.0 go.mod declares go 1.26.0 with toolchain go1.26.10. Node.js 20 LTS and Yarn 1.x are documented for frontend builds.

facts.label: Deployment, upgrades and rollback
facts.value: Official binary/Docker/Helm and SQL setup documented. Release binaries after v4.22 can upgrade from System Info with checksum validation and backup of binary/frontend; container/custom builds use their own upgrade method.

facts.label: Backup/export and sizing
facts.value: Self-host -export writes all instance objects to JSON and exits; import/init supports restoring the objects. No public full SQL/files/keys recovery target or minimum RAM/CPU/capacity guarantee was established.

facts.label: Webhooks and events
facts.value: Native HTTP POST JSON webhooks cover login/signup/logout, user/profile changes, invitations, roles/groups and other resource CRUD. Cloud limits: Basic 3, Premium 20, Enterprise/HA unlimited.

facts.label: Webhook retries and replay
facts.value: Delivery attempts persist as Webhook Event records. Background retry worker runs every 30 seconds, default maximum 3 retries; admins can manually Replay after failure.

facts.label: Custom fields and token claims
facts.value: User Properties is a map[string]string; account view/edit rules and signup fields configure exposure. JWT-Custom can select typed custom attributes; Token fields also restricts UserInfo.

facts.label: User CRUD, search and blocking
facts.value: Admin console/REST API supports user creation, list/search/filter, update, forbidding and hard/soft deletion. All standard Cloud plans include full administration/API access.

facts.label: Management credential scope
facts.value: Client ID/secret API calls run with organization-admin rights of the application; user bearer tokens run with that user’s permissions. Global operations have stricter checks.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: Native session-based impersonation and organization master-password option; Cloud support impersonation requires Premium+. Org admins can impersonate their org; global admins can impersonate across orgs.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking providers
facts.value: Native linking first checks an existing provider identity, then configured binding rules, default Email/Phone. Provider-specific Can unlink settings allow controlled unlinking.

facts.label: Guest upgrades
facts.value: A guest becomes normal-user when its username is changed to one without guest_ prefix or a password is set. The existing user record is updated.

facts.label: CAPTCHA and password controls
facts.value: built_in image CAPTCHA plus connectors for Turnstile, reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha, Aliyun and GeeTest; configurable None/Dynamic/Always/Internet-only rules. Password complexity, history and expiry controls are native.

facts.label: Leaked-password / SMS anti-fraud edition boundary
facts.value: China Commercial explicitly advertises breached-password blocking and SMS anti-abuse extras. Equivalent native free-core/standard Cloud entitlement and service semantics were not established.

facts.label: Authentication limits
facts.value: MFA guide gives default wrong-code/recovery-code limit 5 attempts and 15-minute freeze, configurable via application failed-signin settings. Code resend defaults 60 seconds; verification validity defaults 10 minutes.

facts.label: IP code protection and hosted API quotas
facts.value: v4.25 verification_ip.go implements 5 wrong-code attempts per IP+destination followed by 10-minute freeze; a complete hosted per-plan API/burst quota table was not found.

facts.label: Audit capture and export
facts.value: Native request records with actor/org/action, request URI/body masking and response status/detail. Org admins see their own records, global admins all; read via GET /api/get-records.

facts.label: Cloud Basic audit retention
facts.value: 7 days; Basic supports three webhooks but not Syslog/SIEM forwarding.

facts.label: Cloud Premium audit retention
facts.value: 90 days; up to 20 webhooks; Syslog/SIEM forwarding is not included.

facts.label: Cloud Enterprise/HA audit retention
facts.value: 1 year; unlimited webhooks; Syslog/SIEM forwarding included.

facts.label: Self-host log/token retention
facts.value: Audit records kept forever by default until Record retention days is set. Expired tokens kept default 30 days after expiry; cleanup runs at startup and daily midnight server time.

facts.label: Ordinary user export is masked
facts.value: Cloud includes bulk user export/REST access, but inspected v4.25 get-users/get-user controllers call masking: password becomes *, salt/type and TOTP secret/recovery codes are removed.

facts.label: Self-host full instance export
facts.value: Official -export writes unmasked users plus organizations/apps/providers/certificates/roles/groups/tokens/sessions and other instance objects to JSON. User model contains password/hash type/salt, TOTP secret, recovery codes and WebAuthn credentials.

facts.label: Cloud complete credential export route
facts.value: A public self-service/support process guaranteeing Cloud password hashes, MFA seeds, passkey records and signing configuration, with format/fee/completion deadline, was not established.

facts.label: Native import and identifiers
facts.value: Bulk XLSX import with preview/template, API user creation and JSON/YAML initialization can migrate users; username is unique within organization and a separate stable user ID is stored.

facts.label: Supported password forms and migration
facts.value: Organization storage options include bcrypt, Argon2id, salted SHA256/SHA512/MD5, PBKDF2-salt and Django PBKDF2. Imported user passwordType can preserve a pre-hashed password without hashing it again.

facts.label: Directory sync and credentials
facts.value: Native syncers cover SQL, Entra/Azure AD, Active Directory, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Okta, SCIM, AWS IAM, WeCom, DingTalk and Lark.

facts.label: User deletion and access removal
facts.value: Default delete removes the user row. Optional soft deletion marks it, keeps the record, revokes tokens/sessions and blocks login; deleting again hard-deletes, clearing the flag restores.

facts.label: Cloud suspension/deletion times
facts.value: PAYG zero balance stops instances; no top-up within 7 days permits deletion. Subscription end/failed renewal permits suspension and later permanent deletion without a published fixed purge interval.

facts.label: Retention and backup details
facts.value: Cloud privacy retains account/billing data for account/legal purposes and logs for a limited operational/security period; exact gateway-log and backup retention/restore periods were not published.

facts.label: Basic Cloud location
facts.value: Basic instances can be hosted in Singapore or Japan; a dedicated database is included. Basic does not include later region moves.

facts.label: Premium/Enterprise/HA region menu
facts.value: 23 advertised regions: US West, US East, Canada, Mexico; Brazil, Argentina; UK, Germany, Norway, Finland, Turkey; Australia, New Zealand; Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE; Japan, South Korea; Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam; India.

facts.label: Residency boundaries and self-hosting
facts.value: Privacy permits processing in several countries and directs strict-country requirements to pre-subscription contact. Self-host deployment/database region is selected by the operator.

facts.label: Privacy roles and providers
facts.value: Cloud privacy, updated October 8, 2026: Casbin is controller for website/account/billing and processor for instance Customer Data. Listed providers include Stripe, legacy Gumroad, infrastructure, Alibaba Cloud, Vercel, Tencent Exmail, Twilio and website analytics.

facts.label: DPA availability
facts.value: Terms/Enterprise support offer a DPA on request; an actual public DPA text, signed standard terms and exhaustive named infrastructure subprocessor list were not established.

facts.label: Certifications and assurance scope
facts.value: Cloud pricing FAQ explicitly says Casdoor Cloud does not currently hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification. Enterprise support offers SBOM, security questionnaire and vulnerability-process documentation.

facts.label: Name, operator and URLs
facts.value: Casdoor; Casdoor Cloud operated by Casbin Inc. Open-source/docs site https://casdoor.ai/; Cloud https://www.casdoor.com/; server https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor.

facts.label: Shutdown, sunset and acquisition check
facts.value: No official Casdoor shutdown, sunset or acquisition announcement found in the checked official sites, blog index, README and repository/release metadata.

facts.label: Available service and current release
facts.value: Cloud has public free-trial/instance-purchase paths. Latest non-prerelease server release is v4.25.0, published 2026-10-30T02:06:29Z.

facts.label: Core server license
facts.value: Apache-2.0, allowing commercial use, modification and redistribution subject to the license conditions. Self-host core has no mandatory per-user software license fee.

facts.label: SDK component licenses
facts.value: Official casdoor-js-sdk and casdoor-go-sdk repositories each publish Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Commercial support versus China editions
facts.value: Global Enterprise support page says the support contract is a service and does not gate open-source features. China pricing separately describes commercial-only/Enterprise-specific additions and local hardware/crypto compatibility.

facts.label: Public status endpoint check
facts.value: https://status.casdoor.com/ returned HTTP 500 during this check; no readable current status or incident-history feed was retrieved there.

facts.label: Enterprise HA availability promise
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise HA advertises 99.9% monthly uptime; standard terms guarantee no uptime unless agreed in writing. Basic/Premium/Enterprise comparison cells say no SLA.

facts.label: Enterprise SLA wording conflict
facts.value: Global Enterprise support FAQ says “Casdoor Cloud Enterprise includes a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA,” while its HA section and detailed pricing comparison reserve that SLA to Enterprise HA.

facts.label: Release and repository maintenance
facts.value: Latest stable/non-prerelease server v4.25.0 published October 30, 2026; repository metadata archived=false/disabled=false, latest push November 4, 2026 at this check.

facts.label: Security policy / supported releases
facts.value: SECURITY.md directs private vulnerability reports to admin@casdoor.org. Public guaranteed response deadline and maintained-version/backport matrix were not established; Enterprise support offers a designated LTS line/backports by contract.

facts.label: Community and hosted support
facts.value: Free self-host help: GitHub issues/discussions, Discord and Google Groups. Cloud Basic first response 2 business days; Premium 1 business day with 8×5 support.

facts.label: Enterprise support conditions
facts.value: Cloud Enterprise/HA first response 4 business hours with priority 8×5 support; HA named engineer/extended hours by contract. Global self-host support: annual quote, 8×5/one business day generally, four business hours for production-down incidents.

apps.name: Clerk
apps.line: Hosted sign-in with ready-made components and organizations.

free.text: Hobby: $0/month, 50,000 monthly returning users

cells.freeUsers: 50,000 MRU per app
cells.sso: 1 SSO connection included; extra $75/month each (2-15)

mau.math: 1,000 users is within the 50,000 monthly returning users included, so the base is $0.
10,000 users is within the 50,000 monthly returning users included, so the base is $0.
50,000 users is exactly the limit of monthly returning users included, so the base is $0.
On the Pro plan: $25 base, plus $0.02 for each monthly returning user above the 50,000 included in the plan. For 100,000 users, that is $1,025 in total.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no qualifying finding of sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, major paid feature retirement, data-exposing breach or regulatory action found.

facts.label: User billing definition
facts.value: MRU: a distinct user who visits during the month at least 24 hours after signup; new users who never return after the first day do not count.

facts.label: Organization billing definition
facts.value: MRO: an Organization with at least two members and at least one monthly retained user in that month.

facts.label: Subscription billing scope
facts.value: The plan covers every application in the developer workspace; canceling changes the workspace's plan.

facts.label: Connection-meter details
facts.value: SSO and Directory Sync are separate connection meters. Exact inactive-connection treatment, midmonth proration and rounding were not established.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Hobby: USD $0/month; 50,000 MRU per application.

facts.label: Free business allowance
facts.value: All base plans: 100 MRO/application in production; 50 MRO in Development.

facts.label: Minimum paid plan: monthly
facts.value: Pro: USD $25/month on monthly billing.

facts.label: Minimum paid plan: annual
facts.value: Pro: USD $20/month equivalent, billed annually; USD $240/year is our calculation, 20 × 12.

facts.label: Business: monthly
facts.value: Business: USD $300/month on monthly billing.

facts.label: Business: annual
facts.value: Business: USD $250/month equivalent, billed annually; USD $3,000/year is our calculation, 250 × 12.

facts.label: Enterprise commitment
facts.value: Enterprise: custom price; annual billing only.

facts.label: Payment, renewal and taxes
facts.value: Subscription charges may recur monthly or annually; usage is billed monthly; taxes are extra. Subscriptions renew unless canceled.

facts.label: MRU usage: included and first band
facts.value: Pro/Business: 50,000 MRU/application included; MRU 50,001–100,000: USD $0.02 each/month.

facts.label: Business cost examples
facts.value: A: Pro + Enhanced B2B, $125/month. B: Pro + Enhanced B2B + nine extra SAML connections, $800/month. USD; our calculation.

facts.label: Organization member allowance
facts.value: Without Enhanced B2B: up to 20 members/Organization; default configured limit is 5 and must be raised where needed.

facts.label: Enhanced B2B member entitlement
facts.value: Enhanced B2B permits unlimited members per Organization.

facts.label: Enhanced B2B base fee
facts.value: USD $100/month on monthly billing, or $85/month equivalent billed annually; applies across the workspace's applications.

facts.label: Organization membership and creation limits
facts.value: A user may join unlimited Organizations. User-created Organizations default to 100 per user; higher creation limits require support.

facts.label: Production SSO fee
facts.value: Pro/Business: one SSO connection/application included. Additional connections/month: 2–15 $75 each; 16–100 $60; 101–250 $48; 251+ quote. USD.

facts.label: Hobby and development enterprise connections
facts.value: Hobby has no production enterprise connections. Development SSO connections are free, with a maximum of 25.

facts.label: Directory Sync: current charge
facts.value: Directory Sync production access requires Pro/Business; connections have no charge through December 31, 2026.

facts.label: Directory Sync: announced rate
facts.value: From January 1, 2027: one connection/application included; additional 2–15 $75, 16–100 $60, 101–250 $48 each/month; 251+ quote. USD.

facts.label: Organization-linked self-service setup
facts.value: Self-serve SSO and Directory Sync: Pro/Business + Enhanced B2B in production; free in development.

facts.label: Applications, seats: Hobby and Pro
facts.value: Unlimited applications; up to three developer dashboard seats. Four or more seats require Business.

facts.label: Seats: Business
facts.value: Ten dashboard seats included; additional seats USD $20/month each.

facts.label: Environments
facts.value: Each application has separate Development and Production instances; a new app starts in Development.

facts.label: Domain scope
facts.value: One primary domain with subdomains; additional distinct domains use the satellite-domain feature.

facts.label: Clerk-managed email delivery
facts.value: Clerk can send authentication emails through its own provider; production messages use the app's domain, development uses accounts.dev.

facts.label: Own email or SMS delivery
facts.value: Per-template self-delivery is documented: disable Delivered by Clerk and handle emails.created or sms.created webhooks.

facts.label: Production email price and volume cap
facts.value: No separate public production email-send price or numeric production email allowance was found.

facts.label: SMS: production price
facts.value: Paid production phone authentication: USD $0.01/SMS to US/Canada; other destinations: market rate.

facts.label: SMS country controls
facts.value: Only US and Canada are enabled by default; the SMS country allowlist can be changed.

facts.label: Development delivery limits
facts.value: Free development: 100 delivered emails and 20 SMS/calendar month; daily distinct email recipients: 50 for a workspace's first seven days, then 100.

facts.label: Free MRU/MRO limit behavior
facts.value: One-month grace after exceeding free MRU/MRO allowances, then upgrade required: Pro for users, Enhanced B2B for Organizations.

facts.label: Machine-auth limit behavior
facts.value: Hobby is limited to free API-key/M2M usage; upgrade to Pro to go beyond the included units.

facts.label: Nonpayment
facts.value: Unpaid fees can lead to suspension after ten days' written notice.

facts.label: Hard spending cap
facts.value: A configurable, universal hard spending cap was not found.

facts.label: API-key metering
facts.value: 1,000 creations and 100,000 verifications/month free; paid overage $0.001/creation and $0.00001/verification. USD.

facts.label: M2M metering
facts.value: 2,500 creations and 100,000 verifications/month free; overage $0.001/creation and $0.00001/verification. USD.

facts.label: Protect charges
facts.value: Pricing lists 10,000 protection checks/month free, then USD $0.002/check; custom pricing above 1 million checks.

facts.label: Protect meter boundary
facts.value: Unknown exact events counted as a paid protection check, and whether every Business authentication attempt enters that meter.

facts.label: Administration add-on
facts.value: Five impersonations/month included; Enhanced Administration: $100/month or $85/month equivalent annually for unlimited impersonations. USD.

facts.label: Clerk Billing fee
facts.value: Optional subscription billing: 0.7% of billing volume; payment-processor fees are additional.

facts.label: Billing responsibility
facts.value: The app owner remains merchant of record and handles taxes, refunds and payment disputes.

facts.label: Satellite-domain fee
facts.value: Pro and above: USD $10/month for each satellite domain.

facts.label: Market and legal restrictions
facts.value: Business use; customer must comply with sanctions and export controls and must not be a prohibited/restricted party.

facts.label: Solo-builder and country eligibility
facts.value: Personal workspaces are documented. An exhaustive supported billing-country list and an explicit rule for unincorporated individuals opening production accounts were not found.

facts.label: Free self-service entry
facts.value: Hobby starts without a credit card; ongoing free use is advertised.

facts.label: Trial rules
facts.value: Pro features can be tried in a development instance without a conventional time-limited trial.

facts.label: Production prerequisites
facts.value: A domain the builder owns, DNS editing access and the builder's own production OAuth credentials for each selected social provider.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Vendor-hosted authentication and user management: accounts, sign-up/sign-in, sessions, verification, Organizations and enterprise login connections.

facts.label: Operating responsibilities
facts.value: Clerk runs the account service and authentication APIs; the developer operates the application, handles authorization checks and configures integrations.

facts.label: Password and username login
facts.value: Built-in password sign-in and username identifiers; username is an identifier, not a separate proof of identity.

facts.label: Email-code login
facts.value: Built-in six-digit email codes are included on Hobby.

facts.label: Email-link login
facts.value: Built-in email-link login. Links expire after ten minutes and can require verification in the same device/browser.

facts.label: Phone-code login
facts.value: Built-in SMS OTP; paid plan required in production, available for development testing.

facts.label: Base wallet login
facts.value: Base account login through SIWE-compatible wallet signatures; can link a Base account from UserProfile.

facts.label: MetaMask wallet login
facts.value: Built-in MetaMask wallet login; browser wallet extension setup is documented.

facts.label: Coinbase Wallet login
facts.value: Coinbase Smart Wallet and browser wallet extension supported for wallet authentication.

facts.label: OKX Wallet login
facts.value: Built-in OKX wallet signup/signin and linking through profile UI.

facts.label: Anonymous login
facts.value: Guest/anonymous users appear in the official feature-request backlog; a shipped anonymous-login API was not established.

facts.label: Solana wallet login
facts.value: Built-in Sign in with Solana accepts the user's preferred Solana-enabled wallet rather than one named wallet application.

facts.label: SMS entitlement conflict
facts.value: The official pricing guide's all-plans summary includes SMS OTP, while the current strategy docs require a paid plan for production phone authentication.

facts.label: Social integration model
facts.value: Built-in social connections; production requires provider-specific OAuth credentials. Development often uses shared Clerk credentials.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: Built-in Google OAuth and Google One Tap. Production requires custom credentials and a Google OAuth app published for production.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: Built-in Apple social connection. Web production requires Apple developer setup, Services ID, key, Team ID and Key ID.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: Built-in GitHub OAuth; create a provider OAuth app and set its client ID/secret and callback for production.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: Built-in Microsoft Entra ID social connection supports the common audience: work, school and personal accounts.

facts.label: Other named social providers
facts.value: AgentID, Atlassian, Bitbucket, Box, Coinbase, Discord, Dropbox, Facebook, GitLab, HubSpot, Hugging Face, LINE, Linear, LinkedIn, Notion, Slack, Spotify, TikTok, Twitch, Vercel, X/Twitter v2 and Xero.

facts.label: Custom social provider
facts.value: Custom OIDC-compatible social provider; discovery or manually configured endpoints, attribute mapping, optional Authorization Code with PKCE.

facts.label: Social-connection plan gate
facts.value: Hobby permits up to three social connections; Pro removes that provider-count limit.

facts.label: Passkey production plan gate
facts.value: Passkey sign-in requires a paid production plan; available free in Development.

facts.label: Web autofill
facts.value: Passkey sign-in exposes autofill and discoverable flows in the current SignInFuture API.

facts.label: Passkey domain restrictions
facts.value: A passkey is tied to its registration domain; a root-domain credential can cover its subdomains. It does not move between unrelated primary/satellite domains.

facts.label: Android passkeys
facts.value: Supported on Android 9+ with registered package name and SHA-256 certificate fingerprints; physical device required.

facts.label: Expo passkeys
facts.value: @clerk/expo-passkeys native package; iOS 16+ or Android 9+, native development build; does not work in Expo Go.

facts.label: Electron passkeys: beta
facts.value: Renderer mode uses Chromium WebAuthn on a matching HTTPS origin. Native mode requires optional @clerk/electron-passkeys and is supported on macOS/Windows, not Linux.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Paid production MFA supports authenticator TOTP, SMS and backup codes; can require enrollment app-wide or let users opt in.

facts.label: Passkeys and MFA: versioned support
facts.value: A passkey can satisfy MFA and can be used as a second factor on current SDKs; older instances need the relevant update.

facts.label: Passkey/MFA documentation conflict
facts.value: The current strategy page still says passkeys cannot be enrolled as a dedicated MFA method, while its later section describes passkeys as a second factor. The July security article says second-factor passkeys are unavailable.

facts.label: Backup codes and lost-factor recovery
facts.value: Single-use backup codes are generated at enrollment in prebuilt UI; users can regenerate them. If no factor/passkey/code remains, an admin or custom backend reset is needed.

facts.label: Reset side effects
facts.value: Removing MFA does not revoke sessions or change the password. A compromise response must revoke sessions separately.

facts.label: Email as second check
facts.value: Device Trust can ask for an email code/link on a new-device password login when the user has not enabled MFA.

facts.label: Verification and identifier changes
facts.value: Users can add/change/remove email addresses, phone numbers and usernames; admins can disable those self-service changes.

facts.label: Forgot password
facts.value: Email or phone must be enabled. Clerk sends a code, verifies it, replaces the password and signs the user in; other sessions can be signed out.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: User deletion is supported in prebuilt profile flows when allowed in instance settings, and through dashboard/Backend API administration.

facts.label: Sensitive account actions
facts.value: Prebuilt components reverify identity for changes to password/identifiers, external accounts, MFA/passkeys, session revocation and account deletion.

facts.label: Session token model
facts.value: Stateful sessions plus signed 60-second JWT session tokens; browser SDK refreshes approximately every 50 seconds.

facts.label: Session lifetime: Hobby
facts.value: Fixed seven-day maximum lifetime in production.

facts.label: Session lifetime: paid
facts.value: Custom web maximum/inactivity settings; separate native maximum can be five minutes to ten years where supported.

facts.label: Revoke devices and sessions
facts.value: Dashboard can revoke one device or all devices; Backend SDK revokeSession is documented.

facts.label: Multiple accounts in one browser
facts.value: Simultaneous sessions/account switching moved into Pro in the February 2026 plan change.

facts.label: Unauthorized-device email action
facts.value: Paid production apps can let users revoke an unfamiliar-device session directly from the notification email.

facts.label: Custom session claims
facts.value: Custom claims can be added; browser cookie capacity leaves about 1.2KB for custom claims after default claims.

facts.label: SAML protocol role
facts.value: Inbound enterprise SAML: Clerk connects as the application's service provider to an external IdP. Both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows are supported.

facts.label: OIDC and EASIE protocol roles
facts.value: Inbound OIDC client to custom compatible IdPs; EASIE uses multi-tenant Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra providers.

facts.label: Customer self-service SSO
facts.value: Organization admins can configure SAML or custom OIDC through OrganizationProfile; must enable self-serve SSO per Organization.

facts.label: Customer workspaces and authorization
facts.value: Users may belong to several Organizations and switch active context. Organization membership, roles and permissions are exposed in the session.

facts.label: Built-in roles
facts.value: Admin and Member roles; custom permissions can extend what those roles allow.

facts.label: Custom-role plan and ceiling
facts.value: Production custom roles require Enhanced B2B; docs allow ten custom Organization roles per instance, with support for increases.

facts.label: Custom-role ceiling conflict
facts.value: Pricing says unlimited custom roles; implementation docs specify ten per application instance unless support raises the limit.

facts.label: Role Sets
facts.value: One modifiable Primary Role Set is free. Additional Role Sets require Enhanced B2B; each Organization is assigned one set of available roles.

facts.label: Membership requirement
facts.value: Organizations are disabled initially; enabling them can require every user to create/join an Organization or allow personal accounts.

facts.label: Provisioning protocol and providers
facts.value: Directory Sync supports SCIM 2.0 for Okta, Entra and custom providers; Google Workspace uses Google Admin SDK polling instead.

facts.label: Deactivation behavior
facts.value: On IdP removal/disable, Clerk marks the user deprovisioned and revokes active sessions after the change syncs.

facts.label: Groups, attributes and roles
facts.value: Directory groups can map to Organization roles; precedence follows mapping order. Directory-owned attributes are read-only in Clerk.

facts.label: Self-service Directory Sync
facts.value: Organization admins can set up a directory through OrganizationProfile after self-serve SSO is enabled; Pro/Business + Enhanced B2B in production.

facts.label: Hosted account screens
facts.value: Account Portal hosts sign-in, sign-up, user profile, Organization creation/profile, waitlist and unauthorized-sign-in confirmation.

facts.label: Embedded and custom screens
facts.value: Prebuilt SignIn, SignUp and UserProfile components; low-level API primitives support fully custom flows.

facts.label: Expo native views
facts.value: Prebuilt native Expo components use SwiftUI on iOS and Jetpack Compose on Android; this native-component path is beta.

facts.label: Brand removal by plan
facts.value: Hobby retains Clerk branding; Pro and above allow its removal.

facts.label: Theming depth
facts.value: Appearance settings support themes, colors/fonts, layout options, CSS layers and individual element overrides.

facts.label: Primary custom domain
facts.value: Custom domain included on Hobby; production setup requires DNS records on the builder's domain.

facts.label: Satellite-domain compatibility
facts.value: Paid production feature; supported with server rendering in Next.js, TanStack Start and Nuxt. Other React frameworks require avoiding SSR/hydration.

facts.label: Changing primary domain
facts.value: Production domain can change through dashboard/API; development domain cannot. DNS, certificates, publishable key and provider redirects need updating.

facts.label: Translated embedded UI
facts.value: Experimental @clerk/localizations supplies tags ar-SA, be-BY, bn-IN, bg-BG, ca-ES, zh-CN, zh-TW, hr-HR, cs-CZ, da-DK, nl-BE, nl-NL, en-GB, en-US, fa-IR, fi-FI, fr-FR, de-DE, el-GR, he-IL, hi-IN, hu-HU, is-IS, it-IT, id-ID, ja-JP, kk-KZ, ko-KR, ms-MY, mn-MN, nb-NO, pl-PL, pt-BR, pt-PT, ro-RO, ru-RU, sr-RS, sk-SK, es-ES, es-CR, es-MX, es-UY, sv-SE, ta-IN, te-IN, th-TH, tr-TR, uk-UA and vi-VN.

facts.label: Hosted-page language limit
facts.value: The localization package changes embedded components; the hosted Account Portal remains in English.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Vendor describes prebuilt UI as accessibility-optimized; no public app-UI VPAT/ACR or scoped WCAG audit report was found.

facts.label: Official web integrations
facts.value: Next.js, React, TanStack React Start, React Router, Astro, JavaScript, Nuxt and Vue.

facts.label: Official backend SDKs
facts.value: Express, Fastify, Go, C#, Java, PHP, Python and Ruby/Rails/Sinatra; JavaScript Backend SDK is also documented.

facts.label: Community integrations
facts.value: Angular, Elysia, Flutter, Hono, Koa, Rust, SolidJS, Svelte and Tauri are listed as community-maintained.

facts.label: Runtime compatibility
facts.value: Core 3 JavaScript SDKs: Node.js >=20.9.0 and browsers released within the last two years. Core 2: Node.js >=18.17.0.

facts.label: Next.js integration
facts.value: Official @clerk/nextjs integration includes middleware/proxy setup and ClerkProvider for App Router.

facts.label: Edge backend runtime
facts.value: @clerk/backend is built for Node.js and V8 isolates, including Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge Runtime.

facts.label: Native iOS
facts.value: Official clerk-ios SDK with ClerkKit and optional ClerkKitUI; Native API and associated webcredentials domain setup documented.

facts.label: Native Android
facts.value: Official Kotlin SDK; Android minimum SDK 24 and Java >=17. Separate API and UI packages are documented.

facts.label: React Native / Expo
facts.value: Official @clerk/expo; token storage can use expo-secure-store, and hosted authentication uses Expo browser/auth-session packages.

facts.label: Browser extensions and community mobile/desktop
facts.value: First-party Chrome Extension SDK; Flutter and Tauri listed as community-maintained.

facts.label: Electron storage dependency
facts.value: Electron beta SDK can persist its session token with optional electron-store; current guide supports electron-store@8.

facts.label: Authentication database
facts.value: Clerk supplies its user table. An application can use session claims without maintaining a mirrored local user table.

facts.label: External dependencies
facts.value: Production domain/DNS and chosen social-provider credentials required; own database and webhook endpoint depend on app features.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted Clerk service described here.

facts.label: User metadata
facts.value: Public metadata: backend writes, client reads. Private: backend-only. Unsafe: client and backend read/write. Total metadata limit: 8KB.

facts.label: Custom flows and logic
facts.value: Custom onboarding/auth flows use Clerk APIs; JWT templates support customized tokens for external integrations.

facts.label: Webhook delivery
facts.value: Svix-backed asynchronous events; retries, possible duplicate deliveries and no ordering guarantee; dashboard replay is available.

facts.label: Synchronous hosted hooks
facts.value: A general hosted pre-login/pre-user-create code-hook runtime, its execution limits and price were not found.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Dashboard and Backend SDK/API can create, retrieve/list and delete users; end users manage their own profile through frontend components/APIs.

facts.label: User impersonation
facts.value: Five free impersonations/month; dashboard entry and actor-token API support impersonated sessions.

facts.label: Banning users
facts.value: Banning is a documented Backend API action; the pricing table excludes user bans from Hobby.

facts.label: Developer dashboard access
facts.value: Workspace roles include Owner, Admin, Developer, Support and Viewer, with documented feature permissions.

facts.label: Automatic social account linking
facts.value: Matching email triggers linking; verified provider email links to an existing verified Clerk email, while unverified cases require additional verification/security steps.

facts.label: Linking different emails
facts.value: A signed-in user can add another email through UserProfile so OAuth accounts using either address can link to the same Clerk account.

facts.label: Enterprise account linking
facts.value: Enterprise SSO attempts to link by email; verified IdP email can link to the matching existing account.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and merges
facts.value: A built-in anonymous-to-registered upgrade flow was not established. Separate user.merged events and a backend merge operation are documented.

facts.label: Bot challenges
facts.value: Challenge suspicious sign-ups uses Cloudflare Turnstile; included and on by default for new apps. Business is required to change its setting.

facts.label: Lockout protection
facts.value: Default for new instances: ten failed attempts, then one-hour lockout; included on all plans. Admin/API unlock supported.

facts.label: Breached-password checks
facts.value: Checks known compromised passwords at set/change and sign-in through HaveIBeenPwned; enabled by default for new apps.

facts.label: Device Trust
facts.value: New-device password login can require email/SMS/link verification even without user-enabled MFA; free on all plans.

facts.label: Enrollment restrictions
facts.value: Open, invite-only and waitlist modes; paid production allowlist/blocklist can restrict signup identifiers.

facts.label: User enumeration protection
facts.value: Strict mode masks whether an identifier exists and changes signup/signin responses; password-first flows have documented constraints.

facts.label: Advanced protection example
facts.value: Business can cap signups per email domain per hour; off by default, default threshold 20, minimum 1.

facts.label: Frontend create/attempt limits
facts.value: Per IP/user: create sign-in or sign-up 5 requests/10 seconds; first/second-factor sign-in attempts or signup verification 3/10 seconds.

facts.label: Backend general limit
facts.value: Per application instance/Secret Key: production 1,000 requests/10 seconds; development 100/10 seconds, including GET.

facts.label: Invitation limits
facts.value: Individual application invitations 100/hour; bulk 25/hour. Organization invitations 250/hour; Organization bulk invitations 50/hour.

facts.label: Update limits and recovery
facts.value: User, Organization and membership updates: 10 requests/10 seconds per respective resource. 429 responses include Retry-After seconds; JWKS has no stated rate limit.

facts.label: Logs: Hobby
facts.value: Application and email logs: one day; Admin Logs unavailable.

facts.label: Logs: Pro
facts.value: Application and email logs: seven days; Admin Logs unavailable.

facts.label: Logs: Business
facts.value: Application, email and Admin Logs: 30 days.

facts.label: Logs: Enterprise
facts.value: Custom retention; continuous log drains to customer-owned storage are an Enterprise feature.

facts.label: Application-event coverage
facts.value: Sign-up/sign-in, password/MFA/passkey changes, sessions, Organization activity, Protect and SCIM events are documented.

facts.label: Administrative events
facts.value: Configuration, domain, secret/key, role/permission, connection and dashboard/backend/platform administration events.

facts.label: Email delivery inspection
facts.value: Delivery states include accepted, delivered, deferred, bounced, dropped, blocked and complained; role controls apply.

facts.label: SMS delivery inspection
facts.value: Clerk-sent SMS delivery events share Application Logs retention; own-provider messages are not captured.

facts.label: Self-service export and password hashes
facts.value: Dashboard export produces CSV user data including password hashes; admins or users in their personal workspace can request/download it.

facts.label: Programmatic user retrieval
facts.value: GetUserList / getUserList retrieves users and profile information through the Backend API.

facts.label: Export entitlement
facts.value: Full user-data exports are listed on every plan, including Hobby; no assistance is required for dashboard export.

facts.label: Credential portability gaps
facts.value: Complete CSV column schema, exported provider links/tokens, Organization-role export, and passkey credential export/transfer procedure were not established.

facts.label: Bulk migration in
facts.value: Official JSON/CSV migration tool creates users through the Backend API and respects rate limits; snapshot migrations can require a coordinated cutover.

facts.label: Supported password hash import
facts.value: createUser accepts passwordDigest/passwordHasher, including argon2i/argon2id, bcrypt variants, PBKDF2 variants, Firebase scrypt, Werkzeug scrypt, phpass, LDAP SSHA and legacy MD5/SHA schemes.

facts.label: Lazy migration
facts.value: Trickle migration is documented; the Cognito-specific awscognito hasher can migrate to bcrypt after successful verification.

facts.label: User deletion and app-owned data
facts.value: Clerk can delete the user; a user.deleted webhook can delete/mark that user's records in the application's own database.

facts.label: Vendor account and workspace deletion
facts.value: Cancel the paid plan before deleting the dashboard account. Deleting a sole-member workspace's account also deletes its apps/users; workspace deletion itself requires support.

facts.label: Cancellation behavior
facts.value: Canceling a self-service plan keeps its features until the billing cycle ends, then moves the workspace to Hobby; usage charges accrue until then.

facts.label: End-of-contract data removal
facts.value: DPA: request return/self-service copy by termination/expiry; Clerk deletes other customer personal-data copies within 90 days and seeks subprocessor deletion.

facts.label: Backups and individual deletion timing
facts.value: No public numeric backup-retention/rotation schedule, customer restore target or individual-user purge deadline was found.

facts.label: Builder personal-data retention
facts.value: Privacy policy keeps controller-held information while needed for service, disputes, legal defenses, audits and legal obligations; no single numeric period.

facts.label: Data region and residency
facts.value: US-hosted infrastructure; region choice and regional data residency are not offered.

facts.label: Location detail gaps
facts.value: Exact primary/backup cloud regions and separate log/backup locations were not established.

facts.label: Controller/processor scope
facts.value: Builder account/marketing data: Clerk controller. Customer end-user data: customer controller, Clerk processor/service provider under contract.

facts.label: DPA and international transfers
facts.value: Public DPA; Clerk claims DPF self-certification, with SCC provisions when DPF cannot be relied upon.

facts.label: DPF notice
facts.value: Public EU-US, UK-extension and Swiss-US DPF notice; effective February 22, 2024.

facts.label: SOC 2 evidence and access
facts.value: Clerk claims SOC 2 Type 2 since May 6, 2022; report access is Business and above via support.

facts.label: HIPAA scope
facts.value: Clerk advertises HIPAA evidence; a signed BAA is available on Enterprise.

facts.label: ISO and PCI claims
facts.value: Clerk says it is not ISO 27001 certified; infrastructure-provider certification is separate. Clerk makes no PCI DSS claim because it does not store cardholder data.

facts.label: Subprocessor list retrieval
facts.value: Current subprocessor list is linked from the legal page to Drata trust portal, but the portal did not expose readable list content.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Clerk; contract entity Clerk, Inc.; official site https://clerk.com/ and documentation https://clerk.com/docs.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Available for self-service use; current public docs show Core 3. Signup and production activation were not tested.

facts.label: Retired pricing edition
facts.value: The former Enhanced Authentication add-on was removed in the February 5, 2026 plan change; much of it moved into Pro.

facts.label: Hosted commercial-use terms
facts.value: Hosted service access is licensed under the subscription agreement; use for the customer's business and its own customers/end users is covered, subject to restrictions.

facts.label: SDK license
facts.value: Clerk JavaScript repository: MIT; commercial use, modification and redistribution permitted subject to retaining notices.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: Public component-level status page covers authentication, sessions, webhooks, hosted UI, enterprise/SCIM, email/SMS and dashboard.

facts.label: Availability promise
facts.value: Enterprise advertises 99.99% uptime SLA; other plans have no equivalent percentage established here.

facts.label: SLA terms not public
facts.value: Measurement period, downtime definition, exclusions and service-credit schedule were not found publicly.

facts.label: Supported release families
facts.value: Core 3 active since January 2026; Core 2 in long-term support through January 2027; older Core 1/legacy unsupported.

facts.label: Dated maintenance evidence
facts.value: October 30, 2026 changelog announces public Application Logs API with its retention, limits and export restrictions.

facts.label: Component update control
facts.value: Clerk recommends pinning SDK, ClerkJS and the prebuilt UI layer when a fixed implementation is required.

facts.label: Security reporting policy
facts.value: Public repository security policy routes vulnerability reports to Clerk's disclosure policy; report privately, not through public issues.

facts.label: Vulnerability disclosure terms
facts.value: security@clerk.dev; initial confirmation within three business days; coordinated disclosure window 90 days.

facts.label: Support routes and free limits
facts.value: Hobby: community Discord and email for billing, registration and abuse; Business adds priority support.

facts.label: Enterprise Premium targets
facts.value: P1 <4 business hours; P2 <8; P3/P4 <16. Slack included; no dedicated technical account manager.

facts.label: Enterprise Platinum targets
facts.value: P1 <2 hours, 24/7; P2 <4 business hours; P3 <6; P4 <8. Dedicated technical account manager included.

facts.label: Support submission and scope
facts.value: Designated dashboard-seat contacts can use support@clerk.com or the support portal; Slack is not an approved formal incident-report channel.

cells.freeUsers: 100 users; shared hosting and no SLA
