facts.label: User billing unit
facts.value: Total user accounts connected to a Keycloak deployment, including identity-provider, social, Azure AD and LDAP users; not monthly active users or login days.

facts.label: Inactive users and allowance scope
facts.value: Inactive registered accounts count. Vendor example: 49,000 registered users and 11,000 MAU require the 50,000-user tier.

facts.label: Account-count edge cases
facts.value: Public guidance does not fully specify cross-realm person deduplication or whether every administrative/service-account identity contributes to the commercial user counter.

facts.label: Free allowance
facts.value: Free: €0; up to 100 users and 1 realm on shared AWS eu-west-3 hosting; no SLA.

facts.label: Free management/export restrictions
facts.value: Conflicting: pricing.txt lists one Free export per day and API access, while the current Free/plan and API guides exclude Cloud-IAM export/backups and Cloud-IAM management API access on shared Free hosting.

facts.label: Lowest public monthly paid rate
facts.value: Starter, Scaleway, 250 total users and 100 realms: €99/month excluding tax.

facts.label: Renewal and contractual commitment
facts.value: Monthly or annual advance billing; annual option is 10% lower. Auto-renewal is the documented default; manual renewal can be requested.

facts.label: Termination notice
facts.value: Public Terms of Service specify three months' prior notice for termination; subscription duration is specified in the subscription form.

facts.label: Premium monthly user bands
facts.value: Scaleway Premium: 250 users €1,299; 500 €1,599; 1,000 €1,899; 5,000 €2,599; 10,000 €3,199; 50,000 €4,399; 250,000 €5,199, per month excluding tax. The 1,000,000-user Premium offer is quote-only.

facts.label: Provider differences and negotiated plans
facts.value: At 1,000 users/month Starter is €299 on Scaleway or AWS, €399 on Google Cloud, and €699 on Outscale or Azure. Max and larger negotiated capacities require a quote.

facts.label: Annual pricing and included services
facts.value: Annual subscription receives 10% off the monthly rate for 12 months; infrastructure, monitoring, backups and the selected support level are included. Native SSO/client integrations are not separately metered.

facts.label: Business scenario coverage
facts.value: Our calculation: A (1,000 users, 10 customer organizations, 1 SAML connection) €299/month; B (10,000 users, 100 organizations, 10 SAML connections) €499/month, excluding VAT.

facts.label: Customer organization billing
facts.value: Native Keycloak organizations and groups are server capabilities; the Cloud-IAM rate card does not add a per-customer-organization, per-member-role or per-invitation charge.

facts.label: Organization and member ceilings
facts.value: No numeric Cloud-IAM allowance or per-organization member/invitation ceiling found for native Keycloak Organizations.

facts.label: Business SSO prices
facts.value: Native Keycloak SAML/OIDC identity providers, clients and federation integrations are included without a published per-connection fee or setup fee.

facts.label: SCIM price and version gate
facts.value: Native SCIM is production-ready in Keycloak 26.8, available on Cloud-IAM; no separate native-SCIM license fee is listed. Optional commercial extensions have their own subscriptions.

facts.label: Realm and deployment caps
facts.value: Free: 1 realm. Published paid self-service bands: 100 realms per dedicated deployment. Subscription is per deployment.

facts.label: Developer seats and console organizations
facts.value: Cloud-IAM console organizations have Owner, Editor and narrower operational roles and support invitations. Numeric builder-seat/project caps or extra-seat prices were not found.

facts.label: Transactional email
facts.value: Builder must supply its own SMTP relay/provider for verification, password reset and invitation emails; Cloud-IAM does not provide a built-in SMTP relay.

facts.label: SMS and email OTP delivery
facts.value: SMS/email one-time codes require a Keycloak extension and a delivery integration; the Cloud-IAM SMS catalog example uses Twilio.

facts.label: User/realm limit behavior
facts.value: User and realm limits are soft: Cloud-IAM contacts the customer to remove accounts/realms or upgrade. It says it does not stop deployments without multiple prior notices.

facts.label: Optional extension charges
facts.value: Vendor-maintained paid extensions add a monthly or annual subscription tied to the deployment; price depends on support level.

facts.label: Unpublished add-on amounts
facts.value: Exact public prices for Email OTP, SMS OTP, the IdP Wizard and webhook catalog extensions were not found.

facts.label: Other service charges
facts.value: Extended Security Lifecycle and bespoke consulting are additional offerings; no public complete rate card found for them.

facts.label: Individual or company eligibility
facts.value: Terms define the customer as a natural or legal person, so an incorporated company is not an explicit prerequisite in that definition.

facts.label: Market and restricted countries
facts.value: France-based provider; complete allowed/restricted buyer-country list not found.

facts.label: Self-service entry and free testing
facts.value: Self-service deployment creation; Free/Freemium is offered for learning and testing and is not recommended for production.

facts.label: Signup and card requirements
facts.value: Public signup instructions request first/last name, professional email and password, with email verification; phone is optional. Free signup is advertised without a credit card.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Hosted, managed Keycloak: accounts, login, sessions, verification and business identity brokering. Free shared deployment and paid dedicated deployments.

facts.label: Server and application responsibilities
facts.value: Cloud-IAM runs the managed Keycloak infrastructure. The builder configures realms, clients and login flows, and operates the application and its integrations.

facts.label: Backups and upgrades
facts.value: Vendor manages backup infrastructure and version-tested export/restore procedures; paid deployments expose backups and upgrade controls. Builder still chooses and tests application configuration, themes and extensions.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in: username or email plus password; user self-registration and forgotten-password flows are configurable.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: plugin/custom_code: email magic-link login is not native; use a compatible Keycloak extension and SMTP.

facts.label: Email and phone codes
facts.value: plugin/external_service: email OTP and SMS OTP require extensions; SMS also needs a message provider.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: Anonymous-account login/upgrade and crypto-wallet sign-in were not established.

facts.label: Social Google integration
facts.value: built_in: Google as an external social identity provider; register/configure the Google application and redirect URI.

facts.label: Other native social providers
facts.value: Keycloak 26.8.1 documents GitHub, GitLab, Microsoft, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bitbucket, OpenShift, PayPal and Stack Overflow integrations, alongside generic OIDC/SAML providers.

facts.label: Apple provider status
facts.value: A supported native Apple adapter/setup was not established from the checked provider list; the Cloud-IAM overview's Apple example is not a complete integration guide.

facts.label: Passkeys and security keys
facts.value: built_in: WebAuthn/FIDO2 passwordless sign-in using supported platform authenticators or security keys; can be a first factor or part of MFA.

facts.label: Conditional passkey UI and domain binding
facts.value: Keycloak 26.8.1 supports passkey/conditional UI configuration. Configure the relying-party ID; changing the login domain can affect whether an existing passkey is usable.

facts.label: Native MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: built_in: authenticator HOTP/TOTP and WebAuthn/security-key factors; administrators can configure required actions and conditional flows.

facts.label: Recovery codes and fallback
facts.value: Keycloak 26.8.1 documents built-in recovery authentication codes and multiple credentials; recovery must be enabled in the authentication flow/required actions.

facts.label: Verification, reset and profile lifecycle
facts.value: built_in: email verification, reset password, user-profile/email updates and admin-managed account disable/delete. Delivery uses configured SMTP.

facts.label: End-user account deletion
facts.value: Built-in Account Console can show Delete Account when the delete-account role and required action are configured; deletion is irreversible in the live Keycloak account store.

facts.label: Session and token controls
facts.value: Keycloak supports SSO idle/max lifetimes, remember-me and client/offline-session overrides; OIDC access and refresh tokens are issued by the server.

facts.label: Lost-device sign-out and revocation
facts.value: Users/admins can view and end sessions; OIDC logout, token introspection and revocation endpoints are documented.

facts.label: SSO standards and direction
facts.value: built_in: Keycloak acts as an OIDC/OAuth 2.0 authorization server and SAML 2.0 identity provider for applications; it can broker upstream OIDC and SAML identity providers.

facts.label: Native customer organizations
facts.value: built_in in Keycloak 26.8.1: organizations within a realm, invitations, memberships, organization-scoped groups and associated identity providers.

facts.label: Organization roles and isolation
facts.value: Organization groups can receive realm/client roles; role information can be mapped into organization-context tokens. Organizations isolate their group hierarchies, but those groups cannot be used in Keycloak's realm-level group authorization policies.

facts.label: Older multi-tenant guide
facts.value: Cloud-IAM's older guide describes client-per-tenant or realm-per-tenant patterns. It does not describe the newer native Organizations model.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: built_in/supported in Keycloak 26.8: SCIM user and group create/read/update/patch/delete, membership management, filtering/pagination and schema discovery.

facts.label: SCIM mappings and offboarding scope
facts.value: SCIM active maps to Keycloak enabled; groups map to membership. Core emails is represented as multivalued but only its first value is stored. Instant revocation of every downstream app token on deactivation was not established.

facts.label: Hosted login and account UI
facts.value: Keycloak supplies hosted login/registration and Account Console pages; the builder configures realm flows and links its app to them.

facts.label: Visual branding
facts.value: Paid dedicated deployments on Keycloak 26.2+ have a no-code Theme Generator for login and transactional email branding; Editor permission required.

facts.label: Custom theme depth
facts.value: Advanced branding can use a custom theme JAR, Freemarker templates, or the external Keycloakify project; builders maintain compatibility of their own custom theme.

facts.label: Custom login domain
facts.value: Paid deployments support a CNAME custom domain with managed Let's Encrypt certificate renewal; reverse-proxy/own-certificate configuration is also documented.

facts.label: UI languages
facts.value: Keycloak login, Account Console and Admin Console support configurable internationalization; English is the default. Enable other locales and override theme/realm message bundles.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public Cloud-IAM-specific accessibility conformance report or supported WCAG level found.

facts.label: Official browser integration
facts.value: Official upstream Keycloak JavaScript adapter supports browser applications using OIDC; PKCE and token refresh are documented.

facts.label: Other backend frameworks/runtimes
facts.value: Apps can use standard OIDC/OAuth 2.0 or SAML clients with the hosted server; a complete Cloud-IAM first-party framework/version/edge-runtime support matrix was not found.

facts.label: Mobile and limited-input clients
facts.value: Standard OIDC flows and the official JavaScript adapter's Cordova/native redirect modes are documented; device authorization is available for appropriate limited-input clients.

facts.label: Named mobile SDK support matrix
facts.value: A Cloud-IAM-maintained iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop SDK/version/passkey compatibility matrix was not found.

facts.label: Prerequisites and separate services
facts.value: Managed Keycloak infrastructure/database is included. Builder supplies its app hosting and integrations; its own SMTP provider is needed for outbound account email.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: not_applicable to Cloud-IAM managed hosting. Self-hosting upstream Keycloak after export is a separate deployment choice.

facts.label: Custom server logic
facts.value: Custom Keycloak SPIs/extensions are uploaded as version-compatible JAR releases, validated and installed per deployment; installation/update redeploys the server.

facts.label: Starter extension entitlement
facts.value: Conflicting: human pricing matrix excludes custom JAR extensions and Marketplace on Starter and includes them on Essential/Premium/Max; pricing.txt says paid tiers and the catalog guide includes Starter.

facts.label: User attributes, flows and webhooks
facts.value: Native Keycloak supports custom profile attributes and authentication flows. A Cloud-IAM catalog extension can send login/logout/register/admin-event webhooks.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Native Admin Console and Keycloak Admin REST API manage users, groups, roles and clients, including creating/searching/updating/disabling/deleting accounts.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: Administrators with the appropriate impersonation role can impersonate a user for support.

facts.label: Cloud infrastructure management API
facts.value: Cloud-IAM REST API automates deployment operations, logs, exports, upgrades and extension management; access is documented for dedicated deployments only.

facts.label: Account linking and unlinking
facts.value: Native identity brokering and Account Console support linking external identities; linking flows can require existing-account verification and authentication.

facts.label: Credential-guessing protection
facts.value: Managed load-balancer protection plus native configurable realm brute-force detection, including temporary/permanent lockout and progressive delays.

facts.label: Bots and password policies
facts.value: Native registration reCAPTCHA is configurable with builder-supplied Google keys; native password rules are configurable. The human pricing matrix gates its managed password-deny-list/third-party configuration feature to Essential and above.

facts.label: Numeric login/API burst limits
facts.value: A universal published per-endpoint requests-per-window or concurrent-login quota was not found. Pricing's unlimited/non-metered API wording is not a capacity benchmark.

facts.label: Native user/admin audit events
facts.value: Native Keycloak events record successful/failed login, logout, password/reset, verification, registration and admin changes; storage and expiration are configurable per realm.

facts.label: Cloud operational logs and export
facts.value: Keycloak/load-balancer logs are accessible in the console and API with 30-day retention; polling/export is documented. Cloud-IAM audit logs separately show deployment operations.

facts.label: Paid JSON export
facts.value: Dedicated export includes realms, clients, roles, users and credentials, groups/memberships, identity providers, federation settings, custom attributes and authentication configuration in JSON.

facts.label: Full encrypted backup and exit fee
facts.value: Paid customers can download full PostgreSQL backups containing configurations, events, sessions, users, clients and credentials; own GPG public key is required to decrypt a downloaded copy.

facts.label: Free exit path
facts.value: Current exit guide allows native Keycloak partial export on Free but excludes the Cloud-IAM Export/Backup features; pricing.txt instead advertises a Free daily export.

facts.label: Starter export frequency
facts.value: Conflicting: human pricing matrix gives Starter one export per day, Essential/Premium/Max unlimited; pricing.txt says every paid tier unlimited and the export guide allows dedicated on-demand export.

facts.label: Migration into Keycloak
facts.value: Cloud-IAM documents importing a realm JSON file and user JSON data into a managed deployment; supported dedicated export/import tools use native Keycloak representations.

facts.label: Non-Keycloak hashes and lazy migration
facts.value: No complete Cloud-IAM support matrix or fixed-price turnkey promise for importing other vendors' hashes, preserving every source ID, or lazy password migration was found.

facts.label: Routine retention
facts.value: Deployment JSON exports: 7 days. Cold database backups: 30 days by default. Cloud infrastructure/application/access logs and metrics: 30 days.

facts.label: Backup cadence
facts.value: Detailed docs/pricing specify daily cold backups on Starter/Essential, configurable Premium frequency and 15-minute Max RPO; the security overview instead claims hourly backups across providers.

facts.label: Deployment cancellation and deletion
facts.value: Free deployments have a console delete path; paid customers must submit a support request specifying the cancellation/deletion date.

facts.label: Final deletion deadline
facts.value: Conflicting: current exit policy says complete deletion within 30 days after cancellation; Terms 2023-1 uses 30 working days after termination when no reversibility request is made.

facts.label: Vendor account retention
facts.value: Published subprocessor page says inactive platform customer accounts are reviewed and deleted after six months of inactivity.

facts.label: Deployment region choice
facts.value: Named options include Scaleway Paris fr-par, Amsterdam nl-ams and Warsaw pl-waw; Outscale Paris cloudgouv-eu-west-1; AWS Paris eu-west-3 plus worldwide regions; GCP Europe/worldwide regions; Azure france-central, central-us and southeast-asia. Free: AWS eu-west-3.

facts.label: End-user data, logs and backups
facts.value: End-user data resides in the chosen deployment. Logs/metrics are processed in France on Scaleway; encrypted cold backups use Scaleway and 3DS Outscale in France by default.

facts.label: Outside-EEA contractual scope
facts.value: Public DPA requires a separate agreement for end-user-data processing outside the EEA.

facts.label: Builder account and control-plane data
facts.value: Platform database/control-plane logs: Scaleway France. Support, billing and dashboard communications also use named processors including US-based Stripe, Resend, Google Workspace and HubSpot.

facts.label: Privacy and processing documents
facts.value: Public privacy policy and DPA; customer is controller and Cloud-IAM is processor for hosted end-user data. Named subprocessors are published separately.

facts.label: ISO certificate evidence
facts.value: Vendor-provided IQNET recognition of Standards Institution of Israel certification: ISO/IEC 27001:2022, CLOUDIAM, platform development/maintenance/operation; issued 2024-11-11, expires 2027-11-11; IL-1123679.

facts.label: Other assurance and audit-report limits
facts.value: No completed Cloud-IAM SOC 2 certificate/report established. Vendor security material describes SOC 2 certification as forthcoming; provider certifications do not establish certification of every Cloud-IAM plan.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Cloud-IAM; operated by CLOUDIAM SAS, France (company number 900 205 436). Official site: https://www.cloud-iam.com/; documentation: https://documentation.cloud-iam.com/.

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Self-service hosted service advertised; public deployment instructions available. Signup and production deployment not tested.

facts.label: Dated maintenance evidence
facts.value: Cloud-IAM announced Keycloak 26.8.1 availability on 2026-10-16; its changelog also records a Security Center change on 2026-11-02.

facts.label: Managed service commercial terms
facts.value: Hosted access is governed by the Cloud-IAM subscription terms; remote-use rights apply for the subscription. Vendor platform rights and resale restrictions remain separate from the underlying open-source license.

facts.label: Underlying server license
facts.value: Keycloak: Apache License 2.0; commercial use, modification and distribution are permitted subject to its license conditions.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Public status site reports Cloud-IAM components and incident history; shared Free infrastructure also has its own linked status site.

facts.label: Contractual monthly availability
facts.value: Free: no SLA. Starter 99%; Essential 99.9%; Premium 99.95%; Max 99.98% monthly login availability.

facts.label: Supported versions and upgrade responsibility
facts.value: Cloud-IAM's version table lists Keycloak 26.8 support through end of October 2027. Upgrade procedure takes a backup and requires checking themes/extensions for version compatibility.

facts.label: Security maintenance extension
facts.value: Optional quoted Extended Security Lifecycle backports high/critical Keycloak core fixes, with 1–3 years of coverage and up to three years after the version's release.

facts.label: Ordinary support routes
facts.value: Free/Starter: community documentation and Discord. Essential: ticket/email, 2 French working days response. Premium/Max: ticket/email and 1 French working day response; 1 consulting day/month included.

facts.label: Emergency incident support
facts.value: Starter best effort; Essential critical response 12 hours; Premium 1 hour; Max 30 minutes. Premium/Max have 24/7 customer on-call access.

apps.name: Descope
apps.line: Hosted login flows, account management, and developer APIs.

free.text: Free up to 7,500 MAU

cells.freeUsers: 7,500 MAU; 10 tenants and 3 SSO connections
cells.sso: Free includes up to 3 configured SSO connections

mau.math: 1,000 monthly users fit within the 7,500-user free allowance, so it is free.
This is the Pro plan as a monthly price. The published annual base price is $2,988.
The Growth plan is $799 base, plus $0.05 for each user above the 25,000 included. For 50,000 users, that works out to $2,049 a month.
The Growth plan is $799 base, plus $0.05 for each user above the 25,000 included. For 100,000 users, that works out to $4,549 a month.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot away from auth, major paid feature retirement, data-exposing breach or regulatory action found.

facts.label: User meter
facts.value: MAU: a user who signs up or signs in during one month; repeated sign-ins add no MAU charge.

facts.label: Tenant meter
facts.value: Active tenant: at least two associated users and at least one login in the month.

facts.label: SSO meter
facts.value: Every configured tenant-to-IdP SAML/OIDC connection counts.

facts.label: Other billing definitions
facts.value: Federated apps count when configured; M2M includes client_credentials, /key/exchange and oauth_token_exchange.

facts.label: Company/project allowance boundary
facts.value: Console shows company totals; exact cross-project allowance sharing and cross-project user deduplication are not explicit.

facts.label: Consent meter — MAC
facts.value: Unique user consent to scopes for a specific resource/app/MCP server within a month.

facts.label: Token meter — MATK
facts.value: Token fetched and used during a month; per user/tenant and outbound app/connection, with scope/handle examples.

facts.label: Free — tenant and SSO allowance
facts.value: 10 active tenants; 3 configured SSO connections.

facts.label: Free — additional included units
facts.value: 1 OIDC federated app; 5 test users; 10,000 M2M; 2,000 MAC; 2,000 MATK.

facts.label: Pro — minimum commitment
facts.value: Starts at USD $249/month, billed annually; $2,988 annual base — our calculation.

facts.label: Growth — minimum commitment
facts.value: Starts at USD $799/month, billed annually; $9,588 annual base — our calculation.

facts.label: Enterprise and monthly-only prices
facts.value: Enterprise requires a quote; a separate month-to-month price for Pro/Growth was not located.

facts.label: Currency, tax and refunds
facts.value: USD unless the order/invoice says otherwise; taxes additional; fees non-refundable under the terms.

facts.label: Contract term and renewal
facts.value: Order defines the subscription term; auto-renewal applies only when expressly specified, with the stated 30-day notice rule.

facts.label: Pro — user rate
facts.value: Plan card/rate table: 10,000 MAU included; $0.05 per extra MAU.

facts.label: Growth — user rate
facts.value: 25,000 MAU included; $0.05 per additional MAU.

facts.label: Pro — tenant and SSO rates
facts.value: 35 active tenants, then $1 each; 5 SSO connections, then $50 each.

facts.label: Growth — tenant and SSO rates
facts.value: 100 active tenants, then $1 each; 10 SSO connections, then $50 each.

facts.label: Invoice details not published
facts.value: Overage invoice cadence, partial-month proration, $2/1,000 block rounding and usage reset timezone not located.

facts.label: Pro allowance conflict inside pricing
facts.value: Pro card/rate table: 10,000 MAU; pricing FAQ overage example: 7,500 MAU.

facts.label: Business A — 10 organizations, 1 SAML
facts.value: Our calculation: Free $0; 1,000 MAU, 10 active tenants, 1 configured SAML connection.

facts.label: Business B — 100 organizations, 10 SAML
facts.value: Our calculation: Pro $564/month equivalent; $2,988 annual base plus usage.

facts.label: Tenant membership model
facts.value: Users can belong to zero, one or many customer tenants, with roles per tenant.

facts.label: Members/invites/roles quantity caps
facts.value: Public per-tenant member, role and invitation-count caps or invitation surcharge not located.

facts.label: Invitations
facts.value: Email/SMS invitations; configurable expiry and redirect; optional magic-link token.

facts.label: Business SSO — Free
facts.value: SAML/OIDC supported within the 3-connection allowance; manual Console/API configuration.

facts.label: Business SSO — Pro/Growth
facts.value: SSO Setup Suite on paid plans; connection allowances/overages in F11.

facts.label: SCIM — plan and fee boundary
facts.value: Distinct public per-directory SCIM rate and setup fee not located.

facts.label: Builder dashboard access
facts.value: Descopers have configurable company/project permissions; these are builder accounts.

facts.label: Builder seat and total project caps
facts.value: Explicit per-plan Descoper count, general project cap and extra-seat fee not located.

facts.label: CI/CD edition limits
facts.value: Free: unavailable; Pro: up to 3 projects; Growth: up to 10; Enterprise: unlimited.

facts.value: plugin: omniauth-apple 1.4.0, MIT; depends on omniauth-oauth2 and json-jwt. Docs show Devise configuration for Sign in with Apple.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-microsoft_graph 2.2.0, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0 / omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8.0, JWT >=2.0 and <4.0.

facts.label: Other providers
facts.value: generic/plugin: project guide demonstrates Facebook and links OmniAuth's strategy ecosystem; app can implement a custom strategy.

facts.label: Passkey core versus extension
facts.value: plugin: devise-passkeys 0.3.0 (MIT), requires Devise >=4.7.1 and warden-webauthn >=0.3.0; adds passkey authentication instead of passwords.

facts.label: Passkey UI, recovery and clients
facts.value: Plugin explicitly leaves WebAuthn JavaScript, mailers and error handling to the app; credential list/create/delete and reauthentication concerns require wiring.

facts.label: Core MFA and factor boundary
facts.value: No built-in TOTP, SMS/email second-factor enrollment, security-key MFA enforcement or recovery-code module in core.

facts.label: TOTP plugin and compatible versions
facts.value: plugin: devise-two-factor 6.4.1 (MIT), TOTP plus optional single-use backup codes; Devise >=4.0 and <6.0, Rails/ActiveSupport >=7.2 and <8.2, rotp ~>6.0.

facts.label: MFA recovery and bypass conditions
facts.value: TwoFactorBackupable stores bcrypt backup-code hashes; each code single-use; generating replacement codes invalidates the old set. Application enables strategy/model fields and displays codes.

facts.label: Email confirmation and changes
facts.value: built_in optional Confirmable: token instructions; unconfirmed access defaults 0 days, confirm_within defaults nil (no expiry); reconfirmable=true defers email changes until confirmation.

facts.label: Password reset and update
facts.value: built_in Recoverable: digested reset tokens; default reset window 6 hours. Successful reset signs in by default. Registration account updates normally require current password.

facts.label: Phone verification and self-delete
facts.value: Phone verification requires app/service integration. Registerable exposes signed-in account editing and DELETE account action with a cancellation form.

facts.label: Session model and password invalidation
facts.value: Warden/Rails session stores user key plus authenticatable_salt; fetching reloads record and compares salt. DatabaseAuthenticatable uses the first 29 bcrypt-hash characters as salt.

facts.label: Idle session expiry
facts.value: Optional Timeoutable defaults to 30 minutes inactivity; nil disables timeout. Last request timestamp is tracked in scoped session.

facts.label: Remember me
facts.value: Optional Rememberable defaults 2 weeks; extend_remember_period=false; expire_all_remember_me_on_sign_out=true.

facts.label: Sign-out and lost devices
facts.value: Default sign_out_via=DELETE; sign_out_all_scopes=true clears Devise scopes in the current Warden session. App can sign out a named scope.

facts.label: API bearer tokens and refresh
facts.value: Core HTTP Basic can authenticate each request; core TokenAuthenticatable was removed. JWT/access/refresh functionality comes from custom Warden strategies or separate gems.

facts.label: SAML service-provider role
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-saml 2.2.5, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.1 and ruby-saml ~>1.18. Plugin docs specify Ruby 3.1.x+ and show Devise integration.

facts.label: OIDC client role
facts.value: plugin: omniauth_openid_connect 0.8.0, MIT; OmniAuth >=1.9 and <3, openid_connect ~>2.2. Generic OIDC client strategy with issuer/discovery and callback integration.

facts.label: Identity-provider/server role
facts.value: custom_code/other project needed to issue OAuth/OIDC or SAML federation as an identity provider; no core authorization-server endpoints or signing-key service.

facts.label: Organizations, memberships and roles
facts.value: custom_code or separate authorization/tenant libraries required. Devise authenticates resources; it does not supply organization membership, customer-admin roles or tenant access enforcement.

facts.label: Account invitations extension
facts.value: plugin: devise_invitable 3.1.0 (MIT), Ruby >=2.7, Rails >=7 and Devise >=5 according to its guide; published runtime dependencies actionmailer >=7 and devise >=5.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No core SCIM Users/Groups endpoints, directory connection or deactivation contract found.

facts.label: Account UI provided
facts.value: built_in app-served Rails views/controllers for sign-in, sign-up, account editing/deletion, confirmation request, password reset/request and unlocking.

facts.label: Custom UI and API limitations
facts.value: Views/controller generators copy templates for editing; scoped views can differ per Devise model. API-only setup needs chosen strategy, request shapes and missing Rails middleware/views handled.

facts.label: Branding, domains and customization
facts.value: App owns rendered templates, layouts, route paths and its hosting/domain. MIT code has no branding-removal fee or domain-count licence cap.

facts.label: Built-in language scope
facts.value: Core ships English message locale and Rails I18n integration; generated account views contain English labels/text and can be edited.

facts.label: Additional languages
facts.value: plugin: devise-i18n (MIT) provides translated messages/views; project wiki lists examples including Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Devise-specific public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or completed accessibility assessment found.

facts.label: Framework/runtime floor
facts.value: Core Devise 5.0.4 requires Ruby >=2.7.0 and railties >=7.0. Rails engine/Rack/Warden server integration, not a browser/edge-only package.

facts.label: Database/framework integrations
facts.value: Active Record is default; Mongoid is supported. Release notes add Rails 8 and Ruby 3.4/4.0 support and restore Mongoid tests across Rails 7+.

facts.label: Hotwire/Turbo and API setup
facts.value: Documented Hotwire/Turbo status/redirect integration; new generated initializer configures 422 error status and 303 redirect. HTTP Basic is opt-in for API use.

facts.label: Native/mobile/desktop SDKs
facts.value: No official Devise native iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop SDK/platform compatibility matrix found.

facts.label: Core package/database prerequisites
facts.value: Core runtime dependencies: bcrypt ~>3.0, orm_adapter ~>0.1, railties >=7, responders and warden ~>1.2.3. App supplies persisted Devise user model, schema/indexes and Rails session store.

facts.label: Optional service and secret prerequisites
facts.value: Mail-enabled flows need Action Mailer/provider setup; background delivery needs the app's queue. App secret_key_base supplies Devise's default token key; optional MFA/passkeys add their own keys/models.

facts.label: Deployment, backups and upgrades
facts.value: Deploy as part of Rails; run chosen schema migrations and review initializer/model modules. Operator backs up users, provider links, keys, session data and any extension records, and applies code/dependency fixes.

facts.label: Capacity and sizing
facts.value: No universal Devise server specification, MAU-to-hardware table, throughput guarantee or complete product backup/restore runbook found.

facts.label: Custom attributes and logic
facts.value: built_in extension points: model modules, Warden strategies/configuration, custom controllers/views, callbacks such as after_database_authentication and after_confirmation, parameter sanitizers and custom lookup.

facts.label: Events and webhook delivery
facts.value: App can hook Warden/model/controller actions and notification delivery; no managed Devise webhook queue, signing key service, retry schedule or event-retention product.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: App ORM/controller code can create/find/update/destroy users. Lockable exposes lock_access!/unlock_access!; active_for_authentication? can enforce a custom ban/status policy.

facts.label: Impersonation/support access
facts.value: custom_code: sign_in can set a preauthenticated resource; bypass_sign_in stores it while bypassing Warden callbacks. No built-in approved/audited impersonation workflow.

facts.label: Social account linking
facts.value: custom_code: callback guide finds/creates by provider and uid; app adds fields and defines from_omniauth/new_with_session behavior.

facts.label: Guest upgrade/data transfer
facts.value: custom_code: guest guide calls app logging_in handoff logic and deletes guest row after registration/login.

facts.label: Account lockout
facts.value: Optional Lockable: failed_attempts strategy; maximum_attempts=20; unlock_strategy=:both (email or time); unlock_in=1 hour; last_attempt_warning=true.

facts.label: Enumeration/password checks
facts.value: paranoid=false by default; enabling it uses generic behavior and hashes nonexistent-account password attempts. Validatable defaults password length 6..128; bcrypt cost 12.

facts.label: Optional additional security
facts.value: plugin: devise-security 0.18.0 (MIT; published dependency Devise >=4.3) adds password expiry/history/validation, single-session checks and CAPTCHA integration modules.

facts.label: Request/rate limits
facts.value: No Devise-operated request quota or universal built-in requests-per-second/window contract. App/gateway limits must protect login, reset, confirmation and admin endpoints.

facts.label: Login/audit evidence
facts.value: Optional Trackable records sign-in count, current/last timestamps and current/last IP addresses. Warden/model hooks can feed app-owned audit records.

facts.label: Logs and sensitive tokens
facts.value: README warns Action Mailer DEBUG content and Active Job INFO arguments may leak plaintext reset tokens; operator must configure logging/redaction and retention.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and hash export
facts.value: App/database export possible through operator tooling; Devise has no vendor export queue/fee or fixed CSV format. User schema includes IDs/email, encrypted_password bcrypt hash and optional verification/lock/track fields.

facts.label: Provider/factor/session exit limits
facts.value: Provider/uid links and plugin credential/OTP data live in app-defined tables. Compatibility requires the target to understand those records, password hashing/pepper and keys.

facts.label: Import existing users
facts.value: custom_code/ORM migration: map existing IDs/profile fields, write compatible encrypted_password hashes directly and preserve the correct hashing/pepper semantics; no core bulk-import API/wizard.

facts.label: Legacy password migration
facts.value: Project wiki illustrates custom valid_password? fallback followed by rehash on successful login. Optional devise-encryptable 0.3.0 (MIT, Devise >=2.1) enables other/custom encryptors plus password_salt.

facts.label: User deletion
facts.value: Registerable destroy action destroys the signed-in resource and signs out; user account screen includes a DELETE cancellation action. App model callbacks decide associated-data/soft-delete behavior.

facts.label: Retention and project closure
facts.value: App operator chooses database/log/backup retention and any deletion jobs; no Devise-hosted project or billing account to close.

facts.label: Data location/residency
facts.value: Self-chosen Rails/database/session/log/backup infrastructure; social/SSO and mail calls go to configured providers. No Devise cloud region selector or residency plan.

facts.label: Hosted privacy/DPA/subprocessors
facts.value: Not applicable to Devise as an operated identity processor: the library runs in the developer's app and the app stores account data.

facts.label: Independent assurance
facts.value: No Devise-specific public SOC 2/ISO attestation or completed independent security audit report established.

facts.label: Name, aliases and maintainer
facts.value: Devise; Ruby gem devise; project heartcombo/devise. Earlier plataformatec/devise links remain in older guides. Maintained by individual maintainers through the heartcombo project.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active, not archived or disabled; latest non-prerelease 5.0.4 published May 8, 2026. RubyGems 5.0.4 is not yanked; repository pushed October 6, 2026.

facts.label: Deprecations and older examples
facts.value: Core TokenAuthenticatable was removed; its old wiki examples are explicitly out of date. Mailing lists are deprecated. Version 5 drops Ruby below 2.7 and Rails below 7.

facts.label: Code licence and commercial use
facts.value: MIT; free of charge to use, modify, distribute, sublicense and sell software, retaining required notices. No production, revenue, user or application licence fee.

facts.label: Logo licence
facts.value: Devise logo is separately labelled CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, rather than MIT.

facts.label: Optional extension licences
facts.value: devise-passkeys 0.3.0 and devise-two-factor 6.4.1: MIT; devise_invitable 3.1.0, devise-passwordless 1.1.0 and devise-encryptable 0.3.0 declare MIT.

facts.label: Status page and uptime SLA
facts.value: Not applicable to a Devise-operated runtime login service; app/hosting availability and any SLA belong to its actual operator.

facts.label: Current release/security fixes
facts.value: 5.0.4 released May 8, 2026 fixes CVE-2026-40295 (Timeoutable non-GET redirect); advisory affects <=5.0.3 and identifies 5.0.4 as patched.

facts.label: Email-change security fix
facts.value: 5.0.3 released March 16, 2026 fixes CVE-2026-32700; advisory affects <=5.0.2 with Confirmable reconfirmation email changes.

facts.label: Support policy and test scope
facts.value: README intends to support Ruby/Rails versions still maintained upstream. Current/release CI covers selected Ruby 2.7 to 4.0 and Rails 7.x/8/main combinations, Active Record and Mongoid.

facts.label: Numeric LTS/backport deadlines
facts.value: No exact Devise branch end-of-support dates, guaranteed security-backport years or dedicated supported-version schedule found; rendered security page says no SECURITY.md detected.

facts.label: Community help and reporting
facts.value: Usage help: StackOverflow devise tag; bug reports: project GitHub issues following contribution/wiki rules. Security reports: project address heartcombo.oss@gmail.com, not a public issue.

facts.label: Paid support/response promises
facts.value: No official project paid-support rate card, contracted response hours, 24/7 support commitment or guaranteed fix turnaround found.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable; no MAU, returning-user, stored-account, login, token or builder-seat meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: MIT production use costs 0 software license fees and has no license-imposed user cap.

facts.label: Hosted free allowance
facts.value: Not applicable; no maintained free hosted auth tenant or included monthly delivery allowance.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable; no required paid production license, annual term, base subscription or tax-bearing software rate card.

facts.label: Usage tiers/overages
facts.value: Not applicable; no software usage tiers, connection overage rules or volume rounding.

facts.label: Organization limits/fees
facts.value: Not applicable to a bundled organization product; no customer workspace/member/invitation model or plan.

facts.label: SSO and sync fees
facts.value: Not applicable to a built-in enterprise connection plan; external/custom allauth SSO routes have separate dependencies and operation.

facts.label: Builder seats/apps/projects
facts.value: Not applicable; no vendor dashboard developer-seat, application, environment or domain cap.

facts.label: Email sender and cost
facts.value: Password-reset and optional registration/verification mail use configured Django/allauth email mechanisms; operator supplies sender/backend and pays delivery.

facts.label: SMS/other delivery
facts.value: No default SMS/phone-code delivery flow in the 7.2.0 routes/serializers; custom integration must select and fund a provider.

facts.label: Billing-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable; no MAU allowance triggers an upgrade, overage invoice or automatic auth cutoff.

facts.label: Other billable product limits
facts.value: Not applicable; no software charges for requests, JWT refreshes, MFA, audit events, membership transactions or developer seats.

facts.label: Account eligibility and markets
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted vendor account; individual/commercial software use is allowed under MIT without a company-domain/country billing gate.

facts.label: Hosted signup/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable; install/configure the package and migrations in an existing Django app.

facts.label: Type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Django REST Framework library: account login/logout, user details, password reset/change; optional allauth-backed registration/social login, SimpleJWT and bundled TOTP MFA.

facts.label: Integration boundaries
facts.value: Core token/session endpoints; optional with-social dependency for allauth; optional with-mfa dependency for bundled MFA. The maintainer says allauth support is optional and narrow.

facts.label: Operator/responsibilities
facts.value: Developer or chosen host operates app servers, Django database, sessions/tokens, delivery, keys, patches and backups.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in LoginView/LoginSerializer: username/email plus password; configured backend/allauth settings determine identifier handling.

facts.label: Email links/codes as sign-in
facts.value: custom_code/other endpoints required for general magic-link or email-code login; core link flows reset passwords or verify registration email.

facts.label: Phone-code and wallet login
facts.value: custom_code/other package integration required; no built-in phone-code or wallet-signature credential path in published 7.2.0 serializers/routes.

facts.label: Anonymous access/guest accounts
facts.value: Django anonymous requests/sessions exist; no persisted guest-account creation/upgrade flow supplied by dj-rest-auth.

facts.label: Social integration model
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth with custom SocialLoginView subclasses specifying provider adapter, callback URL and OAuth client where needed.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: plugin: documented GoogleOAuth2Adapter/SocialLoginView recipe, client registration and code/token exchange.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: plugin: documented GitHubOAuth2Adapter/SocialLoginView recipe with authorization-code exchange.

facts.label: Facebook
facts.value: plugin: documented FacebookOAuth2Adapter/SocialLoginView example for code or access-token exchange.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: plugin/custom_integration: allauth Apple adapter is available; dj-rest-auth's social serializer explicitly handles an id_token alongside access_token for Apple.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: plugin/custom_integration: allauth Microsoft/Entra provider is available; a suitable SocialLoginView adapter/client setup is app work.

facts.label: Published passkey installation mismatch
facts.value: Live docs instruct dj-rest-auth[with-passkeys] and dj_rest_auth.passkeys; 7.2.0 metadata declares no with-passkeys extra and the uploaded/tagged source has no passkey .py implementation.

facts.label: Later development passkeys
facts.value: development snapshot: April 25 master commit adds WebAuthn registration/login and credential list/rename/delete using webauthn>=2.0.0.

facts.label: Development domain/client boundary
facts.value: Development guide requires RP ID/name/origins; authenticated registration and usernameless-capable login; server-cached challenge timeout default 300 seconds.

facts.label: Released TOTP MFA
facts.value: built_in optional dj_rest_auth.mfa in 7.2.0; with-mfa adds PyOTP. Defaults: 6 digits, 30-second period; implementation accepts one adjacent time step either side.

facts.label: MFA enablement/enforcement
facts.value: Install app, migrate, mount MFA routes and replace password LoginView with MFALoginView; enrolled users receive an ephemeral challenge instead of full tokens.

facts.label: Challenge and activation state
facts.value: MFA ephemeral/activation tokens expire after 300 seconds by default; signed activation token binds user ID and TOTP secret; confirmation requires a valid TOTP.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: Default 10 recovery codes; generated as 8 hexadecimal characters in xxxx-xxxx format; database used-mask makes successful use one-time with an atomic row lock.

facts.label: Recovery-code retrieval method conflict
facts.value: 7.2.0 guide says GET mfa/recovery-codes/; actual RecoveryCodesView implements POST and no get() handler.

facts.label: Other second factors
facts.value: No released SMS/email authenticator or WebAuthn/security-key MFA type in this bundled module; add a separate integration/policy.

facts.label: MFA data protection
facts.value: TOTP secret is Django-signed, not encrypted; recovery seed/used-state is stored in Authenticator JSON data.

facts.label: Registration/email verification
facts.value: plugin: allauth-backed registration, verify-email POST with key, and resend-verification endpoint; mandatory verification returns a mail-sent result rather than auth tokens.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: built_in reset request and confirmation with uid, token and two new-password fields; chooses Django or allauth reset form/token generator according to installation.

facts.label: Password-change checks
facts.value: Authenticated change endpoint; OLD_PASSWORD_FIELD_ENABLED=False and LOGOUT_ON_PASSWORD_CHANGE=False by default.

facts.label: Email/phone changes and self-deletion
facts.value: Default UserDetailsSerializer makes email read-only; phone verification/contact management and whole-account self-deletion require custom endpoints/serializers.

facts.label: Default auth/session modes
facts.value: Default TOKEN_MODEL is DRF Token, SESSION_LOGIN=True, USE_JWT=False. Login can create/get a token and establish a Django browser session.

facts.label: DRF token lifetime/revocation
facts.value: Default DRF token has no expiry and one token per user; default creator reuses get_or_create. Logout deletes the stored token.

facts.label: Django session expiry
facts.value: Django 6.0.10 default SESSION_COOKIE_AGE = 1209600 seconds (2 weeks); per-session/settings overrides available; save-every-request defaults False.

facts.label: Optional JWT defaults
facts.value: plugin: SimpleJWT; inspected 5.5.1 defaults access 5 minutes, refresh 1 day, rotation=False, blacklist-after-rotation=False, HS256.

facts.label: JWT logout/revocation
facts.value: Logout clears configured cookies and can blacklist a supplied refresh token when SimpleJWT blacklist app is installed; outstanding access token can remain valid until expiry.

facts.label: Password change and token scope
facts.value: Django session auth hashes invalidate other password-bound sessions; default change flow updates the current session hash. DRF/JWT revocation requires separate token policy.

facts.label: Incoming business standards
facts.value: No built-in SAML SP or OIDC issuer/broker management API. Generic allauth OIDC/SAML capability requires separate provider routes/custom integration.

facts.label: Organizations and roles
facts.value: custom_code/other app required for customer organizations, member invitations, tenant-scoped roles and customer administration.

facts.label: SCIM account synchronization
facts.value: No published bundled SCIM endpoint/version or directory provisioning lifecycle found.

facts.label: Ready-made UI
facts.value: Headless REST endpoints; developer builds the customer login/signup/account/MFA UI. Examples/demos illustrate SPA integration.

facts.label: Profile/account API
facts.value: UserDetailsView supplies authenticated current-user GET/PUT/PATCH; custom serializers can extend it with profile fields.

facts.label: Branding/custom domains
facts.value: Own frontend/templates/API host; no vendor-brand-removal or domain-count fee. Cookie domain/path/SameSite/Secure settings configurable.

facts.label: Translation evidence
facts.value: Published-source locale catalogs: ar, az, cs, de, es, fa, fr, hr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, ma, nl, pl, pt_BR, ro, ru, sv, tr, uk, zh_Hans, zh_Hant.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No project-specific public WCAG conformance report, assessment or final customer-UI accessibility statement found.

facts.label: Runtime/framework range
facts.value: 7.2.0 requires Python >=3.10 and Django >=4.2; README advertises Python 3.10–3.14/Django 4.2–6.0 and tox defines version combinations.

facts.label: DRF minimum conflict
facts.value: 7.2.0 setup/PyPI require djangorestframework>=3.13.0; same release's docs require >=3.14.

facts.label: Optional stack compatibility
facts.value: with-social requires allauth[socialaccount]>=64.0.0; current allauth docs list Python 3.11–3.14. SimpleJWT must be installed separately for JWT mode.

facts.label: Native/SPA clients
facts.value: Generic token/JWT HTTP API is documented for mobile and SPA clients; examples use browser frontends. Native code implements redirects, token storage and renewal.

facts.label: Native SDK/platform guarantees
facts.value: No complete native SDK or OS/version compatibility matrix found, including released native passkey support.

facts.label: Base prerequisites
facts.value: Django, DRF, configured database/auth middleware; rest_framework.authtoken installed for the default token model, or TOKEN_MODEL changed/disabled with another auth mode.

facts.label: Optional services/dependencies
facts.value: SMTP/email for resets/verification; allauth for registration/social; SimpleJWT for JWT; PyOTP for bundled TOTP; qrcode optional for server QR rendering.

facts.label: Production deployment
facts.value: Operator deploys supported Django app code, configures HTTPS, secret keys, host/cookie/CSRF/CORS settings, delivery, database and backups.

facts.label: Upgrade and backup work
facts.value: Read versioned upgrade/release notes, migrate schemas, preserve user/token/MFA data and relevant keys, test the chosen dependency combination and restore process.

facts.label: Sizing/capacity
facts.value: No universal CPU/RAM/users-per-server or fixed workload sizing found.

facts.label: Custom logic and user fields
facts.value: Configurable serializers, token model/creator, JWT claim serializer, registration permissions and custom views/signals/profile models.

facts.label: Events
facts.value: Django login/logout signals through session login; allauth-backed registration/social signals where invoked; MFA module emits structured logger events.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Current-user API plus Django admin/ORM for operator account creation/search/edit/deactivation/deletion; no vendor management dashboard.

facts.label: Inactive-account handling
facts.value: Default password login and MFA verifier reject inactive users; custom auth backends/token policies can change effective behavior.

facts.label: Provider linking/listing
facts.value: Authenticated SocialConnectView attaches provider identity to the current User; SocialAccountListView filters to that User; explicit routes must be mounted.

facts.label: Disconnect safety boundary
facts.value: SocialAccountDisconnectView limits records to current user and calls allauth adapter.validate_disconnect before deletion.

facts.label: Guest upgrade/method addition
facts.value: Persisted guest creation/data merging requires custom code. Existing Users can gain provider links or set/change a password through configured flows.

facts.label: Throttling/bot controls
facts.value: Views expose throttle scopes; DRF defaults to no throttle classes. App configures DRF throttles/WAF and any CAPTCHA/live breach/SMS-abuse services.

facts.label: Password/enumeration checks
facts.value: Password set/change use configured Django validators; password-reset view returns generic success. Registration serializer can explicitly reject a verified duplicate email.

facts.label: JWT-cookie security defaults
facts.value: JWT cookies are opt-in; default Secure=False, HttpOnly=True, SameSite=Lax. JWT_AUTH_COOKIE_USE_CSRF=False and enforce-on-unauthenticated=False.

facts.label: Base auth action limits
facts.value: No fixed built-in requests/window limit; main auth/reset/change/register views declare scope dj_rest_auth and use configured DRF throttles.

facts.label: MFA verification limits
facts.value: MFAVerifyView declares dj_rest_auth_mfa_verify; other bundled MFA actions use dj_rest_auth. Operator must configure matching throttle classes/rates.

facts.label: Throttle mechanism/limits
facts.value: DRF throttling uses configured cache/rate policies and can return 429; official guide warns built-in throttles are not a complete brute-force/DoS defense and have concurrency fuzziness.

facts.label: Guaranteed throughput
facts.value: No universal login/management requests-per-second or server burst-capacity guarantee found.

facts.label: MFA audit events
facts.value: dj_rest_auth.mfa logger emits events such as activation/deactivation, verification failures, TOTP success, recovery-code use/regeneration with user/request metadata.

facts.label: Event retention/export
facts.value: App controls log retention, persistence and streaming/export; no included days, managed audit dashboard or log-volume billing plan.

facts.label: User/profile export
facts.value: Operator owns User and custom profile data; Django serialization/dumpdata can export identifiers, fields and relations without a vendor export fee.

facts.label: Password hashes and token data
facts.value: Django encoded password hashes and database token/MFA records are operator-accessible; destination hash/schema support must be checked.

facts.label: Passkey export scope
facts.value: No supported released passkey data/export API is established for standard 7.2.0; development credential/domain data needs a separate migration plan.

facts.label: Import/migration in
facts.value: Use compatible Django schemas/fixtures/data migrations and configured password hashers; custom import logic maps IDs, profiles and provider identities.

facts.label: Earlier-package/settings migration
facts.value: Upgrade guide describes rest_auth→dj_rest_auth imports, REST_AUTH dictionary migration and replacing the older JWT package with SimpleJWT.

facts.label: User deletion/data scope
facts.value: Operator Django User deletion applies configured model relations; default DRF Token and bundled MFA Authenticator have user cascade foreign keys.

facts.label: Session/token/log retention
facts.value: Operator sets session, blacklist, log and backup retention; SimpleJWT documents expired-token cleanup with flushexpiredtokens.

facts.label: Vendor account closure
facts.value: Not applicable; no dj-rest-auth hosted project/account to close.

facts.label: Data location/residency

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Django library/apps: registration, local and social accounts, verification, password recovery, MFA, session management, headless APIs and optional OIDC identity provider.

facts.label: Module/edition boundaries
facts.value: allauth.account, socialaccount, mfa, usersessions, headless and idp. No feature-restricted Pro edition; sponsored users get the same feature set.

facts.label: Account operator
facts.value: Developer or chosen application host operates Django, account data, sessions, email/SMS integration, patches and backups.

facts.label: Password and identifiers
facts.value: built_in account login/signup using configurable username, email and/or phone identifiers with password.

facts.label: Email-code passwordless login
facts.value: built_in, opt-in ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_ENABLED=False by default; code lifetime 180 seconds; maximum 3 entry attempts.

facts.label: Login-code format discrepancy
facts.value: Feature table describes a special 6-digit OTP; current common configuration and 65.21.1 generator instead default to 8 nonnumeric characters with a dash, e.g. WDJB-MJHT.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: General repeatable magic-link login requires custom code/another integration. Built-in email links verify an address or reset a password.

facts.label: Phone verification/login
facts.value: built_in SMS-code login when phone/login-by-code is configured, plus phone verification during signup/login. Login-code expiry/attempts: 180 seconds/3; phone-verification defaults: 900 seconds/3.

facts.label: Anonymous accounts and wallet login
facts.value: custom_code/other package required for persisted guest accounts or wallet-signature login; neither is a delivered account flow in the bundled API/routes.

facts.label: Provider integration model
facts.value: built_in optional socialaccount app with installed provider modules; register external clients and configure client IDs/secrets/callbacks in settings or SocialApp records.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: built_in socialaccount Google OAuth2 provider, including documented One Tap integration.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: built_in socialaccount Apple provider; configure Apple App/Services IDs and signing key.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: built_in GitHub provider with registered OAuth credentials and documented GitHub Enterprise server configuration.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: built_in Microsoft Graph provider; common tenant by default, configurable tenant; generic OIDC path for multiple Entra instances.

facts.label: Facebook
facts.value: built_in OAuth2/JavaScript SDK support; Facebook Limited Login uses headless provider-token flow.

facts.label: Passkey login and signup
facts.value: built_in optional mfa app/extras; WebAuthn and passkey login/signup disabled by default. Passkey signup requires mandatory email verification by code.

facts.label: Verification and domain binding
facts.value: 65.21.1 passkey registration/login require user verification; passwordless registration requests discoverable credentials. Default RP ID is the request hostname.

facts.label: Browser flow and autofill
facts.value: Bundled browser helper invokes WebAuthn creation/get from explicit button interactions; it exposes no conditional-mediation/autofill mode.

facts.label: Credential management and recovery
facts.value: Users can add/rename/remove WebAuthn authenticators; code records public registration credential data against the User; other configured methods/recovery codes provide fallback.

facts.label: TOTP and security-key factors
facts.value: built_in optional mfa module supports TOTP, recovery codes and WebAuthn. Default enabled types are TOTP and recovery codes; TOTP default 6 digits, 30-second period, zero time-step tolerance.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: Default 10 codes of 8 digits; viewing/downloading/regenerating supported; show-once setting defaults False; used codes are marked consumed.

facts.label: Email/SMS second-check boundary
facts.value: Email login confirmation can be required with ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_REQUIRED, globally or for specified methods. SMS phone verification is separate; SMS is not an Authenticator type in the MFA model.

facts.label: Sensitive-action enforcement
facts.value: MFA changes require reauthentication by default. Unverified-email accounts cannot enable MFA by default. Broader mandatory enrollment/role policies need application logic.

facts.label: Trusted-browser option
facts.value: MFA_TRUST_ENABLED=False by default; when enabled, a trust cookie can skip MFA for 14 days by default.

facts.label: Stored MFA secret protection
facts.value: Default MFA adapter encrypt()/decrypt() return the input unchanged; override the hooks to encrypt stored TOTP/recovery secrets.

facts.label: Email verification policies
facts.value: built_in optional/mandatory/none verification; optional by default. Verification links or opt-in codes; link expiry 3 days, code expiry 900 seconds/3 attempts by default.

facts.label: Email/address management
facts.value: built_in add/verify/remove/set-primary email views/API. Default multiple addresses allowed (maximum None), unique-email enforcement True; one-address change mode is opt-in.

facts.label: Password reset and change
facts.value: built_in set/change/reset password. Reset by email link by default or opt-in code; reset-code lifetime 180 seconds and 3 attempts by default.

facts.label: Phone change and verification
facts.value: built_in phone-management API and adapter-backed verification; defaults require verification, with optional resend/change behavior.

facts.label: Self-service account deletion/profile
facts.value: custom_code required for full account deletion and project-specific profile fields/screens; bundled routes/API manage credentials and contacts, not erasing the whole User.

facts.label: Browser sessions and remember-me
facts.value: Django session/cookie model; ACCOUNT_SESSION_REMEMBER=None asks the user. Django 6.1 default persistent age is 1209600 seconds (2 weeks), with per-session/config overrides.

facts.label: Device/session inventory
facts.value: Optional usersessions app lists active sessions and lets users end them. Activity tracking defaults False; middleware can update IP, user agent and last-seen time.

facts.label: Headless session tokens
facts.value: Default headless token strategy uses X-Session-Token for app clients; token is valid only while its backing Django session and auth hash remain valid.

facts.label: Optional headless JWT strategy
facts.value: Access/refresh pair after full authentication; defaults access 300 seconds, refresh 86400 seconds, refresh rotation True, algorithm RS256.

facts.label: JWT revocation limits
facts.value: HEADLESS_JWT_STATEFUL_VALIDATION_ENABLED=False by default; enable it to check access tokens against live session/auth state and invalidate them on logout/password change.

facts.label: Incoming SAML business login
facts.value: built_in optional socialaccount SAML 2.0 service-provider role; saml extras/Python3-SAML required, plus possible XML system libraries.

facts.label: Incoming OIDC federation
facts.value: built_in generic OIDC relying-party/client provider; multiple independent issuers configurable with provider IDs/callbacks.

facts.label: Outgoing OAuth/OIDC issuer
facts.value: built_in optional allauth.idp.oidc provider: authorization code, client credentials, implicit and device authorization grants; password grant intentionally unsupported.

facts.label: Issuer lifecycle configuration
facts.value: OIDC issuer access-token default 3600 seconds, ID token 300 seconds; refresh rotation True and refresh expiry None by default; key rotation/introspection available.

facts.label: Customer organizations, membership and roles
facts.value: custom_code/other app required for customer workspaces, invitations, membership roles and tenant isolation.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No published bundled SCIM implementation/version, directory lifecycle or provisioning API found.

facts.label: Built-in account screens
facts.value: Plain, unstyled Django templates/views cover signup/login/logout, password tasks, email management and enabled social/MFA/session flows.

facts.label: Headless and API-only UI
facts.value: allauth.headless supports custom SPA/mobile frontends; HEADLESS_ONLY=True disables normal account views. API specification and a React example are supplied.

facts.label: Branding
facts.value: Template overrides, base/element layout hooks and custom email text/HTML; no branding-removal fee.

facts.label: Custom domains and routing
facts.value: Own deployment domains; no vendor domain-count tier. Headless browser documentation covers single-domain or shared-main-domain subdomain routing and cookie/CSRF configuration.

facts.label: Translations
facts.value: Release 65.21.1 has translation directories: ar, az, bg, ca, cs, da, de, el, en, es, et, eu, fa, fi, fr, he, hr, ht, hu, id, it, ja, ka, ko, ky, lt, lv, mn, nb, nl, pl, pt_BR, pt_PT, ro, ru, sk, sl, sr, sr_Latn, sv, th, tr, uk, uz, zh_Hans, zh_Hant.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No allauth-specific public WCAG assessment, conformance report or independent template accessibility audit found.

facts.label: Python and Django requirements
facts.value: 65.21.1 package requires Python >=3.11, Django >=4.2.16 and asgiref >=3.8.1. Docs list Python 3.11–3.14; package classifiers list Django 4.2/5.x/6.0/6.1.

facts.label: Framework/client integration
facts.value: Python/Django server code; bundled headless integration for Django REST framework and Django Ninja; React SPA example.

facts.label: Native client API
facts.value: Official headless API explicitly targets native Android/iOS apps as well as browser SPAs; app paths use session-token headers and no cookies.

facts.label: Native SDK and passkey compatibility matrix
facts.value: No complete iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop SDK and passkey-version support matrix found.

facts.label: Base setup/services
facts.value: Django project with auth/messages/session middleware, allauth account middleware, authentication backend, database migrations and production web server; email backend for delivered account mail.

facts.label: Optional dependency extras
facts.value: mfa installs qrcode >=7,<9 and fido2 >=1.1.2,<3; saml installs python3-saml >=1.15,<2; socialaccount/idp-oidc require OAuthLib >=4,<5 and relevant HTTP/JWT libraries.

facts.label: Rate-limit infrastructure
facts.value: Shared Django cache required across workers; sufficient capacity and atomic add/strongly consistent reads needed for reliable enforcement.

facts.label: Production operation
facts.value: Operator deploys supported Django/app code, HTTPS, protected keys, proper hosts/cookies, email/SMS and cache; runs migrations and production checks.

facts.label: Backup/upgrade work
facts.value: Back up app database and media, including account/provider/authenticator data; review allauth release notes for migrations and changed identifiers/defaults before upgrading.

facts.label: Sizing/capacity
facts.value: No universal CPU/RAM/users-per-server or comparable scenario capacity guarantee found.

facts.label: Custom logic and fields
facts.value: Account/social/MFA/session/headless/issuer adapters and forms extend flows, user creation, validation, redirects, sender logic and claims.

facts.label: Events/hooks
facts.value: Python signals cover auth steps, signup/login/logout, password/email/code events, provider link changes and MFA authenticator changes.

facts.label: Operator administration
facts.value: Django admin/ORM manages app users; allauth adds EmailAddress admin search/filter/edit and mark-verified action, plus provider and enabled module records.

facts.label: Ban/deactivate and API boundary
facts.value: Account views reject inactive users. Headless endpoints manage the signed-in user's own account; general staff REST CRUD, support impersonation and a customer-admin portal need app code.

facts.label: Django admin login exception
facts.value: Default Django admin login bypasses allauth workflows, including its rate limiting and MFA enforcement; documented workaround requires login through allauth first.

facts.label: Account linking/unlinking
facts.value: built_in multiple social accounts per local User; connections UI/API. Disconnect flow rejects removal of the last provider in social-only mode, or when it would leave no usable password.

facts.label: Verified-email auto-match/link policy
facts.value: SOCIALACCOUNT_EMAIL_AUTHENTICATION=False and EMAIL_AUTHENTICATION_AUTO_CONNECT=False by default; selectively enable only for trusted providers.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and adding credentials
facts.value: Existing social users can add a local password; persistent anonymous-user creation/data merging requires custom code.

facts.label: Enumeration and signup controls
facts.value: ACCOUNT_PREVENT_ENUMERATION=True; mandatory verification best hides existing accounts. With optional/no verification, uniqueness can reveal existence unless strict policy permits indistinguishable signup behavior.

facts.label: Password checks and request security
facts.value: Allauth's password adapter calls configured Django validators; social login initiation and logout use POST by default; frontend must escape returned user-controlled API data.

facts.label: IP-based enforcement
facts.value: Default trusted proxy count is 0; configure trusted proxies/header or adapter for real client IP. IPv6 rate keys default to /64 prefix.

facts.label: Login action limits
facts.value: Defaults: login 30/min/IP; login_failed 10/min/IP plus 5/5min/key. Configurable via ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMITS; False disables limits.

facts.label: Signup/reset/account-action limits
facts.value: Defaults: signup 20/min/IP; reset_password 20/min/IP and 5/min/email key; change_password 5/min/user; manage_email 10/min/user; reauthenticate 10/min/user.

facts.label: Passkey/code limits and response
facts.value: Default passwordless WebAuthn login 10/min/IP; login/verification/reset codes also have configured entry-attempt caps. Limit hits render 429.html or a custom handler.

facts.label: Guaranteed throughput
facts.value: No universal auth requests/second, cross-worker burst capacity or management API throughput guarantee found.

facts.label: Available auth/security events
facts.value: Account/social/MFA signals expose completed/rejected steps, signup/login/logout, contact/password changes and authenticator/provider events.

facts.label: Event storage and retention
facts.value: Operator configures durable collection/export and retention; no managed audit retention days or streaming plan. Optional UserSession stores IP/user agent/time for session management.

facts.label: User/contact/provider export
facts.value: Operator owns Django User and allauth EmailAddress/SocialAccount records; Django serialization/dumpdata can export compatible database models including IDs and relationships.

facts.label: Password and provider-token export
facts.value: Passwords are Django encoded hashes; provider token storage is off by default (SOCIALACCOUNT_STORE_TOKENS=False). Stored SocialToken data is in operator database.

facts.label: Passkey/MFA export constraints
facts.value: Authenticator type/data can be exported from the app database; WebAuthn data includes public registration credentials; no authenticator private-key export.

facts.label: Import and password compatibility
facts.value: Use Django models/migrations/fixtures for compatible User and allauth records; Django supports configured existing hash verifiers and password upgrades on login.

facts.label: Prior MFA and provider migrations
facts.value: Official guide supplies reference migration from django-allauth-2fa TOTP/recovery data. Recent release notes require stable-ID updates for affected providers.

facts.label: Deletion of users and related data
facts.value: Operator can delete the Django User through ORM/admin; EmailAddress, SocialAccount, MFA Authenticator and UserSession use cascade relationships to the user.

facts.label: Sessions, logs and backup retention
facts.value: No project-operated retention window applies. UserSession purge removes invalid/absent sessions when examined; end() deletes selected session and tracking record.

facts.label: Vendor account/project closure
facts.value: Not applicable; no allauth cloud account or production project to close.

facts.label: Data location/residency
facts.value: Not applicable to a maintainer-hosted service; developer chooses locations for app/database/cache/logs/backups and external providers.

facts.label: Hosted processing/legal agreements
facts.value: Not applicable to the embedded package: no allauth-hosted processor account, DPA/subprocessor tier or hosted assurance plan.

facts.label: Independent assurance evidence
facts.value: No public independent django-allauth-specific audit report or certification scope/date found in the checked project evidence.

facts.label: Password login

facts.label: Email as login identifier

facts.label: Email magic-link login
