facts.value: plugin: django-allauth MFA extras support WebAuthn credentials and passkey login; WebAuthn and passkey login are disabled by default.

facts.label: Core MFA and recovery codes
facts.value: No built-in TOTP, SMS, email second-factor, WebAuthn MFA or recovery-code enrollment/verification flow.

facts.label: Optional TOTP and recovery
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth MFA extras supply TOTP and recovery codes, including viewing, downloading and regeneration.

facts.label: Optional email login confirmation
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth ACCOUNT_LOGIN_BY_CODE_REQUIRED can require an emailed code, including for specified password/MFA/social methods; off by default.

facts.label: Password reset and password change
facts.value: built_in PasswordResetView/ConfirmView and PasswordChangeView with forms. Default reset mails only active accounts with usable passwords.

facts.label: Reset-token lifetime and invalidation
facts.value: Default PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT = 259200 seconds (3 days); token depends on user ID, password state, last login, timestamp and email.

facts.label: Core email/phone verification
facts.value: custom_code/plugin required for verified-address flags, signup confirmation and phone confirmation.

facts.label: Optional address verification
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth supports email verification by link or code, with mandatory/optional/none policy; current default is optional.

facts.label: Profile change and self-deletion
facts.value: custom_code: build protected profile/address-change and self-service account-deletion views; core admin/ORM can edit/delete users.

facts.label: Session model and default storage
facts.value: built_in cookie session ID; default backend django.contrib.sessions.backends.db stores session data server-side.

facts.label: Default expiry and refresh behavior
facts.value: SESSION_COOKIE_AGE = 1209600 seconds (2 weeks); SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE = False; SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST = False.

facts.label: Cookie security configuration
facts.value: Default HttpOnly = True, SameSite = Lax, Secure = False; production HTTPS deployments should explicitly set secure session/CSRF cookies.

facts.label: Logout and session fixation
facts.value: login() cycles the anonymous session key or flushes a mismatched session and rotates the CSRF token; logout() flushes the current session. LogoutView accepts POST.

facts.label: Password-change revocation
facts.value: With AbstractBaseUser session hashes, a password change invalidates other sessions on subsequent checks; built-in change flow preserves the current authenticated session with a new hash/key.

facts.label: Other session backends and revocation limits
facts.value: Optional cached_db, cache, file and signed-cookie backends. Signed cookies are signed, not encrypted, and logout cannot invalidate a stolen old cookie server-side.

facts.label: Core federation role
facts.value: No built-in SAML SP/IdP or OIDC relying-party/issuer service. Custom backends or extensions bridge external identity sources.

facts.label: Trusted upstream SSO
facts.value: built_in RemoteUserMiddleware/RemoteUserBackend accept identity authenticated by a web server or trusted reverse proxy.

facts.label: Optional SAML role
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth SAML 2.0 service-provider flow, with per-organization-slug IdP configuration, ACS/SLS/metadata endpoints; install saml extras.

facts.label: Optional OIDC role
facts.value: plugin: django-allauth generic OpenID Connect relying-party/client provider configuration, including multiple independent issuers.

facts.label: Groups and permissions
facts.value: built_in users can belong to multiple Groups; group permissions and per-user permissions are combined.

facts.label: Permission granularity
facts.value: Default add/change/delete/view model permissions; ModelBackend does not implement object-specific permissions even though an object argument/extensibility exists.

facts.label: Customer workspaces and invitations
facts.value: custom_code/plugin required for organization records, member invitations, tenant-scoped roles and customer administration.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning service
facts.value: Not applicable to the bundled core offer; no built-in SCIM user/group endpoint, deactivation protocol or directory-connection plan.

facts.label: Built-in views and forms
facts.value: Login/logout, password change and password reset Python views/forms are supplied; URLconf can mount them under the app's chosen path.

facts.label: Consumer login templates
facts.value: Core auth views provide no default consumer HTML templates; developer creates and brands the required templates.

facts.label: Signup and account screens
facts.value: UserCreationForm is built in; signup view/routing, profile editor, factor/device screens and self-service deletion need application code or plugins.

facts.label: Administrative interface
facts.value: Django admin supplies an operator-facing login and User/Group management screens.

facts.label: Branding and UI customization
facts.value: Own templates/CSS, view/form overrides and admin customization; no vendor-brand-removal tier.

facts.label: Login domains
facts.value: App runs on operator-configured hosts; no hosted custom-domain count or fee. Cookie domain defaults to None (host-only scope).

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Translation hooks and built-in language catalog codes: af, ar, ar-dz, ast, az, bg, be, bn, br, bs, ca, ckb, cs, cy, da, de, dsb, el, en, en-au, en-gb, eo, es, es-ar, es-co, es-mx, es-ni, es-ve, et, eu, fa, fi, fr, fy, ga, gd, gl, he, hi, hr, hsb, ht, hu, hy, ia, id, ig, io, is, it, ja, ka, kab, kk, km, kn, ko, ky, lb, lt, lv, mk, ml, mn, mr, ms, my, nb, ne, nl, nn, os, pa, pl, pt, pt-br, ro, ru, sk, sl, sq, sr, sr-latn, sv, sw, ta, te, tg, th, tk, tr, tt, udm, ug, uk, ur, uz, vi, zh-hans, zh-hant.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: DSF public statement aims for recognized WCAG/ATAG standards and describes admin/forms improvement work, issue tracking and assistive-technology testing.

facts.label: Python runtime compatibility
facts.value: Django 6.1 supports Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15 (3.15 added in 6.1.3); only supported latest micro releases should be used.

facts.label: Server interfaces
facts.value: Official WSGI and ASGI deployment interfaces; docs cover Gunicorn/uWSGI/Apache and Daphne/Hypercorn/Uvicorn/Granian options.

facts.label: Optional plugin compatibility
facts.value: Current django-allauth requirements list Python 3.11–3.14 and Django 4.2+.

facts.label: Native/mobile client integration
facts.value: custom_code/plugin: core provides Python APIs and browser form/cookie views; no bundled iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop auth SDK.

facts.label: Database prerequisite
facts.value: Standard auth models require the app database. Official backends include PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL, SQLite and Oracle; SQLite is the default, PostgreSQL recommended for production.

facts.label: Session, email and optional dependencies
facts.value: Default sessions use the database; cache/file/signed-cookie alternatives available. Email backend needed for delivered resets; Argon2/bcrypt require added dependencies when selected.

facts.label: Production deployment responsibilities
facts.value: Production web server, HTTPS, protected SECRET_KEY, ALLOWED_HOSTS, DEBUG=False, safe cookies, static files and error handling.

facts.label: Backup and restore planning
facts.value: Operator arranges database and media backups, handles selected storage and verifies the app's recovery process.

facts.label: Upgrade requirements
facts.value: Read release notes and deprecations, check third-party compatibility, upgrade incrementally across feature releases and test the application.

facts.label: Capacity and sizing
facts.value: No universal CPU/RAM/users-per-server sizing or guaranteed capacity for these four user scenarios found.

facts.label: Custom user fields and account model
facts.value: built_in extension mechanism: custom AUTH_USER_MODEL, AbstractUser/AbstractBaseUser, related profile models and pluggable authentication backends.

facts.label: Login events and custom logic
facts.value: built_in user_logged_in, user_logged_out and user_login_failed Python signals; sync/async auth APIs and custom view/backend logic.

facts.label: Admin actions and search
facts.value: UserAdmin creates/edits/deletes users, changes passwords, assigns flags/groups/permissions and searches username, first/last name and email.

facts.label: Deactivation and programmatic management
facts.value: Default ModelBackend rejects is_active=False users; User manager/ORM creates and queries accounts; async counterparts exist.

facts.label: Management API and impersonation boundary
facts.value: Python User/admin APIs are built in; public REST management endpoints and controlled support-user impersonation require custom code or another package.

facts.label: Linking multiple identity providers
facts.value: custom_code/plugin: core has no social-account/provider-link table or ready link/unlink flow.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: AnonymousUser cannot be saved as a database User; login() retains anonymous session data when entering an authenticated session.

facts.label: Login throttling
facts.value: Default ModelBackend provides no brute-force rate-limiting mechanism; implement a backend/proxy control or add a package.

facts.label: Password validation defaults
facts.value: Framework AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS default is []; the standard startproject template enables similarity, minimum-length, common-password and numeric-only validators.

facts.label: Validation enforcement and breach checks
facts.value: Core forms/commands use configured validators; User.objects.create_user()/create_superuser() do not automatically apply them. Custom flows should call validate_password.

facts.label: Other abuse/security controls
facts.value: Built-in CSRF/session protections and configurable HTTPS/cookie settings; CAPTCHA, bot scoring, SMS pumping controls and live breach services need added code/services.

facts.label: Enforced core login quota
facts.value: No default auth login-attempt rate limit; limits must be implemented in the application/server layer.

facts.label: Throughput and management burst capacity
facts.value: No universal login requests/second or management-API burst guarantee found.

facts.label: Authentication events
facts.value: user_logged_in, user_logged_out and user_login_failed signals; failed-login credentials are cleansed for sensitive key names before dispatch.

facts.label: Admin change log
facts.value: Admin LogEntry stores actor, timestamp, content type/object, action flag and change message for admin model actions.

facts.label: Audit retention and streaming
facts.value: custom_code/operator configuration: choose logging handlers, storage, retention and export/streaming; no built-in managed auth-audit retention tier.

facts.label: Profile/identifier/permission export
facts.value: built_in dumpdata and serializers export selected database models; JSON/JSONL/XML and YAML formats supported, with YAML dependency when used.

facts.label: Password-hash export
facts.value: User.password is an encoded hash string in the developer's database and can be included in trusted fixtures/database exports.

facts.label: Provider/passkey records on exit
facts.value: Core has no social-account/passkey records to export. Optional package tables and their identifiers/credential-domain rules need a separate migration.

facts.label: Model-data import
facts.value: built_in loaddata/deserialization can restore compatible model records and relations; primary keys and natural keys need correct schema/relationship handling.

facts.label: Password migration
facts.value: Existing supported encoded hashes can be checked with configured PASSWORD_HASHERS and upgraded on successful password login; custom hashers/wrapped migrations are supported.

facts.label: Custom-user migration limits
facts.value: Changing AUTH_USER_MODEL after tables exist is not automatic and affects foreign keys, many-to-many relations and migration dependencies.

facts.label: User deletion
facts.value: ORM Model.delete()/adelete() or admin deletion removes database objects, subject to configured related-model deletion behavior.

facts.label: Expired session cleanup
facts.value: clearsessions removes expired stored sessions; operator must arrange regular cleanup for database/file storage.

facts.label: Vendor account closure and fixed retention
facts.value: Not applicable; no Django auth vendor account, managed data store, fixed backup window or deletion SLA.

facts.label: Hosted regions and residency
facts.value: Not applicable to a Django-operated service; app operator chooses database, application, log and backup locations.

facts.label: Processing agreement and hosted assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to core as an embedded library: no Django-managed auth processor, customer DPA, subprocessor plan or SaaS SOC 2 tier.

facts.label: Public security process
facts.value: Official security policy defines private reporting, severity/response process and supported release scope.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Django authentication; bundled module django.contrib.auth in the Django framework. Official documentation: https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/topics/auth/.

facts.label: Project stewardship
facts.value: Django Project and contributors; supported by the independent nonprofit Django Software Foundation (DSF). Repository: django/django.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Active maintained open-source project; current official release 6.1.3. Public repository is not archived and not disabled.

facts.label: End-of-support notice
facts.value: Django 4.2 LTS reached the end of extended support on April 7, 2026; official notice directs users to 5.2 or later.

facts.label: Security-reporting route change
facts.value: October 8, 2026: no new Django security reports through HackerOne; existing reports continue; new reports go to security@djangoproject.com.

facts.label: Core license and commercial use
facts.value: BSD-3-Clause; source and binary redistribution, with or without modification, allowed subject to notice, reproduction and non-endorsement conditions. Software license fee: 0.

facts.label: Name and logo rights
facts.value: Django trademark rules are separate from the BSD code license; incorporating the name/logo into a brand can require the trademark license.

facts.label: Optional plugin license
facts.value: Representative optional package django-allauth: MIT license, with notice requirement; no license fee specified.

facts.label: Service status and uptime SLA
facts.value: Not applicable; Django authentication is in the operator's application, with no Django-operated production auth endpoint or subscription availability promise.

facts.label: Current security patch evidence
facts.value: November 3, 2026: Django 6.1.3, 6.0.10 and 5.2.19 released as security patches.

facts.label: Supported branches and end dates
facts.value: 5.2 LTS: latest 5.2.19, extended support until April 2028. 6.0: 6.0.10, extended until April 2027. 6.1: 6.1.3, mainstream until April 2027, extended until December 2027.

facts.label: Announced release-policy transition
facts.value: 6.2 is the final old-style release; from Django 2028, annual year-numbered feature releases receive 3 years of support.

facts.label: Community and bug support
facts.value: Official community page links Django Forum and Discord for help; public issue tracker/contribution routes for normal bugs.

facts.label: Private security support timing
facts.value: Report to security@djangoproject.com; policy says acknowledgment within 3 working days and aims to resolve reports within 90 days; confirmed high-severity issues addressed promptly.

facts.label: Paid app-support price or response SLA
facts.value: No DSF core-auth paid support tariff or binding production-response SLA found in the checked official support, foundation, license and security pages.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable; Djoser has no MAU, returning-user, login, token, stored-account or builder-seat billing meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: MIT production software license fee 0; no license-imposed usage cap.

facts.label: Hosted free allowance
facts.value: Not applicable; the project does not provide a hosted auth tenant or included monthly email/SMS send allowance.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable; no required paid production edition, monthly base fee or annual Djoser license term.

facts.label: Usage tiers and overages
facts.value: Not applicable; no Djoser rate card, per-connection tier, volume rounding or subscription overage.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: Not applicable to a bundled organization product; no customer workspace, membership or invitation model/allowance in 2.3.5.

facts.label: SSO and sync fees
facts.value: No Djoser per-connection software fee. Generic OIDC and SAML are upstream Python Social Auth integrations; no managed SCIM connection plan.

facts.label: Developer seats, apps and environments
facts.value: Not applicable; no vendor dashboard seats, project/app/environment or domain subscription caps.

facts.label: Email delivery and cost
facts.value: Activation/reset/change notifications use the app's Django email backend; developer supplies sender credentials and pays any delivery provider.

facts.label: SMS/other external costs
facts.value: No bundled phone-code/SMS delivery path in released account routes/serializers. Custom messaging must select and fund its own service.

facts.label: Subscription limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable; no Djoser MAU cap causes automatic upgrade, overage invoice or login cutoff.

facts.label: Other billable product limits
facts.value: Not applicable; no Djoser fees for JWT issuance/refresh, WebAuthn, requests, audit events, developer seats or membership transactions.

facts.label: Hosted account/market eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted vendor account; published MIT package can be used by individual and commercial developers without a company-domain billing gate.

facts.label: Hosted self-service/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable; public package installation and Django configuration replace a hosted signup or sales process.

facts.label: Product type and coverage
facts.value: Embedded Python/Django REST Framework library: account registration/profile/deletion, password login/reset/change, activation, token endpoints, JWT and social integration, optional bundled WebAuthn.

facts.label: Core versus integrations
facts.value: Core account API plus DRF token integration; JWT uses SimpleJWT; social uses Python Social Auth; WebAuthn is a bundled optional module with a separate dependency.

facts.label: Who runs and stores accounts
facts.value: Developer or chosen host runs Django, databases, token/session storage, signing keys, mail delivery, backups, restoration and updates.

facts.label: Password and email/password login
facts.value: built_in token login uses the configured user identifier and Django authenticate(). Default LOGIN_FIELD is User.USERNAME_FIELD; email/password requires an appropriate user model/backend.

facts.label: Email magic links/codes
facts.value: custom_code/other package required for general passwordless email-link or email-code sign-in; built-in email links activate accounts or reset credentials.

facts.label: Phone, wallet and anonymous login
facts.value: No bundled phone-code or wallet-signature login, or persisted guest-account creation/upgrade API in the published endpoint/schema scope.

facts.label: Social integration and API maturity
facts.value: plugin: Python Social Auth via djoser.social; provider authorization URL then redirect code/state exchange. API is beta and may break compatibility.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: plugin: social_core.backends.google.GoogleOAuth2, provider google-oauth2; external client credentials and redirect registration.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: plugin: social_core.backends.github.GithubOAuth2, provider github; organization/team/app variants exist upstream.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: plugin: social_core.backends.apple.AppleIdAuth, provider apple-id; Apple registration/signing configuration required.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: plugin: MicrosoftOAuth2/microsoft-graph; Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD provider-specific alternatives are documented upstream.

facts.label: Facebook and other providers
facts.value: plugin: FacebookOAuth2 plus the upstream backend directory; provider-specific configuration/integration required.

facts.label: WebAuthn availability and fee
facts.value: Bundled optional djoser.webauthn module; install djoser[webauthn], enable app/migrations/routes. No software fee; dependency constrained to webauthn<1.0.

facts.label: First-factor WebAuthn flow
facts.value: Username-based registration and assertion login; successful login returns the configured DRF token. Assertion verifier is called with uv_required=False.

facts.label: Credential inventory and domains
facts.value: One CredentialOptions record per user; stores one credential ID/public key/counter. Configure RP_ID/RP_NAME/ORIGIN; defaults target localhost.

facts.label: WebAuthn browser-call documentation
facts.value: Docs tell the login flow to use navigator.credentials.create(); bundled browser example uses navigator.credentials.get() for login, and create() for signup.

facts.label: Native/synced passkey support matrix
facts.value: Not published for this wrapper: native OS/client minimum versions, synced credentials, conditional autofill and lost-device platform recovery guarantees.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: No bundled TOTP, SMS/email second-factor enforcement, factor enrollment policy or recovery-code endpoints in 2.3.5. WebAuthn login is not a password-plus-key MFA flow.

facts.label: Lost-key recovery limitations
facts.value: Custom recovery required for WebAuthn-only users. Default creation omits a password; reset email lookup requires a usable password; self-delete requires current_password.

facts.label: Registration and activation
facts.value: built_in user creation; SEND_ACTIVATION_EMAIL=False by default. If enabled, newly created users become inactive until uid/token activation.

facts.label: Resend and confirmation mail
facts.value: Resend activation supported; active users and users without usable passwords are not sent activation mail. Optional confirmation/change emails default off.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Email request plus uid/token confirmation and validated new password; active user with usable password required. Unknown-email detail hidden by default.

facts.label: Password reset token lifetime
facts.value: Django default_token_generator; PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT default 259,200 seconds (3 days), configurable by the application.

facts.label: Change password or login identifier
facts.value: Set password and set-login-field actions require current_password; retype confirmation can be enabled. Identifier reset also has email/uid/token flows.

facts.label: Change email/phone and deletion
facts.value: If activation is enabled, changing the configured email through UserSerializer marks user inactive and sends activation. Built-in self-delete checks current_password; no built-in phone verification.

facts.label: DRF token sessions
facts.value: Default Token model has one token per user with no expiry field; login gets/creates it, logout deletes it.

facts.label: JWT lifetime and refresh
facts.value: plugin: SimpleJWT access/refresh/verify endpoints. Named 5.5.1 defaults: access 5 minutes, refresh 1 day; refresh rotation and blacklist-after-rotation False.

facts.label: JWT logout/revocation
facts.value: Djoser JWT routes do not include logout/blacklisting. SimpleJWT blacklist support is an additional configured app/route and cleanup responsibility.

facts.label: Django session and password-change behavior
facts.value: CREATE_SESSION_ON_LOGIN=False and LOGOUT_ON_PASSWORD_CHANGE=False by default. Optional Django sessions use framework cookie/session controls.

facts.label: OIDC business login role
facts.value: plugin: Python Social Auth OpenIdConnectAuth is an OIDC relying party/client using an external issuer's discovery and client configuration.

facts.label: SAML business login role
facts.value: plugin/custom integration: Python Social Auth SAMLAuth acts as SAML 2.0 service provider; configure IdP metadata, SP keys/certificates, XML dependencies and routes.

facts.label: Customer organizations, roles and invitations
facts.value: custom_code required; published Djoser models/routes have users, account actions and WebAuthn credentials, not tenant memberships, invitation lifecycles or tenant-scoped roles.

facts.label: SCIM directory sync
facts.value: Not published as a Djoser feature; no SCIM 2.0 Users/Groups API, schema or deprovisioning contract found.

facts.label: Login/account screens
facts.value: Headless account/authentication endpoints; developer builds signup, login, reset/activation landing pages, profile and account-security UI.

facts.label: Examples versus production components
facts.value: Test-project browser WebAuthn example exists; it is example application code, not a maintained React/native component library or hosted account portal.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Application controls its frontend/API domain and email templates; EMAIL_FRONTEND_DOMAIN/PROTOCOL/SITE_NAME override link branding. No Djoser domain fee/cap.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: English source messages plus shipped locale catalog codes ca, de, es, fa, fa_IR, fr, id, ja, ka, me, pl, pt_BR and ru_RU.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Djoser-specific public WCAG conformance statement, VPAT or independently assessed account-UI accessibility report found.

facts.label: Published runtime/framework requirements
facts.value: Djoser 2.3.5 declares Python>=3.9, Django>=3.2, DRF>=3.14; depends on SimpleJWT>=5,<6 and social-auth-app-django>=5,<8.

facts.label: Compatibility documentation discrepancy
facts.value: README says Django 3.2 through 5.2; 2.3.5 release/metadata additionally declare Django 6.0 and 6.1 support, with a 6.1 CI job.

facts.label: Patched social dependency environment
facts.value: 2.3.5 permits patched social-auth majors, but its release says resolving those versions requires Python>=3.10 and Django>=5.2.

facts.label: Mobile/desktop clients
facts.value: Language-neutral HTTP API can be called by external clients; no dedicated Djoser iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop SDK/support matrix found.

facts.label: Database and setup prerequisites
facts.value: Existing Django/DRF application, configured user model/database and URLs; add relevant apps and run migrations for selected token/social/WebAuthn models.

facts.label: Token and social services
facts.value: Default DRF token model stores tokens locally; JWT needs signing configuration; social login needs external provider credentials and Python Social Auth configuration.

facts.label: WebAuthn prerequisites
facts.value: Optional legacy WebAuthn Python dependency, credential database migrations, browser credential API and correctly configured RP/origin.

facts.label: Deployment and backups
facts.value: Deploy as part of Django using the chosen production application server; operator configures TLS, host/cookie security, database/backups and restores.

facts.label: Upgrades and migration guidance
facts.value: Djoser has versioned changelog and a 1.x-to-2.x migration guide; 2.x changes routes/views and is not backwards compatible with 1.x.

facts.label: Sizing/capacity guarantees
facts.value: No published Djoser production sizing table, throughput guarantee or tested concurrent-login capacity found.

facts.label: Custom fields, permissions and flows
facts.value: Override named SERIALIZERS, PERMISSIONS, EMAIL and CONSTANTS mappings; custom user models and view subclasses support application-specific logic.

facts.label: Events and webhook delivery
facts.value: built_in user_registered, user_activated and user_updated Django signals; token utilities also send Django user_logged_in/user_logged_out.

facts.label: Account API and administration
facts.value: UserViewSet supplies registration/list/retrieve/update/delete and /users/me/ actions. Staff can access other users subject to configured permissions.

facts.label: Staff UI, searching and blocking
facts.value: Django admin/ORM and custom serializers/views can manage user fields and is_active; Djoser has no dedicated support dashboard, impersonation or searchable management-service contract.

facts.label: Social linking/unlinking
facts.value: plugin/custom integration: Python Social Auth pipeline associates provider identities; upstream disconnect removes the association and checks another login method by default.

facts.label: Safe linking and guest upgrades
facts.value: Provider identity association and optional email linking require an explicit trusted/verified-email policy. Saved anonymous-to-registered account upgrade is custom application work.

facts.label: Password validation
facts.value: Built-in account create/change/reset serializers call Django validate_password; operator's AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS determine policy.

facts.label: Enumeration and redirect protections
facts.value: Reset 'email not found' disclosure defaults off; HIDE_USERS defaults True; social redirect URI must exactly match the configured allowlist.

facts.label: Authentication warning discrepancy
facts.value: README still warns TokenCreateSerializer bypasses an intentional authenticate() None result; 2.3.5 serializer instead fails, and 2.3.0 changelog records the fix.

facts.label: Rate/bot/abuse integration
facts.value: Custom/global DRF throttles and external bot checks required; released Djoser views do not define dedicated built-in throttle scopes, CAPTCHA or SMS abuse budgets.

facts.label: Published API/login rate limits
facts.value: No vendor-enforced numeric login/management request quota. Default DRF throttle configuration has no throttle classes; application can set classes/rates.

facts.label: Audit event coverage
facts.value: Djoser registration/activation/update signals and Django login/logout signals can feed application logs; no bundled persistent audit store/retention/export service.

facts.label: Export profiles, IDs and password hashes
facts.value: Application owns Django model/database data; Django serialization/ORM can export user IDs, profile fields and encoded password strings.

facts.label: Export social links and WebAuthn records
facts.value: Application can export provider/uid/id_key/extra_data associations and WebAuthn credential ID/public key/sign counter through its database/models.

facts.label: Session/token portability
facts.value: DRF token, Django session and JWT data are application-controlled, but cross-product signed-in-session portability is not supplied.

facts.label: Import profiles/hashes
facts.value: custom_code/framework tooling: use Django ORM/fixtures or an app importer for compatible user schema and encoded passwords; Djoser registration validates a submitted password and creates a user.

facts.label: Identity/hash migration restrictions
facts.value: No Djoser bulk/lazy identity-provider migration service or supported third-party hash conversion matrix found. Custom USER_ID_FIELD controls API identifiers.

facts.label: User deletion API
facts.value: built_in DELETE /users/me/ (or authorized user route), with current_password validation. Current-user deletion logs out through Djoser then deletes the user model.

facts.label: Related credentials and retained copies
facts.value: Djoser WebAuthn credential and upstream social association use cascading foreign keys to the user. Logs, exports, backups and external-provider data need separate cleanup/retention rules.

facts.label: Vendor account closure/retention period
facts.value: Not applicable to a Djoser-hosted account; operator chooses retention and backup deletion for the application it runs.

facts.label: Data location/residency

facts.label: Operator responsibilities
facts.value: Developer runs app, user/entity service, database, signing keys, updates, delivery services, backups and recovery.

facts.label: Local password method
facts.value: plugin @feathersjs/authentication-local: configurable username/email and password fields; LocalStrategy issues an auth result for token creation.

facts.label: Token method
facts.value: built_in JWTStrategy validates an access token; custom AuthenticationBaseStrategy implementations may authenticate other credential types.

facts.label: Anonymous access recipe
facts.value: custom_code official cookbook adds an AnonymousStrategy returning anonymous:true and a hook allowing selected external calls.

facts.label: Magic links, login codes and wallets
facts.value: No native core general email-link/email-code/SMS login or wallet strategy established in current docs/source.

facts.label: Documented social examples
facts.value: plugin OAuth: Google, GitHub and Facebook; generator also offers Auth0 as an external identity integration.

facts.label: Additional provider catalogue
facts.value: OAuth package uses Grant; upstream configuration includes Apple, Microsoft, Discord, GitLab, LinkedIn, Twitter, Spotify, Keycloak and others.

facts.label: Apple implementation
facts.value: Current OAuth callback code verifies Apple's signed ID token and derives profile identity through an Apple-specific helper.

facts.label: Provider mapping and prerequisites
facts.value: Register OAuthStrategy and configure authentication.oauth provider key/secret; getEntityData often needs customization to meet user schema.

facts.label: Passkeys/WebAuthn
facts.value: No official core passkey enrollment/login/recovery or supported-platform flow established.

facts.label: MFA and recovery factors
facts.value: No packaged core TOTP, SMS/email second-factor, security-key enrollment, recovery codes or enforcement flow established.

facts.label: External factor boundary
facts.value: external_service Feathers can delegate identity to a provider such as Auth0 or an OIDC IdP; factors/recovery then follow that provider's integration.

facts.label: Core lifecycle flows
facts.value: Core explicitly excludes verification/password-reset management; generated users service supports signup through create.

facts.label: Verification extension
facts.value: plugin feathers-authentication-management adds long/short signup-verification tokens and isVerified enforcement hooks.

facts.label: Password reset extension
facts.value: Management plugin supports long-token or short-token + user identifier reset; default reset lifetime 7,200,000 ms (2 hours).

facts.label: Password/email change extension
facts.value: Management passwordChange checks old password; identityChange verifies password and pending identity-property change.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: custom_code users-service remove plus related-record/token cleanup; no native self-delete account screen.

facts.label: Default token policy
facts.value: Default access JWT uses HS256, expiresIn 1d, issuer feathers and configurable audience/signing secret.

facts.label: Client storage and transport
facts.value: Authentication client defaults to localStorage when available, otherwise memory; storageKey feathers-jwt; Authorization Bearer for REST.

facts.label: Reauthentication versus refresh
facts.value: Client reAuthenticate reuses stored JWT; JWT strategy returns the same token rather than issuing a fresh one.

facts.label: Logout and revocation
facts.value: Default logout removes client-stored token and calls auth service remove; copied JWT remains usable until expiry absent custom revocation.

facts.label: Entity lookup/stateless boundary
facts.value: Default JWT auth resolves current entity by subject; entity:null skips lookup and preserves token claims until expiry.

facts.label: Real-time connection expiry
facts.value: JWT strategy attaches authentication to connection and schedules disconnect cleanup at token expiry; client reauthenticates after reconnection.

facts.label: Business OIDC role
facts.value: plugin/custom_code OAuthStrategy plus Grant can act as a client of an external OIDC provider; project blog demonstrates Keycloak integration.

facts.label: SAML and issuer roles
facts.value: Native SAML SP/IdP implementation, generic OIDC issuer/authorization server and per-customer connection manager not established.

facts.label: Roles and tenant authorization
facts.value: custom_code services, hooks, schemas and channels enforce role/ownership checks and event audiences.

facts.label: Tenant storage building blocks
facts.value: Database-adapter params.adapter.Model can select different databases per request for multi-tenant systems.

facts.label: Customer organization/invite system
facts.value: No packaged core organization creation, multi-membership/invitation/customer-admin UI or member cap established.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: Native SCIM 2 user/group provisioning, deactivation workflow or directory connector not established.

facts.label: Core UI approach
facts.value: Headless backend/service APIs; app supplies login/signup/account screens and redirects.

facts.label: Official UI example
facts.value: Plain JavaScript frontend guide supplies login/signup, GitHub login and logout for the example chat app.

facts.label: Branding/domain model
facts.value: App owns frontend, hosting domain and OAuth callback path; no auth-brand-removal or custom-domain licence add-on.

facts.label: Redirect configuration
facts.value: OAuth supports fixed redirect or allowed origins plus same-origin path validation; bearer result normally delivered in fragment.

facts.label: Hosted translations/accessibility report
facts.value: Not applicable to core headless library: no vendor-hosted UI language catalogue or shared login-screen conformance score.

facts.label: Server runtime/version scope
facts.value: Reviewed auth package manifests declare Node >=12; project support FAQ promises current Active LTS and newer.

facts.label: Transports and frameworks
facts.value: Official Feathers server integration with Express or Koa; REST and Socket.io transports; JS/TypeScript browser/Node clients.

facts.label: Typed frontend integration
facts.value: Generated application client can be installed in TypeScript applications such as React, Vue and React Native.

facts.label: React Native
facts.value: Official client guide uses React Native with a supplied AsyncStorage adapter; same auth API as Node/browser.

facts.label: Other native/desktop clients
facts.value: REST API can be consumed by other HTTP clients; no official dedicated Swift/Kotlin/Flutter/Desktop auth SDK established.

facts.label: User persistence prerequisite
facts.value: App provides entity service, normally users, backed by chosen adapter/database or a custom service.

facts.label: Database choices
facts.value: Official adapters: Memory, MongoDB and SQL via Knex; SQL catalogue includes MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, SQLite, Redshift, OracleDB and MSSQL.

facts.label: Additional dependencies
facts.value: OAuth needs Grant/provider credentials/transaction sessions; notifications need sender; optional JWT revocation example uses Redis.

facts.label: Management plugin compatibility
facts.value: Reviewed management manifest 5.1.0 declares Feathers peer ^5.0.0 and Node >=14; dependencies include Auth/Local/Client ^5.0.11.

facts.label: Deployment
facts.value: Official Docker recipe treats Feathers as an ordinary Node app, listening on configured port and starting with app's npm start.

facts.label: Backups/upgrades/capacity
facts.value: Operator backs up database/config/signing material and any revoke store, upgrades dependencies and plans runtime capacity.

facts.label: Extensibility
facts.value: Register custom strategies and override AuthenticationService payload, token options, authentication or verification behavior.

facts.label: Hooks and extra fields
facts.value: Around/before/after/error hooks are transport-independent; schemas/resolvers validate, derive and hide user fields.

facts.label: Authentication/service events
facts.value: Authentication service emits app login/logout; services emit created/updated/patched/removed after hooks finish.

facts.label: User administration APIs
facts.value: custom_code users-service find/get/create/update/patch/remove can provide admin functions; app sets authentication/authorization and public methods.

facts.label: Blocking accounts
facts.value: custom_code LocalStrategy/JWTStrategy getEntityQuery can require active:true; app maintains the flag and access rules.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: No native audited impersonation session/UI or first-class operator safety workflow established.

facts.label: Default OAuth matching
facts.value: OAuthStrategy matches profile.sub or profile.id against <providerName>Id; creates new entity or updates matched/current authenticated entity.

facts.label: Authenticated account linking
facts.value: OAuth supports feathers_token with configured linkStrategy (default jwt); current code checks allowed initiating origin and verifies current auth.

facts.label: Unlinking/guest upgrade
facts.value: No packaged native unlink/merge UI or durable-guest-to-registered data migration flow established.

facts.label: Password hashing
facts.value: LocalStrategy uses bcryptjs with configurable hashSize default 10; v5 passwordHash resolver is preferred for storing password data.

facts.label: Failure messages/timing
facts.value: Default message Invalid login covers failed local login; source returns early if no user before running bcrypt compare.

facts.label: OAuth public strategy restriction
facts.value: Browser providers should be registered/configured but omitted from public authStrategies unless getProfile verifies supplied provider tokens.

facts.label: OAuth callback/link hardening
facts.value: Current source validates linking origins, redirect paths and provider callback consistency; dynamic configuration filters protected settings.

facts.label: JWT/browser abuse boundary
facts.value: Bearer-header/localStorage approach avoids automatic cookie attachment for API JWT; XSS can still steal stored token; cookie-based JWT needs CSRF protection.

facts.label: CAPTCHA/compromised-password controls
facts.value: Native core CAPTCHA, breached-password screening, managed SMS-fraud controls or fixed account-lockout policy not established.

facts.label: Management token abuse controls
facts.value: Reset-token default resetAttempts 0 means first invalid attempt clears current reset credentials; reuseResetToken false hashes stored reset tokens.

facts.label: Hosted quotas and capacity
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor login/API endpoint, per-plan request allowance or guaranteed concurrent-login quota.

facts.label: Application rate limiting
facts.value: No default core numeric per-user/IP login or management request rate established.

facts.label: Audit integration
facts.value: App login/logout and service CRUD/error hooks can feed custom audit logs; no built-in hosted audit viewer.

facts.label: Managed log retention/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor auth-audit retention days, log-drain entitlement or storage tariff.

facts.label: Profile/ID export
facts.value: custom_code/operator database access can export entity IDs and profile/provider ID fields; users-service find can paginate results.

facts.label: Password-hash portability
facts.value: bcryptjs hashes live in operator user storage; external resolver normally hides password field, not deletes DB hash.

facts.label: Tokens and linked identities
facts.value: Provider IDs and app-specific linkage fields remain in user data; live app JWTs rely on original signer/issuer/audience policy.

facts.label: Migration-in building blocks
facts.value: custom_code DB/service import can preserve compatible bcrypt hashes and IDs when schema/adapter permits and password hashing is deliberately bypassed.

facts.label: Other hash formats/bulk migration
facts.value: No turnkey core vendor-migration importer, lazy migration bridge or published cross-provider hash compatibility matrix established.

facts.label: User-data deletion
facts.value: custom_code users remove plus selected relationship, session/revocation and plugin-field cleanup; multi-remove must be enabled explicitly.

facts.label: Vendor closure/retention clock
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-hosted Auth app-user database/account to close or vendor backup purge deadline.

facts.label: Data location/residency
facts.value: App operator chooses server/database/log/backup location and upstream providers; no fixed Feathers auth-hosting region.

facts.label: Hosted privacy/assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to code library: no Feathers-operated auth processor DPA, runtime subprocessor list or managed-auth audit/SOC tier.

facts.label: Business A/B — complete baseline

facts.label: Hosted signup/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable; public pip installation plus Flask LoginManager/user-loader configuration.

facts.label: Type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Flask session-management library: current user loading, login/logout helpers, protected views, remember-me cookies and fresh-login checks.

facts.label: Account-system boundary
facts.value: No bundled identity database, registration/reset API, credential checker, social-provider adapters or hosted account service.

facts.label: Operator and responsibilities
facts.value: Developer/chosen host operates the Flask app, user persistence, credential checks, keys, session configuration, backups and updates.

facts.label: Password and email/password
facts.value: custom_code: app looks up a user and verifies credentials, then calls login_user(). It may use an email identifier; library does not impose a credential method.

facts.label: Email-link/code, phone and wallet login
facts.value: custom_code/external_service required; no bundled magic-link, email OTP, phone OTP or wallet-signature verifier.

facts.label: Anonymous users
facts.value: built_in AnonymousUserMixin represents unauthenticated requests, with get_id() returning None; not a saved guest-account product.

facts.label: Request-based authentication
facts.value: built_in request_loader callback lets app code return a user from a Flask request; API keys/Basic header parsing are examples supplied by the app.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft and other social login require separate protocol/provider integration; no bundled adapters or provider directory.

facts.label: Passkeys/security keys
facts.value: custom_code/other package required; no bundled WebAuthn credential models, browser ceremony, passkey endpoints or RP/domain configuration.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: No bundled TOTP, SMS/email second-factor, WebAuthn MFA, recovery codes or enrollment/enforcement policy.

facts.label: Fresh login versus MFA
facts.value: built_in fresh_login_required checks session authentication freshness; confirm_login() marks the session fresh after the app reauthenticates.

facts.label: Registration, activation and verification
facts.value: custom_code/other package: library explicitly excludes registration; no bundled email/phone activation or confirmation sender.

facts.label: Password reset/address changes
facts.value: custom_code/other package: account recovery, password reset/change and email/phone changes are outside core scope.

facts.label: Self-service deletion
facts.value: custom_code: no user-delete endpoint or credential-confirmed account-deletion flow.

facts.label: Flask session storage
facts.value: Stores _user_id/_fresh/_id and related flags in Flask session; default Flask session interface is a signed browser cookie.

facts.label: Ordinary session lifetime
facts.value: login_user does not set session.permanent. Browser-session cookie is the default; named Flask 3.1.3 validates signature age against PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME, default 31 days (2,678,400 seconds).

facts.label: Remember-me duration and renewal
facts.value: Opt-in login_user(remember=True); browser remember cookie defaults to 365 days, configurable by REMEMBER_COOKIE_DURATION or per-login duration. Refresh-each-request defaults False.

facts.label: Remember token validation
facts.value: 0.6.3 remember token signs user ID with HMAC-SHA512; payload has no issued-at or expiry timestamp, and decode_cookie verifies the signature rather than token age.

facts.label: Logout and lost-device revocation
facts.value: logout_user removes current Flask-Login session keys and asks the response to clear that client's remember cookie; no global session/device revocation store.

facts.label: Alternative-ID invalidation
facts.value: Documented custom get_id()/user_loader pattern uses a separate unique random alternative ID; rotating it can invalidate old sessions/remember identities.

facts.label: Freshness and sensitive views
facts.value: login_user defaults fresh=True; remember restoration sets fresh=False. login_required does not require freshness; fresh_login_required redirects to app refresh_view or returns 401.

facts.label: Cookie security defaults
facts.value: Remember cookie defaults: name remember_token; HttpOnly=True, Secure=False, SameSite=None; domain unset, path /. Flask session cookie security has separate settings.

facts.label: Signing-key rotation
facts.value: Flask 3.1 session implementation supports SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS; Flask-Login 0.6.3 remember decoding uses only SECRET_KEY unless custom code supplies a different key.

facts.label: Strong protection cleanup discrepancy
facts.value: Docs describe deletion of the entire session in strong mode; released implementation removes only the listed Flask-Login SESSION_KEYS and sets remember cleanup.

facts.label: SAML and OIDC roles
facts.value: No built-in SAML SP/IdP or OIDC relying-party/provider implementation. External/custom authentication can be followed by a Flask-Login session.

facts.label: Organizations and role authorization
facts.value: custom_code/other package required for customer tenants, memberships, invitations, roles and customer administration.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: Not applicable to a bundled business identity product; no SCIM Users/Groups/deprovisioning implementation in the released package.

facts.label: Login, registration and account screens
facts.value: Developer supplies all production templates/forms/routes; login_view and refresh_view name app-defined endpoints, not hosted pages or packaged account components.

facts.label: Unauthorized/API responses
facts.value: Default unauthorized handler flashes a message and redirects to configured login view; without one returns 401. Custom handler can return an API response.

facts.label: Branding/custom domains
facts.value: App controls templates and its domain; no vendor branding-removal tier/domain fee. Remember cookie name/domain/path can be configured.

facts.label: Languages/localization
facts.value: Default login/reauthentication flash messages are English; set custom messages and localize_callback, for example a gettext function.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No project-specific WCAG/VPAT or independent accessibility assessment of a shipped account UI found.

facts.label: Released requirements/runtime
facts.value: Flask-Login 0.6.3: Python>=3.7, Flask>=1.0.4, Werkzeug>=1.0.1. Backend is Python/Flask; dependencies have their own version requirements.

facts.label: Current dependency and development requirements
facts.value: Current checked Flask 3.1.3 and Werkzeug 3.1.9 require Python>=3.9. Unreleased Flask-Login 0.7.0.dev instead declares Python>=3.8, Flask>=2.3, Werkzeug>=2.3.2.

facts.label: Flask factories and asynchronous views
facts.value: LoginManager.init_app supports Flask factories; 0.6.3 protected-view decorators use Flask ensure_sync when available.

facts.label: Mobile and desktop integration
facts.value: No official Flask-Login native iOS/Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop SDK/client support matrix found.

facts.label: User store/model prerequisite
facts.value: Developer supplies a persistent user store and user_loader callback accepting a string ID, plus is_authenticated/is_active/is_anonymous/get_id behavior.

facts.label: Sessions and secrets
facts.value: A Flask app and securely generated SECRET_KEY are needed for normal cookie sessions/remember tokens. Default session storage is browser-side signed data.

facts.label: Production deployment
facts.value: Deploy the containing Flask app with a production WSGI server/hosting platform; configure HTTPS, proxy trust, host validation and cookies.

facts.label: Backups, restore and upgrade
facts.value: Operator backs up its own user/credential data and configuration; review versioned changes and separate database/session/provider migrations when upgrading.

facts.label: Sizing/throughput evidence
facts.value: No project-specific production sizing table, benchmark guarantee or supported concurrent-user/request capacity found.

facts.label: Custom logic and user data
facts.value: App-defined user object and user_loader/request_loader; custom unauthorized/needs-refresh handlers, anonymous user factory and login/localization settings.

facts.label: Events/webhooks
facts.value: built_in in-process signals for login, logout, user loading/access, login confirmation, unauthorized access, refresh requirements and session protection.

facts.label: Account administration/API
facts.value: No built-in create/list/search/delete user management API, admin dashboard or impersonation function; app owns storage and administration.

facts.label: Disable/ban behavior
facts.value: login_user rejects is_active=False unless force=True; UserMixin defaults is_active=True and is_authenticated follows is_active.

facts.label: Link/unlink login methods
facts.value: custom_code/other package: no provider-account association table, link/unlink endpoint or last-credential recovery check.

facts.label: Saved guest account upgrades
facts.value: custom_code: default anonymous user has no ID and no persisted account; no automatic guest data/account conversion.

facts.label: Session protection defaults
facts.value: built_in basic mode hashes address/user-agent context and marks mismatches non-fresh; strong mode removes Flask-Login keys for non-permanent sessions. Permanent sessions are marked non-fresh.

facts.label: Proxy trust/version difference
facts.value: Released 0.6.3 identifier helper reads the first X-Forwarded-For value when present; unreleased main uses request.remote_addr and expects correct proxy configuration.

facts.label: CSRF, redirects and password checking
facts.value: App supplies CSRF protection and validation of next redirects; no bundled CAPTCHA, password policy/breach feed or lockout/attempt counter.

facts.label: Demo authentication limits
facts.value: 0.6.3 README's request_loader returns an existing user from submitted email alone; the README explicitly warns its examples take production-inappropriate shortcuts.

facts.label: API/login rate limits
facts.value: No built-in numeric login/API quota or request-attempt limiter in released core. App/middleware/proxy supplies any rate policy.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Login/logout, confirmation, user access/loading, unauthorized/refresh and session-protection signals are available; no built-in durable audit log/export/retention policy.

facts.label: Export user profiles and credentials
facts.value: App-controlled storage: export profile data, identifiers and password hashes using the selected database/ORM/tooling; Flask-Login imposes no user export format.

facts.label: Session/remember-token exit limits
facts.value: Sessions contain app-selected IDs; remember token encodes that ID plus a signature. Migrating signed-in state requires compatible IDs, loaders and signing/session configuration.

facts.label: Import existing identities
facts.value: custom_code: import into the chosen user store and implement compatible string-ID loading. No built-in bulk/lazy import, password hash converter or hosted-vendor migration wizard.

facts.label: Password backend migration scope
facts.value: A separately chosen Werkzeug password checker can handle its supported scrypt/PBKDF2 encoded formats; arbitrary vendor hashes require compatible code or reset/rehash policy.

facts.label: Deletion and retained data
facts.value: App must delete its user/credential/profile records and remove or invalidate authentication mappings; logout_user only clears current-client login state.

facts.label: Invalid-loader ID cleanup discrepancy
facts.value: Docs say an invalid loader ID will be removed from session; 0.6.3 _load_user instead falls back to remember/request/anonymous without explicitly removing that stale _user_id.

facts.label: Vendor account closure/retention
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted Flask-Login account; no product-hosted account, log-retention schedule or project closure action.

facts.label: Data location/residency
facts.value: Operator chooses application/user-store regions; default signed session and remember cookies are stored in clients' browsers.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Not applicable to Flask-Login as hosted identity processor; embedded package does not supply a hosted processing agreement/subprocessor roster.

facts.label: Independent assurance report
facts.value: No Flask-Login-specific public SOC 2/ISO certification, independent security assessment or dated control report found.

facts.label: Self-service/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable; install/configure the public Python package and selected model/dependencies.

facts.label: Product type and coverage
facts.value: Embedded Flask account/authentication/authorization toolkit: login/signup/recovery, verification, sessions/tokens, roles/permissions, optional MFA/passkeys/social login and account changes.

facts.label: Core, flags and integrations
facts.value: One MIT package; many features default disabled. Flask-Login, Flask-Principal, Flask-WTF and libpass underpin core; optional extras supply database, mail/Argon2, translations and MFA dependencies.

facts.label: Operator/responsibilities
facts.value: Developer/chosen host runs Flask, account/role/credential storage, mail/SMS, secrets, patches, backups and restores.

facts.label: Password/email/username login
facts.value: built_in email/password login with normalization/validation; optional username identity. Argon2 is default password hash via libpass; install its backend.

facts.label: Unified email/authenticator codes
facts.value: built_in optional UNIFIED_SIGNIN provides identity/passcode login; methods include password, email, authenticator and SMS. Default unified code validity 120 seconds.

facts.label: Phone-code first-factor login
facts.value: built_in optional unified signin plus external SMS sender and phone identity mapping/model fields.

facts.label: Magic-link login
facts.value: built_in older PASSWORDLESS email-link flow and unified signin email verification-link routes; require email delivery and feature configuration.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet methods
facts.value: Anonymous request representation is available; no persisted guest-account upgrade or wallet-signature login implementation in released package.

facts.label: Social integration/scope
facts.value: Built-in glue with optional Authlib; OAUTH_ENABLE defaults False; user must already be registered in the app.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: Bundled GoogleFsOauthProvider uses Google's OIDC discovery and openid/email/profile scopes; maps provider userinfo email to a local identity.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: Bundled GitHubFsOauthProvider uses OAuth endpoints, user:email scope and the user profile API; default mapping uses profile email.

facts.label: Apple/Microsoft/other providers
facts.value: custom_code/plugin integration: create/register FsOAuthProvider with provider configuration and fetch_identity_cb. No bundled Apple/Microsoft adapter in 5.9.2.

facts.label: Passkey availability/maturity
facts.value: Bundled optional WebAuthn relying-party feature, disabled by default and labelled Beta; use mfa dependencies including webauthn>=2.8.0 plus credential models.

facts.label: First factor, MFA and verification
facts.value: Allows first-factor, multi-factor and verification uses by default when enabled. Keys register as first or secondary; actual user-verification result controls multi-factor treatment.

facts.label: Key inventory and discoverability
facts.value: Multiple named credentials per user with public key/counter/transports/backup metadata; add/delete flows. Default first-factor selection CROSS_PLATFORM; user hints True, resident keys preferred.

facts.label: Domain/origin handling
facts.value: WebauthnUtil.origin uses request.host_url without trailing slash; implementation uses request host without port for RP ID; utility methods can be customized.

facts.label: Browser/native/autofill evidence
facts.value: Browser JS for credential create/get is bundled. No wrapper-specific native iOS/Android/synced-passkey version matrix or conditional-autofill contract found.

facts.label: Authenticator-app second factor
facts.value: built_in optional TOTP via encrypted per-user secret and configured app TOTP keys/issuer; default authenticator validity window 120 seconds.

facts.label: Email/SMS second factors
facts.value: built_in optional email code window 300 seconds; SMS code window 120 seconds with external sender. Both are configurable.

facts.label: Enforcement and remembered second factor
facts.value: TWO_FACTOR=False and TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED=False by default; user check_tf_required can enforce per-user/role policy. ALWAYS_VALIDATE=True by default.

facts.label: Recovery/rescue
facts.value: Optional one-use recovery codes default disabled, count 5; can replace configured second factor. Rescue email defaults enabled; admin-help email is another path.

facts.label: Recovery-code storage/expiry
facts.value: Recovery codes are stored without encryption by default; configure Fernet key list for encryption/rotation. Code TTL default None; used code is deleted.

facts.label: Registration and email confirmation
facts.value: Optional REGISTERABLE and CONFIRMABLE default False. Enabled email confirmation uses signed link, resend support and confirmed_at; default link lifetime 2 days.

facts.label: Reset and change password
facts.value: RECOVERABLE/CHANGEABLE default False. Reset-link lifetime defaults 1 day; reset/change hashes the password and rotates fs_uniquifier, invalidating existing sessions.

facts.label: Email/username change and phone proof
facts.value: Optional email change confirms the new address (default link lifetime 2 hours); optional username change/recovery endpoints. SMS setup verifies the code before committing the new configuration.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: Datastore delete_user exists for application administration; no bundled authenticated self-service account-delete endpoint in the published account routes/OpenAPI.

facts.label: Sessions/remembered login
facts.value: Flask-Login sessions use fs_uniquifier as alternative identity; DEFAULT_REMEMBER_ME=False. Underlying default remember cookie duration 365 days, configurable.

facts.label: Authentication tokens and expiry
facts.value: Signed ItsDangerous tokens, not a JWT/OIDC issuer; default max age 15 minutes since 5.9.0, plus optional per-user embedded expiry callback.

facts.label: Refresh-token lifecycle
facts.value: Optional REFRESH_TOKEN defaults False; tracker model required. Defaults: max age 90 days, max idle 7 days, rotating token generation and reuse-detection family revocation.

facts.label: Logout/revocation scope
facts.value: Default logout method POST; LOGOUT_CSRF=False. Supplied/cookie refresh token can revoke its tracker and clear cookie; already issued auth tokens are not universally revoked just by logout.

facts.label: Password change and identity domains
facts.value: By default sessions/auth tokens use fs_uniquifier; password changes rotate it. Optional fs_token_uniquifier separates token/refresh identity from session/password-change identity.

facts.label: Reauthentication freshness
facts.value: Default freshness 24 hours, grace 1 hour; authentication timestamp can come from session or auth token. Verify endpoints support configured password/code/passkey/OAuth proof.

facts.label: OIDC role
facts.value: plugin/custom integration: Authlib supplies an OAuth/OIDC relying-party client; bundled Google provider uses discovery. Other trusted issuers require provider config/identity mapping.

facts.label: SAML enterprise federation
facts.value: custom_code/other package required; no bundled SAML SP/IdP or managed customer-connection integration in 5.9.2.

facts.label: Roles and permissions
facts.value: built_in global roles and string permissions, backed by Flask-Principal; roles_required/accepted and permissions_required/accepted protect app views.

facts.label: Customer workspaces/invitations
facts.value: custom_code required for tenant workspaces, member invitations, tenant-scoped roles and customer-admin flows.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: No SCIM 2.0 Users/Groups/provisioning/deprovisioning implementation or support contract found.

facts.label: Bundled screens
facts.value: built_in Jinja templates/forms for login, registration, verification, reset/change email/password/username, MFA/recovery and passkey setup/signin.

facts.label: Headless/SPA API
facts.value: Built-in JSON/form endpoints and OpenAPI document; SPA guide gives redirect/CSRF configuration for separately served frontends.

facts.label: Branding/custom domains
facts.value: Override security templates, forms, email templates, context and URL prefix/subdomain. App controls login domain; no domain fee or branding-removal license tier.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Flask-Babel integration and bundled catalogs: af_ZA, ar, ar_SA, ca_ES, da_DK, de_DE, es_ES, eu_ES, fr_FR, hu_HU, hy_AM, is_IS, it_IT, ja_JP, nl_NL, pl_PL, pt_BR, pt_PT, ru_RU, tr_TR, zh_Hans_CN.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No published Flask-Security WCAG conformance, VPAT or independent accessibility report found.

facts.label: Runtime/framework requirements
facts.value: 5.9.2 requires Python>=3.11, Flask>=3.1.1, Flask-Login>=0.6.3, Flask-Principal>=0.4.0, Flask-WTF>=1.1.2, libpass>=1.9.3 and WTForms>=3.2.1.

facts.label: Compatibility/maintenance change
facts.value: 5.9 drops Python 3.10 and Pony ORM support; 5.9.2 CI configuration includes Python 3.11 through 3.15 release/low-dependency jobs.

facts.label: Native/mobile/other clients
facts.value: JSON/HTTP endpoints can be called by app clients; no official iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop SDK or OS-version matrix found.

facts.label: Database and account models
facts.value: App supplies SQLAlchemy/Flask-SQLAlchemy(-Lite), MongoEngine or Peewee persistence and User/Role models; optional credential/refresh fields/models depend on enabled features.

facts.label: Secrets and factor dependencies
facts.value: Strong Flask SECRET_KEY; PASSWORD_SALT for double-hash schemes; TOTP key dictionary/issuer for codes; optional mfa extra adds cryptography, QR, phone parsing and webauthn.

facts.label: Mail, hashing and social prerequisites
facts.value: common extra adds Argon2/bcrypt, Flask-Mail and nh3; social login additionally needs Authlib/provider credentials. babel and fsqla extras are separate groups.

facts.label: Production operation
facts.value: Deploy the containing Flask app with production server/hosting; configure TLS, trusted proxy/host handling, cookies, CSRF and selected external delivery.

facts.label: Backup/upgrade/schema work
facts.value: Operator backs up user/role/credential/refresh records and keys, restores application data and performs migrations. Packaged models are versioned; refresh support adds new tracker relationships.

facts.label: Sizing/capacity
facts.value: No official universal hardware size, auth throughput/concurrency guarantee or production capacity table found.

facts.label: Custom logic/forms/payloads
facts.value: Override forms/validators, template context, mail/password/phone/WebAuthn utilities, auth/error handlers and User.get_security_payload/augment_auth_token.

facts.label: Hooks and webhooks
facts.value: Signals for account creation/confirmation/authentication/failure, password changes, factor/passkey changes and refresh tracker creation/revocation.

facts.label: Datastore administration
facts.value: Python UserDatastore API creates/finds/deletes/activates/deactivates users, manages roles/permissions and resets access.

facts.label: CLI and deactivation
facts.value: CLI supports user creation/activation/deactivation/password change/reset_access and role/permission changes. Deactivation rejects future session/token-protected access through library loaders.

facts.label: Safe low-level creation/reset
facts.value: create_user expects already validated/normalized data and a hashed password; stores the supplied password directly. reset_user_access clears factors/passkeys/codes and revokes refresh trackers without changing password.

facts.label: Social matching/linking
facts.value: Bundled OAuth glue looks up an existing local user by configured identity field; no dedicated provider-subject link/unlink inventory or automatic social signup.

facts.label: Other credentials and guest upgrade
facts.value: Registered users can configure passkeys and unified/MFA methods; saved guest accounts and guest-data transfer/upgrade are custom application work.

facts.label: Passwords and breach checks
facts.value: Built-in normalization/length validation; default minimum 8, complexity checker unset, breached-password check off. Optional zxcvbn and k-anonymity Pwned Passwords checks.

facts.label: CSRF, enumeration and redirect controls
facts.value: Flask-WTF form CSRF support and configurable JSON/mechanism handling; generic anti-enumeration responses default False. Redirect validation and subdomain allowlist controls exist.

facts.label: Failed attempts/lockout hooks
facts.value: track_failed_authn sends failure signal by default; is_locked returns False unless overridden. Application supplies counters/rate controls/lockout policy.

facts.label: OTP replay/bot controls
facts.value: Totp supports last-counter storage hooks, but default get returns None and setter does nothing. CAPTCHA, bot/rate and SMS budget controls require app/provider integration.

facts.label: Numeric rate/burst limits
facts.value: No built-in vendor numeric login/management requests-per-window quota or guaranteed burst capacity in the inspected release.

facts.label: Events/login tracking
facts.value: Optional TRACKABLE stores last/current login dates/IPs and count. Signals include failures, account/credential changes and refresh tracker creation/revocation.

facts.label: Audit retention/export
facts.value: No bundled durable full audit-log stream/retention period; app can persist/export received signals and its database tracking fields.

facts.label: Export profiles, IDs and hashes
facts.value: Operator-controlled database/ORM records include profiles, IDs, roles, active/confirmed state, encoded passwords and identity uniquifiers; export uses the chosen datastore/tooling.

facts.label: Export factors/links/session data
facts.value: WebAuthn model holds credential IDs/public keys/counters/backup metadata; user holds encrypted TOTP secrets/recovery data; refresh trackers store token-family state.

facts.label: Import existing account data
facts.value: custom_code/ORM tooling: create compatible user/role/credential records and IDs; create_user can take an existing compatible encoded password without rehashing it.

facts.label: Hash compatibility and rehash
facts.value: Configured libpass CryptContext identifies/checks allowed schemes and verify_and_update_password can rehash after successful login when policy changes.

facts.label: Migration limits
facts.value: No complete provider-by-provider import matrix, managed lazy migration or automatic passkey-domain migration contract found.

facts.label: User deletion/cascades
facts.value: Python delete_user delegates to datastore deletion; caller must commit and ensure related credential/refresh/application data is removed according to its model relationships.

facts.label: Stored refresh cleanup/retention
facts.value: New refresh tracker creation can clean expired/revoked entries; defaults clean expired=True, revoked=False. Operator controls broader cleanup/log/backup retention.

facts.label: Vendor account closure
facts.value: Not applicable to hosted Flask-Security accounts/projects; app operator owns closure/deletion and retention policy.

facts.label: Data location/residency
facts.value: Self-chosen app/database infrastructure; browser session/cookies and configured mail/SMS/IdP processing also carry auth-related data.

facts.label: DPA/subprocessors
facts.value: Not applicable to Flask-Security as a hosted identity processor; no embedded-code DPA/subprocessor roster.

facts.label: Assurance evidence
facts.value: README states OWASP-guided goals; no public project-specific independent security audit, SOC 2/ISO report or dated control assessment found.

facts.label: Current name, owner and package aliases
facts.value: Flask-Security; also distributed as Flask-Security-Too; Python import flask_security. Pallets Community Ecosystem repository; maintained by an individual; originally authored by another individual.

facts.label: Naming/ownership transition
facts.value: As of July 30, 2024, Flask-Security-Too moved into Pallets-Eco and replaced the archived original, now flask-security-3.0. August 1, 2024 changelog announces dual PyPI publication.

facts.label: Current lifecycle
facts.value: Current repository not archived/disabled; latest published release 5.9.2, October 21, 2026; both distribution names publish 5.9.2.

facts.label: Feature lifecycle notices
facts.value: WebAuthn/passkey feature remains labelled Beta in 5.9.2 feature docs. Old standalone PASSWORDLESS flow is being replaced by generalized unified signin; still implemented.

facts.label: Main license/commercial use
facts.value: MIT; use, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale permitted with notice preservation. Flask-Security software license fee 0.

facts.label: Framework/security dependency licenses
facts.value: Flask: BSD-3-Clause; Flask-Login and Flask-Principal: MIT; Flask-WTF and WTForms: BSD-style licenses; libpass: BSD license with incorporated-code notices.

facts.label: Optional integration licenses
facts.value: Authlib 1.9.4 and WebAuthn 3.0.1: BSD-3-Clause; argon2-cffi 25.1.0: MIT. Flask-Mail/Flask-SQLAlchemy publisher metadata identifies BSD licensing.

facts.label: Status and availability contract
facts.value: Not applicable; library maintainers do not operate the deployed auth service or offer a hosted uptime SLA.

facts.label: Release/security update evidence
facts.value: 5.9.2 released October 21, 2026; fixes passkey name regressions and adds Python 3.15 CI. 5.9.1 fixes GHSA-ccgp-pv8r-95wm; 5.8.1/5.8.2 address earlier redirect/OAuth/WebAuthn issues.

facts.label: WebAuthn advisory range discrepancy
facts.value: GHSA-f66q-9rf6-8795 metadata says affected >=5.0.0 through 5.8.1; its body instead specifies >=5.8.0 through 5.8.1. Patched list names 5.8.2/5.9.

facts.label: Security reporting/support policy
facts.value: Project security page directs private GitHub advisory reports or security@palletsprojects.com. Current feature release gets fixes; older-version fixes may be considered, not guaranteed; no fixed timeline.

facts.label: Community support
facts.value: Official GitHub issues/discussions and contribution guide; README invites maintenance help through Pallets Discord.

facts.label: Paid support/response terms
facts.value: No published Flask-Security-specific commercial support price, staffed hours or guaranteed production response time found.

apps.name: Frontegg
apps.line: Hosted account login and customer management for business apps.

free.text: Free PAYG allowance includes 7,500 MAU

cells.freeUsers: 7,500 MAU, 5 enterprise connections, unlimited orgs
cells.sso: 5 connections included; $125 each beyond 5
