apps.news: No qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, product retirement, data breach, or regulatory action found.

facts.label: Published billing meters
facts.value: Pricing labels monthly active users, monthly enterprise connections (SSO/SCIM), and monthly M2M tokens.

facts.label: Counting definition gaps
facts.value: Precise MAU activity/identity deduplication, billing-month timezone, cross-app/environment pooling, connection activity definition and M2M token counting rules were not located.

facts.label: PAYG free production offer
facts.value: $0/month starting allowance: 7,500 MAUs, five enterprise connections (SSO/SCIM), unlimited customer organizations and a custom domain.

facts.label: Minimum public paid rate
facts.value: PAYG has no separate base fee in the public calculator: $0.10 per MAU beyond 7,500, plus connection/M2M usage. Enterprise is custom-priced.

facts.label: Billing period and contract
facts.value: Pricing displays /month; payment frequency and amount follow online subscription/Order. Auto-renewal normally requires 30 days' non-renewal notice unless plan/Order says otherwise.

facts.label: PAYG calculator formula
facts.value: Monthly displayed amount = $0.10 × max(MAU − 7,500, 0) + $125 × max(enterprise connections − 5, 0) + $1 × M2M token input.

facts.label: Calculator rounding and sales threshold
facts.value: Calculator rounds the displayed dollar total with Math.round; when the unrounded subtotal exceeds $2,500, it hides the number and shows Talk to Us.

facts.label: Business comparison result
facts.value: Our calculation with basic included roles: A $0/month; B $875/month for auth usage, before any separately needed delivery.

facts.label: Customer organization allowance
facts.value: PAYG and Enterprise advertise unlimited organizations/tenants; invitations and user groups are included in both.

facts.label: Members, invitations and limits
facts.value: Membership and role-bearing email/link invitations are documented; a numeric universal members-per-tenant ceiling was not located.

facts.label: Role and hierarchy plan gates
facts.value: PAYG includes basic Admin/Viewer roles. Enterprise adds custom roles, permissions, tenant-level roles, ReBAC, entitlements and account hierarchies.

facts.label: SSO/SCIM public connection price
facts.value: PAYG includes five enterprise connections, with calculator charging $125 for each beyond five per monthly input. Enterprise has negotiated pricing.

facts.label: Dashboard seats and applications
facts.value: Both plans advertise unlimited builder seats. Multiple applications, external user pools and federation-broker controls are Enterprise comparison features.

facts.label: Environment cap inconsistency
facts.value: PAYG pricing: one environment; Enterprise pricing: unlimited. Environment guide: up to four distinct environments (Development, Staging, QA, Production), created in order.

facts.label: Project/application caps
facts.value: A full numeric limit/overage schedule for separate workspaces/projects and Enterprise application counts was not located.

facts.label: Default email delivery
facts.value: Frontegg-domain emails use SendGrid and are limited to 100 emails/day; fixed hello@frontegg.com sender/subjects and no template customization on that provider.

facts.label: Own email provider and example cost
facts.value: One configured external provider at a time: Amazon SES, SendGrid or Mailgun. SES publishes $0.10/1,000 outbound emails plus $0.12/GB attachment data.

facts.label: SMS/voice/WhatsApp
facts.value: Twilio or Twilio Verify connector routes login/MFA messages through the builder's account; supported channels include SMS, voice and WhatsApp.

facts.label: Destination rate example
facts.value: Twilio US outbound SMS base rate is $0.0083/segment for long codes, toll-free and short codes, plus applicable carrier/number/registration fees.

facts.label: Usage overage and service continuity
facts.value: Terms permit communicated excess charges and condition exceeding limits on payment; no public fixed grace days, monetary cap or universal automatic-upgrade/login-stop rule was located.

facts.label: Additional meters and premium features
facts.value: M2M calculator input costs $1/unit per month with no free numeric offset in the script; Enterprise add-ons/private deployments/log streaming/advanced security are custom-priced.

facts.label: Other fee precision
facts.value: Full numerical Enterprise add-on schedule, endpoint-request overage tariff and audit/private-deployment setup fees were not located.

facts.label: Individual eligibility and restrictions
facts.value: Terms allow an individual customer, at least 18 or the jurisdiction's minimum consent age, for business activity; export-control and US embargo/denied-person restrictions apply.

facts.label: Self-service route
facts.value: PAYG offers Start for free and quickstart documents portal-based setup, hosted login and SDK integration.

facts.label: Card, trial and production precision
facts.value: A fixed trial duration, universal card requirement, compulsory business-email domain and exact gate to marking a PAYG environment Production were not established.

facts.label: Product and deployment types
facts.value: Proprietary customer identity SaaS with accounts, login, sessions, organizations, authorization and customer self-service; Enterprise also offers private deployments.

facts.label: Managed operating responsibility
facts.value: Frontegg operates the hosted identity platform; builder operates the app, authorization checks and optional external integrations.

facts.label: Private deployment responsibility
facts.value: Private deployments are offered, but the precise split of patching, database operation, restores and support between vendor and customer was not established publicly.

facts.label: Password and email passwordless
facts.value: Native password login with email/username, email magic codes and single-use email magic links; included authentication families on PAYG and Enterprise.

facts.label: Phone-first login
facts.value: Native SMS one-time-code login supports phone-only signup/login; a phone can be verified during signup or first SMS login.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: A native anonymous identity session, wallet authentication and automatic anonymous-to-registered data merge were not established.

facts.label: Built-in social providers
facts.value: Official provider navigation names Apple, Facebook, GitHub, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft and Slack; the pricing matrix includes social login on both plans.

facts.label: Social configuration and custom providers
facts.value: Custom OAuth social providers can be created/updated/deleted by API. Apple guide says up to four social options on the login page.

facts.label: Passkey login and management
facts.value: Native WebAuthn/FIDO passkey login is included on both plans; user enrollment and deletion are exposed through Privacy & Security self-service.

facts.label: Passkey and MFA/SSO restrictions
facts.value: Passkey setup requires SMS or authenticator-app MFA options; users forced into MFA must enroll one of those before passkeys. Enterprise SSO users cannot enroll passkeys.

facts.label: MFA factors and recovery
facts.value: Authenticator apps (TOTP), SMS, email codes, built-in authenticators and security keys (WebAuthn); recovery code at enrollment, plus admin unenrollment.

facts.label: MFA policy gates
facts.value: Global policies: optional, force, or force except enterprise SSO. Per-tenant MFA policy and step-up/advanced identity protection are Enterprise features in pricing.

facts.label: Verification and recovery
facts.value: Email verification can be enabled; username-only signup skips activation. Password reset via email link or SMS recovery code; email-change verification templates are documented.

facts.label: End-user deletion precision
facts.value: A dedicated self-delete flow/permission with defined deletion scope was not established in personal UI and user-management pages.

facts.label: Session defaults and controls
facts.value: Default idle timeout 24 hours; no forced absolute re-login; unlimited concurrent sessions. Configurable idle/absolute/max-session controls; user/admin can revoke one or all sessions.

facts.label: JWT refresh and revocation scope
facts.value: Uses JWT plus refresh token/cookie; default refresh rotation has about 30-second reuse grace where enabled. Browser keepSessionAlive refreshes at 80% of JWT lifetime.

facts.label: Incoming enterprise protocols
facts.value: Frontegg acts as SAML 2.0 service provider and OIDC relying party for customer business IdPs; customer admins can configure connections in self-service.

facts.label: Outgoing identity-provider role
facts.value: Hosted login supports Frontegg as SAML IdP or OIDC provider for third-party apps; documented OAuth authorization-code/PKCE flow returns ID/access/refresh tokens.

facts.label: Membership and identity isolation
facts.value: Accounts/tenants are customer workspaces; each user belongs to at least one. A user can share one ID across multiple accounts and switch active account.

facts.label: Customer administration by plan
facts.value: Both plans include invitations, user groups, user-management component and basic roles; Enterprise adds tenant-custom roles, hierarchies and per-tenant security policies.

facts.label: SCIM protocol and lifecycle
facts.value: SCIM 2.0 provisioning/deprovisioning for users and groups, profile updates and group membership; SCIM-provisioned users authenticate with enterprise SSO.

facts.label: SCIM setup and deletion scope
facts.value: Customer or vendor/API can create directory connections. Dashboard connection deletion defaults to deleting associated users/groups; documented API deletion does not automatically delete them.

facts.label: Login and account UI
facts.value: Hosted login is default; embedded SDK login is available. Self-service portal can be embedded or hosted at /oauth/portal, with profile/security, users, invitations and org controls.

facts.label: Theme and branding
facts.value: PAYG/Enterprise include customizable login and custom domain. Builder controls themes, logos, favicon, title, layout, colors and typography; SDK/API overrides support deeper changes.

facts.label: Domain limits and cutover
facts.value: Docs allow one custom domain per environment and up to two total; additional domains require contact. Configure two CNAMEs and verify DNS.

facts.label: Published translation list
facts.value: Auto-translation for login and self-service: en, es, zh, fr, de, pt-BR, ja, ko, ar, ru, it, nl, he, tr, hi, id, vi, pl, sv, nb, da, th, uk, ro, cs (25 locales).

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A public hosted/embedded login and admin portal WCAG conformance report or precise tested level/version was not located.

facts.label: Official frontend/backend integrations
facts.value: Official index lists React, Next.js, Angular, Vue, Vanilla JS; backend Node.js, Go, Python FastAPI/Flask, and Node/Go/Java entitlements clients; Terraform provider is also listed.

facts.label: React version and runtime scope
facts.value: @frontegg/react 7.20.1 declares react/react-dom >16.9.0 and react-router-dom >5.0.0; no engines field in the checked package metadata.

facts.label: Official mobile clients
facts.value: iOS Swift, Android Kotlin, React Native, Flutter and Ionic Capacitor SDKs are documented.

facts.label: Mobile feature restrictions
facts.value: Mobile matrix excludes self-service portal, entitlements, impersonation, idle-session timeout and social login using Frontegg development credentials.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: App integration, configured allowed origins/redirects and backend validation of identity tokens; a customer-operated identity database is not specified as mandatory for normal hosted use.

facts.label: External service choices
facts.value: External email provider, Twilio/Verify and user pools are optional integrations. External pools can retain the existing auth source or perform JIT migration.

facts.label: Private deployment guidance
facts.value: Enterprise advertises private deployments and terms cover on-premises/private cloud, but public installer, database/version matrix, resource minimums and backup/restore/upgrade runbook were not located.

facts.label: Webhooks and delivery behavior
facts.value: Event webhooks support signed x-webhook-secret verification. Failed individual events are not re-sent; after five consecutive failures the hook is disabled.

facts.label: Prehooks and custom logic
facts.value: Synchronous prehooks can allow/block/challenge/lock, alter claims and route flows; default timeout five seconds, configurable fail-open or fail-close behavior.

facts.label: Administrative actions
facts.value: Vendor dashboard/API can create/invite/search users, edit metadata, lock/unlock, reset passwords/MFA, manage roles/memberships and delete users.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: Included in current PAYG/Enterprise comparison; requires Owner or Impersonator with an appropriate admin/backoffice role, and a reason.

facts.label: Identity linking
facts.value: Docs automatically merge password/social identities by matching email; unverified-email users returning from social to password may be forced to reset password.

facts.label: Guest access and upgrade scope
facts.value: Identified invited Guests have temporary access; account UI/API can change them to permanent and later restore an access period.

facts.label: Unlink and anonymous-merge gaps
facts.value: A universal unlink flow and anonymous-to-registered identity/data merge were not located in the opened user, social, identifier and personal portal docs.

facts.label: Basic versus advanced defenses
facts.value: Both plans include bot detection; Enterprise comparison includes brute-force protection, new-device/suspicious-IP/impossible-travel detection, stale users, step-up and tenant security center.

facts.label: Password and SMS protection scope
facts.value: Password complexity/history/expiry can be configured; rules/prehook can control SMS sends. No complete default SMS fraud allowance or universal spend-protection cap was located.

facts.label: Published auth throughput
facts.value: Docs Launch/Scale/Enterprise: general auth 100/1,000/1,000 requests per minute per IP; password login 10/min/VendorId, 30/min/IP, 100/min/IP; OAuth token 100/min/VendorId, 100/min/IP, 500/min/IP.

facts.label: Management quotas and current-plan mapping
facts.value: User-list V3: Launch 60/min, Scale 100/min, Enterprise 200/min, each per VendorId. PAYG-to-Launch/Scale mapping is not published.

facts.label: Diagnostic and prehook retention
facts.value: Monitoring logs default seven days; prehook execution logs 90 days. Monitoring log streaming only in Production; longer retention requires sales.

facts.label: Audit trail and export
facts.value: Audit docs default 30-day retention configurable per environment; account/environment views, permission fe.secure.read.audits and CSV download/export API are documented.

facts.label: Internal security logs
facts.value: DPA Annex II system-monitoring controls retain key service security logs at least 13 months.

facts.label: Profile retrieval and contract exit
facts.value: User listing API returns paginated JSON for a tenant or environment (50 default, 200 maximum per page); terms allow 30 days after termination to retrieve Content before deletion.

facts.label: Credential portability
facts.value: Password-hash, TOTP-secret, recovery-code and passkey private/credential export procedure was not established publicly.

facts.label: Bulk migration formats
facts.value: API examples support bcrypt, scrypt, firebase-scrypt and PBKDF2 (including Keycloak); 1,000 users per bulk API batch. CSV supports up to 10 files, each 1 MB.

facts.label: IDs, MFA and progressive migration
facts.value: Frontegg generates its user ID; vendorMetadata can preserve an old internal ID. API/CSV accept authenticatorAppMfaSecret. External user pools support irreversible JIT migration or ongoing source sync.

facts.label: SMS migration nuance
facts.value: Migration docs assign a phone as auth or MFA and say not simultaneously both; the current SMS guide allows SMS login plus SMS MFA if another MFA factor is also enabled.

facts.label: Identity deletion versus membership
facts.value: Dashboard supports single/global bulk user deletion; account-scoped removal leaves identity in the environment. App copies and downstream provider data require separate cleanup.

facts.label: Contract closure and data retention
facts.value: Customer can delete its Account; cancellation/renewal follows subscription/Order with default 30-day notice. Terms allow 30 days after termination for Content retrieval; DPA requires return/deletion subject to law.

facts.label: Final erasure gap
facts.value: A complete backup-purge deadline, deletion API completion SLA and public precise console steps for project/subscription closure were not located.

facts.label: Managed regions, inconsistent scope
facts.value: Subprocessor prose says two hosting regions (EU default, US choice); its table lists EU/US/CA/AU/UK. Status page lists EU, US, AU, CA, UK; public API index lists EU/US/CA/AU.

facts.label: Processing beyond primary region
facts.value: Subprocessor list places SMS/email and Anthropic inference in US, some analytics/IP processing in EU and support/affiliates in US/EU/Israel.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Public Customer Data Processing Addendum and authorized subprocessor list; list dated October 8, 2026. DPA covers processor/subprocessor roles and SCC/UK transfer terms.

facts.label: Vendor assurance claims
facts.value: Trust center claims SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; security page describes semiannual penetration tests, WAF/IDS, encryption at rest/in transit and vulnerability disclosure.

facts.label: Name, company and official scope
facts.value: Frontegg. Terms name Frontegg, Inc. or its applicable corporate affiliate; privacy policy names Frontegg Ltd. (registration 516093548).

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Public PAYG/free entry and Enterprise contact-sales offers are live; React v7.20.1 was released October 29, 2026.

facts.label: Platform commercial license
facts.value: Contractual, limited, revocable right to use for business purposes and offer the service only as a feature of the customer's own product.

facts.label: Client SDK license
facts.value: Frontegg React SDK is MIT; the checked @frontegg/react 7.20.1 package also declares MIT.

facts.label: Status evidence
facts.value: Public status lists authentication APIs, management APIs and management portal across five named regions, with incident history.

facts.label: SLA scope and missing credits
facts.value: Enterprise advertises 99.99% uptime SLA; PAYG does not include an uptime/support SLA in the comparison. Full public credit/claim/exclusion schedule was not located.

facts.label: Release and maintenance evidence
facts.value: React v7.20.1 released October 29, 2026; npm latest 7.20.1 published 2026-10-29T13:55:16.339Z. SDK versions released within two years are supported; older are not tested/supported.

facts.label: Support routes and gates
facts.value: PAYG and Enterprise: community and email. Enterprise adds dedicated Slack, support SLA, prioritized integrations and premium support; docs link Help Center/contact support.

facts.label: Response-time precision
facts.value: Numeric standard response/resolution times, universal support coverage hours and public paid-support add-on rates were not located.

The Community software licence costs $0. Infrastructure, email delivery and operations cost extra.

facts.label: Billing unit and definition
facts.value: Paid feature license: monthly active user (MAU), a distinct user account active in a calendar month, counted once despite repeated use. Triggers include creation, login/SSO, application registration, login ping, refresh-token exchange and SCIM provisioning; Import API and profile-only updates do not count.

facts.label: Billing unit and definition
facts.value: License pricing follows production MAU rather than instance count; a licensed plan includes production and non-production license IDs. Non-production logins are excluded. Cloud hosting is separately charged for running deployments.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Self-hosted Community: ongoing free production software with unlimited users and core features. Licensed Community is also free but needs portal registration/activation for WebAuthn and Universal Applications.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Ongoing free managed Cloud production allowance: none established by the reviewed public offer; Cloud deployments are billed, while the free offer is self-hosted Community.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Public entry figures: hosted Community calculator value US$37; Starter headline US$162/month with 'Billed annually', including Basic hosting. The same page's summary says 'Billed Monthly or Annually'; an exact lowest month-to-month production bill is not established.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Self-service monthly and annual billing are offered. Contracted Orders have their own term; agreement default renewal is successive one-year periods, 30-day non-renewal notice and a 5% price increase on renewal. Taxes excluded; standard fees non-refundable unless the Order says otherwise.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Standalone current Starter or Essentials self-hosted license price, separated from bundled hosting: not published in the reviewed current rate tables.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Main-page calculator Starter figures for MAU steps 1,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 25,000 / 50,000 / 75,000 / 100,000: US$162 / 162 / 162 / 312 / 462 / 687 / 837 per displayed month. Higher steps return Contact Us.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Essentials/Enterprise main-page price presentation conflicts internally: static Essentials and Enterprise cards show US$2,970/month billed annually at the initial 1,000-MAU position; executable main-page table uses Essentials US$240 and Enterprise Contact Us at that position.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Official contract estimate calculator: Essentials / Hosted / Softcap at up to 1k / 10k / 50k / 100k MAU is US$240 / 1,500 / 3,250 / 4,750 monthly; maximum listed Essentials tier is 500k. Contract choices: 1, 2 or 3 years.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Same contract estimate calculator: Enterprise Hosted at 1k / 10k / 50k / 100k is US$1,500 / 3,500 / 6,500 / 9,500 monthly; Enterprise Self-Hosted US$1,500 / 3,500 / 5,500 / 8,500. Subject to a chosen 1–3-year contract.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Business baselines can be implemented with Community primitives: customer tenants or groups, registrations/roles, SAML SP login and developer-built invitation/member management. No ready-made organization invitation product is assumed.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Business A/B software-only result: US$0 Community license plus custom-code and operating costs; exact cheapest hosted monthly totals not established. Optional entity modeling, self-service account UI, Tenant Manager and SCIM introduce separate plan gates.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: Community tenant/group model: users, groups and tenants are core; no per-customer-tenant fee or members-per-group quota shown. Separate tenants have separate user accounts/settings; groups contain users, not nested groups.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: Entity-based shared organizations and grants require Starter+. Main price table lists 100 entities on Starter, 1,000 on Essentials and unlimited on Enterprise; no entity overage rate is given.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: Organization invitation quotas, per-member price and a native pending-invitation lifecycle are not published for the modeled organization feature.

facts.label: SSO and account-sync fees
facts.value: SAML/OIDC identity providers: unlimited connections in all published plans, with no separate per-connection price in the rate table. SAML IdP-initiated incoming login requires Starter+; ordinary SAML SP-initiated login is core.

facts.label: SSO and account-sync fees
facts.value: SCIM server and customer Tenant Manager are Enterprise features; no separate per-directory SCIM fee or mandatory setup charge found in current public pricing.

facts.label: Developer team and project caps
facts.value: Developer account portal users: unlimited, email required. Roles: Admin, Billing manager, Deployment manager, Plan manager and Security officer; separate from end-user accounts on each deployment.

facts.label: Developer team and project caps
facts.value: Cloud deployments: as many as desired, each billed while running. Core applications/tenants have no listed plan-count cap; current contract estimates include up to 1 development environment for Essentials Hosted, up to 3 for Enterprise Hosted.

facts.label: Email, SMS, and other extra costs
facts.value: Email: bring your own SMTP server/provider, configure per tenant and supply templates. FusionAuth includes no SMTP server and no published included production email-send allowance; provider bill is separate.

facts.label: Email, SMS, and other extra costs
facts.value: Phone/SMS/voice: Twilio or generic external messenger, credentials and message templates supplied by builder; voice delivery available in current messenger/MFA flows since 1.65.0. External channel/destination charges remain extra.

facts.label: What happens at the limit
facts.value: Month-to-month feature billing follows actual prior-month MAU; annual billing uses an estimated average with year-end settlement. The reviewed pages do not establish a universal hard login cap or customer-set spending ceiling.

facts.label: What happens at the limit
facts.value: Flex-enabled contracted plans only: 15% MAU buffer without overage fees. After three >15% excess months plus notices, vendor may adjust the tier from the next billing period; ≥50% single-month excess can trigger adjustment after notice and 30 days without a new Order.

facts.label: What happens at the limit
facts.value: License deactivation disables use and management of premium features while preserving saved configuration; e.g. SMS MFA prompts cease until reactivation.

facts.label: Other billable limits
facts.value: Contract-estimator add-ons: extra development hosting US$500/month; extra HA production hosting US$1,000/month (Enterprise only); extra DR zone US$1,000/month (Enterprise only); FGA/Permify US$1,000/month.

facts.label: Other billable limits
facts.value: Other Cloud limits: 1,000 indexed user/custom/registration fields; no direct host/database/search access, no deployment-management API or Kickstart execution. Advanced Threat Detection needs Large or X-Large hosting; OpenTelemetry output is unavailable on Cloud.

facts.label: Market and account eligibility
facts.value: Individuals and single legal entities are recognized customers; account creation asks for name, company, email and password. Production Cloud requires a payment method.

facts.label: Market and account eligibility
facts.value: Vendor says it cannot sell software/services to residents of countries under US sanctions; an exhaustive current country list is not supplied in the reviewed FAQ.

facts.label: Self-service and trial rules
facts.value: Self-service Community downloads need no portal account. Cloud accounts and credit-card deployment purchase are documented self-service; invoice-billed accounts must ask support/account staff to launch or alter deployments.

facts.label: Self-service and trial rules
facts.value: Current hosted trial duration, card exception, production permission and expiry handling: not established. A 2024 year-in-review describes a month-long no-card Express trial, but current pricing/deployment docs do not give matching trial terms.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Customer identity and access management server: accounts, authentication, authorization, sessions and user administration. Self-hosted software or dedicated managed FusionAuth Cloud; APIs and SDKs connect applications.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: FusionAuth Cloud: vendor runs isolated compute, database, search and network infrastructure, TLS and OS patches. Customer retains configuration, API-key/admin security and decisions about when to update FusionAuth.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Self-hosted: builder operates the application, database, optional search, networking, TLS, load balancing, backups, monitoring, scaling and updates.

facts.label: Basic login methods
facts.value: Password login: built in, Community+, using email or username; current identity model also accepts phoneNumber as a login identifier. Phone identifier is distinct from the older mobilePhone contact field.

facts.label: Basic login methods
facts.value: Email magic links and one-time codes: built in, core Community passwordless feature. Single-use, configurable lifetime; only the most recently requested code remains valid.

facts.label: Basic login methods
facts.value: Phone-code first-factor login: documented OTP workflow using a phone identity and configured SMS/generic Messenger. Other channels such as Slack/WhatsApp require a connected external delivery implementation.

facts.label: Basic login methods
facts.value: Anonymous/stub accounts: custom code over the User APIs, not supported by ready-made hosted login pages; conversion preserves profile data on the same user.

facts.label: Basic login methods
facts.value: Built-in wallet signature/SIWE login and any dedicated wallet SDK or minimum plan: not published in the reviewed login catalog.

facts.label: Social login providers
facts.value: Built-in named social providers: Apple, Google, Facebook, LinkedIn and Twitter/X; core Community integration options, requiring the upstream app credentials and configured redirect callback.

facts.label: Social login providers
facts.value: GitHub: generic OIDC-provider configuration with manual endpoints and claim mapping, not a dedicated provider type. Public-email linking can fail when GitHub supplies no public email; username/anonymous linking alternatives are documented.

facts.label: Social login providers
facts.value: Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD: documented generic OIDC enterprise login, using registered client/secret, tenant authority and openid scope.

facts.label: Social login providers
facts.value: Gaming providers Epic Games, Nintendo, Sony, Steam, Twitch and Xbox require a paid plan (Starter+ per plan guide).

facts.label: Passkey support
facts.value: Platform passkeys/WebAuthn: built in with free Licensed Community or paid license; hosted login pages and APIs support bootstrap first-factor authentication and device re-authentication. WebAuthn exists since 1.41.0; free Licensed Community gate since 1.52.0.

facts.label: Passkey support
facts.value: Cross-platform/removable authenticators: Enterprise plan. Credentials are scoped to their registration's Relying Party ID; a changed login domain must retain compatible RP scope or users need a new enrollment.

facts.label: Passkey support
facts.value: Fallback to the normal configured login flow is documented on hosted passkey re-authentication pages. Conditional-autofill UX and native iOS/Android credential-manager parity are not established by the reviewed setup and SDK pages.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: TOTP/authenticator-app MFA: built in, free Community. Tenant methods/policy are configurable; MFA may be required on the FusionAuth Admin UI on every plan.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: Email and phone MFA (SMS or voice): Starter+ with external SMTP/Messenger. Application-specific MFA policies and context-aware MFA lambda require Enterprise, except Admin UI enforcement remains free.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: One-time recovery codes and multiple MFA methods are supported. Since 1.68.0 recovery codes are hashed at rest and shown only at generation; support/API can regenerate rather than retrieve plaintext codes.

facts.label: Account verification and reset
facts.value: Email verification: core verification/link-or-code flow; automatic hosted login gating until verified requires Starter+. Community can inspect verification state in application code.

facts.label: Account verification and reset
facts.value: Phone verification: core identity-verification flow; hosted gating requires Starter+ and current phone identity support (since 1.59.0), configured Messenger and message template.

facts.label: Account verification and reset
facts.value: Forgot-password workflow: built-in UI/API; reset identifier defaults to 10 minutes, configurable per tenant. Sends email or current phone-identity SMS using the appropriate configured template; privileged API may supply its own delivery.

facts.label: Account verification and reset
facts.value: Profile/password changes are available through Starter+ self-service account management or developer-built API screens. User deletion can be implemented with the privileged Delete User API; a ready-made end-user self-delete screen is not established.

facts.label: Sessions and revocation
facts.value: Configurable JWTs and refresh tokens; documented defaults: JWT 3,600 seconds, refresh token 30 days, SSO idle timeout 3,600 seconds. Refresh expiry supports fixed, sliding, or sliding with a maximum lifetime; one-time-use rotation can be configured.

facts.label: Sessions and revocation
facts.value: Central sessions use refresh tokens and can be listed/revoked per session/user/application via Admin UI/API. App-managed sessions require app handling; local JWT validation alone does not instantly invalidate an already-issued token.

facts.label: Business login standards
facts.value: OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization server and SAML 2.0 IdP; can also broker upstream OIDC and SAML as a service provider. Core SAML supports HTTP Redirect and HTTP POST; IdP-initiated incoming SAML is Starter+.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: Tenant model: isolated users, applications, groups, API-key scope and settings per customer. The same email in two tenants represents separate accounts, potentially separate passwords and IdP links.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: Shared identity model: groups plus application registrations/roles, or Starter+ entities/grants for distinct permissions in multiple organizations. Entity/organization picker and member-management UI require application code.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: Enterprise Tenant Manager: customer-scoped user administration, read-only or admin role; create/edit/delete/lock/reset users. Since 1.65.0 it also offers OIDC/SAML setup and connection tests for Universal Applications.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: Enterprise SCIM 2.0 provisioning server: Users, EnterpriseUsers and Groups; supports upstream provisioning/deactivation through mapped active state and configurable request/response lambdas. Not a SCIM client.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: SCIM limits: no SCIM bulk operations; requires Elasticsearch/OpenSearch rather than database search. Vendor recommends one SCIM client per tenant to avoid collisions, though that is not a hard enforced count.

facts.label: Ready-made login and account screens
facts.value: Ready-made hosted-on-your-instance pages: login/logout, registration, verification, forgot/change password, MFA, OTP, passkeys and account-linking workflows; APIs allow entirely custom screens.

facts.label: Ready-made login and account screens
facts.value: Starter+ self-service account UI: edit profile/password, enroll/manage MFA and passkeys; application links and separate account logout need configuration.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Community+: simple visual editor and advanced FreeMarker/HTML/CSS/JavaScript themes at tenant level. Starter+ adds direct application-specific theme assignment; templates and messages can be edited.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Cloud custom domains on all plans: creation table says Basic 1, Business 5, HA 20, or unlimited for Enterprise HA. Enterprise HA unlimited-domain mode needs support activation and DNS validation.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Business multiple-domain availability is inconsistent: deployment creation table lists 5, while the custom-domain guide says adding multiple domains is only available on HA.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility evidence
facts.value: Hosted login pages can be localized; default vendor translation is English, with manually installed community bundles including Arabic, simplified Chinese, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish and Ukrainian.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility evidence
facts.value: Public accessibility conformance report, VPAT or tested WCAG version/level: not found in the reviewed official UI/security pages.

facts.label: Web frameworks and runtimes
facts.value: Official front-end SDKs: React, Angular and Vue. Official API clients: TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Java, .NET Core, PHP, Python and Ruby. SDKs manage common login/token flows; API clients are lower-level endpoint wrappers.

facts.label: Web frameworks and runtimes
facts.value: Official quickstarts include Express, .NET, Drupal, Go, Laravel, Next.js, Nuxt, PHP, Django, Flask, Remix, Rails, Rust/Actix, Spring Boot and WordPress; integrations connect to a separate FusionAuth server.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official Swift iOS SDK, Objective-C compatible, uses AppAuth-iOS for OAuth/OIDC and opens Safari for hosted login; token manager supports memory, Keychain or UserDefaults storage choices.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official Kotlin Android SDK, Java compatible, built on AppAuth-Android with token manager; memory storage is default, optional DataStore/custom storage for persistence.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Flutter and React Native: official quickstarts using external AppAuth/secure storage and Expo AuthSession/crypto/browser respectively. React Native example reports testing with 0.72.4 and Node 20.

facts.label: Database and service prerequisites
facts.value: Self-host database required: PostgreSQL 14+ per requirements, with PostgreSQL 15+ recommended by install guide; MySQL 8+ possible with separately installed JDBC connector. Vendor tests PostgreSQL; MySQL Group Replication is unsupported.

facts.label: Database and service prerequisites
facts.value: Search can use the database for simpler lookup; advanced search/SCIM need Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. Documented Elasticsearch range 7.6.1–7.17.x; OpenSearch 2.x expected with FusionAuth 1.42+. SMTP/Messenger is external for delivery.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: Self-host options include Docker, ZIP/DEB/RPM and Kubernetes. Current 1.69+ bundle uses Java 25; general application RAM guidance 512M, excluding database/search/OS. Operator should load-test rather than map MAU directly to that minimum.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: Self-host operator backs up the database, stages updates, applies schema migrations and plans rollback. Rolling and blue-green deployments are documented; schema-changing rollback needs the prior database backup and can lose later writes.

facts.label: Custom logic and events
facts.value: Custom JSON user/registration data, token/IdP/validation lambdas and custom workflows are supported. Lambdas run restricted GraalJS (ECMAScript 2021); cannot import arbitrary modules. HTTP calls from a lambda require Essentials+, contextual MFA lambda Enterprise.

facts.label: Custom logic and events
facts.value: Webhooks publish JSON via HTTP POST; event and receiver must both be enabled. Transaction policies can require receiver success and return HTTP 504 if required endpoints fail; use non-blocking policy for logging. Expanded security events are Enterprise.

facts.label: User administration and API
facts.value: Admin UI and APIs support create/search/update/delete users, lock/unlock, require/reset password, manage groups/registrations, remove MFA and revoke sessions. Scoped support roles separate view and limited edit powers.

facts.label: User administration and API
facts.value: Turnkey 'log in as user' impersonation workflow with consent/audit controls: not found in the reviewed user-support, user-management and session docs.

facts.label: Linking and upgrading accounts
facts.value: Account linking: automatic email/username matching, pending manual link requiring existing-account login, anonymous IdP link, or disabled automatic linking with explicit Link API. Since 1.65.0 change a provider's linking strategy only while disabled; links can be removed.

facts.label: Linking and upgrading accounts
facts.value: Guest-to-registered upgrade is a documented custom API pattern: retain the stub user ID/data, add verified contact identity and password; store protected device association and clean up abandoned stubs.

facts.label: Abuse protection
facts.value: Community account-lockout controls: configurable failed-attempt window, user action and duration; not automatically enabled just because failures are counted. Starter+ adds breached-password checks at creation/change and optionally login, with selectable response.

facts.label: Abuse protection
facts.value: Enterprise Advanced Threat Detection: configurable per-user/identity action throttles, CAPTCHA (reCAPTCHA v2/v3 or hCaptcha), IP restrictions and notifications. Delivery throttles cover OTP, verification and MFA code sending.

facts.label: Abuse protection
facts.value: Cloud infrastructure WAF/CAPTCHA and 429 protection apply separately from the product's Enterprise threat feature. Static dedicated production IP allowlisting may be requested; shared CDN/laptop IPs do not qualify.

facts.label: Abuse protection
facts.value: Essentials threat-detection entitlement is inconsistent across main-page summary copy and the explicit plan matrix/docs: summary names advanced threat detection; matrix and feature docs require Enterprise.

facts.label: API and login rate limits
facts.value: Cloud numeric login/management request-per-second or requests-per-window allowance: not published in the reviewed Cloud security/limits/sizing pages; traffic patterns can trigger 429 and CAPTCHA. Slow requests or seek an eligible static-IP allowlist.

facts.label: API and login rate limits
facts.value: Enterprise product rate limits are customer-configurable per tenant and user/identity action; docs use five attempts per minute as default guidance. Self-host server throughput depends on CPU/hash cost and database/search capacity, not a published per-plan API-call meter.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Audit logs automatically record Admin UI, Tenant Manager and self-service configuration/user changes. Direct API-key writes are not auto-audited; caller must add Audit Log entries or proxy access logs. Export endpoint provides ZIP; monitoring guide identifies zipped CSV.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Audit/login-record retention is configurable in days or indefinite when deletion is disabled; event logs also have count-based retention. Webhook Event Log: disabled by default since 1.57.0; when enabled, default retention 30 days, configurable minimum one day.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Cloud system log files may be removed without notice; exact uniform hosted system/audit/login retention promise and extra-retention price not published in the reviewed pages.

facts.label: Export and ability to leave
facts.value: Self-host export: API/profile access plus read-only database extraction. Official offboarding guide includes IDs, profile fields, password hashes, salts, algorithm/factor metadata, registrations/roles, groups and IdP-link tables; adapt to the deployed schema version.

facts.label: Export and ability to leave
facts.value: Cloud exit export: support-provided secure database export, including password hashes, available on any hosting level/plan when leaving. Regular scheduled full exports for other purposes require Enterprise; no exit-export fee is specified.

facts.label: Import and migration in
facts.value: Bulk import: JSON User Import API with caller-supplied UUIDs, profiles, memberships, registrations/roles and supported password hashes; e.g. bcrypt and PBKDF2/SHA/MD5/phpass variants. Set active=true for usable accounts; recommended batch size depends on deployment, 100,000 is a production-capable example, not a hard cap.

facts.label: Import and migration in
facts.value: Lazy migration and external authentication: Starter+ Connectors for generic HTTP JSON, LDAP or another FusionAuth system. Migrate-on-login can move a user after successful legacy authentication; future source changes then stop propagating.

facts.label: Deletion and retention
facts.value: User deletion: API defaults to soft deletion (deactivate, retain data, prevent login); hardDelete=true permanently removes live user data. Admin UI hard deletion is irreversible except by restoring a database backup.

facts.label: Deletion and retention
facts.value: Delete Cloud deployment to stop its hosting charges; Business/HA backup retained at most 30 days after deletion, Basic has no backups. Account closure also requires changing the feature plan to Community and removing company data in Danger Zone.

facts.label: Deletion and retention
facts.value: Hosted routine restore window: Business/HA last 3 days point-in-time via support; backup taken for an update retained 30 days. Application upgrade rollback loses changes since the restored backup.

facts.label: Deletion and retention
facts.value: Exact retention schedule for vendor account/billing/support personal data and all vendor-held operational copies: not published as fixed day counts in the reviewed privacy pages.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Cloud deployment locations listed: South Africa; Australia, Singapore, South Korea; France, Germany, Ireland, Sweden, UK; Canada and USA. Region selected when creating a deployment; other AWS locations may require sales.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Hosted data is stored in the selected region with vendor-claimed encryption in transit/at rest; authorized engineering staff can access it for required support, with access/privileged commands logged. Optional Enterprise HA DR replicates to an explicitly selected second supported region.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Exact normal backup, support-ticket, billing and infrastructure-log residency beyond the selected deployment region: not established by the reviewed regional and privacy pages. Self-hosted locations are chosen and operated by the builder.

facts.label: Privacy and assurance evidence
facts.value: Vendor claims SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 compliance; reports/certificate details are request-gated. Trust Center advertises SOC 2, ISO and a 2025 penetration-test report for contracted Essentials/Enterprise customers.

facts.label: Privacy and assurance evidence
facts.value: Standard DPA is available on request; FAQ says it is executed only with Enterprise customers with a contract. Product Privacy Policy effective 2025-09-18 describes customer-controlled collection and a vendor breach-email notice within 72 hours.

facts.label: Privacy and assurance evidence
facts.value: Public Trust Center lists Amazon Web Services (AWS) as a subprocessor, data location Worldwide. A complete signed DPA/subprocessor change-notice schedule was not inspected.

facts.label: Name, aliases, owner, URLs
facts.value: FusionAuth; contracting owner Inversoft, LLC., doing business as FusionAuth, a Delaware limited liability company. FusionAuth acquired Permify in 2025; this was an acquisition by FusionAuth, not a sale or ownership change of FusionAuth. Official site https://fusionauth.io/.

facts.label: Name, aliases, owner, URLs
facts.value: Official technical documentation: https://fusionauth.io/docs/; server, hosted-service, API and client-library documentation are separate sections.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active, downloadable and offered for managed deployment. Latest listed server release 1.70.1, published 2026-11-04; 1.70.0 published 2026-10-28. FusionAuth acquired Permify on 2025-11-20 and announced plans to integrate its authorization technology; no FusionAuth shutdown or brand change was found.

facts.label: License and commercial-use rules
facts.value: Server/core: proprietary FusionAuth Customer License Agreement, version 2 dated 2026-05-04; free-tier use is governed by that agreement. Server source is closed; no right to modify, reverse-engineer or redistribute is granted by the free price.

facts.label: License and commercial-use rules
facts.value: Ordinary internal use and authentication for the builder's own web/mobile application can use Community free. Reselling, distributing, embedding the server in downloadable software, or providing private FusionAuth hosting to customers requires a reseller agreement.

facts.label: License and commercial-use rules
facts.value: Official TypeScript API client: Apache-2.0. Other SDKs/examples have their own repository licenses; this checked client license does not license the server.

facts.label: Service status and availability promise
facts.value: Public service status: https://status.fusionauth.io/ lists FusionAuth Cloud and Reactor incidents/maintenance; observed operational status is only a snapshot, not measured annual uptime.

facts.label: Service status and availability promise
facts.value: Enterprise HA hosted SLA: 99.99% availability per calendar month subject to applicable Order/Exhibit B. Basic/Business Cloud and self-hosting have no vendor uptime SLA. Credits use unavailable-minute ratio × applicable monthly fee; claim within 30 days after month-end, capped at three months' fees.

facts.label: Release and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Current server maintenance evidence: 1.70.1 on 2026-11-04 and security-containing 1.70.0 on 2026-10-28; hosted and integration support require a release from the last six months.

facts.label: Release and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Documented deprecation process normally marks features before major-version removal, with security/performance exceptions. Server/SDK integration changes are published in release notes; unsupported internals may change without that process.

facts.label: Support route
facts.value: Community/Starter integration help: documentation, forum and GitHub bugs/features; no guaranteed community response time. Cloud infrastructure-operation help is included but does not cover application integration.

facts.label: Support route
facts.value: Essentials: email/ticket support during business hours, advertised 24–48-hour response. Enterprise: 24/7 email/phone, ongoing engineering assistance; private Slack requires a contract.

facts.label: Support route
facts.value: Current agreement Enterprise support for Priority A: verify/report within 1 hour, status every 2 hours, correction within 24 hours if commercially feasible. Priority B: verify/report within 6 hours, correction within one week if commercially feasible.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: Goth does not meter MAU, returning users, stored users, projects or requests for a licence bill.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: No Goth MIT licence fee or licence-imposed monthly application-user cap.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable to the library: no required paid Goth production plan or annual contract.

facts.label: Software price rule
facts.value: Goth software licence subtotal = 0, independent of user count; included provider adapters have no separate Goth connection tariff.

facts.label: Business cost basis
facts.value: Required organizations/invitations/roles plus active SAML connections are unsupported as a complete packaged Goth baseline.

facts.label: Organization fees and allowances
facts.value: Not applicable to the MIT licence; no Goth customer-team subscription allowance or per-member fee.

facts.label: Included adapter connection fees
facts.value: Bundled OIDC/Okta/Azure adapters have no additional Goth licence/connection fee.

facts.label: Managed SAML/SCIM tariff
facts.value: No Goth managed SAML or SCIM offering and connection rate established in checked README, package API and provider tree.

facts.label: Developer seats/projects
facts.value: Not applicable: no Goth vendor dashboard seats, hosted application projects or environment quota.

facts.label: Login email/SMS delivery
facts.value: No Goth delivery bundle or message tariff for the selected social-login adapters.

facts.label: Over-limit billing behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no Goth hosted usage cap, automatic upgrade, billing grace period or spending limit.

facts.label: Other operating costs
facts.value: App hosting, account storage, chosen gothic session storage and applicable external provider services are separate from the licence subtotal.

facts.label: Core eligibility and countries
facts.value: Vendor production-account eligibility, seller-country list and company-domain signup rules are not applicable to MIT library use.

facts.label: Self-service/trial
facts.value: Not applicable: public Go package installation and configuration, not a Goth-hosted trial or payment-card requirement.

facts.label: Product type
facts.value: Embedded Go library with bundled external authentication providers implementing Provider and Session interfaces.

facts.label: Browser-flow helper
facts.value: Bundled gothic package wraps redirect, provider callback, state validation and temporary flow-session storage; direct Goth use is also possible.

facts.label: Operating responsibility
facts.value: Developer runs the Go web app, configures provider credentials/callbacks and chooses the session store; external identity providers operate their own login endpoints.

facts.label: Local passwords
facts.value: No bundled local user/password database, password hashing/verifier or registration system established.

facts.label: Email link and email code
facts.value: No core email magic-link or email-code issue/send/verify flow established.

facts.label: Phone, guest and wallet methods
facts.value: No packaged core phone-code, anonymous account lifecycle or wallet-signature verifier established.

facts.label: Google social login
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/google; OAuth2 authorization-code flow with app credentials, callback URL and optional scopes.

facts.label: GitHub social login
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/github; OAuth2 with configurable scopes and optional custom endpoints for GitHub Enterprise.

facts.label: Apple social login
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/apple; OAuth2 with client ID, client secret, redirect URL and optional email/name scopes.

facts.label: Microsoft login
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/microsoftonline; Microsoft v2 OAuth2 endpoints and Graph /me; defaults include openid, offline_access and user.read.

facts.label: Microsoft tenant selection
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/azureadv2; supports common, organizations, consumers or a specific tenant ID/domain.

facts.label: Facebook login
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/facebook; OAuth2 with app credentials/callback/scopes and configurable profile fields.

facts.label: Twitter/X integration
facts.value: built_in adapters include twitter and twitterv2; the latter uses OAuth request/access-token endpoints and the /2/users/me API.

facts.label: Deprecated provider distinction
facts.value: v1.82.0 README explicitly labels Google+ deprecated; Google is listed separately.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: No bundled WebAuthn credential registration/assertion or passkey recovery implementation established.

facts.label: MFA factors
facts.value: No core TOTP, SMS/email second-factor enrollment, local factor store or mandatory app MFA policy established.

facts.label: Lost-factor recovery
facts.value: No Goth recovery-code generation, factor-reset flow or organization MFA-enforcement workflow established.

facts.label: Address verification data
facts.value: GitHub private-email retrieval selects a primary, verified address or returns ErrNoVerifiedGitHubPrimaryEmail.

facts.label: Verification/reset/account change flows
facts.value: No core send/confirm-address, reset-password, change-address or user self-delete account workflow established.

facts.label: Flow session, not a full app account session
facts.value: goth.Session marshals provider authorization state between the beginning and end of an external authorization flow.

facts.label: gothic cookie configuration
facts.value: Default helper uses _gothic_session and Gorilla CookieStore; README documents Path=/, MaxAge=86400*30 seconds, HttpOnly=true, Secure=false.

facts.label: Callback cleanup and logout
facts.value: CompleteUserAuth defers Logout after retrieving provider session data; Logout clears the helper session and saves MaxAge=-1.

facts.label: Google provider token refresh
facts.value: Google adapter exposes RefreshTokenAvailable=true and RefreshToken(refreshToken) through its OAuth2 configuration.

facts.label: GitHub provider token refresh
facts.value: GitHub adapter returns RefreshTokenAvailable=false and its RefreshToken method returns a refresh-not-provided error.

facts.label: Microsoft adapter refresh boundary
facts.value: microsoftonline returns RefreshTokenAvailable=false, while exposing RefreshToken(refreshToken) for a supplied token.

facts.label: Device lists and global revocation
facts.value: No packaged Goth device-session inventory, per-device revocation or revoke-all local account endpoint established.

facts.label: OIDC relying-party role
facts.value: built_in adapter: providers/openidConnect consumes discovery or explicit provider endpoints and maps claims to goth.User.

facts.label: SAML role
facts.value: No bundled SAML service-provider or identity-provider implementation established in the checked module.

facts.label: Issuer/server role
facts.value: No Goth OAuth authorization server, token issuer or OIDC client-registration/admin server established.

facts.label: Customer organizations/invitations
facts.value: No bundled customer-workspace, organization membership, invitation or delegated customer-admin data model established.

facts.label: Roles and app isolation
facts.value: No core tenant-scoped RBAC enforcement, app membership-role management or cross-tenant isolation policy established.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: No bundled SCIM user/group provisioning, deactivation endpoint or directory synchronization implementation established.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Library/API integration with provider-owned authorization screens; no Goth-hosted account page or shipped account-profile component established.

facts.label: Example UI scope
facts.value: Example renders provider links and returned user data, with routes for starting login, callback and logout.

facts.label: Branding
facts.value: App controls its local templates/login links; no Goth-hosted branding-removal plan or theme editor.

facts.label: Custom domain and callbacks
facts.value: Adapters take an application callback URL, including an app-owned domain; no Goth domain allowance/connection charge in the library licence.

facts.label: Localization/accessibility
facts.value: No documented Goth UI translation catalogue, screen-language list or public accessibility conformance report established.

facts.label: Web integration
facts.value: Server-side Go interfaces/net/http handlers; bundled gothic provider lookup supports Gorilla mux, chi, request context and Go PathValue.

facts.label: Native mobile SDKs
facts.value: No dedicated Goth iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter or desktop SDK established in checked module docs/tree.

facts.label: PKCE integration hook
facts.value: Generic OIDC Session.Authorize passes code_verifier when supplied; provider exposes additional authorization URL parameters.

facts.label: Account database
facts.value: No core account-schema/database-driver prerequisite established; Goth User is returned data and the app supplies any account persistence.

facts.label: Flow storage and secret
facts.value: gothic default store reads SESSION_SECRET and creates a Gorilla CookieStore; application may replace Store.

facts.label: External libraries and providers
facts.value: v1.82.0 manifest includes oauth2 v0.27.0, gorilla/sessions v1.1.1 and JWT/OAuth helper dependencies; provider client credentials/callback setup are required.

facts.label: Application operation
facts.value: Developer builds/deploys a Go HTTP app with provider registrations, credentials, callback routing and configured storage.

facts.label: Capacity and recovery runbooks
facts.value: No Goth-specific production hardware sizing, supported-user capacity or account backup/restore runbook established.

facts.label: Custom providers
facts.value: custom_code: implement Provider and Session interfaces; register with UseProviders; configurable names allow multiple provider instances.

facts.label: Custom flow and claims handling
facts.value: App can use Goth directly or gothic convenience handlers and process returned User.RawData/profile/token fields.

facts.label: Account administration
facts.value: No core create/search/ban/delete-user or impersonation dashboard/API established.

facts.label: Identity mapping data
facts.value: User includes Provider and UserID, alongside Email/profile data and RawData.

facts.label: Link/unlink and guest conversion
facts.value: No core proof-based provider linking/unlinking or guest-to-registered account merge workflow established.

facts.label: OAuth state handling
facts.value: gothic accepts supplied state or generates 64 random bytes encoded as URL-safe Base64; callback validation compares original and returned state when original state is nonempty.

facts.label: Cookie integrity and encryption scope
facts.value: Default gothic store passes one secret key to Gorilla; Gorilla documents first key as authentication and optional second key as encryption.

facts.label: Other abuse controls
facts.value: No bundled general password throttle, CAPTCHA/bot detection, breached-password check or SMS fraud-control service established.

facts.label: API/login request rates
facts.value: No Goth endpoint requests/window, MAU burst quota, shared tenant rate card or standard retry policy established.

facts.label: Cookie payload limit
facts.value: Pinned Gorilla securecookie v1.1.1 defaults encoded cookie value MaxLength to 4096 bytes and exposes MaxLength configuration.

facts.label: Outcome handling
facts.value: CompleteUserAuth returns goth.User or error to app code; application handlers decide how to record outcomes.

facts.label: Audit retention/export
facts.value: No core audit-log retention days, managed event streaming or audit-export service established.

facts.label: Profile and identity export
facts.value: Application receives structured user/profile/provider identifiers and optional RawData; no local user export endpoint supplied by core.

facts.label: Password/passkey credential export
facts.value: Not applicable to core-owned credential storage: no Goth local password-hash or passkey registry is established.

facts.label: Token portability
facts.value: User can contain access token/secret, refresh token, expiry and ID token depending on adapter.

facts.label: Import and password migration
facts.value: No core bulk-user import, supported password-hash matrix, lazy password migration or import-fee schedule established.

facts.label: Helper-session deletion
facts.value: gothic.Logout clears values and sets MaxAge=-1 on the configured store's session.

facts.label: User retention and backups
facts.value: No Goth-defined retention duration for app users, tokens, audit logs/backups or vendor tenant closure policy established.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: Hosted Goth region selection is not applicable; developer chooses app/store location, while selected providers handle their own authentication data.

facts.label: Applicable legal terms
facts.value: MIT software licence applies; Goth-hosted application-user DPA/subprocessor contract is not applicable to this embedded module.

facts.label: Assurance evidence
facts.value: No Goth-scoped independent SOC 2/ISO report or public application-processing certification established.

facts.value: Project repository and generated Go API documentation; maintained as a public Go project, with individual maintainers rather than a verified hosted-service company.
