facts.label: Cloud Auth counted unit
facts.value: Monthly active user: unique user issued a Hanko session token, or whose token is validated through Hanko during the calendar month; repeated activity in that month does not count again.

facts.label: Allowance aggregation and Passkey API meter
facts.value: Exact standard-plan pooling across projects and a distinct Passkey API billable-unit definition were not established.

facts.label: Starter production allowance
facts.value: Free: 10,000 MAU and 2 projects; includes passkeys, passwords/email codes, social SSO, MFA, custom domain, admin dashboard and community support.

facts.label: Self-host free software
facts.value: Auth and Passkey API AGPL server software have no published per-user license charge under the open-source grant.

facts.label: Minimum paid Cloud plan
facts.value: Pro $29/month plus applicable usage and add-ons; Enterprise custom quote. Taxes are excluded.

facts.label: Billing and cancellation conditions
facts.value: Fixed fees billed at period start, usage after the period; subscriptions renew automatically and can be cancelled for the end of the current period. Refunds only under stated contractual/legal exceptions.

facts.label: Pro usage formula
facts.value: Monthly standard Auth charge = $29 + $0.01 × max(MAU − 10,000, 0), before add-ons and taxes.

facts.label: Enterprise and optional programs
facts.value: Enterprise has custom pricing/volume discounts. Startup program advertises one million free MAU for accepted organizations on Free or Pro, ending at stated revenue/funding thresholds.

facts.label: Business scenario completeness
facts.value: Known Auth/SAML subtotals can be calculated, but a complete native invitation flow and organization capacity limits were not established for the required baselines.

facts.label: Organization plan gate
facts.value: Customer organizations and organization-specific role assignments require Cloud Pro; managed through the Admin API. Cloud Console organization/role management is announced as coming soon.

facts.label: Organization limits, invitations and pricing detail
facts.value: No numeric customer-organization, member-per-organization, role or invitation allowance/overage schedule was found; native invitation acceptance/lifetime rules were not established.

facts.label: Business SAML fee
facts.value: Cloud Pro SAML SSO add-on: $49/month per connection, in addition to the $29 Pro base and extra MAUs. Enterprise custom terms.

facts.label: OIDC and SCIM pricing distinction
facts.value: Generic incoming OAuth/OIDC providers are documented under social SSO; no separately named business-OIDC or SCIM rate card was found.

facts.label: Project caps by Cloud plan
facts.value: Starter 2 projects; Pro 5 projects; Enterprise displays unlimited projects.

facts.label: Builder team access
facts.value: Starter has admin dashboard access; Pro adds team member invites; Enterprise adds admin dashboard SSO. Numeric builder-seat caps/prices were not established.

facts.label: Environment/domain count detail
facts.value: No separate development/production environment allowances or numeric custom-domain cap per project were established.

facts.label: Default email delivery
facts.value: Cloud has a default authentication email service. Public numerical included-send quota, standard per-email charge and delivery guarantee were not found.

facts.label: Custom SMTP / custom mail code
facts.value: Cloud Pro/Enterprise can use custom SMTP or disable default delivery and handle email.send webhooks. The builder supplies and pays for its provider/infrastructure.

facts.label: Self-host messaging
facts.value: Auth backend requires SMTP for passcodes such as verification and recovery; production instructions permit own SMTP or a managed service such as AWS SES.

facts.label: Starter MAU overage
facts.value: Pricing describes a soft cap: signup/login continue above 10k; if over the tier for more than one consecutive month, Hanko asks for an upgrade.

facts.label: Overage contract limits / paid spend controls
facts.value: Free does not convert to paid or charge automatically without agreement; repeated/material excess may cause restrictions or termination. A numeric paid spending-cap/alert configuration was not found.

facts.label: Paid feature boundaries
facts.value: Pro includes Admin API, webhooks and custom SMTP; Enterprise adds extended audit retention, priority support, 99.99% SLA, dashboard SSO, commercial-license option and Private Cloud.

facts.label: Other fees and exact complete bill
facts.value: A numeric tariff for extra projects, commercial licenses, Private Cloud, extended audit retention or separate Passkey API usage was not established.

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Cloud is business/professional only, including self-employed natural persons acting for commercial, craft or professional purposes. Consumer customers under German BGB §13 are excluded.

facts.label: Seller-country eligibility
facts.value: No complete supported/restricted builder-country or payment-country list was found.

facts.label: Free production entry
facts.value: Starter: ongoing Free plan, no credit card required, public self-service setup. No universal expiry date is printed for ordinary Starter.

facts.label: Trial and paid prerequisites
facts.value: A universal timed Pro trial length or compulsory company-email domain was not established; paid plans require valid payment information under the terms.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Auth: whole account system with registration, login, verification, recovery, sessions, profile management and incoming social/business SSO. Available as Cloud or a self-hosted Go server.

facts.label: Separate Passkey API scope
facts.value: Verification add-on: registers/stores/verifies WebAuthn credentials; supports first-factor passkeys, second-factor security keys and transaction authentication. Existing user management and session issuance remain in your application.

facts.label: Cloud operator
facts.value: Vendor operates hosted authentication infrastructure; customer integrates its app, configures identity providers/domains and controls app permissions and submitted data.

facts.label: Self-host operator
facts.value: Builder runs the Go server, SQL database, TLS/networking, email delivery, updates, backups and recovery. Passkey API self-hosting similarly requires its server and SQL store.

facts.label: Password and email-code login
facts.value: built_in passwords and passwordless email passcodes in Auth; Cloud Starter includes both. Username/email identification is configurable.

facts.label: Email links, phone, guests and wallets
facts.value: Native magic-link login, phone/SMS first factor, anonymous/guest accounts and wallet sign-in were not established.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: built_in tested connectors: Apple, Discord, Facebook, GitHub, Google, LinkedIn and Microsoft. Social SSO is included on Cloud Starter.

facts.label: Generic OAuth/OIDC connections
facts.value: Custom incoming OAuth2 or OIDC providers are supported with endpoint/discovery, client credentials, scopes and field mapping.

facts.label: Auth passkeys and autofill
facts.value: built_in first-factor passkeys; included on Cloud Starter and in the self-host server. Custom login example supports passkey autofill/conditional UI on compatible clients.

facts.label: Passkey domain and migration constraints
facts.value: Credentials are scoped to the configured WebAuthn relying-party ID and allowed origins. A parent-domain RP ID can support appropriate subdomains; an unrelated new domain is not automatically compatible.

facts.label: Separate Passkey API features
facts.value: Passkey API supports first-factor authentication, WebAuthn second factors/security keys, per-tenant credentials and transaction confirmation; caller retains accounts/sessions.

facts.label: Auth second factors and plan
facts.value: built_in authenticator-app TOTP and WebAuthn security keys; MFA is listed in Cloud Starter. Self-host config defaults enable both factor types.

facts.label: MFA enforcement and device trust
facts.value: Config supports optional or required enrollment; required MFA prevents deleting the last required credential. Device trust can be always, prompt or never, with default duration 720h.

facts.label: Lost-factor recovery and other factors
facts.value: Native backup/recovery codes, SMS/email as MFA factors and a complete lost-all-factors recovery procedure were not established for Auth.

facts.label: Email verification and password reset
facts.value: built_in email verification/passcodes and password recovery; sample config enables verification and recovery. Account profile supports adding/removing email addresses and password changes/deletion when enabled.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: Profile Flow API has account-deletion states/actions; self-service deletion is configurable. Admin API separately supports DELETE /users/{id}.

facts.label: Session model and storage
facts.value: Auth issues signed JWTs in X-Auth-Token and persists session IDs in SQL for active-session checks. SDK/Elements read the token and set a client-side hanko cookie; component options also support sessionStorage.

facts.label: Session lifetimes and device count
facts.value: Cloud default duration 12 hours, configurable from 1 minute to 1 month. Default concurrent-session limit 5; creation above the limit invalidates the oldest session.

facts.label: Idle timeout and revocation
facts.value: Optional idle timeout is separate from absolute token expiry. POST /sessions/validate updates activity/idle expiry; GET validation does not. Profile can list/revoke other sessions; logout ends the current session.

facts.label: Session claims and current organization roles
facts.value: Session validation returns fresh organization memberships/roles from the database; they are not stored as the authority in the session JWT. JWT templates can add other permitted claims.

facts.label: SAML login role and plan
facts.value: Auth acts as a SAML 2.0 service provider/broker for external business IdPs; SP-initiated and IdP-initiated login are documented. Cloud requires Pro plus $49/month per connection.

facts.label: OIDC direction and metadata constraints
facts.value: Incoming OAuth/OIDC federation is available via built-in/custom social connections. SAML Cloud setup accepts a metadata URL; direct XML-file upload is not currently supported in the guide.

facts.label: Organizations and membership model
facts.value: Native tenant-scoped customer organizations with membership CRUD; a user can belong to multiple organizations and hold different roles in each.

facts.label: Roles and permission enforcement
facts.value: Native tenant-scoped roles have immutable slugs and changeable display names. Session-based role-check endpoint checks the current user in a named organization.

facts.label: Customer administration and invitations
facts.value: Admin API can build a customer-management interface, but no ready-made customer admin portal or native invite/accept workflow was established.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No documented native SCIM v2 user/group provisioning, suspension mapping, offboarding semantics or price was found.

facts.label: Ready-made end-user screens
facts.value: Embedded framework-agnostic Web Components: hanko-auth for registration/login and hanko-profile for email/password, passkey, MFA and session management.

facts.label: Headless / fully hosted UI distinction
facts.value: Flow API and Frontend SDK support custom login/profile UI. A turnkey vendor-hosted end-user login-page product/URL with its own entitlement was not established.

facts.label: Styling and custom domains
facts.value: Elements support CSS variables/Shadow Parts for layout, color, typography and other appearance changes; custom domain is included on Starter and Pro.

facts.label: Brand removal and domain count policy
facts.value: No explicit hosted vendor-brand removal entitlement/fee or numeric custom-domain cap was found. Frontend code is MIT and custom UI is documented.

facts.label: Translations and customization
facts.value: Docs list Bengali, German, English, French, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese and Chinese; 2026 changelog additionally announces Dutch and Korean UI translations. Custom/partial translations and fallbacks are supported.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public WCAG conformance statement, VPAT/ACR or scoped independent accessibility report was established for Elements.

facts.label: Official web integration paths
facts.value: Quickstarts: Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit; Angular, JavaScript, React, Solid, Svelte and Vue; backend guides for Go, JavaScript, Java Spring, Python and Rust.

facts.label: Passkey API SDK runtime
facts.value: Official @teamhanko/passkeys-sdk is a fetch-based JavaScript/TypeScript client for browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun and frameworks such as Next.js, Astro and SvelteKit.

facts.label: Native mobile clients
facts.value: Official FAQ explicitly says no mobile SDKs are currently available; mobile clients can integrate directly with the Hanko Flow API.

facts.label: Mobile OAuth/passkey specifics
facts.value: October 28, 2025 changelog documents code_verifier/PKCE handling where a mobile OAuth state cookie is unavailable. Passkey API server config documents Android APK-key-hash origins.

facts.label: SQL, SMTP and cache prerequisites
facts.value: Self-host Auth supports PostgreSQL or MySQL, requires SMTP for email-based flows and can use Redis instead of per-process in-memory rate-limit state. Cloud customers do not provision the vendor SQL store.

facts.label: Source build toolchain discrepancy
facts.value: Backend README says Go v1.18+, but released backend/v3.1.0 go.mod declares Go 1.26.1.

facts.label: Password default discrepancy
facts.value: Backend README calls passwords disabled by default; current sample config enables them, and config_password.go declares default=true.

facts.label: Self-host deployment and upgrades
facts.value: Official backend instructions cover Docker/container or built executable, SQL migrations, SMTP, public/Admin API serving, CORS, WebAuthn and configuration. v2→v3 migration guide removes old endpoints in favor of Flow API.

facts.label: Backups, sizing and recovery guidance
facts.value: A complete production backup/restore runbook, tested recovery target, minimum RAM/CPU or published capacity guarantee was not established.

facts.label: Webhooks and plan gate
facts.value: Cloud Pro/Enterprise supports signed HTTP POST event webhooks; self-host source has configurable webhook support, disabled in the sample by default.

facts.label: Webhook acknowledgment and retries
facts.value: Guide requires a 2XX response within 30 seconds; longer responses are treated as failures. Retry schedule/count, durable replay window, ordering and delivery SLA were not established.

facts.label: User metadata
facts.value: Private metadata: Admin-only; public: Admin write/client read; unsafe: client read/write. Each category has a 3,000-character compact-JSON limit.

facts.label: Custom claims and login logic
facts.value: Up to 50 typed claim definitions per project; map SAML/custom OIDC attributes and include resolved values in Go text/template JWT claims. Flow API permits a custom client UI.

facts.label: User dashboard and administration API
facts.value: Cloud dashboard can create/import/manage users; paid Admin API lists/searches users and updates/deletes records, with password, credential, OTP and session management endpoints.

facts.label: Ban/suspension and support portal
facts.value: A native persistent ban/suspension flag and a ready-made customer-support/impersonation console workflow were not established.

facts.label: Admin-created session capability
facts.value: Admin API POST /sessions can create a session token for a named user, optionally recording user-agent/IP.

facts.label: Social linking and unlinking
facts.value: Incoming social login provisions a new account or links the provider to an existing account by email. Authenticated profile flow has connect_thirdparty_oauth_provider and disconnect_thirdparty_oauth_provider actions.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and arbitrary merge
facts.value: No native anonymous-to-registered upgrade or generic merge of two existing user IDs/data sets was established.

facts.label: Abuse protection implemented in server
facts.value: Configurable fixed-window throttling, user-ID/IP-based protection and in-memory/Redis storage are documented; email/passcode, OTP, password and token operations have limit configuration.

facts.label: Bot checks and leaked-password protection
facts.value: Native CAPTCHA/Turnstile, breached-password screening, adaptive bot scoring and SMS-pumping protection were not established for core Auth.

facts.label: Configurable operation limits
facts.value: Current config defaults to 3 operations per 1m interval for configured authentication categories, rather than a whole-project throughput allowance.

facts.label: Managed API quotas and burst behavior
facts.value: A complete Cloud per-plan endpoint quota/burst table, Admin API request ceiling, quota headers and documented reset/retry contract were not established.

facts.label: Audit events and access
facts.value: Auth server records API/security audit events; Admin API can query audit logs by time/type/user and pagination. Cloud Admin API is Pro/Enterprise.

facts.label: Audit retention by deployment/plan
facts.value: Self-host source defaults audit console output on, database persistence off and masking on. Enterprise advertises extended retention; exact Cloud Starter/Pro/Enterprise retention days were not found.

facts.label: Organization audit coverage limit
facts.value: Backend README explicitly says organization/role endpoints currently trigger neither audit logs nor webhooks.

facts.label: Self-service Cloud export
facts.value: Paid Admin API retrieves user profiles/IDs, emails, external identities and credential metadata. It does not include password hashes or TOTP secrets; dedicated Cloud export UI is described as upcoming.

facts.label: Complete support-assisted export
facts.value: DPA §11.2 provides complete machine-readable export by contacting Hanko, including accounts, external identities, authentication credentials and relevant project configuration; sensitive data can include password hashes, TOTP secrets and tokens.

facts.label: Passkey portability and self-host exit
facts.value: Import schema includes WebAuthn credential IDs/public keys, user handles and authenticator metadata. Self-host operator owns SQL state; passkey private keys remain on authenticators.

facts.label: Bulk account import
facts.value: Cloud Console imports a JSON array using the published schema; supplied user IDs must be UUIDs. Self-host CLI documents hanko user import.

facts.label: Passwords and MFA/passkey migration
facts.value: Schema supports bcrypt hashes, TOTP secrets using 30-second SHA1 parameters and WebAuthn credentials; October 2026 release adds bcrypt $2b$ import support.

facts.label: Firebase and import size
facts.value: Official Firebase conversion guide preserves Firebase Scrypt password verification using exported users and project hash parameters; Hanko user files support approximately 50 MB.

facts.label: App-user and active-data deletion
facts.value: App-user Admin API deletion is available. For a documented Cloud data-deletion request, DPA §11.3 requires deletion from active production within 30 days, unless law requires retention.

facts.label: Backups and account termination
facts.value: DPA: backups deleted/overwritten within 14 days after active-system deletion. After Cloud account termination, export-request window is up to 30 days; default active deletion no later than 30 days.

facts.label: Controller data and self-host retention
facts.value: Privacy policy retains builder/account, support and business records for their purpose/legal requirements, without one universal numeric period. Self-host deletion/log/backup retention is controlled by the operator.

facts.value: Instant app plus SDK; provider credentials/origins for OAuth; separate email provider optional for custom code delivery.

facts.label: Self-host database prerequisites
facts.value: PostgreSQL 17 with logical replication and pg_hint_plan in AWS guide; backend plus separate dashboard and object storage.

facts.label: Small deployment
facts.value: VPS guide: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, 2 vCPUs/4 GB RAM, Docker Compose, Postgres, MinIO and Caddy.

facts.label: Recovery and upgrades
facts.value: Nightly cloud backups downloadable for the last 7 days and restorable into self-hosting; no universal patch/support cadence established.

facts.label: Production-oriented deployment
facts.value: AWS guide recommends at least two backends, Aurora PostgreSQL and private S3; instances share configuration and discovery.

facts.label: Custom auth and fields
facts.value: Custom server flow can mint tokens; optional fields may be set at signup.

facts.label: Data webhooks
facts.value: Entity create/update/delete webhooks; HTTPS public receiver; up to 100 active hooks per app.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Explorer lists users; Admin APIs retrieve/delete by email, id or refresh token and mint a token, creating a missing user.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: Admin asUser by email applies that user's rules; token/guest-scoped requests can operate without an admin credential.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and conflicts
facts.value: New-email upgrade preserves guest ID/data. Existing-email conflict exposes linked guest users; app must transfer ownership or update rules.

facts.label: Social linking and unlinking
facts.value: Source matches OAuth identities/provider links and email within an app; no end-user arbitrary link/unlink API established.

facts.label: Authorization and signup protections
facts.value: CEL access rules and user creation rules can restrict signup/fields; ordinary data namespaces default to allow when rules are absent.

facts.label: Auth secrets
facts.value: Refresh-token model stores SHA-256 token hashes; no built-in CAPTCHA or compromised-password screening guarantee established.

facts.label: Developer-defined rate limits
facts.value: Rules support per-user/IP token buckets; per-entity evaluation; exhausted bucket returns 429 with retry information.

facts.label: Magic-code throttles and cloud quota scope
facts.value: Source fallback capacity is 20 per email address/app per hour; send and verify have separate token-bucket keys. Live flags can override this.

facts.label: Data-event delivery history
facts.value: Webhook delivery attempts retained about 60 days; SDK manager can inspect and redeliver events.

facts.label: Authentication audit logs
facts.value: No complete end-user login/factor/revocation/impersonation event catalog, audit-log retention or streaming price found.

facts.label: Profile and application export
facts.value: Downloadable ZIP backup includes $users.jsonl with IDs/emails/type, schema, rules, email template and application data/files.

facts.label: Credentials and external links
facts.value: Backup restore does not carry over OAuth client secrets; no portable password/passkey credential export established.

facts.label: Cloud to self-host migration
facts.value: Rehearse restore, pause writes, take final backup, restore and switch clients/app ID/API URLs; users may need to sign in again.

facts.label: Other-provider migration
facts.value: Admin token minting accepts email or UUID and creates missing users; external-provider bridges can keep authentication elsewhere.

facts.label: Deletion behavior
facts.value: Admin delete removes user record and cascade-configured data only; other related application data needs explicit cleanup.

facts.label: Privacy retention and rights
facts.value: Privacy keeps data for stated purposes/legal obligations; users can request access, erasure and portability via support.

facts.label: Cloud residency
facts.value: No current contractual cloud account-data region selection, log/backup country list or residency add-on found.

facts.label: Self-host data location
facts.value: Operator chooses hosting region and infrastructure; AWS guide requires selecting an account/profile and region.

facts.label: Privacy processors and DPA
facts.value: Privacy identifies Google Analytics 4 and PostHog for analytics; other processors' list can be requested.

facts.label: Assurance reports
facts.value: No public SOC 2 audit report, ISO certification scope or auth security trust-center evidence established.

facts.label: Name and official identity
facts.value: Instant; also listed as InstantDB. Auth docs at /docs/auth; official project instantdb/instant.

facts.label: Operator and team announcement
facts.value: Terms name Instant as the service counterparty; the announcement says the team is joining OpenAI. It does not state that Instant or its hosted service was sold or that legal ownership transferred.

facts.label: Cloud sunset and new availability
facts.value: New cloud signups are closed. Cloud apps are scheduled to shut down on 2027-08-31; backups remain available until 2028-08-31. Instant Status currently reports the service operational.

facts.label: Self-hosted availability
facts.value: Public self-hosting and cloud migration guides remain available; the source remains open source; no supported-maintenance end date established.

facts.label: Self-host and SDK license
facts.value: Repository root Apache-2.0: use, modify and distribute commercially under its notice, patent and other conditions.

facts.label: Hosted rights
facts.value: Hosted access governed by Instant Terms and Conditions; content remains the customer's, with a service-delivery license.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Official status page covers Instant API and Instant Reactivity.

facts.label: Hosted SLA
facts.value: No numeric contractual uptime percentage, credit schedule or paid incident response promise established.

facts.label: Maintenance evidence
facts.value: Repository is not archived; latest fetched main commit dated 2026-11-05 fixes self-hosted transaction memory buffering.

facts.label: Versions and security support
facts.value: No GitHub releases listed; no supported-version/EOL matrix established. Main core package version is a 0.0.0 placeholder.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Public site lists hello@instantdb.com; privacy gives support@instantdb.com; official repository/status link community Discord.

facts.label: Paid support and response time
facts.value: No current support plan price, staffed hours or technical support response-time guarantee found.

facts.label: Core billing meter
facts.value: not_applicable: upstream Apache core has no MAU, returning-user, stored-user, login, token or SSO-connection invoice meter.

facts.label: Red Hat commercial entitlement unit
facts.value: RHBK entitlement is included in qualifying Runtimes/Application Foundations/OpenShift subscriptions and usage counts toward their cores. It is not sold as a separate standalone product according to the entitlement article.

facts.label: Free production software scope
facts.value: Core production software is $0 license cost under Apache-2.0 without a time-limited trial or published per-user license cap.

facts.label: Minimum upstream paid commitment
facts.value: not_applicable: there is no minimum mandatory upstream subscription or annual production license payment for core.

facts.label: Downstream supported-build price
facts.value: A comparable public numeric minimum RHBK bundled entitlement price was not established from the support/entitlement pages read.

facts.label: Core usage price rules
facts.value: No upstream per-user, organization, per-connection, token or feature-unlock license tariff; core license component remains $0 as counts rise.

facts.label: Business scenario method
facts.value: Both fixed business baselines have native organization membership, invitations, group/role mappings and SAML connection capability. Software license component $0; SMTP/infrastructure/operator total remains unpriced.

facts.label: Organization fees and published technical caps
facts.value: No per-organization/member/invitation/role software license fee. A documented maximum organization count, members-per-org or plan-style invitation allowance was not found in the current organization/feature guides.

facts.label: Invitation semantics and limits
facts.value: Native email invitation for new or existing realm users; admins track pending/expired state, resend with fresh expiry and delete; successful acceptance removes the invitation record.

facts.label: SSO and SCIM software charges
facts.value: Native incoming SAML/OIDC, downstream OIDC/SAML and current native SCIM have no separate upstream connection/directory license fee.

facts.label: Developer seats, projects and environments
facts.value: not_applicable to a hosted plan: Keycloak has realm/client/admin objects, not an upstream console-seat/project subscription allowance.

facts.label: Login hostname and domains
facts.value: Self-host operator controls public hostname, admin hostname/backchannel behavior and TLS; no upstream per-domain license fee.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: external_service/operator SMTP configured per realm for verification, reset, invitation and event emails; password or supported XOAUTH2 SMTP authentication.

facts.label: SMS and other external services
facts.value: Native general SMS/phone-code delivery was not established; external authenticators/providers/custom code are required where such methods are selected. Google reCAPTCHA integration uses your external credentials.

facts.label: Billing limits versus overload
facts.value: not_applicable to a provider invoice: no upstream free-to-paid transition, MAU overage grace, automatic upgrade or vendor spending cap.

facts.label: Authentication/session limit behavior
facts.value: Configured session-count limiter can deny a new session or terminate the oldest; brute-force protection can temporarily/permanently block password/OTP/recovery attempts.

facts.label: Other feature and operating costs
facts.value: Core features do not add an upstream invoice for API requests, audit events, tokens, MFA, branding, SCIM or SAML. Compute/SQL/cache/SMTP/backup and optional support/plugins remain separate.

facts.label: Solo-builder entry and seller eligibility
facts.value: Public core license grants rights to individuals/legal entities worldwide; production software can be obtained from public downloads without a vendor checkout.

facts.label: Upstream signup, card and trial
facts.value: not_applicable: no upstream hosted production account/trial is selected; public distribution/container is the entry path.

facts.label: Type and account scope
facts.value: Self-hosted IAM/SSO server providing accounts, registration/login, verification/recovery, sessions, identity federation, user administration and authorization.

facts.label: Deployment/commercial boundary
facts.value: Downloadable Java/Quarkus server, official container and Kubernetes/OpenShift Operator. Optional Red Hat build/subscription is customer-installed software, including on managed OpenShift.

facts.label: Operator responsibilities
facts.value: Developer or separately contracted host operates server, database, network/TLS, clusters/cache, storage, patching, backups, monitoring, failover and email sender.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in username/password and configurable email-as-username/login-with-email; self-host core, no paid gate.

facts.label: Email link / email-code login extension
facts.value: plugin: Phase Two keycloak-magic-link supplies magic-link and email OTP authentication and is linked by the official extension catalog. Not established as a built-in core login method.

facts.label: Phone, anonymous and crypto-wallet login
facts.value: Native phone/SMS first-factor login, anonymous guest-account creation/upgrade and Ethereum-style wallet login were not established in the current core feature/authentication guides.

facts.label: Digital credential wallets
facts.value: OID4VCI credential issuance is preview and OID4VP credential verification is experimental in current release notes.

facts.label: Core social providers
facts.value: built_in documented providers include Bitbucket, Facebook, GitHub, GitLab, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft, PayPal, Stack Overflow and Twitter.

facts.label: Apple and generic identity providers
facts.value: Generic OIDC/OAuth2 identity brokering is native; the official extension catalog lists an independently maintained Apple Identity Provider plugin.

facts.label: Passkeys and user experience
facts.value: built_in supported passkeys:v1/WebAuthn: first-factor/passwordless, conditional autofill and explicit modal button; supported feature code enabled by default, realm policy still configured.

facts.label: Passkey RP and federation limits
facts.value: WebAuthn credentials bind to configured RP ID, defaulting to Keycloak base-URL host when blank. WebAuthn user handle has a 64-byte maximum; long external storage IDs can exceed it.

facts.label: Passkeys and conditional second factor
facts.value: Default browser flow skips Conditional 2FA after successful passkey authentication; administrators can change the credential condition to require another factor.

facts.label: Authenticator and security-key factors
facts.value: built_in TOTP/HOTP authenticator generators and WebAuthn security-key/biometric-unlocked authenticators as second factors; no paid core gate.

facts.label: MFA enforcement
facts.value: Authentication flows and required actions can make OTP/WebAuthn optional, conditional or required; enrollment can be required for new users, and post-broker flows can add checks after social/business SSO.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: built_in recovery-codes:v1 supported and enabled at server-feature level; current guide generates 12 sequential single-use backup codes, usable through Recovery Authentication Code Form.

facts.label: Lost OTP and recovery flow
facts.value: Forgot-password/reset-credentials flow can also reconfigure a lost OTP generator; Reset - Conditional OTP can be disabled if that is not desired.

facts.label: Verification and reset
facts.value: built_in verification-email and reset-credential links, required actions and admin-triggered password reset. Your realm SMTP supplies delivery.

facts.label: Email changes and user account deletion
facts.value: Supported Update Email action can require reauthentication and verification before applying a new address. End-user deletion is available after enabling Delete Account and assigning account delete-account role.

facts.label: Session/token model and defaults
facts.value: OIDC access/refresh tokens and SSO/client sessions; 26.8.1 constants: access token 300s, SSO idle 1,800s, SSO max 36,000s, offline idle 2,592,000s.

facts.label: Persistence and browser adapter storage
facts.value: Persistent online sessions are a supported default feature with SQL/cache state. keycloak-js holds access/refresh tokens in memory; it does not persist those tokens in browser storage.

facts.label: Refresh, idle and offline controls
facts.value: Realm/client idle/max/Remember Me settings, refresh-token rotation/reuse policy and offline-session limits are configurable. Refresh/authentication requests can extend idle life within configured maxima.

facts.label: Revocation and sign-out
facts.value: Admin/user session views and remote logout; realm not-before/revocation policy, OIDC logout/session management and token revocation mechanisms are documented.

facts.label: Downstream business protocols
facts.value: Core is an OAuth2/OIDC provider and SAML 2.0 identity provider for connected applications; clients can use standards-based libraries.

facts.label: Incoming business federation
facts.value: Core acts as an OIDC client/relying party and SAML service provider/broker to external IdPs, with metadata/endpoints, claim mapping and logout settings.

facts.label: Realms versus organizations
facts.value: Realms isolate users/credentials/clients. Organizations provide customer/partner context within a realm; a realm user can link to one or more organizations.

facts.label: Groups, roles and tenant checks
facts.value: Native hierarchical organization groups can carry realm/client role mappings; configured OIDC/SAML mappers expose group/role data nested by organization.

facts.label: Membership, invitations and delegated administration
facts.value: Core UI/API supports member add/remove, new/existing-user invitations, organization groups and fine-grained organization administration.

facts.label: Native SCIM maturity and endpoints
facts.value: SCIM API is supported in 26.8, default-supported server feature scim-api:v1; enable per realm. Native v2 Users/Groups CRUD/PATCH, schemas/discovery, filtering and pagination.

facts.label: SCIM deactivation and resource restrictions
facts.value: SCIM active maps to user enabled; user/group deletion is supported. Administrative users/groups are protected from SCIM writes, and organization-group membership cannot be managed through SCIM.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Server-hosted login, registration, verify/reset, MFA enrollment, Account Console and Admin Console; no upstream paid UI plan.

facts.label: Custom/embedded UI boundary
facts.value: Themes customize hosted pages; official React packages let you build your own Account/Admin Console. keycloak-js handles redirect/OIDC integration for your application.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Core supports custom login/account/admin/email/welcome themes with templates, CSS, images and messages; operator chooses hostname/TLS with no per-domain software fee.

facts.label: Domain migration caveats
facts.value: Configured hostname forms issuer/endpoints/action links; proxy headers and admin hostname need careful configuration. Passkeys retain the registered RP ID scope.

facts.label: Locales and language customization
facts.value: Released base login theme lists 40 locale codes: ar, az, ca, cs, da, de, el, en, es, eu, fa, fr, fi, hr, hu, hy, id, it, ja, kk, ko, ky, lt, lv, nl, no, pl, pt, pt-BR, ro, ru, sk, sl, sv, th, tr, uk, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW.

facts.label: Accessibility assurance
facts.value: A current independently scoped WCAG/VPAT/ACR report for upstream 26.8.1 was not established from the public UI/theme/configuration pages searched.

facts.label: Web frameworks and libraries
facts.value: Standards-based OAuth2/OIDC/SAML clients are the primary documented integration path: examples recommend Java/Spring, browser JS, Python, C#/OWIN, Apache mod_auth_openidc and other protocol implementations.

facts.label: Adapter lifecycle and versions
facts.value: Server 26.8.1; JS adapter separately 26.2.5; client libraries shown as 26.0.12; Node.js keycloak-connect is deprecated on Downloads even though its usage guide remains available.

facts.label: Mobile/native integration
facts.value: Official integration guide recommends external AppAuth libraries for Android and iOS; keycloak-js documents hybrid/custom adapters.

facts.label: Cordova, Capacitor and other clients
facts.value: Built-in Cordova/cordova-native modes are deprecated; JS guide shows custom adapter approach for environments such as Capacitor. No current first-party Flutter/React Native SDK support matrix was established.

facts.label: Production database choices
facts.value: Supported versions table: PostgreSQL 14–18, EDB 17–18, Aurora PostgreSQL 15–17; MySQL 8.0/8.4 LTS; MariaDB 10.6/10.11/11.4/11.8 LTS; SQL Server 2019/2022; Oracle 19c 19.3+ or 23.x 23.5+; Azure SQL Database/Managed Instance latest.

facts.label: JVM and infrastructure
facts.value: Current platform guide lists OpenJDK 17/21/25; official container uses 21 and guide recommends 25 generally. Java 17 was deprecated in earlier release notes. TLS/hostname, SQL and cache/network configuration are production prerequisites.

facts.label: Cache and external dependencies
facts.value: Embedded/distributed Infinispan caches are part of clustered server operation; current default transport uses database-backed jdbc-ping. Multi-cluster v2 can use database/stateless design without external Infinispan. SMTP is needed for mail-dependent flows.

facts.label: Installation and upgrade operations
facts.value: Official containers/distribution/Operator plus production, database, hostname and HA guides. Patch rolling-updates v2 is supported; upgrade compatibility check and migration guide must match chosen versions/providers.

facts.label: Published sizing guidance
facts.value: Container guide recommends 2 GB memory limit for smaller production deployments; its 750 MB note approximates an old 512 MB heap. Separate HA sizing example starts at 1,250 MB per pod including 10k cached sessions.

facts.label: Custom fields and Java extension points
facts.value: built_in user-profile schema/validation/visibility plus authentication flows, required actions, protocol mappers and Java Service Provider Interfaces (SPIs).

facts.label: Workflow automation maturity and scope
facts.value: workflows:v1 is a supported default feature in 26.8. Current workflow engine operates on User resources, with events, conditions, scheduled steps and tasks such as notifications, role changes and disabling users.

facts.label: Events and HTTP webhook boundary
facts.value: Built-in Logging and Email Event Listeners; custom Event Listener SPI is documented. The official catalog lists community webhook extensions.

facts.label: JavaScript server scripts
facts.value: scripts:v1 is a preview feature, disabled by default and not recommended for production under the feature policy.

facts.label: Account administration and permissions
facts.value: Admin Console and Admin REST API provide user creation/search/update/deletion, enabled-state changes, credential resets, required actions, role/group membership and session management; service-account access and fine-grained permissions are available.

facts.label: User impersonation
facts.value: Native impersonation requires the impersonation administration role. An administrator can act as a user from the Admin Console.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking sign-in identities
facts.value: Account Console and first-broker-login flows support identity-provider linking; client-initiated account linking is documented via an application-initiated action.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and arbitrary account merge
facts.value: A native anonymous-user-to-registered-user upgrade flow or general automatic merge of two existing user IDs was not established.

facts.label: Brute-force protection defaults
facts.value: Configurable permanent/temporary account lockout applies to passwords, OTP and recovery codes; brute-force detection is disabled by default.

facts.label: Password and bot defenses
facts.value: New realms have no password policy by default. Configurable policies include complexity/history/denylist; registration supports Google reCAPTCHA v2/v3 and Enterprise configuration.

facts.label: Request capacity and overload
facts.value: Production guide documents limiting queued requests and returning HTTP 503 under overload; actual throughput depends on database, CPU, memory, deployment and authentication workload.

facts.label: Universal endpoint quotas
facts.value: No upstream universal login/Admin API requests-per-minute allowance or MAU-based burst entitlement was published in the checked production, sizing, brute-force, session-limit and REST API pages.

facts.label: Audit data and defaults
facts.value: User login/registration/logout/token/credential/linking events and administrator operations can be stored/viewed; persistent event saving is off by default and must be enabled/configured.

facts.label: Audit retention and external logs
facts.value: Realm event Expiration is configurable; events can be cleared/read with Admin Console/API. Logging and Email listeners plus custom Event Listener SPI are documented; server logging supports operator-controlled handlers.

facts.label: Offline user export: profiles, IDs and links
facts.value: Self-operated CLI realm/user JSON export includes user representations, identifiers, profile data, group/role mappings and federated identity links. No per-export upstream license fee.

facts.label: Offline credential export
facts.value: Full internal CLI export traverses stored credentials; released ModelToRepresentation copies credentialData and secretData. Password records contain encoded hash/salt and algorithm/work-factor data.

facts.label: Admin Console partial export and backup limits
facts.value: Admin Console partial export excludes users and masks secrets. CLI export omits user/admin events, persisted sessions, workflow state and revoked tokens; stop all nodes for consistency.

facts.label: Native JSON import
facts.value: CLI import supports native realm/user JSON; startup import skips a realm already present. Override import requires all nodes stopped because it does not join the cluster cache.

facts.label: Password hash formats and custom migration
facts.value: Built-in policies include Argon2 and PBKDF2 variants; non-FIPS default is Argon2, FIPS default PBKDF2-SHA512. User Storage SPI can bridge external stores and validate/update their credentials.

facts.label: Account deletion and organization offboarding
facts.value: Admin API deletes users; configured self-service Delete Account is available. Managed organization-member removal can delete the realm account; unmanaged member removal leaves the realm account.

facts.label: Retention, backups and project closure
facts.value: No upstream-operated customer database or subscription account exists for this self-hosted scope. Operator controls database, audit expiration, logs, replicas, backups and infrastructure account closure.

facts.label: Authentication-data location
facts.value: Self-chosen: operator deploys server, SQL database, caches, logs and backups on its chosen infrastructure. Upstream does not offer a documented region selector for a project-hosted account service.

facts.label: Upstream website legal/privacy scope
facts.value: Linux Foundation privacy policy and website Terms of Use are public and linked by the project. They address Foundation websites/community interactions, not operation of your self-hosted end-user account database.

facts.label: Hosted processing agreement and cloud assurance
facts.value: Upstream-hosted auth-data DPA, subprocessor list, region contract and SOC 2 cloud-service report are not applicable to this self-operated distribution.

facts.label: FIPS evidence and scope
facts.value: Official guide documents FIPS mode, required operating-system/Java/BCFIPS setup and supported cryptographic restrictions; fips:v1 is a supported feature disabled by default.

facts.label: Name, governance and URLs
facts.value: Keycloak; open-source CNCF incubation project, credited to Keycloak Authors and the Linux Foundation. Site https://www.keycloak.org/; source https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak.

facts.label: Lifecycle search and forum shutdown
facts.value: No upstream product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the checked home/download/release/community evidence. Official July 20, 2026 notice winds down Discourse: September archive-only, planned December 2026 shutdown.

facts.label: Current server maintenance
facts.value: Server 26.8.1 published 2026-10-13T08:58:15Z; download/docs pages identify 26.8.1; repository archived=false and disabled=false at this check.

facts.label: Component deprecations
facts.value: Downloads mark Node.js adapter deprecated. Current JS guide deprecates built-in Cordova/cordova-native modes; feature table deprecates legacy login v1, old conditional-passkey authenticator, and multi-site v1 among other components.

facts.label: Server license and commercial use
facts.value: Apache-2.0: no-charge copyright/patent grant for using, modifying and distributing the core, subject to notice/license requirements and other stated conditions.

facts.label: Official browser adapter license
facts.value: Current separate keycloak/keycloak-js repository publishes Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Third-party email passwordless plugin license
facts.value: Official extension index links Phase Two keycloak-magic-link; its current COPYING is Elastic License 2.0, separate from Keycloak core Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Service status and uptime promise
facts.value: A hosted authentication-service status page and upstream percentage uptime SLA are not applicable to the self-hosted server; Apache license supplies software without warranty.

facts.label: Released and supported versions
facts.value: Current upstream server 26.8.1 released October 13, 2026. Security policy targets the current major.minor release for fixes; lower-severity fixes may wait for the next minor release.

facts.label: Commercial downstream lifecycle boundary
facts.value: Red Hat build of Keycloak publishes its own lifecycle: 26.x major support minimum two years, 27.x onward minimum three years, with phased minor-version support.

facts.label: Community and commercial routes
facts.value: Community help uses GitHub Discussions, mailing lists and CNCF Slack; issue tracking is available through the project. Commercial support is available separately through Red Hat’s qualifying entitlements.

facts.label: Forum guidance conflict
facts.value: Community page still advertises the Discourse forum for new questions while the July 20, 2026 notice announces its archive/shutdown schedule and recommends replacements.

facts.label: Security-report response
facts.value: Private suspected-vulnerability route: keycloak-security@googlegroups.com. Published acknowledgment target is seven business days.

facts.label: MAU definition
facts.value: One active user per billing period if issued at least one access token; repeat sign-ins count once. Created/deleted before sign-in is not counted; signed in then deleted still counted.

facts.label: MAO definition
facts.value: Organization has at least two users, with at least one signing into that organization during billing period. Created/deleted org counts only if active by this definition.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Free: USD 0/month; 10,500 MAU.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Pro: USD 25/month.

facts.label: Payment and commitment
facts.value: Credit-card payments; Enterprise can arrange invoicing/annual/currency terms. Upgrade immediately charges full subscription; metered usage still payable on downgrade.

facts.label: Public unit prices
facts.value: USD/month: Pro base 25, extra MAU .0175; Plus base 75, extra MAU .0163; Scale base 250, extra MAU .0151. Each includes 10,500 MAU.

facts.label: Business scenarios
facts.value: Our derived cost records appear below.

facts.label: Organization allowance
facts.value: Free 5 MAO; Pro/Plus/Scale 50 MAO. Extra MAO USD .50/.47/.43 respectively.

facts.label: MAO allowance corroboration
facts.value: Free includes 5; Pro, Plus, Scale and Enterprise include 50 MAO; extra units charged at plan rate.

facts.label: Enterprise SSO connections
facts.value: Free and Pro: 1 enterprise connection; Plus and above: unlimited. Kinde acts as service provider.

facts.label: Dashboard and application limits
facts.value: Dashboard seats/applications unlimited. Environments Free/Pro 2, Plus 6, Scale 11.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: Default emails sent from @kinde.com; custom SMTP sender supported and recommended before production. Kinde monitors default email routing/delivery.

facts.label: Custom SMTP requirements
facts.value: One sender; provider must support username/password and TLS. Signup/sign-in/OTP/reset mails use chosen sender; team invitations/export notices still from Kinde.

facts.label: SMS delivery
facts.value: Default Kinde SMS supports live environments on all plans. Free 10/month total including MFA; paid usage billed/message. BYO Twilio or Sinch Engage requires paid plan; no Kinde charge for BYO messages.

facts.label: SMS rate notation
facts.value: Pricing prints "$7c per SMS".

facts.label: Limit behavior
facts.value: Paid additional MAO billed at plan rate; dashboard shows Free approaches/excesses and paid usage costs. Exact Free login-stop behavior, grace period, auto-upgrade and spend cap unknown.

facts.label: Cancellation/downgrade
facts.value: Account closure guide says paid downgrade must go through support; no self-serve cancellation. Change-plan guide also gives dashboard downgrade steps.

facts.label: Other metered items
facts.value: Plan usage also tracks M2M tokens, enterprise connections and environments; Kinde Care Enterprise separately quoted.

facts.label: Optional billing charges
facts.value: Optional customer billing changes charges; excluded from fixed auth-only sub-scenario.

facts.label: MAO definition conflict
facts.value: Usage guide requires at least two stored users with one active; pricing excludes organizations containing only one active user. Different for two members with one active.

facts.label: BYO SMS plan conflict
facts.value: Phone guide requires paid plan for own provider; pricing Free customization row says custom SMS provider included.

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Terms refer to a person or entity; EULA minimum age 16. Exhaustive restricted-country list and one-person production eligibility not established.

facts.label: Self-service and card
facts.value: Free signup without credit card.

facts.label: Production entry
facts.value: Free plan can run a business; paid features available by upgrading through dashboard.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Cloud SaaS: accounts, authentication, authorization, verification, user management, feature management and customer billing.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Vendor-managed infrastructure; developer integrates SDK/API and operates their app.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: yes; email/username with password, built_in.

facts.label: Email code and magic link
facts.value: Email OTP yes; magic links explicitly not supported as password alternative. OTP expiry 2 hours; email passwordless default for new businesses.

facts.label: Phone code
facts.value: yes; SMS OTP primary authentication; WhatsApp when configured; SMS also usable for MFA.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: Fully anonymous users explicitly disallowed in username signup; email also required. Wallet-login support unknown.

facts.label: Social providers
facts.value: Built_in guides: Apple, Bitbucket, Clever, Discord, Facebook, GitHub, GitLab, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Roblox, Slack, Twitch, X/Twitter, Xero.

facts.label: Social platform limitation
facts.value: Hosted auth screens show configured providers on all devices; no platform-conditional show/hide. Custom pages can supply this logic.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: yes; all paid plans. Existing users sign in using WebAuthn biometrics/security key; not first-time signup. Setup follows credential login; not social/enterprise login.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: Email OTP, SMS OTP, authenticator-app code. Optional or mandatory MFA; recovery codes offered. Per-organization enforcement documented as Scale.

facts.label: MFA plan mismatch
facts.value: MFA guide says organization MFA requires Scale; pricing groups organization MFA under advanced orgs on Plus/Scale.

facts.label: Verification and address changes
facts.value: Email/phone identities verified in auth flow; trusted provider email can create/link identity. Admin changes contact identity by adding new identity and deleting old.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Dashboard/API can mark password reset required; user prompted on next sign-in. User-facing forgot-password flow linked in password guide.

facts.label: Sessions and revocation
facts.value: Persistent/non-persistent SSO cookies, per-app policy; idle default 86,400 seconds. DELETE user sessions ends SSO sessions and refresh tokens; existing access JWTs valid until expiry.

facts.label: Token expiry
facts.value: Access/ID/refresh lifetimes configurable in seconds. Client-specific refresh cookie option requires custom domain. /oauth2/revoke documented.

facts.label: Business login standards
facts.value: Kinde SP for SAML, Entra ID OAuth2/WS-Fed and named enterprise integrations. JIT/pre-provisioning supported; logout usually leaves upstream IdP session active.

facts.label: Identity-provider role
facts.value: Kinde can act as SAML 2.0 IdP for third-party tools on Scale.

facts.label: Organizations and roles
facts.value: User groups separated as organizations; user may join multiple orgs. Roles defined at business level and applied per user per organization. Nested project/org hierarchy unsupported.

facts.label: Membership, invites and customer admin
facts.value: Organization portal can expose members, invitations, roles and pending-invite revocation; Members switch available to every business, off by default.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: Coming soon/in development; production SCIM support not established. Planned user provisioning/deprovisioning and IdP group-role mapping.

facts.label: Hosted login and account screens
facts.value: Hosted authentication pages plus configurable user and organization self-service portals. User portal account details; organization portal membership/roles; APIs can support custom portal.

facts.label: Custom domain
facts.value: Custom auth domain via DNS CNAME and vendor-provisioned certificate; configure environment and provider callbacks.

facts.label: Branding removal
facts.value: Powered by Kinde can be disabled; applies to all applications without redeploy. Paid plan required by pricing.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: UI translations: English en/en-US/en-AU/en-GB, Dutch, German, Polish, Hebrew, Italian, French, Malay, Spanish, Russian, Brazilian Portuguese, Norwegian, Swedish. RTL supported.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: unknown: public accessibility conformance report and independently assessed scope.

facts.label: Web frameworks
facts.value: Official SDK index: .NET, Elixir, Express, Go, Java, JavaScript, Next.js, Node.js, Nuxt, PHP, Python, React, Remix, Ruby, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, TypeScript, GraphQL; Angular labelled community.

facts.label: Runtime/version example
facts.value: Next.js App Router guide: Next.js 13+, Node.js 20+. Compatibility table: Next 16 requires SDK >=2.11.0; 12.3/13.5/14.2/15.2 use SDK 2.x.

facts.label: Edge runtime
facts.value: Cloudflare Workers Next.js guide with OpenNext adapter and Node compatibility flags; server auth patterns recommended over KindeProvider for SSR.

facts.label: Mobile and desktop
facts.value: Official SDK index lists Android, iOS, React Native, Expo, Flutter. Electron integration guide also listed in developer docs.

facts.label: Database/service prerequisites
facts.value: Hosted identity service; client app connects via SDK/API. Own social-provider credentials required for production. External SMTP/SMS optional/configurable.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: not_applicable for hosted auth server.

facts.label: Custom logic
facts.value: TypeScript/JavaScript workflows synced from developer Git repo and executed by Kinde at defined triggers. One workflow/trigger; no custom triggers.

facts.label: Events/webhooks
facts.value: Webhooks send signed JWT event payloads to own endpoint. HTTP 200 acknowledges; failures retried with backoff. Endpoint must verify and deduplicate events.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Dashboard create/import/search/update users/identities and role permissions; Management API provides most admin operations. Built-in support impersonation explicitly unavailable.

facts.label: Suspend/delete
facts.value: Owner/Admin can suspend, restore or permanently delete user via Dashboard/API. Sessions/refresh tokens invalidated; access tokens remain until expiry.

facts.label: Linking/unlinking
facts.value: Matching verified email from trusted social provider can link social and email identities. Enterprise identity replaces other identity types; original credentials removed in enterprise migration.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: Fully anonymous signup disallowed in username guide; built-in guest-to-registered upgrade not established.

facts.label: Attack protection
facts.value: AWS WAF, application throttling and account lockout; five wrong attempts locks for five minutes; common-password blocking. Native bot detection roadmap; Cloudflare proxy/Turnstile alternative.

facts.label: Configurable protection
facts.value: Credential enumeration protection configurable; disposable email blocking requires Plus+, off by default.

facts.label: API limits
facts.value: Management API returns HTTP 429 for excess frequency/concurrency; RateLimit-Reset gives seconds until reset. GET pages max 500 results; bulk POST/PATCH max 100 objects.

facts.label: Numerical burst/rate caps
facts.value: not_published in reviewed Management API limit/security pages: universal requests/second, concurrency slots and login-endpoint burst caps.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Signup, auth, access-token grant and policy-acceptance events. Free 1 day; Pro 7; Plus 14; Scale 30; Enterprise extended retention contact sales.

facts.label: Portal feature freshness gap
facts.value: Portal overview says SSO enterprise self-management coming soon; detailed self-service SSO guides already appear in docs. Passkey guide describes account portal passkey controls absent from overview.

facts.label: Export and leaving
facts.value: Owner-only NDJSON export of users, organizations and access requests. Includes user IDs, identities, external IDs, org memberships; optional password hashes/algorithm/config.

facts.label: Import and migration
facts.value: CSV/NDJSON import, UTF-8 or UTF-16 BOM, max 49MB/file. Firebase NDJSON with modified scrypt parameters supported; rehashed to bcrypt after first login.

facts.label: Delete account/business
facts.value: Business Owner can delete Free business; paid must contact support to downgrade. Full account closure requested by owner email. Deletes product data; legal/billing records may remain.

facts.label: Retention
facts.value: Privacy policy retains data as reasonably necessary for purpose/legal/tax/reporting; complaints/litigation can extend. Exact backup retention/purge duration unknown.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: Choose at signup: Sydney Australia, Oregon USA, Quebec Canada, Dublin Ireland, London UK. Region cannot later be changed. In-region failover; no cross-region failover.

facts.label: Processing exceptions
facts.value: Hosting/SMS/webhooks align to chosen region; default AWS email processes in Australia. Support providers process in Australia, USA or UK.

facts.label: Privacy documents
facts.value: Privacy policy and public subprocessor list; DPA requested from support@kinde.com.

facts.label: Assurance evidence
facts.value: Vendor claims ISO 27001:2022 certification by Compass Assurance Services and SOC 2 Type 2 by AssuranceLab. Certificate/attestation public; full SOC2 report paid plans and NDA.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Kinde; Kinde Australia Pty Ltd, ACN 655 096 263. Site https://www.kinde.com/; docs https://docs.kinde.com/.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Available; self-service signup advertised; signup not tested. No product shutdown, sunset, rebrand, pivot, signup closure or major paid-feature retirement found.

facts.label: 2025 authentication privacy breach
facts.value: On 2025-09-03, a deployment bug caused OAuth/OIDC logins to show some users another user’s profile. Kinde calls this a privacy breach; fewer than 150 profiles were exposed to other users for 68 minutes. It says the bug was fixed, tokens invalidated, with no external attacker or cross-business exposure.

facts.label: Hosted commercial-use rules
facts.value: Subscription platform under vendor terms; personal, non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable, worldwide, non-transferable platform-use licence, subject to terms. Not a licence to distribute the server.

facts.label: Client SDK licence
facts.value: Next.js SDK: MIT; permits use, modification, distribution and sale with copyright/permission notice.

facts.label: Status and SLA
facts.value: Official status https://status.kinde.com/; current/past incidents and maintenance.

facts.label: Availability promise
facts.value: Enterprise advertises custom uptime SLAs; displayed average availability 99.99% is marketing observation, not a published standard contract SLA. Contract percentage/period/exclusions unknown.

facts.label: Release/maintenance evidence
facts.value: Next.js SDK release page marks 2.13.2 latest; date label 05 Oct 04:20. Compatibility docs name SDK 2.11.0 minimum for Next 16.

facts.label: Support route
facts.value: Email support@kinde.com, help widget, Slack/Discord communities. Team mainly Australia; opposing time zones may wait a few hours; 24-hour coverage an aim, not guaranteed response.
