facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: Fortify, Sanctum and Passport do not bill for MAU, returning users, stored users, tokens or OAuth clients.

facts.label: Free production software allowance
facts.value: $0 software licence charge under MIT; no numerical production-user quota or monthly allowance reset in the three licences.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable: no required package production subscription, annual contract or auth-plan minimum.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Not applicable: no per-user/token/connection price tiers, overages or paid package editions to calculate.

facts.label: Organization fees and caps
facts.value: Not applicable to package pricing: the three packages contain no licensed organization/membership allowance or per-team price.

facts.label: SSO and SCIM connection fees
facts.value: Not applicable to core package pricing: no hosted SAML/SCIM connection product or per-connection fee.

facts.label: Builder seats, projects and domains
facts.value: Not applicable: no shared vendor auth dashboard or paid seat/project/environment/domain caps.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: Fortify password-reset and verification flows use Laravel notifications/mail; developer configures a mail transport and sender.

facts.label: Messaging cost and channels
facts.value: No included email credits or vendor-auth SMS allowance; actual delivery cost depends on the chosen sender, volume and provider. TOTP uses an authenticator app, not SMS.

facts.label: Hosted limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no package MAU cap that automatically bills, suspends login or forces an upgrade.

facts.label: Other billable package limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no package API-request, JWT, MFA, audit-log or transaction-fee tariff.

facts.label: Hosted eligibility and country restrictions
facts.value: Not applicable to these embedded packages: no vendor production tenant or seller-account opening requirement.

facts.label: Trial, card and self-service account
facts.value: Not applicable: Composer/app installation replaces a hosted authentication trial; no auth-vendor card or sales step is needed by these package instructions.

facts.label: Fortify scope
facts.value: Headless account backend: login/logout, registration, password reset, email verification, profile/password updates, TOTP/recovery and passkey integration when enabled.

facts.label: Sanctum scope
facts.value: First-party SPA cookie-session authentication and simple bearer API tokens with abilities; authenticates existing app users.

facts.label: Passport scope
facts.value: OAuth 2 authorization server and bearer-token API authentication, built on league/oauth2-server; clients, grants, access/refresh tokens and scopes.

facts.label: Framework core scope
facts.value: Laravel guards/providers handle request authentication and user retrieval; session services maintain browser state; gates/policies handle authorization.

facts.label: Who runs and stores accounts
facts.value: Developer operates the Laravel app, user database, sessions/tokens, signing/encryption keys, mail delivery, backups and package updates, directly or through chosen hosting.

facts.label: Fortify password login and registration
facts.value: built_in backend routes for username/email plus password, optional remember flag, and registration through a published CreateNewUser action.

facts.label: Passwordless passkey login
facts.value: Fortify 1.41.0 wraps laravel/passkeys and registers passkey login routes when enabled; this is distinct from email magic-link login.

facts.label: Email link/code, phone, wallet and anonymous accounts
facts.value: No such first-factor account flows in the three core package route/source inventories; custom_code/external_service is needed.

facts.label: Sanctum and Passport credential boundaries
facts.value: Sanctum tokens authenticate an existing user; mobile login endpoint is an app-written credential exchange. Passport grants issue OAuth tokens; password grant is opt-in and no longer recommended.

facts.label: Optional first-party Socialite providers
facts.value: plugin: Laravel Socialite, separately installed, supports Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Google, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Slack in current Laravel 13 docs; MIT software licence.

facts.label: Apple, Microsoft and other providers
facts.value: No Apple/Microsoft adapter is claimed by the checked Socialite first-party provider list. Other adapters are community integrations; WorkOS starter variants document Apple/Microsoft through an external provider.

facts.label: Fortify passkey backend
facts.value: built_in integration via laravel/passkeys; configure Features::passkeys, implement PasskeyUser and use the Fortify PasskeyAuthenticatable trait; supports register, login, confirmation and deletion.

facts.label: Passkey domains and management protection
facts.value: Default relying_party_id is APP_URL's host, allowed_origins contains APP_URL, user-handle secret derives from app key unless separately configured, ceremony timeout is 60000 milliseconds.

facts.label: Passkey browser client and autofill
facts.value: Optional official @laravel/passkeys client has React, Vue and Svelte helpers. Current main README documents autofill:true plus an input autocomplete containing webauthn, with explicit-button fallback.

facts.label: Fortify TOTP factor
facts.value: built_in configurable six-digit time-based authenticator code. Published install stub enables confirmation before enrollment completes and password confirmation before factor management.

facts.label: Recovery and storage
facts.value: Fortify generates eight recovery codes, encrypts the secret and recovery-code JSON, and replaces a consumed recovery code. Regeneration and disable endpoints are provided.

facts.label: MFA scope across token flows
facts.value: Fortify's two-factor challenge is part of its session-login pipeline; custom Sanctum mobile credential exchanges and Passport grants need their own enforcement design.

facts.label: Fortify email verification
facts.value: Enable emailVerification, implement MustVerifyEmail and protect relevant routes with verified middleware; registration dispatches the framework verification workflow.

facts.label: Verification expiry and email changes
facts.value: Framework verification URL defaults to 60 minutes. Fortify's published profile action updates a changed email, clears email_verified_at and sends a new verification notification for MustVerifyEmail users.

facts.label: Password reset and confirmation
facts.value: Fortify reset routes use Laravel password brokers. Framework users broker defaults: reset expiry 60 minutes; token-generation throttle 60 seconds; sensitive-action password confirmation defaults to 10800 seconds.

facts.label: Profile/password updates and deletion
facts.value: Fortify can publish profile/password update actions. Account deletion, phone verification and broader lifecycle cleanup are app/starter-kit work, without a core deletion route.

facts.label: Framework/Fortify browser sessions
facts.value: Laravel session guard with cookie and configured backing store; framework defaults to database session driver and 120 minutes idle lifetime, configurable in session.php.

facts.label: Remember me and logout
facts.value: Fortify accepts remember through the framework guard. Its logout calls guard logout, invalidates current session and regenerates the CSRF token.

facts.label: Other-device browser logout
facts.value: Framework Auth::logoutOtherDevices(currentPassword) can invalidate other browser sessions when AuthenticateSession/auth.session middleware is installed.

facts.label: Sanctum bearer lifetime and storage
facts.value: API tokens are SHA-256-hashed in the app database; plaintext is returned at creation. No expiry by default; set global expiration minutes and/or per-token expires_at.

facts.label: Sanctum expiry checks and revocation
facts.value: Released Guard requires both the global-age check and individual expires_at check to pass; deleting one or all token records revokes them.

facts.label: Passport access/refresh lifetimes
facts.value: Passport defaults access, refresh and personal access token intervals to one year; client-credentials interval follows access-token interval unless set separately.

facts.label: Passport refresh and revocation
facts.value: OAuth refresh-token grant exchanges a refresh token for new tokens. Revoke access token and related refresh token explicitly; editing table expires_at does not revoke an issued signed token.

facts.label: Passport SPA cookie mode
facts.value: Optional CreateFreshApiToken middleware sets encrypted laravel_token JWT cookie with lifetime equal to session.lifetime; requires CSRF header handling.

facts.label: Passport protocol and role
facts.value: OAuth 2 authorization server: authorization-code grant, PKCE, device authorization, client credentials, refresh tokens and personal access tokens. Password/implicit grants require opt-in and are discouraged.

facts.label: Enterprise login boundary
facts.value: Fortify and Sanctum do not supply SAML or generic business OIDC federation; Passport is an OAuth server, not an external enterprise identity broker. Add separate integrations for those roles.

facts.label: Core memberships and permissions
facts.value: Fortify/Sanctum/Passport do not provide customer organization, invitation or role models. Framework gates/policies express app-defined resource authorization.

facts.label: Optional starter-kit teams
facts.value: Current first-party React, Svelte, Vue and Livewire starter kits can be generated with teams, personal/current team, switching, invitations and team management screens.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: No SCIM User/Group server, directory provisioning or automatic enterprise deactivation mapping in the three packages; custom_code/external_service required.

facts.label: Fortify UI
facts.value: Headless backend: app supplies login/register/reset/verification/password-confirmation/MFA/passkey screens, or uses a separate starter kit.

facts.label: Sanctum and Passport UI
facts.value: Sanctum provides no account screens. Passport requires application-provided OAuth consent and device-code/approval views through response/view callbacks.

facts.label: Optional starter-kit screens
facts.value: First-party React, Svelte, Vue and Livewire kits scaffold app authentication UI using Fortify and allow full customization.

facts.label: Branding
facts.value: Application-owned frontend code, layouts, response contracts and email notifications are customizable; MIT has no paid white-label tier.

facts.label: Domains and route configuration
facts.value: Fortify prefix/domain/routes are configurable. Sanctum SPA/API must share the same top-level domain, with stateful-domain, CORS and cookie configuration; Passport clients require matching redirect URIs.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: Framework localization supports PHP/JSON translation files and per-request locale; Fortify status/error text uses language keys. UI translations are app/starter-kit work.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independent accessibility assessment specifically covering these three packages' resulting auth UI located.

facts.label: Fortify runtime declaration
facts.value: Fortify 1.41.0 declares PHP ^8.2, ext-json, Illuminate console/support ^11.0 or ^12.0 or ^13.0; passkeys ^0.2.0, google2fa ^9.0 and QR-code ^3.0 dependencies.

facts.label: Sanctum runtime declaration
facts.value: Sanctum 4.3.3 declares PHP ^8.2, ext-json and Illuminate console/contracts/database/support ^11.0 or ^12.0 or ^13.0.

facts.label: Passport runtime declaration
facts.value: Passport 13.10.0 declares PHP ^8.2, JSON/OpenSSL, Illuminate ^11.35 or ^12.0 or ^13.0, and league/oauth2-server ^9.2.

facts.label: Current framework and frontend options
facts.value: Laravel 13 requires PHP >=8.3. Official starter UIs cover React, Svelte, Vue and Livewire; headless Fortify accepts app-designed frontends.

facts.label: Sanctum mobile integration
facts.value: Documented bearer-token flow for mobile clients: app writes a username/password/device-name token endpoint and returns plaintext token once; client sends Authorization: Bearer.

facts.label: Passport public/native/device clients
facts.value: Authorization code with PKCE supports public clients that cannot protect a client secret; device authorization supports limited-input/browserless devices.

facts.label: Database prerequisites
facts.value: App database for users, session/token/reset state and optional passkey credentials. Framework docs list MariaDB 10.3+, MySQL 5.7+, PostgreSQL 10.0+, SQLite 3.26.0+, SQL Server 2017+.

facts.label: Package-specific storage and keys
facts.value: Fortify needs account schema and TOTP/passkey migrations when used; Sanctum needs personal_access_tokens; Passport needs OAuth tables and private/public signing keys.

facts.label: Mail, session and throttle services
facts.value: Developer configures mail transport, persistent session store and appropriate cache backend for rate limiting. Redis is optional when choosing Redis sessions/cache, not compulsory for every app.

facts.label: Deployment and app operation
facts.value: Operate a Laravel PHP app with required extensions, public/ web root, writable storage/bootstrap cache, protected secrets and production debug disabled.

facts.label: Upgrades and cleanup
facts.value: Review Passport major upgrade guide and package/framework support policy; schedule expired-reset/token cleanup if desired and maintain long-running workers.

facts.label: Backup and restore runbook
facts.value: No combined Fortify/Sanctum/Passport backup schedule, tested restore procedure or recovery-time/recovery-point promise located in the checked core deployment/source docs.

facts.label: Capacity evidence
facts.value: No auth-package MAU ceiling, minimum RAM/CPU or measured login/token requests-per-second commitment published in the checked installation/deployment docs.

facts.label: Fortify hooks and custom account fields
facts.value: Published CreateNewUser, ResetUserPassword, profile/password actions are replaceable; authenticateUsing, authenticateThrough and response contracts customize login and output.

facts.label: Sanctum token customization
facts.value: Use custom token model and token abilities; released guard exposes access-token retrieval and authentication callbacks and dispatches TokenAuthenticated.

facts.label: Passport events and extension points
facts.value: Custom OAuth models/routes, scopes and authorization/device views; AccessTokenCreated, AccessTokenRevoked and RefreshTokenCreated events.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Use application Eloquent/query APIs and app-built protected admin UI for user creation, search, updates, suspension/deletion; none of the three packages is a vendor user-admin console.

facts.label: Sanctum token administration
facts.value: App code can list a user's tokens and delete all, current or named token records through HasApiTokens; build any desired UI.

facts.label: Passport OAuth management
facts.value: ClientRepository, model APIs and Artisan commands create/manage OAuth clients and tokens; old JSON management routes are deprecated and off by default in 13.x.

facts.label: External identity linking
facts.value: custom_code: optional Socialite retrieves provider IDs/tokens; app callback chooses lookup, creation and linking behavior.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: No persistent anonymous-account conversion/merge workflow provided by Fortify, Sanctum or Passport.

facts.label: Login and factor throttling
facts.value: Published Fortify install provider defines login 5 requests/minute by normalized username plus IP, TOTP challenge 5/minute by login.id, and passkeys 10/minute by credential ID or session ID plus IP.

facts.label: Password checks and optional abuse controls
facts.value: Fortify published rules require string/confirmation and Password::default(); framework fallback is minimum 8 characters. Additional complexity and uncompromised checks are opt-in rule configuration.

facts.label: SPA and OAuth request protections
facts.value: Sanctum SPA flow uses CSRF initialization, stateful domains and cookies; Passport code-grant docs require state checking and offer PKCE for public clients.

facts.label: Fortify named and fallback limits
facts.value: Fresh published provider: login 5/minute, two-factor 5/minute, passkeys 10/minute. If no named login limiter is configured, internal LoginRateLimiter blocks after five failed attempts with a 60-second counter decay.

facts.label: Verification and reset limits
facts.value: Fortify verification handlers default to throttle:6,1; framework broker defaults reset-token regeneration to 60 seconds per user and 60-minute token validity.

facts.label: Passport OAuth endpoint throttles
facts.value: Released /oauth/token and device-code routes use generic throttle middleware. Framework default without override is 60 requests per minute; signature is authenticated user ID or route domain plus IP.

facts.label: Sanctum quota and throttle response
facts.value: Sanctum does not impose a hosted per-project API quota; app middleware defines request throttles. Framework throttle exceptions expose Retry-After and rate-limit headers.

facts.label: Authentication events
facts.value: Framework auth events include registration, login/failure, verification, logout/other-device logout, lockout and password-reset events; listeners can store or forward them.

facts.label: Package-specific events and metadata
facts.value: Fortify emits MFA/recovery events; Sanctum emits TokenAuthenticated and updates last_used_at; Passport emits access/refresh creation and access revocation events.

facts.label: Log retention versus audit retention
facts.value: Framework daily logging channel defaults max_files to 14 via LOG_DAILY_DAYS; monthly channel max_files is 3. Default stack aggregates single channel unless configured otherwise.

facts.label: Managed audit product promise
facts.value: No core hosted audit viewer, complete standardized security-event export or immutable retention-days promise located for the three-package family.

facts.label: User/profile/hash export
facts.value: App owns user and auth-related database records and can export through database tools or Eloquent/JSON code; no vendor export approval or export fee.

facts.label: Sanctum token export
facts.value: Token metadata and SHA-256 hashes are app data; original bearer plaintext cannot be recovered from the hash. PersonalAccessToken hides token during normal serialization.

facts.label: Passport OAuth export
facts.value: OAuth client/token/refresh data are local model records; client secrets are hashed in Passport 13 and tokens depend on configured signing/encryption keys and identifiers.

facts.label: TOTP and passkey exit constraints
facts.value: Fortify TOTP secret/recovery data are encrypted and require the right app encryption material. Passkey credentials and user identifiers are app-managed but use configured relying-party ID/origins.

facts.label: Existing users and hashes
facts.value: custom_code import into app schema/user provider. Laravel Hash supports bcrypt, argon and argon2id, and can rehash passwords on login when settings change.

facts.label: Migration rules and limits
facts.value: No core hosted bulk-import API/CSV contract or lazy-migration service. Custom providers/authenticateUsing can implement migration logic; algorithm verification rejects mismatches unless deliberately configured otherwise.

facts.label: Deleting application accounts
facts.value: Use app-owned Eloquent delete/forceDelete workflows and secure self-service/admin routes. Fortify core registers no delete-account route.

facts.label: Token and reset record cleanup

apps.name: Logto
apps.line: Open-source login service with a managed Cloud option.

free.text: Cloud Free: 50,000 MAU and 50,000 access tokens

cells.freeUsers: 50,000 MAU; token allowance also applies
cells.sso: $48/month per incoming enterprise SSO connector

mau.math: At 2,000 assumed access tokens (passes that prove a sign-in), Free covers 1,000 users. Users alone cannot set the real token bill.
At 20,000 assumed access tokens (passes that prove a sign-in), Free covers 10,000 users. Users alone cannot set the real token bill.
With 2 sign-ins per user, that is 100,000 access tokens. Pro is $24, plus $0.08 for each 100 tokens over the included amount, which is 100,000 minus 50,000. That comes to $64 a month.
With 2 sign-ins per user, that is 200,000 access tokens. Pro is $24, plus $0.08 for each 100 tokens over the included amount, which is 200,000 minus 50,000. That comes to $144 a month.

facts.value: Identity server and hosted identity platform: accounts, login, verification/recovery, sessions, authorization, organizations and SSO.

facts.label: Deployment options
facts.value: Logto Cloud Free/Pro/Enterprise; dedicated Azure Private Cloud; self-hosted OSS Community plus paid self-host licenses/support.

facts.label: Cloud operator
facts.value: Vendor hosts/manages Cloud infrastructure; developer integrates clients and enforces app/backend permissions.

facts.label: Self-host operator
facts.value: Developer runs server, PostgreSQL, networking, upgrades/security fixes, backups, recovery and optional cache/storage.

facts.label: Identifier/password login
facts.value: built_in username/password, email/password and phone/password flows; Cloud core/OSS.

facts.label: Email and phone codes
facts.value: built_in email/SMS one-time verification-code sign-in and signup through configured connectors.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: built_in one-time-token APIs plus custom_code landing link/send flow; email identifiers only; default token expiry 600 seconds.

facts.label: Guest/anonymous login

facts.label: Wallet login

facts.label: Generic and custom providers
facts.value: OAuth2/OIDC generic social connectors and developer-built OSS connectors are supported.

facts.label: Passkey first-factor gate
facts.value: built_in passkey sign-in is listed on Cloud Pro, not Free; OSS supports the core flow. Credential can also be used as a WebAuthn MFA factor.

facts.label: Passkey paths and fallback
facts.value: Dedicated button, identifier-first verification and compatible-browser autofill/conditional UI; alternative configured password/code methods remain fallback.

facts.label: Passkey domains and mobile versions
facts.value: Passkeys bind to their registration domain. Swift v2/system browser and Android v3/Custom Tabs support passkey sign-in; older embedded-WebView SDK versions do not.

facts.label: MFA factors and edition prices
facts.value: built_in TOTP, WebAuthn/passkeys, SMS, email and backup codes; Cloud Pro all-factor add-on $48/month; end-user MFA available in OSS.

facts.label: MFA enforcement
facts.value: Optional, adaptive or mandatory global policy; organization-level enrollment requirement can be configured.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: built_in 10 generated single-use backup codes; setup requires another primary MFA factor; Account API/UI can regenerate/manage.

facts.label: Email/phone verification
facts.value: End-user email/phone signup requires code verification; Account API can verify changes to identifiers.

facts.label: Password reset and setting a password
facts.value: Built-in forgot-password email/SMS code flow; custom one-time-email-token reset links also documented.

facts.label: User account settings and deletion
facts.value: Account API/prebuilt UI supports profile/identifier/password/social/MFA settings. End-user deletion is implemented via your backend using Management API.

facts.label: Session model
facts.value: Logto-domain sign-in cookie session, per-user/app grants and app-local tokens/session are separate layers.

facts.label: Session and refresh expiry
facts.value: Default sign-in-session TTL 14 days; default grant TTL 180 days. App refresh-token default 14 days, configurable up to 180 days.

facts.label: Device control and revocation
facts.value: Console, Account API and Management API list/revoke sessions; optional per-app maxAllowedGrants evicts oldest grants.

facts.label: Logout and already-issued tokens
facts.value: Admin session revoke also revokes first-party grants/opaque tokens/refresh tokens; end-session with offline_access can leave app grants valid. Back-channel logout is supported.

facts.label: Incoming business standards
facts.value: SAML and OIDC upstream connectors; domain-based routing; SP- and IdP-initiated enterprise SSO are documented.

facts.label: Outgoing identity-provider roles
facts.value: Logto is an OAuth/OIDC provider and also supports SAML 2.0 IdP applications with assertion signing/encryption and attribute mapping.

facts.label: Customer organization model
facts.value: Organizations group users under one Logto tenant/user pool; users can have memberships/roles in multiple organizations.

facts.label: Organization roles and invitations
facts.value: Native organization template/role/permission APIs, membership management, invitations and JIT provisioning; customer-admin screens are your integration work.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning support
facts.value: No supported native SCIM 2.0 Users/Groups endpoints, sync lifecycle or deactivation SLA was located.

facts.label: Ready-made login UI
facts.value: Logto-hosted redirect signup/signin, social/SSO, code/password/passkey, MFA and reset experiences; same server supplies the experience when self-hosted.

facts.label: Ready-made account UI
facts.value: Prebuilt /account profile/security and identifier/password/passkey/TOTP/backup-code pages; configure enabled fields through Account API.

facts.label: Custom sign-in UI
facts.value: Cloud Pro Bring your UI hosts uploaded SPA assets; self-host commercial license enables the asset-upload feature with your configured storage.

facts.label: Branding controls
facts.value: Brand colors, logos, favicon, dark mode, custom CSS and app/organization branding; hide Powered by Logto on Cloud Pro or a paid self-host license.

facts.label: Custom-domain allowance
facts.value: Cloud Free one custom domain; Pro one included and $48/month bundle for up to 10 total; Dev two; Enterprise beyond that by agreement.

facts.label: Domain migration effects
facts.value: Changing domain requires SDK endpoints and provider callback/ACS updates; passkeys registered under a prior domain may stop working on the new one.

facts.label: Shipped languages and customization

facts.value: No public scoped WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independent accessibility assessment was established.

facts.label: Web framework coverage
facts.value: Official quick-start index includes React, Vue, Angular, Next.js App/Pages Router, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Express, .NET, Go, Python, PHP, Ruby and Java Spring Boot.

facts.label: Authentication versus API runtime
facts.value: SDKs manage OIDC client flows; separate validation guides cover backend JWT verification in Node, Python, Go, Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby and Rust.

facts.label: iOS and Android
facts.value: Official Swift iOS 13+ SDK: v2 system browser/passkeys, v1 embedded WebView/native social plugins. Android API24+: v3 Custom Tabs/passkeys, v2 WebView/native social connectors.

facts.value: Official Expo/React Native guide uses @logto/rn; Flutter SDK supports iOS/Android/web. Index also has Capacitor, Chrome-extension and device-flow guides.

facts.label: Self-host database/runtime
facts.value: PostgreSQL ^14.0 is documented. OSS setup/current upgrade guides say Node.js ^26.0.0, while v1.45.0 root package declares ^22.14.0.

facts.label: Cache, storage and external services
facts.value: Redis 6.0 central cache is optional; object storage enables file uploads and paid custom UI assets. Own email/SMS and external IdPs are separate services.

facts.label: Deployment and sizing
facts.value: Docker/Node deployment and Kubernetes examples; published minimum recommendation: two vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, 256 GiB disk.

facts.label: Upgrade and restore preparation
facts.value: Pin a release, back up PostgreSQL, deploy new-version database alterations once, then replace running instances; pg_dump/provider snapshots are named.

facts.label: Recovery objectives
facts.value: No generic guaranteed OSS recovery-time/recovery-point objective or complete tested disaster-recovery runbook was found.

facts.label: Custom claims and synchronous Actions
facts.value: Custom token-claims callback on Cloud Pro; synchronous JavaScript Actions on Cloud Enterprise or OSS v1.43.0+, at password-migration/post-sign-in points.

facts.label: Webhooks and retries
facts.value: Native asynchronous auth/data-change events; Free one webhook, Pro 10. HTTPS delivery with HMAC-SHA256 signature; documented 5xx retry up to three times.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Console/API create, search, edit, suspend/reactivate, reset/expire passwords, delete users and manage sessions/social connections.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Native subject-token/token-exchange APIs on Cloud Pro; developer implements its authorized support endpoint.

facts.label: Social linking/unlinking
facts.value: Built-in manual signup linking and optional automatic linking on matching email/phone; Account API/prebuilt center can link/unlink social identities.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: No documented persistent anonymous-account upgrade or arbitrary two-user merge flow was found.

facts.label: Password and foundational protections
facts.value: Argon2 password storage; configurable strength/Have I Been Pwned checks; OIDC state/PKCE and session protections.

facts.label: Advanced bot and lockout controls
facts.value: Cloud Pro Advanced security bundle $48/month covers CAPTCHA/lockout/email controls; CAPTCHA supports reCAPTCHA Enterprise or Turnstile.

facts.label: Mandatory message anti-abuse limit
facts.value: System-level cap: 10 email/SMS sends per recipient per rolling 10 minutes, regardless of tenant plan; excess 429 request.message_rate_limited.

facts.label: Cloud API rate limit
facts.value: Default per-tenant token bucket: 200 requests per 10 seconds, approximately 20 sustained requests/second, with bucket-sized bursts.

facts.label: Entity/token caps and self-host capacity
facts.value: Pro starting token cap 10M/month; Dev hard token cap 50k/month. Pro guards can be raised; Enterprise is contract-defined.

facts.label: Audit event scope
facts.value: Native authentication/Experience events include token exchanges, signin/signup/reset, MFA and Actions; Management API and Account API audit coverage is described as not yet available.

facts.label: Audit retention and self-host cleanup
facts.value: Cloud Free three days; Pro 14 days; Enterprise negotiated. Self-host docs tell operators to periodically remove old audit logs.

facts.label: Log extraction
facts.value: Management API GET /api/logs supports filtered pagination for external collection/export.

facts.label: Profile/identifier export route
facts.value: Paginated Management API GET /api/users and per-user reads return profiles, custom data and social identity mappings; includeSsoIdentities includes enterprise identities.

facts.label: Password-hash export
facts.value: GET /api/users/{userId}?includePasswordHash=true returns passwordDigest and passwordAlgorithm in the public Cloud API reference.

facts.label: Other credentials and full migration export
facts.value: A portable export contract for TOTP seeds, WebAuthn credentials/private-provider secrets and every linked relationship, plus a full-export fee/format, was not established.

facts.label: Bulk/hash import
facts.value: Management API user creation imports profiles/custom data and compatible hashes; Argon2, Bcrypt, MD5, SHA1/SHA256 and Legacy formats including PBKDF2/Firebase-scrypt are documented.

facts.label: Preserving user IDs
facts.value: Self-host can supply custom IDs of 1–128 permitted characters; Cloud rejects supplied IDs with 501 request.feature_not_supported.

facts.label: Just-in-time password migration
facts.value: Post first-factor verification Action validates against the old service when local password verification fails, then creates/updates the user and stores a local hash.

facts.label: User and production tenant deletion
facts.value: User deletion is irreversible via Console/Management API. Admin tenant deletion permanently removes associated users/configuration; cancellation alone does not delete it.

facts.label: Development retention
facts.value: Dev-tenant users older than 90 days are automatically deleted; configurations remain. Production Free/Pro/Enterprise are excluded.

facts.label: Controller account retention and service exit
facts.value: Privacy policy retains Account Data during the account and up to 30 days after closure, subject to legal/business/security exceptions. DPA promises deletion/return of Customer Data at termination.

facts.label: Backup purge and exact end-user deadlines
facts.value: A numeric hosted identity-backup purge schedule or fixed DPA completion deadline after deleting a production tenant was not found.

facts.value: Tenant selection: Europe (Netherlands), West US (Arizona), Australia (Australia East), Japan (Japan East); cannot change an existing tenant's region.

facts.value: Customer Data is stored in the selected region; privacy permits security/support/customer-instructed exceptions. DPA names Azure infrastructure and Cloudflare global edge metadata processing.

facts.value: Public numerical builder-seat/project/domain caps and extra-seat/project prices not found.

facts.label: Multiple websites
facts.value: One app/account can be used across multiple sites, with default redirect and analytics limitations.

facts.label: Managed transactional email
facts.value: Memberstack sends password reset and verification emails; welcome emails are documented at no additional charge.

facts.label: Custom sender and own email provider
facts.value: Verified custom sender domain uses Memberstack's Resend infrastructure. Arbitrary SMTP, SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark or SES connections are explicitly unsupported.

facts.label: Sending quota and usage rates
facts.value: Exact transactional send allowance, overage rate and SMS destination rate not found.

facts.label: Live member threshold behavior
facts.value: Basic/Professional 'up to' limits coexist with automatic upgrade at 100% of the limit; email alerts at 90% and 100%; immediate prorated charge.

facts.label: Avoiding automatic upgrade
facts.value: Contact support before the usage limit to discuss options; vendor may require deleting inactive members or temporarily blocking new signup.

facts.label: Payment transaction fee formula
facts.value: Membership revenue × plan percentage, plus subscription base fee and separate Stripe processing charges. No Memberstack transaction fee if every member is free.

facts.label: Other extra charges
facts.value: No complete public schedule of message, token, log or security overages found.

facts.label: Individual and age eligibility
facts.value: Terms define a customer as an individual or company; account users must be at least 16 or have parent/guardian agreement. Service end users must be at least 13.

facts.label: Countries and restricted markets
facts.value: Complete supported or restricted customer-country list not found.

facts.label: Self-service test access
facts.value: Unlimited-duration test-site trial, no credit card; pay when ready to launch for real members.

facts.label: Evaluation terms qualification
facts.value: General terms default Evaluation Services to 30 days unless an Order says otherwise; pricing advertises an unlimited test trial.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Hosted membership service supplying accounts, login, sessions, member profiles, content gating and Stripe-connected paid memberships.

facts.label: Operational responsibilities
facts.value: Memberstack runs the account service and says it encrypts stored data, forces HTTPS and regularly backs up critical application data offsite.

facts.label: Email and password
facts.value: Built-in email/password signup and login through the DOM package or website forms; all paid tiers advertise the same features.

facts.label: Email passwordless codes
facts.value: Built-in six-digit email code for signup and login; documented code expiry 10 minutes.

facts.label: Other basic methods
facts.value: Current native email-link login, phone/SMS login, anonymous accounts and wallet login not established.

facts.label: Current provider catalog
facts.value: Google, Facebook, LinkedIn, GitHub, Spotify and Dribbble are the documented native social providers.

facts.label: Google setup
facts.value: Quick Setup uses Memberstack's Google credentials; Custom Setup accepts the builder's Google client ID/secret.

facts.label: Microsoft and unsupported providers
facts.value: Microsoft guide is deprecated; a separate unsupported-provider guide explicitly lists Twitter as unsupported and documents Microsoft/Webflow limitations.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: Native passkey/WebAuthn login, enrollment, fallback, autofill and domain-migration behavior not found.

facts.label: App-user MFA and recovery
facts.value: End-user TOTP, SMS/email second factor, passkey/security-key MFA and recovery codes not established.

facts.label: Developer dashboard MFA
facts.value: Authenticator-app TOTP and single-use backup codes; app owner can require 2FA for dashboard team members.

facts.label: Verify email
facts.value: Built-in email verification uses a link, with configurable strict or lenient access behavior and resend action.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Built-in reset sends a six-digit code; prebuilt modal handles the flow, custom Webflow forms require a reset-code form.

facts.label: Change email and password
facts.value: Profile forms support email change and password updates; prebuilt profile UI is also available.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: Opt-in self-service deletion in profile modal or custom attributes; disabled by default. Deletes the account, logs it out and cancels recurring subscriptions.

facts.label: Session storage and logout
facts.value: localStorage by default, optional cookie storage and root-domain cookie setting; DOM logout and auth-change listener are documented.

facts.label: Session duration
facts.value: Configurable inactivity expiry in days; minimum 1 day. Shorter inactivity logout needs linked custom code.

facts.label: Multiple logins and revocation
facts.value: Concurrent logins enabled by default; an optional setting makes the newest login invalidate older instances.

facts.label: Per-device session administration
facts.value: Named-device list, selective remote device revocation, token lifetime guarantees and immediate invalidation of already-issued JWTs not found.

facts.label: OIDC provider role
facts.value: Memberstack is the OpenID Connect identity provider for connected relying-party applications; discovery and openid/email/profile scopes are documented.

facts.label: Incoming federation role
facts.value: Memberstack explicitly does not accept external identity providers such as Auth0 or Okta.

facts.label: Customer team membership and invitations
facts.value: Team owner shares an invite link; new users sign up and existing signed-in users join. Owner can view/remove members and upgrade.

facts.label: Permissions and security boundary
facts.value: Plan-based permissions can be checked in backend tokens; content access must be enforced on the backend for sensitive resources.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: SCIM 2.0 user/group provisioning, deactivation, supported directories and price not found.

facts.label: Prebuilt screens
facts.value: Embedded login, signup, profile/security/team/subscription UI and forgot/reset-password modals; custom/headless DOM flows also supported.

facts.label: Hosted SSO page
facts.value: Vendor-hosted login screen is used for outgoing SSO; custom login subdomain can be configured.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Any paid plan can configure custom social-auth and SSO domains using the supplied CNAME records and updated header script.

facts.label: Email and UI customization
facts.value: Branded emails are included on all standard paid tiers; custom website UI can use Memberstack attributes and components.

facts.label: Translation
facts.value: Dashboard Translations covers errors and hosted SSO pages; prebuilt modals require a window.memberstackTranslations object before the installation script.

facts.label: Accessibility assurance
facts.value: Public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or tested accessibility guarantee not found.

facts.label: Web client integrations
facts.value: Official integration guidance covers Webflow, WordPress plugin and custom HTML/JS, including React, Next.js, Vue and Svelte through @memberstack/dom.

facts.label: Browser/server separation
facts.value: DOM package runs in the browser; Next.js examples need client components. Server-side Node Admin SDK and REST endpoints are separate.

facts.label: Backend runtime
facts.value: Admin SDK guidance includes Express, Next.js API routes and serverless AWS Lambda/Vercel; REST can be called from other backends.

facts.label: Native/mobile clients
facts.value: Vendor says mobile social login can use its JavaScript API; its packages are JS based and native code without JavaScript is not compatible.

facts.label: Website prerequisites
facts.value: Website must allow custom JavaScript in its head and the necessary HTML data attributes, or use custom JS integration.

facts.label: Payment and mail dependencies
facts.value: Stripe is the payment processor for memberships; default mail is Memberstack managed.

facts.label: Self-host operation
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented standard hosted service; no public supported installable Memberstack account server, sizing or backup/restore runbook established.

facts.label: Custom member data
facts.value: Custom fields, backend-controlled metadata, per-member JSON and DataTables. Maximum 100 custom fields/project; JSON limit 1 MB/member.

facts.label: Webhooks and delivery
facts.value: Signed Svix-powered HTTP webhooks cover member create/update/delete, plan changes and team member additions/removals.

facts.label: Team event/API limits
facts.value: No dedicated Teams API or team.created event; documented workarounds use member plan connections and team.member.added/removed webhooks.

facts.label: User management API
facts.value: Server Admin SDK supports paginated list/retrieve/create/update/delete and member-plan operations; list defaults to 50 and max 100 records/page.

facts.label: Dashboard impersonation
facts.value: Login as Member opens the chosen member's redirect on an app domain; admin/member can both remain logged in despite the no-concurrent-login setting.

facts.label: Server verification
facts.value: Admin verifyToken validates a JWT; guide recommends app audience validation. Webhook signature verification is also documented.

facts.label: Link and unlink providers
facts.value: Signed-in members can connect/disconnect supported social providers and add a password through profile UI or DOM methods.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and automatic merges
facts.value: Native anonymous-to-registered upgrade, safe cross-account merge rules and same-email auto-link behavior not established.

facts.label: Disposable email blocking
facts.value: Enabled by default for known disposable email domains; can be disabled in Application Settings.

facts.label: Bot check
facts.value: Optional hCaptcha during signup; requires adding the CAPTCHA element for custom Webflow signup forms and enabling the dashboard setting.

facts.label: Enumeration and other abuse controls
facts.value: Forgot-password form always returns success for unrecognized addresses. Published leaked-password screening and default per-account login lockout thresholds not found.

facts.label: Admin API limit
facts.value: 25 requests/second for Memberstack Admin package; REST guide also documents 25 requests/second, HTTP 429 and exponential-backoff recovery.

facts.label: DataTables limit
facts.value: DataTables guide: create 10/minute, read 25/second, write 30/minute and global 200 requests/30 seconds.

facts.label: Authentication endpoint quotas
facts.value: Exact signup/login/passwordless/resend per-IP/per-account request windows and paid higher-rate pricing not found.

facts.label: Member events
facts.value: Dashboard Event Log supports member/event/source filtering and event details. Sources include DASHBOARD, STRIPE, PACKAGE, ADMIN_API, PLAN_LOGIC, ZAPIER and MAKE.

facts.label: Administrative logs
facts.value: App Access Logs retain data for two weeks and record IP, name, email and activity hour. App Events cover admin membership, owner, domain, Stripe and bulk deletion changes.

facts.label: Member event retention/export
facts.value: Fixed member-event retention, complete historical audit CSV export and paid retention tiers not found.

facts.label: Profile and plan export
facts.value: Self-service members/plans CSV; can filter by plan/status. Member export includes email, Stripe customer ID, custom fields and plan/price data.

facts.label: DataTable export
facts.value: DataTables gained a direct whole-table CSV export on September 22, 2026.

facts.label: Credential portability
facts.value: Current 2.0 password-hash export, OAuth token/credential export, hash algorithm, fee and support-assisted credential export not found.

facts.label: CSV migration
facts.value: Bulk import up to 10,000 rows with required email, optional password/hashed password, recommended member ID and custom/profile/plan/JSON/metadata columns.

facts.label: Paid member migration conditions
facts.value: Paying-member import requires Stripe customer ID and, for recurring plans, subscription ID. One subscription is imported initially; Sync with Stripe adds others.

facts.label: App closure
facts.value: Delete all plans, disconnect Stripe, then Delete App in Danger Zone; guide says app/member data deletion is permanent and irreversible.

facts.label: Deleted member recovery
facts.value: Vendor says it does not retain backups of deleted member information; recommends customer CSV exports to prevent accidental loss.

facts.label: Legal retention
facts.value: DPA says securely delete client personal data after service end under its retention schedule, subject to law; Appendix A uses agreement term unless law requires otherwise.

facts.label: Log/backup purge deadlines
facts.value: Numerical deletion deadlines for every backup, operational log and account record not found.

facts.label: Trial inactivity and export loss
facts.value: Terms allow no-cost accounts and data to be deleted without notice after more than two consecutive months of non-use; suspension/termination immediately removes export access.

facts.label: Hosted customer data location
facts.value: Vendor TIA states customer data storage is in the United States of America.

facts.label: Other processing and choice of region
facts.value: Privacy policy permits processing in the US or elsewhere and storage with hosting providers; selectable residency and detailed backup/log geography not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Public DPA and transfer clauses
facts.value: Public processor DPA incorporates EU controller-to-processor SCCs and UK transfer addendum; breach notice without undue delay; annual compliance information on written request at customer cost.

facts.label: US processing addendum
facts.value: Public US DPA addresses CCPA service-provider processing; using the service accepts it; signed copy can be requested by email.

facts.label: SOC 2 evidence
facts.value: Security overview claims SOC 2 certification and links a report download.

facts.label: Subprocessor list retrieval
facts.value: Privacy policy links https://www.memberstack.com/legal/sub-processors, but list could not be read.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Memberstack; Memberstack, Inc., a Delaware company. Official site https://www.memberstack.com/; developer docs https://developers.memberstack.com/; help centre https://docs.memberstack.com/.

facts.label: Earlier name
facts.value: Authramp was the name used during July 2018 development; Memberstack publicly launched in March 2019.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Active public product, pricing and self-service entry. Signup and production activation were not tested.

facts.label: Deprecated client packages
facts.value: Dedicated React and Next.js packages are deprecated for new projects; existing implementations remain available. Use @memberstack/dom for new projects.

facts.label: Deprecated provider guide
facts.value: The Microsoft Authentication guide is explicitly labelled Deprecated.

facts.label: Hosted service rights
facts.value: Proprietary hosted service; terms grant a nonexclusive, nontransferable, revocable worldwide right to use it with end users.

facts.label: DOM package license
facts.value: @memberstack/dom 2.1.0 vendor-published package metadata declares MIT.

facts.label: Admin package license
facts.value: @memberstack/admin 1.7.0 vendor-published package metadata declares MIT.

facts.label: Public status
facts.value: Public component status page at https://status.memberstack.com/.

facts.label: Availability terms
facts.value: Terms promise commercially reasonable efforts for 24/7 availability, with planned-downtime and external-event exclusions.

facts.label: Numerical SLA
facts.value: Public percentage uptime commitment, measurement period, claim procedure and credits not found.

facts.label: DOM release evidence
facts.value: @memberstack/dom latest package tag was 2.1.0, published 2026-11-03T16:57:04.332Z.

facts.label: Admin release evidence
facts.value: @memberstack/admin latest package tag was 1.7.0, published 2026-09-16T14:38:56.736Z.

facts.label: Hosted maintenance and support window
facts.value: Official changelog includes September 22, 2026 table-export and billing fixes; formal SDK LTS/end-of-support matrix not found.

facts.label: Support channels and response target
facts.value: Help centre, Rey AI assistant, support ticket/email and Slack community; vendor aims to answer within 24 hours during workweek, weekends off.

facts.label: Premium support commercial terms
facts.value: Terms allow purchased upgraded support through an Order; public premium-support price and binding response/resolution SLA not found.

apps.name: Microsoft Entra External ID
apps.line: Microsoft hosted customer identity service for app login.

free.text: Basic includes first 50,000 MAU each month

cells.freeUsers: 50,000 MAU/month on Basic
cells.sso: SAML/OIDC available; connection pricing not published

mau.math: Users above the 50,000 included cost $0.03 each. With 1,000 users, none are above it, so the cost is $0 a month.
Users above the 50,000 included cost $0.03 each. With 10,000 users, none are above it, so the cost is $0 a month.
With one active builder, there are 50,001 users, and the one user above the 50,000 included is billed at $0.03. That totals $0.03 a month. With no active builder, the total is $0.
With one active builder, there are 100,001 users, and the users above the 50,000 included are billed at $0.03 each. That totals $1,500.03 a month. With no active builder, the total is $1,500.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signup, major paid-feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found for Microsoft Entra External ID.

facts.label: User billing definition and aggregation
facts.value: Basic MAU counts unique users authenticating in a calendar month; usage from workforce/external tenants linked to one subscription is combined.

facts.label: Admins are also metered
facts.value: All users in an external tenant can count, including admins with directory roles, irrespective of UserType.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Basic: first 50,000 MAU per month free under the subscription's aggregation rules; add-ons do not inherit that free tier.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Basic is usage-based above its allowance; public pay-as-you-go entry has no upfront commitment. Add-ons/support/other resources can incur separate charges.

facts.label: Current Basic rate
facts.value: Global USD retail: first 50,000 Basic MAU at $0; subsequent MAU at $0.03 per user/month. API effectiveStartDate: 2025-07-01.

facts.label: Distinct older Core meter
facts.value: API also returns a separately named Core meter at USD $0.01625 above 50,000, effectiveStartDate 2025-05-01; new Basic eligibility for that meter was not established.

facts.label: Business calculations
facts.value: Full A/B totals not established for a packaged customer-organization product; app-owned membership/invitation logic remains necessary.

facts.label: Customer organization limits/fees
facts.value: No packaged SaaS customer-organization/member/invitation tariff or organization-object limits located for the external-tenant customer app.

facts.label: Enterprise federation and tariff scope
facts.value: Custom OIDC and SAML/WS-Fed customer federation are documented. No separate per-connection setup/active-connection rate located in the public Basic/add-on rate card.

facts.label: SCIM license/fee precision
facts.value: Outbound SCIM support is documented for standard-mode tenants; a customer-tenant SCIM-specific license/add-on fee and inbound directory connection quote were not established.

facts.label: Tenant and directory object caps
facts.value: 20 external tenants/subscription. Default 300,000 objects per non-trial tenant; increase via Support. Trial: 10,000 objects, not extendable.

facts.label: Application and builder distinctions
facts.value: 100 redirect URLs/application and one sign-out URL/application. Builders use admin roles; an active builder can count in MAU rather than an unrelated customer seat allowance.

facts.label: Default email and custom sender
facts.value: Built-in email OTP/verification/reset flows exist; OnOtpSend can use an app-owned REST API and Azure Communication Services or SendGrid for custom email.

facts.label: Default email allowance and optional sender bill
facts.value: A complete default-email send allowance/overage tariff was not located.

facts.label: SMS verification rates
facts.value: USD/attempt: Low Cost $0.03; Mid Low $0.07; Mid High $0.15; High $0.35. Retail meter effectiveStartDate: 2024-11-01.

facts.label: Overages and service limits
facts.value: Basic usage over the free threshold is metered; auth requests, directory capacity and SMS have independent quotas/throttles.

facts.label: Hard monetary stop
facts.value: No External ID-specific automatic dollar spending cap, grace period or forced feature upgrade policy located.

facts.label: M2M add-on
facts.value: Global USD $0.001 per M2M Authentication Token; API effectiveStartDate 2025-11-01. Transaction-based, separate from interactive MAU; no add-on free tier.

facts.label: Go-Local and other infrastructure
facts.value: Go-Local: Global USD $0.02/MAU/month, effectiveStartDate 2025-09-01, with no add-on free tier. Proxies, REST APIs, monitoring and support are separate resources.

facts.label: Individual signup eligibility
facts.value: Public Azure subscription agreement explicitly allows an individual subscriber. Account setup accepts a Microsoft/GitHub account, phone and qualifying card.

facts.label: Complete builder-country coverage
facts.value: A complete External ID-specific allowed/restricted builder-country list was not established.

facts.label: Self-service paid/production path
facts.value: Create an external tenant in the admin center and link an Azure subscription for billing; suitable roles/permissions are required.

facts.label: Trial versus ongoing free use
facts.value: First-time setup can offer a 30-day external-tenant trial without an Azure subscription. Production/billing linkage is distinct from that trial and Azure promotional credit.

facts.label: Customer-tenant scope
facts.value: Hosted customer directory, account registration, authentication, verification, tokens, federation and user management for registered apps.

facts.label: Workforce versus external configuration
facts.value: Workforce tenants support employee/guest collaboration; external tenants support consumer and business-customer apps with different capabilities.

facts.label: Operating responsibilities
facts.value: Microsoft operates hosted identity infrastructure; builder registers apps, configures policies/permissions and operates app code, native UI, optional REST extensions and log destinations.

facts.label: Local first-factor methods
facts.value: Email/password and email OTP; username/password aliases are also documented. First-factor SMS is currently unsupported in external tenants.

facts.label: Other primary methods
facts.value: Native email magic-link, anonymous user accounts and wallet sign-in were not established.

facts.label: Social and compatible identity providers
facts.value: Named social: Google, Facebook and Apple. Microsoft Entra federation, custom OIDC and SAML/WS-Fed are documented; personal Microsoft account appears in the feature list via OIDC.

facts.label: Native social-login documentation conflict
facts.value: Authentication-approach table says native supports Apple/Facebook/Google via a browser step; identity-provider overview says federation is browser-delegated only and native supports local accounts only.

facts.label: Passkeys: price and roles
facts.value: Passkeys have no extra authentication fee in External ID tiers; available as passwordless first factor satisfying MFA, or as MFA after a password.

facts.label: Passkeys: clients and recovery
facts.value: WebAuthn browser/device required; embedded WebView/WKWebView not supported. Device-bound and synced credentials are documented; fallback can use password plus another MFA method.

facts.label: MFA factors and gates
facts.value: Customer-tenant factors: email OTP, paid SMS and passkey FIDO2. Conditional Access can require MFA; the same email OTP cannot be both first and second factor.

facts.label: Recovery codes and authenticator TOTP
facts.value: Native customer-tenant TOTP-authenticator enrollment and printable recovery codes not established.

facts.label: Verification and self-service reset
facts.value: Local user flows verify email through OTP; self-service password reset supports email OTP and configured SMS. SMS reset requires a registered phone method.

facts.label: Post-signup profile and user deletion
facts.value: Admin/Graph user update and deletion exist; no complete hosted end-user profile/change-contact/self-delete center established.

facts.label: Token default lifetimes
facts.value: Microsoft identity-platform defaults: access tokens usually 60 to 90 minutes; refresh tokens 24 hours for SPA redirects and email-OTP flows, 90 days in other documented scenarios.

facts.label: Revocation and session controls
facts.value: External-tenant feature table supports admin refresh/session revocation. Existing self-contained access tokens can remain usable to expiry; upstream federation sessions need their own logout.

facts.label: Upstream enterprise federation
facts.value: External tenant acts as relying party/service provider for custom OIDC or SAML/WS-Fed identity providers; issues tokens for the app after successful upstream authentication.

facts.label: Downstream app protocols
facts.value: Customer app integration supports OIDC/OAuth2; SAML relying-party apps are also documented through Enterprise applications.

facts.label: Groups and application roles
facts.value: Create/manage security groups; assign app roles to users; group-to-role and group claims assignments have documented Microsoft Graph paths.

facts.label: Customer invitation conflict
facts.value: October 15, 2026 invitation guide explicitly allows consumers/business customers; feature comparison says invited external-tenant users are for administrative purposes only and incompatible with customer user flows.

facts.label: Organization isolation model
facts.value: No native packaged customer-organization entity or tenant-scoped membership/role administration workflow established.

facts.label: SCIM outbound: standard mode
facts.value: Current docs support outbound SCIM 2.0 user provisioning from external tenants to supported apps in standard mode, including change-based synchronization.

facts.label: SCIM outbound: HSC mode
facts.value: HSC mode does not support SCIM outbound user provisioning or directory delta/advanced queries, per the external-tenant limits table.

facts.label: Customer inbound SCIM details
facts.value: A turnkey inbound SCIM directory connection for each SaaS customer, with external-tenant-specific users/groups/offboarding and pricing, was not established.

facts.label: Hosted login screens
facts.value: Browser-delegated user flows provide hosted signup/sign-in and configured password reset/MFA; flow defines local/provider methods and collected attributes.

facts.label: Native authentication UI
facts.value: MSAL/native authentication APIs let the builder implement local-account screens in the app; browser fallback may be needed for unsupported scenarios.

facts.label: Hosted branding
facts.value: Neutral default branding; customize images, layout, header/footer, form text, links and CSS.

facts.label: Custom domains and costs
facts.value: Verified custom URL domains can replace ciamlogin.com endpoints through a reverse proxy such as Azure Front Door; multiple domains are possible within service limits.

facts.label: Hosted language list
facts.value: Arabic (Saudi Arabia); Basque; Bulgarian; Catalan; Chinese (China/Hong Kong SAR); Croatian; Czech; Danish; Dutch; English (US); Estonian; Finnish; French; Galician; German; Greek; Hebrew; Hungarian; Italian; Japanese; Kazakh; Korean; Latvian; Lithuanian; Norwegian Bokmål; Polish; Portuguese (Brazil/Portugal); Romanian; Russian; Serbian (Latin); Slovak; Slovenian; Spanish; Swedish; Thai; Turkish; Ukrainian.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A public External ID hosted/customer-login-specific accessibility conformance report and exact WCAG level/version were not located.

facts.label: Official web/server integration
facts.value: MSAL and customer samples cover JavaScript, React, Angular, Node.js/Express, ASP.NET Core, Python and Java, with browser-delegated OIDC flows.

facts.label: Mobile and desktop clients
facts.value: Official guides include Android Kotlin/Java, iOS/macOS Swift/Objective-C, .NET MAUI/WPF and Electron; native UI paths differ from browser-delegated redirects.

facts.label: React Native and Flutter precision
facts.value: First-party customer-tenant React Native/Flutter SDK feature/version coverage was not established in the checked MSAL and customer sample lists.

facts.label: Prerequisites and dependencies
facts.value: External tenant, app registration, user flow and required permissions; linked Azure subscription for production billing. Customer identity storage is managed, with no builder database needed just for the directory.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: Not applicable to the managed External ID service; client libraries and custom extension infrastructure do not provide a customer-run identity server edition.

facts.label: Extension events and attributes
facts.value: REST-backed custom extensions support token claims, browser-flow attribute collection and custom OTP sending; JIT password migration has an OnPasswordSubmit event.

facts.label: Extension execution limits
facts.value: Reference limits: 100 custom extensions, 2,000 ms maximum timeout, one retry and 50 combined extension requests/second/tenant.

facts.label: Admin and Graph operations
facts.value: Create, read, update, reset passwords, disable/block and delete customer users via admin/Graph paths; security group/app-role operations have documented permissions.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Packaged audited support-agent impersonation/act-as-user feature not established.

facts.label: Local identities and API updates
facts.value: Admin account creation supports multiple email identities; Graph's identities collection can represent multiple sign-in identities and updates replace the collection.

facts.label: Social linking and guest conversion
facts.value: Ready-made verified end-user link/unlink/merge and anonymous-to-registered app-data upgrade flows were not established.

facts.label: Built-in security and optional defenses
facts.value: Smart lockout/common network protections are documented as enabled by default; custom risk logic, WAF and bot defenses require configuration/integrations.

facts.label: Advanced controls scope
facts.value: Comparison lists global/custom banned password protection and customer Conditional Access/MFA; workforce Identity Protection and ID Governance are unavailable in external tenants.

facts.label: Authentication request quotas
facts.value: External tenant: 200 requests/second total; 20/second per IP/tenant. Trial: 20/second total. Token, discovery, keys and logout endpoints each consume requests.

facts.label: SMS throttles
facts.value: Per phone: 15 texts/15 minutes, 20/hour, 30/day and 50/week. Per tenant: 500/15 minutes, 1,500/hour and 5,000/day.

facts.label: Log types and retention conflict
facts.value: Audit/sign-in logs are available. Basic retention is seven days in the retention/comparison docs, while the External ID operations guide states 30 days.

facts.label: Exports and previews
facts.value: Diagnostic settings/Azure Monitor can route external-tenant logs to storage/analytics; the comparison labels Azure Monitor external integration and signup logs preview.

facts.label: Profile export
facts.value: Graph List users supports profile export with selected attributes/pagination; general Entra portal guide documents a user-profile CSV download.

facts.label: Credential export
facts.value: No public customer-tenant password-hash, passkey credential or MFA-secret export procedure established.

facts.label: Bulk migration and IDs
facts.value: Create destination customer accounts with attributes through Graph; current migration guidance supports legacy identity providers, including B2C.

facts.label: Password-preserving migration
facts.value: JIT OnPasswordSubmit extension validates against the legacy IdP using an encrypted password payload; legacy-initiated credential capture or password reset are other documented paths.

facts.label: Individual account deletion
facts.value: Delete user via admin/Graph; soft-deleted accounts can be restored for 30 days, or permanently removed sooner. After the window, irreversible deletion begins.

facts.label: External tenant closure
facts.value: Delete other users and applications, including extension app as required; pass tenant deletion checks, remove remaining flows/resources and delete the tenant.

facts.label: Contract retention after subscription end
facts.value: November 2026 DPA: except free trials/LinkedIn, remaining service Customer Data is retained in a limited-function account for 90 days; deletion follows within an additional 90 days unless retention is authorized.

facts.label: Specific backup purge deadline
facts.value: Final internal backup purge timing after individual customer deletion was not established.

facts.label: Customer directory location
facts.value: Tenant Country/Region choice maps to geo-locations such as North America, EMEA and Asia/Pacific and cannot be changed after creation.

facts.label: Go-Local and cloud scope

facts.label: MSAL JavaScript license

facts.label: Customer feature freshness

facts.label: Included help and paid technical plans
facts.value: Basic Azure billing/subscription and self-help/community routes included. Developer USD $29/month; Standard $100/month; ProDirect $1,000/month on comparison page.
