facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Distinct monthly active users (MAU), counted once in a calendar month; pricing defines authentication at least once, not total registrations or login count.

facts.label: Non-login activity and sharing scope
facts.value: Concept guide also counts token validation/refresh and certain login attempts; cross-project pooled MAU allowance is not established.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Current rate card: $0/month for up to 25,000 MAUs, unlimited total users; email OTP, magic links, Google and Facebook.

facts.label: Free allowance disagreement
facts.value: Pricing says 25,000 MAUs; general documentation FAQ says 1,000 MAUs.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Business Pro starts at $150/month with a 2,500-MAU selected tier; normal subscriptions billed monthly on the subscription anniversary.

facts.label: Annual and Enterprise commitments
facts.value: Startup/non-profit program advertises 50% off annual billing; other custom annual and Enterprise terms arranged through sales.

facts.label: Overage and larger volumes
facts.value: Pricing: $0.06 per MAU above the chosen tier; above 100,000 MAUs contact sales. General FAQ instead says prorated overage at the current tier rate.

facts.label: Business calculation basis
facts.value: Two required calculations are below; exact usable totals cannot be established from public evidence.

facts.label: Customer-organization limits and fees
facts.value: Included customer organizations, members per organization, invitation limits and organization charges not published in the checked materials.

facts.label: Business SSO charges
facts.value: Customer-facing SAML/OIDC SSO is a project-level add-on enabled through support; no public connection allowance, per-connection fee or setup fee found.

facts.label: SCIM fees
facts.value: Enterprise SCIM available on request; price, included directories and setup/minimum fees not published.

facts.label: Project and brand scope
facts.value: One subscription initially creates one project; additional projects require support/upgrade; one app/domain/brand per project, with multiple websites allowed for the same brand.

facts.label: Developer dashboard seats
facts.value: Owner, Admin and Developer roles; invited by email; team changes apply across the developer account’s projects. Numerical included seat caps/fees not published.

facts.label: Environments
facts.value: Project guide includes one development and one production environment without separate environment payment; Pro pricing names test/production; Enterprise pricing adds development/staging/production.

facts.label: Default email delivery
facts.value: Default SMTP is for development/testing; numerical send quota depends on project/plan and must be requested from support.

facts.label: Own email sender
facts.value: Custom SMTP and branded sender are included as Business Pro features; configure credentials in Marketplace. External email-provider charges are separate.

facts.label: SMS delivery
facts.value: Phone OTP starts on Business Pro; Twilio integration uses the customer’s SID, auth token and sending number/account.

facts.label: Other delivery channels
facts.value: WhatsApp OTP, HOTP and Mobile Silent Auth are Enterprise methods; channel/carrier costs and included verification/message volumes are quote-only or not published.

facts.label: Usage overflow and spending controls
facts.value: MAU pricing permits tier overages; FAQ says service continues and usage alerts are sent. Exact Free overflow enforcement, spending cap and numeric grace period not established.

facts.label: Sender quota exhaustion
facts.value: Default SMTP quota exhaustion returns HTTP 429 and prevents email OTP/magic-link delivery; other authentication methods continue.

facts.label: Payment, plan changes and cancellation
facts.value: Failed payments retried for a few days, then account may be downgraded/suspended; downgrade next billing cycle; cancellation keeps access to cycle end; no mid-cycle prorated refund.

facts.label: Peak request billing applicability
facts.value: Current pricing is MAU-tier based and publishes no peak-RPS price; concept guide says monthly peak RPS is billed and extra RPS cost $10 each.

facts.label: Project add-ons and other charges
facts.value: Add-on guide lists support-enabled security controls, MFA, SSO, audit logs/event streaming, generally priced per project; current pricing already includes several controls within Pro/Enterprise.

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Website/service user must be at least 18; terms address a natural person using the service.

facts.label: Builder-country eligibility
facts.value: Complete allowed/restricted seller-country and payment-country list not published in the checked materials.

facts.label: Self-service Free and Pro trial
facts.value: Free signup advertised without a credit card; permanent Free plan; 30-day Business Pro trial available from the dashboard.

facts.label: Enterprise entry
facts.value: Private Cloud and tailored enterprise arrangements require contact with sales.

facts.label: Product scope
facts.value: Managed customer identity platform supplying accounts, passwordless and social login, signed tokens/sessions, user administration and enterprise federation.

facts.label: Deployment editions
facts.value: Shared hosted cloud; Enterprise dedicated managed cloud, bring-your-own-cloud, or fully self-managed private/on-premise deployment.

facts.label: Who operates hosted and private editions
facts.value: Shared Cloud is vendor operated; Enterprise can be vendor managed, deployed in the customer’s cloud, or fully customer managed on-premise.

facts.label: Email login methods
facts.value: Magic links and email OTP are built-in Free methods; production delivery capacity has the separate SMTP restriction in F17.

facts.label: Phone and password methods
facts.value: Phone SMS OTP and password login for migration start on Business Pro.

facts.label: Wallet login
facts.value: Official SIWE guide describes Ethereum-wallet integration using frontend wallet libraries plus custom server-side message/signature/nonce validation.

facts.label: Anonymous login
facts.value: A built-in anonymous/guest-account login and its plan were not found.

facts.label: Free social providers
facts.value: Google and Facebook built in on Free; configure the provider application credentials and allowlisted redirect URL.

facts.label: Paid social providers
facts.value: Business Pro adds built-in Apple and generic OIDC providers; product page names GitHub, LinkedIn, Microsoft, X/Twitter, Slack and Discord via OIDC.

facts.label: Passkey methods and plan
facts.value: Business Pro/Enterprise FIDO2/WebAuthn first-factor authentication; hosted/SDK flow supports enrollment and login, with credential list/rename/delete operations.

facts.label: Passkey domains and platforms
facts.value: HTTPS or localhost; IP-address origins unsupported. Product page names Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge, iOS 16+, Android 9+, Windows 10+ and macOS Ventura+.

facts.label: Passkey fallback and recovery
facts.value: Offer another configured login method when passkeys are unavailable; multiple devices and platform passkey sync supported. Detailed conditional-autofill and cross-domain credential migration not published.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Business Pro includes MFA/TOTP; MFA guide names email OTP, SMS OTP, authenticator apps and FIDO2/security-key factors, with optional or enforced policies by group/role.

facts.label: MFA recovery detail
facts.value: Guide mentions fallback email/admin-assisted recovery and says enrollment may provide recovery codes; code count, lifetime, regeneration/revoke APIs and exact plan availability not published.

facts.label: Email/phone verification and address changes
facts.value: Email/phone OTP ownership verification is used to attach or merge an identifier; signed-in user token plus project API key required.

facts.label: Verified-email claim caution
facts.value: Migration guide says email_verified is true when email scope is granted regardless of login method; match an existing account only after email OTP, passkey, or a provider that actually verifies email.

facts.label: Password reset and user deletion flows
facts.value: Error catalogue documents reset verification token/link expiry and reuse errors; full password-reset setup, address-replacement screen and user-initiated delete-account procedure not found.

facts.label: Sessions and token model
facts.value: Signed JWT access/session tokens; refresh tokens supported; OIDC apps configure ID/access/refresh token lifetimes; OIDC ID-token default 3,600 seconds.

facts.label: Logout and revocation
facts.value: OIDC logout endpoint, per-token invalidation and all-device session revocation are documented; user-management dashboard/API advertises session revocation.

facts.label: Client-secret lifecycle
facts.value: Application secret displayed once; rotating it immediately replaces the old secret; disabling an application blocks new authorization/token exchanges.

facts.label: Incoming business SSO
facts.value: SAML 2.0 SP role connecting an external IdP; guide configures Microsoft Entra ID using SP Entity ID, ACS URL, IdP metadata and attribute mapping.

facts.label: Outgoing standards
facts.value: MojoAuth as OIDC provider for client applications; authorization-code and refresh-token grants, PKCE and discovery. Also SAML IdP for downstream service providers.

facts.label: External SSOJet integration scope
facts.value: MojoAuth is the OIDC identity provider; SSOJet is an external client/broker in the integration guide.

facts.label: App-user roles
facts.value: Enterprise RBAC provides roles, permissions and access claims managed through dashboard/API.

facts.label: Customer organization administration
facts.value: Native customer workspaces, membership, invitations, isolation model and customer-admin member-management screens not established.

facts.label: SCIM availability
facts.value: Enterprise SCIM provisioning on request through sales; not self-service in the dashboard.

facts.label: SCIM implementation details
facts.value: SCIM version, supported user/group schemas, deactivation behavior, directory limits and endpoint reference not published in the checked documentation.

facts.label: Hosted and embedded login UI
facts.value: Hosted login/registration page with OIDC redirects; browser SDK can render an embedded passwordless form; custom headless API UI is also documented.

facts.label: Account screens
facts.value: No complete vendor-hosted profile, organization-member or delete-account screen suite established.

facts.label: Branding by plan
facts.value: Free includes hosted login; Business Pro adds branded email, own SMTP and custom domain; Enterprise offers full white-label APIs/flows.

facts.label: Domain setup and session changes
facts.value: Custom domain requires Pro or higher, DNS CNAME/TXT verification and a subdomain; root and wildcard domains unsupported; managed TLS certificates included.

facts.label: Domain-count mapping
facts.value: Guide says one domain per project, but also lists Pro=1, Business=5 and Enterprise=unlimited; current pricing calls the middle plan Business Pro.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Specific guide lists ar, nl, en, ph, fr, de, id, it, pt, ru, es, tr; general FAQ claims 30+ languages including several not in that list.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independent accessibility assessment not found.

facts.label: Web frontend integration
facts.value: Official React browser-SDK guide; Next.js App Router/Pages Router hosted-login guide using NextAuth.js and OIDC.

facts.label: Backend SDKs
facts.value: Official Node.js, Go, Java, PHP and .NET SDK guides; Node sample uses Express, Java uses Maven, .NET package MojoAuth.NET.

facts.label: Runtime/version coverage
facts.value: A complete supported-runtime version matrix and serverless/edge compatibility guarantee not published in the checked SDK pages.

facts.label: iOS and Android clients
facts.value: Official Swift hosted-login guide uses external AppAuth-iOS, Xcode 14+, iOS 13+; Kotlin guide uses AppAuth-Android and Android API 21+.

facts.label: React Native and Flutter clients
facts.value: Official React Native guide uses react-native-app-auth; Flutter guide uses flutter_appauth, Flutter 2.5+/Dart 2.14+ and iOS target 11+.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: MojoAuth project/application credentials, own app frontend/backend and provider configurations; no customer-operated identity database required for shared hosted service.

facts.label: Private deployment dependencies
facts.value: Enterprise on-premise architecture uses PostgreSQL primary/replica, Redis, HAProxy/NGINX and Prometheus/Grafana/ELK monitoring.

facts.label: Self-host deployment and prerequisites
facts.value: Docker Compose for development/testing; production Kubernetes, VM or bare metal; Ubuntu 20.04 LTS/RHEL 8+, Docker 20.10+/containerd 1.4+, Kubernetes 1.24+.

facts.label: Published small-production sizing
facts.value: ‘Up to 10,000 users’ table lists eight servers: app 2×4vCPU/8GB/100GB; DB primary 8/16/500; replica 4/8/500; Redis 2×2/4/50; load balancer 2×2/4/50.

facts.label: Sizing arithmetic disagreement
facts.value: Small-production table claims total 22 vCPU/44GB RAM/1.2TB SSD; its component quantities sum to 28 vCPU/56GB RAM/1,400GB SSD.

facts.label: Backup and upgrade operating detail
facts.value: Guide names off-site backup, monitoring and HA components; exact customer-run restore/runbook, supported upgrade sequence and private release lifecycle not published in checked pages.

facts.label: Custom claims and authentication UI
facts.value: OIDC apps map custom claims/constants and token lifetimes; reserved standard claims cannot be overridden; custom API/UI flows are supported.

facts.label: Webhooks and delivery
facts.value: Dashboard/API webhooks for user.created/updated/deleted, authentication success, passkey registration/login and suspicious activity; HTTPS and HMAC-SHA256 signatures.

facts.label: Webhook retries and secrets
facts.value: Five retries after initial delivery at 10s, 30s, 1m, 5m, 30m; 10s response timeout; 410 Gone not retried; secret rotation accepts old/new secrets for seven days.

facts.label: Arbitrary hooks and execution limits
facts.value: FAQ advertises Actions/Hooks and a rules engine; public hook runtime, trigger schema, timeout, execution quota and current price not found.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: User-management page advertises add/edit/remove users, profiles, login activity and session revocation through dashboard/API.

facts.label: Management API completeness
facts.value: Exact public create/search/ban/delete/impersonation endpoints, privilege controls and action-specific plan gates not established.

facts.label: Linking, merging and unlinking
facts.value: Built-in signed-in account-link request/verify flow; attach new email/phone or merge an existing user; remove identifier and unmerge endpoints documented.

facts.label: Application data and guest upgrades
facts.value: Linking does not migrate app orders/content; app must associate business data with the primary account. Managed anonymous-to-registered upgrade flow not published.

facts.label: Default and paid abuse controls
facts.value: Free basic attack protection; Business Pro enhanced bot/risk detection and MFA; Enterprise adaptive MFA/device fingerprinting.

facts.label: Breached passwords
facts.value: Security guide claims breached-password checks against known compromised hashes, blocking/reset flow and privacy-conscious comparison.

facts.label: SMS abuse thresholds
facts.value: Project add-on guide offers per-user/IP/device request controls; no exact default destination caps, SMS fraud budget or SMS-specific recovery timer found.

facts.label: Published request throttles
facts.value: General FAQ defaults per minute: authentication 100/IP, management 1,000/API key, registration 50/IP, OTP 5/user; Enterprise custom limits/burst capacity.

facts.label: Limit errors and burst billing scope
facts.value: Error 1003 means too many requests; default SMTP separately produces HTTP 429. Current tier-specific RPS allowances, concurrency, Retry-After and reset-window details not published.

facts.label: Audit events and streaming
facts.value: Login/user/passkey/security webhooks and delivery logs documented; project-level audit/event-streaming add-on available through support.

facts.label: Audit retention and pricing
facts.value: Enterprise DPA commits to immutable audit logs for at least 12 months; Free/Pro auth-event and webhook-delivery retention, export caps and streaming fees not published.

facts.label: Profile export
facts.value: FAQ advertises full user-data export through dashboard/API in JSON, CSV or custom format, including bulk and scheduled export.

facts.label: Credential and relationship export
facts.value: Password hashes, WebAuthn credentials/credential IDs and linked-account relationship export schema, self-service procedure and fees not published.

facts.label: Leaving and domain portability
facts.value: Subscription agreement allows Customer Data retrieval for 30 days after termination; Enterprise DPA permits a machine-readable personal-data export request within 30 days.

facts.label: Documented migration route
facts.value: Specific migration guide: no self-service CSV/dashboard import or user/hash import API; contact support for bulk transfer. Recommended path verifies email then matches an existing application database record.

facts.label: Import and hash disagreement
facts.value: Password product page says existing hashes such as bcrypt can be imported; FAQ/user-management page advertise bulk/JIT/API import; detailed migration guide says no self-service import/API.

facts.label: Passwordless migration and passkey enrollment
facts.value: Guide recommends one-time email OTP proof then matching verified email; passkey enrollment offered after OTP when enabled; magic-link login skips that offer.

facts.label: User deletion and data subject requests
facts.value: Administrator remove-user operation advertised; privacy policy permits correction/erasure requests by contact, with lawful/business retention exceptions.

facts.label: Post-cancellation retention
facts.value: General FAQ: 30-day export/reactivation period and deletion after 90 days. Enterprise DPA: after 30-day export window, securely delete personal data, copies/backups/archives unless law requires retention.

facts.label: Backups and log retention
facts.value: FAQ claims hourly snapshots retained 30 days; Enterprise DPA requires immutable audit logs retained at least 12 months.

facts.label: Shared-cloud data location
facts.value: Enterprise overview advertises multi-tenant AWS hosting with US/EU/Asia-Pacific data residency; DPA names AWS US as primary with additional enterprise regions.

facts.label: Private location choices
facts.value: Enterprise private deployment can use a chosen cloud region or customer’s on-premise environment; managed, BYOC and fully self-managed models documented.

facts.label: Residency scope and price
facts.value: Free/Pro region-selection procedure/fees and an exact location matrix for logs, backups and failover not published.

facts.label: DPA eligibility
facts.value: DPA effective 2025-02-01 is expressly for Enterprise customers and offers countersignature through sales; FAQ says DPA available for all customers.

facts.label: Subprocessors and transfer provisions
facts.value: DPA names AWS hosting, Cloudflare global DNS/security edge and Stripe billing; says Stripe does not process end-user authentication data; SCC Module 2/UK addendum and 30-day new-subprocessor notice.

facts.label: Certification disagreement
facts.value: Information-security policy and Enterprise page claim SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification; security-overview doc says the vendor is working towards those certifications.

facts.label: Reports and technical commitments
facts.value: Enterprise DPA offers SOC 2 report, penetration-test summaries/certifications under NDA; describes AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+, and breach notice within 72 hours.

facts.label: Opt-in Zero-Store
facts.value: Enterprise MojoShield Zero-Store enabled per project through support keeps email/phone PII off vendor persistence; other projects remain independent.

facts.label: Name, owner and official pages
facts.value: MojoAuth; MojoAuth, Inc.; official site mojoauth.com, documentation under /docs/.

facts.label: Lifecycle and entry path
facts.value: Public Free, Business Pro and Enterprise offers remain advertised; no whole-product shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice found in the checked official pages.

facts.label: Service and private-server rights
facts.value: Proprietary service governed by terms and subscription agreement; customer owns Customer Data, supplier retains the service and its intellectual property.

facts.label: Official Node.js SDK license
facts.value: MIT; use, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale permitted with the copyright/permission notice and warranty disclaimer.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Public status page at status.mojoauth.com lists API/console/JavaScript service components and incident history.

facts.label: Availability promises
facts.value: Free: no SLA; Business Pro 99.9% monthly; Enterprise 99.99% monthly. SLA effective 2025-02-01 excludes scheduled maintenance, customer problems, force majeure, beta and non-production services.

facts.label: Service credits
facts.value: SLA credits range 10%/25%/50% at specified uptime bands; written claim within 30 days of incident; approved credit applied to next invoice.

facts.label: Checked code version and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Official node-sdk main package version 1.4.3; repository not archived; latest listed commit bd7eebf0891b1283f191d6c3f8bc7b1a3c39aceb dated 2025-01-25T04:42:01Z.

facts.label: Release/support policy
facts.value: Node repository releases endpoint returns an empty list; no complete supported-SDK/private-server version or vulnerability-patch schedule found. Support terms promise deprecated features 12 months after notice unless otherwise stated.

facts.label: Standard support
facts.value: Current support terms: Free and Pro below 50,000 MAU get email, M–F 09:00–17:00 PST excluding holidays, 24-hour initial response, two authorized contacts.

facts.label: Premium and Enterprise support
facts.value: Pro at 50,000+ MAU includes 12-hour Premium response and five authorized contacts; Enterprise 24/7/365, one-hour critical/four-hour high response and account manager.

facts.label: Free-support eligibility disagreement
facts.value: Current support terms list Free under Standard, yet their customer-responsibility clause still requires a paid subscription to receive support.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, merger, product shutdown, rebrand, pivot, signups closure, major paid-feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found.

facts.label: Monthly active user definition
facts.value: MAU means a unique user authenticating at least once during a billing cycle; monthly plan allowance is 50,000 MAUs.

facts.label: Aggregation and counting precision
facts.value: Cross-application/tenant/environment pooling, billing-cycle timezone and treatment of linked/duplicate identities were not established.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Free: $0, 50,000 MAUs/month, 5,000 M2M tokens/month, 25 SMS/month, five applications, three API resources, two groups and three-day audit retention.

facts.label: Minimum paid public plan
facts.value: Pro: $24.99 per month, including 50,000 MAUs and 5,000 M2M tokens; add-ons are optional and priced separately.

facts.label: Billing, cancellation and failed payment
facts.value: Subscriptions bill in advance, recur automatically, and renewal can be cancelled through account management or support; failed automatic billing can terminate access immediately.

facts.label: Pro MAU and M2M formula
facts.value: Pro monthly base $24.99 + $0.015 × max(MAU − 50,000, 0) + $0.0008 × max(M2M tokens − 5,000, 0), before optional add-ons/messages.

facts.label: ScaleX add-on
facts.value: $99.99/month: token introspection, opaque/session-bound tokens, long-lived sessions/refresh tokens, application group restrictions and Google Analytics.

facts.label: Secure+ add-on
facts.value: $99.99/month: consent/user-grant management, back-channel sign-out, JAR/PAR and audit retention extendable to 30 days.

facts.label: mTLSConnect add-on
facts.value: $199.99/month includes 25,000 mTLS tokens, 10,000 OCSP validations and one trust store. Extra mTLS token $0.002; extra OCSP check $0.003; extra trust store $99.99/month.

facts.label: Workload Identity add-on
facts.value: $24.99/month for SPIFFE X.509-SVID/JWT-SVID authentication and one SPIFFE trust store; additional trust store $24.99/month.

facts.label: Business comparison result
facts.value: Exact prices for A (1k users/10 organizations/one SAML connection) and B (10k users/100 organizations/10 SAML connections) cannot be established.

facts.label: Customer organization offer
facts.value: B2B page advertises customer organizations with separate users, settings, roles and SSO, plus customer IT self-service.

facts.label: Organization and invitation limits/pricing
facts.value: Per-organization/member caps, active-organization definition, invitation workflow/expiry/quotas and plan-specific organization fees were not located.

facts.label: SSO and directory connection fees
facts.value: SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM are advertised; no included connection count, per-connection rate, minimum, setup fee or SCIM price was found.

facts.label: Free versus Pro builder resources
facts.value: Free: five applications, three APIs, one tenant API key, two client secrets per app. Pro: unlimited applications/APIs, up to three tenant API keys and 50 client secrets per app.

facts.label: Seats, projects and environments
facts.value: Dashboard collaborator seats, extra tenant/environment allowances, environment isolation and tenant/custom-domain quantity prices were not established.

facts.label: Email provider responsibility
facts.value: Free and Pro can use a custom email provider; public schema supports MonoCloud delivery or SendGrid and a tenant-specific sender address.

facts.label: SMS allowance and paid delivery
facts.value: Free allows 25 SMS/month. Pro includes 25 SMS/month then charges market rate or permits own SMS provider; schema identifies MonoCloud/Twilio.

facts.label: Overage and Free-limit behavior
facts.value: Pricing says usage beyond included limits is billed per unit; exact Free-to-Pro activation, MAU exhaustion grace/shutdown and user-configurable spend caps were not established.

facts.label: Feature-cap enforcement
facts.value: Creating more than two groups requires Pro; session-management endpoints require Pro and document HTTP 402 Payment Required.

facts.label: Other cost drivers
facts.value: M2M issuance, optional mTLS tokens/OCSP/trust stores, optional SPIFFE trust stores, SMS delivery and optional ScaleX/Secure+ charges are separate from MAUs.

facts.label: Individual account eligibility
facts.value: Terms permit use by individuals aged at least 18 who can enter the agreement; registration details must be accurate.

facts.label: Seller-country eligibility
facts.value: No complete supported/prohibited builder-country list was located.

facts.label: Free self-service entry and card
facts.value: Free forever entry, no credit card, and production-ready authentication are explicitly advertised; docs give dashboard-based application creation.

facts.label: Optional trial conditions
facts.value: Terms allow discretionary time-limited trials, may require billing details, and may charge the chosen subscription when a trial expires unless cancelled.

facts.label: Product type and account scope
facts.value: Hosted identity/authentication platform with accounts, hosted login, passwordless methods, sessions, user administration and OAuth/OIDC API protection.

facts.label: Who operates identity infrastructure
facts.value: Vendor provides the hosted tenant and identity APIs; builder configures applications, redirects, credentials and application/API enforcement.

facts.label: Password and username login
facts.value: Built-in password and unique username authentication are included in Free and Pro.

facts.label: Email magic links and numeric codes
facts.value: Built-in email magic-link and OTP authentication included in Free and Pro; Pro enables code-length/expiry customization.

facts.label: Phone OTP
facts.value: Built-in SMS phone-code sign-in/signup, including optional JIT provisioning; Pro adds code-length/expiry customization and own-provider configuration.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No explicit anonymous account/guest login or crypto-wallet authentication flow was found.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Public authenticator enum lists Google, Apple, Facebook, Microsoft, GitHub, GitLab, Discord, Twitter, LinkedIn and Xero; social login is included in both plans with unlimited social providers.

facts.label: Generic and enterprise providers
facts.value: Schema also defines custom_oidc, custom_enterprise and entra_oidc; OIDC connection config uses discovery URL, PKCE mode, claims mappings and home-realm domains.

facts.label: Passkeys and autofill
facts.value: Built-in first-factor WebAuthn passkeys in Free/Pro; public schema includes sign-in/signup, progressive/device enrollment, identifier-field autocomplete and a passkey button.

facts.label: Fallback and credential scope
facts.value: Product FAQ says synced credentials follow platform sync; unsynced-device loss can use enabled magic link/OTP and enroll another passkey. API returns passkey identifier/public key/AAGUID and backup flags.

facts.label: MFA factor availability
facts.value: Homepage/B2B marketing advertises MFA and per-organization enforcement, but precise native factors, enrollment, step-up, recovery codes and plan gates were not established.

facts.label: Account recovery configuration
facts.value: Email recovery supports link/code/both, expiry, code length and cross-browser settings; phone recovery supports code length/expiry. Passwordless FAQ describes alternative-method recovery.

facts.label: Email and phone verification
facts.value: Native signed, time-bound email verification link can be generated/sent; API can mark email/phone verified or unverified, while signup/login can verify a delivered code.

facts.label: Password reset and address changes
facts.value: Native reset flow can send or return a secure time-bound link; APIs add email addresses and set the primary email used for authentication/recovery.

facts.label: User account deletion
facts.value: DELETE user permanently removes the specified user and is irreversible; a universal ready-made end-user delete-account screen was not established.

facts.label: Session and refresh model
facts.value: Native sessions have sliding/absolute expiry and persistence configuration; browser SDK supports silent iframe restoration and refresh-token renewal with offline_access.

facts.label: Revocation and logout plan gates
facts.value: Pro provides user session management/front-channel logout; Secure+ adds back-channel logout and user-grant revocation. ScaleX adds token/session binding and long-lived controls.

facts.label: Numeric lifetime defaults
facts.value: Exact default access-token/session/refresh lifetimes and complete maximum values per plan were not established.

facts.label: OAuth/OIDC provider and broker roles
facts.value: Hosted platform configures OAuth 2.0/OIDC clients and issues access/ID/refresh tokens; external-provider APIs broker OIDC identities.

facts.label: SAML implementation precision
facts.value: B2B page explicitly advertises SAML SSO with company IdPs; public SAML metadata/certificate setup and complete SP/IdP direction/plan detail were not established.

facts.label: Groups and membership
facts.value: Native groups, user-to-group assignments and application group relationships; Free allows two groups and Pro unlimited groups.

facts.label: Per-organization roles and invitations
facts.value: B2B page claims roles/settings/SSO per customer organization, but detailed isolation/multi-membership, invitation acceptance and delegated customer-admin safeguards were not established.

facts.label: SCIM sync scope
facts.value: B2B marketing says directories add/remove users and synchronize groups. SCIM version, connector provisioning, group schema, suspension/session effects and plan entitlement were not established.

facts.label: Hosted screens and SDK controls
facts.value: Hosted sign-in/signup/reset/verification pages plus Next.js/React sign-in/out controls and auth-state/protection helpers.

facts.label: Free versus Pro branding
facts.value: Free has basic page customization and retains MonoCloud branding; Pro has advanced customization and can remove the watermark.

facts.label: Custom domains
facts.value: A dedicated custom-login-domain setup, DNS/TLS instructions, numeric allowance, fee and passkey domain-migration procedure were not located.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: No complete hosted-screen locale list, translation override guide, WCAG conformance statement or VPAT was located.

facts.label: Official web SDKs and integrations
facts.value: Official monorepo supplies framework-neutral auth-core, browser auth-web-js, React, Node core, Next.js and backend-node for Node API servers.

facts.label: Management language SDKs
facts.value: Official JavaScript Management SDK and .NET Management SDK automate hosted users/apps/groups/settings. README supports .NET Standard 2.0, .NET Framework 4.6.1+ and .NET 6+.

facts.label: Runtime requirement conflict
facts.value: Next.js install guide recommends Node.js 18 or later, but current @monocloud/auth-nextjs 0.2.10 metadata requires Node >=20.

facts.label: Mobile and nonbrowser clients
facts.value: Public schema recognizes mobile technology labels and PKCE/public-client settings; device grant is documented for TVs, consoles, IoT and CLIs.

facts.label: First-party native SDK coverage
facts.value: No dedicated first-party iOS/Swift, native Android, React Native or Flutter login setup/SDK was located.

facts.label: Hosted integration prerequisites
facts.value: MonoCloud tenant and registered application, exact callback/sign-out URLs, client configuration and builder-operated app; server-rendered apps also use a client secret/cookie secret.

facts.label: API and optional service dependencies
facts.value: API servers configure tenant issuer/audience; opaque-token introspection additionally needs credentials. Own SendGrid/Twilio delivery requires the chosen provider account; browser storage can be configured.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented hosted subscription. Public SDKs run in the app and call MonoCloud; no separately deployable production identity-server edition is documented in this offer.

facts.label: Profile data and custom forms
facts.value: Native public/private user metadata APIs, claims updates and configurable sign-up custom fields are documented.

facts.label: Custom access logic
facts.value: Basic structured API policies compile to Cedar; advanced Cedar policies can test groups, network zones, time/location, certificate and authentication context before token issuance.

facts.label: Webhooks and custom runtime precision
facts.value: A generic lifecycle webhook subscription/delivery/retry specification, custom-code execution environment and hook resource limits were not found.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Dashboard/product and APIs provide creation, paginated search/filter/sort, profile updates, password reset, disable/enable, lockout reset and deletion.

facts.label: Impersonation controls
facts.value: No dedicated support-user impersonation operation, approval/audit safeguards or price gate was located.

facts.label: Linked identity visibility and removal
facts.value: User response includes linked external providers, provider user IDs/claims; native API disconnects an external authenticator.

facts.label: Linking, merges and guest upgrade
facts.value: Explicit new-identity linking/merging, verified-email automatic merge rules and anonymous-to-registered preserved-ID upgrade were not established.

facts.label: Native brute-force controls
facts.value: Free/Pro include brute-force protection; schema supports user-account/IP lockouts, failed-attempt threshold, separate lockout durations, allowlisted IPs and email unblock.

facts.label: Paid policies and missing defenses
facts.value: Pro adds sign-up identifier allow/block rules and password strength/history customization. Native CAPTCHA/bot challenge, breached-password lookup and SMS fraud/spend-cap configuration were not established.

facts.label: API and login request limits
facts.value: No published login/token/management requests-per-second/minute limits, burst bucket, quota-sharing scope or Retry-After contract was located.

facts.label: Plan-specific audit retention
facts.value: Free: three days. Pro: seven days. Secure+ add-on: extendable up to 30 days.

facts.label: Audit API and export
facts.value: Paginated log retrieval/search/sort covers authentication, authorization and administrative activity with event/actor/target/request details; max 50 entries/page and a log-window response header.

facts.label: Profile, identifier and link extraction
facts.value: Paginated user API supports up to 50 users/page; detailed user response exposes identifiers, claims, public/private data, external provider IDs and passkey public metadata.

facts.label: Credential and full exit portability
facts.value: Password-hash export, a turnkey complete user/credential archive, export fee and guaranteed passkey/domain migration were not found.

facts.label: Password/user migration in
facts.value: CreateUser accepts a pre-hashed bcrypt password, verification states and optional policy-bypass flags. PasswordAlgorithms enum contains bcrypt only.

facts.label: Import completeness
facts.value: Custom original user-ID preservation, bulk import size/rate, lazy legacy password validation and additional hash algorithms were not established.

facts.label: Deletion and vendor account closure
facts.value: User DELETE is permanent/irreversible. Privacy accepts personal-data deletion requests through support@monocloud.com; paid renewal cancellation uses account management or support.

facts.label: Retention and backups
facts.value: Privacy retains personal data as needed for stated purposes/legal obligations/disputes, without numeric purge periods; exact user-deletion, backup purge and account-close completion times were not established.

facts.label: Published hosted regions
facts.value: Public Management API server template is {tenant}.{region}.monocloud.com/api (HTTPS) with region codes us, eu and in.

facts.label: Transfer countries and residency gaps
facts.value: Privacy names United States, United Kingdom, Germany, India and Singapore as processing/transfer destinations; full user/profile/log/backup/support residency commitments were not established.

facts.label: Privacy rights and named services
facts.value: Public privacy policy describes access/rectification/deletion/portability requests, analytics/service providers and payment processing; terms name Google Analytics and Datadog.

facts.label: DPA, subprocessors and audit evidence
facts.value: No public scoped DPA, complete named subprocessor list, SOC 2 report or ISO 27001 certificate was located.

facts.label: Product, owner and official URLs
facts.value: MonoCloud; terms/privacy name MonoCloud (India) LLP. Official website and documentation use monocloud.com.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Public Free and Pro offers, signup instructions and maintained SDK publications are available; no retirement notice was found.

facts.label: Hosted platform license
facts.value: Proprietary service under MonoCloud's terms; service functionality/content remains vendor/licensor property.

facts.label: Authentication SDK license
facts.value: monocloud/auth-js is MIT; checked @monocloud/auth-nextjs and @monocloud/auth-react packages also declare MIT.

facts.label: Public status and SLA
facts.value: No linked public operational status dashboard or quantified contractual uptime/credit schedule was located.

facts.label: Current code publications
facts.value: @monocloud/auth-nextjs 0.2.10 published 2026-09-30T06:44:03.622Z; @monocloud/auth-react 0.2.9 published 2026-09-30T06:42:50.114Z. Official auth-js repository is not archived.

facts.label: Support lifecycle precision
facts.value: No published universal SDK LTS/security-fix window or dated end-of-support policy was found.

facts.label: Support channels and response scope
facts.value: Free/Pro have Discord support; Pro adds email ticket support. Docs give support@monocloud.com and GitHub issue routes; contact page says typical response within one business day.

facts.label: Auth billing unit and definition
facts.value: MAU = unique user authenticating at least once in a monthly billing period. Allowance is per project: Free 60,000 MAU; Launch and Scale 1,000,000 MAU.

facts.label: Database billing alongside Auth
facts.value: Managed Better Auth has no separate charge within allowances. Database compute billed in CU-hours and storage in GB-months; other backend services have separate meters.

facts.label: Free allowance — Auth and database
facts.value: Free: 60,000 MAU/project; 100 CU-hours/project/month; 1 GB Postgres/project with 20 GB account total; 5 GB public transfer/project/month; up to 2 CU.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Launch and Scale have no monthly minimum or base fee; usage starts metering from zero. Docs say invoices under $0.50 are not collected. Higher-volume annual commitments are negotiated separately.

facts.label: Usage price — Launch
facts.value: $0.106/CU-hour compute; $0.35/GB-month database storage; $0.20/GB-month retained history/data changes; 500 GB public transfer/project included then $0.10/GB.

facts.label: Usage price — Scale
facts.value: $0.222/CU-hour; $0.35/GB-month database storage; $0.20/GB-month history; same 500 GB public transfer inclusion then $0.10/GB. Private transfer $0.01/GB.

facts.label: Auth above published allowances
facts.value: Paid plans include up to 1M MAU/project; above that requires contacting Neon/requesting an increase. No public per-extra-MAU rate is published.

facts.label: Business cost method
facts.value: Both requested SAML baselines unsupported by the documented managed plugin set. Organizations/invitations exist in beta, but native business SAML/SCIM is not a verified managed feature.

facts.label: Customer organization defaults
facts.value: Organization plugin enabled per branch by default; beta/partial. Default per-user created+joined organization membership limit 10; default members per organization 100. Settings can be changed.

facts.label: Organization invitations and limitations
facts.value: Invitations, owner/admin/member roles and membership APIs included. Invitation email toggle requires Verify email at signup; builder supplies accept-invitation route/UI. Teams, server hooks, custom roles/permissions and dynamic access control unsupported.

facts.label: SSO and account-sync fees
facts.value: No native managed SAML/SCIM rate or connection allowance found. Downstream OAuth Provider is a supported managed plugin with no separate add-on price listed.

facts.label: Builder seats and project caps
facts.value: Unlimited developer organization members on all plans. Free and Launch 100 projects; Scale 1,000 with increase on request. Branches/project: 10 Free, 10 Launch, 25 Scale.

facts.label: Additional branch costs
facts.value: Paid extra branches $0.002/branch-hour; docs also headline $1.50/branch-month, prorated hourly. Free branch creation stops at 10/project.

facts.label: Email sender
facts.value: Shared auth@mail.myneon.app is for development/testing. Production checklist directs custom SMTP for reliable delivery/higher limits; link-based email verification requires custom email provider.

facts.label: Email send allowance and tariff
facts.value: No numeric default/shared-email allowance, exact shared SMTP throttle or included-send tariff found in current pricing or managed email guides.

facts.label: SMS delivery and charges
facts.value: Managed service generates phone OTP but does not deliver SMS. A blocking send.otp webhook forwards to the builder's own provider; destination/message charges are external.

facts.label: Free resource limits and paid controls
facts.value: Free compute suspended on 100 CU-hours or 5 GB transfer until next billing period/upgrade; storage-growing operations fail over 1 GB/project or 20 GB total. Paid alerts at 80%/100% do not stop usage; project consumption limits can suspend compute.

facts.label: Auth MAU exhaustion behavior
facts.value: Exact request-level behavior at the Free 60k MAU threshold and paid 1M threshold was not specified in current Auth/about, pricing, plans or management docs.

facts.label: Other billable components
facts.value: Paid snapshots/scheduled backups $0.09/GB-month; extra branches, retained history, Functions and Object Storage can add charges. No separate managed Auth security/plugin fee listed.

facts.label: Individual account eligibility
facts.value: Neon Product Specific Schedule explicitly says Customer may be an individual or a legal entity.

facts.label: Country and market coverage
facts.value: No complete public list of allowed builder/seller countries located; MCSA requires compliance with export controls and trade sanctions.

facts.label: Self-service and free entry
facts.value: Free plan is ongoing, $0, no time limit and no credit card required. Enable managed Auth through Console, CLI or API; Launch/Scale are self-service usage plans.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Vendor-managed Better Auth REST service coupled to Neon Postgres; accounts, login, stored sessions, verification, organizations and downstream OAuth provider capability. Auth data lives in neon_auth schema.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Neon operates the Auth service in the same region as the Neon database. Builder runs the app, configures origins/OAuth/delivery, and writes appropriate database permissions and RLS policies.

facts.label: Email/password login
facts.value: Built-in managed email/password signup and signin; credentials hashed in neon_auth.account. Password maximum 128 characters; longer signup/signin input returns PASSWORD_TOO_LONG.

facts.label: Email OTP
facts.value: Managed Email OTP plugin supports passwordless signin, verification and password reset; service generates/delivers codes or calls a configured delivery webhook.

facts.label: Magic link
facts.value: Supported managed plugin. Link expiry configurable 5–1,440 minutes, default 5; Allow New User Registration toggle controls whether links create accounts.

facts.label: Phone OTP
facts.value: Supported for existing users with linked, verified phone only; no phone-first signup. E.164 numbers, fixed 6 digits, 60–600 second expiry configurable, default 300; invalidates after 3 incorrect codes.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: SDK allowAnonymous provides anonymous-role Data API tokens, not persistent anonymous user accounts. No managed anonymous-user upgrade or native wallet/SIWE plugin documented in the supported set.

facts.label: Social providers
facts.value: Current guide supports Google, GitHub, Vercel, Microsoft and Apple. Google alone has shared development credentials; use own provider apps/credentials in production.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: No managed passkey/WebAuthn plugin, enrollment flow or browser/native compatibility matrix located in current supported-plugin docs, roadmap and SDK plugin configuration.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: Managed app-user MFA remains 'coming soon' on the roadmap; current SDK managed plugin set has no two-factor client plugin. No managed TOTP/recovery-code entitlement established.

facts.label: Email verification and reset
facts.value: Verification via code or link; code supports shared/custom mail, link verification requires custom provider. Password reset through request/reset methods or email OTP is documented.

facts.label: Profile and password changes
facts.value: Self-service name update and password change with currentPassword; optional revokeOtherSessions: true. Self-service email change explicitly not supported in the guide.

facts.label: Sessions, cookies and access JWT
facts.value: Opaque server session token in HTTP-only cookie, stored sessions in Postgres; SDK retrieves an Ed25519-signed access JWT for Data API, documented expiry 15 minutes.

facts.label: Revocation and cache boundaries
facts.value: Admin APIs list/revoke one or all user sessions. SDK signOut clears current session state; client in-memory cache 60 seconds and Next.js signed session-data cache default 300 seconds.

facts.label: Managed session lifetime and rotation
facts.value: Exact hosted session default/max lifetime, rolling-renewal schedule and per-device ceiling not established in Neon docs or current SDK server/session code.

facts.label: Standards — upstream and downstream roles
facts.value: Upstream managed social OAuth is documented. OAuth Provider plugin turns the app into a downstream OAuth 2.1/OIDC authorization server with discovery/JWKS, token refresh and managed client onboarding.

facts.label: SAML and generic business federation
facts.value: No managed SAML service-provider/identity-provider plugin or generic customer enterprise SSO configuration found in supported-plugin docs, roadmap or current managed client plugin list.

facts.label: Customer organizations, invitations and roles
facts.value: Managed Organization plugin supports tenants sharing a branch, members, invitations and owner/admin/member permissions. Active org can be selected in a session; predefined org context can be included in JWTs.

facts.label: Unavailable organization customization
facts.value: Teams subgroups, server-side organization hooks, custom roles/default-permission changes and dynamically created roles are not supported.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No managed SCIM v2 user/group provisioning, directory sync or deprovisioning behavior found in the managed plugin list, roadmap, SDK plugin registration or management guide.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Better Auth UI supplies sign-in, signup, password-reset, settings and user-menu components copied into the builder's app via shadcn CLI; custom forms supported through SDK methods.

facts.label: Branding — UI and email
facts.value: Edit copied UI/theme freely; app name is configurable per branch. Full email HTML/branding/localization requires custom delivery webhooks; custom SMTP alone retains default templates.

facts.label: Domains — redirect allowlist vs service hostname
facts.value: No managed custom Auth API hostname entitlement, maximum domain count or custom Auth hostname fee established in current domain/configuration guides or rate card.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: Custom UI and webhook emails can be localized; SDK changelog describes localized Better Auth UI error handling. No Neon-specific supported-language matrix or public accessibility conformance report located.

facts.label: Official framework support
facts.value: Neon docs support Next.js, Vite/React, React Router and TanStack Router; vanilla and React adapters plus combined Auth/Data API client are available.

facts.label: Runtime and architecture limits
facts.value: Framework-agnostic @neon/auth/server toolkit is beta and Web Standards based. Roadmap still calls separate frontend/backend deployments unsupported; app cookie architecture needs careful same-site integration.

facts.label: Native mobile and desktop clients
facts.value: No first-party native iOS/Android, Flutter, React Native or native passkey guide established for this managed service in current roadmap, SDK docs, package exports and plugin list.

facts.label: Required services and setup
facts.value: Neon project/database, managed Auth endpoint and builder-hosted frontend. Next.js requires an app cookie secret of at least 32 characters; social login requires provider apps and production delivery requires configured sender.

facts.label: Network prerequisites and incompatibilities
facts.value: Auth available in AWS regions only; currently incompatible with projects using IP Allow or Private Networking.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: Neon-managed Auth itself is not presented as a separately self-hostable server. Self-hosting standalone Better Auth is explicitly a separate option for custom hooks/plugins/infrastructure.

facts.label: Custom auth logic and event types
facts.value: Managed webhooks: blocking send.otp, send.magic_link, user.before_create; non-blocking user.created, phone_number.verified, organization invitation created/accepted.

facts.label: Delivery reliability and signature
facts.value: HTTPS webhook; Ed25519 detached JWS signatures via JWKS. Up to 3 attempts, no backoff, total 15-second budget; per-attempt timeout 1–10 seconds, default 5; 5xx/429/408/network retryable.

facts.label: User management — Console, control API and admin plugin
facts.value: Console assigns admin role; Admin plugin creates/lists/searches/updates users, sets password/role, bans/unbans, lists/revokes sessions. Neon control API documents user create/delete/role management.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Admin plugin supports impersonateUser and stopImpersonating. Impersonation lasts for the active browser session or up to 1 hour.

facts.label: Account linking/unlinking — client evidence and hosted uncertainty
facts.value: Current SDK advertises getUserIdentities/linkIdentity/unlinkIdentity and implements listAccounts/linkSocial/unlinkAccount. Managed server's complete enablement, merge safeguards and restrictions are not fully established.

facts.label: Guest upgrades
facts.value: allowAnonymous only issues anonymous-role data access; no persistent anonymous user or managed guest-to-registered-account upgrade flow located.

facts.label: Abuse protections — redirects, verification and signup hook
facts.value: Trusted redirect domains, HTTPS cookies and optional email verification; user.before_create webhook can apply custom allowlists/validation before account write. Localhost access starts enabled and should be disabled for production.

facts.label: CAPTCHA, breached-password and spend-fraud controls
facts.value: No managed CAPTCHA/Turnstile plugin, breached-password service or SMS-fraud/spend cap documented in supported plugins, roadmap, production guide or current SDK plugin list.

facts.label: Phone OTP limits
facts.value: Phone-number endpoints: 10 requests per 60 seconds per IP, in addition to global limits; OTP invalidated after 3 wrong codes.

facts.label: Global auth and email-code quotas
facts.value: Numeric global Auth endpoint and email-code throttle windows not found in current managed docs or public SDK configuration.

facts.label: Control-plane management API limit
facts.value: Neon API: 700 requests/minute, 40 requests/second burst per route; organization API-key creation 10/second. HTTP 429 on excess, exponential backoff recommended.

facts.label: Auth events and observability
facts.value: Webhooks provide listed auth/org lifecycle events but guide explicitly says no test events, event logs or redelivery. SDK has structured warning/error logging and custom logger support.

facts.label: Security audit retention/export
facts.value: No managed Auth audit-event catalogue, security-log retention/export/streaming SLA or per-log Auth price located.

facts.label: Export — profiles and database data
facts.value: Auth profiles and relational auth state live in the customer's neon_auth Postgres schema; docs permit direct SQL queries. Neon documents pg_dump/pg_restore for database backup/export.

facts.label: Export — hashes, sessions and passkeys
facts.value: No explicit managed password-hash export procedure, credential compatibility matrix, supported session-secret export or passkey migration guarantee found.

facts.label: Migration in — Supabase and legacy Stack
facts.value: Current Supabase guide says existing password users cannot migrate due to different hash algorithms; users need new accounts or OAuth reauthentication. Legacy Stack migration guide covers changing SDK/UI/configuration.

facts.label: Migration in — bulk/lazy import and IDs
facts.value: No managed bulk hash-import endpoint, lazy migration callback, supported foreign-hash list or complete preserve-custom-ID import procedure located.

facts.label: Account and service deletion
facts.value: Neon management API can delete users. Disabling Auth defaults delete_data=false, retaining neon_auth; delete_data=true permanently removes schema/auth tables. Self-service delete flow not established by current user guide.

facts.label: Retention, backups and closing Neon
facts.value: Database history: Free up to 6 hours/1 GB changes; Launch up to 7 days; Scale up to 30 days, as configured. Deleted Neon builder account can be reactivated within 30 days; after 30 days account-related data is permanently deleted per account guide.

facts.label: DPA termination deletion
facts.value: Public Databricks DPA sample v3 (2023-07-21) section 9.3 says deletion/assistance within 30 days after a written request following termination/expiry; Neon schedule modifies DPA audit provisions.

facts.label: Hosted regions
facts.value: Managed Better Auth available in AWS N. Virginia, Ohio, Oregon, Frankfurt, London, Singapore, Sydney and São Paulo; Auth and database share project region.

facts.label: Residency boundaries
facts.value: A project has one fixed region; changing region requires a new project and migration. Full all-category residency guarantees for logs, support, email and subprocessors were not found.

facts.label: Public legal/privacy evidence
facts.value: Current Neon schedule incorporates Databricks MCSA/DPA; public DPA sample and signing route. Subprocessor list is Databricks-wide, with Neon schedule additionally naming Grafana Labs in the US.

facts.label: Assurance and scope
facts.value: Neon claims SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27701, TLS 1.2+ and AES-256; security page links Trust Center and says public SOC 3 summary available. HIPAA/report entitlements appear on Scale.

facts.label: Name, aliases and owner
facts.value: Neon Auth is now presented as Managed Better Auth, part of Neon's backend. Neon joined Databricks after its announced 2025 acquisition; current company and platform pages identify Neon as part of Databricks and name Databricks, Inc. with affiliate Neon, LLC.

facts.label: Acquisition and product lifecycle
facts.value: Neon announced it would join Databricks after the transaction closed on 2025-05-14; its current company page says it is part of Databricks. Managed Better Auth is generally available and currently operational; no product shutdown or sunset found.

facts.label: Legacy auth and UI notices
facts.value: Legacy Stack-based Neon Auth is labeled 'no longer accepting new users'; existing Neon Auth users remain supported and new setups are directed to Managed Better Auth. @neondatabase/auth-ui is deprecated; new apps use Better Auth UI.

facts.label: Azure deprecation relevant to deployment
facts.value: Azure regions deprecated 2026-04-07 and stopped platform updates 2026-10-05; new projects unavailable. Inactive Free Azure projects may be deleted after 90 days. Managed Better Auth runs on AWS, not Azure.

facts.label: License — Neon SDK
facts.value: Current @neon/auth package is Apache-2.0; public SDK source and license are in neondatabase/neon-pkgs.

facts.label: Commercial service terms
facts.value: Hosted use governed by Neon Product Specific Schedule updated 2026-10-14 plus Databricks MCSA. Self-service subscriptions renew monthly; schedule says cancel at least 14 business days before the subscription month ends.

facts.label: Public status
facts.value: Neon public status page reports service incidents/components.

facts.label: Paid SLA scope
facts.value: Neon Scale platform SLA targets 99.95% monthly uptime for Compute Endpoints only; document explicitly excludes all other platform APIs/products/services.

facts.label: SLA claim deadline conflict
facts.value: Same SLA section 2.2 says ticket within 21 days of awareness, while section 3.1.1 says within 24 hours; section 3.1.2 requires claim by end of following month.

facts.label: Managed/server and SDK versions
facts.value: About page says managed service runs Better Auth 1.7.12. Current @neon/auth latest package is 0.8.2, published 2026-10-30T16:36:05.641Z; docs require at least 0.8.1.

facts.label: Maintenance and security process
facts.value: Current plugin announcement 2026-11-02, docs/release updates in October, SDK changelog and security page demonstrate dated maintenance. Vendor claims severity-based remediation windows: critical 7, high 30, medium 60, low 90 days.

facts.label: Support — plan channels
facts.value: Free community; Launch billing tickets only; Scale support tickets for any Neon issue. Discord and AI assistance explicitly not official support channels.

facts.label: Support response promises

facts.label: Auth billing unit
facts.value: Current credit-based/Enterprise plans include Identity at no extra auth charge with unlimited active and invite-only users.

facts.label: Platform billing period
facts.value: Credits cover team usage and reset with billing cycle; all projects on a team share allowances.

facts.label: Legacy billing scope
facts.value: Accounts created before September 4, 2025 may retain legacy plans; Identity features depend on old service level.

facts.label: Current Free auth
facts.value: Unlimited active/invite-only users; email/password, four documented social providers, functions integration, recovery and email change.

facts.label: Free platform allowance
facts.value: $0/month with 300 credits/month hard limit; no auto recharge or paid credit top-up while on Free.

facts.label: Published Personal entry
facts.value: Public Personal-vs-Free comparison states $9/month for 1,000 credits, one builder.

facts.label: Current paid price applicability
facts.value: Main price extraction shows Personal $9/$12/$15 and Pro $20/$20/$25, with See pricing in your dashboard; applicable checkout amount unresolved.

facts.label: Enterprise and commitment
facts.value: Enterprise custom quote; subscription term shown in account/order. Fees tax-exclusive and generally non-refundable.

facts.label: No user excess tariff
facts.value: Current Identity has no published paid user bands or per-login tariff; legacy service-level price schedule not restated.

facts.label: Credit pack rates
facts.value: Personal adds 500 credits for $5; Pro adds 1,500 for $10; auto recharge optional.

facts.label: Business A/B
facts.value: No qualifying native hosted plan established for customer organizations, invitations/roles inside them and 1/10 app-customer SAML connections.

facts.label: Customer-organization limits
facts.value: No native customer organization/member-per-org quota or tariff published for Identity.

facts.label: App SAML/SCIM fees
facts.value: No hosted Identity SAML-connection/SCIM-directory price established.

facts.label: Builder seats
facts.value: Free/Personal: one builder, no extra member seats. Credit Pro: unlimited members included since April 14, 2026.

facts.label: Projects and shared capacity
facts.value: Free, Personal and Pro each allow up to 500 projects/team; all share the same team credit allowance.

facts.label: Default hosted email
facts.value: Native confirmation, invitations, password recovery and email-change mail sent from no-reply@netlify.com by default.

facts.label: Custom SMTP gate
facts.value: Pro/Enterprise may connect third-party SMTP for own sender; custom templates also Pro+. External sender bill separate.

facts.label: Managed delivery tariff
facts.value: Exact included send quota, per-message price and deliverability/sending ceiling not published in reviewed current docs.

facts.label: GoTrue mail cooldown
facts.value: Standalone/source default SMTP_MAX_FREQUENCY: 900 seconds between signup confirmation or password-reset mail for the same account.

facts.label: Credit exhaustion
facts.value: Projects pause when team allowance is exhausted; one project's excess can pause all team projects. Paid auto recharge is off by default.

facts.label: Free service conditions
facts.value: Free can be changed, suspended or discontinued at vendor discretion; no service-level commitment for Free.

facts.label: Traffic and compute meters
facts.value: 20 credits/GB bandwidth; 10 credits/GB-hour compute; 2 credits/10,000 web requests; 15 credits/production deploy.

facts.label: Pro tier resources
facts.value: 3,000-credit base; optional 5,000/10,000/15,000/20,000 monthly credits. Current docs allow rollover at 5,000+, one further cycle.

facts.label: Individual eligibility and country rules
facts.value: Service contract accepts individual or entity; excludes access violating US export restrictions or from embargoed countries/regions.

facts.label: Age wording mismatch
facts.value: Current service agreement permits persons 13+ subject to higher local minimum; privacy notice says service is not knowingly provided to under-16 users.

facts.label: Hosted entry and trial
facts.value: Self-service Free advertised; no separate free trial offered. Existing project can enable Identity through dashboard.

facts.label: Payment requirement
facts.value: Personal/Pro credit plans require a valid saved payment method to keep projects active; Enterprise also supports ACH/wire.

facts.label: Hosted auth scope
facts.value: Managed accounts, password/social login, verification/recovery, sessions, roles, invitations and administrative APIs per Netlify project.

facts.label: Open-source boundary
facts.value: GoTrue can run as a standalone auth API; this does not reproduce Netlify hosting, dashboard, CDN rules or hosted plan entitlements.

facts.label: Hosted responsibilities
facts.value: Netlify runs the auth service; builder enables it, supplies app UI/policies and protects privileged function endpoints.

facts.label: Standalone GoTrue responsibilities
facts.value: Operator supplies database, auth server, signing secrets, mail transport, patches and recovery operations.

facts.label: Email/password login
facts.value: built_in native signup/password login on current plans; optional required confirmation and invite-only mode.

facts.label: Passwordless/phone/guest methods
facts.value: No native general email magic-link, email-code, phone/SMS, wallet or persistent guest-login flow established.

facts.label: Documented social providers
facts.value: Google, GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket; hosted Native external-provider login available on all current plans.

facts.label: Bring own OAuth brand
facts.value: Default shared Netlify OAuth application or own client ID/secret to display builder's app name; custom credentials allowed across current plans.

facts.label: Passkeys/WebAuthn
facts.value: Native passkey enrollment/login, recovery and platform/plan support not published.

facts.label: MFA and recovery factors
facts.value: Native app-user TOTP/SMS/security-key MFA and recovery-code enrollment/enforcement not established; vendor directs advanced MFA needs to Auth0.

facts.label: Email verification
facts.value: Confirmation token processed by confirmEmail()/handleAuthCallback(); signup confirmation on by default; autoconfirm setting can skip it.

facts.label: Recovery and credential changes
facts.value: requestPasswordRecovery/recoverPassword; updateUser changes email/password/metadata; verifyEmailChange requires active browser session.

facts.label: Invitations and deletion
facts.value: Invite token requires chosen password through acceptInvite(); user deletion available to server admin, not a documented built-in self-delete screen.

facts.label: Hosted session model
facts.value: nf_jwt access JWT default 1 hour; nf_refresh refresh credential. Browser auto-refresh 60 seconds before expiry.

facts.label: Current SDK storage
facts.value: Browser persists session via gotrue-js/localStorage; nf_jwt and nf_refresh cookies use Secure, SameSite=Lax, path=/, HttpOnly=false.

facts.label: Revocation and refresh core behavior
facts.value: GoTrue swaps/revokes used refresh tokens; logout deletes all refresh tokens for user; access JWT remains valid until expiry unless checked separately.

facts.label: Core lifetime defaults
facts.value: GoTrue source default access 3,600 seconds; refresh 2,592,000 seconds (30 days), configurable.

facts.label: Hosted SAML/OIDC role
facts.value: No public customer-Identity SAML SP/OIDC issuer or generic OIDC connection setup/entitlement established.

facts.label: GoTrue SAML component
facts.value: Self-operated GoTrue source contains inbound SAML SP adapter, metadata endpoint and assertion callback.

facts.label: Netlify dashboard SSO
facts.value: Enterprise SAML config/Directory Sync secure access to Netlify teams and organizations, separate from app identities.

facts.label: Flat app roles
facts.value: Roles stored in app_metadata.roles, editable by admin; JWT/redirect rules can restrict content; user metadata cannot grant roles.

facts.label: Organizations/invitations boundary
facts.value: Project invitations supported; no native customer workspace creation, per-org member invite/admin UI or member-specific role model established.

facts.label: App SCIM
facts.value: Native SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning for Identity app accounts not published.

facts.label: Recommended UI approach
facts.value: @netlify/identity is headless: standalone signup/login/logout/account functions; builder renders forms and account screens.

facts.label: Optional existing widget
facts.value: netlify-identity-widget supplies login/signup modal and recovery UI; still works, but not recommended for new projects.

facts.label: Own domain and frontend brand
facts.value: Identity lives at project's /.netlify/identity path; custom frontend UI and custom HTTPS domain supported.

facts.label: Email/provider brand gates
facts.value: Pro+ custom SMTP sender and templates; all current plans may use own supported OAuth client credentials.

facts.label: Widget locales
facts.value: Legacy widget documents en, fr, es, pt, hu, pl, cs, sk, de, it, ar, zhCN, nl, sv, sw, ru.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: Trust Center lists VPAT/Accessibility Statement behind access request; no inspected public Identity/widget-specific conformance report.

facts.label: Web/runtime clients
facts.value: Official @netlify/identity browser and Netlify modern/v2 Functions/Edge Functions; Next.js, Astro, Remix, SvelteKit, TanStack Start examples.

facts.label: Runtime version
facts.value: SDK 2.0.0 requires Node >=22.12.0 and exports ESM/CommonJS bundles.

facts.label: Local development conflict
facts.value: SDK README says netlify dev exposes Identity endpoint; official knowledge base says /.netlify/identity/* cannot be exercised locally and to test a real deploy.

facts.label: Native mobile/client scope
facts.value: No current official native iOS/Android/Flutter SDK or documented secure native redirect/storage integration established.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Netlify account/project, enabled Identity, HTTPS and app UI/callback handling; no customer-managed auth database required.

facts.label: Self-operated GoTrue prerequisites
facts.value: Go executable/container, documented MySQL connection, signing configuration and SMTP for recovery/verification mail.

facts.label: Managed-only operational boundary
facts.value: Netlify's dashboard/CDN/Identity hosting are not offered as a self-installable managed edition.

facts.label: GoTrue operations
facts.value: Standalone GoTrue requires database migrations, database/config backup, upgrades, TLS/proxy and mail operations by the operator.

facts.label: User fields and browser events
facts.value: Arbitrary signup/user metadata, separate server-owned app metadata; onAuthChange covers login/logout/token refresh/update/recovery.

facts.label: Hosted event hooks
facts.value: Typed userValidate, userSignup, userLogin, userModified and userDeleted handlers; deny can block first four; background mode for async work.

facts.label: Dashboard and server administration
facts.value: List/paginate, retrieve, create, update and delete Identity users; SDK admin API server-only with operator token.

facts.label: Admin safety and creation
facts.value: admin.createUser auto-confirms and accepts allowed role/app/user metadata; caller must authorize requests to its function.

facts.label: Banning/impersonation
facts.value: No documented first-class ban field or audited support impersonation API/UI established.

facts.label: Core email/provider matching
facts.value: GoTrue source reuses an existing same-audience account when provider email is verified or autoconfirm permits it; invite acceptance checks matching email.

facts.label: Explicit merge/guest upgrade
facts.value: No current documented merge/unlink API or guest-to-registered data-preserving flow established.

facts.label: CSRF protection
facts.value: SDK verifyRequestOrigin checks request Origin against endpoint origin; apply to exposed server login/signup/logout mutations.

facts.label: Signup and custom abuse policy
facts.value: Invite-only registration; event hooks can deny validation/signup/login; platform code-based rate-limit rules available.

facts.label: Native password/bot controls
facts.value: GoTrue hashes passwords with bcrypt and bounds maximum to 72 bytes; no current hosted breached-password screening/CAPTCHA entitlement established.

facts.label: Core request limiter rates
facts.value: GoTrue source rate parameters: signup 10/min, recover 5/min, token 30/5 min, verify 30/min; HTTP 429 on excess.

facts.label: Hosted limits and capacity
facts.value: Current per-plan hosted Identity overrides, admin quotas, concurrency and guaranteed login capacity not published.

facts.label: Identity audit feature
facts.value: Pro+ searchable Identity events: login/logout/signup/delete/modify/token revoke/refresh/recovery request/invite.

facts.label: Audit retention/export
facts.value: No Identity-specific guaranteed retention days, log-drain/streaming format or extra storage fee established.

facts.label: Profile/ID export
facts.value: Paginated admin.listUsers permits export of normalized IDs, email, roles, metadata and supported timestamps.

facts.label: Hosted password-hash export
facts.value: No current documented self-service hash-export route/permission or fixed support export fee established.

facts.label: GoTrue operator export
facts.value: Configured export secret enables export endpoint with encrypted_password field (bcrypt hash), separate from normal user responses.

facts.label: Supported creation versus import
facts.value: Admin creation can pre-create auto-confirmed accounts using plaintext password and metadata; no public hash/bulk/lazy migration importer established.

facts.label: App-user deletion
facts.value: admin.deleteUser removes a user by ID; GoTrue emits audit/userDeleted hook; builder can expose an authorized deletion flow.

facts.label: Account termination and return
facts.value: Export before termination; after termination no general retention obligation, subject to DPA. DPA provides export on request at customer expense or deletion.

facts.label: Retention timelines
facts.value: Exact Identity database/log/backup deletion schedule and recoverable backup retention not public in inspected material.

facts.label: Hosted auth data residency
facts.value: No Identity-specific database region selector, primary/backup locations or EU-only residency commitment established.

facts.label: Processor and self-operated scope
facts.value: Netlify lists US AWS/GCP/SendGrid infrastructure/service processing; self-operated GoTrue operator chooses deployment/provider location.

facts.label: DPA
facts.value: Public DPA last updated June 9, 2026; forms part of applicable self-serve/Enterprise agreement; transfer safeguards and deletion clauses included.

facts.label: Assurance and subprocessors
facts.value: Trust Center claims SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27018 and publishes subprocessor inventory; SOC 2 2026 report access-on-request.

facts.label: Identity and operator
facts.value: Netlify Identity; hosted app-user auth operated by Netlify, Inc., a Delaware corporation.

facts.label: Product and code URLs
facts.value: Official product docs under /manage/security/secure-access-to-sites/identity/; recommended client @netlify/identity in netlify/primitives.

facts.label: Deprecation reversed
facts.value: Original announcement dated February 28, 2025; update dated February 19, 2026 says Identity continues as a supported option.

facts.label: New-project availability
facts.value: Current setup docs explicitly recommend @netlify/identity for new projects and instruct Enable Identity in the project dashboard.

facts.label: Separate Git Gateway lifecycle
facts.value: Git Gateway remains deprecated: existing enabled sites continue; new configurations discouraged; only major security fixes, no functional bug fixes.

facts.label: Hosted license/contract
facts.value: Vendor service governed by self-serve or Enterprise agreement; no self-host license for the whole managed platform.

facts.label: Current SDK license
facts.value: @netlify/identity package declares MIT.

facts.label: GoTrue and widget licenses
facts.value: Netlify GoTrue server and Identity Widget are MIT; commercial use, modification and distribution allowed subject to notice/warranty terms.

facts.label: Status and availability
facts.value: Public status page lists Identity Operational in retrieved snapshot.

facts.label: SLA scope
facts.value: Enterprise markets 99.99% platform SLA; applicable service scope/credits per order. No Identity-specific public SLA confirmed; Free has no commitment.

facts.label: SDK release and requirements
facts.value: @netlify/identity 2.0.0 released August 18, 2026; breaking requirement Node >=22.12.0.

facts.label: Core maintenance evidence
facts.value: netlify/gotrue unarchived; live metadata pushed October 27, 2026. gotrue-js/widget also unarchived with November 2026 activity.

facts.label: Support version policy
facts.value: Hosted GoTrue version and a public SDK/core LTS or security-fix support-until schedule not established.

facts.label: Support routes
facts.value: Official support page, documentation and community forums; paid plans offer priority/dedicated routes.

facts.label: Support commitments
facts.value: Personal priority email; Pro priority email; Enterprise dedicated 24/7 marketed. Ordinary response-time hours not established.
