facts.label: Billing unit and definition — Cloud
facts.value: One subscription per builder organization, covering its projects; included resource allowances aggregate across projects. All plans list unlimited total Auth users.

facts.label: Billing period and compute
facts.value: Calendar month, first through last day; midmonth starts prorated. Compute billed for allocated running time, by the minute; paused/deleted projects stop compute charges.

facts.label: Free production allowance — Cloud Starter
facts.value: $0/month, unlimited Auth users, 1 active project and 1 builder member; 1 GB database, 1 GB storage, 5 GB egress; pauses after 1 week of inactivity.

facts.label: Free allowance — self-hosted
facts.value: MIT software license has no per-user or monthly software charge; infrastructure and delivery services are supplied separately.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment — Cloud Pro
facts.value: From $25/month per organization, including $15 compute credit; one basic project within included usage is shown at $25/month in billing example 1.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment — Team / Enterprise
facts.value: Team from $599/month with $15 compute credit; Enterprise custom quote.

facts.label: Usage price rules — Pro and Team resources
facts.value: 10 GB database capacity included then $0.20/GB; 50 GB storage included then $0.05/GB; 50 GB egress included then $0.10/GB.

facts.label: Usage price rules — compute
facts.value: Shared $0.00034/vCPU/minute, headline $15/core/month; dedicated $0.0012/vCPU/minute, headline $50/core/month; 2 GB memory per vCPU in the rate card.

facts.label: Usage price rules — conflicting billing example
facts.value: Billing example 4 prints a $66 total, but its listed parts are $25 + ($50 − $15), which equal $60 by our calculation.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: A and B below: no native turnkey customer-organization/invitation model established. WorkOS SSO and custom app data/code are required; complete usable-plan total remains unknown.

facts.label: Customer organization limits and fees
facts.value: No native Auth customer-organization/member/invitation allowance or tariff located; build membership tables and authorization rules in the app database.

facts.label: SSO fees — WorkOS external service
facts.value: Nhost documents WorkOS OAuth integration for enterprise SSO/SAML. WorkOS Single Sign-On costs $125/connection/month for 1–15 connections.

facts.label: SCIM / Directory Sync fees
facts.value: WorkOS separately prices Directory Sync at $125/connection/month for 1–15 connections; a native Nhost SCIM integration or included sync allowance was not located.

facts.label: Builder team and projects — Starter
facts.value: 1 active project and 1 workspace member. FAQ allows multiple paused projects as long as only one is active.

facts.label: Builder team and projects — paid Cloud
facts.value: Pro, Team and Enterprise list unlimited projects and workspace members; additional running projects consume shared allowance and billable compute.

facts.label: Email — Starter default delivery
facts.value: Without custom SMTP, email-sending Auth endpoints share a nonconfigurable global limit of 10 emails/hour per project; Starter does not include custom SMTP or custom emails.

facts.label: Email — paid Cloud and self-hosted
facts.value: Pro/Team/Enterprise include custom SMTP and custom emails; configure SMTP credentials or Postmark integration. External sender costs are separate; no complete destination/send tariff published by Nhost.

facts.label: SMS delivery
facts.value: SMS OTP needs an SMS provider configured under provider.sms; carrier/provider charges depend on the external service and destination. No Nhost bundled SMS allowance or all-destination tariff found.

facts.label: Over-limit behavior — metered usage and alerts
facts.value: Pricing FAQ says excess usage is billed. Spending notifications at 75%, 90% and 100% of a chosen amount are informational and do not stop service.

facts.label: Over-limit behavior — nonpayment / inactivity
facts.value: Starter pauses after 1 week inactivity. Unpaid paid subscriptions progress through LOCKED (configuration blocked), DISABLED (projects paused), and CANCELLED (support required to restore).

facts.label: Other charges — functions and recovery
facts.value: Pro/Team: 50 functions then $5 per 50; 10 GB-hours execution then $0.18/GB-hour billed per second. Point-in-time recovery starts at $100 with 7-day retention.

facts.label: Other charges — domains and optional infrastructure
facts.value: Custom domains $10/project/month on paid tiers; Run services, replicas, extra compute and dedicated Enterprise clusters can add charges.

facts.label: Market and account eligibility
facts.value: Free self-service developer entry is advertised. Only adults over 18 may contract the service; a complete permitted-country list and mandatory business-registration requirements were not located.

facts.label: Self-service and trial rules
facts.value: Starter: free ongoing tier, no credit card required; public Get Started route. Pro and Team have Get Started routes; Enterprise requires contact.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Managed backend authentication service and separately deployable open-source server: users, login, sessions, verification, GraphQL authorization integration, and a WorkOS SSO bridge.

facts.label: Who operates it — Cloud
facts.value: Nhost operates managed Cloud infrastructure; an Enterprise dedicated cluster is also operated by Nhost.

facts.label: Who operates it — self-hosted
facts.value: The developer operates infrastructure, deployment, security configuration, backups and updates; optional professional support agreement is available.

facts.label: Basic login — password
facts.value: Built-in email/password, enabled by default; verified email required by default. Config default minimum password length 9; bcrypt password hashes.

facts.label: Basic login — email magic link
facts.value: Built-in passwordless email link flow, enabled through configuration; uses transactional email and client redirect handling.

facts.label: Basic login — email OTP
facts.value: Built-in emailed one-time codes; enable auth.method.otp.email. Codes expire after 5 minutes and are single-use.

facts.label: Basic login — phone OTP
facts.value: Built-in SMS one-time code login; enable auth.method.otp.sms and configure delivery. Codes expire after 5 minutes and are invalidated after 5 wrong attempts.

facts.label: Basic login — anonymous / wallet
facts.value: Anonymous sign-in is built in, disabled by default, and can be upgraded to a permanent account. Native wallet/sign-in-with-Ethereum flow not located.

facts.label: Social providers — configured OAuth
facts.value: Configuration lists Apple, Azure AD, Bitbucket, Discord, Entra ID, Facebook, GitHub, GitLab, Google, LinkedIn, Spotify, Strava, Twitch, Twitter, Windows Live and WorkOS.

facts.label: Social providers — native ID tokens
facts.value: Apple and Google ID tokens can be exchanged for Nhost sessions and linked to accounts.

facts.label: Passkeys — availability and registration
facts.value: WebAuthn/FIDO2 is built in and checked on all Cloud plans; browser registration/sign-in and adding a security key to an existing user are documented.

facts.label: Passkeys — domain and client limits
facts.value: WebAuthn requires frontend client URL/origin and relying-party configuration; existing key migration to a different relying-party domain is not promised. Full native-mobile passkey parity not established.

facts.label: MFA — authenticator codes
facts.value: Built-in TOTP MFA for email/password login; enable project setting, then each user enrolls with a generated secret/QR code and confirms a code. 2FA is included on all Cloud plans.

facts.label: MFA — elevated permissions
facts.value: Stable auth@0.52.0 has WebAuthn elevation for signed-in users. Config modes disabled (default), recommended, required; elevated claim lasts until the access token is renewed.

facts.label: MFA — rolling API differs from stable
facts.value: Live OpenAPI lists additional TOTP, email OTP and SMS OTP elevation routes that are absent from the auth@0.52.0 API definition.

facts.label: MFA recovery and enforcement details
facts.value: No documented user recovery-code set, complete lost-factor recovery procedure or all-login-method mandatory enrollment policy located.

facts.label: Verification, reset and address changes
facts.value: Email verification/resend, password reset and verified email change are built in; link flows use PKCE. Phone change stages the new number and only replaces the current number after SMS verification.

facts.label: Password change and self-service deletion
facts.value: Changing a password revokes all existing regular sessions, including the current one. No native DELETE /user route in the published Auth API; custom self-deletion needs protected database/GraphQL logic.

facts.label: Sessions — duration and rotation
facts.value: Default access JWT 15 minutes; refresh token 30 days. /token rotates the refresh token and revokes the one used.

facts.label: Sessions — revocation and verification
facts.value: Signout invalidates the current refresh token, optionally all devices; already issued JWTs remain usable until expiry when verified offline. JWT signing supports symmetric and asymmetric keys.

facts.label: Business standards — upstream SSO bridge
facts.value: Enterprise SAML login is documented through external WorkOS OAuth integration; configure WorkOS client ID, secret and callback in Nhost.

facts.label: Business standards — downstream OAuth2/OIDC provider
facts.value: Nhost Auth can act as an OAuth2/OIDC authorization server for other apps; disabled by default, requires RSA JWT signing and a developer-built login/consent UI.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: Built-in default/allowed user roles and Hasura row/column permissions; default role user, default allowed roles user and me. Customer membership, workspace invitations and tenant-admin screens need app data and code.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: Native SCIM v2 provisioning, user/group mappings and deprovisioning behavior not found in Nhost Auth docs or API.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: Headless Auth service with SDK calls and framework quickstarts; app developer supplies login, registration, profile, MFA and consent UI. No complete Nhost-hosted end-user account portal located.

facts.label: Branding and domains — Cloud
facts.value: App-owned frontend controls login branding. Custom Auth/service domains are a $10/project/month add-on on Pro, Team and Enterprise; Starter has no custom-domain entitlement.

facts.label: Branding and domains — self-hosted
facts.value: Operator controls frontend, service hostname, TLS, redirect allowlist and WebAuthn relying-party configuration; no Nhost managed-domain add-on fee applies to self-hosted infrastructure.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility evidence
facts.value: Email/SMS template folders support per-user locale, configured default-locale fallback, then built-in English. No public end-user UI language list or accessibility conformance report located.

facts.label: Web frameworks and runtimes
facts.value: Official quickstarts for React, Next.js, Vue, SvelteKit and React Native; JavaScript/TypeScript client @nhost/nhost-js. Next.js guide documents framework-specific session integration.

facts.label: Mobile and other clients
facts.value: Official React Native/Expo quickstart; official Dart/Flutter repository includes nhost_dart, nhost_flutter_auth and GraphQL adapters. Apple/Google ID-token flow is separately documented.

facts.label: Prerequisites — Cloud
facts.value: Managed Postgres/Auth/GraphQL stack; developer supplies frontend, permission rules and any social-provider credentials, custom SMTP, SMS or WorkOS accounts used.

facts.label: Prerequisites — self-hosted
facts.value: Docker reference stack includes Postgres, Auth, GraphQL and related backend services; production requires persistent data, secret/signing-key management, network/TLS configuration and a real email sender.

facts.label: Self-host operations and sizing
facts.value: Official Docker Compose reference is for demonstration; community support or a separately agreed professional support contract. No production Auth-only sizing guarantee located.

facts.label: Database backup and restore
facts.value: Cloud Pro/Team: daily backups, 7-day retention, download/restore, including external Postgres restore. Starter: manual pg_dump. PITR is an optional paid alternative.

facts.label: Custom fields and logic
facts.value: User metadata is JSONB; add GraphQL relationships and permissions without altering the managed auth schema/root fields. Database event triggers invoke HTTP handlers on insert/update/delete/manual events.

facts.label: Event delivery and authenticity
facts.value: Retries on non-2xx/network errors; defaults 0 retries, 10-second interval, 60-second timeout. Configure and validate a shared nhost-webhook-secret header.

facts.label: Administration and API
facts.value: User records are accessible through Dashboard/database/GraphQL and Auth /user GET; normal creation uses signup/login flows. Admin import, searches and changes use appropriately privileged data access.

facts.label: Banning and support impersonation
facts.value: User disabled status exists in the Auth API/error model; complete public dashboard ban/unban workflow and audited administrator impersonation controls were not established.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking
facts.value: Signed-in users can connect configured OAuth providers even when provider email differs; list/remove provider links through appropriately permissioned auth.user_providers GraphQL access.

facts.label: Guest upgrade
facts.value: Anonymous user can convert with email and optional password, provider connection, or verified SMS phone flow; identity upgrade is documented.

facts.label: Abuse protection — bot and password controls
facts.value: Optional Cloudflare Turnstile protects listed signup, reset and message-triggering signin endpoints. Configurable breached-password checking uses Have I Been Pwned, disabled by default.

facts.label: Abuse protection — registration and SMS
facts.value: Config supports allowed/blocked emails and email domains, disabling signup/auto-signup; SMS OTP expires after 5 minutes and burns after 5 failed attempts.

facts.label: Rate limits — default email delivery
facts.value: Any email-sending endpoint without custom SMTP: 10/hour, global project category, not configurable. With custom SMTP: default 10/hour/client IP, configurable.

facts.label: Rate limits — Auth categories
facts.value: Default per client IP: SMS sends 10/hour; brute-force-sensitive signin/verify/authorize/login 10/5 minutes; signup 10/5 minutes; OAuth2 server-to-server 100/5 minutes; total Auth 100/minute.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: Cloud centralized logs include Auth with service/time-range/regex filters; public docs do not give a complete security-event catalog, retention-days matrix, export/streaming guarantees or audit-log surcharge.

facts.label: Export — profiles, identifiers and hashes
facts.value: Self-service Postgres access and pg_dump/database backups can carry auth.users identifiers, profiles and bcrypt password_hash values; relational provider records can be included in a database export.

facts.label: Export — credential portability limits
facts.value: Exporting relational rows does not establish that another vendor accepts Nhost hashes, encrypted provider tokens, refresh sessions or WebAuthn keys. Passkeys retain relying-party/domain constraints.

facts.label: Import and migration in
facts.value: Official guide imports users through direct SQL or GraphQL, preserving supplied IDs and password_hash; passwords use bcrypt.

facts.label: Import — compatibility and lazy migration
facts.value: Supported foreign bcrypt variants/cost ranges, bulk import limits, non-bcrypt hash support and a built-in lazy password-migration callback were not located.

facts.label: Deletion and retention — live app data
facts.value: User removal can be implemented through controlled database/GraphQL access; no DELETE /user Auth endpoint. Developer must handle related app rows and a safe self-service deletion flow.

facts.label: Deletion and retention — Cloud policies
facts.value: DPA section 9.1 provides deletion of covered copies within 10 business days after cessation; Pro/Team daily backup retention is 7 days. Individual-user purge timing across logs/backups is not specified.

facts.label: Data location — Cloud
facts.value: Public status components name Northern Virginia, Frankfurt, Sweden, London, Singapore, Mumbai and Sydney; privacy hints says the subscriber chooses a region.

facts.label: Data location — complete residency boundary
facts.value: Exact current signup-region choices and plan gates, log/backup/support processing locations, and a comprehensive data-category residency guarantee were not established.

facts.label: Privacy evidence — agreement and subprocessors
facts.value: Public DPA describes Nhost as processor for customer-controlled data; agreement page offers a pre-signed PDF to complete and email. Privacy-hints subprocessor list names Amazon and subscriber-chosen region.

facts.label: Assurance evidence — SOC 2 / HIPAA
facts.value: Vendor claims SOC 2 Type II; report available to Team and Enterprise customers through Dashboard. HIPAA is explicitly 'coming soon'.

facts.label: Security claims and encryption caveat
facts.value: Security page claims AES-256 at rest and TLS in transit; compute guide says only volumes provisioned after December 2024 are encrypted and explains pause/unpause migration.

facts.label: Name, aliases, owner, URLs
facts.value: Nhost Auth, the authentication service in Nhost's backend platform; website owner Nhost AB (Sweden). Older source repository is called Hasura Auth.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle — current offer
facts.value: Cloud Starter, Pro, Team and Enterprise offers remain publicly available; no whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in this bounded official review. Signup not tested.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle — old repository
facts.value: nhost/hasura-auth is deprecated; its README directs all development to nhost/nhost.

facts.label: License — self-hosted Auth
facts.value: MIT at auth@0.52.0; commercial use, modification and redistribution permitted subject to preserving the copyright and permission notice.

facts.label: License — Cloud and website terms
facts.value: Cloud is a paid or free managed service; public website Terms of Service last revised 2025-02-11. Section 6 restricts downloaded website materials to personal, noncommercial viewing.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Public Nhost status page reports incidents and per-region service components.

facts.label: Cloud availability promise
facts.value: Pricing lists 99.9% SLA only on Enterprise; Starter/Pro/Team do not have the comparison-table entitlement. Public SLA page specifies support targets, not full uptime measurement/credit terms.

facts.label: Release and maintenance — Auth server
facts.value: Latest stable Auth release located: auth@0.52.0, published 2026-09-15T11:13:53Z; config default 0.52.0. auth@0.53.0-beta1 is a prerelease published 2026-10-29.

facts.label: Security policy and version support
facts.value: Public SECURITY.md asks for private vulnerability reports and says investigation begins within 72 hours; no dated LTS/end-of-support matrix found. Auth changelog documents recent security and session fixes.

facts.label: Support — Cloud plans
facts.value: Starter community; Pro email; Team email SLA and dedicated Discord; Enterprise dedicated technical account manager and 24x7x365 support with SLA.

facts.label: Support — published response targets
facts.value: SLA page Premium/Standard: urgent <2/<4 hours; high <4/<8 business hours; normal <8/<16; low <16/<24. Business hours 08:00–17:00 CET.

facts.label: Resource overages by plan
facts.value: Free: $0.06/million extra tokens, $1.50/extra GB. Pro: $0.05/million, $1.00/GB. Scale: $0.04/million, $0.75/GB.

facts.label: Auth calculator conflict
facts.value: Scale display says 500M included tokens, calculation code uses 1B; Free calculation returns zero regardless of usage.

facts.label: Billing precision and extras
facts.value: No complete storage aggregation, token rounding, tax, paid-security add-on or provisioned-compute price schedule established.

facts.label: Business pricing scope
facts.value: Organizations/invites/memberships exist, but SAML availability is inconsistent; no fully usable fixed-SAML baseline total established.

facts.label: Customer organization limits
facts.value: Unlimited active tenants and MAUs per tenant advertised on all plans; no separate standard tenant charge listed.

facts.label: Invites and member caps
facts.value: Built-in emailed invitations; no published per-tenant member count, invitation quota or separately priced invite fee found.

facts.label: Enterprise connection and SCIM fees
facts.value: No per-SAML/OIDC enterprise connection count, setup fee or SCIM directory tariff established.

facts.label: Developer workspace and apps
facts.value: Unlimited databases; Free lacks workspace sharing, Pro/Scale include it.

facts.label: Environments and domains
facts.value: No fixed production/staging app count, developer seat count or auth-domain allowance table established.

facts.label: Login and lifecycle email
facts.value: Builder supplies SMTP provider/settings and valid sender for magic links, verification, reset and invitations; customizable HTML templates.

facts.label: SMS and country/channel tariffs
facts.value: No built-in SMS/WhatsApp/voice primary login route or associated rate card established.

facts.label: Resource limit behavior
facts.value: Nile says it contacts near limits, sends notice near 70%, and usually permits paying for more capacity without upgrading, including Free.

facts.label: Stay on Free with overage
facts.value: Official pricing article says Free can be retained indefinitely; enter payment information to pay extra usage.

facts.label: Resource costs beyond auth
facts.value: Connections: Free 500, Pro 10,000, Scale 100,000; compute/storage also used by app data share workspace allowances.

facts.label: Backups relevant to identity recovery
facts.value: Paid tiers have assisted database backup/restore, three daily backups; backup team acknowledges urgent request within 15 minutes.

facts.label: Market and eligibility
facts.value: B2B product for businesses/representatives; public terms require 18+. No exhaustive seller-country allowlist or sole-builder company requirement found.

facts.label: Self-service entry
facts.value: Public console and pricing advertise self-service Free/Pro/Scale entry; signup not tested.

facts.label: Production and free-tier framing
facts.value: Free is advertised for prototyping/side projects and never pauses; Pro is recommended for production with SLA.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Auth service with user accounts, login, sessions, tenant membership/management and embedded UI; managed and self-hosted routes.

facts.label: Tenant-aware access
facts.value: User may belong to multiple tenants; SDK context scopes API/database access to a selected tenant.

facts.label: Managed operations
facts.value: Nile runs hosted database/auth; builder runs application routes/proxy, provider setup, email delivery account and authorization configuration.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: Builder can run the auth server/Next.js service and supply database settings; local testing image includes Nile Postgres and optional auth.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built-in email/password; bcrypt verification in source. Users guide discourages passwords for production and recommends social alternatives.

facts.label: Email magic link
facts.value: Built-in passwordless link; configured SMTP; token stored in auth.verification_tokens, default validity 4 hours.

facts.label: Other primary login methods
facts.value: No documented primary phone OTP, guest/anonymous account creation, wallet sign-in or standalone email-code login established.

facts.label: Google and GitHub
facts.value: Documented Google/GitHub OAuth integrations with own client ID/secret, callback to builder's app and React login buttons.

facts.label: Microsoft Azure
facts.value: Documented Azure app registration, client secret and Directory tenant ID integration.

facts.label: Discord and LinkedIn
facts.value: Documented provider integrations with client ID/secret, configured callbacks and login buttons.

facts.label: HubSpot, X and Slack
facts.value: Documented OAuth integrations; each needs provider registration and client configuration.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: No public built-in WebAuthn/passkey enrollment, sign-in, recovery, conditional UI or mobile compatibility guide established.

facts.label: MFA factors
facts.value: Native authenticator-app TOTP and email one-time codes; setup/challenge/removal APIs and React components documented.

facts.label: MFA recovery
facts.value: Authenticator setup produces recovery keys; source generates 7, hashes them and consumes a matching key once.

facts.label: MFA challenge limits
facts.value: Source challenge lifetime: authenticator 30 seconds, email 2 minutes; email code generated with 6 digits.

facts.label: Verification
facts.value: SMTP email verification links and middleware check emailVerified; dashboard can manually verify/unverify.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Built-in two-step emailed reset link, default token validity 4 hours; reset request and new-password components.

facts.label: Email change and deletion
facts.value: Current-user profile API cannot modify email/id/tenants; removeSelf performs soft deletion.

facts.label: Session types and expiry
facts.value: Docs: password login uses JWT; other providers use database sessions. Default expiry is 30 days.

facts.label: Cookie and sign-out model
facts.value: Secure HttpOnly session cookie with SameSite=Lax; SDK signOut clears server session/CSRF context; browser sign-out component clears browser cookies.

facts.label: JWT revocation conflict
facts.value: Docs call JWT sessions stateless/non-revocable. Current source requires a JWT sid that matches an unexpired database session and a non-deleted user.

facts.label: Membership versus sign-out
facts.value: Removing a membership does not delete the account, remove other memberships or invalidate existing session tokens.

facts.label: OAuth/OIDC role
facts.value: Documented client/relying-party integration with external providers, including Microsoft Azure; per-tenant provider restrictions.

facts.label: SAML availability
facts.value: Paid pricing includes SAML check marks; current auth README says OIDC/OAuth and soon SAML; FAQ says SSO not yet supported despite provider docs.

facts.label: Organizations and selection
facts.value: TenantSelector lists/switches organizations, persists choice in a cookie and supports creating a tenant.

facts.label: Memberships, roles and invitations
facts.value: Membership table has roles text[]; SDK offers member add/remove/list and emailed invitation acceptance.

facts.label: Tenant-specific auth and administration
facts.value: Developer console manages tenants/users and can disable selected auth providers per tenant.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: No native SCIM 2.0 user/group provisioning endpoint, directory sync price or deactivation semantics established.

facts.label: Ready-made auth UI
facts.value: React sign-in, signup, sign-out, user/profile and tenant selector components; MFA setup/challenge and reset components documented.

facts.label: Headless integration
facts.value: Server/client APIs and React hooks can drive own UI; server routes proxy auth calls.

facts.label: UI and email branding
facts.value: React/Tailwind components accept CSS classes/variables and some text props; hooks allow custom components. HTML email templates are builder-controlled.

facts.label: Domains and callbacks
facts.value: App hosts its UI/proxy and configures provider callback URLs; callbackUrl/origin/routes can be overridden.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: No official locale catalog or auth-component WCAG/VPAT conformance report established.

facts.label: Framework support
facts.value: Official guides list Next.js, Express, React, Remix, Nitro, Nuxt and Elysia.

facts.label: Server runtime and SDK boundary
facts.value: TypeScript/JavaScript service and SDK; auth server is a Next.js application; REST API available to other languages.

facts.label: Native mobile and other clients
facts.value: No official Swift/Kotlin/React Native/Flutter auth SDK, mobile passkey guide or native secure-session storage contract established.

facts.label: Auth database dependency conflict
facts.value: Auth intro says self-hosted auth still uses hosted Nile Postgres; README says any PostgreSQL database, migration guide describes creating required tables.

facts.label: Other prerequisites
facts.value: Application backend routes, database credentials/connection, provider client credentials and optional SMTP account.

facts.label: Self-host deployment routes
facts.value: Docker Compose and Helm chart supplied; local testingcontainer combines Nile Postgres and auth.

facts.label: Production operations evidence
facts.value: No complete self-host HA, secure backup rotation, capacity benchmark, supported upgrade cadence or recovery SLA established.

facts.label: Custom context and hooks
facts.value: SDK extensions provide pre/post processing per API request; configuration supports routes, headers, tenant/user context and custom logger.

facts.label: Profile data and events
facts.value: Tenant table can be extended for app metadata; current-user SDK accepts a fixed profile-field list. No complete auth lifecycle webhook contract found.

facts.label: Developer user administration
facts.value: Console supports user create/search/edit/delete and manual email verification; last-login column helps identify inactive users.

facts.label: Application API administration
facts.value: Current-user SDK has get/update/delete-self; tenant module lists/mutates members. No packaged permanent ban/support impersonation portal established.

facts.label: Automatic identity linking
facts.value: Same-email SSO methods link to one user ID. Mixing password and SSO requires email verification; existing SSO user can add password through reset.

facts.label: Unlinking and guest upgrade
facts.value: No documented end-user unlink-provider API or native guest-account conversion workflow established.

facts.label: Browser flow protections
facts.value: Secure/HttpOnly cookies, CSRF token, OAuth state/nonce and PKCE cookies documented; password source verifies bcrypt hashes.

facts.label: Automated abuse controls
facts.value: No built-in CAPTCHA, compromised-password database, credential lockout policy or SMS fraud-control schedule established.

facts.label: Rate and burst limits
facts.value: No public auth/login/Admin requests-per-window, tenant/user/IP quota or retry-after policy established.

facts.label: Available account/activity evidence
facts.value: Developer users dashboard has last-login; tenant insights retention Free 1 day, Pro 2 weeks, Scale 2 months.

facts.label: Security audit stream
facts.value: No complete login/factor/admin-change event catalog, export/webhook delivery contract or auth audit-log retention fee established.

facts.label: Profile/credential export access
facts.value: User, membership, session and credential tables are documented and accessible in own database; scripts can extract data via SQL.

facts.label: OAuth tokens and portability
facts.value: Source stores provider access/refresh tokens in credentials payload; app/provider callbacks and credentials need reconfiguration when leaving.

facts.label: Auth0 migration
facts.value: Official guide imports users/organizations with custom SQL/script; without usable hashes users reset passwords; staged fallback is app logic.

facts.label: Firebase hash compatibility
facts.value: Migration guide explicitly supports importing password hashes only when bcrypt is used; otherwise reset/passwordless login needed.

facts.label: NextAuth migration
facts.value: Guide maps users/accounts/sessions/verification tokens into Nile tables; integer user IDs require mapping to UUIDs.

facts.label: User and tenant deletion
facts.value: User removeSelf and tenant delete are soft deletes; tenant data can remain and tenant can be restored.

facts.label: Database closure and billing
facts.value: Delete database marks it and queues data deletion; connections can still work and compute charges apply until deletion completes.

facts.label: Retention policy scope
facts.value: Public privacy retention is purpose/legal based; backup archives may be isolated until deletion is possible. It excludes customer-processed platform data.

facts.label: Database regions
facts.value: 2024 announcement offers AWS us-west-2 Oregon and eu-central-1 Frankfurt; current API schema also includes AZURE_EASTUS.

facts.label: Residency limits
facts.value: No auth-specific contractual region/backup/log residency matrix or exclusive-country processing guarantee established.

facts.label: Customer privacy and processor evidence
facts.value: Policy effective 06/10/2022 excludes data processed for business customers; that is governed by customer agreements.

facts.label: Assurance and certifications
facts.value: Pricing SOC 2 entries are labelled coming soon; no audit report/certificate scope or assessed auth controls established.

facts.label: Name, operator and URLs
facts.value: Nile Auth; operated within Nile Platform Inc. Product thenile.dev/auth; documentation /docs/auth/introduction; source niledatabase/nile-auth.

facts.label: Operating and new-customer evidence
facts.value: Public site advertises Build for free; console has Get Started with Google/GitHub. No shutdown, sunset, acquisition or closed-signup notice found.

facts.label: Status and lifecycle qualification
facts.value: Official status reports Website/App operational; repositories unarchived with recent changes. Support page still calls platform technical preview.

facts.label: Auth source license
facts.value: Nile Auth repository MIT: commercial use, modification and distribution allowed under notice/warranty conditions.

facts.label: Hosted legal scope
facts.value: Public terms identify site access as personal/noncommercial; complete hosted subscription/service-use agreement not established.

facts.label: Status and advertised SLA
facts.value: Official public status page; Pro pricing advertises 99.95%, Scale 99.99%; Free no SLA.

facts.label: SLA contract details
facts.value: No full contractual availability measurement, claim deadline, exclusions or service-credit schedule established.

facts.label: Maintenance and archive status
facts.value: Auth repository not archived; latest main commit read dated 2026-10-26 updates Dependabot/CI/release restrictions.

facts.label: Version/support policy
facts.value: No GitHub releases listed, no supported-version/EOL matrix established; auth server package is private with 0.0.0 placeholder version.

facts.label: Support routes and plan split
facts.value: Discord, GitHub discussions and support@thenile.dev; Free community/email; Pro email-with-SLA; Scale designated support advertised.

facts.label: Response promise limits
facts.value: Paid backup/restore page promises acknowledgment within 15 minutes; no general all-incident response hours/target established.

cells.freeUsers: No licence user cap; you host

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: MIT module has no licence fee or licence-imposed monthly app-user production cap.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable: no required paid-core subscription, minimum usage spend or annual production contract.

facts.label: Usage rate card
facts.value: Not applicable: no core usage bands, overage rates, message packs or billing rounding.

facts.label: Business comparison
facts.value: Complete A/B organization/invitation/role plus 1/10 SAML-connection baseline unsupported by module alone.

facts.label: Organization quota/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted customer organizations/member caps or organization billing allowance.

facts.label: SSO/directory fee model
facts.value: Not applicable to module: no per-SAML/OIDC/SCIM connection subscription or setup fee.

facts.label: Seats/projects/environments
facts.value: Not applicable: no module developer-dashboard seats, app count, environment or domain cap.

facts.label: Message sending
facts.value: custom_code app sends confirmation/reset/login notifications through chosen provider; module is not a mail/SMS delivery service.

facts.label: Delivery allowance/rates
facts.value: Not applicable: no bundled send quota, country/channel tariff or carrier surcharge.

facts.label: Vendor quota exhaustion
facts.value: Not applicable: no core hosted pause, automatic upgrade, recharge, spending cap or billing alert.

facts.label: Other billable meters
facts.value: Not applicable: no module request/token/security/audit/transaction usage bill.

facts.label: Technical session-size limit
facts.value: Nuxt 4.6 sealed cookie serialized limit 4096 bytes; oversized session write throws HTTP 500.

facts.label: Core account/country eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to library use: no vendor production signup, seller-country whitelist or company-domain approval.

facts.label: Self-service/trial/card
facts.value: Not applicable: public module installation, not a hosted trial, card requirement or sales-led tenant.

facts.label: Product scope
facts.value: Nuxt server module for sealed-cookie sessions, OAuth callback helpers, password hashing and optional WebAuthn/AT Protocol helpers.

facts.label: Stateless session versus account storage
facts.value: Session data lives in encrypted/sealed browser cookie; account/credential persistence is app-owned when required.

facts.label: Operator responsibilities
facts.value: Builder deploys Nuxt server, manages app secret, user/credential stores, runtime updates, delivery and backups.

facts.label: Password login building blocks
facts.value: built_in hashPassword, verifyPassword and passwordNeedsReHash use Scrypt; app supplies user lookup/login endpoint and sets session.

facts.label: Passwordless sign-in
facts.value: Optional WebAuthn integration provides passkey register/authenticate handlers; OAuth helpers delegate login to providers.

facts.label: Email-link/code, phone and wallet methods
facts.value: Native general email magic-link/code, SMS login or wallet-auth flow not established.

facts.label: Anonymous identity
facts.value: Anonymous session GET returns empty object without creating a cookie; no packaged persisted-guest identity/upgrade system established.

facts.label: Google and GitHub
facts.value: built_in OAuth event-handler helpers for Google and GitHub; provider app credentials/callback setup required.

facts.label: Apple and Microsoft
facts.value: built_in Apple and Microsoft provider handlers; Apple requires team/key/private-key/client identifiers; Microsoft requires tenant/client credentials.

facts.label: Other OAuth providers
facts.value: Module advertises 40+ providers; configured handlers include Discord, Facebook, GitLab, Spotify, Twitch and X.

facts.label: AT Protocol
facts.value: Optional atproto:true integration for Bluesky requires @atproto/oauth-client-node and @atproto/api peers.

facts.label: Passkey integration and peers
facts.value: Optional built-in WebAuthn helpers enabled with auth.webAuthn:true; SimpleWebAuthn server ^13.3.2 and browser ^13 peers required.

facts.label: Registration/storage
facts.value: Register handler returns credential ID/public key/counter/transports/backup metadata; app onSuccess stores user and credential.

facts.label: Challenge/replay boundary
facts.value: Without storeChallenge/getChallenge hooks, helpers use an empty challenge; README strongly recommends storing and consuming single-use challenges.

facts.label: Device verification and RP binding
facts.value: Verification expects current request origin/hostname; requireUserVerification:false; registration prefers device verification but does not enforce it.

facts.label: Browser/autofill client
facts.value: useWebAuthn exposes browser/platform/autofill capability checks and optional useBrowserAutofill:false default.

facts.label: MFA/recovery codes
facts.value: Native TOTP/SMS/email second-factor enrollment, enforcement, backup recovery codes and lost-device recovery not established.

facts.label: Verification/reset/change/delete
facts.value: Core account-verification, password-reset, email-change and self-delete workflows are app code or external-provider work.

facts.label: Sealed cookie/session format
facts.value: v0.6 uses Nuxt server session; cookie default nuxt-auth-session, sealed using key derived from NUXT_APP_SECRET.

facts.label: Cookie defaults
facts.value: Underlying Nuxt 4.6 defaults HttpOnly true, Secure true, SameSite lax, path /; runtimeConfig.session.cookie can override.

facts.label: Lifetime and renewal
facts.value: maxAge is configurable seconds and each write renews it. With default options and no maxAge, cookie has no Max-Age; sealed TTL 0 means no expiry.

facts.label: Session get/set/replace
facts.value: setUserSession merges with defu; replaceUserSession replaces data; both preserve session ID through update; clear creates/clears current session.

facts.label: Client-visible versus secure data
facts.value: GET /api/_auth/session removes top-level secure field; other session/user data is returned to client.

facts.label: Logout/revocation scope
facts.value: clearUserSession expires current cookie; no server-side session denylist or device registry supplied by default.

facts.label: Fetch-hook enforcement boundary
facts.value: sessionHooks.fetch runs on session GET; requireUserSession only checks presence of user after reading session.

facts.label: Generic OIDC client
facts.value: built_in defineOAuthOidcEventHandler supports discovery URL or explicit endpoints, authorization-code exchange, PKCE, state and nonce checks.

facts.label: External business identity helper
facts.value: WorkOS handler accepts organizationId/connectionId and returns provider user/access/refresh tokens to app callback.

facts.label: SAML/issuer roles
facts.value: Native SAML SP/IdP, generic OIDC issuer and per-customer SSO connection-management API not established.

facts.label: Roles and tenant models
facts.value: custom_code app can put IDs/roles in session and check database/policies; module only validates presence of user in requireUserSession.

facts.label: Customer organizations/invitations
facts.value: Packaged customer workspace creation, memberships/invitations and customer-admin UI not established.

facts.label: Optional authorization extension
facts.value: plugin nuxt-authorization provides low-level abilities and server/client allows/denies/authorize helpers; explicitly not ACL/RBAC itself.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: Native SCIM user/group provisioning, deactivation workflow and directory connector not established.

facts.label: Ready-made UI scope
facts.value: AuthState is a renderless scoped-slot helper exposing loggedIn/user/session/clear after ready; no login form or account portal.

facts.label: Browser session composable
facts.value: useUserSession exposes ready, loggedIn, user, session, fetch, clear and popup OAuth flow.

facts.label: Passkey example UI
facts.value: README/playground demonstrates register/sign-in forms; production credential listing/recovery/admin screens are app work.

facts.label: Branding/custom domains
facts.value: Operator controls Nuxt routes, frontend and app domain; no module branding-removal or custom-domain price gate.

facts.label: Shared session scope
facts.value: Shared app secret + cookie name and parent cookie domain can share sessions across trusted subdomains/apps.

facts.label: Language/accessibility catalogue
facts.value: Not applicable to core renderless/headless module: no vendor-hosted language pack list or final login-screen accessibility score.

facts.label: Framework/version requirements
facts.value: v0.6.1 requires Nuxt >=4.6.0; Nuxt 4/Nitro 2 and Nuxt 5/Nitro 3 event compatibility described.

facts.label: Node compatibility
facts.value: Exact v0.6.1 engines.node range: ^22.22.3 or ^24.15.0 or >=26.0.0.

facts.label: Other runtimes/Cloudflare
facts.value: README advertises Node/Deno/Workers; Workers need compatibility date >=2025-04-01 or nodejs_compat_populate_process_env flag to read runtime secrets.

facts.label: SSR/hybrid session loading
facts.value: SSR authenticated requests use useRequestFetch or useFetch to forward request context; default server-first, optional client-only/none loading.

facts.label: Browser versus native clients
facts.value: Vue/browser composables and cookie-based server helpers are documented; dedicated native iOS/Android/Flutter auth SDK not established.

facts.label: WebSocket behavior
facts.value: requireUserSession can check upgrade/peer session; set/replace/clear helpers reject WebSocket contexts as read-only.

facts.label: Session prerequisites
facts.value: Compatible Nuxt server and production app secret; no database/cache needed solely to carry sealed session data.

facts.label: Account and passkey storage
facts.value: App supplies user/password/provider-link store; WebAuthn callbacks store public-key credentials/counters; optional DB/KV challenge store.

facts.label: Optional dependency groups
facts.value: WebAuthn and AT Protocol peers installed/enabled separately; built-in Scrypt utilities depend on @adonisjs/hash.

facts.label: Deployment/operations
facts.value: Deploy a running Nuxt server, configure runtime secrets/provider credentials and preserve account/credential storage/backups.

facts.label: Upgrade migration
facts.value: 0.5→0.6 requires new NUXT_APP_SECRET, removal of old session password configuration, new cookie format and callback event imports.

facts.label: Session hooks
facts.value: sessionHooks.fetch can enrich/reject API-fetched session; clear runs before session clearing.

facts.label: Provider/passkey callbacks
facts.value: OAuth onSuccess/onError and WebAuthn validation/storage/options/success callbacks implement app logic.

facts.label: Custom fields and security boundary
facts.value: Type-augmentable User, UserSession and SecureSessionData; session secure data omitted only by built-in session GET.

facts.label: User administration

facts.label: Banning/impersonation

facts.value: Provider helpers return user/tokens to callback; application chooses persistent account match and link/unlink policy.

facts.label: Passkey linking
facts.value: Registration validateUser callback can check current session before associating a new credential; app persists account relationship.

facts.label: Guest upgrade/merge
facts.value: No packaged persisted-guest upgrade, account merge or provider-unlink management workflow established.

facts.label: Password controls
facts.value: Scrypt hash/verify/rehash helpers; no automatic user lookup timing equalization or app password policy included.

facts.label: OAuth transaction cookies
facts.value: State/nonce/PKCE helpers use short-lived 600-second HttpOnly cookies, normally Secure and SameSite lax.

facts.label: OIDC validation scope
facts.value: Generic OIDC helper checks state, PKCE and nonce; parseJwt uses jose.decodeJwt for ID-token claims.

facts.label: Passkey validation scope
facts.value: Helper verifies origin/RP ID/signature via SimpleWebAuthn; required device user verification is false and replay challenge storage opt-in.

facts.label: App abuse/CSRF controls
facts.value: Native universal API CSRF middleware, CAPTCHA, breached-password screening and managed SMS-abuse controls not established.

facts.label: Hosted request quota
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor-managed login/API rate card or per-plan concurrent-request allowance.

facts.label: Core throttling
facts.value: No fixed built-in per-user/IP login, challenge, session or management request throttle established.

facts.label: Audit hooks
facts.value: Fetch/clear hooks and OAuth/WebAuthn callbacks can feed app-owned security logging.

facts.label: Managed log retention/fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor audit-retention days, log-streaming entitlement or per-event storage charge.

facts.label: Profile/credential export
facts.value: custom_code/operator export of own DB can include account IDs, profiles, password hashes, provider links and WebAuthn public-key records.

facts.label: Session/passkey portability
facts.value: Session cookies require matching secret/name/format; v0.6 invalidates older format. WebAuthn expects current request origin/hostname.

facts.label: Hash import/rehash
facts.value: App may import supported Scrypt hashes and use verifyPassword/passwordNeedsReHash; choose compatible encoding/configuration.

facts.label: Bulk/lazy migration tooling
facts.value: Turnkey cross-vendor importer, arbitrary bcrypt/Argon2 compatibility or lazy credential-migration bridge not established.

facts.label: Deletion scope

facts.label: Vendor retention/closure

facts.label: Hosted processing/assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to core module: no vendor-operated identity processor DPA, subprocessor inventory or hosted-auth SOC tier.

facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted trial. Installation/configuration is self-directed and needs no OmniAuth sales, payment card or company-domain signup.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Ruby/Rack middleware framework for provider authentication. Strategies run request/callback phases and return normalized data in env['omniauth.auth'].

facts.label: Core versus provider strategies
facts.value: Only Developer strategy ships in core, explicitly insecure and unsuitable for production. Real provider/password/SAML/OIDC strategies are separate gems or app code.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer/chosen host operates app/callbacks, account and identity stores, session middleware, external credentials, upgrades, keys, logs and backups.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-identity 3.2.1 (MIT), with app-owned Identity persistence/model; provides traditional password authentication and optional registration, returning an OmniAuth callback.

facts.label: Email magic links/codes, phone, wallet
facts.value: custom_code/external strategy or IdP required for email-link/code, verified phone-code or wallet-signature login; none is a production core strategy.

facts.label: Anonymous/saved guests
facts.value: custom_code/account framework required for persisted guest accounts and upgrade; core only supplies authentication middleware/callback data.

facts.label: Provider strategy model
facts.value: One or more independently installed strategy gems supply external protocol/API details. Builder composes multiple Rack middlewares; each provider needs its own credentials/options.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-google-oauth2 1.2.3, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0, omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8, OAuth2 ~>2.0, JWT >=2.9.2,<4.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-github 2.0.1, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0 and omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8. Strategy supports configurable GitHub Enterprise endpoints.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-apple 1.4.0, MIT; json-jwt and omniauth-oauth2 dependencies; Sign in with Apple strategy.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-microsoft_graph 2.2.0, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0, omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8.0, JWT >=2.0,<4.

facts.label: Custom/generic OAuth2
facts.value: plugin building block omniauth-oauth2 1.10.0 (MIT), requiring OmniAuth ~>2.3 >=2.3.1 and OAuth2 >=2.0.2,<3; subclass supplies UID/profile logic.

facts.label: Passkeys and WebAuthn
facts.value: No bundled WebAuthn registration/assertion verification, authenticator inventory or conditional-autofill UI; external IdP/strategy or account-layer code required.

facts.label: MFA and recovery
facts.value: No core TOTP/SMS/email/security-key second-factor enrollment, enforcement or recovery-code store. Upstream IdP/account layer or separate strategy supplies factors and policy.

facts.label: Verification/reset/account changes
facts.value: Application/account framework or IdP owns email/phone verification, password reset/change and user self-deletion. Core does not implement those account lifecycle routes.

facts.label: App login session
facts.value: Application must create, keep and end its own authenticated session after callback. OmniAuth requires a Rack session for transaction continuity but does not sign a local User in.

facts.label: Callback state and cookies
facts.value: Rack session preserves request/callback data. SameSite=Lax typically permits top-level GET callbacks; Strict can lose session; cross-site POST SAML/OIDC form_post needs compatible None; Secure cookie setup.

facts.label: Several in-progress logins
facts.value: Core 2.3 opt-in strategy API remembers latest 5 keyed origin/params records in session['omniauth.sign_ins']; callback consumes matching record, otherwise falls back to latest single fields.

facts.label: OAuth2 transaction state/PKCE
facts.value: omniauth-oauth2 1.10.0 tracks latest 5 state/redirect/PKCE records, checks returned state by default and supports PKCE S256 when pkce=true; pkce defaults false.

facts.label: Provider tokens and refresh
facts.value: Auth hash may carry token/secret/refresh_token/expires/expires_at from provider strategy. Core has no app access/refresh-token issuer or token-family database.

facts.label: Logout/revocation
facts.value: Local logout and revoking sessions/provider tokens are app/strategy/IdP work; no core all-devices sign-out endpoint or automatic password-change revocation.

facts.label: SAML SP/browser login
facts.value: plugin: omniauth-saml 2.2.5 (MIT), OmniAuth ~>2.1 and ruby-saml ~>1.18; docs require Ruby 3.1.x+. Supplies SAML service-provider login and SP metadata.

facts.label: OIDC relying-party role
facts.value: plugin: omniauth_openid_connect 0.8.0 (MIT), OmniAuth >=1.9,<3 and openid_connect ~>2.2; client/RP strategy with issuer/discovery and provider token/user-info processing.

facts.label: OAuth/OIDC/SAML server role
facts.value: Core is provider-login middleware, not an OAuth/OIDC authorization server or SAML identity-provider implementation; issuing federation credentials requires another product/code.

facts.label: Customer organizations/authorization
facts.value: custom_code/account framework required for workspaces, memberships, invitations, tenant roles and customer administration.

facts.label: SCIM account synchronization
facts.value: No bundled SCIM Users/Groups, directory connection/deactivation behavior or official core SCIM integration established.

facts.label: Core screens
facts.value: Core's form helper and Developer screen are development building blocks; core supplies no production registration/reset/profile/account-center product.

facts.label: Local-password strategy UI
facts.value: omniauth-identity adds login/registration forms and custom Rack endpoint/form options; application supplies persistence/model and local User association/session.

facts.label: Branding/custom domains
facts.value: App owns login/callback UI, labels, route prefix and domain; MIT has no branding-removal/domain-count fee. full_host can be fixed globally or per strategy.

facts.label: Languages/localization scope
facts.value: No bundled production account-UI language catalogue. App/IdP owns user-facing account screens; core Form and optional Identity labels/messages can be customized.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No OmniAuth-specific public WCAG assessment, VPAT or completed accessibility conformance report found.

facts.label: Core runtime/framework requirements
facts.value: OmniAuth 2.3.1 requires Ruby >=2.5 and Rack >=2.2.8; Rack middleware supports Rails/Sinatra or other compatible Rack apps.

facts.label: Rails/API integration
facts.value: README shows Rails middleware and callback controller. Rails API-only apps must add cookies/session middleware with actual session_options; CSRF validator must match app token handling.

facts.label: Rails CSRF optional package
facts.value: omniauth-rails_csrf_protection 2.0.1 (MIT; actionpack >=4.2, OmniAuth ~>2.0) is a maintained alternative Rails-aware request-token verifier.

facts.label: Mobile/desktop clients
facts.value: No official core iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop SDK or platform/passkey compatibility matrix found.

facts.label: Core prerequisites
facts.value: Core runtime dependencies: hashie >=3.5.2, logger, Rack >=2.2.8 and rack-protection >=2.2.0. Must provide Rack session before strategy handling.

facts.label: Local account/credential persistence
facts.value: App supplies user/identity records and provider secrets. Optional Identity supports chosen ORM adapters, with password_digest/secure-password model interfaces.

facts.label: Operation/upgrades/backups
facts.value: Deploy with Ruby/Rack app; configure provider credentials/callbacks, trusted host, CSRF and session middleware; patch core/strategies and back up app identity/session data and keys.

facts.label: Sizing/restore evidence
facts.value: No universal hardware sizing, MAU-to-capacity table, login throughput guarantee or complete deployment-independent backup/restore runbook found.

facts.label: Custom strategies/setup
facts.value: Core supports strategy subclasses/mixin, UID/info/credentials/extra fetchers, custom paths/forms and request-time setup Proc/app endpoint.

facts.label: Hooks/events/webhooks
facts.value: before_options, request_validation, before_request, after_request, before_callback and on_failure hooks receive Rack env. No operated event queue/webhook retries or delivery contract.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Core has no create/search/ban/delete user API, admin dashboard or impersonation workflow; application/account framework performs them.

facts.label: Linking identities
facts.value: custom_code: official wiki models User separately from Identity(provider,uid) and shows app-written callback linking decisions.

facts.label: Guest upgrade/data merge
facts.value: custom_code/account framework required; core provides no saved-guest upgrade or transfer of app-owned records.

facts.label: Request-phase CSRF
facts.value: Core defaults allowed_request_methods=[:post] and AuthenticityTokenProtection request validator; form must include a compatible CSRF token/session. Rails token key/validator needs configuration.

facts.label: CSRF guide wording conflict
facts.value: Wiki prose says older apps should 'only accept get requests', but the same section's config is [:post]; current core code and guide context require POST request initiation.

facts.label: Host/origin protection
facts.value: 2.3.1 can use fixed full_host or allowed_hosts string/whole-host regex allowlist. With neither configured, request host remains usable and core logs a warning.

facts.label: Account/bot protections
facts.value: No core account lockout, password-breach feed, CAPTCHA, device-risk, MFA or SMS-budget policy. App/gateway/IdP or chosen strategy supplies those controls.

facts.label: API/login request limits
facts.value: No OmniAuth-operated numeric request quota, per-IP/login throttle or universal burst/requests-per-second contract.

facts.label: Logging/audit events
facts.value: Core configurable logger defaults STDOUT; logs strategy request/callback/setup and failures, and exposes hooks/error env data to the app.

facts.label: Credential/privacy handling
facts.value: Auth hash can contain access/refresh tokens, secrets and provider profile/raw_info; app decides what to persist/log. Core filters authenticity_token from request params saved for callback.

facts.label: Profile and identifier exit
facts.value: Callback exposes provider + provider-specific uid and available profile fields; app may persist/export its own records through database/tooling. No core bulk-user export service/format or exit fee.

facts.label: Passwords/factors/tokens export
facts.value: Core has no password/factor database. Upstream social passwords/private passkey keys are not supplied by auth hash; tokens/expiry may be present. Optional Identity hashes belong to app-owned storage.

facts.label: Import users/credentials
facts.value: No core bulk/lazy user import or password-hash migration facility. App maps existing provider/uid/account IDs; optional Identity can use an existing/custom persistence model and compatible password_digest data.

facts.label: Middleware/API migration
facts.value: Changelog documents 2.0 POST/CSRF changes, 2.2 runtime/param/Builder changes and 2.3 sign-in state support; old schema used user_info, current schema uses info.

facts.label: User data deletion
facts.value: App/account framework deletes local users/identities, invalidates sessions/provider tokens and applies associated-record/log/backup retention. No core account-deletion route or erasure deadline.

facts.label: Transient data/closure
facts.value: Core stores transaction metadata in supplied Rack session and consumes callback records; session lifecycle, residual keys/log retention and app shutdown are operator-controlled.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: Self-chosen app/account/session/log/backup infrastructure plus configured provider endpoints; no OmniAuth-hosted user region selector.

facts.label: Hosted privacy/DPA/subprocessors
facts.value: Not applicable to core as an operated identity-data processor; middleware runs in builder's application.

facts.label: Independent assurance
facts.value: No core-specific public SOC 2/ISO attestation or completed independent security audit report established.
