facts.label: Client and validation stacks
facts.value: Client connects to remote OAuth/OIDC providers; validation authenticates API tokens. Client, server and validation can be used independently or together, with optional Core persistence.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer operates the protocol host, user-authentication integration, database, keys/certificates, HTTPS/proxy settings, logs, backups and upgrades, or selects providers to do that work.

facts.label: Password and other user authentication
facts.value: custom_code/external account stack: OpenIddict accepts identities authenticated by the app, including password, token, federated or Windows authentication. It does not validate a user's stored password itself.

facts.label: Passwordless email/phone and wallet flows
facts.value: No built-in account magic-link/email-code/phone-code/wallet-signature system in the reviewed core. Supply those through application/account logic or an upstream identity provider.

facts.label: Anonymous accounts and machine identities
facts.value: Client-credentials grant authenticates an application, not an anonymous end-user account. Stored guests and guest upgrades are application/account-system work.

facts.label: Official web-provider companion package
facts.value: OpenIddict.Client.WebIntegration supports named OAuth/OIDC provider integrations and can run independently of the server. Our count of released 7.8.0 provider definitions is 114.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Released definitions include Google, GitHub, Facebook, Sign in with Apple, Microsoft Account/Entra ID, X/Twitter, Discord, Amazon, LinkedIn, GitLab and others.

facts.label: Provider-specific setup differences
facts.value: Apple definition requires an ECDSA signing key and team ID. Microsoft definition supports a tenant setting, default common. GitHub definition includes authorization-code and device-code grants.

facts.label: Passkey feature boundary
facts.value: OpenIddict core does not supply WebAuthn enrollment/assertion verification, authenticator credential storage or passkey account-management UI; application/account provider supplies them.

facts.label: Passkey UX and recovery responsibility
facts.value: Conditional autofill, browser/native passkey support, relying-party domain policy and lost-passkey recovery belong to the selected authentication implementation.

facts.label: MFA and recovery codes
facts.value: Core does not enroll TOTP/SMS/email/security-key factors or generate user recovery codes. The app/account stack or upstream provider performs/enforces the user authentication.

facts.label: Client authentication versus user factors
facts.value: built_in protocol client authentication includes client secrets, private_key_jwt and opt-in mutual TLS. These authenticate client software/certificates, not user TOTP/SMS MFA.

facts.label: Registration, confirmation and recovery
facts.value: User signup, email/phone confirmation, password reset, address changes and self-service deletion are supplied by the application's account system; core is protocol-only.

facts.label: Consent and userinfo are different
facts.value: Core supports authorization consent records and OIDC userinfo/token claims. The app decides consent presentation, identity fields and account state.

facts.label: Access and identity token defaults
facts.value: Released 7.8.0 defaults: access token 1 hour; identity token 20 minutes. Lifetimes are configurable; tokens are distinct from the application's browser login session.

facts.label: Code lifetimes
facts.value: Released defaults: authorization code 5 minutes; device code and user code 10 minutes each. Device authorization approval can extend the device-code expiry for redemption.

facts.label: Refresh policy
facts.value: Released default refresh lifetime 14 days; rolling refresh tokens and sliding refresh expiration are enabled unless disabled. Redeemed rolling refresh tokens have 30-second reuse leeway for concurrent refresh requests.

facts.label: Client state-token protection
facts.value: Client is stateful by default, persists state-token payloads and automatically redeems state tokens to resist callback replay. StateTokenLifetime defaults to 15 minutes.

facts.label: Token storage and revocation
facts.value: Core stores token metadata; JWT/Data Protection tokens can be revoked when storage is enabled. Reference access/refresh tokens are optional, and revocation is not restricted to reference-token format.

facts.label: Immediate API revocation is opt-in
facts.value: Default API validation does not check token-entry or authorization-entry status on every request. EnableTokenEntryValidation/EnableAuthorizationEntryValidation add database checks; remote APIs can use introspection.

facts.label: Browser sessions and logout
facts.value: Application authentication cookies/session policy govern user login persistence. OpenIddict supplies protocol end-session/logout request processing and pass-through hooks; app clears its actual user session.

facts.label: Native protocol roles and grants
facts.value: built_in OAuth 2.0/OIDC server, OAuth/OIDC client and API token validator. Supported flows include authorization code/hybrid, client credentials, refresh, device authorization and token exchange; server also supports legacy implicit/ROPC scenarios.

facts.label: Client and API integration
facts.value: Client uses remote provider configuration and credentials; API validation can import a local server's configuration/keys or use remote discovery/introspection.

facts.label: SAML extension roles
facts.value: plugin/commercial: project integrations and Rock Solid Knowledge's OpenIddict product page offer SAML2P Identity Provider and Service Provider roles, with cross-protocol SSO.

facts.label: SAML exact-version compatibility
facts.value: No definitive public matrix tying the offered SAML2P component release to OpenIddict 7.8.0 found in the reviewed product page, current SAML overview and licence FAQ.

facts.label: Scopes/permissions versus organizations
facts.value: Core enforces protocol client permissions and supports scopes, claims and consent grants. Customer organizations, invitations, member roles and tenant isolation require the surrounding app/framework.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No built-in SCIM Users/Groups provisioning or directory offboarding API in the reviewed core. Implement separately against the application's user system or choose a compatible external component.

facts.label: Account and consent UI
facts.value: No turnkey built-in login/signup/profile/MFA/consent dashboard. App supplies views/controllers; official docs point to samples and separate ABP/OrchardCore or commercial integrations for more finished experiences.

facts.label: Branding, issuer and callbacks
facts.value: Developer controls app UI/host/domain and configures issuer, redirect and post-logout redirect URIs. No core branding-removal tier or hosted custom-domain charge.

facts.label: Localized protocol metadata
facts.value: Application descriptors support culture-specific display names for client applications; the app supplies its actual translated user screens.

facts.label: UI languages and accessibility scope
facts.value: Not applicable as a core UI catalogue/conformance rating: OpenIddict does not ship the end-user account interface. Assess the app/framework/provider actually rendering the screens.

facts.label: Current host integrations
facts.value: Current guides/released README specify ASP.NET Core 2.3+ or ASP.NET 4.6.2+ with the relevant ASP.NET Core/OWIN packages; MVC, Razor Pages, minimal API or middleware can host the flows.

facts.label: Homepage minimum-version discrepancy
facts.value: Homepage advertises ASP.NET Core 2.1+ / ASP.NET 4.6.1+, while current integration guide and released 7.8.0 README require 2.3+ / 4.6.2+.

facts.label: Released server package targets
facts.value: OpenIddict.Server 7.8.0 publishes .NET Framework 4.6.2/4.7.2/4.8, net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 and .NET Standard 2.0/2.1 assets.

facts.label: Official native client
facts.value: OpenIddict.Client.SystemIntegration integrates Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows client authorization/logout and callback processing.

facts.label: Native target documentation discrepancy
facts.value: Operating-system guide still lists net9.0-or-net10.0 Android/iOS/Apple targets; release 7.7.0 removed the net9.0 mobile/Apple targets and released 7.8.0 package metadata has only the net10.0 variants.

facts.label: Native browser and callback behavior
facts.value: Default Linux/Windows interaction uses system browser; Apple platforms use ASWebAuthenticationSession with custom-scheme callbacks; Android uses CustomTabsIntent and needs a callback activity/intent filter.

facts.label: Application-model limits
facts.value: System integration relies on .NET Generic Host. MAUI needs adapters for required host abstractions; UWP/WinUI and Avalonia have documented constraints. Official examples include console, WinForms, WPF and Blazor Hybrid on WPF.

facts.label: Protocol persistence backends
facts.value: Official Core integrations support Entity Framework Core, Entity Framework 6.x and MongoDB; custom stores can supply another provider. They store applications, authorizations, scopes and tokens.

facts.label: Stateful versus degraded configurations
facts.value: Server can run in advanced degraded mode without normal Core database services, with implementer-supplied validation/security. Interactive client normally requires a token store for one-use state-token protection.

facts.label: Keys, certificates and Data Protection
facts.value: Configure signing/encryption credentials for protocol tokens. Production credentials must be persisted/shared appropriately; optional Data Protection tokens use a separate key ring.

facts.label: Package dependencies and remote services
facts.value: Companion HTTP packages handle remote discovery/token/userinfo/introspection communication. Published server package depends on matching abstractions, Microsoft logging and IdentityModel JWT libraries.

facts.label: Deployment and upgrades
facts.value: Host as the chosen ASP.NET Core/OWIN/.NET application, configure HTTPS/proxy scheme and production keys, create required store schema/indexes and apply documented version migrations.

facts.label: Stable cleanup versus preview worker
facts.value: Stable 7.8 cleanup is opt-in via OpenIddict.Quartz and a configured hosted Quartz scheduler, or app-operated manager pruning. 8.0 preview 5 replaces it with a default Core background worker.

facts.label: Backup/restore and capacity guidance
facts.value: No complete OpenIddict-specific tested database/key/account backup-restore runbook, RPO/RTO, hardware minimum or fixed MAU/RPS sizing guarantee found in reviewed setup, storage, key and migration material.

facts.label: Custom logic and protocol hooks
facts.value: OpenIddict exposes an ordered events model and pass-through handlers; app supplies identities/claims, custom checks, consent decisions and host responses.

facts.label: Claims and custom metadata
facts.value: Application descriptors/entities can be extended and store custom properties/settings; explicit claim destinations control exposure in access/identity tokens, normally based on granted scopes.

facts.label: Protocol administration
facts.value: In-process managers create/list/update/delete client applications and manage scopes, authorization grants and tokens; token/authorization managers support revocation by identifiers/subject/client filters.

facts.label: User search, bans and impersonation
facts.value: Application/account framework supplies user CRUD/search/bans/support impersonation. OpenIddict can revoke protocol grants/tokens but does not own the underlying membership records.

facts.label: Optional admin products
facts.value: Official integrations list separate ABP/OrchardCore solutions and Rock Solid Knowledge AdminUI for management interfaces.

facts.label: Linking provider identities
facts.value: Client authenticates with remote providers and returns claims; app decides how to create/find/link/unlink local accounts and authorize those changes.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and identity merge
facts.value: No stored guest-user upgrade/merge lifecycle in the protocol core. The app/account layer must retain or reassign guest data when a durable account is created.

facts.label: Protocol security controls
facts.value: built_in request/client/redirect validation, state-token one-use protection, explicit client permissions, and encrypted/signed token mechanisms; PKCE and PAR are supported.

facts.label: Password/bot/SMS abuse boundary
facts.value: Password lockout, breached-password checks, CAPTCHA/risk scoring, email-code throttles and SMS fraud/spend controls are responsibilities of the user-authentication app/provider, not native protocol-account features.

facts.label: Transport and credential configuration
facts.value: ASP.NET Core client/server integration requires HTTPS by default; configure proxy-forwarded scheme correctly. Keys, private_key_jwt and optional mTLS have documented production requirements.

facts.label: Endpoint/API rate and burst ceiling
facts.value: No universal OpenIddict login, token, introspection or management requests/window or concurrency allowance published in reviewed guides/options/HTTP/source material.

facts.label: Outbound HTTP recovery
facts.value: Official HTTP integration documents retrying transient failures up to 4 times; .NET 8+ uses a configurable resilience pipeline, while older targets use a configurable Polly policy.

facts.label: Logging and audit extension points
facts.value: Protocol stacks use Microsoft logging and custom event handlers; token/grant stores expose metadata such as subject, client, status, creation and expiry for app-owned investigation.

facts.label: Sensitive payload logging default
facts.value: 7.8.0 stops logging HTTP response payloads by default on errors; EnableSensitivePayloadLogging can opt back into that behavior.

facts.label: Audit retention/export promise
facts.value: No fixed managed audit-retention days, immutable event history, guaranteed export window or outbound webhook retry contract found in reviewed logging/options/events/storage material.

facts.label: User profiles and password-hash export
facts.value: User profiles, password hashes, factors and external-account links reside in the chosen account stack, not OpenIddict's standard protocol model; export them from that actual store.

facts.label: Protocol metadata export
facts.value: App owns client/scope/authorization/token data and can enumerate it through managers or the database. No standard one-click cross-vendor migration bundle or vendor export charge.

facts.label: Secret and token portability limits
facts.value: Application manager hashes client secrets by default; server-stored reference-token payloads may be encrypted. Existing tokens also depend on issuer, signing/decryption keys, token format and validation configuration.

facts.label: Importing users
facts.value: User import/password migration is handled by the selected membership system or custom app code; OpenIddict does not include a user/password import endpoint or hash-migration engine.

facts.label: Protocol/schema migration
facts.value: Managers/custom entities support app-controlled protocol data migration; official 6.x-to-7.x guide requires a schema update for token Type length and documents package/API changes.

facts.label: Deletion responsibilities
facts.value: App removes user records in its account system and explicitly revokes/deletes related grants/tokens through managers/stores; hosted vendor-account closure is not applicable.

facts.label: Stable pruning defaults
facts.value: Opt-in Quartz integration sets minimum token and authorization age to 14 days, configurable down to a 10-minute minimum; failed jobs retry twice after the initial failure.

facts.label: Pruning wording conflict
facts.value: Quartz guide broadly says all records older than 14 days are removed; authorization guide says permanent grants are never removed. Released EF Core stores instead apply age plus status/expiry/orphan checks, including eligible invalid permanent grants with no tokens.

facts.label: Backup/log deletion retention
facts.value: No fixed project-wide deleted-user backup lifetime, log-retention period or deletion SLA found in the reviewed core policy, storage, setup and pruning material.

facts.label: Data location
facts.value: Developer chooses where protocol/user stores, app hosts, signing keys, logs and backups live; no OpenIddict-hosted region list or residency tier.

facts.label: Processing-policy applicability
facts.value: Not applicable as a hosted-auth processing agreement/subprocessor list: core is app-operated code and supplies no vendor-hosted user tenant.

facts.label: Public project privacy/assurance evidence
facts.value: No project-specific website privacy policy, hosted-auth DPA or independent SOC 2/ISO report established in the checked homepage, docs, support/security material and official-site searches.

facts.label: OIDC conformance scope
facts.value: Project README says a reference implementation would not guarantee the compliance of custom deployments, and recommends running conformance tests against the actual implementation.

facts.label: Name, project and maintainer
facts.value: OpenIddict, maintained under the openiddict project organization by an individual maintainer in France; official project site openiddict.com and documentation.openiddict.com.

facts.label: History and related old name
facts.value: Started in late 2015; AspNet.Security.OpenIdConnect.Server (ASOS) was merged into OpenIddict 3.0+ in 2020. Client stack arrived in 2022; desktop support in 4.1 and mobile support in 5.8.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Active, public source/packages; latest stable 7.8.0 published 2026-11-03T15:53:15Z. Core repository is not archived or disabled.

facts.label: Preview boundary
facts.value: 8.0.0-preview.5 is a prerelease, published 2026-11-03T15:53:32Z. It replaces opt-in Quartz pruning with a default background worker; those 8.x changes are not assigned to stable 7.8.

facts.label: Version lifecycle scope
facts.value: Normal support is for the latest stable version only. Sponsors and qualifying ABP users have explicit older-major exceptions; 7.x is listed current.

facts.label: Core licence and commercial use
facts.value: Apache-2.0: royalty-free commercial use, modification and redistribution, with licence/notice obligations and the licence's patent conditions; no compulsory paid production key.

facts.label: Redistribution conditions
facts.value: Redistributors must supply the Apache licence, mark modified files, retain applicable attribution/legal notices and preserve NOTICE content if supplied. Trademark rights are not generally granted by the licence.

facts.label: Optional SAML extension licence
facts.value: Rock Solid Knowledge's SAML2P is a separately licensed commercial component; standard purchase does not include source code. Enterprise perpetual and separately quoted redistribution terms are described.

facts.label: Hosted status and uptime SLA
facts.value: Not applicable: core exposes no vendor-operated production auth tenant or endpoint with a hosted uptime SLA/status promise.

facts.label: Current release and maintenance
facts.value: Latest stable release API identifies 7.8.0, published 2026-11-03T15:53:15Z; public NuGet 7.8.0 and active/nonarchived core repository corroborate current maintenance.

facts.label: Security fix evidence
facts.value: Official September 6, 2026 advisory GHSA-925x-4h4v-2792 concerns client-assertion audience validation; patched releases include stable 7.7 and 8.0 preview 4.

facts.label: ABP 6.x exception
facts.value: Project support policy lists OpenIddict 6.x with ABP Framework 9.x patches through November 2026, including users of free ABP packages.

facts.label: ABP 7.x exception
facts.value: Project policy lists OpenIddict 7.x with ABP Framework 10.x through November 2027; ordinary core support otherwise targets latest stable only.

facts.label: Sponsor older-major exceptions
facts.value: Published policy lists Tier 9 support for 5.x through December 17, 2026 and 6.x through July 7, 2027. Other older-branch tier dates shown in the policy have already ended on the checked date.

facts.label: Support routes
facts.value: Project support policy offers dedicated help to regular contributors, sponsors and custom-contract customers. Requests use GitHub or tier-eligible private email; contact@openiddict.com is the project support-contract route.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 1 (hobby)
facts.value: $2 per month; 1 GitHub support ticket per year; explicitly hobbyist-only, excluding professional projects.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 2 (hobby)
facts.value: $5 per month; 2 GitHub support tickets per year; explicitly hobbyist-only, excluding professional projects.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 3 (hobby)
facts.value: $10 per month; 3 GitHub support tickets per year; explicitly hobbyist-only, excluding professional projects.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 4
facts.value: $25 per month; 4 GitHub support tickets per year.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 5
facts.value: $50 per month; 5 GitHub support tickets per year.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 6
facts.value: $100 per month; 6 public/private support tickets per year; important-event notifications; guaranteed reply within 24 hours and previous-major support for 1 month after a new major release.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 7
facts.value: $250 per month; 7 public/private support tickets and 1 code review per year; 24-hour reply guarantee; previous-major support extended 6 months.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 8
facts.value: $500 per month; 8 public/private support tickets and 3 code reviews per year; 24-hour reply guarantee; previous-major support extended 12 months; early security announcements/patch access.

facts.label: Sponsor Tier 9
facts.value: $1,000 per month; unlimited public/private tickets, 5 code reviews per year; 24-hour reply guarantee; previous-major support extended 24 months; early security announcements/patch access.

facts.label: Sponsorship cancellation conditions
facts.value: Sponsorship can be cancelled at any time, but cancelling within the first 12 months permanently loses tier benefits; a one-time $500 sponsorship is required to reactivate benefits.

facts.label: Private vulnerability report route
facts.value: Security policy requests private reports at security@openiddict.com and says a response should arrive within 24 hours.

facts.label: Custom support price and fix SLA
facts.value: Custom-contract pricing, hours and repair-time guarantees are not published in the checked support policy/sponsor offer; project invites discussion.

cells.freeUsers: No free live production environment

Assumes each of the 50,000 users is active on 2 days of a 30-day month. $70 base, plus $0.14 per average daily active user, minus a $21 credit. That totals $515.67 a month.
Assumes each of the 100,000 users is active on 2 days of a 30-day month. $70 base, plus $0.14 per average daily active user, minus a $21 credit. That totals $982.33 a month.

facts.label: Average daily active users
facts.value: Network aDAU = sum of each day's unique users using Ory Identities APIs in the month / number of days in that month.

facts.label: Other usage meters and scope
facts.value: M2M = tokens issued through OAuth2 client-credentials flow; permission check = request to the Permissions check API. Workspace subscription covers its projects.

facts.label: Billing window and credits
facts.value: Usage invoiced monthly even with annual base billing; credits apply to total service usage and do not roll over.

facts.label: Network free production
facts.value: Developer: free, 0 production environments, 0 staging environments, 2 development environments.

facts.label: Self-host free software
facts.value: Apache-licensed Kratos/Hydra/Polis core has no per-user software royalty; hosting and operations remain extra.

facts.label: Production minimum commitment
facts.value: Network Production: $70/month monthly billing, or $770/year annual base commitment; applicable taxes extra.

facts.label: Growth and commercial minimums
facts.value: Growth publishes $9,350/year. Network Enterprise and self-host OEL are custom-priced.

facts.label: Renewal and cancellation rules
facts.value: Subscription/order defines term and renewal. Fees are non-refundable/non-cancelable except stated exceptions; early termination can make remaining term fees due.

facts.label: Production usage prices
facts.value: $21 monthly usage credit; $0.14/aDAU/month; $0.007/M2M token; $0.000090/permission check.

facts.label: Growth usage prices
facts.value: $255 monthly usage credit; $0.12/aDAU/month; $0.006/M2M token; $0.000085/permission check.

facts.label: Enterprise pricing and rounding
facts.value: Enterprise rates and committed-use discounts require a quote; invoice rounding of fractional aDAU was not found.

facts.label: Hosted business scenarios
facts.value: A and B require an Enterprise quote: Growth allows only 3 organizations and OIDC business SSO; SAML is Enterprise-only.

facts.label: Self-host business scenarios
facts.value: Kratos OSS alone lacks native B2B organizations/multitenancy. OEL can provide those; Polis OSS brokerage can be combined with app-owned membership and roles.

facts.label: Hosted organization caps
facts.value: Developer/Production: no B2B organizations. Growth: 3 maximum. Enterprise: unlimited in public table.

facts.label: Organization member and invitation caps
facts.value: No numeric member-per-organization, invite quota, per-org overage fee or paid extra-organization tariff was found.

facts.label: Network incoming SSO and SCIM prices
facts.value: Growth includes OIDC B2B only. SAML, SCIM and Directory Sync are Enterprise-only; connection/setup/directory fees are not public.

facts.label: Self-host SSO fee boundary
facts.value: Polis Apache core can broker incoming SAML/OIDC and directory sync without a published per-connection royalty; Identity Federation needs enterprise licensing.

facts.label: Developer dashboard capacity
facts.value: Developer: 1 member, 2 development environments, no production/staging. Production: unlimited members, 1 production, 3 staging, 5 development.

facts.label: Growth and Enterprise capacity
facts.value: Growth: unlimited members, 2 production, 5 staging, 20 development. Enterprise: unlimited members and custom environment allowances.

facts.label: Builder permissions
facts.value: Workspace and project Owner/Developer/Viewer roles; workspace access is inherited and project roles can raise access.

facts.label: Hosted email delivery
facts.value: Network provides a default SMTP sender. Own SMTP/HTTP delivery is supported; custom sender/name/content requires your own SMTP.

facts.label: SMS and external delivery
facts.value: Developer supplies an HTTP SMS gateway, such as Twilio, Plivo or AWS SNS, and its credentials.

facts.label: Self-host delivery worker
facts.value: Kratos self-host needs a singleton mail courier plus SMTP/HTTP sender; default message_retries is 5 for SMTP/SMS.

facts.label: Paid excess and throttling
facts.value: Paid usage above credit is billed monthly. Operational rate limits can return 429; terms permit throttling or suspension for nonpayment, harmful use or legal restrictions.

facts.label: Spend cap and grace behavior
facts.value: No customer-set hard spending cap, usage alert threshold, automatic upgrade rule or overage grace period was found.

facts.label: Other metered and commercial costs
facts.value: M2M tokens and permission checks consume the same dollar credit. Additional multi-tenant production environments may add charges.

facts.label: Self-host vendor bill
facts.value: No Network aDAU invoice applies to running only Apache core on your own infrastructure.

facts.label: Individual and market eligibility
facts.value: Terms define Customer as an individual or organization; use must be lawful and authorized.

facts.label: Seller-country restrictions
facts.value: No complete supported or restricted seller-country list was found.

facts.label: Self-service entry
facts.value: Public free Developer entry and Production/Growth Buy links; Enterprise and OEL require contact.

facts.label: Trial, card and company-domain requirements
facts.value: A timed production trial, trial-day count, card-free guarantee and company-email requirement were not established.

facts.label: Hosted Network scope
facts.value: Managed identity platform: accounts, login, recovery, verification, sessions, OAuth2/OIDC, permissions and enterprise SSO through integrated components.

facts.label: Kratos scope
facts.value: Self-hosted API-first identity server for users, credentials, login/signup, MFA, recovery, verification, profile settings and sessions.

facts.label: Hydra scope
facts.value: OAuth2 authorization server and OpenID Connect provider; delegates user authentication to Kratos or another identity system.

facts.label: Polis scope
facts.value: Business SSO broker: consumes SAML/OIDC and exposes an OAuth2 flow; also supplies SCIM directory sync.

facts.label: Network operator
facts.value: Ory operates hosting, scaling, patching and availability infrastructure.

facts.label: Self-host operator
facts.value: Developer operates OSS or OEL servers, database, networking, upgrades, backups and restore procedures.

facts.label: Password authentication
facts.value: Kratos built-in password login with schema-defined email, username or phone identifier; Network lists password on every tier.

facts.label: Email and SMS first-factor codes
facts.value: Network supports first-factor one-time email and SMS codes; both are listed on every tier. Self-host code strategy is documented.

facts.label: Magic-link first-factor scope
facts.value: Recovery/verification links are documented, but a current dedicated first-factor login-link flow was not established.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet methods
facts.value: No native persistent anonymous-account issuance, guest-promotion flow or wallet/SIWE sign-in guide was found.

facts.label: Google social login
facts.value: Built-in provider configuration; customer supplies Google OAuth client ID/secret and approved redirect URI.

facts.label: Apple social login
facts.value: Built-in Sign in with Apple connector, with web and native setup.

facts.label: GitHub and Microsoft social login
facts.value: Named built-in GitHub and Microsoft connectors; each has a provider-specific setup guide.

facts.label: Other and generic providers
facts.value: Docs advertise 15+ tailored connectors, including Facebook and Slack, plus generic OIDC. Network lists unlimited social connections on every tier.

facts.label: Passkeys and conditional UI
facts.value: Kratos passkey strategy supports first-factor login/registration, discoverable credentials and conditional autofill. Network includes passkeys on all tiers.

facts.label: Passkey platform and domain conditions
facts.value: Web uses WebAuthn. iOS uses AuthenticationServices/AASA; Android uses CredentialManager/Digital Asset Links. RP ID and allowed origins must match.

facts.label: Network MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Built-in TOTP, WebAuthn hardware factors, email/SMS codes, lookup recovery codes and documented device authentication. Step-up can require AAL2.

facts.label: MFA recovery and self-host config
facts.value: Lookup secrets are single-use, do not expire by time, and old sets are invalidated when regenerated. Self-host docs configure TOTP, WebAuthn and lookup secrets.

facts.label: Recovery-factor policy
facts.value: Account recovery normally yields a privileged session without second factor; required_aal can demand the highest available factor before settings changes.

facts.label: Email and phone verification
facts.value: Built-in address verification for browser and API flows; code/link options, automatic verification initiation at signup, and manual verification.

facts.label: Reset and contact changes
facts.value: Recovery via email/SMS code or legacy link; settings support password/profile changes and provider linking with a fresh privileged session.

facts.label: User-initiated deletion
facts.value: No built-in self-service delete flow. Builder can add a button/backend endpoint that calls DELETE /admin/identities/{id}.

facts.label: Session model and duration
facts.value: Kratos browser flows issue session cookies; native flows issue opaque session tokens. Lifespan and privileged-session age are configurable.

facts.label: Session/device revocation
facts.value: Users can list active sessions and revoke other sessions; admins can list, get, deactivate/delete sessions or invalidate an identity's sessions.

facts.label: Deactivation behavior
facts.value: Marking an identity inactive prevents self-service login and revokes all sessions; reactivation does not restore sessions.

facts.label: Hydra OAuth2/OIDC provider role
facts.value: Hydra supplies OAuth2/OIDC provider/authorization-server functions, including cross-app SSO and client credentials; Network lists these on all tiers.

facts.label: Incoming SAML/OIDC business login
facts.value: Polis acts as broker/service provider to incoming SAML/OIDC IdPs and presents OAuth2 to the application. Network uses organizations for business SSO.

facts.label: Downstream SAML federation
facts.value: Polis can act as SAML identity provider and federate multiple upstream IdPs through its Identity Federation feature.

facts.label: Native organization membership model
facts.value: Network identity belongs to at most one organization or none. Organization owns domains and multiple SSO connections; members must use its SSO.

facts.label: Invitations and application roles
facts.value: Invitations are an integration: create identity, generate recovery link, send it. Basic roles can live in admin-controlled metadata; Keto supports app-defined roles/permissions.

facts.label: Self-host tenant boundaries
facts.value: Kratos OSS is documented as single-tenant; native organizations and multitenancy require OEL or Network. Polis uses tenant/product-scoped SSO connections.

facts.label: Network SCIM
facts.value: Enterprise organization-scoped SCIM 2.0 server supports Users and Groups, including nested groups, mappings and multiple clients per organization.

facts.label: SCIM offboarding
facts.value: Network DELETE /Users/{id} deletes the identity; active=false deactivates instead. Deactivation revokes Kratos sessions.

facts.label: Self-hosted Polis directory sync
facts.value: Polis service/npm core documents SCIM 2.0 Users, Groups and membership events; available since the old v1.2.1 line.

facts.label: Hosted self-service screens
facts.value: Network Account Experience provides login, registration, recovery, verification, settings and consent screens; new projects use it by default.

facts.label: Embedded and custom UI
facts.value: Ory Elements supplies React components; headless APIs permit a custom UI. Self-host requires deploying/integrating UI separately from Kratos/Hydra.

facts.label: Polis administrative UI
facts.value: Polis deployed as a service includes an Admin Portal for SSO connections, Directory Sync and setup links.

facts.label: Network branding and custom domains
facts.value: All tiers list themeable/BYO pages. Custom domains: none on Developer, 1 per project on Production/Growth, custom quantity on Enterprise.

facts.label: Domain operating limits
facts.value: Network custom domain needs CNAME; up to 50 CORS origins. Request body maximum 10 MiB, response maximum 64 MiB, with possible lower API limits.

facts.label: UI languages
facts.value: Account Experience/Elements document 83 bundled languages. Default enabled set: en, de, es, fr, it, ja, nl, pt, ru, zh; custom messages supported.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independent accessibility assessment was found for hosted login or Elements.

facts.label: Network SDKs and web integration
facts.value: Official generated SDKs: TypeScript, Go, Python, Java, PHP, Dart, Ruby, C# and Rust. React/Next.js UI integration is documented.

facts.label: Self-host SDK and Polis runtime
facts.value: Kratos has service-specific generated SDKs including Dart, .NET, Elixir, Go, Java, JS/TS, PHP, Python, Ruby and Rust. Polis can embed in a Node.js web app.

facts.label: Mobile clients
facts.value: Official React Native example and native API/token flow; iOS/Android social auth via system browser and app-link return. Passkey integration uses native platform APIs.

facts.label: Other native framework coverage
facts.value: Dart SDK is published; a dedicated Flutter guide shows a native bridge for device-key authentication. A complete turnkey Flutter/desktop account SDK and OS-version matrix were not established.

facts.label: Network dependencies
facts.value: Ory operates the account database/services. Builder supplies app integration, provider credentials, and any own sender, SMS gateway or webhook endpoints.

facts.label: Kratos and Hydra database
facts.value: Kratos production requires PostgreSQL, MySQL or CockroachDB; SQLite is discouraged for production. Hydra guide lists PostgreSQL 12.0+, MySQL 8.0+, CockroachDB and SQLite.

facts.label: Polis dependencies
facts.value: Separate Next.js service or Node.js library with database storage. Docs name MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis and PlanetScale options.

facts.label: Self-host deployment and hardening
facts.value: Docker/Kubernetes/Helm and production guides; operator must set secrets, TLS/networking and protect admin APIs.

facts.label: Backups, migrations and restore
facts.value: Hydra requires explicit schema migration before startup/after upgrades and a database backup first. Polis upgrade notes also require backups for schema changes.

facts.label: Scaling and commercial operations
facts.value: Kratos can run multiple instances with a singleton courier. Polis shares database state across replicas and requires consistent SAML signing keys. OEL adds optimized builds/zero-downtime migration support.

facts.label: Custom identity data
facts.value: Kratos traits use JSON Schema; public/admin metadata is set through admin APIs. Metadata can hold subscription state, legacy IDs or basic roles.

facts.label: Hooks and external custom logic
facts.value: Actions/webhooks can run before or after self-service flows, call external endpoints and map payloads with Jsonnet. Network lists Actions on every tier.

facts.label: Webhook delivery rules
facts.value: Network attempts webhook delivery up to 3 times; each attempt times out after 30 seconds. Backoff is 1 second, then 2 seconds.

facts.label: Account administration
facts.value: Admin API/SDK can create, list, fetch, update/delete identities and credentials, generate recovery codes/links and manage sessions. Network supplies Console.

facts.label: Search and bans
facts.value: Network Console full-text search is on every tier; full-text search API is Enterprise-only. Identity deactivation blocks login and revokes sessions.

facts.label: Manual linking and unlinking
facts.value: Users can link multiple social methods through settings or during login/registration, proving the existing account where required.

facts.label: Automatic linking gates
facts.value: Imported-user auto-link requires a feature flag enabled through support and is Network/OEL-only. Google consumer Gmail and Apple verified-email auto-link have separate documented rules.

facts.label: Guest account upgrade
facts.value: No built-in guest identity promotion or anonymous-session-to-registered-account migration guide was found.

facts.label: Hosted abuse controls
facts.value: Pricing lists brute-force, DoS, credential-stuffing, suspicious-IP and breached-password protections on every tier.

facts.label: Configurable brute-force and CAPTCHA gates
facts.value: The 2026-10-30 release makes identifier/IP exponential-delay brute-force settings Enterprise-only. Managed Turnstile CAPTCHA is Enterprise-only in pricing; docs also allow BYO keys.

facts.label: Self-host password and delivery abuse
facts.value: Kratos checks prospective passwords with a k-anonymity breached-password API; can use a private compatible endpoint or disable it.

facts.label: Network login submit limits
facts.value: POST /self-service/login uses kratos-public-low. Developer development: 10 requests/second burst, 20/minute sustained. Production live: 10/second, 60/minute.

facts.label: Network session and admin limits
facts.value: GET /sessions/whoami shares kratos-public-high: Production live 134/second, 1,400/minute; Growth 384/second, 4,500/minute; Enterprise 750/second, 15,000/minute.

facts.label: Limit behavior and endpoint protections
facts.value: Project buckets vary by tier/environment; enforced endpoint rules return 429. Some inflight rules are report-only, and Ory manages the rules.

facts.label: Hosted event/history allowance
facts.value: Historical analytics/insights: Developer 24 hours, Production 7 days, Growth 30 days, Enterprise 90 days.

facts.label: Event export and initiator evidence
facts.value: Network Enterprise can stream signups, login/session/admin actions and other events to customer infrastructure; event records can identify API-key/Console/SCIM initiators.

facts.label: Self-host logs
facts.value: Ory components emit stdout/stderr logs in text/JSON; operator collects, stores and retains them.

facts.label: Profile and password-hash export
facts.value: Admin getIdentity with include_credential=password exports identities including hashed password credentials.

facts.label: Self-host credential inclusion API
facts.value: Current Kratos getIdentity accepts include_credential entries including password, oidc, totp, lookup_secret, webauthn, passkey, saml and deviceauthn.

facts.label: Other credential export portability
facts.value: A complete hosted export bundle with a documented credentials-preserving migration for provider links, TOTP, passkeys, recovery codes and sessions was not established.

facts.label: Self-host exit and domain caveat
facts.value: Self-host operator holds its database/configuration; Network and OEL APIs share core concepts. Passkeys remain tied to RP ID and origin constraints.

facts.label: Bulk/hash import
facts.value: Kratos supports imported password hashes: BCrypt, Argon2, MD5, SHA, SSHA variants, PBKDF2, SCrypt/Firebase SCrypt, crypt(3) and HMAC.

facts.label: Lazy import and other credentials
facts.value: Password-migration webhook can verify against a legacy system on first login. Import guide also documents OIDC/SAML subjects, TOTP and passkey/WebAuthn credential data.

facts.label: IDs, verified addresses and import limits
facts.value: Verified addresses can be imported when represented correctly in the identity schema. Legacy identifiers can be retained in metadata/external IDs rather than assuming server UUID preservation.

facts.label: Deletion and retained copies
facts.value: Identity deletion is permanent through admin API. Service termination requires return/destruction on request, with legal-compliance and backup-copy exceptions.

facts.label: Hosted backup commitment
facts.value: DPA says Ory maintains a recoverable customer-personal-data backup at least once a day and regularly tests disaster recovery.

facts.label: Network retention and account closure
facts.value: A fixed deleted-user backup purge period, full log-retention schedule and account/project-closure timetable were not found.

facts.label: Self-host retention
facts.value: Database, logs, backups and deletions are the operator's responsibility; no Ory-hosted backup-retention policy applies to a purely self-hosted deployment.

facts.label: Network data residency
facts.value: Paid plans allow PII storage-region selection. Personal data remains in its chosen region; operational data is replicated globally.

facts.label: Enterprise regional placement
facts.value: Global/US Continental PII placement and intelligent homing are Enterprise features. Identity-region changes are supported within project home-region constraints.

facts.label: Self-host data location
facts.value: Builder chooses database/service locations for OSS/OEL. Ory's telemetry page documents outbound anonymized quality reports.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Public DPA updated 2026-08-31 includes SCCs, UK transfer addendum, technical measures and a named subprocessor/country list.

facts.label: Assurance claims
facts.value: Ory claims ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Type 2 and PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ D service-provider assessment; PCI scope named as Ory Network.

facts.label: Privacy and model-training terms
facts.value: Service terms prohibit training AI/ML models on Customer Data without authorization, with exceptions for aggregated/de-identified data and certain service-operation uses.

facts.label: Name, operator and URLs
facts.value: Ory; hosted Ory Network; Ory Kratos, Hydra and Polis components. Service agreement names Ory Corp and affiliates.

facts.label: Polis product rebrand
facts.value: Ory acquired BoxyHQ and launched the former BoxyHQ Jackson as Ory Polis on 2025-05-29; the embedded npm package remains @boxyhq/saml-jackson. This changed the in-scope Polis product name, not Ory's ownership.

facts.label: Hosted availability
facts.value: Network has public Get Started and paid purchase routes; Developer, Production, Growth and Enterprise are listed.

facts.label: Self-host lifecycle
facts.value: Kratos, Hydra and Polis have current official docs and public release channels; OEL is separately offered.

facts.label: Polis lifecycle event
facts.value: Ory launched the renamed Ory Polis on 2025-05-29 after acquiring BoxyHQ; current docs and releases show the product remains available.

facts.value: Apache-2.0; no-charge copyright/patent grant subject to license terms, notices and redistribution conditions.

facts.value: Apache-2.0; commercial use and modifications under the stated attribution and redistribution conditions.

facts.label: Polis core and enterprise code
facts.value: Polis root LICENSE is Apache-2.0; ee/LICENSE labels that directory Ory Enterprise License / EE License.

facts.value: Network is a commercial service; OEL is commercial self-host software/support. Hosted/enterprise additions can be proprietary and unavailable in source form.

facts.label: Status and hosted SLA
facts.value: Public Network status page; Enterprise SLA promises 99.99% availability. Developer, Production and Growth show no SLA.

facts.label: SLA remedy and exclusions
facts.value: Credits are based on monthly subscription base fee, not total metered usage; staging/development, beta, customer-caused problems and other exclusions apply.

facts.label: Current self-host release channels
facts.value: Official latest-release APIs return Kratos v26.2.0 (2026-03-20 14:10:32 UTC), Hydra v26.2.0 (13:23:08 UTC), Polis v26.2.0 (18:49:46 UTC).

facts.value: Apache users receive patches only for current release, no security SLA. Network auto-deploys fixes; OEL support/version scope depends on agreement.

facts.label: Community and standard support
facts.value: Developer/Production: community support. Growth adds standard ticketing; public support table gives Growth no response-time SLA.

facts.label: Enterprise and OEL support
facts.value: Network Enterprise/OEL add dedicated channels, response SLAs and premium support by contract. OEL intro advertises 24/7 engineering access.

facts.label: Scale allowance and rate

facts.label: Unlisted capacities
facts.value: Exact price above 100,000 contacts and a current intermediate 50,000-contact tier not published on the directly retrieved rate card.

facts.label: Business cost coverage
facts.value: Required customer-SAML scenarios cannot be priced from the documented native offer; no incoming SAML implementation/rate was established.

facts.label: Group memberships
facts.value: All current standard tiers advertise individual and group memberships; Team registration mode lets multiple people share an account with individual credentials.

facts.label: Customer organization fees and caps
facts.value: No separate per-organization/per-customer-team platform fee, maximum organizations, or maximum members per team found.

facts.label: OIDC commercial inclusion
facts.value: Authentication, API/webhooks and group memberships are included on all listed tiers; separate outgoing OIDC connection fee/cap not found.

facts.label: Customer SAML/SCIM fees
facts.value: Incoming SAML connection pricing, enterprise setup fees and SCIM subscription fees not established.

facts.label: Builder seats
facts.value: Unlimited seats for the builder's own team at no additional seat charge on every current plan.

facts.label: Builder roles and invitations
facts.value: Dashboard roles include Admin/Primary Contact, Admin, Member and restricted Operator.

facts.label: Projects, domains and staging
facts.value: One Outseta installation can serve multiple domains/subdomains; no public numerical project/domain allowance or per-extra-project rate found.

facts.label: Test environment
facts.value: No out-of-the-box separate staging environment; use code overrides/demo accounts, or request a second staging account after launch.

facts.label: Managed mail sender
facts.value: Privacy policy names Twilio SendGrid for transactional and marketing email delivery.

facts.label: Custom sender domain
facts.value: Custom Support Email Address becomes the From address for transactional mail; deliverability guide documents mail forwarding plus SPF/DKIM configuration.

facts.label: Message quota and price
facts.value: Current exact transactional send allowance, overage rate, own-SMTP option and SMS destination prices not found.

facts.label: Contact-cap enforcement
facts.value: Exact behavior on reaching/exceeding contact cap, alert thresholds, upgrade timing, grace period and spending controls not found.

facts.label: Payment fee formula
facts.value: Platform subscription + successful payment volume × applicable Outseta percentage + separate Stripe charges.

facts.label: v3 payment dependency cost
facts.value: v3 uses Stripe Billing; launch comparison names an additional 0.7% Stripe Billing fee on subscriptions, with one-time products unaffected.

facts.label: Solo-builder audience and markets
facts.value: Entry plan is explicitly aimed at bootstrapped solopreneurs; no complete supported/restricted customer-country list found.

facts.label: Age and country eligibility detail
facts.value: Privacy policy says its service does not address people under 18. Exhaustive seller-country, entity and production-account eligibility rules not found.

facts.label: Self-service trial
facts.value: Current pricing advertises a 14-day full-feature trial and self-service signup links.

facts.label: Card and trial conversion rules
facts.value: Current trial card requirement and exact automatic conversion behavior not established.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Vendor-hosted membership/business platform combining authentication, accounts, subscription billing, CRM, email, protected content and support tools.

facts.label: Operations and responsibilities
facts.value: Outseta operates hosted servers on AWS and uses Amazon RDS encryption for stored data, including backups and replicas.

facts.label: Password authentication
facts.value: Built-in email/password registration and login through embedded forms or hosted OIDC login.

facts.label: Passwordless sign-in
facts.value: Optional single-use emailed magic link, valid for 10 minutes, alongside email/password and Google.

facts.label: Other basic methods
facts.value: Native first-factor email OTP, phone/SMS OTP, anonymous/guest login and wallet sign-in not established.

facts.label: Google social login
facts.value: Documented Google signup/login with the builder's Google project/client ID and authorized JavaScript origins.

facts.label: Other social providers
facts.value: Native Apple, GitHub, Microsoft, Facebook and arbitrary incoming social-provider configuration not established.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: Native passkey/WebAuthn enrollment, first-factor sign-in, autofill, recovery, native-client support and domain migration rules not found.

facts.label: End-user MFA and enforcement
facts.value: Built-in email second-factor codes and authenticator-app TOTP; enable optional enrollment or require all users to enroll at next login.

facts.label: Recovery codes and assisted recovery
facts.value: Users can copy/download recovery codes; an admin can regenerate codes after verifying the user's identity.

facts.label: Recovery API semantics
facts.value: Recovery-code regeneration invalidates all previous recovery codes while leaving existing TOTP/email mechanisms enrolled.

facts.label: Email verification
facts.value: Signup includes an emailed confirmation step before the user sets a password; confirmation emails can be resent.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Forgot-password API sends a reset link valid for 24 hours; login UI and hosted forgot-password page are documented.

facts.label: Email/profile/password changes
facts.value: Profile embed maintains person/account information and supports password change; Embed JavaScript API documents updating personal details including email.

facts.label: Member self-deletion
facts.value: A documented end-user delete-account button/flow with complete billing and data consequences was not found.

facts.label: Browser session storage
facts.value: Default tokenStorage is sessionStorage: current tab only, cleared on tab close. Optional localStorage persists across tabs/visits; cookie mode can support subdomains.

facts.label: JWT and refresh token
facts.value: Login returns bearer JWT and refresh token. API overview says tokens expire after approximately one year; login example gives expires_in 31536000.

facts.label: v3 authorization refresh
facts.value: v3 script checks owned products on page load at most once per five minutes/browser session and refreshes the token if changed.

facts.label: v2 versus v3 token claims
facts.value: v3 carries account/person identity, isPrimary and productUids; v2 planUid/addOnUids/subscriptionUid claims are absent on v3.

facts.label: Concurrent login control
facts.value: November 5, 2026 release adds a Block concurrent logins toggle under advanced Login Settings.

facts.label: Selective revocation details
facts.value: Per-device session listing, named-device revocation, refresh-token lifetime and immediate invalidation guarantees for issued JWTs not found.

facts.label: OIDC provider role
facts.value: Outgoing OpenID Connect provider for connected websites/products; create an OAuth client per relying application and use hosted login.

facts.label: Protocol discovery
facts.value: Per-account OIDC discovery document and JWKS endpoints are documented for issuer metadata/signature validation.

facts.label: Incoming business federation
facts.value: Incoming customer SAML or generic external OIDC broker configuration not established.

facts.label: External authentication integration
facts.value: Can keep a separate authentication system: after external login, backend obtains an Outseta token and passes it to the profile embed.

facts.label: Customer organizations and multi-membership
facts.value: Person can belong to multiple Accounts; an Account can have multiple People. At login a person selects which account to represent when more than one applies.

facts.label: Customer administration and invites
facts.value: Profile embed supports maintaining account information and adding/managing customer team members.

facts.label: Primary member and access isolation
facts.value: v3 primary contact gets every owned product; other account people receive only products configured for Team registration.

facts.label: Membership API
facts.value: API can add a person to an existing Account; sendWelcomeEmail=true sends a welcome email.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: SCIM 2.0 directory provisioning, user/group sync, deactivation semantics and pricing not found.

facts.label: Ready-made website UI
facts.value: Signup, login and profile embeds can appear as popups or directly in pages; profile includes account, password, team and membership management.

facts.label: Hosted auth/profile pages
facts.value: OIDC uses a hosted login page; hosted profile and forgot-password pages are documented on the account's outseta.com subdomain.

facts.label: v3 billing UI
facts.value: v3 signup remains on the builder's domain while payment checkout is Stripe hosted; self-service subscription changes use Stripe Customer Portal.

facts.label: Branding and themes
facts.value: Design controls include fonts, accent colors, light/dark mode, buttons, fields, corners, borders and custom CSS.

facts.label: Auth custom domains
facts.value: Embedded login can live on the builder's own website; a supported custom domain mapping for the OIDC hosted auth endpoint and numerical domain allowance not found.

facts.label: Translations
facts.value: Automatic browser-language translations: Arabic, Chinese, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Norwegian Bokmål, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Spanish (Spain), Swedish and Turkish.

facts.label: Copy customization
facts.value: Dashboard copy overrides replace default form wording; changes can take 2 to 3 minutes to appear.

facts.label: Accessibility assessment
facts.value: Public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independent accessibility test evidence not established.

facts.label: Official React integration
facts.value: Official guidance integrates the browser outseta.min.js script with React, including client-rendering and DOM lifecycle handling.

facts.label: Official Next.js integration
facts.value: App Router and Pages Router guidance uses Next.js Script with beforeInteractive to load Outseta before hydration.

facts.label: Server runtimes and REST
facts.value: Standard HTTPS/JSON REST API plus JWT verification examples for server environments such as Node.js and Python.

facts.label: Community packages
facts.value: Vendor lists community Java, Laravel, Dart and UserFrosting packages plus a Next.js starter.

facts.label: Mobile integration evidence
facts.value: API overview supports bearer tokens for logged-in browser/mobile sessions; vendor lists a community Dart package.

facts.label: Database and app backend
facts.value: Outseta handles users/auth/billing; the builder supplies storage and a backend for product data outside CRM.

facts.label: Website and payment prerequisites
facts.value: Embed setup requires website JavaScript, configured products/auth settings and a connected Stripe account in the documented signup setup.

facts.label: Self-hosted operations
facts.value: Not applicable to standard Outseta: documented deployment is vendor-hosted; no public installable auth-server edition, sizing or operator backup/upgrade runbook established.

facts.label: Custom fields and logic
facts.value: Custom Person, Account and Deal properties support checkbox/list, number, select/radio, text/textarea and date types.

facts.label: Custom browser logic
facts.value: Embed API allows retrieving and updating logged-in person/account details and configured custom properties.

facts.label: Webhook events and retries
facts.value: Activity notifications can email or POST to a callback URL; failed callbacks retry 20 times at 20-minute intervals.

facts.label: Webhook verification
facts.value: Optional configured 32-byte hex signature key; verify HMAC-SHA256 of raw UTF-8 body against x-hub-signature-256.

facts.label: v3 product change events
facts.value: Account webhook payloads include CurrentStripeProductInstances; AccountProductsChanged identifies added/removed product UIDs.

facts.label: Administration API
facts.value: REST supports People/Account management, filtering, pagination and custom property operations; list People returns stored person records.

facts.label: Admin support controls
facts.value: Admins can send confirmation email, set a temporary password and regenerate MFA recovery codes from a Person record.

facts.label: Banning and impersonation
facts.value: Dedicated reversible user-ban endpoint, device-session administration and audited dashboard impersonation controls not established.

facts.label: Social linking and account merging
facts.value: Explicit social-link/unlink UI/API, same-email auto-link rules, collision protection and merge of existing Person records not established.

facts.label: Anonymous upgrades
facts.value: Native guest-to-registered identity upgrade and data-preservation rules not found.

facts.label: Bot protection
facts.value: Optional Google reCAPTCHA v2 using site/secret keys; signup toggle plus email/help-desk/lead forms are documented.

facts.label: Enumeration protection
facts.value: Magic-link request endpoint always returns 200 whether a user exists or the feature is enabled.

facts.label: Other managed abuse controls
facts.value: Exact configurable lockout thresholds, breached-password screening, disposable-email blocklist and SMS pumping protection not established.

facts.label: Server API-key quota
facts.value: 7 requests per 5 seconds per API key; fixed window starts with first request.

facts.label: Bearer/client request quotas
facts.value: External access-token client: 20 requests per 5 seconds per user. HTTP-library calls without an API key: 5 per 5 seconds per IP and user agent.

facts.label: Unauthenticated and recovery behavior
facts.value: Other unauthenticated callers: 20 requests per 10 seconds per IP, with some endpoint-specific lower limits. Excess returns HTTP 429.

facts.label: User activity visibility
facts.value: Outseta auth automatically tracks customer login activity on CRM records; activity/lack of activity can trigger email campaigns.

facts.label: Activity API and time filter
facts.value: Activity API supports event-type/date filtering; results default to the last year unless ActivityDateTime is specified.

facts.label: Audit retention and exports
facts.value: Complete security/admin audit catalog, fixed retention period, audit-specific export/streaming entitlement and paid retention tiers not found.

facts.label: Self-service account export
facts.value: CRM > Accounts export produces a spreadsheet with account details and Stripe customer/payment tokens; filters restrict exported rows.

facts.label: Programmatic profile and membership export
facts.value: People and Account REST collections can be read with field selection and pagination; supports profile/identifier/membership extraction.

facts.label: Credential export and migration-out limits
facts.value: Password-hash export, full OAuth credentials, MFA secret/recovery export and support-assisted credential-export fee/process not found.

facts.label: v3 subscriber migration
facts.value: CSV Account import can recreate subscriptions/one-time products using account details, Stripe Price IDs and Stripe customer ID; paying customers get free migration assistance.

facts.label: Contact imports and updates
facts.value: CSV People import requires email; UID is used when updating an existing contact; custom properties should be created first.

facts.label: v2 migration differences
facts.value: v2 subscriber import uses plan UID/start/renewal/term plus Stripe customer/payment tokens; users then establish a new password.

facts.label: Person deletion API
facts.value: Authenticated DELETE /api/v1/crm/people/{personUid} is documented.

facts.label: Expired account retention statement
facts.value: Security article says customer data is retained for one year after the Outseta subscription expires, then data not needed for operations/reporting is deleted; earlier deletion on request.

facts.label: DPA cessation deletion deadline
facts.value: DPA section 9 requires deleting/procuring deletion of all copies and written certification within 10 business days after services involving personal data cease.

facts.label: Privacy retention and closure
facts.value: Privacy policy retains personal data as necessary for stated purposes/legal obligations; users can request deletion through settings where available or contact Outseta.

facts.label: Hosted data country
facts.value: DPA section 11 says Outseta stores/processes personal data on US servers; privacy policy also states US transfers/processing.

facts.label: Region selection and backup geography
facts.value: Named AWS region, selectable EU residency, plan-specific regional hosting and exact log/backup/subprocessor geography not found.

facts.label: Public DPA/SCC evidence
facts.value: Public downloadable DPA and EU Module 2 controller-to-processor SCCs; service use accepts DPA; signed vendor copy included.

facts.label: Subprocessors
facts.value: Privacy policy names AWS hosting/storage; Stripe payments; Twilio SendGrid email; Google Analytics/PostHog analytics; Anthropic Claude for internal operations/development/data analysis.

facts.label: Security control claims
facts.value: Vendor states PBKDF2 password hashing, TLS transport, encrypted RDS database/backups, restricted operations access and monitored dependencies/security incidents.

facts.label: Independent audit evidence
facts.value: Current Outseta SOC 2/ISO 27001 report/certificate, auditor, scope and observation period not established.

facts.label: Account/membership deletion API
facts.value: Authenticated account-record deletion and removal of person-account membership are documented; primary contact cannot be removed through the membership-removal operation.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Outseta; legal operator Outseta LLC. Site https://www.outseta.com/; knowledge base https://go.outseta.com/support/kb; API documentation https://docs.outseta.com/.

facts.label: Current version and availability
facts.value: Outseta v3 launched October 1, 2026 and is the product new customers receive. Existing customers may continue using v2.

facts.label: Lifecycle and component notice
facts.value: No whole-service shutdown, sunset or completed acquisition notice found in the bounded official-source search. November 5 update replaces the old MCP endpoint with agent.outseta.com/mcp for future updates.

facts.label: Hosted commercial-use rules
facts.value: Service and original features/content remain Outseta LLC/licensor intellectual property; access governed by subscription terms.

facts.label: Client SDK license
facts.value: Public license identifier for the vendor-delivered outseta.min.js embed script not established.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Public https://status.outseta.com/ monitors Outseta Website and Application/API.

facts.label: Availability guarantee
facts.value: Numerical SLA, measurement period, claim deadline and service-credit schedule not found; terms disclaim uninterrupted availability.

facts.label: Maintenance evidence
facts.value: Current v3 launch October 1, 2026 and November 5, 2026 product update; v2 maintenance and shared-feature updates expressly continue.

facts.label: Client version/support policy
facts.value: Precise currently deployed outseta.min.js version, formal LTS matrix, minimum runtime versions and public SDK security support window not established.

facts.label: Standard support
facts.value: Every current plan includes human support and free data migrations; API help email is support@outseta.com.

facts.value: Pro and Max advertise priority support; Start and Scale list human support without that priority label.

facts.value: Binding first-response/resolution times, staffed hours, emergency telephone route and separately priced enhanced support not found.
