facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: no core MAU, returning-user, stored-account, login or developer-seat billing meter.

facts.label: Production software allowance
facts.value: No core software licence fee or licence-imposed MAU production cap.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable to core use; no mandatory paid consulting/support purchase.

facts.label: Usage price rules
facts.value: Not applicable: no public core tier/overage tariff for an embedded dependency.

facts.label: Organizations and invitation limits
facts.value: No finished customer-organization, invitation or organization-billing package established.

facts.label: Business SSO software fees
facts.value: Core first-party protocol modules use the project Apache licence; no per-SAML/OIDC-connection royalty in that licence.

facts.label: Builder/project/domain caps
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted developer-dashboard seats, project or environment plan allowance.

facts.label: Login-message delivery
facts.value: No bundled email/SMS sender or send allowance established for core authentication.

facts.label: External delivery responsibility
facts.value: In delegated OIDC/CAS/SAML login, the chosen identity provider performs its own login flow; any messaging there belongs to that provider.

facts.label: Hosted allowance exhaustion
facts.value: Not applicable: core use has no vendor monthly allowance, automatic plan upgrade or overage charge.

facts.label: Other billable core limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no core token, API, audit-retention or membership-transaction rate card.

facts.label: Hosted-account eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to using the embedded Apache-licensed core.

facts.label: Self-service/trial gate
facts.value: Not applicable: public library dependencies, not a hosted trial or card-gated production tenant.

facts.label: Product type and coverage
facts.value: Embedded Java security engine for login flows, user profiles, authorization and web protection across framework integrations.

facts.label: Protocol module boundary
facts.value: Separate first-party modules supply OAuth, OIDC, SAML, CAS, HTTP and other mechanisms; host-framework integration supplies web/session adapters.

facts.label: Operating responsibility
facts.value: Developer operates the Java application, configured session/store adapters and any local user database; upstream providers operate their own login services.

facts.label: Username/password
facts.value: First-party pac4j-http supplies FormClient/DirectFormClient and basic-auth clients; configure an Authenticator for credential validation.

facts.label: Email link/code and phone code
facts.value: No packaged email magic-link, email OTP or phone/SMS OTP lifecycle established in reviewed core/module docs.

facts.label: Anonymous login
facts.value: First-party AnonymousClient supplies AnonymousProfile for a request.

facts.label: Digital-wallet login
facts.value: First-party pac4j-openid4vp authenticates through OpenID4VP 1.0 final; app acts as credential verifier.

facts.label: Named OAuth providers
facts.value: Dedicated clients include Google2Client, GitHubClient, FacebookClient, LinkedIn2Client, TwitterClient and others listed in the OAuth reference.

facts.label: Apple and Microsoft OIDC
facts.value: Dedicated provider clients are documented for Apple, Google, Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD and Keycloak; generic OidcClient also supported.

facts.label: Direct passkey implementation
facts.value: No first-party WebAuthn/passkey registration-and-login module established.

facts.label: Delegated factors and domain scope
facts.value: Federated login happens at the upstream provider; pac4j consumes the resulting profile rather than enrolling a local authenticator.

facts.label: Local MFA and recovery codes
facts.value: No first-party authenticator-app TOTP/HOTP, SMS/email-factor enrollment or recovery-code lifecycle established.

facts.label: Authentication-level checks
facts.value: Built-in authorizers distinguish anonymous, authenticated, remembered and fully authenticated profiles.

facts.label: Upstream assurance claims
facts.value: OidcProfile exposes getAcr(), getAmr() and getAuthTime(); application authorizers can evaluate supplied attributes.

facts.label: Verification claims
facts.value: OidcProfile exposes email_verified and phone_number_verified claims.

facts.label: Reset, address change and user deletion UI
facts.value: No ready-made password-reset token/email flow, address-change workflow or self-service deletion screen established.

facts.label: Stateful and direct authentication
facts.value: Indirect clients normally save profiles in the web session; direct clients normally save them in the request and validate per request.

facts.label: Session-store integration
facts.value: SessionStore abstracts session get/set, destroy, renew and trackable-session operations; backend differs by framework.

facts.label: Ordinary session duration
facts.value: No universal framework-wide idle/absolute session timeout or concurrent-device limit established.

facts.label: Session renewal on login
facts.value: DefaultCallbackLogic renewSession defaults to true.

facts.label: OIDC expiry and refresh
facts.value: OidcProfile expiry follows the access-token lifetime from expires_in or JWT exp; an available refresh token can renew an expired profile.

facts.label: Local and central logout
facts.value: Local logout true by default; destroySession false; centralLogout false.

facts.label: Single logout and global devices
facts.value: Callback endpoint handles IdP-initiated logout requests and session correlation; SessionStore supports trackable sessions.

facts.label: JWT validation/creation
facts.value: pac4j-jwt validates JWTs and can generate signed/encrypted JWTs; expiration can be configured.

facts.label: OIDC role
facts.value: pac4j-oidc is an OpenID Connect client/relying party using an upstream provider; authorization code flow is default.

facts.label: SAML role
facts.value: pac4j-saml supplies SAML2Client as a service provider/relying party; configure IdP metadata and application key material.

facts.label: CAS role
facts.value: pac4j-cas connects applications to a CAS server, including login/logout, proxy tickets and optional CAS REST authentication.

facts.label: OpenID Federation role
facts.value: pac4j-oidc includes OpenID Federation 1.0 relying-party support since 6.4.0.

facts.label: Roles and attribute authorization
facts.value: RequireAnyRoleAuthorizer/RequireAllRolesAuthorizer and attribute/profile authorizers check application profiles.

facts.label: Customer tenant model
facts.value: Custom profile attributes and roles can represent application-defined organization data.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No first-party SCIM user/group provisioning module, deactivation contract or directory connection plan established.

facts.label: Local login screens
facts.value: FormClient requires an application-defined login URL and form posting to its callback; parameter names configurable.

facts.label: Federated and account screens
facts.value: Indirect clients redirect to identity-provider login UI; no complete first-party profile/settings/registration console established.

facts.label: Branding
facts.value: Application-owned form pages and redirects can be styled by the developer; no core branding-removal subscription.

facts.label: Domains and callback routing
facts.value: Configure callback URL and URL resolver; client can be distinguished by query or path parameter.

facts.label: UI language/accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public translated first-party account-screen catalog or accessibility conformance report established.

facts.label: Current runtime
facts.value: pac4j 6.x requires Java 17; older 5.x/4.x use Java 11/8 with the maintenance limits stated at the top.

facts.label: Framework integrations
facts.value: Official index links Spring MVC/Boot, Spring Security, WebFlux, Jakarta EE, Play 2/3, Vert.x, JAX-RS, Dropwizard, Javalin, Undertow, Shiro, Jooby, Spark, http4s and Ratpack integrations.

facts.label: Mobile/API integration
facts.value: CAS guide documents a standalone/mobile caller using an app service backed by CAS REST authentication; direct clients can secure web APIs.

facts.label: Native SDK and passkey parity
facts.value: No first-party iOS, Android, React Native or Flutter account-SDK compatibility matrix established.

facts.label: Application/framework prerequisite
facts.value: Add pac4j protocol module plus the selected framework integration; guide's OIDC path requires Java 17+, Maven and a registered provider.

facts.label: SQL local accounts
facts.value: pac4j-sql DbProfileService requires javax.sql.DataSource and user schema; password encoder must be configured.

facts.label: LDAP prerequisite
facts.value: pac4j-ldap LdapProfileService validates users and supplies profile CRUD through an external LDAP directory.

facts.label: MongoDB prerequisite
facts.value: pac4j-mongo MongoProfileService supplies password authentication and profile CRUD in an operator-selected MongoDB database/collection.

facts.label: Cache and session costs
facts.value: Store implementations include ConcurrentMapStore without extra dependency, and optional capped GuavaStore.

facts.label: Deployment and backup responsibilities
facts.value: Embed modules and integrate web security into the application; preserve app configuration, local profile storage and key material in operator-managed backups.

facts.label: Capacity/restore targets
facts.value: No universal hardware minimum, MAU sizing curve, backup schedule or restore-time guarantee established.

facts.label: Upgrade compatibility
facts.value: Keep pac4j-core/javaee/jakartaee dependency aligned with upgraded pac4j modules; review stream and integration compatibility.

facts.label: Custom authentication/profile logic
facts.value: Replace or extend Client, CredentialsExtractor, Authenticator, ProfileCreator, Authorizer, Matcher and AuthorizationGenerator.

facts.label: Custom web flow and persistence
facts.value: Config supports custom session/profile-manager factories, HTTP action adapter and security/callback/logout logic.

facts.label: Programmatic account CRUD
facts.value: ProfileService exposes create, update, remove/removeById, findById and findByLinkedId.

facts.label: SQL store administration
facts.value: DbProfileService validates credentials and creates/updates/deletes application-owned SQL profile records.

facts.label: Ban, search and impersonation controls
facts.value: No complete built-in ban/unban/search/impersonation administration workflow established.

facts.label: Linked-account primitive
facts.value: Profiles expose linkedId; LoadLinkedUserAuthorizationGenerator loads a locally mapped profile through ProfileService.

facts.label: Safe linking/unlinking and guest upgrade
facts.value: No finished user-facing link/unlink verification or durable guest-data upgrade flow established.

facts.label: CSRF checks
facts.value: First-party CsrfAuthorizer checks CSRF token on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE by default; optional checkAllRequests.

facts.label: CSRF documentation mismatch
facts.value: Web-authorizer prose describes POST-only checking, while released 6.6.1 CsrfAuthorizer code checks POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE by default.

facts.label: Default security and session caveat
facts.value: Security logic applies CSRF checks by default for indirect-client web profiles; direct clients made sessionful need explicit csrfCheck configuration.

facts.label: Security headers
facts.value: Default securityHeaders matchers include HSTS, content-type sniffing, frame, caching and XSS-protection response headers.

facts.label: Login/API rate limits
facts.value: No universal numeric requests-per-window, login burst quota, automatic failed-login lockout threshold or core throttle policy established.

facts.label: Diagnostic protocol logs
facts.value: Current modules expose PROTOCOL_MESSAGE.* DEBUG loggers; OIDC docs warn that raw exchanged messages can include tokens.

facts.label: Audit retention and streaming
facts.value: No managed security-audit event store, fixed retention days, export tier or durable webhook delivery guarantee established.

facts.label: Local profile export
facts.value: SQL schema stores id, username, password, linkedid and serializedprofile; operator can migrate its own records.

facts.label: Local password-hash export scope
facts.value: Local password values reside in the configured SQL user table, alongside IDs and linked identifiers.

facts.label: Portable identifiers
facts.value: Typed profile IDs include the profile class to distinguish identifiers from different identity providers.

facts.label: Import by application storage/API
facts.value: ProfileService create/update and configurable SQL attribute/column names support application-directed user migration.

facts.label: Existing password hash compatibility
facts.value: Use a PasswordEncoder that matches existing hashes; adapters wrap Spring Security Crypto, Apache Shiro or jBCrypt with explicit extra dependencies.

facts.label: Avoid re-encoding imported hashes
facts.value: AbstractProfileService create/update encode a supplied nonblank password before storage.

facts.label: Local account deletion
facts.value: ProfileService remove/removeById delegates deletion to the local profile store.

facts.label: Session/profile-data removal
facts.value: ProfileManager.removeProfiles clears pac4j profiles from the current request and session.

facts.label: Retention and account closure
facts.value: No universal profile/log/backup retention or purge schedule for developer-operated deployments.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: Application operator selects deployment and local session/database locations; federated providers process their own login traffic/data.

facts.label: Hosted processing agreement/assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to core as a vendor-operated customer-account hosting service.

facts.label: Public project legal/policy evidence
facts.value: Apache licence and security policy are public; separate project website privacy/terms pages were not found in this bounded check.

facts.label: Maintainer and ownership scope

facts.label: Retired lines and integrations

facts.label: Older framework adapters

facts.label: Core licence and commercial use
facts.value: Apache-2.0; permits commercial use, modification and distribution subject to licence conditions, without a core royalty.

apps.news: No qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signups, major paid feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found for Parse Server.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: No Parse Server MAU, returning-user, stored-user, login or token billing meter; Apache-2.0 grants the server software without a royalty.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: Core server may be used in production under Apache-2.0 without a license payment or stated user-count ceiling.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: No mandatory server license fee, annual commitment or paid production edition was found in the server license and deployment entry points.

facts.label: Usage pricing
facts.value: Core software license subtotal remains zero as users/logins grow; no project-owned monthly usage tariff is published in the server license or setup documentation.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Both fixed SAML business baselines are unsupported by the unextended server offer: native customer-org/invitation workflows and a native SAML service-provider adapter were not established.

facts.label: Customer organizations and member fees
facts.value: No packaged customer-organization subscription or native org/member/invitation allowance found. Builder can model workspaces, membership and invitations as objects/relations and secure them with roles/ACLs.

facts.label: Business connection and sync fees
facts.value: No core per-connection royalty. Included auth adapters support upstream services including Keycloak, LDAP and OAuth2 introspection; SAML and SCIM require an unverified extension or external service.

facts.label: Builder seats, projects and environments
facts.value: No purchased developer-seat or project quota. Dashboard configuration supplies its own admin users and app list; separate server processes/deployments provide app isolation.

facts.label: Email delivery and costs
facts.value: Operator installs/configures an email adapter and pays its sender. Maintained API Mail Adapter supplies templates/localization and integration examples for AWS SES, Mailgun and ZeptoMail, or a custom API.

facts.label: SMS delivery and costs
facts.value: Built-in MFA adapter's SMS method requires operator-supplied sendSMS callback; operator chooses and pays an SMS provider.

facts.label: Over-limit behavior and budget controls
facts.value: Vendor billing upgrades, spend caps and free-tier pauses do not apply. Configured request limits reject traffic; compute/storage exhaustion depends on the operator's infrastructure.

facts.label: Other billable items
facts.value: No server feature royalty for MFA, sessions, custom domains, hooks or logs under the core license; infrastructure, database, file storage, domain, mail, SMS and external IdPs remain separate costs.

facts.label: Eligibility and market
facts.value: Server license grants rights worldwide to individuals or legal entities. No hosted Parse Community signup, seller-country matrix or company-domain requirement applies to local software use.

facts.label: Self-service, trial and card
facts.value: Local npm/Docker setup and public deployment are documented without a vendor account or sales step; hosted trial length, card requirements and hosted production signup are not applicable.

facts.label: Product type and auth scope
facts.value: Self-hosted backend server with user accounts, password/provider login, revocable sessions, email verification/reset, role-based authorization and configurable auth adapters.

facts.label: Who operates production
facts.value: Builder or separately chosen host operates Node.js, database, files, TLS/network security, mail integration, backups, monitoring and upgrades.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built-in username or email plus password. Email can be used as username; current router also accepts the email field. Passwords use bcrypt, cost factor 10.

facts.label: Anonymous login
facts.value: Built-in anonymous auth provider; enableAnonymousUsers defaults true in 9.11.0.

facts.label: Email link/code, phone-first and wallet login
facts.value: No dedicated core magic-link sign-in, email-code sign-in, phone-first passwordless or wallet-signature adapter was found in the current user routes, adapter registry or auth source tree.

facts.label: Named social and platform adapters
facts.value: Core registry contains Apple, Google, Facebook, GitHub, Microsoft, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, Spotify, LINE, QQ, WeChat, Weibo, VKontakte, Meetup, Game Center and Google Play Games adapters.

facts.label: Provider setup and secure exchange
facts.value: Code-based adapters exchange an authorization code server-side; insecure adapter mode is deprecated and enableInsecureAuthAdapters defaults false in 9.11.0.

facts.label: Passkeys and WebAuthn
facts.value: No shipped WebAuthn/passkey adapter, credential routes or files found in the 9.11.0 auth registry, user router or repository tree.

facts.label: MFA factors and enrollment
facts.value: Built-in mfa adapter supports TOTP and SMS when configured in auth.mfa.options. Defaults: 6 digits, 30-second period, SHA1; SMS needs sendSMS.

facts.label: MFA enforcement
facts.value: Enrolled MFA is an additional auth policy. Login checks for a saved additional provider and rejects missing additional authData; solo-policy adapters can bypass additional-provider requirements.

facts.label: MFA recovery
facts.value: TOTP enrollment generates two single-use recovery codes; a recovery code can replace a TOTP token and is consumed on successful use.

facts.label: Other factors and recovery coverage
facts.value: Native email OTP, passkey/security-key second factors and a packaged lost-all-factors self-service recovery flow were not found in the MFA adapter or account APIs.

facts.label: Email verification and enforcement
facts.value: verifyUserEmails defaults false; can be true or a function. Verification sends a link and tracks emailVerified. preventLoginWithUnverifiedEmail separately defaults false; provider login bypasses that email-verification check.

facts.label: Verification-token expiry
facts.value: emailVerifyTokenValidityDuration is in seconds and defaults undefined, meaning no expiry; reuse of a still-valid verification token defaults false.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Built-in requestPasswordReset email link and server page. passwordPolicy.resetTokenValidityDuration defaults undefined/no expiry; revokeSessionOnPasswordReset defaults true.

facts.label: Email/phone changes and account deletion
facts.value: Updating email resets verification when enabled; signed-in users can update their account and delete it through DELETE /users/:objectId, subject to permissions. SMS MFA validates a mobile change through an OTP confirmation.

facts.label: Session model and lifetime
facts.value: Server-side _Session records with opaque sessionToken, user pointer, installationId, createdWith and expiresAt. sessionLength defaults 31,536,000 seconds; expireInactiveSessions true.

facts.label: Renewal and client persistence
facts.value: extendSessionOnUse defaults false. If enabled, a valid session is extended only after at least half its lifetime has passed. JS SDK caches the current user in localStorage or configured storage.

facts.label: Logout and device revocation
facts.value: Logout deletes the current _Session; a user can query/delete their other sessions, and an admin can manage them. Invalid revocable tokens produce Parse error 209.

facts.label: Upstream OAuth/OIDC role
facts.value: OAuth2 adapter performs RFC 7662 token introspection. Keycloak adapter validates the upstream access token's signature, issuer, authorized client and subject.

facts.label: SAML and identity-provider server roles
facts.value: No native SAML service-provider or SAML/OIDC identity-provider implementation found in the server's shipped auth registry, routes and source tree.

facts.label: Roles, membership and isolation
facts.value: Built-in Parse.Role groups users and nested roles; ACLs and class-level permissions grant data access. Customer-org, invitation, tenant-admin and membership-lifecycle workflows require app code.

facts.label: App/process tenancy limitation
facts.value: README explicitly says no multi-tenancy: only one Parse Server instance per Express app, with no isolation between apps in the same process.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: No built-in SCIM routes, v2 user/group mapping or directory deprovisioning workflow found in the source tree, auth registry and account APIs checked.

facts.label: Core end-user screens
facts.value: Core is an API/SDK backend; builder supplies normal web login/signup/profile UI. Server ships password-reset and email-verification feature pages, configurable through pages/customPages.

facts.label: Optional Android login UI
facts.value: ParseUI-Android is a separate project with login/signup-flow library and configurable XML/Intent styling.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Operator chooses frontend/API domains and publicServerURL; pages, appName, email templates and action URLs can be customized. No core domain or branding fee under the server license.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Server feature pages support locale/language/default fallback using directories or a JSON translation resource. Localization must be enabled; email adapter supports a localeCallback.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public end-user UI accessibility conformance report or tested accessibility matrix found in the server pages, SDK docs or optional Android UI README.

facts.label: Node 22 minimum discrepancy
facts.value: 9.11.0 README lists Node 22 minimum 22.12.0; the same release's package.json requires >=22.13.0.

facts.label: Web and server-rendered clients
facts.value: Project-maintained JS SDK has browser, Node, React Native and WeChat builds; REST works from any HTTP-capable client. JS SDK >=5 supports Parse Server >=7.

facts.label: Apple and Android clients
facts.value: Project-maintained Apple SDK supports iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS/tvOS; Android SDK supports Java/Kotlin integrations and lists Android API >=21 for SDK 2.1.

facts.label: React Native, Dart and Flutter
facts.value: React Native uses parse/react-native.js. Parse Community's Flutter repository ships parse_server_sdk for Dart and parse_server_sdk_flutter for Flutter.

facts.label: Database prerequisites
facts.value: MongoDB or PostgreSQL; operator supplies and maintains the database and indexes. 9.11.0 README lists MongoDB 7/8 and PostgreSQL 16/17/18 compatibility; PostGIS applies to geographic features.

facts.label: Other services
facts.value: Email adapter/sender required for reset and verification; Redis cache/shared throttling and file-storage adapters are optional architecture choices.

facts.label: Deployment and upgrades
facts.value: npm CLI, Express integration and Docker deployment documented. Operator owns network/firewall hardening, secrets, database indexes and version upgrades; README links the deprecation plan and LTS policy.

facts.label: Backup and restore procedure
facts.value: No single current, complete Parse-owned backup/restore runbook for user data, files, settings and hooks found in the server guide's deployment/database/best-practice sections and release README.

facts.label: Published sizing
facts.value: No universal CPU/RAM/disk requirement or safe MAU-to-machine sizing table found in deployment, database and performance guidance.

facts.label: Custom logic and user fields
facts.value: User objects support custom fields; Cloud Code provides functions and before/after save/delete hooks. Current server source also exposes beforeLogin, afterLogin, afterLogout and beforePasswordResetRequest triggers.

facts.label: Webhooks and authentication
facts.value: Function/trigger webhooks are managed through the master-key Hooks API. Outgoing requests can carry X-Parse-Webhook-Key when webhookKey is configured.

facts.label: Event delivery guarantees
facts.value: No durable event queue, delivery-retention window, retry/backoff schedule or exactly-once guarantee found in Hooks docs, controller and HTTP request implementation.

facts.label: User management
facts.value: REST/SDK and optional Parse Dashboard can create, query, update and delete _User records, with ACL/master-key authorization.

facts.label: Ban and unlock controls
facts.value: Custom beforeLogin can reject banned users. accountLockout supports failed-login threshold/duration. An empty user ACL set by master key prevents new logins; existing sessions must also be destroyed to revoke access.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: POST /loginAs creates a target-user session using the full master key; read-only master key is rejected. It bypasses normal login triggers and account-lockout checks.

facts.label: Link and unlink identities
facts.value: Built-in authData links multiple provider identities to an existing account; unlink sets that provider's authData to null. Current login rejects an identity already linked to another user.

facts.label: Upgrade anonymous account
facts.value: Matching JS SDK 8.7.0 strips anonymous authData when linking a provider or setting username, then saves against the existing user; failed provider linking restores the cached anonymous data.

facts.label: Login abuse and password policy
facts.value: Configurable accountLockout threshold/duration, password pattern/callback, username exclusion, password age and history; API throttling is configurable. Unknown-user login performs a dummy bcrypt comparison to reduce timing enumeration.

facts.label: Bot, breached-password and SMS protections
facts.value: No packaged CAPTCHA, breached-password feed or SMS destination-budget/fraud policy found in auth adapters, config and security guide. Custom validators/hooks and external edge/provider controls are available integration points.

facts.label: Default and configurable request limits
facts.value: No vendor plan quota; rateLimit defaults []. Rules specify requestPath/methods, requests per IP, millisecond time window and whether internal/master-key traffic is included.

facts.label: Limit response and distributed use
facts.value: Configured limits return HTTP 429 with a configurable message; default message Too many requests. Redis storage can coordinate counters; in-memory counters otherwise vary by server instance.

facts.label: Logs, events and export
facts.value: Default console and daily rotating JSON log files, viewable in Dashboard. Custom logger adapters/transports and auth hooks can record/export app-specific login/security events.

facts.label: Log retention
facts.value: maxLogFiles is unset by default: no files removed by that option; configure a file count or duration with d suffix. Logger query's default seven-day search range is not a seven-day retention policy.

facts.label: Profile and identifier export
facts.value: Self-service Dashboard class export downloads CSV; exporting all rows is capped at 10,000 per class. REST/SDK queries provide JSON user profiles/objectIds subject to permissions.

facts.label: Password hashes and provider links
facts.value: Operator controls the database, which stores bcrypt password hashes and provider authData. Normal account API responses do not provide a portable password export; a full exit needs deliberate database-level extraction and destination mapping.

facts.label: Profile/ID import
facts.value: Dashboard imports CSV/JSON into a class. Preserve object IDs requires allowCustomObjectId; preserve timestamps requires a Dashboard maintenanceKey. JSON uses Parse typed-object format.

facts.label: Foreign passwords and lazy migration
facts.value: No documented turnkey foreign-hash matrix, bulk auth migration package or lazy password migration workflow found in user docs, password helper, RestWrite and maintenance-key instructions.

facts.label: Account deletion and app cleanup
facts.value: Authenticated user deletion is available. afterDelete hooks can remove app-owned related records/files, but cleanup is developer logic and hook failure does not roll back a successful deletion.

facts.label: Retention and closure
facts.value: No vendor-held auth-project closure process. Operator chooses database/file backup retention and log policy; no fixed Parse Community end-user-data erasure deadline is published in the server materials checked.

facts.label: Data types and location
facts.value: Operator chooses server, database, file, backup and log locations. Auth data includes usernames/emails, bcrypt hashes, provider authData, MFA material and session records; outbound mail/SMS/provider calls involve chosen external services.

facts.label: Processing agreement and subprocessors
facts.value: A Parse Community hosted-auth DPA and subprocessor list are not applicable to the self-hosted server offer documented here; operator selects its own processors.

facts.label: Assurance reports
facts.value: No public server-scoped SOC 2/ISO 27001 certificate, audit report, trust-center report or compliance edition found in README, license, security policy and public legal pages checked.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Parse Server; part of Parse Platform, maintained in the parse-community organization. Node.js/Express server repository: parse-community/parse-server.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active: npm latest is 9.11.0, published 2026-11-03; a separate 8.x LTS branch is receiving updates. No current server shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the lifecycle sources checked.

facts.label: Historical transfer notice
facts.value: Parse Dashboard's license says Parse, LLC transferred its code to parse-community on 2017-04-05 and stopped contributing/distributing that code.

facts.label: Server license and commercial use
facts.value: Apache-2.0: no-charge copyright and patent grants, including modification and distribution, subject to license/notice obligations; no production subscription condition in this license.

facts.label: Dashboard license — separate component
facts.value: Custom Parse Dashboard license: royalty-free use/copy; redistribution as part of your own software only if that software is not solely the Dashboard; modifications granted for internal use.

facts.label: JS and Dart/Flutter SDK licenses
facts.value: JS SDK 8.7.0 and the checked Dart/Flutter repository license use Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Android and Apple SDK licenses
facts.value: Checked Android and Apple SDK license files use BSD terms with three redistribution/name-endorsement conditions.

facts.label: Status and uptime promise
facts.value: No Parse Community hosted-auth SLA/status service applies to an operator-run deployment. Local /parse/health reports initialization/startup/ok/error state; license supplies software as-is.

facts.label: Stable release and LTS evidence
facts.value: npm latest 9.11.0 dated 2026-11-03; GitHub latest endpoint returned 8.6.122 dated 2026-11-05, an LTS patch. 9.11.1-alpha.2 was a prerelease when checked.

facts.label: Current security advisories
facts.value: Nov 4/5 advisories cover beforeSave dot-notation denial of service and field-policy bypass. Listed patched lines include 8.6.121/8.6.122 and 9.11.1 alpha releases; stable 9.11.0 falls within the affected 9.x ranges.

facts.label: Maintenance and deprecations
facts.value: Previous major receives LTS security work until displaced by the next major; project warns LTS is transitional and some fixes may be left to community contributors. Deprecations are tracked separately.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Repository issues/contribution process, Parse Community Forum and project chat are the public support routes linked in the README.

facts.label: Support prices and response promises
facts.value: No mandatory paid support plan, staffed hours or ordinary support response-time commitment found in README, contributing guide or license.

facts.label: Hosted billing meter
facts.value: Not applicable: Passport core has no vendor MAU, returning-user, stored-user or request billing unit.

facts.label: Free production use
facts.value: Core MIT license permits production/commercial use without a license fee or licensed user-volume cap.

facts.label: Hosted paid minimum
facts.value: Not applicable: no Passport core subscription, annual commitment or vendor production minimum.

facts.label: Hosted usage tiers and overages
facts.value: Not applicable: no Passport-hosted usage ladder, member tiers or platform overage formula.

facts.label: Business cost applicability
facts.value: Hosted B2B plan prices are not applicable. SAML is a plugin; customer organizations, invitations and roles must be built separately.

facts.label: Organization platform fees/caps
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted Passport plan: no vendor organization allowance, per-team price or 100-member commercial cap.

facts.label: SAML/OIDC license and connection fee
facts.value: MIT-covered SAML/OIDC strategies have no per-connection software-license fee in their licenses; no hosted connection billing applies.

facts.label: Builder seats, projects and domains
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor dashboard seat plan, project quota, staging subscription or per-domain fee.

facts.label: Login email delivery dependency
facts.value: Email magic-link tutorial uses a builder-supplied SendGrid account/API key; Passport core does not operate a mail sender.

facts.label: Sender flexibility and message fee
facts.value: passport-magic-link delegates delivery to the application's sendToken callback; no Passport message allowance or delivery fee applies.

facts.label: Hosted cap enforcement
facts.value: Not applicable: no Passport-hosted member cap, automatic tier upgrade, grace period or spending alert.

facts.label: Other platform charges
facts.value: Not applicable: core does not bill token usage, security add-ons, logs or membership transactions.

facts.label: Hosted eligibility and markets
facts.value: Not applicable: no Passport-hosted customer account or seller-country gate for using the core library.

facts.label: Hosted signup, card and trial
facts.value: Not applicable: install the npm library and chosen strategy packages; no Passport SaaS signup or production trial.

facts.label: Type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Node.js request-authentication middleware using separately installed strategies; application supplies routes, account database and account lifecycle.

facts.label: Who operates accounts and sessions
facts.value: Developer operates the application, account storage, selected strategies and session middleware/store; Passport authenticates incoming requests inside that app.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Plugin: passport-local parses username/password and calls the app's verify function. Database lookup and password-hash verification are app code.

facts.label: Email magic link
facts.value: Plugin: passport-magic-link; current README defaults ttl to 10 minutes and allowReuse=false; application supplies user lookup and sending.

facts.label: Anonymous requests
facts.value: Plugin: passport-anonymous can pass a request with req.user remaining undefined.

facts.label: Phone/email OTP and wallets
facts.value: Core has no bundled first-factor phone OTP, email-code sender or wallet-account implementation; an appropriate separate strategy/custom flow would be required.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: Plugin passport-google-oauth20 by the project author; OAuth 2.0 callback flow with registered Google app/client credentials.

facts.label: Facebook
facts.value: Plugin passport-facebook by the project author; OAuth 2.0 login with provider client ID/secret and callback configuration.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: Community plugin passport-github2 from cfsghost/passport-github; OAuth 2.0 authentication.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: Community plugin passport-apple from ananay/passport-apple, with Apple app/team/key/callback configuration.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: Community plugin passport-microsoft from seanfisher/passport-microsoft uses OAuth 2.0/Microsoft Graph with tenant/scope options.

facts.label: WebAuthn/passkey mechanism
facts.value: Plugin passport-fido2-webauthn authenticates public-key WebAuthn credentials and registers credentials via application callbacks.

facts.label: Challenge and origin validation
facts.value: WebAuthn strategy source validates a challenge, origin and RP ID hash; default SessionChallengeStore stores challenges in req.session.

facts.label: Passkey client/fallback details
facts.value: Complete conditional-autofill, synced-passkey, native iOS/Android, credential-domain migration and recovery matrix not published in the WebAuthn docs checked.

facts.label: Authenticator MFA
facts.value: Plugin passport-totp verifies a TOTP after an initial factor has already authenticated the user.

facts.label: MFA recovery and other factors
facts.value: Core does not supply managed recovery codes, factor reset, SMS/email delivery or a global MFA-enforcement setting; implement policy and recovery around chosen strategies.

facts.label: Signup and verification
facts.value: Application builds signup routes/forms and stores account records. Email tutorial demonstrates verifying ownership when a magic link is clicked.

facts.label: Reset/change/delete lifecycle
facts.value: Password reset, address changes and account deletion are application-owned routes/database operations, not Passport core account-management APIs.

facts.label: Stateful sessions
facts.value: Core offers session authentication plus serializeUser/deserializeUser hooks; application chooses which user data/ID is stored and reloaded.

facts.label: Login/logout regeneration
facts.value: Since 0.6.0, req.login and req.logout regenerate sessions and clear session information by default; keepSessionInfo=true opts into preserving prior session data.

facts.label: Current-session logout
facts.value: req.logout removes login state/req.user; session manager saves cleared login state and regenerates the current session.

facts.label: Expiry and cookie controls
facts.value: With express-session, cookie defaults are path /, httpOnly true, secure false and maxAge null; developer configures expiry, secure transport and SameSite.

facts.label: Stateless API/JWT path
facts.value: session:false can disable login-session creation; passport-jwt validates a token supplied by the request using application-configured key/extractor and optional issuer/audience/algorithm rules.

facts.label: Account-wide/device revocation
facts.value: Implement named-device inventory and cross-session revocation in the app/session store. deserializeUser can reject a user and remove its login state on a later request.

facts.label: Incoming SAML
facts.value: Plugin @node-saml/passport-saml implements the SAML 2.0 service-provider side: redirect to an IdP and validate its response.

facts.label: Multiple SAML customer IdPs
facts.value: MultiSamlStrategy selects per-request configuration through getSamlOptions; provider lookup and trust boundaries are application code.

facts.label: Incoming OIDC
facts.value: Plugin passport-openidconnect is an OIDC relying-party/client strategy authenticating against an OpenID Provider.

facts.label: OAuth authorization server boundary
facts.value: Core authenticates requests/tokens; official API-auth docs refer to sibling OAuth2orize for implementing an OAuth 2.0 authorization server.

facts.label: Customer organizations and roles
facts.value: No core organization/invitation/role data model or admin workflow; build these in the application's own schema and route authorization.

facts.label: SCIM account provisioning
facts.value: Not provided by Passport core; SCIM endpoints, user/group schema mapping, deactivation and storage require another component/custom service.

facts.label: Login/account UI
facts.value: Application builds forms, pages and routes; official tutorial supplies example HTML/templates and route code rather than hosted pages or a drop-in account dashboard.

facts.label: Themes and custom domains
facts.value: No Passport-hosted branding/theme/domain tier applies; application owns its UI, hosting and callback URLs.

facts.label: UI languages and accessibility
facts.value: Not applicable to a core-hosted UI: Passport supplies middleware, not a localized login screen or assessed component set.

facts.label: Primary runtime/framework
facts.value: Node.js with Connect-style request middleware, especially Express; core package declares node >=0.4.0.

facts.label: Selected strategy runtime floors
facts.value: passport-magic-link 4.1.0 declares Node >=22; @node-saml/passport-saml 5.1.1 declares Node >=18 and a separate LTS-only support policy.

facts.label: Browser/edge framework boundary
facts.value: Passport core is a server-side Node/Connect middleware API, not a React/Vue browser SDK or a Web Request-only edge adapter.

facts.label: Mobile and desktop clients
facts.value: Core runs on the application's Node backend; browser/native clients can call an app API protected by bearer/JWT strategies.

facts.label: User database dependency
facts.value: Application supplies account/profile/password/federated-identity storage and verify callbacks; Passport does not prescribe SQL/NoSQL or a schema.

facts.label: Session store dependency
facts.value: Stateful tutorials use express-session with connect-sqlite3; session package defaults to MemoryStore, explicitly unsuitable for production and multiple processes.

facts.label: External services and secrets
facts.value: Social/OIDC/SAML strategies need configured IdP credentials/certificates; email links need an application sender. Core password requests need neither a vendor account DB nor per-login mail.

facts.label: Deployment/backup/upgrade responsibility
facts.value: Install library and selected strategies into the application; operator deploys Node app, database/session stores, TLS, backups and dependency updates.

facts.label: Capacity guidance
facts.value: No universal supported-user count, minimum RAM/CPU, scaling benchmark or tested fixed-user cost profile published in the core docs/source checked.

facts.label: Custom authentication and callbacks
facts.value: Application configures named strategies and verify callbacks; can write a custom strategy and handle success/failure/error/redirect behavior.

facts.label: Custom authenticate completion
facts.value: authenticate accepts a custom callback; when used, the app is responsible for login/session handling and appropriate response behavior.

facts.label: User fields and webhooks
facts.value: User fields belong to the app schema; outbound webhooks/jobs are app code, not a managed Passport event-delivery service.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Core has no hosted user dashboard or CRUD management API; creating, querying, disabling and deleting accounts are developer database/application operations.

facts.label: Support/impersonation controls
facts.value: No core-managed impersonation, admin roles or consent/audit workflow; req.login(user) can establish an app session once the app has chosen the user.

facts.label: Connecting provider accounts
facts.value: passport.authorize runs a strategy and assigns its result to req.account without changing the existing req.user/login session; app associates and saves that account.

facts.label: Guest upgrades
facts.value: passport-anonymous leaves req.user undefined; it does not mint a stored guest identity. Persistent guest data/upgrade/linking must be designed by the app.

facts.label: Session-fixation mitigation
facts.value: 0.6.0 changelog records session-fixation hardening through login/logout regeneration; current session manager implements regeneration.

facts.label: Route authorization boundary
facts.value: Session middleware may pass an unauthenticated request onward; protected routes must enforce authentication/permissions themselves.

facts.label: Brute-force, bot and password controls
facts.value: Core does not bundle a CAPTCHA service, leaked-password checking, login-throttling policy or SMS-spend guard; integrate controls in app/strategy/provider layers.

facts.label: Password-check recipe
facts.value: Official password example performs application PBKDF2 hashing and timingSafeEqual comparison, returning a generic incorrect-credentials message.

facts.label: Hosted API quota
facts.value: Not applicable: Passport has no vendor login/management endpoint quota, billed request window or shared tenant rate limit.

facts.label: Local throughput and rate enforcement
facts.value: No universal built-in logins/second or per-IP/per-account lockout threshold; app decides throttling and capacity.

facts.label: Audit events and retention
facts.value: App can log custom strategy/authenticate outcomes; core does not operate a persistent security-event log, audit export or retention service.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and credential data ownership
facts.value: Account/profile/password data remain in the application's selected database; core does not impose an export schema or hold a vendor copy for later export.

facts.label: Hash and account-link extraction
facts.value: Exportability/formats come from the app database/schema; tutorial example stores username, hashed_password and salt, while provider associations are app records.

facts.label: Passkey and OAuth migration caveats
facts.value: WebAuthn app stores credential/public-key/user associations and validates origin/RP identity; provider tokens/account links are also application-managed.

facts.label: Existing database and hashes
facts.value: App verify function can authenticate against an existing user database and whichever password verification function the app supplies.

facts.label: Bulk import and signup distinction
facts.value: Core has no bulk-user import service or prescribed migration file. Official signup recipe inserts users through application route code.

facts.label: Account deletion and retention
facts.value: App deletes user/credential/provider-link records and configures session/log/backup retention; Passport is not the hosted record owner.

facts.label: Current session deletion
facts.value: express-session Session.destroy destroys the current session; Passport logout clears its login state, not all account data.

facts.label: Vendor data residency
facts.value: Not applicable: Passport core supplies no hosted member-data region or residency subscription.

facts.label: Vendor DPA/subprocessors/assurance
facts.value: Not applicable to core as a hosted processor: it is locally executed MIT-licensed software, not a vendor account-processing service.

facts.label: Name, author and URLs
facts.value: Passport.js, published as npm package passport; authored by an individual. Official site https://www.passportjs.org/; docs https://www.passportjs.org/docs/; core repository under the author’s GitHub account.

facts.label: Availability and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Core repository is public, archived=false and disabled=false. No official whole-project shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found.

facts.label: Dated core release and activity
facts.value: Latest npm tag: 0.7.0, published 2023-11-27T22:57:38.830Z; latest default-branch commit found: 2024-08-16T21:56:08Z, Update README.

facts.label: SAML package rename/deprecation
facts.value: Unscoped passport-saml 3.2.4 is deprecated; package notice directs versions 4+ to @node-saml/passport-saml.

facts.label: Core license and commercial use
facts.value: MIT: use, copy, modify, distribute, sublicense and sell are allowed, retaining copyright/permission notices; no license fee or user-count condition.

facts.label: Password strategy license
facts.value: passport-local: MIT.

facts.label: WebAuthn and TOTP licenses
facts.value: passport-fido2-webauthn and passport-totp: MIT.

facts.label: Magic-link license
facts.value: passport-magic-link: MIT.

facts.label: Enterprise strategy licenses
facts.value: @node-saml/passport-saml and passport-openidconnect: MIT.

facts.label: Selected social strategy licenses
facts.value: Google passport-google-oauth20, passport-facebook, passport-github2 and passport-microsoft have MIT license text in their repositories.

facts.label: Apple/JWT package licensing
facts.value: passport-apple package.json declares MIT; passport-jwt has MIT license text.

facts.label: Status page and uptime SLA
facts.value: Not applicable: library project does not operate the application's production authentication service or sell a core uptime SLA.

facts.label: Core release
facts.value: passport 0.7.0 latest npm release dated 2023-11-27; changelog agrees on version/date.

facts.label: Selected strategy release ages
facts.value: passport-fido2-webauthn 0.1.0 published 2022-06-06; passport-totp 0.0.2 published 2015-08-27.

facts.label: Newer strategy maintenance
facts.value: passport-magic-link 4.1.0 published 2026-08-26; @node-saml/passport-saml 5.1.1 published 2026-09-28.

facts.label: Core support/security policy
facts.value: Formal supported-version/LTS matrix, guaranteed patch window and security-response deadline not found.

facts.label: Community help and bugs
facts.value: Issue template directs integration help to passport/discuss and reserves core issues for reproducible defects or incorrect docs.

facts.label: Security reporting
facts.value: Potential security vulnerabilities should be reported privately to jaredhanson@gmail.com per project issue/PR templates.

facts.label: Hosted premium support
facts.value: Not applicable: no Passport core hosted support tier or subscription response SLA.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Per cluster subscription, not registered users, MAU, returning-user days or SSO connections; users are unlimited on all tiers.

facts.label: Published load definition
facts.value: Sizing assumes each active user performs 30 logins and 1,000 token refreshes per month, roughly 1,030 token requests. Starter 5k, Premium 100k, Enterprise 500k such users.

facts.label: Ongoing free hosted allowance
facts.value: No public ongoing free-production quota located; current free offer is the 30-day Starter trial.

facts.label: Lowest paid monthly rate
facts.value: Starter: US$149/month per dedicated cluster, monthly-only billing after its trial.

facts.label: Commitment wording
facts.value: Unclear: self-service pricing/billing says cancel at paid-period end, but the SaaS service agreement lists a one-year order-form term with automatic renewal and 30-day non-renewal notice.

facts.label: Taxes and refunds
facts.value: United States currency, applicable taxes additional. Ordinary subscription payments are non-refundable; SaaS agreement separately provides unused prepaid monthly-fee refunds after contractual termination.

facts.label: Monthly and annual rates
facts.value: Starter US$149/month; Premium US$999/month or US$749/month billed annually; Enterprise US$2,999/month or US$2,499/month billed annually; Custom quoted.

facts.label: Capacity, not user overage
facts.value: Starter sized for 5,000 standard-load users; Premium 100,000; Enterprise 500,000. No per-user charge or automatic surcharge at the sizing threshold.

facts.label: Annual amounts
facts.value: Our calculation: Premium US$749 × 12 = US$8,988/year; Enterprise US$2,499 × 12 = US$29,988/year, before tax.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Our calculation under the same standard traffic: A (1k users/10 orgs/1 SAML) Starter US$149/month; B (10k users/100 orgs/10 SAML) Premium US$999/month.

facts.label: Organization features and charge
facts.value: Phase Two Organizations extension provides memberships, org-specific roles/attributes, invitations, IdP links and customer administration; included suite has no separately listed per-org/member charge.

facts.label: Organization/member ceilings
facts.value: No public numeric customer-organization/member/invitation ceiling or per-unit overage tariff located.

facts.label: Business SSO connection charges
facts.value: Unlimited SSO connections on Starter/Premium/Enterprise; SAML/OIDC and the included IdP Wizard do not have a published per-connection fee.

facts.label: SCIM charge and maturity
facts.value: SCIM user provisioning is listed in the included suite; Phase Two organization-scoped SCIM is explicitly experimental, disabled until the realm flag is enabled.

facts.label: Infrastructure and resource caps
facts.value: Per cluster: realms Starter 5/Premium 20/Enterprise 100; custom themes 1/1/unlimited; own extension JARs 0/1/unlimited.

facts.label: Builder teams and API clients
facts.value: Dashboard teams support roles, member invitations, billing contacts and SSO. Maximum 10 API secrets per owning team/organization; eleventh returns HTTP 400.

facts.label: Custom domains
facts.value: Included domain count Starter 2, Premium 5, Enterprise 15; Custom scoped. Wildcards and app-association files have separate plan gates.

facts.label: Outbound email
facts.value: Customer configures its internet-reachable SMTP server/provider for verification, magic links/codes, resets, invitations and other account email.

facts.label: SMS dependency/cost
facts.value: SMS is not built into Keycloak or bundled in the Phase Two image. Docs recommend netzbegruenung/keycloak-mfa-plugins plus a customer SMS-provider HTTP endpoint; hosted setup is support-assisted.

facts.label: Exceeding load vs hard quotas
facts.value: Past the active-user sizing nothing is blocked, throttled or surcharged solely for user count; latency can degrade and staff contact the customer. Realm/resources/domain/IP quotas remain enforced.

facts.label: Failed payments and cancellation
facts.value: Failed renewal leaves cluster running as Billing required while retried/resolved; eventual removal date is communicated. Cancellation ends charging after paid period, with the documented deletion timeline.

facts.label: Other priced/quoted features
facts.value: Own extensions may incur complexity-based fees; Enterprise 99.99% SLA extension/private connectivity and special regions are additional quoted charges.

facts.label: Optional telemetry
facts.value: Enterprise includes the experimental Telemetry Export feature; it sends logs/events to a customer OTLP endpoint.

facts.label: Solo-builder eligibility
facts.value: Service agreement expressly accepts a person or legal entity; Starter targets new projects/small teams and can be bought through self-service.

facts.label: Country restrictions
facts.value: Terms prohibit US-embargo/restricted-party access; a complete explicit buyer-country list was not found.

facts.label: Self-service trial and payment
facts.value: Starter has a 30-day free trial once per customer. Stripe checkout requires a payment method; after trial it continues at US$149/month unless canceled.

facts.label: Account entry requirements
facts.value: Dashboard signup requires email or linking an SSO provider; current docs describe a self-service path to a realm/cluster.

facts.label: Product type and coverage
facts.value: Managed Keycloak hosting plus an extension suite for accounts, login, sessions, verification, business organizations, SSO, self-service and events; a self-host container is also available.

facts.label: Distribution scope
facts.value: Self-host image uses p2-inc/keycloak with added CockroachDB support, plus bundled extensions. Hosted control plane and some scale/storage code are not included in the image.

facts.label: Hosted operator responsibilities
facts.value: Phase Two operates dedicated compute/network/storage, database backups, monitoring and hosted version upgrades. Customer configures apps, realms, authentication, user policies and custom resources.

facts.label: Self-host operator responsibilities
facts.value: Builder operates the server/database, backups, monitoring, security patching, capacity and upgrade rollout. Managed dashboard, hosted operations and paid uptime commitments do not come with the image.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in: username/password or configured email login; self-registration and reset/verification policies are realm settings.

facts.label: Email magic link
facts.value: plugin, bundled: keycloak-magic-link on every Phase Two cluster; ordinary link completes sign-in on the opening device, continuation mode completes in the original waiting browser.

facts.label: Email code
facts.value: plugin, bundled: keycloak-magic-link Email OTP sends a six-digit code and can be first-factor passwordless login or a second factor.

facts.label: Phone code
facts.value: additional_plugin/external_service: SMS authentication uses the separately installed recommended SMS authenticator and provider API; phone validation/update actions are configured.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: Anonymous-account login/guest conversion and crypto-wallet sign-in were not established.

facts.label: Social: GitHub and generic providers
facts.value: GitHub has a documented native provider setup; other built-in social adapters and generic OIDC providers can appear in the browser login flow.

facts.label: Social: Apple
facts.value: Apple sign-in is bundled via klausbetz/apple-identity-provider-keycloak, supporting web and native token exchange; requires Apple service/client, team/key configuration and redirect registration.

facts.label: Social: Google/Facebook and inventory scope
facts.value: Vendor CIAM guide explicitly names Google, Facebook and GitHub social login. A complete current provider/build matrix or personal Microsoft setup was not established.

facts.label: Passkeys and WebAuthn
facts.value: built_in: passwordless passkey or password plus WebAuthn second factor; native Enable Passkeys offers conditional autofill and a passkey button while retaining password fallback.

facts.label: Passkey domain/client limitations
facts.value: Credentials bind to relying-party ID/domain; hostname changes can require re-enrollment. Mobile apps should use the system browser; embedded in-app browsers may not support passkeys.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Native authenticator-app TOTP and WebAuthn; bundled email-code extension can be a second factor. SMS needs the extra plugin/provider path.

facts.label: Recovery codes and lost-device handling
facts.value: Keycloak recovery codes are documented; the browser flow's recovery-code form must be enabled as an alternative before generated codes can be used. Admin can remove a lost credential and require re-enrollment.

facts.label: Verification/reset/profile lifecycle
facts.value: Email verification, registration, reset/change password, profile attributes and linked-account management are configurable. Default collected fields: username, email, first/last name.

facts.label: User self-service and deletion
facts.value: Account Console/Admin Portal expose profile and credential management with account roles; account deletion can be exposed through the applicable Keycloak action.

facts.label: Session defaults and controls
facts.value: Vendor guide for Keycloak 26.8.1 lists access tokens 5 minutes, SSO idle 30 minutes/max 10 hours, offline idle 30 days, refresh revocation off by default; all configurable.

facts.label: Revocation and offline sessions
facts.value: Logout ends regular sessions/refresh validity; offline sessions must be revoked separately. Locally verified access tokens can remain usable until their expiry.

facts.label: Business protocol roles
facts.value: Keycloak issues OIDC/OAuth 2.0 tokens to apps and brokers external SAML/OIDC identity providers. Organization associations support domain-directed business SSO.

facts.label: SSO wizard editions
facts.value: Guided SAML/OIDC/LDAP setup and vendor flows are available. Public image contains generic wizards; vendor-specific wizards can require a supported/licensed private image.

facts.label: Organization memberships and roles
facts.value: Phase Two extension models many customer organizations within one realm; members get independent org-specific roles that do not inherit Keycloak realm/client roles.

facts.label: Invitations and delegation
facts.value: Keycloak/org admins can invite existing/new users and preassign org roles via API. Verified email is required for acceptance; user must accept/decline after authentication.

facts.label: Shared or multiple IdPs
facts.value: Realm configuration controls sharing one IdP across organizations, multiple IdPs within one organization, portal-link expiry and automatic org-admin creation.

facts.label: Organization-scoped SCIM
facts.value: plugin/experimental: Phase Two Organizations exposes per-org SCIM endpoints over the organization member graph, including /Users and /Groups paths.

facts.label: SCIM auth/offboarding limits
facts.value: Configurable Keycloak bearer token, external JWT, bearer secret or HTTP Basic. Credentials/configuration are scoped to the organization; stored shared passwords/secrets use Argon2id.

facts.label: Hosted and self-host UI
facts.value: Default phasetwo-ui theme covers login, account, admin and email. Separate Admin Portal offers user/org self-management with a generated portal link.

facts.label: Portal access controls
facts.value: Profile/credential/linked-account screens use account-client roles; org details/members/invitations/IdPs use organization member roles and optional visibility attributes.

facts.label: Theme customization and quotas
facts.value: Runtime realm-attribute branding/CSS is included. Uploaded custom themes: Starter 1, Premium 1, Enterprise unlimited; resources are uploaded per Keycloak major version.

facts.label: Custom domains and platform files
facts.value: Starter 2/Premium 5/Enterprise 15 domains; wildcard domains Enterprise+; app association files Premium+. Certificate/DNS setup is documented.

facts.label: Attribution removal
facts.value: Complete attribution-removal rights/controls were not established. Email guide says default footer includes Powered by Phase Two; customer CSS/custom themes are available.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Vendor documents multi-language login support and realm localization overrides; passkey labels can be overridden per language.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public Phase Two-specific accessibility conformance/audit report found for the default hosted UI.

facts.label: Browser and server clients
facts.value: Any compliant OIDC relying-party library can integrate. Vendor guides/examples cover Django, JavaScript, React, Next.js, Vue, Nuxt, React Router/Remix, SvelteKit and Angular.

facts.label: React and Next.js details
facts.value: React guide uses react-oidc-context/oidc-client-ts or oidc-spa with code+PKCE. Next example uses Next.js 16, NextAuth.js 4.24, Node.js 24 and server-side encrypted session cookies.

facts.label: Administration SDKs
facts.value: Phase Two extension/admin API libraries are listed for Java/JVM, JavaScript/TypeScript and Python; OpenAPI permits generating other clients.

facts.label: Native apps
facts.value: Vendor recommends external AppAuth for Android, iOS and macOS with browser login/redirect back to the app and configured standard-flow client/redirect scheme.

facts.label: Other mobile/runtime detail
facts.value: Complete Phase Two React Native, Flutter, desktop OS/version or native-passkey compatibility matrix was not found.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Phase Two operates the hosted CockroachDB-backed identity stack. Builder supplies app hosting/database/integration and its own SMTP or SMS provider when used.

facts.label: Self-host prerequisites
facts.value: Self-host image supports upstream Keycloak databases plus CockroachDB; PostgreSQL is the simplest documented default. Production also needs hostname/TLS, persistent database and operator-managed services.

facts.label: Self-host deployment
facts.value: Docker image plus Helm codecentric keycloakx or matching Keycloak Operator are documented. Multi-node cache discovery defaults to database-backed jdbc-ping from Keycloak 26.1.

facts.label: Self-host upgrades and recovery
facts.value: Pin full image tag, back up database before schema migration and test themes/providers. Patch upgrades can often roll; minor/major cache/schema changes may require a stop window.

facts.label: Native/custom flow logic
facts.value: Custom authentication flows, profile attributes, token mappers and SPIs are available. Own JARs: no Starter slot, 1 Premium, unlimited Enterprise, with possible complexity fees.

facts.label: Events and webhook customization
facts.value: Bundled events extension supports access/admin/custom events, filtered webhooks, HMAC/bearer/unsigned delivery options and retries after committed transactions.

facts.label: User administration
facts.value: Keycloak Admin Console/Admin REST API provide user/account administration; Phase Two extension APIs add orgs, membership, roles, invitations and event capabilities.

facts.label: Impersonation scope
facts.value: Specific hosted Phase Two impersonation controls/entitlement/audit behavior were not established from the reviewed public guides.

facts.label: Linked login methods
facts.value: Account Console/Admin Portal can manage social/brokered logins when manage-account-links is granted; external-provider token storage is configurable.

facts.label: Native account/password protection
facts.value: Native configurable per-user brute-force detection and password rules; customer-uploaded password denylists are available on all hosted tiers.

facts.label: Bots and SMS abuse
facts.value: Bundled keycloak-magic-link Turnstile steps are included on every cluster but off until own Cloudflare keys/theme/flow are configured. Per-IP WAF and native lockout provide different protections.

facts.label: Edge requests by tier
facts.value: Per client IP over rolling 5 minutes, all cluster paths: Starter 1,000 requests; Premium 2,000; Enterprise 4,000; Enterprise custom limits by arrangement.

facts.label: Rate enforcement and management gap
facts.value: Edge returns HTTP 429, Retry-After: 300 and no-store; blocking lifts as previous-five-minute traffic drops, and blocked retries still count. Separate control-plane numeric quota not located.

facts.label: Hosted event capture
facts.value: Hosted access/admin events are captured automatically by the platform; customer does not need realm Save Events enabled, and native realm event expiry does not bound the platform's copies.

facts.label: Logs, exports and retention unknown
facts.value: Dashboard offers streaming/event/request tables and downloadable retained files. Exact hosted event/log retention days by plan were not found.

facts.label: Telemetry edition
facts.value: Enterprise Telemetry Export streams logs/events to customer's OTLP collector, experimental; downstream retention/storage is customer's responsibility.

facts.label: Hosted profile/config export
facts.value: Realm configuration and user/organization data can be exported; org export supports roles, provider links and optional member/invitation content.

facts.label: Hosted credentials and database dump
facts.value: Backup guide explicitly says credentials are not exportable in reusable form; EU exit page offers a database dump on request without specifying reusable credential/key material.

facts.label: Self-host exit scope
facts.value: Self-host operator owns the database/export process and can retain configuration plus Phase Two organization representations; target Keycloak/extension/version and credential compatibility must be preserved.

facts.label: Lazy migration in
facts.value: Bundled user-migration extension can look up users and validate passwords against a customer-supplied legacy REST service on first login.

facts.label: Bulk migration and relationships
facts.value: Docs support Keycloak partial import, PBKDF2/Argon2 hashes when exportable, or password reset otherwise. Org import supports custom IDs and strict/skip-missing referenced users/IdPs.

facts.label: Ending a lazy migration
facts.value: Unlink imported users before disabling/deleting the federation provider; provider deletion can delete linked users, and disabling can prevent their login.

facts.label: Cancellation/deployment retention
facts.value: After paid period: cluster available for up to 7 days, removed at day 7, realms/data permanently purged at day 14 according to billing guide; no further subscription charges after period end.

facts.label: Backup and legal retention scope
facts.value: Hosted encrypted hourly backups are retained 30 days. Whether deleted customer data is also removed from older backups by the day-14 purge is not explained.

facts.label: Primary region options
facts.value: Self-service: AWS Frankfurt eu-central-1, N. Virginia us-east-1, Oregon us-west-2. Additional-fee assisted regions include AWS Ireland/Mumbai/Singapore and listed GCP locations.

facts.label: EU data location map
facts.value: EU cluster database, credentials, sessions/cache, event store, logs/metrics and realm signing keys: Frankfurt; encrypted backups: Ireland. Builder dashboard/support/billing systems: US.

facts.label: Keys and overseas access
facts.value: EU keys held in vendor-controlled AWS KMS Frankfurt, not customer-held/BYOK. Named operations staff outside the EU can access clusters; access logs are internal, not exposed to customers.

facts.label: Self-host/global location scope
facts.value: Self-host operator chooses location; custom/global clusters may span regions and require a scoped region set. Global CockroachDB clusters are described as beta.

facts.label: Processing agreement and entities
facts.value: Public Article 28 processing summary; signature DPA on request without NDA. EU/UK processor: Phase Two UK, Ltd (England/Wales 16815578); elsewhere Phase Two, Inc.; parent Inc. is a UK entity's operations subprocessor.

facts.label: Assurance evidence
facts.value: Vendor states current SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001; reports/certificate, penetration summaries and recovery plan are available through approval-based Trust Center requests.

facts.label: Subprocessor list retrieval
facts.value: Known Trust Center/subprocessors URLs returned a JavaScript shell with no readable list through direct/web retrieval.

facts.label: Breach and deletion process
facts.value: Published DPA summary says personal-data breach notice within 48–72 hours after awareness, assistance with rights requests, and return/delete on customer choice/request; no formal deletion certificate today.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Phase Two; Phase Two, Inc., a Washington corporation, Seattle, United States. Site https://phasetwo.io/; docs https://phasetwo.io/docs/introduction/.

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Public self-service hosted cluster creation and Starter/Premium/Enterprise plans are offered; Custom is sales-scoped. Signup and checkout not tested.

facts.label: Management API lifecycle
facts.value: Management API and its credentials are experimental and unsupported; docs recommend test environments rather than production automation for now.

facts.label: Underlying server license
facts.value: Keycloak base: Apache License 2.0, with commercial use/modification/distribution rights subject to conditions.

facts.label: Phase Two Organizations license
facts.value: keycloak-orgs: Elastic License 2.0; source available, royalty-free within its restrictions, including a restriction on offering substantial functionality as a hosted/managed service.

facts.label: Magic-link/container licenses
facts.value: keycloak-magic-link and phasetwo-containers each contain Elastic License 2.0 COPYING files.

facts.label: Commercial hosted and on-prem terms
facts.value: Paying hosted customers use the SaaS service agreement's license; on-prem/other commercial licensees use their negotiated agreement. Some vendor-specific code is not public.

facts.label: Public status evidence
facts.value: No public status/incident-history URL located in the bounded check.

facts.label: Uptime promises
facts.value: Starter targets 95% best effort with no SLA; Premium 99.5%; Enterprise 99.95%, optionally 99.99% for an additional written fee. Measurement is calendar-month authentication availability.

facts.label: SLA remedies
facts.value: Premium/Enterprise credit: 10% below plan commitment down to 99%; 25% below 99% down to 95%; 50% below 95%; maximum 50% of affected cluster's monthly fee.

facts.label: Hosted version maintenance
