apps.news: No qualifying sale, product shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signups, major paid feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found.

facts.label: Billing unit and definition
facts.value: No PocketBase-hosted subscription, MAU, stored-user, returning-user or request billing unit for the self-hosted core.

facts.label: Free production allowance
facts.value: MIT software has no license charge and no vendor-defined free-production user quota. Actual deployment is bounded by operator resources and the pre-v1 production warning.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: No paid PocketBase core tier, monthly minimum, annual commitment or enterprise quote applies to this self-hosted product.

facts.label: Usage prices
facts.value: No core per-user, organization, SSO connection, request or token usage tariff.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Both fixed SAML business baselines are unsupported by the unextended core: no native SAML connection or packaged customer-org/invitation system established.

facts.label: Customer organizations and fees
facts.value: Customer orgs, memberships, invitations and per-org roles require app collections, relations, rules and code. No core org/member subscription fee or native member allowance applies.

facts.label: SSO and account-sync fees
facts.value: No PocketBase core per-connection license charge. Generic upstream OIDC is built in; native SAML and SCIM connection products are not documented in the core APIs/options checked.

facts.label: Developer team and project caps
facts.value: No vendor dashboard-seat or project plan. Each deployment has its own superusers, collections and data directory; auth collections may be created as needed.

facts.label: Email delivery and price
facts.value: Default delivery uses Unix sendmail; production guide strongly recommends a local SMTP server or external mail service. Operator supplies the sender and pays its delivery bill.

facts.label: Login alerts and email demand
facts.value: AuthAlert is enabled by default for new-device login; OTP, reset, verification and address-change flows also send emails when used.

facts.label: SMS and other channels
facts.value: No native phone/SMS delivery provider, included SMS allowance or destination tariff found in current auth docs, route registry, auth options or OTP request handler.

facts.label: Over-limit behavior
facts.value: No vendor billing upgrade, hosted grace period or spend cap applies. Operator-set throttles can reject requests with HTTP 429; resource exhaustion is an infrastructure concern.

facts.label: Other charges and limits
facts.value: No core premium charge for auth methods, custom domains, logs or token issuance; external server, domain, storage, mail and federation bills remain separate.

facts.label: Vendor account eligibility
facts.value: No PocketBase vendor production account, seller-country enrollment or company-domain requirement applies to using the self-hosted core.

facts.label: Self-service and trial
facts.value: Download and run the executable or build the Go framework without a vendor signup, card or sales call; local superuser setup is required. No hosted trial is offered.

facts.label: Product type and auth scope
facts.value: Self-hosted backend and Go framework with embedded SQLite, auth collections, login/token APIs, user administration and access rules.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Self-hosted only; developer or chosen hosting operator runs servers, stores users, configures email/TLS, applies updates and handles backup/restore.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built-in password auth; email identity by default, or another field with a unique index such as username. New auth collection password field minimum 8 characters; bcrypt hashing.

facts.label: Email OTP login
facts.value: Built-in email OTP, disabled by default; new collection defaults 8 decimal digits and 180 seconds. Requests for unknown emails return a dummy otpId without creating a user or sending email.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: OTP can be presented as an email link by changing the template to include {OTP} and {OTP_ID} and building a client page that exchanges them.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No dedicated anonymous-account or wallet/SIWE auth method found in current authentication guide, auth route registry or collection auth options.

facts.label: Named OAuth providers
facts.value: Provider source directory includes Apple, Bitbucket, Box, Discord, Facebook, Gitea, Gitee, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Instagram, Kakao, Lark, Linear, LiveChat, Mailcow, Microsoft, Monday, Notion, Patreon, Planning Center, Spotify, Strava, Trakt, Twitch, Twitter, VK, WakaTime and Yandex.

facts.label: Generic OIDC and OAuth limitations
facts.value: Built-in generic OIDC registrations oidc, oidc2 and oidc3; custom providers can be registered in the Go provider map. _superusers do not support OAuth2 login.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: No built-in WebAuthn/passkey registration, assertion API or credential settings found in the v0.41.1 core inspected.

facts.label: MFA methods and enforcement
facts.value: Built-in MFA requires two different method categories among password, OAuth2 and email OTP, in either order. Disabled by default; optional rule targets users, empty rule applies to everyone when enabled.

facts.label: MFA challenge and recovery
facts.value: MFA challenge default duration 600 seconds. Production guide documents superuser email-OTP MFA and a server CLI command to generate a superuser OTP if email delivery fails.

facts.label: Other factors and end-user recovery
facts.value: TOTP enrollment, native SMS/passkey second factors, downloadable recovery codes and a packaged lost-factor end-user flow were not found in docs or current auth options/routes.

facts.label: Email verification
facts.value: Built-in request/confirm verification API and default confirmation page. Default verification token lasts 86,400 seconds; requiring verified login must be configured through authRule, e.g. verified = true.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Built-in emailed reset token, default 1,800 seconds; confirm requires password and passwordConfirm. Successful reset invalidates the user's previously issued auth tokens.

facts.label: Email change and account deletion
facts.value: Email-change confirmation requires emailed token plus account password; default token duration 1,800 seconds. Success marks verified and invalidates old tokens. Self-delete uses record DELETE with a suitable deleteRule.

facts.label: Auth token model
facts.value: Stateless HS256 JWTs, no traditional stored server sessions. Default auth token duration 432,000 seconds (5 days), configurable per collection.

facts.label: Refresh and logout
facts.value: authRefresh returns a new token and latest record data without invalidating older tokens. Logout clears the local SDK auth store; there is no logout endpoint.

facts.label: Revoke access and devices
facts.value: Changing an auth record's tokenKey or password invalidates its prior tokens; changing collection auth-token secret invalidates that collection's tokens. No built-in list/revoke-one-device session API is documented.

facts.label: Business login — OIDC relying party
facts.value: Generic OIDC provider is an upstream OAuth2/OIDC client, with openid/email/profile scopes, PKCE and configurable provider endpoints; user data comes from UserInfo or the exchanged ID token.

facts.label: Business login — native SAML and identity-provider roles
facts.value: No native SAML service-provider endpoint or SAML/OIDC identity-provider server was found in the documented API, registered auth routes, options or provider implementation tree.

facts.label: Organizations, roles and tenant isolation
facts.value: Custom collection fields and relations support app-owned roles/ownership and customer-workspace models; API rules filter records using @request.auth and related collection values.

facts.label: Authorization defaults and privileged access
facts.value: List/view/create/update/delete API rules default to locked/null for superusers only. Empty rule means public; auth collections additionally have a manageRule for admin-like account changes.

facts.label: SCIM account sync
facts.value: No native SCIM v2 routes, user/group mapping, directory lifecycle or deactivation implementation documented or found in the API source tree and auth configuration inspected.

facts.label: Login, registration and profile screens
facts.value: No ready-made frontend login/register/profile UI; official SDKs provide client integration. Builder creates those screens.

facts.label: Default email-action screens
facts.value: Default user-facing confirmation pages exist for password reset, verification and related email links; their URLs can be replaced in collection templates.

facts.label: Branding and domains
facts.value: Operator controls own frontend/domain and server URL; production executable can issue Let's Encrypt TLS for the supplied domain. Email templates and app/sender settings are configurable.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: Builder owns end-user UI localization and accessibility. Email templates are customizable, but a supported UI locale matrix or public accessibility conformance report was not located.

facts.label: Web client and framework integration
facts.value: Official JavaScript SDK supports browser and Node.js use; frontend framework is developer's choice. Docs discuss SvelteKit, Nuxt and Next.js server rendering, with integration cautions.

facts.label: Server extension runtime
facts.value: Native Go framework; v0.41.1 module declares Go 1.27. Prebuilt executable also embeds goja for custom JavaScript hooks/routes.

facts.label: Mobile and desktop SDKs
facts.value: Official JS SDK covers React Native, including AsyncAuthStore for custom persistent storage. Official Dart SDK targets web/mobile/desktop/CLI; its default AuthStore is not persistent.

facts.label: Mobile OAuth limitations
facts.value: All-in-one OAuth relies on a realtime connection staying active. Dart docs flag Android 15 background networking and dual-stack IP mismatches; manual code exchange plus deep link is an alternative.

facts.label: Database and services required
facts.value: Embedded SQLite in WAL mode; no external database/cache needed for the prebuilt executable. Operator needs persistent pb_data and frontend; production mail requires sendmail or preferably SMTP.

facts.label: Optional external dependencies
facts.value: OAuth needs configured provider credentials; optional S3-compatible storage/backups, reverse proxy and external mail provider are operator supplied.

facts.label: Deployment and scaling model
facts.value: Single server, vertical scaling; portable executable or custom Go build. Production guide gives reverse-proxy/systemd examples and a sample Dockerfile, but no official Docker image.

facts.label: Backup and restore
facts.value: Copy/replace pb_data while stopped, or use built-in snapshot ZIP backup/restore APIs/dashboard. Local or S3-compatible backup destination; files already in S3 are excluded from the snapshot.

facts.label: Backup retention and scheduling
facts.value: Auto-backup cron starts empty/disabled; default CronMaxKeep is 3 and only applies when a valid cron schedule is configured.

facts.label: Updates and migrations
facts.value: Prebuilt binary update command is available; read changelog and apply any manual migration steps. Go/JS migrations version collection changes and custom data logic.

facts.label: Custom fields, hooks and routes
facts.value: Auth collections accept custom fields/relations; Go/JS request hooks can validate or change auth, OAuth linking, OTP and reset behavior. Developers can add HTTP routes and server-side account logic.

facts.label: Hook delivery and external webhooks
facts.value: Hooks execute in the application process; after-success record hooks distinguish committed writes. No managed durable outbound webhook queue, retry tariff or exactly-once delivery contract is documented.

facts.label: User administration and account APIs
facts.value: Superuser dashboard and record CRUD APIs create/search/update/delete auth records. Server Go/JS methods can manage records; manageRule can delegate selected account administration.

facts.label: Banning and revoking a user
facts.value: Implement a custom disabled/status field and authRule for login/refresh; rotate that user's tokenKey and apply appropriate record-access rules when ending existing access.

facts.label: Support impersonation
facts.value: Built-in superuser-only impersonate endpoint creates nonrefreshable user tokens with optional custom duration; SDK returns a standalone client with in-memory auth state.

facts.label: OAuth account linking
facts.value: Core first finds an existing provider-ID link, then a signed-in same-collection user, then an account matching the provider's verified email; otherwise it creates an auth record subject to access rules.

facts.label: Unverified-account safety and unlinking
facts.value: OAuth flow resets an unverified existing user's password where needed and clears earlier links on verified upgrade; provider links are stored in _externalAuths and can be managed by privileged server code.

facts.label: Guest-to-account upgrade
facts.value: No dedicated guest-user conversion API found; build guest state or temporary records and an explicit custom upgrade flow if needed.

facts.label: Abuse controls — limiter and privileged access
facts.value: Built-in configurable IP rate limiter is disabled by default; production guide recommends enabling it. Superuser IP/subnet whitelist and optional superuser MFA are documented.

facts.label: Abuse controls — OTP
facts.value: Built-in OTP validation adds 5 attempts/180 seconds per auth record and client IP; used OTP is deleted. Unknown-email OTP requests return a dummy ID; more than 9 unexpired OTPs causes reuse of the latest code in production.

facts.label: Bot and breached-password checks
facts.value: No built-in CAPTCHA/Turnstile setting, breached-password lookup or SMS-fraud/spending service found in current auth options, password validator, request hooks and production recommendations.

facts.label: Rate limits — configured defaults
facts.value: If enabled: default rules *:auth 2 requests/3 seconds; *:create 20/5 seconds; /api/batch 3/second; /api/ 300/10 seconds. Rules support guest/auth audiences, path/action matching and excluded IPs.

facts.label: Rate limits — response and recovery
facts.value: Exceeded limiter returns HTTP 429. Implementation uses fixed windows and restores allowance at the next window; superusers and configured excluded IPs bypass the general limiter.

facts.label: Request/security logs and retention
facts.value: Dashboard and superuser Logs APIs list/filter/read/statistically query/truncate logs; source default MaxDays 5 and LogIP true. LogAuthId is separately configurable.

facts.label: Export and external log handling
facts.value: Operator can page through Logs API or use server logQuery; log-write hooks can forward data externally. Retention, level and IP logging are operator settings, with no PocketBase log fee.

facts.label: Export — full account data
facts.value: Operator can back up/copy the SQLite data directory, preserving auth records, identifiers, bcrypt hashes and _externalAuths provider-ID links in the database.

facts.label: Export — REST versus password hashes

facts.label: Migration in — hashes and records

facts.label: Migration in — unsupported assumptions
facts.value: No ready-made bulk/lazy migration pipeline, foreign-hash compatibility matrix or documented non-bcrypt verifier was found in FAQ, record docs and auth/password source.

facts.label: Live deletion and data relationships
facts.value: Record DELETE respects deleteRule; server code can delete users. Relation settings determine cascading/dependent-data handling, and required references can block deletion.

facts.label: Retention and closing the deployment

facts.label: Type and delivered scope
facts.value: Library / framework generator: writes User, Session and Current models, authentication concern, login/logout and password-reset controllers, migrations, mailer and browser views into the app.

facts.label: Registration boundary
facts.value: Signup is custom_code, outside the generator; Rails supplies a separate tutorial for adding it.

facts.label: Who operates accounts and infrastructure
facts.value: The developer operates the Rails app and its database, session storage, secrets, email setup, backups and updates; deployment may be on chosen infrastructure.

facts.label: Email and password login
facts.value: built_in; generated SessionsController authenticates email_address and password through User.authenticate_by and starts a database session.

facts.label: Email link/code and phone/SMS code
facts.value: custom_code / external_service; no passwordless sign-in or phone credential flow in the released generator.

facts.label: Guest and wallet authentication
facts.value: custom_code; no anonymous authenticated user record, wallet signature verification or wallet identity model is generated.

facts.label: Social provider support
facts.value: No generated Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft or other social-provider integration; provider OAuth clients, callback routes and account links require separate code/libraries.

facts.label: Passkeys and WebAuthn
facts.value: custom_code / separate library; no generated passkey registration, authentication, credential storage, conditional UI or recovery flow.

facts.label: MFA factors
facts.value: custom_code / external_service; no generated TOTP, SMS/email second factor or WebAuthn second-factor challenge/enrollment.

facts.label: Recovery codes and MFA enforcement
facts.value: custom_code; no generated recovery-code inventory, second-factor enforcement policy or lost-factor management screens.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: built_in when Action Mailer is available: request email, open signed token link, submit matching new password and confirmation; successful reset destroys all user sessions.

facts.label: Reset expiry and invalidation
facts.value: 15 minutes by default; configurable through has_secure_password reset_token: { expires_in: ... }. Reset tokens are bound to the password salt.

facts.label: Email verification and change
facts.value: custom_code in the follow-on tutorial: add unconfirmed_email, validate the current password, send confirmation, then update the stored email; example token lasts 7 days.

facts.label: Logged-in password/profile changes and self-deletion
facts.value: custom_code; official follow-on tutorial adds Settings controllers, views and routes for these account tasks.

facts.label: Session storage and current identity
facts.value: Database Session belongs_to User; Current.session exposes Current.user. Browser holds a signed session_id referring to the database row.

facts.label: Cookie lifetime and attributes
facts.value: Generated session_id uses cookies.signed.permanent, httponly:true and same_site:lax. Rails defines permanent as expiry 20 years from creation.

facts.label: Logout and revocation
facts.value: terminate_session destroys the current database Session and deletes the session_id cookie. Password reset destroys every session for that user.

facts.label: Multiple devices and expiry policy
facts.value: Multiple Session rows per user are supported by the association; device listing, selective remote revocation and idle expiry require custom code.

facts.label: WebSocket authentication
facts.value: When Action Cable is present, generated connection reads the signed session cookie, finds Session and identifies current_user; unauthorized connection is rejected.

facts.label: SAML and OIDC roles
facts.value: No generated SAML service provider/identity provider, OIDC relying party/provider or identity broker; separate libraries/services and integration code are needed.

facts.label: Organizations and invitations
facts.value: custom_code; no generated organizations, memberships, tenant isolation, invitation lifecycle or customer admin model.

facts.label: Authorization and roles
facts.value: custom_code; generator enforces authentication. Follow-on tutorial adds an admin boolean and an Authorization concern to restrict routes.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No generated SCIM 2.0 endpoint, User/Group resource contract or directory deactivation mapping; requires separate implementation.

facts.label: Browser screens
facts.value: built_in generated ERB screens: sign in, request password reset and submit new password. Generated files live in the app.

facts.label: Account and signup screens
facts.value: custom_code: signup, profile, password/email change, self-deletion and app admin screens are supplied as a follow-on tutorial.

facts.label: API option
facts.value: The released generator exposes --api to skip view generation; the same controller/model templates still use cookies, redirects and flash-style notices.

facts.label: Branding and layout
facts.value: App-owned ERB/HTML and mail templates can be edited; no generated vendor logo or plan-based white-label restriction in the checked login/reset templates.

facts.label: Login domain and domain count
facts.value: Uses the Rails application's own routes/domain; no vendor custom-domain subscription, domain verification screen or licensed domain count.

facts.label: Languages and translation work
facts.value: Generated login/reset UI and controller notices are English literals. Rails I18n supports app-defined translations; default locale is en.

facts.label: Accessibility assessment
facts.value: No generator-specific public WCAG conformance statement, VPAT or independent accessibility report located.

facts.label: Framework and minimum runtime
facts.value: Official Rails/Railties feature, introduced in Rails 8.0. Checked release: 8.1.4.1; Railties requires Ruby >=3.2.0.

facts.label: Execution environment
facts.value: Backend Ruby/Rails app with Active Record and Action Controller; browser ERB views for normal web mode. Framework can render JSON after app integration work.

facts.label: Generated tests
facts.value: Default test-unit generator supplies User fixtures/model test, session/password controller tests, session helpers and conditional mailer preview.

facts.label: Native iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop
facts.value: No native auth SDK or token protocol is generated; native/SPA integration requires application API and client work.

facts.label: Database prerequisite
facts.value: Application relational database with users and sessions migrations; Rails defaults to SQLite. PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB are documented framework database choices.

facts.label: Password dependency and data schema
facts.value: bcrypt required for has_secure_password; generated users have non-null email_address with unique index and non-null password_digest. Sessions reference user and store IP and user-agent strings.

facts.label: Mail, queue and cache prerequisites
facts.value: Password-reset email requires Action Mailer plus working delivery and job backend. Rate limiting requires an ActiveSupport cache store that supports increment.

facts.label: Secrets and transport
facts.value: App secret_key_base is used for signed cookies; deploy the app with appropriate HTTPS and real mailer host configuration.

facts.label: Deployment and upgrades
facts.value: Operate a Rails application; official tutorial documents container deployment with Kamal. Upgrade Rails/Ruby with tests, incremental version changes and configuration review.

facts.label: Backup and restore ownership
facts.value: Operator must protect the application database, deployment secrets and dependent storage. Rails schema dumps describe table structure and are not a user-data backup.

facts.label: Auth-specific backup runbook
facts.value: No generator-specific automated backup schedule, tested restore procedure, recovery-point target or recovery-time promise located.

facts.label: Published auth sizing
facts.value: No generator-specific minimum RAM/CPU, maximum MAU or measured requests-per-second capacity published in the checked installation/auth/deployment sources.

facts.label: Custom fields and flows
facts.value: custom_code: edit generated Ruby models/controllers and add migrations/validations. Official tutorial adds names, email confirmation, account settings and authorization.

facts.label: Hooks and event delivery
facts.value: Rails model lifecycle callbacks and ActiveSupport::Notifications support app-defined hooks/events. Durable outbound auth webhooks require application implementation.

facts.label: Create, read and update users
facts.value: Application model/console API: User.create!, lookups and normal Active Record CRUD. Follow-on tutorial shows an admin-only user list and editing controllers.

facts.label: Ban, impersonate and support devices
facts.value: custom_code; no generated ban/suspension column, admin impersonation flow, support-session grant or device administration screen.

facts.value: custom_code; generator has only a local email/password User credential and no social identity/provider-link model.

facts.value: custom_code; public unauthenticated access is supported, but no persistent guest-account conversion or merge workflow is generated.

facts.label: Generated brute-force controls
facts.value: Login create and, when mail is present, reset-request create each get rate_limit to:10, within:3.minutes, with a redirect and retry-later alert.

facts.label: Enumeration defenses
facts.value: Local password lookup uses authenticate_by, which hashes even when the account does not exist; login uses a generic error and reset request uses a generic sent-if-present notice.

facts.label: Password policy and bots
facts.value: Presence and maximum 72-byte password validation are built into has_secure_password, with confirmation when supplied. Minimum length, complexity, breached-password lookup and CAPTCHA enforcement are app work.

facts.label: SMS fraud and paid security
facts.value: No SMS flow or SMS-abuse module is generated. Bot/risk services or extra factors would be separate app integrations.

facts.label: Login and reset request rate limits
facts.value: Each generated create endpoint permits 10 requests per 3-minute cache-counter window per source IP/controller scope; excess requests invoke the generated redirect callback.

facts.label: Configuration and scope of limits
facts.value: Change to:, within:, by:, store:, name: or scope: in application code. Cache store defaults to the controller/global configured cache store.

facts.label: Session and request evidence
facts.value: Session rows record user reference, IP and user agent; framework logging/instrumentation can expose controller processing and rate-limit events.

facts.label: Audit retention and export guarantee
facts.value: No generator-provided security audit dashboard, immutable event store, standard audit-export format or retention-days promise located.

facts.label: Sensitive log parameters
facts.value: Fresh Rails app initializer filters partial matches including passw, email, secret, token, _key, crypt, salt, certificate and otp.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and password digest export
facts.value: Developer-controlled SQL/Active Record data can be read and exported using app code or database tools. Schema includes email_address/password_digest and Session associations.

facts.label: Credential portability limits
facts.value: Password hashes use bcrypt; plaintext passwords cannot be recovered from those hashes. A destination must accept the existing bcrypt format and mapped identities to preserve password login.

facts.label: Provider links and passkey export
facts.value: Core has no social identity links or passkey credential records to export. Any such records come from the app's added integrations.

facts.label: Import of existing users
facts.value: custom_code: map existing records into the app schema; compatible bcrypt digests can be assigned to password_digest without passing through the plaintext-password setter.

facts.label: Other hash types and bulk/lazy migration
facts.value: No generated importer, Argon2/PBKDF2/scrypt verifier, bulk CSV contract or lazy credential-migration handler. Build conversion/verification or require password reset.

facts.label: User deletion and dependent sessions
facts.value: Application code can destroy a User; generated has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy removes associated sessions through Active Record callbacks.

facts.label: Logs, backups and retention periods
facts.value: No generator-wide retention/deletion deadline for server logs, deleted-user backups, email-provider data or restored databases is published.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: Builder chooses app/database, backup, log and mail-provider locations. There is no Rails-generator vendor region selector or fixed account-data hosting region.

facts.label: Hosted processing agreement and subprocessors
facts.value: Not applicable for the embedded generator: no Rails-operated auth tenant or end-user processing service contract.

facts.label: Independent assurance evidence
facts.value: No generator-specific SOC 2 report, ISO certificate, penetration-test report or certified compliance scope located in the checked public material.

facts.label: Project stewardship
facts.value: Ruby on Rails project; Rails Core stewards framework releases and policy. The Rails Foundation supports documentation, education, marketing and events.

facts.value: Active project; repository archived=false. Rails/Railties 8.1.4.1 is published, not yanked; release dated 2026-11-04. No whole-product shutdown, acquisition or replacement notice found in the bounded lifecycle check.

facts.label: Old series sunset
facts.value: Rails 8.0 security support ends 2026-11-07; latest checked 8.0 security release is 8.0.5.2. This is a framework-series end date, not retirement of the authentication generator.

facts.label: Framework and generator licence
facts.value: MIT; free commercial use, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale, subject to preserving the copyright and permission notice in copies or substantial portions.

facts.label: Password-hashing dependency licence
facts.value: bcrypt-ruby: MIT wrapper licence; its licence separately identifies underlying C bcrypt as public domain and includes jBCrypt attribution.

facts.label: Password login

facts.value: Microsoft, Apple and other named social-provider recipes/guarantees not established in the reviewed guide and released provider type list; generic OIDC/Custom configuration is the documented route.

facts.label: Passkey primary login and account conversion
facts.value: Native WebAuthn/FIDO2 security keys and passkey-only accounts. Passkey-only accounts require user verification; a password account can convert after registering a UV-capable key.

facts.label: Resident keys and stale guide
facts.value: v0.37.2 supports default nonresident keys and resident/discoverable keys. Only resident keys work with the direct Passkey button without entering email. Older live passkey prose says resident keys cannot be used.

facts.label: Passkey domains and clients
facts.value: RP ID is the effective domain; configured RP origin includes scheme and explicit port. Changing RP ID breaks existing credentials. No complete native-mobile or conditional-autofill support matrix found.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Built-in passkey/security-key MFA; configurable per-client force_mfa and admin_force_mfa. Compiled default admin_force_mfa=true. Optional email OTP is globally disabled by default, then uses six digits and five-minute expiry when enabled.

facts.label: TOTP and SMS status
facts.value: TOTP and phone/SMS OTP are not implemented in released validation: both Time and Phone variants return the unimplemented error.

facts.label: Recovery and backup codes
facts.value: Register backup passkeys or rely on administrator reset if passkey-only credentials are all lost; passkey-only users cannot use normal password-reset emails. No printable one-use recovery-code facility found.

facts.label: Email verification and password reset
facts.value: Native activation validates email and initializes password/passkey. Reset magic link defaults to 30m; initial setup link defaults to 3d. Existing WebAuthn accounts must satisfy a key check during password reset.

facts.label: Email change, phone verification and self-deletion
facts.value: Self email change sends a confirmation to the new address, uses a one-hour link, then marks email verified, invalidates Rauthy sessions and notifies old/new addresses. Native self-deletion is optional and disabled by default; rauthy_admin cannot self-delete.

facts.label: Rauthy browser sessions
facts.value: Encrypted browser cookies; default session maximum 10h and renewable idle timeout 90m; these authorize Rauthy itself and are distinct from app sessions/tokens. Per-client MFA can be required.

facts.label: Access/refresh token lifetimes and rotation
facts.value: New static Client default access-token lifetime 1800 seconds; global refresh-token default 2d, refresh-use grace 5s. Device-flow refresh default 3d. Refresh tokens rotate; values are configurable.

facts.label: Logout, forced logout and revocation limits
facts.value: Session logout targets that session. Admin global user logout deletes sessions and refresh tokens and triggers configured backchannel logout; device-flow credentials require separate handling. Existing JWTs need online checks/blacklisting to reflect revocation immediately.

facts.label: Session peer-IP binding default
facts.value: Compiled session_validate_ip=true and reference example true; sessions prose also says the feature is disabled by default.

facts.label: OIDC/OAuth business login roles
facts.value: Native downstream OIDC provider/OAuth authorization server; upstream generic OIDC client/broker with provider settings. Supports RP-initiated and backchannel logout, device authorization, client credentials and configured token exchange.

facts.label: SAML roles
facts.value: No published SAML identity-provider, service-provider or broker implementation established in the official book, provider models or released API registry.

facts.label: Groups, roles and delegated administration
facts.value: Native custom groups/roles; rauthy_admin:<group> delegates user administration for matching groups, with exact names, prefix * and global * patterns. Full rauthy_admin controls the whole instance.

facts.label: Customer isolation and invitations
facts.value: Delegated admins see the same minified full user list as full admins. Native strict tenant isolation and customer-org invitation acceptance are not established; group-admin guide says stricter isolation could be a future opt-in.

facts.label: SCIM direction and resource coverage
facts.value: Native SCIM v2 provisioning client pushes Rauthy users/groups to downstream apps. Requires those apps' /Users and /Groups endpoints, externalId support and documented filters/group PatchOp behavior.

facts.label: SCIM deletion, scope and retries
facts.value: Default sync_delete_users=false and sync_delete_groups=false: detach externalId rather than delete remote records. Opt-in deletion uses DELETE; per-client group-prefix filtering scopes sync. Failed tasks default to 100 retries, every 60 to 90 seconds.

facts.label: Ready-made UI
facts.value: Server-hosted login, registration, initial setup/reset, Admin UI and user Account Dashboard. Account self-service covers profile, credentials/passkeys and optional self-deletion.

facts.label: Branding and domain control
facts.value: Per-client login color theme, logo and favicon; the default rauthy client's theme also styles account/admin pages. Use your own configured public URL and TLS/domain.

facts.label: UI and email languages
facts.value: English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian Bokmål, Dutch, Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian and Simplified Chinese are documented, including in the v0.37.2 source guide/type enum.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independently assessed accessibility statement found.

facts.label: Official web/runtime integration
facts.value: Official Rust rauthy-client has Actix Web, Axum and generic examples, plus optional backchannel-logout, device-code, scim, userinfo and RSA support. Generic OIDC clients may also integrate.

facts.label: Mobile, CLI and other clients
facts.value: OAuth device-code flow supports headless/IoT/CLI clients; official Rust client includes device-code/qrcode features. Separate PAM/NSS modules cover Linux logins.

facts.label: Native mobile SDKs
facts.value: No official iOS, Android, React Native or Flutter SDK/quickstart found in the book index, official Rust client or released provider/API overview.

facts.label: Database, cache and service prerequisites
facts.value: Embedded Hiqlite/SQLite primary storage by default; optional PostgreSQL. Hiqlite also provides cache/Raft state, including with PostgreSQL. Persistent volumes, stable encryption keys and cluster authentication secrets are required for a normal durable deployment.

facts.label: Deployment and high availability
facts.value: Official Docker/container and Kubernetes guides; published images for x86_64 and arm64. Native source build or extracting the binary is described. HA recommends 3 replicas, or 5 for additional resilience.

facts.label: Backup and restore
facts.value: Hiqlite scheduled backups, optional encrypted S3 upload and documented restore from file/S3. Defaults: 02:30 backup cron, 3d local retention and 30d S3 retention. PostgreSQL backups/restores use outside native tooling.

facts.label: Upgrade and sizing guidance
facts.value: Operator must follow release-specific changes/security fixes; no LTS or security backports. Published tuning ties concurrency and memory to Argon2 and worker/cache settings, rather than a fixed per-MAU hardware minimum.

facts.label: Custom attributes and token claims
facts.value: Native named attributes mapped through custom scopes and client permissions. Released schema supports JSON values and optional user_editable; type field is currently marked ignored/future.

facts.label: Events and custom logic
facts.value: Native event API/SSE, built-in email/Matrix/Slack notification targets and custom-scoped claims. Custom external event handling requires your own subscriber application; no general hosted function/hook runtime established.

facts.label: Terms acceptance and messaging customization
facts.value: Operator-managed terms-of-service records/acceptance are implemented; config defaults to a 15m acceptance extension. Email templates support configured per-language/type content; deeper template changes require rebuilding.

facts.label: User administration and API
facts.value: Admin dashboard/REST API create, list/search, read, update/disable/delete users, reset factors/passwords and invalidate sessions; fine-grained API keys supply selected create/read/update/delete permissions.

facts.label: Delegated administration and impersonation
facts.value: Group-delegated writes are bounded; no ordinary support-agent 'sign in as this user' UI/workflow established. Configured RFC 8693 token exchange includes impersonation/delegation semantics and is a separate protocol capability.

facts.label: Linking and unlinking
facts.value: One upstream provider link per user is represented by auth_provider_id/federation_uid. Authenticated linking verifies matching provider/user/email cookie; optional provider.auto_link can attach an otherwise unlinked matching-email account.

facts.label: Federated credential upgrade and guest accounts
facts.value: Federated-only accounts can initialize local password/passkey using the reset flow; v0.37.2 improves enrolling their first MFA key. No anonymous-to-registered upgrade path established.

facts.label: Password security and account-abuse controls
facts.value: Native Argon2id hashing, configurable password length/character/expiry/history policy, enumeration-resistant registration response, proof-of-work registration and domain allow/deny restrictions.

facts.label: IP blacklisting and stuffing protection
facts.value: Failed-login thresholds: 7 -> 1m, 10 -> 10m, 15 -> 15m, 20 -> 1h, 25+ -> 1d; increasing response delays between thresholds. Credential-stuffing defaults: threshold 15 combinations, 3h window, 24h IP blacklist.

facts.label: Endpoint and concurrency limits
facts.value: Default maximum simultaneous password-hash workers=2. Dynamic client registration without a registration token defaults to one per-IP timeout of 1h; token-authenticated registration bypasses that limiter. Device-flow poll interval defaults 5s; start limiter is separately configurable.

facts.label: Universal API capacity and managed quotas
facts.value: No published single login/management requests-per-second allowance, per-MAU throughput guarantee or hosted quota escalation policy found.

facts.label: Audit and security events
facts.value: Native events include invalid logins, new users/admins, email/password changes, token issuance, forced logout, suspicious scans, stuffing, blacklist, SCIM/backchannel failures and system/key events. Admin UI, JSON fetch and SSE stream are available.

facts.label: Audit persistence default conflict
facts.value: Logging prose says info+ events persist 31 days, while that same page's config says 60d and released default is 60 × 24 × 3600 seconds.

facts.label: Profile, identifier and federation export
facts.value: Management API returns profiles, IDs, roles/groups, user values and provider/federation identifiers; ordinary UserResponse excludes password hashes and complete passkey credential material.

facts.label: Credentials, native backups and exit limits
facts.value: Operator controls the database containing Argon2 password hashes, IDs, group/role data, provider links and WebAuthn credential records. Native backups and Rauthy-to-Rauthy database migration preserve the native data; destination compatibility needs custom work.

facts.label: Packaged portable credential export
facts.value: No documented one-click/bulk vendor-neutral export containing password hashes, all passkey records, linked identities and required keys found.

facts.label: Bootstrap user/profile/hash import
facts.value: Advanced JSON bootstrap can load users, roles/groups, attributes and chosen user IDs into an empty deployment. Password input accepts Plain, Argon2ID or generate; supplied Argon2ID value is stored directly.

facts.label: Migration scope and unsupported guarantees
facts.value: MIGRATE_DB_FROM copies native Rauthy data between Hiqlite/PostgreSQL or instances and overwrites target data. No released bulk bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2 import, lazy foreign-password verification or passkey/federation import recipe established.

facts.label: User deletion and retained copies
facts.value: Admin deletion and optional self-delete remove the native user; delete path handles sessions/PAM/picture data and database relations, and schedules downstream SCIM cleanup. External backups, logs and mail copies have their own retention.

facts.label: Event, backup and other retention
facts.value: Source defaults persist info+ events for 60d; Hiqlite backups default 3d local/30d S3. Operator can configure them. No universal lifetime for external logs/email or post-deletion copies found.

facts.label: Data location and residency
facts.value: Self-hosted operator chooses compute/database/backup regions and external email/alert services; no project-hosted selectable-region plan applies.

facts.label: Independent security assessment
facts.value: Public Radically Open Security penetration/code-audit report v1.0 dated 2025-09-15; work ran 2025-07-14 to 2025-08-22 against the Rauthy identity provider/0.32-era code. Seven findings: 1 elevated, 3 low, 3 not-applicable severity.

facts.label: Privacy, processing and certification policies
facts.value: No project-operated hosted DPA, subprocessor list, SOC 2 report, ISO certificate or universal production privacy/retention contract found.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Rauthy; maintained by the individual maintainer (GitHub sebadob). Official repository github.com/sebadob/rauthy; documentation sebadob.github.io/rauthy. Maintainer says no separate official legal entity stands behind the project.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active; latest stable server v0.37.2, published 2026-10-19T12:43:46Z; prerelease=false, draft=false. Repository archived=false and disabled=false; pushed_at 2026-11-04T18:50:47Z.

facts.label: Core and official Rust client license
facts.value: Server v0.37.2 and rauthy-client: Apache License 2.0. No-charge use, modification and redistribution, including commercial use, subject to the license's notice, change-marking and other conditions.

facts.label: PAM/NSS component license
facts.value: Separate rauthy-pam-nss project declares GPLv3; current main workspace version 0.3.1.

facts.label: Service status and uptime promise
facts.value: A vendor-hosted production status page/SLA percentage does not apply to the researched self-hosted release. Test Swagger instance is explicitly not always online and may run nightly code.

facts.label: Release and security maintenance
facts.value: v0.37.2 published 2026-10-19; fixes concurrent refresh/admin-logout session reinsertion and an unauthenticated denial-of-service possibility. Security policy: below v1, no LTS and no security backports; fix in the next patch regardless of major/minor.

facts.label: Community and paid support
facts.value: Free help through GitHub Discussions Q&A. Professional paid support by mail@sebadob.dev; no public rates, support hours or response-time commitment found.

apps.news: No qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signups, major paid feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: no core MAU, stored-user, login, request, token or developer-seat subscription meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: Rodauth core software licence fee = $0 for commercial/production use, without licence-imposed user/app count or time limit.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable; no paid core production edition or hosted plan with monthly/annual minimum.

facts.label: Usage tiers/overages
facts.value: Not applicable; no core vendor usage price tiers, volume brackets or bill rounding.

facts.label: Customer organization fees/limits
facts.value: Not applicable to a bundled organization product; no core organization membership/invitation/role quotas or per-organization charge.

facts.label: SSO/SCIM connection fees
facts.value: No Rodauth connection meter. Optional omniauth-saml 2.2.5 / omniauth_openid_connect 0.8.0 declare MIT; rodauth-oauth provider code is Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Builder seats/apps/environments/domains
facts.value: Not applicable to a vendor dashboard; MIT imposes no subscription cap on builders, apps, environments or domains.

facts.label: Email sending/dependency
facts.value: Email flows use email_base and the Mail gem by default; app configures delivery or overrides email creation/sending. Rails wrapper uses Action Mailer.

facts.label: SMS sending/dependency
facts.value: sms_codes provides enrollment, confirmation and challenge logic but deliberately does not send SMS. Builder must implement sms_send using a chosen service/library.

facts.label: Password baseline delivery
facts.value: Core password login has no compulsory email per returning login. Email-auth login sends links; optional verification/reset/notifications generate their own sends.

facts.label: Vendor over-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted Rodauth free-plan cutoff, auto-upgrade, spend cap or vendor billing grace period.

facts.label: Other core charges
facts.value: Not applicable: core MFA, passkeys, JWT refresh and audit code have no separate paid feature/transaction/request fee.

facts.label: Hosted account/market eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to a Rodauth-hosted production account; the MIT library runs in the builder's app without one.

facts.label: Self-service/trial/card rules
facts.value: Not applicable to a hosted trial. Obtain the gem and configure routes/features/database; no Rodauth card, sales call, business-domain account or vendor signup is needed for code use.

facts.label: Type and scope
facts.value: Embedded Ruby account/authentication framework built with Roda and Sequel; can serve Rack middleware, HTML forms, JSON API or internal library calls.

facts.label: Feature activation and editions
facts.value: Features must be explicitly enabled; shared base features autoload as dependencies. One MIT core package, without paid core feature tiers.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer/chosen host operates app, account/password/feature tables, database roles/functions, sessions, mail/SMS, keys, logs, updates and backup/restore.

facts.label: Password and HTTP Basic
facts.value: built_in opt-in login with database bcrypt by default; optional HTTP Basic feature also supported. Login uses configured account/login/password fields.

facts.label: Email magic links
facts.value: built_in email_auth: emailed passwordless login link, default deadline interval 1 day and resend spacing 300 seconds; successful use removes its key.

facts.label: Email codes/phone first factor/wallets
facts.value: custom_code/external_service needed for standalone email-code login, first-factor phone-code accounts or wallet-signature verification; these are not core registered login features.

facts.label: Anonymous/guest users
facts.value: plugin: rodauth-guest 0.0.1 (MIT; rodauth ~>2.0) creates/logs in anonymous database accounts on routes calling allow_guest.

facts.label: Social/provider integration
facts.value: plugin: rodauth-omniauth 0.6.2 (MIT; rodauth ~>2.36, OmniAuth ~>2.0); provider strategy gems separately installed/configured.

facts.label: Google
facts.value: plugin chain: rodauth-omniauth plus omniauth-google-oauth2 1.2.3 (MIT, OmniAuth 2.x). Rodauth extension explicitly demonstrates Google registration.

facts.label: GitHub
facts.value: plugin chain: rodauth-omniauth plus omniauth-github 2.0.1 (MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0 / omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8); GitHub is shown in extension configuration.

facts.label: Apple
facts.value: plugin chain: rodauth-omniauth shows Apple; omniauth-apple 1.4.0 declares MIT and depends on omniauth-oauth2/json-jwt.

facts.label: Microsoft
facts.value: generic/plugin path: OmniAuth-compatible omniauth-microsoft_graph 2.2.0, MIT; OmniAuth ~>2.0, omniauth-oauth2 ~>1.8.0 and JWT >=2.0,<4.

facts.label: Other external providers
facts.value: rodauth-omniauth explicitly shows Facebook/Twitter and can configure additional OmniAuth 2-compatible strategies; no fixed vendor provider count.

facts.label: Passkeys/security keys
facts.value: built_in opt-in webauthn for MFA, webauthn_login for passwordless first-factor login, webauthn_verify_account for passwordless setup during verification.

facts.label: Conditional autofill
facts.value: built_in webauthn_autofill enables conditional mediation and username-less credential lookup. Bundled JavaScript checks browser support before activating.

facts.label: Passkey policy, domain and recovery
facts.value: Core WebAuthn supports multiple authenticators/removal; origin defaults base_url and RP ID derives from origin. Generic WebAuthn defaults userVerification=discouraged; login counts authenticator verification as an extra factor only if configured.

facts.label: TOTP
facts.value: built_in opt-in otp using rotp/rqrcode; default drift 30 seconds and 5 failed attempts before OTP lockout. Enrollment/authentication/disable routes included.

facts.label: SMS MFA/phone confirmation
facts.value: built_in sms_codes: backup MFA by default when other primary factors exist; configurable as primary MFA. Defaults: 6-digit auth code valid 300 seconds, 5 failures; phone-confirm code length 12 valid 86,400 seconds.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: built_in recovery_codes: single-use codes; limit 16; view/add flows; auto-add/remove flags default false. Codes are stored in plain text so authenticated users can view them.

facts.label: MFA enforcement and fallback
facts.value: App must invoke require_authentication / require_two_factor_authenticated and optionally require_two_factor_setup on appropriate routes. Core supports WebAuthn and TOTP primary factors, SMS/recovery backup options.

facts.label: Account/email verification
facts.value: built_in verify_account blocks login until email link verification; defaults: set password during verification, autologin after verification true. Its verification keys do not expire by default.

facts.label: Email/login change verification
facts.value: change_login changes login; add verify_login_change to defer change until new address is verified, with default 1-day token interval and no verification autologin.

facts.label: Password reset/change
facts.value: built_in reset_password email flow: 1-day interval, 300-second resend spacing, autologin=false; change_password supports signed-in changes.

facts.label: User close-account and phone scope
facts.value: built_in close_account; normally requires an existing password for modification, otherwise no password check. SMS feature confirms its registered MFA phone number.

facts.label: Session model/status checks
facts.value: Core uses the chosen Rack session, caching authentication/account state to avoid a database query per request. Closing/changing an account elsewhere does not automatically invalidate every cached session.

facts.label: Session expiration feature
facts.value: Opt-in session_expiration: inactivity timeout 1,800 seconds, absolute maximum lifetime 86,400 seconds; app must call check_session_expiration.

facts.label: Active sessions and revocation
facts.value: Opt-in active_sessions stores an ID per login; app calls check_active_session to enforce revocation. Supports current/selected/all-session removal and global logout.

facts.label: Remember login
facts.value: Opt-in remember: 14-day deadline; deadline extension disabled by default; cookie defaults path /, httponly true, secure for HTTPS requests. App calls load_memory for autologin.

facts.label: JWT API session
facts.value: Opt-in jwt uses a configured jwt_secret, HS256 by default, to carry session state; clients must persist updated Authorization response headers.

facts.label: JWT access/refresh tokens
facts.value: Opt-in jwt_refresh: access token default 1,800 seconds; refresh token default 14 days; successful refresh replaces/removes the used refresh token.

facts.label: Logout, account changes and single session
facts.value: Logout can remove current session; refresh token revocation requires submitted token or all. active_sessions supports global logout; single_session enforces one stored session key if check_single_session is called.

facts.label: SAML browser-login client
facts.value: plugin/custom integration: rodauth-omniauth accepts OmniAuth 2 strategies; omniauth-saml 2.2.5 (MIT) supplies SAML service-provider login, metadata and configurable SLO.

facts.label: OIDC relying party/client
facts.value: plugin/custom integration: omniauth_openid_connect 0.8.0 (MIT; OmniAuth >=1.9,<3 and openid_connect ~>2.2) can be used through rodauth-omniauth's OmniAuth 2 integration.

facts.label: OAuth/OIDC authorization server
facts.value: plugin: rodauth-oauth 1.7.1 implements OAuth2 authorization server and OpenID Connect provider features, including token/revocation/introspection, PKCE and optional logout/registration features.

facts.label: SAML assertion grant boundary
facts.value: rodauth-oauth lists oauth_saml_bearer_grant for SAML assertion-to-OAuth exchange; this is distinct from browser SAML SP or IdP login.

facts.label: Organizations/memberships/roles
facts.value: custom_code/other libraries required for customer workspaces, tenant memberships, invitations, member roles and customer admin permissions.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No core SCIM Users/Groups/directory provisioning or documented SCIM deactivation behavior established.

facts.label: Ready account and factor UI
facts.value: built_in opt-in app-served HTML forms for login/create/change/reset/verify/close, remember/logout and MFA setup/authentication/manage/removal; JSON support also available.

facts.label: Headless/API support
facts.value: built_in json provides API responses with Rack session; jwt carries API session state in tokens. json: :only avoids normal HTML plugins; mail bodies may need custom rendering.

facts.label: Branding/domains/themes
facts.value: App owns templates/layout, messages, route prefix and domain. Core MIT code has no branding-removal fee or licence cap on domains.

facts.label: Translations/locales
facts.value: Core translates user-facing configuration through translate; plugin rodauth-i18n 0.11.1 (MIT; i18n ~>1.0, rodauth ~>2.19) loads configurable locale files.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Rodauth-specific public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or completed accessibility assessment found.

facts.label: Core runtimes/frameworks
facts.value: Rodauth 2.50.0 declares Ruby >=1.9.2, roda >=2.6.0, sequel >=4. Supports Roda/Rack middleware; non-web library mode still needs a Sequel database.

facts.label: Rails integration
facts.value: plugin rodauth-rails 2.2.3 (MIT): railties >=5.2, roda ~>3.76, rodauth ~>2.36 and rodauth-model ~>0.2.

facts.label: Other web clients/frameworks
facts.value: Can mount Roda middleware before another Rack framework; README gives Sinatra/Grape/Hanami integration examples. JSON/JWT APIs can be used by custom browser clients.

facts.label: Native/mobile/desktop clients
facts.value: No official core iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter/desktop SDK or maintained platform compatibility matrix found.

facts.label: Database and password storage
facts.value: Sequel-connected database required for normal account features. Recommended PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server setup separates password hashes and app/password-owner roles with authentication functions.

facts.label: Feature-dependent dependencies/secrets
facts.value: Feature gems such as bcrypt, Mail, tilt, rotp/rqrcode, jwt and webauthn must be supplied when used; gemspec places many in development dependencies because not all features require them.

facts.label: Deployment/upgrades/backups
facts.value: Runs inside app process. README documents schema, database functions/roles and PostgreSQL 15+ schema-grant setup; operator deploys/patches and backs up records, keys and permissions/functions.

facts.label: Capacity/restore guidance limits
facts.value: No universal core CPU/RAM sizing, guaranteed login requests per second, MAU capacity table or complete deployment-independent backup/restore procedure established.

facts.label: Custom fields, flows and hooks
facts.value: built_in configuration DSL overrides values/methods per request; before/after hooks, custom feature modules, account columns, template changes and route-level overrides supported.

facts.label: Events/webhooks
facts.value: Core hooks and audit_logging can record account/security actions. No operated webhook delivery service, managed retries, queue retention or webhook signing service.

facts.label: Administrative account API
facts.value: built_in internal_request can create/change/close/verify accounts and invoke enabled feature operations from Ruby methods without the user's normal login/password confirmation.

facts.label: Search/ban/impersonation boundary
facts.value: Account lookup/status changes use operator DB/custom code and configured status checks; no core admin dashboard or complete safe impersonation workflow.

facts.label: External identity linking/unlinking
facts.value: rodauth-omniauth stores provider/uid; new identities match an existing account by email by default and may automatically verify matching unverified accounts.

facts.label: Guest to registered account
facts.value: rodauth-guest can delete guest account when creating a new account; before_delete_guest lets app transfer owned data. Deletion is normally skipped if create-account autologin is false.

facts.label: Account lockout and token throttles
facts.value: Opt-in lockout default max_invalid_logins=100 and account-lockout deadline interval 1 day; unlock resend spacing 300 seconds. Email-auth/reset have their own 300-second resend controls.

facts.label: Password and bot protections
facts.value: Core password minimum 6 characters; max characters/bytes nil by default in 2.50.0. Optional disallow_common_passwords ships a 10,000-password list; other features add complexity/history checks.

facts.label: Breached-password lookup extension
facts.value: plugin: rodauth-pwned 0.2.1 (MIT; pwned ~>2.1, rodauth ~>2.0) checks new passwords through Pwned Passwords API.

facts.label: CSRF, domain and HMAC configuration
facts.value: Core uses Roda request-specific CSRF protection by default; trusted domain/base_url and HMAC secret strengthen email/remember/OTP/challenge/session tokens.

facts.label: Endpoint rates/throughput
facts.value: No Rodauth-operated requests-per-second quota or universal login/management burst contract. App/gateway supplies general throttling and provider budgets.

facts.label: Built-in audit events
facts.value: Opt-in audit_logging stores action messages/custom JSON metadata in an operator-owned table; hooks with an account ID are recorded. Logout uses before hook in 2.50.0 to avoid duplicates.

facts.label: Audit retention/export
facts.value: No fixed vendor retention days, export charge or event-streaming subscription; operator queries/exports/prunes own audit table and protects sensitive app logs.

facts.label: Profile/identifier/password export
facts.value: Operator-controlled database/schema makes profile, IDs and supported password-hash export possible with appropriate tooling and privileges; no core vendor CSV/export job or export fee.

facts.label: Other identity/factor records
facts.value: External identities live in extension tables; WebAuthn stores credential IDs/public keys/counters/user IDs; OTP/HMAC, recovery/session/token tables follow enabled schemas.

facts.label: Import/legacy schema

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Two TypeScript-first libraries: @simplewebauthn/server prepares/verifies WebAuthn ceremonies; @simplewebauthn/browser wraps browser credential APIs and serializes responses.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: Developer operates the relying-party backend, user/credential database, challenge storage and login sessions; browser/credential manager supplies authenticator interaction.

facts.label: Password/email/phone/wallet methods
facts.value: No password verifier, email/SMS OTP sender, OAuth login or wallet account implementation in the public server/browser API surface.

facts.label: Social provider support
facts.value: Apple, Google and Microsoft passkey platforms are authenticators/credential managers in this context, not built-in social OAuth/OIDC login providers.

facts.label: Passkey registration and login
facts.value: Built-in generateRegistrationOptions/verifyRegistrationResponse and generateAuthenticationOptions/verifyAuthenticationResponse server functions, paired with browser startRegistration/startAuthentication.

facts.label: Credential storage requirements
facts.value: App stores credential ID, public key bytes, counter, associated user and transports; must save updated counter after successful authentication.

facts.label: Discoverable/usernameless login
facts.value: allowCredentials can be empty/omitted so a user selects a discoverable credential; app locates the account by verified credential ID/userHandle and creates its own session.

facts.label: Registration defaults
facts.value: v14.0.3 registration generator defaults to residentKey preferred, userVerification preferred, attestation none and 60,000 ms ceremony timeout.

facts.label: Autofill/Conditional UI
facts.value: Browser startAuthentication supports useBrowserAutofill:true; input autocomplete must include webauthn, normally at the end.

facts.label: Automatic passkey enrollment
facts.value: Conditional Create via useAutoRegister:true can attempt silent enrollment after successful non-passkey authentication in supported browsers/password managers.

facts.label: Cross-device and hardware credentials
facts.value: Supports platform authenticators/security keys; transports and authenticator hints help browsers offer local, security-key or remote/hybrid experiences.

facts.label: Passkey feature detection
facts.value: browserSupportsPasskeys checks WebAuthn and capabilities for platform/hybrid authentication; it does not detect whether this particular user has a passkey.

facts.label: PQC option
facts.value: v14 supports ML-DSA-44/65/87 on supported runtimes; generator can prefer ML-DSA-44 when supported.

facts.label: WebAuthn as second factor
facts.value: Example shows adding WebAuthn 2FA to an existing account system. User verification can require a PIN/biometric factor within the authenticator interaction.

facts.label: Verification enforcement
facts.value: v14.0.3 verifyAuthenticationResponse defaults requireUserVerification=true; generation and verification settings must match the application's policy.

facts.label: Recovery and additional factors
facts.value: Synced credentials may help survive device loss, but app recovery codes, factor reset, TOTP/SMS/email second factors and account recovery are not implemented by the package APIs.

facts.label: Account ownership verification
facts.value: Passkey registration verifies a credential ceremony, not ownership of an arbitrary email/phone. Guide recommends application verification of a unique contact before new-user enrollment.

facts.label: Reset/change/delete account flows
facts.value: Password reset, email/address changes, self-service account deletion and account data policies belong to the surrounding application.

facts.label: Login sessions
facts.value: After successful verification, app must associate the credential with its internal user and establish its own session/cookie/token.

facts.label: Challenge lifetime and replay handling
facts.value: App must remember the generated challenge, pass it back as expectedChallenge and delete/consume it even after failed verification.

facts.label: Browser ceremony timeout/abort
facts.value: Generation source defaults ceremony timeout to 60,000 ms; WebAuthnAbortService cancels active browser ceremonies and starts fresh abort signals.

facts.label: SAML/OIDC federation
facts.value: Not applicable to the library's own protocol offer: server/browser packages implement WebAuthn relying-party ceremonies, not SAML SP/IdP or OIDC client/provider flows.

facts.label: Organizations, invitations and roles
facts.value: No customer workspace/role/invitation model in the libraries. Application owns internal users and associates stored credentials with them.

facts.label: SCIM
facts.value: Not applicable to the WebAuthn API itself; no bundled SCIM user/group provisioning/deactivation server.

facts.label: Ready-made screens
facts.value: No hosted login/profile portal or complete account dashboard. Browser library calls navigator.credentials; the browser/OS displays its authenticator prompt.

facts.label: Browser UI errors and capabilities
facts.value: WebAuthnError provides typed contextual errors; capability helpers let the application adapt UI instead of assuming universal passkey support.

facts.label: Domains and relying-party scope
facts.value: App configures rpID and expected origins/RP IDs; verification supports arrays of permitted origins/RP IDs.

facts.label: Cross-origin embeds
facts.value: Optional expectedTopOrigin constrains top-level sites for cross-origin authentication; app/browser iframe configuration is required.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility
facts.value: Not applicable to vendor-hosted UI: app and platform own user-facing copy, language and accessibility; no library screen catalog/VPAT established.

facts.label: Browser/platform limits
facts.value: Safari guide distinguishes iOS 17.4/macOS 14.4+ from older gesture-limited Safari; older Firefox Ed25519 quirks are also documented.

facts.label: Database and state prerequisites
facts.value: Documented integration requires user-linked credential storage and temporary challenge state; library suggests structures rather than requiring a particular database.

facts.label: Secure origin prerequisite
facts.value: WebAuthn needs a secure context: HTTPS with a valid certificate, with localhost development exception described by the guide.

facts.label: Optional external metadata

facts.value: Browser sendSignal can report unknown credential, all accepted credentials or current user details to supporting credential managers.

facts.label: Guest upgrade and password-to-passkey transition
facts.value: Conditional Create can add a passkey after another successful auth, but guest account upgrade and merging records remain application logic.

facts.label: Replay and origin checks
facts.value: Library generates cryptographically random 32-byte challenges and verifies expected challenge/origin/RP ID and response signature.

facts.label: Counter/backup behavior
facts.value: Verifier rejects a non-increasing signature counter when either stored/returned counter is positive; zero counters from some authenticators limit clone detection.

facts.label: Bot and volume protection
facts.value: No managed CAPTCHA, signup throttling, password-breach list or SMS-pumping control; operator protects its own generation/verification/enrollment routes.

facts.label: Vendor API quota

facts.label: Private-key/domain portability

facts.label: Existing credential migration
facts.value: No built-in bulk importer; app can preserve/migrate compatible credential records and feed them to verification methods.

facts.label: Custom user IDs
facts.value: Default WebAuthn user ID is opaque/random; custom userID uses byte values and must not contain identifying information such as email.

facts.label: Server deletion and retention
facts.value: Application deletes user/credential records, sessions and challenges and defines log/backup retention; there is no vendor account-close/purge schedule.

facts.label: Credential-manager deletion caveat
facts.value: Signal API can help update/remove stale passkeys or names, but does not guarantee receipt or successful processing by the authenticator.

facts.value: No universal requests/second quota or same-number cooldown duration published in the reviewed Verification docs.

facts.label: Observable security/verification events
facts.value: Final result and SMS delivery callbacks; CDR result/reason, request metadata and amounts support investigation.

facts.label: Audit retention / event streaming / fees
facts.value: No public Verification-specific retained-day schedule, guaranteed webhook replay/retry policy or audit-export surcharge found.

facts.label: Exportable verification records
facts.value: Downloadable semicolon-separated daily CDR files for previous UTC day, including verification ID, method, destination, country, reference/custom, amount, currency and result.

facts.label: Contractual data return
facts.value: DPA allows written request by termination for machine-readable personal-data copy and/or deletion certificate; additional return costs borne by customer.

facts.label: Account/password migration in
facts.value: Not applicable to importing users, password hashes, passkeys or social account links.

facts.label: Close developer account
facts.value: Request deletion through Sinch Online team with account ID and associated email address.

facts.label: Contract-end processor data deletion
facts.value: DPA: delete processed personal data within 90 days after account termination unless return requested; statutory/contractual record-retention duties remain.

facts.label: Project deletion restrictions
facts.value: No dashboard self-service project/subproject deletion; parent project deletion exceptional through support; some subproject API automation supports deletion.

facts.label: Live verification logs / backups / per-record deletion
facts.value: No public numeric live Verification-record/CDR/backup retention period or dedicated end-user-record deletion API found.

facts.label: Published Verification processing locations
facts.value: Subprocessor list names AWS Verification hosting locations Germany, Ireland, USA, Singapore and India.

facts.label: Support processing / transfers
facts.value: Zendesk support processing for Verification listed in USA, EU and APAC; DPA permits group transfers with contractual safeguards.

facts.label: Customer-selectable residency / backup geography
facts.value: No Verification-specific public region selection procedure, exclusive residency commitment, backup-region list or residency price found.

facts.label: DPA and role boundary
facts.value: Public DPA and privacy notice; DPA contains independent-controller exclusion for necessary communications/network functions.

facts.label: Assurance scope
facts.value: Trust Center lists ISO 27001: 2022 and SOC 2 badges/reports, and places Verification in Sinch Voice; says certifications may apply to specific products.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Sinch Verification; supplied by Sinch. Product: https://sinch.com/verification-api/; developer docs: https://developers.sinch.com/docs/verification/introduction

facts.label: Online contracting entities
facts.value: Online terms: USA/Canada customers contract with Sinch America, Inc.; rest of world with Sinch Sweden AB. Certain pre 2025-09-29 signups outside Europe/USA/Canada remain with Sinch UK Ltd.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active public documentation and trial entry path; Sinch announced a group-wide brand identity refresh on 2026-02-12. No separate Verification product rename, shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the sources searched.

facts.label: Component lifecycle boundary
facts.value: Current Node repository flags the separate SMS API as end-of-sale and directs new SMS integrations to Conversation API.

facts.label: Hosted commercial-use terms
facts.value: Commercial service governed by the applicable agreement, general terms and Verification supplement; no self-hosted Verification server license offered in these sources.

facts.label: Node SDK license
facts.value: Apache-2.0 for the official sinch-sdk-node repository; commercial use and modification subject to its license conditions.

facts.label: Status page
facts.value: Public Sinch status page includes Verification, Flash Call Verification, SMS Verification and Verification Text to Speech components.

facts.label: Availability promise
facts.value: Published SLA v 7.0(2024-01-12): reasonable endeavours toward minimum 99.95% monthly availability for ordered services.

facts.label: Node maintenance/version evidence
facts.value: SDK core changelog lists 1.8.0 and Verification dependency 1.8.0; repository documents current/previous-major support policy.

facts.label: Native integration maintenance caveat
facts.value: Android SDK 2.x rewritten and not backwards compatible; pre 2.1.3 SMS hash configuration has documented potential security issue.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Documentation, official community and support portal; published SLA helpdesk 24/7 for covered services.

facts.label: Contractual response targets
facts.value: SLA initial-response targets P 1: 30 minutes; P 2: 1hour; P 3: 24 hours; P 4: 48 hours; reasonable efforts for at least 90% of fault-response performance.
