apps.news: No sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found in the public sources reviewed.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Flat workspace subscription plus provisioned infrastructure/add-ons; unlimited users/MAU and core Keycloak SSO/MFA/SAML. No per-MAU growth fee.

facts.label: Allowance scope
facts.value: Workspace owns its subscription, clusters and shared developer-team resources; additional clusters consume size-specific slots.

facts.label: Ongoing free production allowance
facts.value: No published ongoing free-production quota found; the documented free offer is time-limited trial hosting.

facts.label: Trial expiry and retention
facts.value: Conflicting: terms suspend at trial expiry and delete generated data seven additional days later; plan docs give a three-day upgrade grace period and 30 days after suspension.

facts.label: Minimum paid subscription
facts.value: Developer: US$29/month, including one Small cluster and one custom domain. Annual price advertised as US$278/year.

facts.label: Commitment, tax and cancellation
facts.value: Monthly/annual recurring renewal; cancel in the account, effective at the end of the current paid term. Applicable sales tax is additional; terms specify USD.

facts.label: Refund rules
facts.value: Conflicting: public terms say purchases are non-refundable; subscription/billing docs advertise a 14-day money-back guarantee.

facts.label: Published base plans
facts.value: Monthly USD: Developer $29; Launch $149; Business $599; Enterprise custom quote. Advertised yearly amounts: $278 / $1,430 / $5,750 respectively, with a stated 20% saving.

facts.label: Infrastructure add-on rates
facts.value: Additional cluster/month: Small US$39, Medium US$199, Large US$625. Additional custom domain: US$49/month. Private network: US$299/month.

facts.label: Launch included cluster size
facts.value: Unclear: plan guide describes one Small-or-Medium cluster, while pricing calls Medium 'available' and its mini calculator lists a paid Medium selection.

facts.label: Business cost scenarios
facts.value: Native organization/role/SSO capabilities are available without per-organization or SAML connection pricing. A/B each have a US$29 base-fee candidate, conditional on a suitable supported version and Small capacity.

facts.label: Customer organization charging
facts.value: No published separate per-customer-organization, member-role or invitation price for native Keycloak Organizations; core Keycloak features are included in the subscription.

facts.label: Organization/member ceilings
facts.value: Native Organizations model is documented, but no numeric Skycloak customer-organization/member/invitation allowance or overage tariff was found.

facts.label: Business SSO fees
facts.value: OIDC and SAML business identity providers are core features, with no published per-connection or compulsory setup charge.

facts.label: SCIM fees and implementations
facts.value: SCIM feature page labels provisioning included on all plans. Native SCIM requires Keycloak 26.8 for supported status; an older vendor guide instead uses a marketplace SCIM server extension.

facts.label: Included infrastructure
facts.value: Developer: 1 Small cluster. Business: 1 Small + 1 Medium. Enterprise: 1 Small + 1 Medium + 1 Large. Launch has 1 cluster; Medium inclusion/upgrade pricing is unresolved under F11.

facts.label: Builder team access and keys
facts.value: Launch advertises team-member invitations; developer API key caps are Developer 10, Launch 25, Business 50, Enterprise 100.

facts.label: Workspace creation and domain count
facts.value: Signup creates one builder workspace; joining further workspaces requires invitation. Plan/domain guide says 1 custom domain on Developer/Launch/Business and 5 on Enterprise.

facts.label: Email delivery dependency
facts.value: Own SMTP configuration is documented for app-user email, including verification, password reset, invitations and email codes; SendGrid, SES, Mailgun and Google Workspace examples are provided.

facts.label: SMS and other delivery fees
facts.value: SMS OTP requires an SMS authenticator SPI plus a configured gateway (Twilio/AWS SNS/custom example). No destination rate or bundled SMS quantity established.

facts.label: Resource and request limit behavior
facts.value: No MAU overage. Cluster creation/size picker prevents exceeding available size slots; existing clusters are not deleted or resized solely because a plan's included slots change.

facts.label: Downgrades, failed payment and webhook quota
facts.value: Billing guide describes a 30-day downgrade adjustment period and resource limiting afterwards. Exact webhook monthly-request overage behavior and a universal hard spending-stop guarantee were not found.

facts.label: Optional security rates
facts.value: Monthly USD: WAF $149; geo-blocking $49; advanced rate limiting $59; IP access control $99; SIEM export $199; CAPTCHA protection calculator price $39.

facts.label: Extension and retention add-ons
facts.value: Bring Your Own Extension: US$99/month; Custom Extension Development: US$299/month. Extended logs: 1 year US$49/month, 2 years US$99/month; custom retention quote.

facts.label: Webhook allowance
facts.value: Developer: 1 destination/50 requests per month; Launch: 3/5,000; Business: 10/50,000; Enterprise: unlimited.

facts.label: Individual eligibility
facts.value: Personal accounts and an individual-developer plan are explicitly offered. Terms apply personally or on behalf of an entity and require age 18 or above.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: No complete public allowed/restricted buyer-country list located.

facts.label: Trial paths and card
facts.value: Default: 21-day trial of a managed realm on the shared US cluster. Expert path: 7-day dedicated Small cluster. Neither requires a credit card.

facts.label: Trial limits and extensions
facts.value: Trial is US-only, with no custom domains. Earned extensions can reach 45 days total on the shared path or 31 days on Expert.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Hosted managed Keycloak: accounts, login, sessions, verification, roles and SSO brokering. Shared-realm trial and dedicated paid clusters.

facts.label: Operational responsibilities
facts.value: Skycloak manages infrastructure, OS/container patches, Keycloak upgrades/CVEs, database, backups, network/TLS and monitoring. Builder manages realm/app policies, users, client secrets, IdPs, themes and application integration.

facts.label: Database and deployment ownership
facts.value: Paid clusters are fully managed, with dedicated compute/database/credentials according to the security page; no unmanaged operating mode is documented.

facts.label: Password sign-in
facts.value: built_in: username/email and password, self-registration controls, temporary passwords and reset flows.

facts.label: Email magic link
facts.value: Advertised as included on all plans, but exact native-vs-marketplace implementation, compatible extension/build and fee conditions were not established.

facts.label: Email and phone codes
facts.value: Email OTP is described with SMTP dependency. SMS OTP explicitly requires an authenticator SPI and external gateway; full minimum-plan/extension fee for each implementation is unresolved.

facts.label: Anonymous/wallet login
facts.value: Native anonymous-account login/guest upgrade and crypto-wallet sign-in were not established.

facts.label: Social providers
facts.value: Provider templates documented for Google, GitHub, Microsoft and Facebook; Microsoft setup example is organizational Entra/Azure AD. Generic OIDC/SAML is also available.

facts.label: Apple and broader inventory
facts.value: A Skycloak-specific supported Apple configuration/native-iOS flow and complete versioned social-provider inventory were not established.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: built_in: WebAuthn/FIDO2 first-factor or MFA using platform authenticators and hardware keys; core capability included on all plans.

facts.label: Passkey UI, recovery and domain
facts.value: Vendor tutorial covers conditional autofill, multiple credentials, Account Console management and cross-device browser passkeys; relying-party ID must match the registered domain.

facts.label: Native MFA and user recovery
facts.value: Authenticator TOTP, WebAuthn/security keys and backup recovery codes are documented; admins can reset factors/require re-enrollment and enforce MFA with realm flows.

facts.label: Workspace MFA enforcement
facts.value: Business and Enterprise can require MFA for the builder's Skycloak team; this is separate from native realm-user MFA included on lower plans.

facts.label: Adaptive MFA
facts.value: Free Adaptive Risk marketplace extension is documented for browser-login scoring and conditional OTP/WebAuthn step-up; it requires explicit install/flow configuration.

facts.label: Verification and credential lifecycle
facts.value: Email verification, password reset, profile/email updates, administrative disable/delete and credential required actions are documented.

facts.label: End-user account deletion
facts.value: Keycloak Account Console self-deletion is available when the delete-account role and required action are configured; vendor account deletion is separate.

facts.label: Session controls
facts.value: Configurable SSO/client idle and absolute lifetimes, remember-me bounds, access-token lifetime and offline-session caps; refresh-token rotation is optional in the vendor recipe.

facts.label: Session revocation
facts.value: Admins can list active user sessions, inspect device/IP/client details and revoke individual or all sessions.

facts.label: Enterprise login protocols
facts.value: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 and SAML 2.0 identity brokering: Skycloak/Keycloak accepts an upstream enterprise IdP. SP-initiated flow is guided; IdP-initiated/proxy flows need additional configuration.

facts.label: Issuing SAML to applications
facts.value: Keycloak can act as the SAML identity provider for SaaS applications; the application gallery and custom SAML app setup are documented.

facts.label: Native customer organizations
facts.value: Native Keycloak Organizations supports customer memberships/invitations and IdP/domain routing in one realm. Vendor walkthrough uses Keycloak 26.2.4 and says to verify that Organizations is supported/enabled.

facts.label: Roles and customer administration
facts.value: Keycloak 26.8.1 documents organization-group role mapping, invitations and scoped administration; realm/client roles and groups are also managed by Skycloak.

facts.label: Alternative tenant isolation
facts.value: Realm-per-customer is also documented, with separate users/clients/configuration; Organizations avoids separate realms when shared realm policies are acceptable.

facts.label: Native SCIM version scope
facts.value: Native Keycloak SCIM API is supported/default-enabled at server level in 26.8, with per-realm opt-in. It accepts inbound user/group provisioning, updates, PATCH and deletion.

facts.label: SCIM extension alternative and offboarding
facts.value: Older setup uses marketplace SCIM 2.0 Server for Keycloak with KEYCLOAK/EXTERNAL authentication modes and instance/realm/organization configuration.

facts.label: Login and self-service screens
facts.value: Keycloak hosts login/registration, reset/MFA screens and Account Console; Skycloak can brand login, account and admin screens.

facts.label: Branding by plan
facts.value: Launch removes Skycloak branding; Business/Enterprise allow uploaded/downloaded custom theme packages. Developer branding is inconsistent: pricing advertises custom branding with attribution, but plan docs exclude branding customization.

facts.label: Custom domains and extra fee
facts.value: Domain guide: Developer/Launch/Business 1 included, Enterprise 5; extra domains US$49/month. Cloudflare for SaaS handles ownership checks/TLS and certificate renewal.

facts.label: Calculator domain discrepancy
facts.value: Conflicting: advanced calculator's default Launch configuration says 2 included domains; pricing and domain/plan guides say 1.

facts.label: App-user login languages
facts.value: Launch+ guide lists 18 languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Swedish, Czech, Danish, Norwegian and Finnish.

facts.label: Builder dashboard languages
facts.value: Skycloak dashboard/sign-in pages support English, French and German, with account-saved choice; untranslated sections fall back to English.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No public Skycloak-specific WCAG conformance report or accessibility audit found for hosted login/account screens.

facts.label: Web framework scope
facts.value: Vendor integration guides cover React, Vue, Angular, Next.js/Nuxt, JavaScript, Node.js, Python, Java/Spring, PHP/Laravel, Go and .NET; these use standard OIDC/SAML libraries.

facts.label: React integration
facts.value: React guide: React 17+, Node.js 14+, using react-oidc-context (recommended) or @react-keycloak/web.

facts.label: Next.js integration
facts.value: Next.js 13+ App/Pages Router and Node.js 16+ guide uses NextAuth.js with Keycloak, server/client sessions and API protection.

facts.label: Android integration
facts.value: Official vendor guide uses external AppAuth for Android/Kotlin; minimum SDK 21 (Android 5.0), Android Studio Arctic Fox+ documented.

facts.label: iOS integration
facts.value: Official vendor guide uses AppAuth-iOS 1.6.2+, iOS 13+ target and Xcode 14+, with Swift URL callbacks/keychain integration.

facts.label: React Native and Expo
facts.value: Guide documents React Native 0.70+, Node 16+, iOS 12+/Android API21+ using react-native-app-auth; Expo uses expo-auth-session instead.

facts.label: Flutter
facts.value: Guide documents Flutter 3.19+ (3.24+ recommended), Dart 3.3+, flutter_appauth and platform-specific secure storage/deep links.

facts.label: Prerequisites and costs outside hosting
facts.value: Skycloak supplies the managed Keycloak/database stack. Builder supplies application hosting/backend, app integrations, IdP credentials and a suitable SMTP/SMS service when used.

facts.label: Self-host operation requirements
facts.value: not_applicable to the managed Skycloak purchase. Self-hosting Keycloak after export is a separate operating choice.

facts.label: Custom SPIs and attributes
facts.value: Custom Java JAR authenticators, protocol mappers and event listeners can be uploaded on Enterprise or Business with BYO add-on; vendor docs limit own JARs to under 50 MB and require malware scan.

facts.label: Custom upload plan ambiguity
facts.value: Specific extension guide says Business+BYO or Enterprise; advanced calculator labels extensions Launch+, while subscription page contains broad all-paid add-on wording.

facts.label: Webhook behavior
facts.value: Platform and Keycloak event webhooks have HMAC-SHA256 signing, filters and retries. Repeated failures pause delivery with health checks; events can be replayed.

facts.label: User admin and API
facts.value: Vendor dashboard and native Keycloak administration support create/search/update/disable/delete users, roles/groups, credentials, profile attributes and session revocation.

facts.label: Automation and human administration
facts.value: Keycloak Admin Console uses Skycloak SSO by default; machines use a per-cluster confidential automation client in the master realm.

facts.label: Native impersonation
facts.value: Keycloak 26.8.1 permits admin impersonation with the realm impersonation role.

facts.label: Account linking
facts.value: Provider guide documents manual/automatic identity linking, verified-account checks and first-login flow control.

facts.label: Native brute-force/password controls
facts.value: Realm-level failed-login lockout and password policy are configurable independently of the paid edge-security add-ons.

facts.label: Managed edge protection
facts.value: Paid optional WAF, IP/CIDR/path access rules, geo-blocking and advanced rate limiting; CAPTCHA uses Cloudflare Turnstile per realm.

facts.label: Management API quotas
facts.value: Per workspace: 5 requests/second, 300/minute, 5,000/hour, 25,000/day. Exceeded window returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After; rate-limit headers expose remaining budget/reset.

facts.label: Login edge rate configuration
facts.value: Optional ingress limiter supports global/per-IP RPM and exact-path limits, Redis-backed with roughly 5 seconds to 1 minute propagation.

facts.label: User and infrastructure log retention
facts.value: Developer: no vendor events/log viewer. Launch: user events 7 days, system logs 3; Business 30/30; Enterprise 90/90. Trial 7/7.

facts.label: Platform audit retention/export
facts.value: Audit logs: Trial 7 days, Launch 3, Business 30, Enterprise 90; Developer not included. Business/Enterprise export CSV/JSON; owners/admins only.

facts.label: System logs export
facts.value: Vendor Logs Viewer exports CSV/JSON/TXT with up to 10,000 entries per export; visibility is role-gated and plan-limited.

facts.label: Full database export and plan
facts.value: Launch/Business/Enterprise support manual PostgreSQL export; Trial/Developer do not. SQL or pgdump ZIP, with optional sensitive-data inclusion.

facts.label: Realm export contents
facts.value: Launch+ realm export includes all users and stored credentials, password hashes/OTP, roles/groups, clients, providers/mappers, flows and configuration; always encrypted.

facts.label: Backups and exit caveats
facts.value: Business/Enterprise downloadable backups are full PostgreSQL .dump archives, including credentials; one-time links expire after 15 minutes.

facts.label: Realm/database migration in
facts.value: Realm import is Launch+ and available during trial; importing in trial preserves that import access after conversion below Launch. Full database migration wizard is documented for Launch+.

facts.label: Self-hosted database migration
facts.value: Wizard accepts PostgreSQL dump upload/URL up to 10 GB compressed; MySQL/MariaDB conversion is support-assisted. Legacy /auth path, themes and custom extensions can be staged.

facts.label: Auth0 password migration
facts.value: Manual migration guide offers reset-all, lazy migration with a custom authenticator, or hash migration with a custom password-hash provider; no automated Auth0 migration toolkit is supplied.

facts.label: User/account deletion
facts.value: Live realm users can be administratively deleted. Builder account deletion is self-service in settings; privacy policy permits residual records for fraud/legal/operational needs.

facts.label: Trial/termination retention
facts.value: Conflicting: terms trial data seven extra days; plan docs 30 days after suspension. Security page says 60-day export grace after account termination.

facts.label: Backup retention and deletion
facts.value: Backup guide: Business 14-day automatic retention, Enterprise 30-day; manual retention 1–14 / 1–30 days. Cluster deletion deletes backups immediately; security overview instead says seven-day backups.

facts.label: Named production regions
facts.value: US East: Azure eastus2, Virginia; US West: AWS us-west-2, Oregon; EU: OVHcloud DE1, Germany; Canada: OVHcloud BHS5, Beauharnois/Quebec; Australia: Akamai/Linode Sydney.

facts.label: Backups and international processing
facts.value: Conflicting: backup feature guide says backups stay in cluster region; security page and current subprocessor list say database backups run in the US, with AWS Ohio us-east-2 plus Cloudflare storage listed.

facts.label: DPA, privacy and subprocessors
facts.value: Public privacy/subprocessor policies; DPA and Standard Contractual Clauses are available on request, rather than a public complete agreement located in this check.

facts.label: Vendor assurance claims
facts.value: Vendor claims SOC 2 Type II audit and ISO 27001 certification, with reports/certificate supplied on request/NDA. Public audit period, auditor, certificate validity and detailed scope were not established.

facts.label: Trust Center access
facts.value: Trust Center could not be read: HTTP 403 through direct public fetch and web reader.

facts.label: Regulated-data eligibility
facts.value: Security advertises HIPAA/BAA readiness; Terms section 1 restricts HIPAA/FISMA-regulated use; AUP allows regulated data only with a separate written agreement.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: Skycloak; legal operator: Logiciel D’identité Skycloak inc., registered in Canada, Montreal, Quebec. Site https://skycloak.io/; docs https://skycloak.io/docs/.

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Self-service account creation and paid Developer/Launch/Business subscriptions are publicly documented; Enterprise is sales-led. Signup not tested.

facts.label: API lifecycle
facts.value: Skycloak's public management API is beta; integrations must send API-Version: 2026-06-01.beta. Breaking changes may occur during beta.

facts.label: Hosted service terms
facts.value: Vendor service/content rights are governed by Skycloak's Terms of Service, with limited access rights and restrictions on redistribution/commercial exploitation.

facts.label: Server license
facts.value: Underlying Keycloak server: Apache License 2.0, permitting commercial use/modification/distribution subject to its conditions.

facts.label: Public status access
facts.value: Vendor documentation names status.skycloak.io, but direct retrieval failed DNS resolution and the public web reader could not access it.

facts.label: SLA scope by plan
facts.value: Developer/Launch: best effort, no contractual SLA. Business: 99.9% monthly availability on its included Medium cluster only; Enterprise: up to 99.99% as contracted.

facts.label: Conflicting Launch headline and credits
facts.value: Launch pricing card advertises 99.9%, but pricing FAQ, plan docs and SLA deny a contractual Launch promise. Business SLA credits: 10% below 99.9%, 25% below 99.5%, 50% below 99.0%.

facts.label: Version and upgrade policy
facts.value: Version catalog has active/inactive entries; auto-upgrade takes clean sequential steps in the maintenance window. Major/breaking changes require human action; schema downgrades are not supported.

facts.label: Current supported release inventory
facts.value: A complete current public Skycloak Keycloak version/support-end-date list was not found.

facts.label: Dated maintenance evidence
facts.value: API getting-started documentation records a 2026-10-15 update; native-SCIM article is dated 2026-10-02/updated 2026-10-06; public API versioning documents breaking beta response changes.

facts.label: Ordinary and urgent support
facts.value: Developer email best effort. Launch urgent 4 hours/normal 1 day in business hours; Business urgent 1 hour/normal 8 hours in extended hours; Enterprise urgent 1 hour/normal 3 hours, 24/7.

facts.label: Support and security contacts
facts.value: Dashboard problem reports/support portal and support@skycloak.io; billing@skycloak.io for billing. Vulnerabilities: security@skycloak.io, acknowledgment within two business days.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: the Apache core has no MAU, stored-user, login or message billing meter.

facts.label: Free production software
facts.value: No core software licence fee or user-count production cap in Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment
facts.value: Not applicable to core use; no compulsory commercial subscription established.

facts.label: Usage price formula
facts.value: Not applicable to the embedded core: no vendor usage tariff.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: No published customer-organization/invitation package or per-organization tariff found; JDBC groups are authorization groups.

facts.label: Business-SSO software fees
facts.value: SAML relying-party and OAuth/OIDC code use the core Apache licence; no per-connection licence charge in that licence.

facts.label: Developer seats/projects
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted dashboard-seat, project, environment or domain plan allowance.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: For one-time-token email/magic-link login, supply a custom delivery handler and mail sender.

facts.label: SMS and delivery charges
facts.value: SMS can be the delivery channel for server-generated OTTs; sender integration and charges are external.

facts.label: Vendor usage-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted core allowance that auto-upgrades or triggers an overage bill.

facts.label: Other core billable limits
facts.value: Not applicable: no core token, API-request, audit-retention or transaction-fee rate card.

facts.label: Hosted-account eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to the embedded open-source framework.

facts.label: Self-service and trial
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted production signup, card gate or trial period for the core framework.

facts.label: Product type
facts.value: Embedded Java security framework: authentication, authorization and protection against common attacks; Servlet and reactive applications.

facts.label: Authorization-server scope
facts.value: The OAuth2 authorization-server module supplies a foundation for OAuth 2.1 authorization servers and OpenID Connect 1.0 identity providers.

facts.label: Who operates it
facts.value: The application developer deploys and operates the application and selected credential/session stores.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in: username/password form authentication; the username can be an email if the application models it that way.

facts.label: Passwordless link/code login
facts.value: built_in OTT authentication; custom_code/external_service for delivery, including email magic links.

facts.label: Anonymous access
facts.value: built_in anonymous Authentication/authorities in the security context.

facts.label: Wallet login
facts.value: No first-party wallet-signature login flow established in the reviewed authentication documentation and source paths.

facts.label: Named preset providers
facts.value: Google, GitHub, Facebook and Okta have CommonOAuth2Provider configuration presets.

facts.label: Other social/enterprise providers
facts.value: Generic OAuth2/OIDC client registration supports provider-specific endpoints or issuer discovery.

facts.label: Passkey sign-in

apps.news: No qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signup, major paid feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found for Supabase Auth.

facts.label: MAU definition
facts.value: Distinct users who sign in or refresh their token during the billing cycle, including social sign-in; count each unique user once per cycle and reset next cycle. Allowances aggregate project usage within the builder's billing organization.

facts.label: Separate SSO and third-party meters
facts.value: SAML logins/refreshes count as Monthly Active SSO Users. Third-party JWT integrations count as Monthly Active Third-Party Users; social sign-in through Supabase is ordinary MAU.

facts.label: Free hosted production allowance
facts.value: 50,000 ordinary MAU and separately 50,000 Third-Party MAU per billing organization; unlimited stored users advertised; two active Free projects across Owner/Admin memberships. 500 MB DB/project, 5 GB egress and other resource limits apply.

facts.label: Pro minimum and billing
facts.value: From USD $25/month per billing organization; monthly subscription paid up front, usage billed in arrears. Includes $10 monthly compute credit, covering one Micro instance under the published monthly estimate.

facts.label: Team minimum
facts.value: From USD $599/month per billing organization; first project's Micro compute covered by the same $10 monthly credit. Adds team controls, longer retention and support SLA.

facts.label: Enterprise price and commitment
facts.value: Custom quote/order; no universal minimum monthly price, annual commitment, usage allowance or negotiated support amount published.

facts.label: Ordinary and third-party usage rates
facts.value: Free: 50,000 MAU per respective meter, no paid overage rate. Pro/Team: 100,000 ordinary MAU and 100,000 Third-Party MAU included; each respective excess user USD $0.00325 per billing cycle. Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Compute formula and rounding
facts.value: Micro compute USD $0.01344 per running hour, approximately $10/month; paid organizations get $10/month compute credit. A partial hour is billed as a full hour; compute is outside Spend Cap.

facts.label: Business scenario completeness
facts.value: Customer organization membership, invitation acceptance and roles need application-owned tables/policies/workflows. SAML is native on Pro+. Conditional platform examples are possible, but no turnkey complete B2B plan total is verified.

facts.label: Customer organization limits and fees
facts.value: No native customer-org/member/invitation allowance or per-customer-organization tariff found in the reviewed Auth and pricing docs. Use application tables/RLS for your workspace model.

facts.label: SAML SSO fees
facts.value: Free unavailable. Pro/Team include 50 SSO MAU, then USD $0.015 per additional SSO MAU per billing cycle. Enterprise custom. No per-connection fee or published connection-count tariff located.

facts.label: SCIM pricing and delivery status
facts.value: No public customer SCIM plan/rate card or complete supported account/group-sync product verified. v2.197.0 adds SCIM tables/discovery scaffolding; its router exposes only config/resource/schema discovery in the read SCIM block.

facts.label: Builder team, project and environment allowances
facts.value: All plan cards list unlimited team members. Free has two active projects, counted across organizations where members are Owner/Admin. Paid subscriptions cover all projects in one billing organization; each project has compute cost.

facts.label: Builder roles by plan
facts.value: Free/Pro: Owner, Admin, Developer. Team: adds Read-only and predefined project-scoped roles. Enterprise: custom project-scoped roles. Dashboard SSO is separate from Auth SAML.

facts.label: Default versus production email
facts.value: Default SMTP is non-production, only sends to addresses in the builder's project team, currently 2 messages/hour, with no delivery/uptime SLA. Production email flows need custom SMTP or a Send Email hook/provider.

facts.label: SMS/WhatsApp delivery
facts.value: Phone OTP and Phone MFA require your messaging provider or Send SMS hook. Named integrations include MessageBird, Twilio, Twilio Verify and Vonage; WhatsApp is documented only for Twilio/Twilio Verify.

facts.label: Free limit and Pro Spend Cap behavior
facts.value: Free has no paid overage; Pro Spend Cap is on by default and restricts covered usage beyond quotas under Fair Use. With cap off, permitted overage is billed; Team/Enterprise do not use the Pro-only cap.

facts.label: Spend Cap exclusions
facts.value: Compute, branches, read replicas, custom domains, extra IOPS/throughput, IPv4, log-drain usage, Phone MFA and PITR are outside the cap. AWS Marketplace-managed organizations cannot use Spend Cap.

facts.label: Phone MFA add-on
facts.value: Pro/Team: first project USD $0.1027/hour (advertised $75/month); additional projects $0.0137/hour (advertised $10/month each). Partial hour rounds up; SMS/WhatsApp extra. Enterprise custom.

facts.label: Other relevant add-ons and resource costs
facts.value: Paid custom domain $10/domain/month/project; log drain $60/drain/month plus $0.20/million events and $0.09/GB egress; paid DB disk beyond included $0.125/GB and egress $0.09/GB. Auth itself uses project resources.

facts.label: New log-usage billing timing
facts.value: Published log ingest rate $0.50/GB after quota; Free 1 GB, Pro/Team 20 GB included. September 25, 2026 notice gives existing organizations grace through early 2027, with potentially shorter grace for newer organizations.

facts.label: Individual and country eligibility
facts.value: Privacy notice explicitly covers individual accounts; standard cloud terms also address an individual acting for an organization. Export-control restrictions apply. No exhaustive allowed/restricted signup or billing-country list found.

facts.label: Hosted self-service and trial entry
facts.value: Free, Pro and Team have self-service start paths; Enterprise is contact-sales/custom. Free is ongoing at $0/month, not a fixed-duration trial. No universal trial-day allowance or mandatory company-domain rule established.

facts.label: Card and special entry restrictions
facts.value: A universal credit-card-free or no-payment-verification guarantee for every new account/project was not found in pricing, billing FAQ and current terms.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Backend platform with hosted Auth, also usable as a standalone Auth service or self-hosted server. Accounts, password/passwordless/social/wallet login, sessions/JWTs, verification, MFA and enterprise SAML are documented.

facts.label: Hosted operating responsibilities
facts.value: Supabase runs project infrastructure and Auth updates. Builder configures app authorization, keys, SMTP/SMS, OAuth providers, session policy and suitable compute; daily platform backups apply on paid plans.

facts.label: Self-hosted operating responsibilities
facts.value: Builder operates Go Auth/Postgres or the Docker stack, gateway/TLS, persistent data, secrets/signing keys, mail/SMS integrations, updates and independent database/Storage backups.

facts.label: Password methods
facts.value: Native email/password and phone/password. Email login is enabled by default; hosted email confirmation defaults on, local/self-host defaults off.

facts.label: Email passwordless methods
facts.value: Native magic links and six-digit email OTP; signInWithOtp sends a magic link by default, changed through the email template. Defaults: 60-second resend window and one-hour expiry.

facts.label: Phone codes, anonymous and wallets
facts.value: Native phone OTP via SMS/WhatsApp, anonymous sign-in and Ethereum/Solana wallet-message authentication. Wallet and anonymous users need not supply email/phone.

facts.label: Built-in social providers
facts.value: Official list: Apple, Azure/Microsoft, Bitbucket, Discord, Facebook, Figma, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Kakao, Keycloak, LinkedIn, Notion, Slack, Spotify, Twitter, Twitch, WorkOS and Zoom.

facts.label: Custom OAuth/OIDC provider caps
facts.value: Free: up to 3 custom providers. Pro and above: unlimited custom providers. Native OAuth2 manual endpoints and OIDC discovery with custom: identifiers.

facts.label: Provider-specific conditions
facts.value: Apple web/OAuth client secret must be regenerated every 6 months; native-only Apple setup differs. Google uses your OAuth client/branding settings. Azure account eligibility depends on supported account type and tenant URL.

facts.label: Passkey stage, login and eligibility
facts.value: Experimental WebAuthn passkeys; opt-in plus dashboard/server setup. Discoverable primary sign-in requires no email/username prompt. Registration requires a confirmed, signed-in, non-anonymous user; SSO users cannot register.

facts.label: Passkey domains and mobile scope
facts.value: Bare RP ID plus at most 5 allowed origins; HTTPS except loopback; origin host must match/be below RP ID. Android app origins supported. Swift end-to-end APIs: iOS 16+, macOS 13+, visionOS 1+; lower-level APIs cover more Apple platforms.

facts.label: Stable MFA and enforcement
facts.value: Native TOTP on all plans; Phone MFA on paid add-on. App must implement enrollment/challenge/verify and enforce aal2 claims in APIs/RLS/SSR. Optional, mandatory or selected-group policies are application choices.

facts.label: Experimental WebAuthn MFA and recovery codes
facts.value: Swift reference documents experimental WebAuthn second factor. JavaScript recoveryCodes.generate/verify require auth.experimental.recoveryCodes=true; codes are shown once and single-use verification upgrades to aal2.

facts.label: Recovery documentation mismatch
facts.value: Swift MFA overview still says recovery codes unsupported and suggests up to 10 TOTP factors, while JavaScript now publishes experimental recovery-code methods.

facts.label: Verification, reset and sensitive changes
facts.value: Native email/phone confirmation, reset-password email and updateUser flows. Configurable password-change reauthentication nonce/current-password requirement. Secure email change and security notification templates are documented.

facts.label: Account deletion by users
facts.value: Admin deleteUser is available; an app's user-facing delete-account flow needs a trusted backend calling it after authorization. No ordinary browser-secret-key deletion flow should be inferred.

facts.label: Default sessions and refresh behavior
facts.value: Default session lasts indefinitely, with unlimited concurrent sessions/devices. Access JWT defaults to 1h; refresh token rotates on use, with 10s reuse interval and an exception for the active token's parent.

facts.label: Paid session controls
facts.value: Pro and above support maximum lifetime, inactivity timeout and single active session per user. Checks occur at refresh; settings do not proactively destroy all sessions immediately.

facts.label: Logout and revocation semantics
facts.value: signOut defaults to global; local affects current session, others keeps current and revokes others. Offline JWTs remain valid until expiry; sensitive actions can check session_id against a live auth.sessions row.

facts.label: Business protocol roles
facts.value: Native SAML 2.0 service provider on Pro+ accepts customer IdPs, supports SP- and IdP-initiated sign-in and attribute mapping. Generic custom OIDC/OAuth2 is an upstream client integration. OAuth 2.1 Server issues downstream authorization-code/PKCE/OIDC tokens.

facts.label: SAML limits and identity behavior
facts.value: SAML Single Logout not supported despite an advertised SLO URL. SAML users cannot identity-link to ordinary accounts; same email may correspond to multiple distinct UUID users.

facts.label: Customer workspaces, roles and isolation
facts.value: Custom-code approach: create organization/membership/role tables and RLS policies; Custom Access Token hook can add authorization claims. SAML provider UUID can be mapped to your customer tenant.

facts.label: Invitation scope versus builder organization
facts.value: Admin inviteUserByEmail sends an Auth invite link. Supabase billing organizations contain builder projects/team members, not the customer's application organizations.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: Full native customer SCIM v2 Users/Groups create/update/deactivate support, plan availability and offboarding semantics remain unverified. Released v2.197.0 router has discovery-only SCIM routes in the inspected block.

facts.label: Current ready-made screens
facts.value: Supabase Library provides copyable Next.js password-auth pages/components, including signup, login and password reset/update paths. Auth APIs also support custom/headless UI.

facts.label: Legacy Auth UI package lifecycle
facts.value: supabase-community/auth-ui is archived; README says Supabase maintenance stopped 2024-02-07. Historical React/Solid/Svelte components remain published source.

facts.label: Branding and email templates
facts.value: Your app controls its own login/account UI. Runtime email templates exist; pricing gates removal of Supabase email branding to paid plans. New Free projects on default SMTP cannot customize templates from 2026-06-03; custom SMTP and older projects have documented exceptions.

facts.label: Hosted custom domains
facts.value: Paid add-on for paid projects: $10/domain/month/project; one custom domain per project, CNAME/subdomain configuration. Enterprise comparison lists one included, additional at $10; docs still limit a project to a single attached custom domain.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility evidence
facts.value: App-owned screens and email hooks/templates can be localized by the builder. Archived Auth UI supports imported localization files. No maintained full language matrix or product-wide WCAG/VPAT assessment found for customer Auth UI.

facts.label: Web packages and runtimes
facts.value: supabase-js is the browser/server client; @supabase/ssr handles cookie sessions for Next.js/SvelteKit/TanStack Start; @supabase/server handles per-request Bearer auth in Edge Functions, Workers, Vercel, Bun and framework APIs.

facts.label: Other SDKs and current framework changes
facts.value: Docs provide Python, Swift, Dart/Flutter and Kotlin integration examples; .NET became officially supported 2026-10-09. New official Go SDK is public alpha with GetClaims/GetUser and database coverage, not full signup/auth feature parity.

facts.label: Mobile clients and redirects
facts.value: Documented native Swift, Flutter/Dart, Kotlin and Expo React Native flows; deep links are needed for email confirmations/reset links and browser OAuth return paths. Native ID-token linking is also documented.

facts.label: Database and external services
facts.value: Hosted Auth uses the project's Postgres auth schema. Self-hosted standalone Go Auth needs Postgres; full Docker stack adds gateway, Studio and optional backend services. Email/SMS/OAuth/CAPTCHA providers require external configuration.

facts.label: Self-hosted deployment and sizing
facts.value: Official Docker/Compose guide supports self-hosting. Full-stack minimum: 4 GB RAM, 2 CPU cores, 40 GB SSD; recommended 8 GB+, 4 cores+, 80 GB+ SSD. Removing unused services can reduce requirements.

facts.label: Self-hosted upgrades, backup and restore
facts.value: Stable tested Compose snapshots are published roughly monthly; service versions may lag individual latest images. update.sh merges release configuration, preserves operator edits and flags conflicts/breaking changes; database and Storage backups must be taken separately.

facts.label: Hosted backup coverage
facts.value: Free: operator should export/offsite-backup regularly. Pro: 7 days of daily backups; Team: 14 days; Enterprise docs: up to 30 days. Optional PITR paid; database backups omit actual Storage objects.

facts.label: Hooks by plan
facts.value: Free/Pro docs: Before User Created, Custom Access Token, Send Email and Send SMS. Team/Enterprise add Password Verification Attempt and MFA Verification Attempt. Pricing's short Free/Pro hook list omits Before User Created.

facts.label: Hook execution and event delivery
facts.value: HTTP hooks use signed Standard Webhooks headers and JSON; payload limit 20 KB. Postgres hooks have 2s, HTTP 5s total budget. Retryable HTTP 429/503 with nonempty Retry-After can get up to 3 retries with 2s backoff, within the same budget.

facts.label: User metadata and custom permissions
facts.value: Native user_metadata/app_metadata and custom-token claims; app authorization roles/permissions can be stored in protected tables and issued by a token hook.

facts.label: Admin APIs and dashboard
facts.value: Dashboard user management plus server-side create/read/list/update/delete/invite, bans, factors and passkey administration. Secret/service credentials required for privileged actions.

facts.label: Identity linking and guest upgrade
facts.value: Automatic linking of verified matching-email identities; authenticated manual linking can be enabled, including different-email/native-ID-token flows. Unlink needs at least 2 identities. Anonymous users can link email/phone/OAuth to become permanent.

facts.label: Bot and password-abuse controls
facts.value: Native Auth throttles plus configurable hCaptcha/Cloudflare Turnstile integration; production signup/anonymous/wallet abuse can use CAPTCHA. Configurable password length/character policy; leaked-password checking via Have I Been Pwned is Pro+.

facts.label: Email, SMS and user cooldowns
facts.value: Default built-in email 2/hour/project; SMS 30/hour/project. Per-user OTP/magic-link, signup-confirmation and password-reset request cooldown defaults to 60s.

facts.label: IP and token endpoint rates
facts.value: Default signup/signin endpoints: 30/5m/IP, burst 30, excluding anonymous; verification 30/5m/IP burst 30; token endpoint 150/5m/IP burst 30; MFA challenge/verify 15/min/IP burst 30 (not configurable in table).

facts.label: Auth event coverage and export
facts.value: Auth audit records signup/login, password/reset, email verification, refresh/revoke/signout, linking, MFA/passkey/recovery actions; dashboard external storage plus optional auth.audit_log_entries database writes. Logs UI exports filtered CSV/JSON up to 1,000 rows per export selection.

facts.label: Retention by hosted plan
facts.value: Auth Audit Logs: Free 1 hour, Pro 7d, Team 28d, Enterprise included with no exact auth-specific duration in comparison. API/DB logs: Free 1d, Pro 7d, Team 28d, Enterprise 90d.

facts.label: Profile, IDs, hashes and account-link export
facts.value: Operator can query/export auth data via database tooling; bcrypt password hashes are in auth.users.encrypted_password, and ordinary user JSON omits them. Full auth-schema migration includes hashed passwords and related native tables.

facts.label: Exit constraints and passkeys
facts.value: Native DB export/restore can preserve passwords between Supabase projects. Tokens may require fresh login if signing keys/issuer configuration changes; passkeys need the original RP domain and complete compatible credentials.

facts.label: Direct user/hash import
facts.value: Released v2.197.0 admin API accepts password_hash and a custom nonnil UUID ID. User constructor validates bcrypt, Argon2-prefix and a specific Firebase-scrypt encoded format.

facts.label: Migration strategies and limits
facts.value: Official guide covers one-off and rolling Auth0 migration, including compatible hash creation and fallback logic; native auth-schema backup/restore covers Supabase-to-Supabase. Other providers/credentials need case-specific work.

facts.label: User deletion semantics
facts.value: Hard delete is default; optional shouldSoftDelete=true irreversibly anonymizes/soft-deletes the account. Release delete code removes factors/WebAuthn credentials/sessions on the soft-delete path; hard delete uses database deletion/relations.

facts.label: Hosted retention and contract exit
facts.value: DPA v1 dated 2026-08-01: request Covered Data return within 30 days after agreement expiry; after that Retention Period, covered copies are to be deleted. Project deletion removes associated backups per docs; general account/privacy retention is purpose/law-based.

facts.label: Anonymous cleanup and account closure
facts.value: Anonymous users have no automatic cleanup; application/operator deletes them. Native account/project closure and withdrawal rights are governed by platform controls/terms; a full universal account-close erasure timetable was not located.

facts.label: Hosted primary regions
facts.value: Specific regions: us-west-1, us-west-2, us-east-1, us-east-2, ca-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-west-3, eu-central-1, eu-central-2, eu-north-1, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-2, sa-east-1.

facts.label: Residency boundaries and self-hosting
facts.value: Database, Auth, Storage objects and backups are in the selected project region. Account/billing, support, telemetry/logs and CDN can process elsewhere; logs are ingested/stored in EU data centers per October 6, 2026 FAQ. Self-hosted operator selects locations.

facts.label: Public privacy/processing and subprocessors
facts.value: Public ToS, Privacy Notice, DPA and subprocessor-list page. DPA applies Supabase as processor/subprocessor for covered customer data; privacy notice mainly covers its controller use. Subprocessor page lists October 12, 2026 and June 1, 2026 revisions.

facts.label: Assurance claims and access scope
facts.value: Vendor says SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and ISO 27001 certified; Team/Enterprise can access reports/certificate via dashboard. HIPAA requires BAA and customer obligations; Team/Enterprise paid add-on available.

facts.label: Name, alias, owner and URLs
facts.value: Supabase Auth, the Go-based authentication/user-management server powering Supabase. Originated as a Netlify GoTrue fork; the projects have diverged. Standard hosted contracting entity: Supabase Pte. Ltd.; AWS Marketplace purchases normally contract with Supabase, Inc.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Active hosted product and maintained source; Auth repository archived=false, disabled=false, pushed_at 2026-11-04T12:04:48Z. Latest GitHub release v2.197.0 published 2026-09-09T15:27:11Z.

facts.label: Component sunsets and preview scope
facts.value: Old Auth UI repo archived and no longer maintained by Supabase since 2024-02-07. Auth Helpers are deprecated in favor of @supabase/ssr. Four @supabase/server framework adapters remove on 2026-12-01; hosted legacy TLS cipher removal starts 2026-11-10 at earliest. Passkey APIs are experimental.

facts.label: Slack provider retirement
facts.value: Legacy Slack v1 provider deprecated; replacement Slack (OIDC). Dated 2024-12-02 notice set 2025-01-15 dashboard-configuration removal, while the current Slack guide still says the old integration works until '10th October' without a clear current year.

facts.label: Self-hosted license
facts.value: Auth v2.197.0: MIT License; permits commercial use, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale, provided the copyright/permission notice is retained.

facts.label: Hosted use and preview terms
facts.value: Hosted access is governed by the Supabase Terms/Order and DPA, separately from MIT source rights. Beta/alpha features are optional, as-is, outside support/SLA obligations and may change or be discontinued.

facts.label: Status and availability SLA
facts.value: Public status at status.supabase.com. Enterprise order-covered GA products: 99.9% per calendar month; Auth scope is per project and depends on Postgres. Free/Pro/Team have no published uptime SLA.

facts.label: Release and maintenance evidence
facts.value: Auth v2.197.0 GitHub release published 2026-09-09; release body labels changes 2026-09-03. Repository active November 4. Self-hosted stack snapshots and hosted releases have separate cadences.

facts.label: Free and Pro support
facts.value: Community support on Free; billing/account support for all. Pro includes limited technical support through dashboard/web ticket or registered-account email fallback; no Pro target response SLA.

facts.label: Team and Enterprise response targets
facts.value: Team: Urgent 24h (24/7), High/Normal 1 business day, Low 2 business days. Enterprise Standard: Urgent 1h (24/7), High 2 business hours, Normal 1 business day, Low 2 business days. Business hours 6am to 6pm local unless stated.

facts.value: No universal paid base subscription is listed. The service cover sets one-month subscription periods and at least 10 days' non-renewal notice.

facts.label: Currency, tax and payment
facts.value: Incorporated standard terms use USD and exclude taxes; cover says monthly invoicing, payment five days from the last day of the subscription period.

facts.label: Cloud basic usage calculation
facts.value: Calculator: base(N) = $0 when N < 5,000; otherwise ceil(0.02 × N) per month.

facts.label: Conflicting Cloud worked prices
facts.value: Official vendor article estimates 10k $100, 50k $900 and 100k $1,900 by deducting 5,000; the main calculator instead yields $200/$1,000/$2,000.

facts.label: MFA add-on prices
facts.value: Cloud $0.01/MAU/month; self-hosted calculator $0.02/MAU/month; minimum $100/month when enabled.

facts.label: Account-linking add-on prices
facts.value: Cloud $0.005/MAU/month; self-hosted calculator $0.01/MAU/month; calculator applies a $100/month add-on minimum.

facts.label: Account-linking minimum conflict
facts.value: Page example at 5,000 Cloud MAU totals $125; calculator's base $100 plus $100 linking minimum totals $200.

facts.label: Discounts and estimate range
facts.value: Pricing invites discount discussions above 10,000 MAU or more than five customer organizations; no public discount schedule is supplied.

facts.label: Business scenario software subtotals
facts.value: Assuming nine/90 ordinary large tenants plus one/10 SSO tenants: Cloud A $95, B $1,150/month; self-host paid-feature subtotal A $95, B $950/month.

facts.label: Ordinary small customer tenants
facts.value: Tenants with fewer than five users: first 25 free; each additional such tenant $2/month, in the public calculator for Cloud and self-host.

facts.label: Ordinary larger customer tenants
facts.value: Password/social/passwordless tenant with five or more users: $5/tenant/month; both Cloud and self-host calculator.

facts.label: Membership and invitation limits
facts.value: Native tenant associations and role APIs exist; React/Node tenant plugin adds invitations, join requests and tenant administration. Numeric member/invite caps were not found.

facts.label: Enterprise SSO tenant fee
facts.value: $50 per enterprise SSO tenant per month, including a tenant with zero users; Cloud and self-host calculator.

facts.label: Connection allowances and SCIM tariffs
facts.value: Included SAML clients per SSO tenant, extra-client/setup fees and a native SCIM/directory-sync price were not found.

facts.label: User-management dashboard credentials
facts.value: First three dashboard users free; $20 per additional dashboard user/month, both deployment options.

facts.label: Additional apps and environments
facts.value: Calculator charges $50 per additional app/environment per month within multitenancy estimation.

facts.label: Vendor dashboard seats and project caps
facts.value: A separate numerical SaaS-dashboard collaborator limit, maximum apps/environments and custom-domain cap were not established.

facts.label: Default and own email delivery
facts.value: Backend SDK can use SuperTokens' default email service or your own SMTP/custom delivery; default service does not support custom templates.

facts.label: Email fees and quotas
facts.value: A current numeric default free-send quota, guaranteed delivery allowance and public per-email tariff were not found.

facts.label: SMS sender choices
facts.value: Default SuperTokens SMS service, own Twilio or custom delivery are documented for the backend SDK.

facts.label: SMS delivery prices and quotas
facts.value: Destination tariffs and guaranteed included-send amounts are not public in the pages checked.

facts.label: Threshold and non-payment behavior
facts.value: Calculator begins billing at 5,000 MAU; incorporated terms permit suspension for unpaid undisputed balances more than 30 days beyond the payment period and for specified harmful/restricted use.

facts.label: Budget controls and overage grace
facts.value: A self-service hard spending cap, exact usage-alert thresholds, free-tier grace period and cardless threshold behavior were not found.

facts.label: Quote-only additions
facts.value: Unified Login, machine-to-machine auth, multiple availability zones/uptime SLAs, Attack Protection Suite and implementation help say Contact us.

facts.label: Commercial-license dependency for MFA
facts.value: MFA's required AccountLinking recipe may affect the combined charge; compulsory combined billing treatment is not stated.

facts.label: Individual eligibility
facts.value: Service cover defines Customer as a company or person.

facts.label: Seller-country eligibility
facts.value: A complete eligible/restricted seller-country and payment-instrument list was not found.

facts.label: Self-service production entry
facts.value: Public managed setup and a Cloud free-usage tier are advertised; production and development Core instances are distinguished.

facts.label: Trial and checkout requirements
facts.value: Timed trial length, mandatory card, company-domain requirement and payment-method list were not established.

facts.label: Account-system scope
facts.value: Authentication server plus frontend/backend SDKs: accounts, signup/login, sessions, verification, reset, roles and optional business authentication.

facts.label: Hosted versus self-hosted architecture
facts.value: Cloud operates Core and its database; self-hosted runs Core on your infrastructure. Both use an SDK inside your own backend.

facts.label: Managed responsibilities
facts.value: Vendor operates Core/database infrastructure and scaling; developer runs its backend SDK, frontend, application data and delivery configuration.

facts.label: Self-host responsibilities
facts.value: Developer operates Core, PostgreSQL, private networking/API-key protection, deployment, upgrades, database backups and recovery.

facts.label: Email and password
facts.value: built_in EmailPassword recipe, in Cloud core and Apache self-host core.

facts.label: Username and phone with password
facts.value: Username/password is custom_code over EmailPassword; pricing also lists phone-number/password among core methods.

facts.label: Email link and email OTP
facts.value: built_in Passwordless recipe supports email magic links and one-time codes.

facts.label: Phone OTP and phone link
facts.value: built_in Passwordless supports SMS codes and magic links; sender is external_service/default vendor service or your provider.

facts.label: Anonymous and guest access
facts.value: custom_code anonymous JWT workflow; no persistent Core guest account is created by that guide.

facts.label: Wallet authentication
facts.value: Pricing's SuperTokens comparison column says Web3 login No; no native wallet recipe was found in the docs index.

facts.label: Built-in social/provider configuration
facts.value: Named providers include Google, Google Workspace, GitHub, GitLab, Facebook, Discord, Twitter, LinkedIn, Apple, Okta and Active Directory.

facts.label: Apple platform restriction
facts.value: Apple uses a POST callback to the backend and does not accept localhost as its redirect domain.

facts.label: Generic providers
facts.value: Custom OAuth2/OIDC providers can be configured with discovery/endpoints and profile mapping.

facts.label: Standalone passkey sign-in
facts.value: built_in WebAuthn first-factor recipe; Node.js, Python and Go backends; React prebuilt or custom web UI.

facts.label: Passkey recovery and domain constraints
facts.value: Recovery email token permits a new credential. Production needs HTTPS, an appropriate RP ID and an exactly configured origin.

facts.label: Native passkey client work
facts.value: Mobile guide uses platform APIs or a React Native passkey library; Flutter uses native platform channels.

facts.label: Conditional autofill evidence
facts.value: An explicit supported conditional-autofill/browser matrix was not established.

facts.label: MFA factors and enforcement
facts.value: Paid MFA: TOTP authenticator codes, email/SMS OTP, WebAuthn/passkeys; per-user enforcement and sensitive-action step-up are documented.

facts.label: MFA recovery codes
facts.value: custom_code recovery codes, stored as hashes via UserMetadata, with developer-built endpoints and UI.

facts.label: Magic-link MFA restriction
facts.value: Prebuilt UI supports email/SMS magic link as a first factor only; use OTP for the second factor.

facts.label: Email verification and password recovery
facts.value: built_in optional/required email verification plus emailed password-reset links and reset screens.

facts.label: Phone confirmation and account changes
facts.value: Phone passwordless OTP proves possession in its login flow. Backend user-management functions expose user lookup and changes; deletion is a backend action.

facts.label: Session lifecycle and token transport
facts.value: built_in access/refresh tokens; cookie web authentication or header transport; automatic refresh and retry; refresh-token rotation.

facts.label: Expiry controls
facts.value: Scalability documentation gives a default access-token validity of 3,600 seconds and describes tuning access_token_validity.

facts.label: Sign-out and lost-device revocation
facts.value: Backend APIs revoke one or all sessions; revocation/deletion removes refresh-session state. Immediate access-token rejection requires checkDatabase.

facts.label: Incoming enterprise SAML
facts.value: Native paid SAML service-provider/broker recipe, Core 12.0+, Node.js/Python; Go unsupported.

facts.label: Incoming OIDC versus outgoing OAuth
facts.value: ThirdParty custom OIDC connects an external provider. Unified Login makes a common OAuth2 authorization server for multiple apps.

facts.label: Unified Login edition restriction
facts.value: Unified Login docs say managed service only, Node.js/Python, with magic-link login unsupported; pricing FAQ says both deployments have the same features.

facts.label: Tenant and user isolation
facts.value: App contains tenants; tenants can use shared/separate user pools and per-tenant login methods; session identity is tenant-scoped.

facts.label: Roles and permissions
facts.value: built_in UserRoles recipe supplies role/permission definitions and per-tenant user-role assignments.

facts.label: Customer administration and invitations
facts.value: plugin: React/Node tenant manager adds creation, invitations, join requests, role changes, member removal and switching.

facts.label: Tenant plugin release caveat
facts.value: Published 0.2.0 Node and React references warn that packed declaration graphs import unpublished @shared modules.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: A documented native SCIM 2.0 User/Group API, directory connection allowance, deactivation contract and price were not found.

facts.label: Ready-made login screens
facts.value: Embedded React prebuilt signup/signin, reset, verification and supported passwordless/MFA/passkey flows; custom headless UI is available.

facts.label: Account profile and tenant screens
facts.value: plugin: React/Node profile and tenant-management screens; custom UI possible via plugin hooks.

facts.label: Themes and own application domains
facts.value: Prebuilt UI supports styles/components overrides; websiteDomain/apiDomain and auth route paths point at developer-controlled domains.

facts.label: Branding fee and domain cap
facts.value: An explicit watermark-removal entitlement/fee and numeric included custom-domain cap were not established.

facts.label: UI localization
facts.value: Prebuilt React strings can be overridden with translation configuration/custom language mappings; external i18n integration is illustrated.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A public WCAG conformance report, VPAT or scoped accessibility audit was not found.

facts.label: Official backend and web support
facts.value: Official backend SDKs: Node.js, Python, Go; frontend React prebuilt and JavaScript headless. Framework examples include Express, Hapi, Fastify, Koa, Next.js, NestJS; FastAPI, Flask, Django; Go HTTP/Gin/Chi/Mux.

facts.label: Serverless and compatibility
facts.value: Official guides cover Next.js App/Pages Router, NestJS, AWS Lambda, Netlify and Vercel; update guide supplies a Core/SDK compatibility selector.

facts.label: Official mobile SDKs
facts.value: iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter SDK/update routes are documented.

facts.label: Persistent database prerequisite
facts.value: Self-host Core 11.0.0+ supports PostgreSQL; current docs say MySQL and MongoDB support was removed in 11.0.0.

facts.label: Other service dependencies
facts.value: Own application backend is required; email/SMS senders are external/default vendor services; CAPTCHA providers and OpenTelemetry collectors are optional integrations.

facts.label: Self-host deployment and network
facts.value: Docker or VM deployment; Core default port 3567; keep it private or configure an API key. Database tables can be created/migrated with suitable privileges.

facts.label: Upgrades and sizing
facts.value: Update guide requires stopping Core and applying intervening migrations. Scalability guide describes horizontal Core scaling and t3.micro as a possible 100k-MAU starting example.

facts.label: Backup/restore guarantees
facts.value: A complete versioned backup/restore runbook, managed backup retention schedule and recovery-time/recovery-point objectives were not found.

facts.label: Custom authentication logic
facts.value: built_in function/API overrides run in your backend process; frontend hooks/components can be overridden.

facts.label: Additional profile data
facts.value: built_in UserMetadata stores arbitrary JSON by user ID; profile plugin adds UI-managed fields.

facts.label: External event delivery guarantees
facts.value: A vendor-managed auth-event webhook delivery SLA, retry schedule, durable queue and event-retention tariff were not found.

facts.label: Administrative API and dashboard
facts.value: SDK/Core user lookup, per-tenant pagination, count and delete; dashboard lists/details users and edits supported user information.

facts.label: Banning users
facts.value: plugin: React/Node banning assigns a banned role, revokes sessions and overrides session validation.

facts.label: User impersonation
facts.value: custom_code protected admin endpoint creates a session for the target user.

facts.label: Automatic linking
facts.value: Paid AccountLinking matches verified identifiers within a tenant under a backend callback policy; Node.js/Python, not current Go.

facts.label: Manual linking and unlinking
facts.value: Paid backend APIs create primary users, test whether linking is allowed, link and unlink login methods.

facts.label: Link callback and guest upgrade
facts.value: onAccountLinked is after-commit and is not automatically retried; guest-to-registered transition is custom session/data transfer.

facts.label: Paid attack protection
facts.value: Attack Protection Suite is beta, off by default and contact-priced; docs name brute-force, breached-password, bot, suspicious-IP, impossible-travel and new-device protection.

facts.label: CAPTCHA integration
facts.value: plugin for React/Node: Google reCAPTCHA v2/v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile with developer-supplied provider keys.

facts.label: Password hashing and session protections
facts.value: Core uses bcrypt by default with Argon2 support/configuration; session stack supplies token rotation and cookie/CSRF mechanisms.

facts.label: Managed free rate limit
facts.value: Core requests limited per app and source IP: 50 requests/second, with a 50-request burst described in the guide.

facts.label: Managed paid rate limit and retries
facts.value: Paid limits/bursts adjust dynamically with a minimum 100 requests/second; request higher limits from support. Backend SDK retries 429 up to five times.

facts.label: Health endpoint and self-host throttling
facts.value: /hello: 5 requests/second per app regardless of IP. Self-host otherwise has no general Core rate throttle; add proxy limits if needed.

facts.label: Application observability
facts.value: plugin: Node.js OpenTelemetry instruments overridable functions/APIs and sends traces using your configured OpenTelemetry setup.

facts.label: Audit-event retention and export
facts.value: A managed end-user audit-log event catalog, numeric retention, export/stream entitlement and pricing were not established.

facts.label: Profile and identifier extraction
facts.value: custom_code can paginate tenant users and fetch account identifiers, login methods and metadata through backend APIs.

facts.label: Hosted password and secret export
facts.value: A documented self-service Cloud export of password hashes, TOTP seeds, all linked credentials and passkey records, plus its format/fee, was not found.

facts.label: Self-host exit and passkey portability
facts.value: Self-host operator controls PostgreSQL and can retain its own database; passkey credentials are RP-domain scoped.

facts.label: Bulk and ongoing import
facts.value: Core 10.0.0+ persistent storage supports asynchronous bulk import, at most 10,000 users per request, plus direct/on-the-fly imports.

facts.label: Password and linked-account migration
facts.value: Import guide supports compatible bcrypt, Argon2 and Firebase scrypt hashes; multiple login methods require account linking enabled.

facts.label: Identity and session migration
facts.value: Legacy user-ID mapping is documented, with a 128-character external-ID limit in that guide; session migration exchanges an authenticated old-provider session through app code.

facts.label: Deleting an app user
facts.value: Backend deleteUser permanently removes the user's associated Core information and database sessions.

facts.label: Post-termination deletion promise
facts.value: Upon expiration/termination and Customer's request, Provider will delete Customer Content within 60 days; incorporated terms also preserve ordinary-backup/record-retention and legal exceptions for Confidential Information.

facts.label: Privacy-policy scope and retention
facts.value: Privacy policy updated 2023-01-02 excludes customer end-user data processed on customer instructions; controller-data retention is purpose/contract/legal based.

facts.label: Auth-data backup/log retention and account closure
facts.value: Exact hosted identity-backup purge periods, auth-log retention and a public self-service vendor-account closure procedure were not established.

facts.label: Managed region selection
facts.value: Public setup advertises any AWS-supported region worldwide and recommends deployment near the backend; status page names N. Virginia, Ireland and Singapore components.

facts.label: Backup, log and support data location
facts.value: No complete per-data-type region list or contractual guarantee that identity backups, logs and support access stay in the chosen region was found.

facts.label: Self-host location control
facts.value: Developer chooses Core/PostgreSQL location; default email/SMS delivery may still send data to SuperTokens services.

facts.label: SOC 2 assurance claim
facts.value: Service cover commits to annual SOC 2 Type II reporting/certification maintenance; public pricing also claims SOC2 compliance.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessor publication
facts.value: A public vendor-specific signed/standard DPA and complete customer-auth-data subprocessor list were not found in readable legal pages.

facts.label: Trust-center retrieval
facts.value: Security page redirects to security.supertokens.com; public extraction returned only a shell/title, so gated reports and processor documents could not be inspected.

facts.label: Name, owner and official entry points
facts.value: SuperTokens; service provider SuperTokens, Inc. Official site https://supertokens.com/; docs https://supertokens.com/docs; Core repository https://github.com/supertokens/supertokens-core.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Public managed-service setup and self-host deployment instructions are available; Core 12.4.1 was published 2026-10-23.

facts.label: Open-source component licenses
facts.value: Core outside commercial exceptions, supertokens-node and supertokens-auth-react publish Apache-2.0 licenses.

facts.label: Self-hosted commercial features
facts.value: The ee license requires an agreed subscription or other agreement and valid production license; development/testing has a separate permission.

facts.label: Tenant plugin license evidence
facts.value: A clear license grant for the separate tenants plugin packages was not established.

facts.label: Public service status
facts.value: Official API Status link leads to supertokens.instatus.com with named regional/development/production components.

facts.label: SLA promise and contract scope
facts.value: Setup advertises 99.9% Uptime SLA; pricing makes multi-AZ infrastructure and uptime SLAs contact-priced. Public plan-specific credits/measurement window were not found.

facts.label: Latest release evidence
facts.value: GitHub latest endpoints: Core 12.4.1, published 2026-10-23; Node SDK 24.1.0, 2026-10-29; React SDK 0.51.2, 2026-02-13.

facts.label: Security maintenance policy
facts.value: All security fixes backported for at least one year; Core policy currently names 11.0+ for all fixes and 6.0+ for critical fixes.

facts.label: Managed update control inconsistency
facts.value: Setup advertises automatic latest-version updates; update guide directs users to select a managed deployment and click Upgrade Core.

facts.label: Community and paid support
facts.value: Core pricing includes community support; evaluation links to Discord/calls. Professional support offers email, Slack, MS Teams and video, with advertised response options from two hours to two days.

facts.label: Security-report response policy
facts.value: Private GitHub vulnerability reporting or security@supertokens.com; acknowledgement within five business days and initial assessment within 14 days.
