apps.news: No qualifying sale, shutdown, rebrand, pivot, closed signup, major paid feature retirement, customer-data breach, regulatory action or licence change found for Symfony Security.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Not applicable: the embedded packages do not meter MAUs, stored users, returning users, logins or tokens for a vendor authentication invoice.

facts.label: Free production use
facts.value: Core MIT software may be used in production without a licence charge; its terms impose no user-count allowance or monthly reset.

facts.label: Minimum paid auth commitment
facts.value: Not applicable: no paid core production subscription, annual commitment or compulsory commercial licence.

facts.label: Usage tiers and rounding
facts.value: Not applicable: no Symfony Security per-user tier table, overage unit, invoice rounding rule or negotiated auth plan.

facts.label: Organization limits and fees
facts.value: No built-in customer organization/membership/invitation service or organization tariff in the reviewed core. Tenant models, member roles and invitations are application code.

facts.label: SSO and SCIM fees
facts.value: Not applicable as vendor connection billing: core OIDC/CAS token validation has no per-connection subscription. SAML/SCIM services or bundles, if selected, need separate research and terms.

facts.label: Builder seats and projects
facts.value: Not applicable: no vendor Security dashboard seats, hosted projects, app/environment quota or domain-overage bill.

facts.label: Email delivery
facts.value: Login-link delivery is application code, using Mailer/Notifier or another sender. Reset and verification examples also require the app's mail delivery.

facts.label: SMS and optional factors
facts.value: Core supplies no managed phone-OTP/SMS sending service. Scheb's reviewed factor providers cover TOTP/Google Authenticator/email; extra SMS flows require a separate integration.

facts.label: Hosted over-limit behavior
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted free-user cap, automatic auth subscription upgrade, spending cap or quota-triggered suspension in these libraries.

facts.label: Other package tariffs
facts.value: Not applicable: no core token/request/MFA/audit-log/transaction-fee tariff. Hosting, database, delivery, monitoring and optional commercial services remain outside the software figure.

facts.label: Hosted account eligibility
facts.value: Not applicable to the embedded library: there is no Symfony Security production tenant or hosted seller-account opening process.

facts.label: Trial, card and self-service signup
facts.value: Not applicable: public Composer installation replaces a hosted authentication trial, card check or sales approval.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: embedded PHP library/framework module: authentication, user loading, password hashing, sessions, authorization and integration hooks; runs inside your application.

facts.label: Separate pieces
facts.value: SecurityBundle integrates the framework; Security Core supplies users/tokens/authorization, Security HTTP supplies request authenticators and sessions, and CSRF/PasswordHasher are separate dependencies.

facts.label: Who operates accounts
facts.value: Developer operates the PHP app, user store, sessions, signing secrets, caches, mail integration, deployments, patches and backups, or selects providers to do that work.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: built_in: form login with user identifier/password, JSON credential login and HTTP Basic, configured per firewall.

facts.label: Passwordless login links
facts.value: built_in login_link authenticator; signed URLs, default lifetime 600 seconds, configurable. App supplies link-request endpoint, recipient lookup and delivery.

facts.label: Other built-in authentication
facts.value: built_in access-token authentication, X.509 client certificates and REMOTE_USER integration; custom authenticators extend the pipeline.

facts.label: Email code, phone code, wallet and guests
facts.value: No core first-factor email/phone OTP, wallet-signature login or stored anonymous-account lifecycle in the reviewed released authenticator inventory; custom_code or another package/service is needed.

facts.label: Social-login integration
facts.value: plugin: KnpUOAuth2ClientBundle v2.20.2, with a separately installed league/oauth2-client provider adapter and provider app credentials; MIT bundle.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: The bundle's supported-client list names Google, GitHub and Facebook, plus Apple, Microsoft, Azure, GitLab, LinkedIn, Discord and others through listed adapter packages.

facts.label: Passkeys and security keys
facts.value: plugin: web-auth/webauthn-symfony-bundle 5.3.12 and webauthn-lib; WebAuthn registration/assertion verification and Symfony authenticator integration. Not core SecurityBundle.

facts.label: Passkey UI and autofill
facts.value: Current official bundle guide shows a developer-written controller, authenticator and Twig/Stimulus login form with useBrowserAutofill:true and autocomplete='username webauthn'.

facts.label: Usernameless login and recovery
facts.value: Plugin docs require resident credentials, user verification and an empty allowed-credential list for usernameless authentication; they advise username-based fallback on failure.

facts.label: Passkey domain binding
facts.value: Plugin relying-party ID is a domain, defaulting to the current domain when unset; a configured common parent can cover intended subdomains. It must not contain scheme, port or path.

facts.label: TOTP and email MFA
facts.value: plugin: SchebTwoFactorBundle v8.7.0 integrates TOTP, Google Authenticator and email second-factor providers via their separate scheb/2fa-* packages.

facts.label: Recovery codes
facts.value: plugin: scheb/2fa-backup-code adds single-use backup-code checks. App implements the backup-code interface and generates, stores, presents and regenerates codes.

facts.label: MFA enforcement and token boundaries
facts.value: Scheb inserts an intermediate two-factor state and withholds ordinary roles until completion. Configure protected firewall paths and compatible security token classes.

facts.label: Registration and email confirmation
facts.value: custom_code/scaffold plus plugin: MakerBundle's make:registration-form can use SymfonyCasts VerifyEmailBundle 1.18.0; app stores the user and verification flag and sends the signed confirmation link.

facts.label: Verification expiry and cross-device flow
facts.value: VerifyEmailBundle 1.18.0 default link lifetime is 3600 seconds. Its guide shows optional anonymous validation with a user identifier so a link can be opened on another device.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: plugin: SymfonyCasts ResetPasswordBundle 1.26.1, commonly scaffolded with make:reset-password. Requires a reset-request repository and application mail/controller/templates.

facts.label: Reset lifetime and throttling
facts.value: ResetPasswordBundle 1.26.1 defaults: lifetime 3600 seconds; throttle_limit 3600 seconds; automatic expired-request garbage collection enabled.

facts.label: Address changes, phone verification and deletion
facts.value: custom_code: application changes/validates profile addresses, implements any phone verification and deletes accounts. Core's UserInterface does not supply a self-service account lifecycle API.

facts.label: Browser sessions and expiry
facts.value: Stateful firewalls serialize the security user into the app's session and refresh it from its provider. Session cookie lifetime and server cleanup/TTL are separately configurable; unset values rely on PHP configuration.

facts.label: Session cookies and login rotation
facts.value: Framework session cookie HttpOnly defaults true and SameSite defaults lax. Secure-cookie behavior is configured. SecurityBundle defaults session_fixation_strategy to MIGRATE, rotating the session ID at authentication.

facts.label: Remember-me duration
facts.value: Opt-in remember_me signed cookie; published default lifetime is 31536000 seconds (one year). The user's password is the default signature property.

facts.label: Logout and revocation
facts.value: Configured logout invalidates the session by default. Stateful user refresh logs out a user when compared identifier/password/salt changes, subject to custom EquatableInterface behavior.

facts.label: API token expiry and refresh
facts.value: Access-token authenticators consume tokens; handlers must verify their validity, signature, expiry and revocation as applicable. Token issuance, refresh policy and device-token management belong to the chosen implementation/provider.

facts.label: Stable OIDC token consumer
facts.value: Symfony 8.1 access_token supports OIDC userinfo validation via HttpClient and OIDC token validation via web-token/jwt-library, with configured issuer/audience/keys/discovery.

facts.label: CAS and SAML roles
facts.value: Stable docs include a CAS 2.0 validation handler. No built-in SAML service-provider or SAML identity-provider flow, OAuth authorization server or OIDC issuer was established in the released core inventory.

facts.label: OIDC browser login preview
facts.value: preview: oidc_login authorization-code browser authenticator is introduced in Symfony 8.2 development docs, including PKCE and ID-token verification; not assigned to stable 8.1.

facts.label: Roles and customer workspaces
facts.value: built_in role checks, role hierarchy, access_control and custom voters; customer workspaces, scoped membership/invites and customer administration require app models/logic.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: No built-in SCIM Users/Groups service or automatic directory offboarding in the reviewed released core; custom_code or a separate provider/bundle is needed.

facts.label: Login and account screens
facts.value: MakerBundle can generate a form-login controller/template; core also documents JSON/headless authentication. Registration/reset screens require separate scaffolding/packages or custom UI.

facts.label: Branding and custom domains
facts.value: Application controls its own routes, Twig/other frontend templates and domain. No SecurityBundle branding-removal tier or hosted custom-domain subscription.

facts.label: Translation catalogues
facts.value: Security Core v8.1.11 ships 58 security.*.xlf locale catalogues, including en, fr, de, es, ja, ar, zh_CN and zh_TW; app templates/messages can use Symfony translation services.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No product-specific WCAG conformance report, VPAT or independently assessed accessibility statement found for Symfony Security's generated login/account experience.

facts.label: Current stable PHP requirement
facts.value: Conflict: Symfony 8.1 release overview says PHP >=8.4.0; SecurityBundle, Security Core and Security HTTP v8.1.11 composer.json require PHP >=8.4.1.

facts.label: Framework and standalone integration
facts.value: SecurityBundle targets Symfony applications. Security Core/HTTP are Composer PHP components with declared Symfony/PSR dependencies; user/authenticator/voter interfaces support custom PHP integration.

facts.label: Maintained older runtime lines
facts.value: Official release pages: Symfony 7.4 LTS, current patch 7.4.23, PHP >=8.2.0; Symfony 6.4 LTS, current patch 6.4.50, PHP >=8.1.0.

facts.label: Mobile/API integration path
facts.value: JSON credential requests and bearer access-token authentication can serve an app-written HTTP API. Browser sessions and external identity-provider flows are separately configured.

facts.label: Named native SDK evidence
facts.value: No Symfony Security-maintained iOS, Android, React Native or Flutter SDK and native passkey compatibility matrix found in the reviewed guide, component inventories or WebAuthn integration docs.

facts.label: User storage prerequisites
facts.value: Entity provider uses the application's Doctrine database; other documented providers use LDAP, configuration memory or a chain; custom providers can use another store.

facts.label: PHP and package dependencies
facts.value: SecurityBundle v8.1.11 requires PHP >=8.4.1, composer-runtime-api >=2.1, ext-xml and declared Security/PasswordHasher/HTTP/Foundation/EventDispatcher/DI dependencies.

facts.label: Sessions, rate limits and link cache
facts.value: App supplies its configured session backend and shared storage as needed. Login throttling uses cache.rate_limiter by default; capped login-link reuse needs a cache.

facts.label: External providers and delivery
facts.value: Social login needs provider credentials and adapters; OIDC/CAS token handlers need HttpClient, and OIDC token verification additionally needs web-token/jwt-library. Email flows need app delivery.

facts.label: Deployment responsibilities
facts.value: Deploy the Symfony application: install production dependencies, configure secrets, run relevant database migrations, compile assets when needed and clear/warm cache. Official guide covers multiple deployment approaches.

facts.label: Upgrade guidance
facts.value: Official major-upgrade guide recommends removing deprecations, updating Composer constraints and adapting code to changed APIs. Release-line maintenance windows determine patch support.

facts.label: Backups, restore and capacity
facts.value: No SecurityBundle-specific complete backup/restore runbook or hardware/RPS sizing guarantee found in the deployment, provider, session or released configuration material.

facts.label: Custom users and login logic
facts.value: custom_code extension points: UserInterface/user providers, authenticators with Passport/UserBadge/credentials/badges, user checkers and authorization voters; extra user fields belong to the app model.

facts.label: Authentication events
facts.value: Synchronous event subscribers/listeners can handle CheckPassportEvent, AuthenticationSuccessEvent, LoginSuccessEvent, LoginFailureEvent, InteractiveLoginEvent and LogoutEvent; firewalls have their own dispatcher.

facts.label: Creating, searching and deleting users
facts.value: Application repositories/services implement CRUD and search for the chosen user store. Security user providers retrieve/refresh users; they are not a vendor management REST API or admin dashboard.

facts.label: Banning and account checks
facts.value: custom user checkers can reject disabled, expired or otherwise invalid accounts before/after authentication, using application-defined flags and exceptions.

facts.label: User impersonation
facts.value: built_in opt-in switch_user; default permission ROLE_ALLOWED_TO_SWITCH, configurable voter, _switch_user parameter and _exit return. IS_IMPERSONATOR can identify the impersonated state.

facts.label: Social linking and unlinking
facts.value: custom_code: KnpU's example looks up an external provider ID and associates it with an app user. Core does not manage a universal linked-identity table or safe unlinking/reconfirmation UI.

facts.label: Guest-to-registered upgrade
facts.value: No stored anonymous-user creation/upgrade workflow in the reviewed core. Preserve or merge guest application data through custom code when creating/authenticating a registered account.

facts.label: Login throttling
facts.value: built_in integration, opt-in via login_throttling and the symfony/rate-limiter component. Defaults when enabled: 5 failed attempts per minute for identifier+IP and 5 times that allowance per IP.

facts.label: CSRF and session protections
facts.value: Symfony has CSRF support, but a manual form-login example requires explicit enable_csrf and matching token submission. Session ID migration is the default authentication strategy.

facts.label: Compromised-password validation
facts.value: Optional Symfony Validator NotCompromisedPassword constraint checks Have I Been Pwned using a SHA-1 prefix, not the raw password. Default threshold 1; skipOnError defaults false.

facts.label: Magic-link abuse and tenant binding
facts.value: Configure trusted hosts, rate-limit link requests and choose unique signature properties. Login-link hashes do not include host/firewall by default; add tenant-specific properties where relevant.

facts.label: Login limit and recovery semantics
facts.value: When enabled with default settings: 5 attempts/minute per normalized identifier+IP and 25/minute per IP (our calculation: 5×5). Successful login clears the local limiter, while the IP-wide limiter remains.

facts.label: Management/API throughput
facts.value: No universal core requests/second, concurrent-login or management-endpoint quota published in reviewed configuration, rate-limiter source and deployment docs.

facts.label: Audit events and export route
facts.value: Security events can be subscribed to and written to app-owned logs/storage; Symfony supports PSR-3 logging and optional Monolog handlers for chosen destinations.

facts.label: Retention and delivery guarantees
facts.value: No fixed managed audit-retention days or guaranteed webhook/export/retry window found for this library; logging destinations/rotation are app configuration.

facts.label: Profiles, IDs and password hashes on exit
facts.value: App owns its user model/provider and backing store; exporting profiles, identifiers, roles and stored password hashes is an application/database task rather than a vendor export ticket or fee.

facts.label: External links, sessions and factor data
facts.value: Export provider links and optional MFA/passkey records from their actual application/bundle storage. A copy of core user data alone does not establish portable external tokens, active sessions or usable passkeys.

facts.label: Password hash migration
facts.value: built_in PasswordHasher supports legacy-hash migration via migrate_from and PasswordUpgraderInterface. Successful password authentication can rehash and persist a stronger current hash.

facts.label: Import path and limits
facts.value: Application imports its user records/IDs/roles and provider associations into its chosen schema, or supplies a custom provider/hasher. No universal hosted bulk-import endpoint or row quota.

facts.label: Account deletion and session cleanup
facts.value: Application removes user records and related credentials through its storage/provider logic; it should also invalidate relevant sessions, remember-me tokens, reset requests and optional factor/link records.

facts.label: Data/log/backup retention
facts.value: No fixed SecurityBundle user-deletion SLA, deleted-user backup retention or universal security-log retention period found in the deployment, session, logging or privacy sources reviewed.

facts.label: Residency for app data
facts.value: Developer chooses where the PHP app, user database, sessions, caches, logs and backups run; no Symfony-hosted authentication region menu applies.

facts.label: Privacy and service-policy scope
facts.value: Public Symfony SAS privacy policy covers named Symfony websites/services. SymfonyInsight terms cover that separate hosted code-analysis service. Core software use is governed by its MIT licence.

facts.label: DPA and independent assessment for this module
facts.value: No module-specific hosted-processing DPA, subprocessor roster or public SOC 2/ISO assurance report established for the app-operated SecurityBundle deployment in the reviewed sources.

facts.label: Name and project
facts.value: Symfony Security: the Symfony framework's authentication and authorization libraries, integrated by symfony/security-bundle; main project Symfony.

facts.label: Company and policy identity
facts.value: Symfony SAS is the company named by Symfony's website privacy policy, in France; Symfony is the project name and trademark.

facts.label: Lifecycle and start path
facts.value: Maintained, public Composer installation. Official stable line is Symfony 8.1; checked patch 8.1.11. Main repository is neither archived nor disabled.

facts.label: Deprecated name and preview boundary
facts.value: The old symfony/security umbrella package is explicitly deprecated because it was split into smaller packages. Symfony 8.2 is under development, separate from current stable 8.1.

facts.label: Core software licences
facts.value: SecurityBundle, Security Core and Security HTTP v8.1.11 use MIT: commercial use, changes, distribution, sublicensing and sale permitted with notice retention; supplied without warranty.

facts.label: Social-login and MFA bundle licences
facts.value: KnpUOAuth2ClientBundle v2.20.2 and SchebTwoFactorBundle v8.7.0 use MIT.

facts.label: Passkey, reset and verification licences
facts.value: web-auth/webauthn-symfony-bundle 5.3.12, SymfonyCasts ResetPasswordBundle 1.26.1 and VerifyEmailBundle 1.18.0 use MIT.

facts.label: Documentation and trademarks
facts.value: Symfony code uses MIT; website/documentation content uses CC BY-SA 3.0; the Symfony trademark has separate ownership and use rules.

facts.label: Hosted status and uptime SLA
facts.value: Not applicable: embedded SecurityBundle has no Symfony-operated production auth endpoint whose availability is covered by a hosted status page/SLA.

facts.label: Stable release evidence
facts.value: Symfony 8.1.11 is the checked current stable patch; official release announcement dated November 5, 2026, with package versions independently shown in publisher metadata.

facts.label: 8.1 maintenance window
facts.value: Symfony 8.1 first released May 2026; maintained, end of support January 2027.

facts.label: Long-term support windows
facts.value: 7.4 LTS: bugs through November 2028, security through November 2029. 6.4 LTS: bugs through November 2026, security through November 2027.

facts.label: Latest-release metadata conflict
facts.value: GitHub /releases/latest returns tag v8.2.0-BETA1, published 2026-11-04T12:41:17Z, but marks prerelease:false; Symfony's release pages call 8.2 under development and 8.1 current stable.

facts.label: Security handling policy
facts.value: Core policy routes vulnerability reports privately to security@symfony.com and describes triage, patching maintained versions, coordinated release and CVE publication.

facts.label: Community and professional support
facts.value: Official support page directs open-source questions to GitHub Discussions and Symfony Slack; professional consulting/training/technical assistance is offered by SensioLabs.

facts.label: Response times and prices
facts.value: No guaranteed ordinary SecurityBundle community-response hours, service-level target or fixed package-support tariff found on the official support/security/deployment pages.

facts.label: Standard billable unit
facts.value: USD 0.05 per successful verification plus channel fees; ordinary OTP success means correct code approved by Verify.

facts.label: Custom-code billing exception
facts.value: When customer creates and validates its own passcodes, verification fee is charged per created verification attempt.

facts.label: Failed-check and delivery distinction
facts.value: Failed, expired, incorrect and uncompleted normal verifications have no USD 0.05 success fee; underlying delivery attempts may still cost money.

facts.label: Trial and post-upgrade free units
facts.value: 40 Verify trial units; another 40 free Verify units after upgrade, shared at parent-account level.

facts.label: Ongoing free production allowance
facts.value: No recurring free monthly Verify production allowance published in current pricing/trial pages.

facts.label: Minimum paid model
facts.value: Public pay-as-you-go usage pricing; custom volume/committed-use contracts available separately. No fixed monthly Verify subscription stated.

facts.label: Initial funding requirement
facts.value: Exact current minimum payment/deposit at upgrade could not be verified from the public upgrade article.

facts.label: Pay-as-you-go formula
facts.value: Normal OTP: USD 0.05 × approved verifications + billable channel usage + applicable carrier/related charges and taxes.

facts.label: Volume/commitment offer
facts.value: Custom prices, typically evaluated at 100,000+ verifications/month or combined messaging thresholds; exact discounts/minimum commitments quote-only.

facts.label: Business comparison scope
facts.value: Both fixed business baselines unsupported by Verify alone: no complete customer organization/invitation/role/SAML account product.

facts.label: Customer-organization limits and fees
facts.value: Not applicable to Verify's verification resources.

facts.label: Customer SSO/SCIM connection fees
facts.value: Not applicable to this add-on; no Verify customer SAML/OIDC/SCIM connection product to price.

facts.label: Developer dashboard users and roles
facts.value: Twilio organization/account invitations and staff roles include Administrator, Billing Manager, Developer and Support.

facts.label: Builder seat/project/environment caps
facts.value: No Verify-specific numeric dashboard-seat, Service-count, environment or custom-domain allowance/overage schedule found.

facts.label: US SMS delivery
facts.value: United States destination, outbound SMS: USD 0.0083 per segment, in addition to USD 0.05 per successful Verify check.

facts.label: US AT&T carrier surcharge
facts.value: US outbound SMS to AT&T: USD 0.0035 per segment for listed long-code, toll-free and short-code routes, extra to base message pricing.

facts.label: US T-Mobile carrier surcharge
facts.value: US outbound SMS to T-Mobile: USD 0.0045 per segment for listed long-code, toll-free and short-code routes, extra to base message pricing.

facts.label: US WhatsApp price conflict
facts.value: US authentication-template delivery: channel table USD 0.0034/message; FAQ USD 0.0147/message, each plus USD 0.05 per successful verification.

facts.label: US Voice channel costs
facts.value: US/Canada outbound local or toll-free Voice calls: published linked rate USD 0.0140/minute; Alaska USD 0.0945/minute; Verify success fee extra.

facts.label: Email channel dependency
facts.value: Verify email requires Twilio SendGrid integration, verified From address, API key and dynamic template; each Verify Service has one email integration.

facts.label: Email provider plan prices
facts.value: SendGrid Email API, US-site USD rate card, not destination-country-priced: Essentials starts USD 19.95/month; Pro USD 89.95/month; Premier custom.

facts.label: Push/Silent Device Approval
facts.value: No destination-country delivery rate: channel fee included in Verify fee; billed when request is approved OR denied.

facts.label: TOTP
facts.value: No destination-country delivery fee: channel fee included in Verify fee; billed when request is approved.

facts.label: Silent Network Auth
facts.value: Per-country channel fee, sales-quoted, plus USD 0.05 successful-check fee; no public country dollar table found.

facts.label: Trial cap/expiry
facts.value: 30-day trial expiry and finite channel/verification unit pools restrict continued use until upgrade.

facts.label: Prepaid balance and payment failure
facts.value: Twilio may suspend services across the account for insufficient prepaid balance or payment-method failure.

facts.label: Spending cap precision
facts.value: Pricing mentions spending caps, balance alerts and usage monitoring; exact Verify-wide hard-cap coverage/overshoot behavior not established.

facts.label: Optional paid extras
facts.value: Lookup prescreening, dedicated numbers/short codes and premium support may add charges; managed number pool is included in standard Verify.

facts.label: Taxes and communications surcharges
facts.value: Published fees exclude taxes and applicable communications/carrier surcharges; these can appear as extra invoice items.

facts.label: General SMS failed-processing fee applicability
facts.value: US Programmable Messaging page lists USD 0.001 per Failed message, but a separate Verify application of that fee was not established.

facts.label: Destination and consent restrictions
facts.value: Country/channel restrictions apply; generic managed senders do not remove local requirements. China template registration and Singapore/Canada restrictions are linked.

facts.label: Solo-builder and seller-country eligibility
facts.value: No complete public Verify-specific seller-country/individual-eligibility matrix found in the pages checked.

facts.label: Self-service trial
facts.value: 30-day trial, no credit card; email and phone verification and account information required.

facts.label: Trial recipients and channels
facts.value: Console trial supports SMS/Voice to up to 5 verified phone numbers; API trial also permits testing additional factors including Push/TOTP.

facts.label: Production activation
facts.value: Upgrade and approved Primary Customer Profile (PCP) required to send SMS/Voice OTPs to unverified recipients.

facts.label: Product type and coverage
facts.value: Hosted verification add-on. Checks possession of a phone, email or device; app owns account storage and the action taken after approval.

facts.label: Hosted operator and customer responsibility
facts.value: Twilio operates Verify. Builder operates its app, user-to-Entity mapping, authorization and sessions, and connects optional channel dependencies.

facts.label: Contracting entity depends on country
facts.value: US customers generally contract with Twilio Inc.; EEA/UK customers with Twilio Ireland Limited. Other country-specific entities/rules exist.

facts.label: Phone and email one-time codes
facts.value: Built-in hosted verification through SMS, Voice, WhatsApp and email; SNA verifies phone possession without typing an OTP.

facts.label: Full account login methods
facts.value: Password storage/login, anonymous accounts, wallet-account login and email-link account sessions are outside Verify's add-on scope.

facts.label: Social provider catalogue
facts.value: Not applicable: Verify is not the app's Google/Apple/GitHub/Microsoft OAuth sign-in provider catalogue.

facts.label: Passkey capability and gate
facts.value: Private beta/pilot; supports registration, public-key storage and authentication flows; early-access iOS/Android SDKs.

facts.label: Passkey commercial/platform details
facts.value: Stable unit price, browser conditional-autofill support matrix and cross-domain migration guarantees not published in the public overview/pricing checked.

facts.label: MFA factors and device control
facts.value: TOTP plus Push/Silent Device Approval; SMS/Voice/email can be used as additional checks. Builder decides enforcement in its login flow.

facts.label: TOTP recovery/re-enrollment boundary
facts.value: App owns identity mapping and recovery workflow. TOTP docs recommend deleting the old seed when issuing a new one.

facts.label: Verification/reset use cases
facts.value: Message templates explicitly support account validation and password-reset use cases; Verify supplies the check, not the password-change/account-deletion transaction.

facts.label: Sessions and sign-out
facts.value: Not applicable to whole-app sessions, refresh tokens, cookies and lost-device sign-out; these are supplied by the consuming app.

facts.label: Business login protocol roles
facts.value: Not applicable: no Verify SAML identity-provider, OIDC issuer or enterprise-login broker is being offered.

facts.label: Customer workspaces, invitations and roles
facts.value: Not applicable to Verify's verification-only resources; app supplies business workspaces and authorization.

facts.label: Customer SCIM provisioning
facts.value: Not applicable to this verification add-on.

facts.label: Ready-made account UI
facts.value: Headless API, quickstarts and sample apps; builder supplies production signup/login/profile screens and session handling.

facts.label: Message branding
facts.value: Service friendly name and template choices; custom company-name override requires Sales enablement and is limited to 30 characters.

facts.label: Domains and custom message content
facts.value: Custom templates can carry domain-bound SMS/WebOTP codes; customer-submitted custom templates are approved case by case.

facts.label: Localization
facts.value: Locale/country-code selection and explicit locale overrides; language availability differs by template and channel. English/Spanish SMS example documented.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Verify-specific public accessibility conformance report established in the API, quickstart, template and language pages checked.

facts.label: Web/runtime integration
facts.value: HTTPS REST API and official helper examples for Node.js, Python, C#/.NET, Java, Go, PHP and Ruby; API-key secret remains server-side.

facts.label: Native Push clients
facts.value: Official iOS and Android Verify Push SDKs; React Native wrapper is linked by Twilio's Verify documentation.

facts.label: iOS compatibility and device storage
facts.value: iOS Push README: iOS 12+, Swift 5.2, Xcode 16.3+; APNs registration needed for push notifications.

facts.label: App and channel prerequisites
facts.value: Twilio account, Verify Service and protected backend credentials; app user store/mapping. Email adds SendGrid, Push notifications add APNs/FCM configuration.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: Not applicable: no self-hosted Verify server edition documented for this hosted API.

facts.label: Custom verification logic
facts.value: Customer-generated OTPs supported after service configuration; app must report verification feedback/status to Twilio.

facts.label: Events and extensions
facts.value: Self-service Verify Events through Twilio Event Streams to webhooks or Amazon Kinesis; no additional Verify charge.

facts.label: Hosted administration
facts.value: Console/API create, list, update and delete Verify Services; Console searches verifications by ID/destination and filters channel/status/country/time.

facts.label: Verification identities and factors
facts.value: Entity and Factor APIs support verification-identity/factor administration; identity should be an immutable non-PII external ID, 8–64 characters.

facts.label: Factor linking versus account linking
facts.value: An Entity can have multiple Factors; app decides which factor/user mapping to use. Whole-account social merging and guest upgrades are outside Verify.

facts.label: SMS pumping protection
facts.value: Verify Fraud Guard is configurable, SMS-only, with Basic/Standard/Max protection; Standard is the documented default protection level.

facts.label: Geographic and customer rate controls
facts.value: Geo Permissions can disable/allow country/channel traffic; Safe List bypasses relevant blocks. Service Rate Limits can meter customer-supplied identifiers.

facts.label: OTP send/check limits
facts.value: Five send attempts per destination within 10 minutes documented; five code-check attempts before waiting for expiry/new verification.

facts.label: Verification status polling
facts.value: Maximum 60 status requests/minute, 180/hour and 250/day.

facts.label: Reporting and configurable limits
facts.value: Verification Attempts API: 100 requests/minute, HTTP 429 at limit. Service Rate Limit buckets define customer-selected max requests/seconds.

facts.label: Logs, history and export
facts.value: Console verification/blocked-request logs; Attempts API lists last 30 days of SMS/Voice/WhatsApp/RBM/email attempts, including conversion/price details.

facts.label: Delivery-status stream conflict
facts.value: General Verify Events guide describes message delivery/status streaming; current deprecation notices say Attempt DLR events/status updates were stopped.

facts.label: Verification-log export
facts.value: Console CSV export of up to 9,000 Verify logs per export, including blocked-verification logs.

facts.label: Credential portability limits
facts.value: TOTP Factor binding/secret is returned only at creation and never afterward; no later bulk secret export through normal Factor fetch.

facts.label: Identity migration into Verify
facts.value: App chooses an external immutable Entity identity; existing account IDs can be mapped without creating a new account store in Verify.

facts.label: TOTP seed import
facts.value: Factor creation accepts a Base32 binding.secret; otherwise a secret is generated. Timing, code length, skew and algorithm are configurable.

facts.label: Verification resource lifetime
facts.value: Default OTP validity 10 minutes; Support may change to 2 minutes–24 hours. Verification resource deletion/expiry is distinct from retained logs.

facts.label: Entity/factor deletion
facts.value: Entity DELETE endpoint exists; individual factor deletion is documented. Customer must also delete its external mapping/account data.

facts.label: Provider retention and account closure
facts.value: Twilio retention article: remaining Customer Content deleted 30 days after closure; Customer Account Data generally 60 days, subject to exceptions.

facts.label: Complete Verify backup/deletion schedule
facts.value: Exact Verify-specific backup purge interval and all data-category deletion deadlines not found in public pages checked.

facts.label: SNA regional processing
facts.value: Silent Network Auth supports US1 (US, default) and IE1 (Ireland); region-specific credentials and Services required.

facts.label: Residency limitations
facts.value: Twilio explicitly does not guarantee all data remains in selected region; account billing and usage records are globally shared.

facts.label: Processing agreement
facts.value: Public DPA defines processing roles, instructions, transfer safeguards and return/deletion terms; some account/usage processing has distinct purposes.

facts.label: Subprocessors and telecom boundary
facts.value: Public named subprocessor list with service/location information, last updated September 2026; telecom providers are not treated as Twilio subprocessors.

facts.label: Independent assurance claims
facts.value: Twilio Security Overview claims SOC 2 Type 2 for all Services and ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018 for Twilio Services; Trust Center provides documentation.

facts.label: Product and official URLs
facts.value: Twilio Verify; product of Twilio; Verify v2 documentation and API are the current integration surface.

facts.label: Related acquisition, not a Verify rename
facts.value: Twilio completed its acquisition of Stytch on 2025-11-14; Stytch remains a separately branded product.

facts.label: Lifecycle and predecessor
facts.value: Verify v2 is recommended for new work. Verify v1 is closed to new customers; Authy API is closed to new customers and scheduled for full deprecation.

facts.label: Channel maturity differs
facts.value: Passkeys: private beta. Silent Network Auth: beta and carrier onboarding. Core OTP methods remain publicly documented.

facts.label: Hosted service/commercial-use terms
facts.value: Commercial service under Twilio Terms of Service; may be incorporated into the customer's end-user application, subject to use restrictions.

facts.label: Mobile Push SDK licences
facts.value: Official iOS and Android Verify Push SDKs: Apache-2.0; licence conditions, notices and warranty exclusions apply.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: Public Twilio status page includes a Verify component and subscription route.

facts.label: Standard API availability promise
facts.value: Monthly Twilio Services API SLA threshold 99.95%; eligible breach gives 10% API service credit, subject to claim process/exclusions.

facts.label: Enhanced-edition availability promise
facts.value: 99.99% monthly API threshold during purchased Twilio Enterprise Edition or eligible legacy Administration Edition months; 10% service credit.

facts.label: Hosted maintenance evidence
facts.value: Verify Events GA announcement dated 2026-11-04; Verify v2 is recommended for new integration.

facts.label: Client SDK maintenance evidence
facts.value: iOS Push changelog top entry 3.0.2 dated 2025-12-02; Android Push 0.9.1 dated 2026-03-09.

facts.label: Free support
facts.value: Developer support plan included, web support; no guaranteed response time. Published estimate 3 business days.

facts.label: Production support add-on
facts.value: USD max(250/month, 4% monthly Twilio spend); business-critical guaranteed response 3 business hours.

facts.label: Business support add-on
facts.value: USD max(1,500/month, 6% monthly Twilio spend); business-critical 1 hour, 24/7.

facts.label: Personalized support add-on
facts.value: USD max(5,000/month, 8% monthly Twilio spend); business-critical 1 hour, 24/7; sales route.

facts.label: Email verification and password reset
facts.value: Hosted verify-account and forgot/reset-password screens; tenant email verification can be required, disabled or delayed after signup.

facts.label: ID/access tokens and refresh model
facts.value: Token guide explicitly gives ID tokens a one-hour validity, distinct from the app/login session. Access tokens call UserInfo; new access tokens can be obtained through another authentication flow.

facts.label: Revocation and lost devices
facts.value: Application logout is described as ending the user's hosted sessions; no device/session listing, administrator kill-all API or immediate offline-token revocation policy established.

facts.label: OIDC provider and relying-party roles
facts.value: Auth service acts as OIDC/OAuth provider to the builder's apps, with registered callbacks and signed ID tokens; it also consumes social-provider authentication.

facts.value: Enterprise SAML support is advertised, but operational SAML IdP/SP/broker roles, metadata/setup steps, supported bindings and per-customer isolation are not settled.

facts.label: Tenant isolation and admin API scopes
facts.value: Tenants hold separate account/configuration groups. Global API keys can be restricted by tenant and resource, with None/Read/Write permissions.

facts.label: Customer memberships, invitations and roles
facts.value: No native customer-organization invitation flow, member-role matrix or delegated customer-admin membership API established.

facts.label: Success exception
facts.value: Under Verify Success, Silent Authentication events with Rejected status are also charged as legitimate authentication attempts.

facts.label: Ongoing free production
facts.value: No recurring free production verification allowance found; published EUR 2 credit is a trial.

facts.label: Public paid model
facts.value: Usage-based Verify Conversion; successful-check rate EUR 0.052 or published USD 0.06084 plus channel fees. Enterprise Success/volume offers are sales-quoted.

facts.label: Initial account funding cap
facts.value: New-account funding cap EUR 10 per 24 hours; higher funding and auto-reload activation require approval.

facts.label: Minimum first funding/commitment
facts.value: Exact universal minimum first deposit and any applicable account-specific minimum commitment not established.

facts.label: Conversion price formula
facts.value: EUR 0.052 × successful checks, or USD 0.06084 × successful checks, plus account/destination/channel usage and applicable extras.

facts.label: Success/volume pricing
facts.value: Sales quote required; Success price depends on destination country regardless of workflow channel mix; no public comparable numeric country table established.

facts.label: Business comparison boundary
facts.value: Both business scenarios unsupported by Verify alone: customer account memberships/invitations/roles and SAML connections are external.

facts.label: Customer organization fees/limits
facts.value: Not applicable to this verification add-on.

facts.label: Customer SSO/SCIM fees
facts.value: Not applicable to Verify's offering.

facts.label: Dashboard staff and invitations
facts.value: One primary user with controlled team-member access; up to 10 team-member invitations/day.

facts.label: Accounts and environments
facts.value: Primary/subaccounts separate API configuration, billing and reporting; Subaccounts API restricted/beta, generally partner access, ordinary accounts can request secondary API keys.

facts.label: Total seat/application caps and fees
facts.value: No public Verify-specific total dashboard-seat/application/environment cap or per-seat overage schedule found.

facts.value: Own WABA required; Verify configuration via Sales/account manager. Channel usage fee extra under Conversion; exact US authentication-message all-in rate not established.

facts.label: Exact Verify delivery/carrier rate mapping
facts.value: Exact US Verify SMS/TTS/WhatsApp/email/Silent Authentication account rates and managed-route carrier-fee inclusion not found in accessible public material.

facts.label: Credit exhaustion and monitoring
facts.value: At zero prepaid balance APIs stop; virtual numbers may be cancelled. Balance notifications and auto-reload exist; credit facilities change available funds.

facts.label: Abuse limits and failover costs
facts.value: Fraud network blocks can become permanent; custom-code requests must call check or unnecessary failover sends may accrue channel costs.

facts.label: Redaction and audit extras
facts.value: Technical docs: Redact API free, Auto-redact paid. Messages page lists Auto-redact USD 1,100/month and Audit API USD 550/month.

facts.label: Redact naming conflict
facts.value: RCS rate card labels USD 1,100/month 'Vonage Redact API'; technical guide says Redact API free and automatic redaction paid.

facts.label: Taxes and suspension
facts.value: Applicable non-US sales/indirect taxes depend on service address; tax/recurring charges can be deducted after invoicing and cause suspension if funds are insufficient.

facts.label: Signup-country restrictions
facts.value: Published restrictions include Cuba, Crimea, North Korea, Sudan, Iran, Syria, Russia, Belarus; specified occupied Ukrainian regions; China, Hong Kong and Macau.

facts.label: Verification destination restrictions
facts.value: Published high-risk destination list is blocked by default, including Afghanistan, Albania, Algeria and many others; managed high-volume customers may request review.

facts.label: Number and individual eligibility
facts.value: v2 also blocks Vonage Long Virtual Numbers; business information is requested at signup and proof of registration may be needed for larger funding.

facts.label: Self-service entry and trial
facts.value: Public account creation and Verify getting-started guide; free credit, no credit card required to begin.

facts.label: Trial credit and recipient rules
facts.value: EUR 2 test credit; account-support article permits registered number plus 4 verified test numbers for SMS; Voice restricted to registered number.

facts.label: Trial recipient-limit conflict
facts.value: Account trial article says4 additional test numbers; Messages getting-started guide says up to 10 destination numbers in DEMO mode.

facts.label: Product type and verification scope
facts.value: Hosted verification add-on for OTP/contact-possession, second-factor and step-up checks; SMS, Voice, Email, WhatsApp, RCS and Silent Authentication workflows.

facts.label: Boundary with the app
facts.value: Vonage generates/delivers/checks a code and request ID; builder binds it to the right user/session, authorizes account actions and stores app users.

facts.label: Who operates what
facts.value: Vonage runs verification delivery/checking infrastructure. Customer runs backend, user database, session state and secure callback handlers.

facts.label: Phone/email OTP methods
facts.value: Built-in hosted SMS, Voice, WhatsApp, RCS and email OTP workflows; Silent Authentication uses carrier verification without a typed code.

facts.label: Full-account methods
facts.value: Password account storage, email-link sessions, anonymous accounts and wallet-account management are outside this add-on's documented scope.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: External/custom implementation: official tutorial combines app-owned WebAuthn passkeys with Verify Silent Authentication for signup/recovery.

facts.label: Social providers
facts.value: Not applicable: Verify is not a Google/Apple/GitHub/Microsoft social-login provider catalogue.

facts.label: MFA and recovery responsibility
facts.value: OTP and SIM checks can be second-factor or step-up components. App controls enforcement, trusted recovery and account/session binding.

facts.label: Contact verification and account actions
facts.value: Phone/email confirmation provided by start/check workflow. App must authorize and implement password resets, contact changes and app-user deletion.

facts.label: Sessions and revocation
facts.value: Not applicable to whole-app signed-in sessions, refresh tokens, cookies or lost-device sign-out.

facts.label: Enterprise login protocol roles
facts.value: Not applicable: Verify is not the app's SAML IdP, OIDC issuer/client directory or enterprise SSO broker.

facts.label: Customer workspaces and roles
facts.value: Not applicable to Verify's verification request model.

facts.label: SCIM provisioning
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer-account provisioning/directory product to assess within Verify.

facts.label: Production user interfaces
facts.value: Headless API with code snippets/getting-started guide; Dashboard has a browser verification sandbox for builders.

facts.label: Brand and custom templates
facts.value: brand length 1–18; SMS/Voice/RCS custom-template management requires account write enablement via Support; up to 10 custom templates/account.

facts.label: RCS sender branding
facts.value: Default Agent sender name fixed to Vonage Verify; brand appears in message body. Own branded agent can be registered separately.

facts.label: Email domain setup
facts.value: Custom email sender domain available through support onboarding for managed and unmanaged accounts.

facts.label: Message localization
facts.value: Channel-specific locale table; English US/UK, French, German, Spanish, Hindi and other locales documented. Some languages require custom templates.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: No Verify-specific public accessibility conformance report found in product, getting-started, template/language and support pages checked.

facts.label: Server runtimes and SDKs
facts.value: HTTPS REST, Basic auth or JWT; official server SDK index lists Node.js, Python, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP and .NET.

facts.label: Native Silent Authentication clients
facts.value: Official cellular client libraries for iOS13+ and Android; force cellular requests even when Wi-Fi is active. Standard Silent Authentication needs mobile data.

facts.label: Advanced client restrictions
facts.value: Silent Authentication Advanced alpha currently Android-only; Android SDK requires Android14/API34+ and compatible TS.43 SIM/carrier.

facts.label: Required services and secure setup
facts.value: Vonage account/credit, backend and Verify-capable Application/key pair for JWT; public webhook endpoint for async flows. App supplies account/session database.

facts.label: Self-host operations
facts.value: Not applicable: hosted Verify API has no self-hosted server edition established in its deployment docs.

facts.label: Workflow and custom code
facts.value: Up to3 workflow actions; custom alphanumeric code4–10 chars supported only on Verify Conversion. Customer must submit correct code to check endpoint.

facts.label: Webhooks and reliability
facts.value: Signed webhooks by default; summary callback per finished workflow, event callbacks per channel attempt with account-level enablement (standard Silent Auth sends them by default).

facts.label: Verification administration
facts.value: API starts/checks requests, cancels active workflow and moves to next step; Dashboard logs/analytics support investigation.

facts.label: App-user administration
facts.value: Not applicable to creating, banning, impersonating or deleting whole app user accounts.

facts.label: Account linking and guests
facts.value: Not applicable to whole-account social linking or guest-to-registered upgrades.

facts.label: Network anti-fraud controls
facts.value: Verify network blocks affect SMS/Voice for an API key; temporary blocks may become permanent; network-unblock features require enablement.

facts.label: Customer application protection
facts.value: Customer must bind request ID to user/session, apply phone/user/IP rate limits, validate webhook signatures and control code-check lifecycle.

facts.label: Account throughput
facts.value: Standard account Verify v1/v2 requests up to30 requests/second; higher throughput subject to account-manager review.

facts.label: Per-request checking/concurrency
facts.value: OTP PIN can be retried at most3times; Silent Authentication check allows1submission. Concurrent verifications to same number rejected.

facts.label: Timeouts by model/channel
facts.value: Conversion channel_timeout15–900 seconds, default180; Success minimum60 seconds; Silent Authentication fixed60 seconds regardless of pricing model.

facts.label: Logs and retrieval window
facts.value: Verify Logs searches up to30 days; older records through Reports API. v2/email/Silent Auth records separate from SMS/Voice/Messages logs.

facts.label: Security/event streaming
facts.value: Signed event/summary callbacks supply outcomes; account-level Audit API is a separate paid administrative-event product.

facts.label: History/report export
facts.value: Dashboard analytics downloads Excel; Reports API supports individual JSON records and bulk CSV reporting across older histories.

facts.label: Exit boundary
facts.value: No Verify-stored app passwords/social identities to export; app retains its own account store. Migration must replace delivery/approval integration and preserve necessary transaction history.

facts.label: Migration into v2
facts.value: Official v1-to-v2 guide changes endpoints, credentials, request fields and callbacks; legacy Verify Search/PSD2 do not transfer as equivalent features.

facts.label: Verification cancellation versus erasure
facts.value: Cancelling an active request aborts workflow; it is not documented as deletion of all transaction/log data.

facts.label: Published retention
facts.value: Communications detail records13 months; technical logs up to30 days. Financial records10 years with no personal data per support article.

facts.label: Verify personal-data redaction
facts.value: Redact API supports Verify CDRs; Standard Auto-redact covers destination phone/email and client reference; Advanced can also cover server logs.

facts.label: Account closure/backups
facts.value: Exact current non-Video API account-closure process, post-closure data deadlines and backup-purge schedule not established.

facts.label: Regional endpoints
facts.value: Silent Authentication best practices list api-us.vonage.com, api-eu.vonage.com and api-ap.vonage.com for regional routing/latency.

facts.label: Complete Verify residency guarantee
facts.value: No complete Verify-wide storage/processing/backup residency matrix or priced regional guarantee established.

facts.label: DPA/privacy content access
facts.value: Official legal index links a DPA and Privacy Policy; substantive current processing/transfer/subprocessor clauses could not be read.

facts.label: Security assurance evidence
facts.value: Vonage publicly claims independently assessed frameworks across product lines, including ISO27001, PCI-DSS, SOC, HITRUST and CSA STAR.

facts.label: Identity and current API
facts.value: Vonage Verify; current Verify API v2; legacy Nexmo branding remains in API/dashboard hostnames.

facts.label: Parent-company acquisition
facts.value: Ericsson completed its acquisition of Vonage on 2022-07-21; Vonage continued under its existing name and brand.

facts.label: Lifecycle and legacy migration
facts.value: Verify v2 current; Verify Legacy/v1 deprecated and being sunset. No Verify v2 shutdown found in lifecycle/current docs checked first.

facts.label: Channel maturity
facts.value: Silent Authentication Advanced is alpha; live carrier onboarding ongoing and end-to-end live testing not yet generally possible. Virtual Operator available for development.

facts.label: Hosted service licence/terms
facts.value: Paid hosted service; exact current commercial-use, resale and termination clauses could not be read from the linked terms pages.

facts.label: SDK licences
facts.value: Official Android/iOS cellular client libraries and Python server SDK inspected: Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Status service
facts.value: Public Vonage API Status includes Verify, Verify V2 and region-specific SilentAuth components.

facts.label: Availability promise and limits
facts.value: Premium/Enterprise support offering advertises99.99%platform availability SLA. Exact Verify-specific calculation period, credit remedies and exclusions not established from accessible contract text.

facts.label: Current API/client maintenance evidence
facts.value: v2 recommended in migration docs; SDK index dates Android cellular library release2026-05-12 and iOS2026-03-02.

facts.label: Human activity meter
facts.value: MAU: a distinct user that authenticates or refreshes a token at least once during the monthly billing period.

facts.label: Tenant and machine activity meters
facts.value: MAT: at least one active user or tenant machine; successful external-IdP authentication also activates the tenant without local user provisioning. MAM: OAuth2 client issuing a client_credentials access token that month.

facts.label: Pooling and billing cycle
facts.value: Users, tenants and machines aggregate across all applications in the account. Billing renews on the same day each month; Pro upgrade starts a fresh billing period.

facts.label: Standard free production allowance
facts.value: $0 base includes 5 active tenants, 10,000 active users and 20 active machines per account/month, plus SSO/MFA/RBAC and hosted auth pages.

facts.label: Minimum paid commitment and currency
facts.value: Standard can incur only usage charges above allowances; Pro base is US$39/month. Terms specify U.S. dollars and applicable sales tax added.

facts.label: Renewal, downgrade and refunds
facts.value: Pro subscription charged upfront; usage charged after the period. Downgrade takes effect at paid-period end. Upgrades charged immediately/in full; no refunds or prorating.

facts.label: Premium pricing and commitments
facts.value: Premium base, volume tenant/user discounts and higher support/availability commitments are quote-only.

facts.label: Business comparison result
facts.value: Our calculation: Standard A = US$2.50/month; Standard B = US$47.50/month for required tenants, roles, invitations and SAML. No per-SSO-connection line item is required.

facts.label: Customer organization allowance and fees
facts.value: Standard includes 5 MATs; Pro includes 50. Both charge $0.50 per additional active tenant; Standard/Standalone tenant counts are documented as unlimited.

facts.label: Invitations and limits
facts.value: Native new/existing-user invite workflows send emails; new-user links can instead be generated/shared. New-user generated link lifetime is configurable from 10 minutes to 7 days.

facts.label: Tenant member and invitation-volume caps
facts.value: No fixed per-tenant member maximum or complete invitation-per-day/rate/overage quota was located.

facts.label: Enterprise SSO charge and scope
facts.value: SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO is included in Standard, Pro and Premium; public tariff has no per-SSO connection surcharge.

facts.label: SCIM/directory-sync fees
facts.value: No native SCIM plan, connection allowance or price schedule was located.

facts.label: Applications and environments
facts.value: Separate Wristband applications are recommended for dev/QA/staging/production; each has its own resources/config and vanity domain. Usage allowances pool at account level.

facts.label: Builder seats and object caps
facts.value: No explicit developer dashboard-seat, application/project, OAuth-client or domain quantity cap/overage schedule was found.

facts.label: Hosted email delivery
facts.value: Wristband sends native transactional emails using a managed domain for magic links, verification, invitations, password resets and change-email notices.

facts.label: Custom sender and unpriced channels
facts.value: Pro/Premium enable application/tenant custom email domains, requiring DNS ownership verification. No SMS delivery allowance/rate card was found.

facts.label: Over-allowance behavior
facts.value: Standard overages accrue and bill at period end; no card needed initially. An over-limit account receives an email invoice link, and the paying method becomes its future default.

facts.label: Failed payments and budget precision
facts.value: Failed charges retry up to 8 times over the following 2 weeks; vendor reserves suspension after multiple missed payments and aims to contact billing email first.

facts.label: Other usage charges
facts.value: Public recurring units are active tenants, users and machines; no per-human-token or ordinary management-request rate is listed.

facts.label: Individual eligibility and country restrictions
facts.value: Terms allow agreement personally or on behalf of an entity, require age 18+, and require legal/local-law compliance.

facts.label: Self-service production and card rules
facts.value: Standard starts at $0 with no card and explicitly permits production. Accounts start on Standard; Pro upgrade is available through owner-managed checkout.

facts.label: Time-limited trial and extra signup gates
facts.value: No fixed trial duration or compulsory company-domain email rule was located.

facts.label: Hosted service and scope
facts.value: Hosted multi-tenant identity platform: accounts, authentication, sessions, email verification, invitations, SSO and role/permission management.

facts.label: Vendor and builder operations
facts.value: Vendor runs hosted identities/authentication APIs and advertises automated backups/HA controls; builder runs app servers, protected business data, local sessions and API authorization checks.

facts.label: Password and username/email login
facts.value: Native Wristband IdP password login, enabled by default; can be password-only or combined with magic links.

facts.label: Magic-link login
facts.value: Native email one-time login link, enabled independently or alongside password; all plans include it.

facts.label: Standalone email/phone OTP precision
facts.value: Verification/reset/tenant-discovery workflows can use codes, but a general standalone numeric email-OTP sign-in or native phone/SMS-code account flow was not established.

facts.label: Anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No explicit guest/anonymous identity type or crypto-wallet login implementation was located.

facts.label: Named social integrations
facts.value: Official guides list Apple, Bitbucket, GitHub, GitLab, Google and Microsoft; all plans include social login.

facts.label: Social provider setup
facts.value: Google integration requires a Google OAuth web client, consent configuration, registered external IdP redirect URI and provider client ID/secret.

facts.label: Passkeys
facts.value: Native first-factor passkey/WebAuthn support, conditional autofill, platform matrix, recovery and domain-transfer rules were not established.

facts.label: Native second factor and plan
facts.value: TOTP authenticator-app MFA included in every plan; optional or required enrollment with app policies and per-tenant overrides.

facts.label: Recovery codes and external-IdP boundary
facts.value: Optional single-use backup recovery code is issued after TOTP enrollment; fresh TOTP re-enrollment invalidates/regenerates the old code. External IdPs enforce their own MFA.

facts.label: Verification and password reset
facts.value: Native email verification and user/admin password reset through hosted pages/API; reset can use a link or OTP and has maximum generated-link lifetime 1,440 minutes.

facts.label: Change email
facts.value: Verified workflow confirms the new address, notifies the old address and sends completion mail; identity proof depends on password, magic-link or external IdP.

facts.label: Self-deletion authorization
facts.value: Delete User API includes a Self permission boundary, as well as tenant/application administrative boundaries.

facts.label: Authentication-session expiry
facts.value: Tenant-domain persistent auth cookie points to Wristband server state; configurable idle expiry up to 90 days and absolute expiry up to 365 days.

facts.label: Application sessions, refresh and logout
facts.value: App maintains its own session/tokens. Logout requires clearing local state, revoking any refresh token and redirecting the browser to the tenant Logout endpoint.

facts.label: Session administration and default precision
facts.value: User dashboard can delete one/all authentication sessions. Exact universal default access-token/refresh lifetimes and default auth-session durations were not established.

facts.label: Protocol and SAML role
facts.value: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE for apps, OAuth client credentials for machines; Wristband is a SAML 2.0 service provider/broker for customer IdPs.

facts.label: Tenant membership and isolation
facts.value: Every user belongs to exactly one tenant. Tenant/IdP pairs scope identifier uniqueness; the same email can represent distinct users across tenants or IdPs.

facts.label: Roles and customer administration
facts.value: Native application/tenant custom roles, role assignments to users/machines, default signup/IdP roles and invitation role grants.

facts.label: SCIM account synchronization
facts.value: No complete native SCIM 2.0 provisioning/deactivation/group connector was found; documented offboarding can use a builder wrapper API, support or customer user-management portal.

facts.label: Hosted UI versus embedded widgets
facts.value: Hosted signup, tenant discovery, login, verification/reset/MFA/invite/change-email workflows; Custom Page URLs enable own UI. Vendor explicitly says no embedded frontend widgets.

facts.label: Standard versus paid branding
facts.value: All plans support app-level branding and auth-page/workflow customization. Pro/Premium add watermark removal, tenant white-labeling, app/tenant custom domains and custom email domains.

facts.label: Custom domain configuration and caveats
facts.value: Pro/Premium own domains require DNS verification/activation; tenant domain overrides app domain. Default vanity APIs keep working; app custom domains change JWT issuer and generated flow/IdP redirect URLs.

facts.label: Languages and accessibility evidence
facts.value: No complete hosted UI locale list, translation-override guide, WCAG assessment or VPAT was located.

facts.label: Official web/backend SDK coverage
facts.value: ASP.NET Core, Django, Express, FastAPI, Go, NestJS and Next.js auth SDKs; React client SDK; separate M2M, session and JWT helpers.

facts.label: Versioned runtime requirements
facts.value: Next.js SDK 5.0.0: Node >=22.0.0, npm >=10.5.1, Next peer ^14 \

facts.label: Native mobile/desktop integration
facts.value: Official protocol guide covers iOS/Android/macOS/Windows using a system browser, OIDC code+PKCE, registered redirects and platform secure storage.

facts.label: Native SDK and passkey precision
facts.value: Dedicated first-party Swift/Kotlin/React Native/Flutter SDKs and tested mobile passkey matrices were not established.

facts.label: Required app/credential setup
facts.value: Create hosted Wristband application, tenant and suitable OAuth client; configure allowed login/callback/logout URLs and app-side session management.

facts.label: Outside dependencies and operating costs
facts.value: Builder supplies application runtime/business storage and custom UI/session store as chosen. Vendor sends default emails; Pro webhooks use vendor-managed Svix with a builder receiver.

facts.label: Self-hosted operation requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the documented hosted platform; self-hosted workflow UI and MIT SDKs call Wristband's service.

facts.label: Metadata and token customization
facts.value: Native user/tenant metadata and custom token claims are included; user metadata objects max 4 KB, nesting depth 3 and 15 top-level fields.

facts.label: Webhook plan and event model
facts.value: Pro/Premium webhooks, disabled by default per application, delivered by Svix as HTTP POST; event types include user creation/update/deletion.

facts.label: Webhook delivery rules
facts.value: Verify signatures/timestamps; acknowledge with HTTP 2xx within 15 seconds. Failed deliveries retry on a published eight-step schedule, support manual replay and disable persistently failing endpoints after five days.

facts.label: Custom runtime and hook limits
facts.value: No vendor-hosted arbitrary custom-code hook runtime, execution CPU/time quota or universal webhook volume/retention fee schedule was located.

facts.label: User query and administration
facts.value: Dashboard/API support user creation/query/profile updates, invitation/reset/email verification, status changes, role assignment and deletion.

facts.label: Session controls and impersonation gap
facts.value: Dashboard can delete a user's individual/all auth sessions; a controlled support-user impersonation feature and its approval/audit guarantees were not established.

facts.label: Identity linking and shared-user model
facts.value: Native records are scoped to one tenant and IdP; no explicit safe multi-provider account linking/unlinking/merge or guest-upgrade lifecycle was located.

facts.label: Password and bot defenses
facts.value: All plans include breach detection and native TOTP. Password policy can block breached credentials/force reset; hosted signup/login pages integrate risk-based Google reCAPTCHA.

facts.label: Disposable email and protection precision
facts.value: Pro/Premium add disposable-email blocking. Exact brute-force request thresholds/lockout windows, independent SMS-fraud controls and hard spend caps were not established.

facts.label: Request rate and burst limits
facts.value: No public per-login/token/management request quota, burst bucket, retry header contract or per-account/per-user sharing scope was found.

facts.label: Event access and audit scope
facts.value: Pro/Premium native lifecycle webhooks can be exported to a builder receiver through Svix, with endpoint history/manual replay tools.

facts.label: Audit retention and export precision
facts.value: Customer-visible login/security audit retention days, immutable archive, full event coverage and export/stream retention limits were not established.

facts.label: Ready-made CSV export scope
facts.value: Official Python export script writes exactly tenantName, givenName, familyName, email and status to CSV.

facts.label: Broader profile/API extraction
facts.value: Get User schema exposes user/tenant/application IDs, IdP name/type, externalId, verification, profile attributes, status and metadata.

facts.label: Credential and archive portability
facts.value: No public password-hash export, full credentials/links/roles archive, export fee or guaranteed credential/domain migration procedure was found.

facts.label: User import and password limitation
facts.value: Official Python script imports CSV users into a selected tenant and can assign roles/invite users. FAQ explicitly says existing password hashes cannot be imported.

facts.label: Migration size and stable IDs
facts.value: Bulk import maximum/rate, legacy chosen user-ID preservation and universal lazy-password migration support were not established.

facts.label: User deletion and account closure paths
facts.value: Dashboard deletes a user; API supports administrative/self deletion. Privacy allows account termination/deletion requests through account settings or contact; paid cancellation takes effect at term end.

facts.label: Published privacy retention
facts.value: Privacy says no stated purpose requires personal data longer than 12 months after an account's idle period starts, subject to legal exceptions; unneeded data is deleted/anonymized or isolated in backup archives until deletion is possible.

facts.label: Detailed deletion/log/backup windows
facts.value: Exact end-user deletion completion, backup purge, security-log retention and tenant/account-close timetable were not located.

facts.label: Public US hosting statement
facts.value: Terms describe the Site as hosted in the United States and consent to transfer/processing there.

facts.label: Service residency choice and copies
facts.value: No complete selectable production-region list, region-by-plan fee, EU-only commitment or identity/log/backup/support location map was located.

facts.label: Security and assurance evidence
facts.value: Vendor claims AES-256 at rest, TLS in transit, Argon2 passwords/client secrets and isolated/rotatable app signing keys. Trust center lists current SOC 2 Type II Report – 2026; full report requires request/NDA.

facts.label: Processing/subprocessor documents
facts.value: A complete public end-user DPA or named subprocessor registry was not found. Privacy names Stripe and Metronome payment processors and analytics/social-login processing.

facts.label: Premium HIPAA contractual scope
facts.value: Premium advertises signed HIPAA BAAs, while generic Site terms say Site is not tailored to HIPAA/FISMA and restrict regulated use.

facts.label: Name, company and official URLs
facts.value: Wristband, operated by Apitopia, Inc., doing business as Wristband; terms identify a California company with a Berkeley registered office.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Standard and Pro are publicly self-service; Premium is sales-assisted. Current Next.js SDK v5.0.0 was published October 28, 2026.

facts.label: Hosted platform commercial rights
facts.value: Proprietary platform; API specification labels its license Private and public terms reserve Site/software rights.

facts.label: SDK license
facts.value: Wristband Next.js auth SDK is MIT; checked Next.js and React client package metadata also declare MIT.

facts.label: Status and advertised SLA
facts.value: Official site links status.wristband.dev. Pricing FAQ advertises 99.9% uptime SLA on every plan; Premium can negotiate a higher guarantee.

facts.label: SLA contract precision
facts.value: Detailed availability calculation period, exclusions, claim process and credit schedule were not located publicly.

facts.label: Dated SDK maintenance
facts.value: Next.js 5.0.0 published 2026-10-28T19:22:39.545Z; GitHub v5.0.0 release 2026-10-28T19:19:30Z. React client 3.3.0 published 2026-08-08T04:17:51.986Z.

facts.label: LTS and security support window
facts.value: No universal SDK LTS, supported-major retirement date or guaranteed vulnerability-fix duration was located.

facts.label: Support by plan
facts.value: Standard/Pro include email and community Slack. Premium adds dedicated Slack, integration/migration help, feature priority and negotiated response SLAs.

facts.label: Custom commitment

facts.label: Essential resource bundle

facts.label: Pro resource bundle

facts.label: Business pricing applicability

facts.label: Customer organizations and limits

facts.label: Organization fees and caps

facts.label: App-user SSO and SCIM fees
facts.value: No published app-user SAML connection, OIDC enterprise-connection, SCIM-directory, setup or per-connection rate card found.

facts.label: Free builder/project limits
facts.value: 1 workspace, 1 builder team seat; no custom backend domain, paid branches or extra data-source bundle.

facts.label: Essential builder/project limits
facts.value: 3 workspaces, 5 team seats; 3 data sources; branches/merging; 10 schema versions; custom backend domain.

facts.label: Pro and Custom builder/project limits
facts.value: Pro: 5 workspaces, 10 seats, 3 data sources, 20 schema versions; Custom: negotiated counts.

facts.label: Builder access controls
facts.value: Owner/admin/developer/read-only/suspended team roles; owner adds existing Xano accounts; Pro/Custom granular workspace permissions.

facts.label: Transactional email delivery
facts.value: Own email service or imported Action: Postmark, Brevo and custom API integrations; SendGrid used in older auth snippets.

facts.label: Email test credits

facts.label: Billing and resource-limit behavior

facts.label: Payment failure

facts.label: Optional capacity and security add-ons

facts.label: Unpriced add-on details

facts.label: Account eligibility
facts.value: Terms accept a person or an entity; account holder must be at least 18 and legally able to contract.

facts.label: Country restrictions

facts.label: Card and company-domain requirements
facts.value: No explicit public no-card promise or universal company-email requirement found in the checked signup guide, pricing and terms.

facts.label: Product type and auth scope

facts.label: Other deployment editions
facts.value: Custom/BYOC or on-premises platform; local Xano Engine binary with TypeScript SDK.

facts.label: Managed operator responsibilities
facts.value: Xano runs cloud infrastructure and managed database; builder designs schema, auth rules, endpoints, client storage and data access.

facts.label: Custom and local operation
facts.value: BYOC/on-prem offered on Custom under an agreed deployment; local Engine runs on developer machine.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built-in editable signup/login/me endpoint generators; email or username plus password; password validation and token creation functions.

facts.label: Email magic-link login
facts.value: Template/extension + own SendGrid; configurable redirect URL, token secret, email template and expiration.

facts.label: Phone passwordless methods
facts.value: SMS magic-link extension workflow with Twilio; phone code verification through custom Twilio Verify API endpoints.

facts.label: Email OTP, anonymous and wallet login
facts.value: No maintained native method contract found for email-code first-factor login, anonymous/guest sessions or wallet-signature login.

facts.label: Named social providers
facts.value: Marketplace OAuth flows: Facebook, Google, LinkedIn and GitHub; own OAuth app credentials and redirect setup required.

facts.label: Google integration detail
facts.value: Prebuilt Google OAuth init/continue APIs, with client ID/secret and registered redirect URI; client then stores returned Xano token.

facts.label: Apple and Microsoft app-user social login
facts.value: No specific maintained Apple or Microsoft app-user social integration contract found in the checked auth/provider docs.

facts.label: Passkey sign-in
facts.value: No native app-user WebAuthn/passkey registration, assertion, autofill, mobile, fallback or relying-party-domain support contract found.

facts.label: App-user second-factor SMS
facts.value: custom_code + external_service: Twilio Verify send/check endpoints; builder must gate sensitive access or session issuance on approved verification.

facts.label: Other app-user MFA and recovery
facts.value: TOTP enrollment, email second factor, WebAuthn second factor, backup codes and lost-device recovery policy not published as a native app-user package.

facts.label: Builder MFA boundary
facts.value: Xano dashboard accounts support authenticator-app six-digit 2FA; eligible instance Security Policy can require it for team members.

facts.label: Email confirmation
facts.value: Email Verification with SendGrid snippet creates signup/verification endpoints, Verified flag and MagicVerify token/expiration/used fields.

facts.label: Password reset
facts.value: Imported snippet: request magic link, validate it through authMagicLogin, submit new password to updateUserPassword; own frontend and email provider.

facts.label: Phone confirmation and profile changes
