facts.label: App-user account deletion
facts.value: Custom authenticated endpoint can invoke Delete Record; related membership, event and external-provider data need an explicit cleanup workflow.

facts.label: Session token model and expiry
facts.value: Encrypted JWE bearer tokens identify an auth-enabled table and record; Create Authentication Token takes expiration in seconds and optional extras.

facts.label: Refresh-token support

facts.label: Client logout and storage
facts.value: JS SDK setAuthToken(null) clears stored client token; storage can be localStorage, sessionStorage or custom storage.

facts.label: Revocation and multi-device controls
facts.value: A native global revoke, per-device session console, refresh reuse-detection or automatic revocation on password change was not found.

facts.label: App OAuth client role
facts.value: Imported OAuth authorization-code flows exchange an external provider’s authorization for a Xano JWE token.

facts.label: MCP OAuth/OIDC boundary
facts.value: MCP Hosted mode: Xano authorization server plus your login/consent page. External mode: validates OIDC-provider JWTs and maps claims to existing auth-table rows.

facts.label: Customer SAML and general OIDC service
facts.value: No documented generic customer-app SAML SP/IdP, OIDC provider/discovery or per-organization SAML setup contract found.

facts.label: Organizations and customer roles

facts.value: XanoScript/visual function stacks on Xano; official TypeScript backend authoring SDK compiles deployable definitions; JavaScript/TypeScript Lambdas can import supported NPM packages.

facts.label: Mobile clients
facts.value: REST integration advertised for React Native, Flutter, native iOS and Android.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Managed PostgreSQL and backend runtime included; builder supplies auth-enabled schema/table, frontend, policies and OAuth credentials; external mail/SMS as needed.

facts.label: Local Engine prerequisites
facts.value: SDK runs a downloaded platform binary with bundled Postgres; first download needs network, cached Engine runs without account/network.

facts.label: Custom production hosting
facts.value: BYOC AWS/Azure/GCP and on-premises; multi-zone/high-availability options and cross-zone backups negotiated through Custom.

facts.label: Local Engine operational limits
facts.value: Free binary runs until stopped; updates are pinned/explicit, but restart/update starts empty; --keep-data only preserves matching tables/columns across redeploys while that Engine runs.

facts.label: Hosted backup/restore
facts.value: Free: no backups. Paid: automatic rolling and manual backups/restores, optional media inclusion and configurable backup window.

facts.label: Paid backup retention conflict
facts.value: Essential 7 days / Pro 14 days on pricing cards; backup guide says all paid plans retain 3 days.

facts.label: Custom fields and logic
facts.value: Editable user tables, reusable functions, preconditions, custom claims/extras, database triggers and API workflows.

facts.label: Middleware plan gates
facts.value: Essential: 10 middleware objects and 10 background tasks; Pro: unlimited middleware/tasks; Free: no middleware/background tasks.

facts.label: Webhooks and external calls
facts.value: Build POST receivers, validate incoming signatures, process raw data and call external APIs; event payload, retries and idempotency depend on your workflow/provider.

facts.label: Runtime limits
facts.value: Lambdas run under a configured timeout; NPM import compatibility is limited; slow work can move to background tasks.

facts.label: User CRUD and support access
facts.value: Database user table and custom authenticated APIs support list/search/create/update/delete; Run & Debug can generate a test token for a selected app user.

facts.label: Ban and impersonation policy
facts.value: No native app-user ban/unban action or documented audited production impersonation permission model found.

facts.label: Account linking, unlinking and guest upgrade
facts.value: No maintained multi-provider account-link/unlink or anonymous-to-registered upgrade contract found.

facts.label: Endpoint protection defaults
facts.value: Auto-generated CRUD starts unauthenticated and externally reachable; builder must enable auth, filter records, restrict CORS and hide/secure Swagger where appropriate.

facts.label: Login throttling
facts.value: Paid backends have no default platform rate cap; guide recommends explicit login/signup throttles by IP/user; Redis Rate Limit function has key, maximum and TTL seconds.

facts.label: Bot checks
facts.value: Google reCAPTCHA is available as a Marketplace extension; builder integrates and configures it.

facts.label: Leaked credentials and SMS abuse
facts.value: No default breached-password screening, automated SMS spend guard or turnkey app-user risk policy found.

facts.label: Free and paid API ceilings
facts.value: Free: 10 requests/20 seconds; paid: no platform rate limit, still constrained by provisioned compute and application-defined limits.

facts.label: Management API and rate response detail
facts.value: Distinct Metadata API auth-admin limit, sliding/fixed-window semantics, Retry-After header and guaranteed HTTP status were not established by the checked public limit docs.

facts.label: Request and security-event history
facts.value: Live API/function/middleware/trigger/tool request history: 24h; background tasks: 7 days. Filter requests by authenticated user/IP/status; API-history export available.

facts.label: Workspace audit history by plan
facts.value: Free 24h; Essential 7 days; Pro 28 days; Custom unlimited, per pricing. Events cover workspace/schema/code/team operations, not a default full app login ledger.

facts.label: App-user audit extension
facts.value: B2B quick start has a custom event-log table and account/member history endpoints; builder controls event coverage, retention and exports.

facts.label: Profiles and identifiers export
facts.value: Self-service CSV export of table/view or selected records; use user and custom account/provider tables to export stored profile/ID/link columns.

facts.label: Credential export boundary
facts.value: Password field is hidden in database UI, but database queries can return its stored protected value; plaintext password cannot be retrieved.

facts.label: Full workspace export and execution rights
facts.value: Metadata API can export a complete data/configuration archive with optional password encryption; code/schema can also be handled with SDK pull/export.

facts.label: Exit protection and fees
facts.value: Terms promise a free perpetual self-host license if Xano ceases operation during an active paid subscription; enterprise custom terms may differ.

facts.label: Bulk import and custom IDs
facts.value: CSV creates new tables or appends/updates existing ones; imports over 5,000 records run in background; guide supports integer CSV primary keys.

facts.label: Password/provider migration in
facts.value: Supported existing-password hash algorithms, raw-hash import bypass, lazy rehash/migration and complete provider-link migration recipe not published in the checked docs.

facts.label: App data removal
facts.value: Delete Record deletes matching database records; builder must remove dependent membership/profile/event records and external-provider data as required.

facts.label: Backup and log retention
facts.value: Request history has published per-type windows; paid backup windows conflict between pricing and backup guide; exact erasure timing for deleted rows in all backups not published.

facts.label: Subscription cancellation and account closure
facts.value: Cancel Instance Subscription from Billing; cancellation effective at end of paid term. Privacy requests can be sent to privacy@xano.com.

facts.label: Privacy notice retention scope
facts.value: Vendor-account personal information kept while needed/account exists; DPF section says valid deletion requests result in deletion/anonymization within 30 days, with legal/claims exceptions.

facts.label: Refund terms conflict and upgrade exception
facts.value: Terms say all purchases non-refundable; Billing allows discretionary annual refund within first month minus used time; Instance Settings offers 48-hour Essential→Pro difference refund.

facts.label: Free data location
facts.value: Free hosted instance: United States only.

facts.label: Paid server regions
facts.value: Essential/Pro pricing: Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, Switzerland, India, Indonesia, Japan, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Korea, UK, United States.

facts.label: Region changes and Custom placement
facts.value: Paid region change has no separate fee but restarts/credits billing; changes API base URL and does not migrate unpublished drafts; Custom can deploy in chosen cloud/on-prem regions.

facts.label: Residency scope and subprocessors
facts.value: App database, media, logs, backups and support/AI processing do not have one fully published same-region guarantee.

facts.label: DPA availability
facts.value: DPA with SCCs available on paid plans, excluding Free, by emailing security@xano.com; full DPA text not publicly supplied on the checked trust page.

facts.label: Subprocessors and privacy roles
facts.value: Public list current 2026-10-20: GCP core infrastructure; Intercom and Segment support; Google Gemini and Anthropic optional AI. Xano is processor for customer apps.

facts.label: Assurance evidence and scope
facts.value: Vendor SOC 2 Type II claim: IT Consulting Services System, Security criteria, examination 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31; detailed report access requested through trust center.

facts.label: Health-data agreement boundary
facts.value: Regulated health data requires an eligible plan/add-on and an executed BAA/BASA/HDS or other applicable written health-data agreement before processing.

facts.label: Name, owner and official URLs
facts.value: Xano; Xano, Inc.; official website and documentation. No product-wide rebrand established.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Public self-service Free, Essential and Pro; Custom through sales; maintained. Signup and checkout not tested.

facts.label: Component lifecycle notices
facts.value: Logic Assistant deprecated in favor of Xano Agent; old Marketplace being phased out in favor of Actions; existing installed Marketplace items do not disappear.; MCP SSE transport deprecated in 2.5, with future removal announced.

facts.label: Hosted platform commercial terms
facts.value: Proprietary service, subscriptions governed by Terms & Conditions; website content rights do not grant an open-source server license.

facts.label: Xano Engine license
facts.value: Binary-only, free to run; no source code licensed. Current text is explicitly a placeholder pending final terms; each release retains its shipped license.

facts.label: SDK licenses
facts.value: Official TypeScript backend SDK: MIT; Xano JavaScript client SDK: MIT.

facts.label: Public status
facts.value: Public regional status and incident history at status.xano.com.

facts.label: Availability promise conflict
facts.value: Pro card advertises 99.99% SLA; same pricing comparison says 99.95% uptime guarantee for Pro/Custom; support guide lists SLAs only for Custom.

facts.label: Platform maintenance evidence
facts.value: Official Xano 2.7 announcement dated Fri Oct 23, 2026 describes deployment approvals, MCP OAuth and PHP runtime security fixes.

facts.label: Managed update scheduling
facts.value: Paid plans: Immediate default or Flexible preferred window/day; enterprise Manual; emergency patches can override preferences.

facts.label: Deployable component maintenance
facts.value: TypeScript SDK main package version 1.0.19; changelog latest entry 1.0.18 dated 2026-10-30; Engine version pinned per project, not silently advanced.

facts.label: Support channels by plan
facts.value: Free community; paid in-product realtime support; Custom dedicated personnel and 24/7 emergency outage support; support@xano.com and community are documented.

facts.label: Response/resolution times and extra support price
facts.value: No public severity-by-severity response/resolution hours found; Custom emergency escalation White House Support add-on price not published.

apps.name: ZITADEL
apps.line: Open-source identity platform with a Cloud or self-host option.

free.text: Cloud Free: $0/month, 100 daily active user units

cells.freeUsers: 100 DAU (Free); 25,000 DAU units on Pro
cells.sso: Pro: $100 per 5 extra external IdPs after 3

apps.news: ZITADEL's core repository changed from Apache 2.0 to AGPL-3.0 with the v3.0.0 release on 2025-05-02.

facts.label: Active-user billing definition
facts.value: Cloud Pro uses sum of daily active users across the billing month: login, refresh-token activity or service-account authentication makes a user active once for that day.

facts.label: External provider meter
facts.value: Activated/ready-for-use external IdPs across instances are counted each day; monthly bill uses the monthly daily average rounded up to an integer. Inactive configured providers are excluded.

facts.label: Management requests and seats
facts.value: Authenticated /zitadel.*, /v2alpha*, /v2beta*, /v2*, /admin*, /management* and /system* requests are billable management units; customer Portal administrators are a separate seat measure.

facts.label: Free Cloud allowance
facts.value: US$0/month; 100 DAU units, 3 active external IdPs, 5,000 management requests, 1 instance, 1 Portal admin; unlimited stored users, organizations and applications.

facts.label: Free production conditions
facts.value: Free is an ongoing advertised tier, not a timed trial; default Cloud SMTP is testing/evaluation only and must be replaced for production email.

facts.label: Self-host software allowance
facts.value: AGPL core can run without a vendor per-user software charge when license conditions are met; hosting and operations are customer costs.

facts.label: Cloud Pro minimum
facts.value: US$100/month base; 25,000 summed DAU units, 3 active external IdPs, 500,000 management requests, 3 Portal admins and 1 custom domain included.

facts.label: Enterprise minimum and commitment
facts.value: Cloud and self-host Enterprise: quote-only minimum annual contract value, plus add-ons and usage. Enterprise/support annex describes a minimum 12-month term.

facts.label: Pro DAU excess
facts.value: After 25,000 monthly summed DAU units, US$50 per additional started block of 2,500.

facts.label: Pro provider excess
facts.value: 3 active external IdPs included, then US$100 per started block of 5 additional connections.

facts.label: Pro API excess
facts.value: 500,000 management requests included, then US$100 per additional started block of 500,000.

facts.label: Calculator quote threshold
facts.value: The current Pro calculator displays 'Contact Us for a Quote' when its computed monthly total exceeds US$3,000.

facts.label: Enterprise usage model
facts.value: No DAU/MAU price under Enterprise; base includes users/tenants/clients. Contract usage can include external/LDAP/SCIM connections, organization types, policies and Actions/workflows.

facts.label: Business scenarios
facts.value: Our exactly-two-day calculation gives Pro auth subtotals A US$100 and B US$300. Baseline totals remain unsettled by active days, API/service-user usage and invitation email delivery.

facts.label: Organization allowance: Free/Pro
facts.value: Unlimited customer organizations and stored users are advertised; no separate Pro per-organization fee appears in the rate card.

facts.label: Enterprise organization charges
facts.value: Enterprise base advertises unlimited instances/organizations/projects/clients/users, but contract pricing can include B2C/M2M organization metrics and organization-specific policies.

facts.label: Business SSO price: Free/Pro
facts.value: SAML/OIDC upstream customer IdPs use the same active-external-provider meter as social providers. Free/Pro include 3; Pro extra blocks cost US$100 per 5.

facts.label: SCIM price and maturity
facts.value: Pricing marks inbound SCIM included across Free/Pro/Enterprise; API reference labels SCIM v2.0 Preview. Enterprise separately lists SCIM connections as contract usage.

facts.label: Free developer/project capacity
facts.value: Cloud Free: 1 instance and 1 customer Portal admin; unlimited clients/applications and organization domains.

facts.label: Pro developer/project capacity
facts.value: Cloud Pro: unlimited instances/applications, 3 Portal admins and 1 custom domain included. Extra Portal admins US$20 each/month; extra custom domains US$50 each/month.

facts.label: Enterprise capacity
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud/self-host table advertises unlimited instances, applications, Portal administrators and organization domains; specific commercial conditions remain in the order.

facts.label: Production email dependency
facts.value: Built-in Cloud SMTP is for development/testing. Production must use customer SMTP or an HTTP email relay; documented templates include Amazon SES, Mailgun, Mailjet and SendGrid, plus generic SMTP.

facts.label: SMS and custom delivery
facts.value: No default SMS provider is configured. Customer supplies Twilio credentials or an HTTP notification endpoint; Twilio Messages or Verify can be selected.

facts.label: Sender domain conditions
facts.value: Default-settings guide says a custom instance domain is needed for mail from a domain you own; sender-domain matching can be configured.

facts.label: At quotas and excessive use
facts.value: Paid excess units are billed at period end; terms permit suspension for exhausted credit, reached credit limits, nonpayment or harmful use. Rate limiting returns HTTP 429.

facts.label: Free exhaustion and spending control
facts.value: Exact Free DAU/API exhaustion behavior, automatic paid upgrade, usage grace, customer-configurable spend cap and alert thresholds were not found.

facts.label: Inactive accounts and refunds
facts.value: Terms allow Free termination after 30 days with no DAU. Refund policy permits requests for accidental overages/unused auto-renewals within 3 business days; ordinary consumed usage is nonrefundable.

facts.label: Optional Pro support/SLA add-on
facts.value: Published Pro calculator prices Extended Support & SLA at US$999/month upfront, in addition to base/usage.

facts.label: Other Enterprise costs
facts.value: Enterprise add-ons can include private Slack, extra technical-account-manager hours, custom MSA/liability/compliance terms and enterprise-only features; all are quote-only.

facts.label: Individual and country eligibility
facts.value: Public self-service targets developers and startups. An exhaustive seller/billing-country list, age rule and explicit sole-person eligibility clause were not found.

facts.label: Self-service and Free entry
facts.value: Cloud Free signup is public and no credit card is required. Pro is self-service with credit-card monthly billing; no fixed Free trial expiry is advertised.

facts.label: Product type and scope
facts.value: Cloud identity service and self-hosted server: accounts, authentication, verification, sessions, authorization, organizations, OIDC/SAML brokering and administration APIs.

facts.label: Cloud operator
facts.value: Vendor operates Cloud infrastructure and updates; customer configures policies, clients and integrations and operates its application.

facts.label: Self-host operator
facts.value: Customer operates server/login app, PostgreSQL, TLS/proxy, backup/restore, upgrades and monitoring; commercial support does not transfer disaster-recovery responsibility.

facts.label: Password login
facts.value: Built-in username/password, including email or phone as a login identifier when policy allows. Available in Cloud all-security tiers and self-host core.

facts.label: Email/SMS OTP and email-link scope
facts.value: Email and SMS OTP are documented MFA factors and verification mechanisms. A built-in standalone first-factor email code, SMS code or magic-link login was not established.

facts.label: Anonymous guest and wallet login
facts.value: No documented native anonymous-account issuance/guest promotion or wallet/SIWE login route was found in the login, user-model and API material checked.

facts.label: Built-in social/provider templates
facts.value: Catalog lists Google, GitHub, GitLab and Apple, plus Microsoft Entra ID OIDC/SAML, LDAP, Okta OIDC/SAML, Keycloak generic OIDC and JWT-provider setup.

facts.label: Generic external providers
facts.value: OIDC-compliant custom providers and SAML upstream IdPs can be configured; optional just-in-time user creation/update and organization-specific providers are documented.

facts.label: Passkeys and security keys
facts.value: Built-in FIDO2/WebAuthn first-factor passkeys, platform/cross-platform authenticators and user-controlled enrollment/deletion; available in Free/Pro and self-host core.

facts.label: Domain and native requirements
facts.value: Passkeys are domain-bound; choose a stable/custom domain before enrollment. Native iOS/Android platform APIs need app/domain association files, served from OIDC application settings.

facts.label: Moving login domains
facts.value: Hosted-login guide warns existing passkeys may stop working if Login V2 runs on a different domain; placing it under the existing instance domain can avoid that issue.

facts.label: MFA factors and policy
facts.value: Built-in TOTP, email OTP, SMS OTP, U2F security key and WebAuthn/passkey factors; policy can force MFA globally or for local-authenticated users.

facts.label: MFA recovery codes
facts.value: User v2 API can generate single-use recovery codes for the authenticated user when other second factors are unavailable.

facts.label: Cloud administrator lockout recovery
facts.value: Vendor access-recovery policy covers paid Cloud Portal/instance-manager lockouts with identity verification; Free instances, self-host and ordinary end-user requests are excluded.

facts.label: Verification and contact changes
facts.value: Built-in email/phone verification via OTP and self-service contact/profile changes; imports or admin creation can mark a verified email explicitly.

facts.label: Password reset and initial invitations
facts.value: Hosted password reset sends a link to the verified email address. Invitations initialize authentication; Login V2 can let the user choose password, passkey or configured external provider.

facts.label: Self-deletion
facts.value: User can permanently delete its own account via User v2 API or Console Delete Account button, requiring user.self.delete permission.

facts.label: Session model and checks
facts.value: Server-side login sessions associated with a user-agent cookie; Session API stores factor checks and verifiedAt times. Custom clients must verify sufficient factors and freshness.

facts.label: Session expiry
facts.value: Session API accepts a lifetime when creating/updating a session; update recalculates expiry. If no lifetime is set, the custom Session API session never expires.

facts.label: OIDC token lifetimes
facts.value: Instance-level access/ID-token lifetimes and absolute/idle refresh expiration can be changed by Console, API or Terraform; seconds-level API values are supported.

facts.label: Revocation and logout
facts.value: Session API supports delete/terminate by the authenticated user or authorized admin; OIDC RP-initiated and back-channel logout are documented. Front-channel logout is explicitly not implemented.

facts.label: OIDC/OAuth and downstream SAML
facts.value: ZITADEL acts as OIDC provider/OAuth authorization server and SAML 2.0 identity provider to application clients; SAML supports HTTP-Redirect/POST bindings.

facts.label: Incoming business SSO
facts.value: ZITADEL acts as broker/service provider for upstream SAML or OIDC IdPs configured per customer organization or at instance level.

facts.label: Organizations and isolated user pools
facts.value: Native organizations isolate users/settings; a project can be granted to other organizations with selected roles and delegated user-role administration.

facts.label: Membership and invitations
facts.value: Customer administrator can create/invite team members, assign organization/project roles, configure its own SSO and manage organization security/branding.

facts.label: Shared users and tenant switching
facts.value: External user grants let users from another organization access a project. Organization context is resolved from login/scopes/domain; users are not documented as freely moving their home account between tenants.

facts.label: SCIM implementation and maturity
facts.value: Built-in inbound SCIM 2.0 service-provider API at /scim/v2/{orgId}; currently labelled Preview. Supports user create/read/search/replace/patch/delete and Bulk.

facts.label: SCIM scope and deactivation
facts.value: SCIM supports user deactivation via active=false. Only core User schema is supported; Group provisioning and extended schemas are explicitly unsupported.

facts.label: Hosted login and account UI
facts.value: Built-in hosted signup/login, account picker, reset, MFA/passkey enrollment and self-service profile/security screens. Cloud and self-host can use them.

facts.label: Custom Login V2
facts.value: Next.js Login app can be forked/self-hosted; uses Session/User APIs and a server-side service-account PAT. Custom login API integration is also supported.

facts.label: Brand customization
facts.value: Per-instance/organization light/dark logos, colors, custom fonts and watermark visibility; project policy controls which organization's branding appears.

facts.label: Cloud domains
facts.value: Pro/Enterprise Cloud include one custom instance domain; Pro extras US$50/domain/month upfront. Free's custom-domain cell is blank; generated domains are included.

facts.label: Self-host domains
facts.value: Operator sets its own domain, DNS, TLS/proxy and external-domain configuration; Cloud domain subscription rates are not applicable.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: Documented languages: German, English, Spanish, French, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Simplified Chinese, Bulgarian, Portuguese, Macedonian, Czech, Russian, Dutch, Swedish, Hungarian, Korean, Romanian, Turkish, Ukrainian and Arabic.

facts.label: Accessibility evidence
facts.value: A public WCAG conformance statement, VPAT or complete accessibility assessment for current login/Console was not found.

facts.label: Web integration routes
facts.value: Vendor SDK catalog links React/Vue and Go integrations, plus OIDC library examples for Angular, Next.js, Nuxt, Svelte, Express, Django, Flask, FastAPI, Laravel and other frameworks.

facts.label: Browser, server and API runtime roles
facts.value: SPA/native clients use Authorization Code with PKCE; server web apps can protect a client secret. Administration uses REST/gRPC/Connect APIs; Next.js Login app has a server component.

facts.label: Native/mobile/desktop clients
facts.value: Native app type covers iOS, Android and desktop such as Electron/Tauri with Authorization Code/PKCE; vendor Flutter guide covers iOS, Android and Web.

facts.label: Native SDK and passkey limits
facts.value: Native platform passkeys are documented through OIDC app associations; dedicated vendor Swift/Kotlin/React Native SDK support/version matrix was not established.

facts.label: Hosted prerequisites
facts.value: Cloud hosts identity storage; customer supplies app/redirect setup, backend token validation, production SMTP and SMS provider if used.

facts.label: Self-host database and runtime
facts.value: PostgreSQL 14–18 supported; Docker Compose v2 or Kubernetes deployment. HTTP/2-capable upstream proxy required; Redis is optional cache, standalone only, not Cluster/Sentinel.

facts.label: Deployment and operating work
facts.value: Official server is stateless with state in PostgreSQL; production guide recommends HA, HTTP/2 networking/WAF, TLS, monitoring, secret storage and tested database restores.

facts.label: Published sizing
facts.value: Production doc says server approximately 512MB RAM and less than 1 CPU core can operate; recommends 4 CPU cores for password hashing and a minimal HA cluster of 3 nodes × 4 CPUs/16GB.

facts.label: Upgrades and backup
facts.value: Run setup/migrations for each new version before rolling out runtime processes; official Helm separates init/setup jobs. Back up PostgreSQL/event store and test restores.

facts.label: Actions v2 and custom data
facts.value: Built-in configuration can call customer HTTP endpoints on API request/response, functions or stored events; user metadata supports custom attributes and token claims.

facts.label: Webhook delivery semantics
facts.value: Targets can be Webhook, Call or Async. InterruptOnError can halt the execution on HTTP status >=400; request headers include ZITADEL-Signature HMAC with timestamp.

facts.label: Administration and API lifecycle
facts.value: Console and APIs create/read/search/update users, metadata, organizations, projects, role grants and authentication methods. New integrations should use v2; v1 remains supported but is not extended.

facts.label: Disable and restore access
facts.value: User v2 deactivation blocks login while retaining data; reactivation restores login. Lock is a separate temporary state with dedicated endpoint.

facts.label: Impersonation
facts.value: OAuth token exchange supports impersonation with an actor token and explicit impersonator permission; end-user impersonators cannot impersonate an administrator with memberships.

facts.label: External identity linking
facts.value: Multiple external identities can link to one ZITADEL user. Manual/authenticated linking and configured automatic match criteria are documented.

facts.label: Linked-account login choices
facts.value: Current account-linking page says linked users are auto-routed and local fallback occurs on IdP failure; older self-service wording says users can log in with either local or linked methods.

facts.label: Guest promotion
facts.value: A native anonymous-account-to-registered-account upgrade preserving an existing guest ID was not found.

facts.label: Password and lockout controls
facts.value: Configurable password complexity/expiry, failed password/OTP attempt thresholds and unknown-username response behavior.

facts.label: Bot/CAPTCHA protection scope
facts.value: Vendor FAQ says suspicious-activity CAPTCHA uses Google Cloud Armor and registration CAPTCHA is a feature request; it also makes an unqualified self-host-default claim.

facts.label: Cloud UI/API rate limits
facts.value: Per IP: /ui/* login/register/reset 10 requests/second over 1 minute, banning threshold 15/second over 3 minutes; other gRPC/REST/OAuth paths 50/second over 1 minute and 50/second over 3 minutes.

facts.label: Self-host throttling
facts.value: Operator should configure WAF/rate limits and bot detection; Cloud's IP policy is not an included fixed throughput SLA for self-host.

facts.label: Audit history definition and export
facts.value: Audit history is past object-change events retrievable through Console/API; Event API supports filters/time ranges and external SIEM pull/Action-webhook integration.

facts.label: Free history/log windows
facts.value: Cloud Free: 1 day audit history; 30 minutes logs.

facts.label: Pro history/log windows
facts.value: Cloud Pro: 2 weeks audit history; 1 day logs.

facts.label: Enterprise history/log windows
facts.value: Enterprise Cloud/self-host pricing table marks audit history and logs unlimited; customer-run retention/storage still needs configuration.

facts.label: User and credential export
facts.value: Admin /admin/v1/export can write JSON response/file or GCS; with_passwords includes password hashes and with_otp includes users' OTP data. Select/include/exclude organizations.

facts.label: What resource migration excludes
facts.value: Documented script omits global policies, instance members, global IdPs/global MFA, machine/PAT/application keys, passkey authentication and the event stream/audit history.

facts.label: Bulk user/hash import
facts.value: Admin /admin/v1/import accepts formatted organization/user data, custom userId and bcrypt password hashes in the vendor migration example.

facts.label: Lazy migration
facts.value: Vendor JIT guide uses Login V2 + Actions v2 and a customer legacy adapter: find/create missing user, verify legacy password, set a ZITADEL password on first successful login.

facts.label: User deletion and audit
facts.value: Self-deletion is permanent; user state becomes deleted and sessions/tokens are invalidated. Admins can still audit deletion through Event API.

facts.label: Cloud account closure and retention
facts.value: Customer Portal settings allow account/personal-information deletion. DPA requires return or destruction of customer data/copies at termination, except legally required retention.

facts.label: Cloud backups and recovery
facts.value: Vendor says daily full backups plus more frequent differential backups; disaster RPO goal 1 hour and somewhat longer/similar RTO, normal-operation goals below 1 minute.

facts.label: Selectable Cloud primary regions
facts.value: US us-central1; EU europe-west3; Switzerland europe-west6; Australia australia-southeast1. Region selected when creating an instance, including Free.

facts.label: Backup residency and access
facts.value: Region article says encrypted backups remain in GCP in the instance's region; international user traffic may cross regions. Support/engineering access requires explicit customer authorization/instruction.

facts.label: Self-host location
facts.value: Customer chooses infrastructure location and controls storage/network/access; Cloud's fixed region menu is not applicable to own deployment.

facts.label: Public privacy and transfer evidence
facts.value: Public privacy policy and DPA; customer controller/vendor processor; SCC/UK safeguards and vendor Data Privacy Framework self-certification described.

facts.label: Subprocessor objection deadlines
facts.value: Same DPA contains an objection period of 5 calendar days in one paragraph and 15 calendar days in the next, with 15-day advance-change notice.

facts.label: Assurance claims
facts.value: Cloud rate card and plan guide claim ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II; self-host table marks hosted certifications not applicable to customer infrastructure.

facts.label: Detailed trust reports and subprocessors
facts.value: Trust Center and its subprocessors route returned a client-rendered shell without readable report/list content; complete live subprocessor list and gated audit evidence were not retrieved.

facts.label: Name, owner and URLs
facts.value: ZITADEL; parent ZITADEL Inc., San Francisco, USA; wholly owned operating subsidiary CAOS AG, Switzerland. Site https://zitadel.com/; docs https://zitadel.com/docs.

facts.label: Contracting entity
facts.value: Self-service Cloud globally: CAOS AG under Swiss law. US Enterprise: ZITADEL Inc.; Enterprise elsewhere: CAOS AG.

facts.label: Availability and lifecycle
facts.value: Cloud signup and maintained self-host code are available. Latest returned stable release v4.20.1 published 2026-11-03 08:08:50 UTC.

facts.label: Self-host core license
facts.value: Current server root LICENSE: AGPL-3.0; v3.0.0's release notes date the Apache-2.0 to AGPL-3.0 change to 2025-05-02. Earlier releases retain their original terms.

facts.label: Login UI and generated clients
facts.value: apps/login has its own MIT license. Vendor FAQ says proto definitions, SDKs and tools remain Apache-2.0.

facts.label: Commercial license
facts.value: Self-host Enterprise can buy a commercial license instead of AGPL; modifications/redistribution conditions and fee depend on the commercial agreement.

facts.label: Public status
facts.value: Official public status dashboard: https://zitadelstatus.com/; separates Global Portal/Billing and US/EU/CH/AU service components and incident history.

facts.label: Cloud uptime promise discrepancies
facts.value: Pricing/plan/legal pages differ: Pro detail says 99.5% add-on; legal describes default 99.5% and extended 99.95%; Pro guide says optional 99.9%. Enterprise guide/metrics also differ on default 99.5% versus 99.9%.

facts.label: SLA coverage and credits
facts.value: Legal SLA measures calendar-month core auth/OIDC/SAML/login/brokering availability; excludes announced/emergency maintenance and force majeure. Credits require claim/proof within 30 days and are future invoice credit, not cash.

facts.label: Release and support lifecycle
facts.value: Public release API returned stable v4.20.1 on 2026-11-03. Release policy distinguishes preview/alpha/beta from GA; only GA features have normal support coverage.

facts.label: Self-host support and security reporting
facts.value: Enterprise annex can withhold support on builds more than 180 days older than latest stable until upgraded/recertified; security policy directs private reports to vulnerability portal and security.txt.

facts.label: Support routes
facts.value: Community chat/GitHub; paid support tickets through customer Portal and support@zitadel.com. Enterprise can include TAM and private support; billing@zitadel.com handles billing.

facts.label: Support hours/response conflict
facts.value: Current detailed pricing says Pro 24/7, 48-hour response, 1-hour upgrade. Older support annex says Production 48 business hours and extended 1 business hour, with Swiss business/extended office hours.
